Q24555195.lead: Love Station is a 2016 Odia-language drama film directed by Ashok Pati, with Babushaan Mohanty and Elina Samantray in the lead roles.

p: Sanju is the younger son of Rudra Narayan Satapathy, a retired headmaster in Rourkela who keeps a count of every family member's mistakes and turns out anyone who reaches one hundred. Sanju already has ninety-nine against his name when the family sets off by train for his elder brother's wedding in Puri. He misses the train along with Rani, a young woman bound for Puri, and the two chase it from station to station by auto-rickshaw, bus and police van, falling for each other along the way. At the wedding, Sanju's part in helping the bride elope is exposed, and his father is finally persuaded to give up his rule of banishment.

The film was made under the Tarang Cine Productions banner and produced by Jagi Mangad Panda. Santosh Narayan Das wrote the story, while Ashok Pati wrote the screenplay as well as directing. Sitanshu Mohapatra handled the cinematography.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak. The playback singers included Babushaan, Ira Mohanty, Papu Pom Pom, Tariq Aziz, Pamela Jain and Sanju.
The film was released on 12 June 2016.

Q6376113.lead: Kathantara (Another Story) is a 2007 Odia-language disaster drama written and directed by Himansu Khatua, set among survivors of the 1999 Odisha super cyclone.

p: The film follows Kalpana, a young widow who lost her entire family in the October 1999 cyclone and lives in a Bengali Hindu refugee settlement on the Odisha coast, where her father had come from East Bengal at Partition. Dipankar, a television journalist from Bangladesh, comes to document the cyclone anniversary and later proposes that she settle with him in Dhaka. During a stop in Kolkata she decides against it and returns to her village, only to receive a deportation notice. Resolving to stay in the land of her birth, she turns to her childhood friend Akshaya and asks him to marry her.

Iti Rani Samanta produced the film, and Khatua wrote the story as well as directing. Sameer Mahajan was the cinematographer, Rabi Pattnaik edited it and Amiya Maharana was the art director. The dialogue is in Odia and Bengali, and the running time is 116 minutes.
Swarup Nayak composed the score and also wrote the song lyrics.
The film was released on 14 December 2007 and distributed by Kadambinee Media.

Kathantara won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia. At the Orissa State Film Awards for 2006 it was named best feature film of the year, and Khatua took Best Director and Best Story. Further state awards went to Swarup Nayak for music direction, Sameer Mahajan for photography, Manas Chaudhry and Gitimugdha Sahani for audiography, Bhaswati Basu as supporting actress and Hadu as supporting actor.

Q115096622.lead: DAMaN is a 2022 Odia-language adventure drama written and directed by Vishal Mourya and Debi Prasad Lenka, starring Babushaan Mohanty and Dipanwit Dashmohapatra. It won the National Film Award for Best Odia Film.

p: In 2015, Siddharth, a newly qualified doctor from Bhubaneswar, is sent against his will to the Janbai primary health centre in a remote, Naxal-affected part of Malkangiri district, which serves 151 villages. He is about to resign when a girl believed to be possessed by a spirit turns out to have malaria. With the pharmacist Rabindra, he begins visiting villages that rely on exorcism, testing and treating people and securing mosquito nets; when the nets go unused and malaria returns, he presses for a wider awareness campaign. Three years on, infection levels have fallen sharply and he leaves Janbai for further studies.

The title is an acronym for Durgama Anchalare Malaria Nirakarana (malaria control in inaccessible areas), the name of an Odisha government scheme covering eight malaria-endemic southern districts. The two directors also wrote the story and screenplay, and Debi Prasad Lenka edited the film. Deependra Samal produced it through JP Motion Pictures and Mentis Films, with Pratap Rout as cinematographer. The budget is given as ₹94 lakh, and the film runs 121 minutes.
Gaurav Anand composed the soundtrack. The songs were written by lyricists including JP Wordsmith and Bapu Goswami, and sung by Ruturaj Mohanty, Babushaan, Anurag Das and Gaurav Anand among others.

The film opened on 4 November 2022 in 51 theatres in Odisha and 15 more in cities such as Bengaluru, Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata and Hyderabad. Reviewers from The Times of India, The Hindu, The Quint and Zee Odisha responded positively; The Times of India rated it four out of five. It became the highest-grossing Odia film, overtaking God Father-True Story of a Man (2016). The Odisha government made it tax-free, and a Hindi-dubbed version, whose trailer was launched by Ajay Devgn, followed on 3 February 2023 through Panorama Studios.
At the 70th National Film Awards, DAMaN was named Best Odia Film, an award carrying a Rajat Kamal and a cash prize of ₹2 lakh.

Q30612729.lead: Abhaya (Fearless) is a 2017 Odia-language action thriller directed by Murali Krishna and produced by Tarang Cine Productions, starring Anubhav Mohanty, Elina Samantray and Manoj Mishra.

p: Abhaya is an ordinary middle-class young man whose father serves in the police. After a student injured in violence engineered by a corrupt law minister dies, Abhaya secretly abducts the minister's brother Satyaprakash and holds him in an abandoned building site, never revealing his identity; the minister loses his post and is arrested. Once freed, Satyaprakash hunts for his captor and seizes Abhaya's girlfriend Anu, leading to a final confrontation in which Abhaya rescues her.

The film is a remake of the Tamil film Ivan Veramathiri (2013), with key sequences taken from the Kannada film Chakravyuha (2016). Debidatta Mohanty wrote the screenplay and Santosh Narayan Das the dialogue. Amit Nayak was the cinematographer and Rajesh Das the editor.
Prem Anand composed the music to lyrics by Basant Raj Samal and Subrat Swain. Humane Sagar, Ananya Sritam Nanda, Diptirekha Padhi and Lopamudra Das were among the singers.
Abhaya was released on 11 June 2017, during the Raja festival.

At the Chalachitra Jagat Pratibha Samman, Manoj Mishra was named best villain and Mihir Das received the Dukhiram Swain memorial award. Elina Samantray won the best actress award at the 12th Film and Television Award Show Time in 2018.

Q6986923.lead: Neeraba Jhada (The Silent Storm) is a 1984 Odia-language drama film produced and directed by Manmohan Mahapatra, about impoverished peasants in an Odisha village and a landlord's hold over their land.

p: In a poor, isolated village, most farmers have mortgaged their land to the landlord Janardhan, and many are driven to leave as contract labourers; Haria goes to raise money for his daughter's dowry. Bhamar, whose plot is the last one Janardhan does not control, angers the landlord by working in a stone quarry instead of labouring on his fields, and is later ostracised after a scandal involving his daughter Phoola. Haria returns ill and empty-handed, and the film ends with Bhamar leaving for contract work, vowing to come back and reclaim his land.

The film was made by Chayyadhwani Productions, with Mahapatra also writing the screenplay. B. Bindhani and Rajsekhar shot it, Satyendra Mohanty edited it and Shantanu Mahapatra composed the music. Hemanta Das, Niranjan Patnaik, Robin Das, Jaya Swami and Manimala headed the cast. It runs 120 minutes and was distributed by the National Film Development Corporation of India.
Critics described it as an unsparing portrait of villagers held down by poverty, superstition and feudal custom that nonetheless pays tribute to their endurance and hope.
It won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia (Silver Lotus) and the National Film Award for Best Cinematography in the black-and-white category.

facts: National Film Development Corporation of India

Q45284622.lead: Prema Adhei Akshara is a 2010 Odia-language romantic drama directed by Sudhakar Basant, starring Babushaan Mohanty and Riya Dey. It is a remake of the 2007 Telugu film Aadavari Matalaku Arthale Verule.

p: Amar, an unemployed young man from a middle-class family, falls for Chandini and gets a job at the software firm where she works. She rejects him, saying her marriage to a cousin has been arranged, and after his father dies Amar goes with his friend Raja to Raja's village, where Chandini turns out to be Raja's fiancée. She comes to realise she loves Amar, and after he is stabbed by goons and hospitalised, her family accepts the couple.

Narayan Chandra Nayak produced the film for Umamani Visual Creations. Basant wrote the screenplay, Rajani Ranjan the dialogue, and the story is credited to Sunita Narendra Singh. Ramesh Babu was the cinematographer. The dancer Riya Dey made her screen debut after an event manager recommended her to the director. Part of the shoot took place in Bhingarpur, and Babushaan was injured while filming an action scene.

Malay Misra composed the music, with lyrics by Basantaraj Samal, Arun Mantri, Nirmal Nayak and Subrat Swain. Mohammed Aziz, Babushaan, Ira Mohanty, Udit Narayan and T. Souri were among the singers. The song "Megharu Tu Jharilu" was adapted from "Yemaindi Ee Vela" in the Telugu original.
The film was released on 14 October 2010 and did well at the box office, though the producer did not profit from it. Tarang TV broadcast it on 12 November 2017.
At the Odisha State Film Awards, Babushaan Mohanty won Best Actor and Best Singer, Riya Dey won Best Actress and Mihir Das won Best Supporting Actor.
It remakes the Telugu film Aadavari Matalaku Arthale Verule (2007).

Q6796727.lead: Maya Miriga (The Mirage) is a 1984 Odia-language family drama written and directed by Nirad N. Mohapatra, following three generations of a household under one ageing roof.

p: Raj Kishore, a headmaster close to retirement, has staked his family's future on his sons' education, and their hopes rest on the second son, who joins the Indian Administrative Service. His marriage to a well-off city woman unsettles the household: she lives apart from the joint family, and Prabha, the overworked wife of the eldest son, persuades her husband to seek a posting in Cuttack. The youngest son, keener on cricket, does well in his exams and gets his brother to pay for his studies in Delhi, while the shy third son, who manages only a second division, is left behind with a sense of failure.

Mohapatra co-wrote the film with Bibhuti Patnaik. Lotus Film International produced and distributed it. Raj Gopal Mishra was the cinematographer and Bibekanand Satpathy the editor, and Bhaskar Chandavarkar composed the music. Bansidhar Satpathy played Raj Kishore, with Kishori Devi, Sampad Mahapatra, Manaswini Mangaraj, Binod Mishra and Manimala in the cast. It runs 120 minutes.

Critics noted its restraint and naturalistic staging, and the sepia-toned images through which it turns an everyday family story into something quietly melancholic. It played in the Critics' Week section at Cannes in 1984 and at the London, Locarno and Los Angeles film festivals.

The film received the National Film Award for Second Best Feature Film (1984) and the Best Third World Film prize at the Mannheim-Heidelberg International Film Festival. At the 1985 Odisha State Film Awards it won Best Film and Best Director, and it earned a special jury commendation at the Hawaii Film Festival.

Restoration began in November 2020 after the director's son Sandeep Mahapatra approached Shivendra Singh Dungarpur of the Film Heritage Foundation. Twelve reels of the original 16 mm camera negative were found abandoned in a warehouse at Prasad Lab in Chennai, badly deteriorated and with some sections missing images, and a 35 mm print at the NFDC-National Film Archive of India was also used. Scanning was done in Bologna, and footage from both sources was combined and colour-graded over nearly three years of work funded by the foundation. The restored film premiered at Il Cinema Ritrovato in 2024 and was shown in the Restored Classics section of the MAMI Mumbai Film Festival the same year.

Q6787604.lead: Matira Manisha (Man of the Soil) is a 1966 Odia-language drama film directed by Mrinal Sen, adapted from Kalindi Charan Panigrahi's novel of the same name.

p: Before he dies, the farmer Shama Pradhan asks his elder son Baraju to look after his younger brother Chakadi and never divide the family land. Chakadi, an idler, is pushed by his jealous wife Netramani and the scheming moneylender Hari Mishra into demanding a partition. To keep both his promise and the peace, Baraju gives the house and land to Chakadi and leaves with his own family, and Chakadi soon comes to regret the split.

Babulal Doshi produced the film. Panigrahi had agreed to its adaptation on condition that either Satyajit Ray or Mrinal Sen direct it, and Sen was chosen when Ray could not spare the time. Gopal Chhotaray wrote the screenplay and dialogue, Sailaja Chatterjee shot it, Gangadhar Naskar edited it and B. Kalyan handled art direction. Sarat Pujari and Prashanta Nanda played the brothers, with Bhanumati Devi, Sujata Anand and Dukhiram Swain in the main supporting roles.
Bhubaneswar Mishra composed the music. Akshaya Mohanty sang "Rama Bibha Ghare Ho Lakhmana Bara Jaatri" and "Udigale Gendalia Jhadidele Para".

The film moved away from the novel, which was written in 1932: it gave more weight to Chakadi, brought in the Second World War, and replaced the novel's Gandhian outlook with a Marxist one. Panigrahi objected after its release; Sen declined to make changes and asked that his name be removed if any were made, and the film was later re-released in an altered version without his name. It was the first Odia film to be shown at international film festivals.
It won the National Film Award (Silver Lotus) for Best Odia Film at the 1967 awards.

facts: Matira Manisha, novel by Kalindi Charan Panigrahi
Rama Bibha Ghare Ho Lakhmana Bara Jaatri; Udigale Gendalia Jhadidele Para

Q19898516.lead: Super Michhua is a 2015 Odia-language romantic comedy-drama directed by Ashok Pati and produced by Sitaram Agrawal of Sarthak, starring Babushaan Mohanty and Jhilik Bhattacharjee. It is a remake of the 2005 Tamil film Priyasakhi.

p: Romeo, an orphan raised by his uncle Makaradhwaja, a peon, lives by telling lies to borrow money. After his uncle gets him a bank job, he wins over Isha, the daughter of the wealthy Srikant Chhotray, by pretending to be rich, and the two marry in court after he spirits her away from an arranged wedding. When she discovers the truth they quarrel and divorce, but Romeo reforms, and the couple are reunited after he is injured in an accident.

The story is credited to Siddharth, with Ranjit Pattnaik as writer and Ashok Pati writing the screenplay. Sitaram Agrawal and Raj Thorani produced the film. R. Ramesh was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor, while Sudhakar Basant and Ashok Pati choreographed the dances. Unlike the eleven earlier releases from Sarthak, which all had purely Odia titles, this one mixed Odia and English in its name.

Bikash Das composed the music, and Srikant Gautam wrote all five songs. The singers included Nibedita, Saurin Bhatt, Babushaan, R. S. Kumar and Dibya. The tracks are "Kemiti Kahibi Tate", the title song "Super Michhua", "Kut Kut Dhana Lo", "Sunyata Ku Pachare Jebe" and "Tu Mora Mandira".

The film opened on 12 June 2015, during the Raja festival, alongside Gapa Hele bi Sata and Love You Hamesha. It was a box-office success, one of only six of the 28 Odia films released in 2015 to do well commercially, and its songs proved popular.
It is a remake of the Tamil film Priyasakhi (2005).

facts: Kemiti Kahibi Tate; Tu Mora Mandira

Q21468138.lead: Aakhi Palakare Tu is a 2010 Odia-language action drama written and directed by Rabindra Pradhan and produced by Giridhari Mallick, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Babli.

p: After their journalist father and mother are murdered by criminals he exposed, Munna and his little sister Mama are left orphans; Munna grows up to become a powerful gangster who keeps a tight watch over her. In college, Mama falls in love with Rajesh, the son of a retired teacher, after he saves her from kidnappers sent by Munna's rival Bitu. Munna's men then attack Rajesh and bury him, while a tractor driver named Bhagia, who looks exactly like Rajesh, enters the story.

Pradhan wrote the story and screenplay, edited the film and directed it, with dialogue by Pradipta Nanda and cinematography by S. Ranjan. The film marked Babli's first lead role in Odia cinema; she had earlier appeared in Odia music albums and in a small part in the film Keun Duniaru Asila Bandhu. Mukesh Rishi played Munna, and the cast also included Mihir Das, Asrumochan Mohanty, Bijay Mohanty, Harihara Mohapatra, Gloria Mohanty, Minaketan and Papu Pam Pam.
Shantiraj Khosla composed the music.
The film was released on 12 February 2010.

Q21283010.lead: Chanda Na Tame Tara is a 2012 Odia-language romantic action film directed by Ramesh Rout and produced by Chittaranjan Prusty, starring Dipak Barik and Prachi Singh.

p: Badal, the engineer son of a truck driver, has been secretly in love with Chandini, whose father runs a small hotel and is an old friend of Badal's father. The two fathers learn of the romance and happily arrange the marriage. Meanwhile Dadabhai, a local strongman who has bought up 399 of the 400 acres he needs for a project, wants the last acre on which the hotel stands; he gets Badal sent away to a job in Rourkela, kills Chandini's father after forcing him to sign over the land, and abducts Chandini.

Chittaranjan Prusty and Ramesh Rout wrote the story, with Bharadwaj Panda and Rout credited as writers. Ranjan Mishra, Dhrubananda Panda and Rabindra Sethi handled the cinematography, and Sukumar Mani edited the film. Mihir Das and Aparajita Mohanty played Badal's parents, Ajit Das played Chandini's father, Manoj Das played Dadabhai and Pintu Nanda played Gudu, a mute boy raised in Chandini's household.
Prem Anand composed the music.
The film was released on 28 September 2012.

Q388642.lead: Sita Bibaha is a 1936 Odia-language mythological film produced and directed by Mohan Sundar Deb Goswami. Depicting the marriage of Rama and Sita from the Ramayana, it was the first Odia feature film.

p: The sage Vishwamitra asks King Dasharatha for the help of Rama and Lakshmana against the Asuras. The princes go with him to an ashram, where Rama kills Tadaka and drives away Subahu as they try to disrupt a sacrifice, and the brothers are then welcomed at the ashram of the sage Goutam. The story leads to Rama's marriage to Sita.

The film was adapted from a play by Kamapala Mishra, with dialogue by Adwaita Mohanty. Rehearsals began in Puri in early 1935, the company travelled to Calcutta on 29 July that year, and shooting at Kali Studios began on 19 September; production finished on 23 March 1936. It cost ₹29,781 and 10 annas, which Goswami raised by mortgaging his house and borrowing to pay the cast. Makhanlal Banerjee received ₹120 to play Rama, the Lakshmana actor ₹35 for travel, and Prabhavati Devi, who played Sita, the highest fee of ₹150. Goswami himself played Vishwamitra. The black-and-white sound film was certified by the Bengal censor board, with the certificate issued by the police commissioner at Lal Bazaar.

The film had fourteen songs, rooted in Odissi music and sung by the actors themselves, all of them from Odisha. Goswami wrote most of them, with Narasingha Nanda Sharma also contributing; Haricharan Mohanty is credited with the music. The songs include "Ehi Je Ashrama Dekhuchhu Sri Rama", "Debanka Tarane, Danuja Marane", "Apurba Kumari Tripura Sundari", "Kali Dekhithili Madhura Chaliki" and "Kahniki Go Priya Sakhi".

It premiered on 28 April 1936 at Laxmi Talkies in Puri, later ran at Cinema Palace in Cuttack, and drew large crowds through travelling shows such as the Radhakishen Chamelia Touring Cinema. It was a commercial success, and Makhanlal Banerjee as Rama and Narasingha Nanda Sharma as the boatman were singled out for their performances. No silent film had been made in Odisha, so this was also the state's first film of any kind, and the next Odia film did not follow until 1949. All its reels were later destroyed in a fire when the film was taken to Calcutta for screening.

Q29842060.lead: Tulasi Apa is an Odia-language biographical film directed by Amiya Patnaik and produced by Anupam Patnaik, about the educator and social activist Tulasi Munda of Keonjhar. It was the first Odia biopic.

p: The film traces the life of Padma Shri recipient Tulasi Munda, who grew up in a poor tribal area of Odisha and began teaching people around her, an effort that grew into a wide movement. It follows her opposition to injustice, from the exploitation of mine workers to the divide between rich and poor.

Research began in November 2014 with Abha Rani Bal, a primary school teacher in Barbil, who visited Tulasi Munda at her home in Serenda every week to record her story; the script was ready by the end of that year, and Chinmay Das Pattnaik is credited as writer. Barsha Nayak, chosen through auditions while working at an IT company in Hyderabad, played the lead, with Madhusmita as the young Tulasi. After a workshop in Bhubaneswar in January 2015, shooting started in February and was completed in 30 days in and around Keonjhar, Joda and Barbil, including the places where Tulasi Munda spent her childhood. Arjun Jena was the cinematographer and Deben Mishra the editor. The director said the challenge was to dramatise a real life without taking liberties or turning it into a documentary.
Pankaj Jal composed the music to lyrics by Nimai Mohanty, and Eastern Media Entertainment acquired the music rights.

The film premiered at the 21st Kolkata International Film Festival in 2015 and was shown at festivals in Bengaluru, Nashik, Shimla and Haryana, as well as at the 4th Tehran Jasmine International Film Festival, where it was the first Odia film screened. It reached cinemas on 19 May 2017, and in November 2019 it became the first Odia film released worldwide on Amazon Prime Video.

The film won six Odisha State Film Awards for 2015, including Best Music Director, Best Cinematography and Best Singer for Goutam Giri and Antara Chakraborty. It was named best feature film at the 2nd International Film Festival of Shimla, and Barsha Nayak won best actress at the Haryana International Film Festival.

Q6741115.lead: Malajahna (Dead Moon) is a 1965 Odia-language drama film directed by Nitai Palit, adapted from Upendra Kishore Das's novel of the same name. Akshaya Mohanty (Kashyap) and Jharana Das play the leads.

p: Sati, the daughter of a Brahmin family, is loved by her neighbour Nath, but her parents force her to marry Narahari Mishra, a wealthy older landlord who keeps a mistress. Separated from her husband's family during a storm on a pilgrimage to Dhabaleswar, she is sheltered by Nath, and Mishra, doubting her, refuses to take her back. Nath settles her in Cuttack, but gossip about the pair spreads in the village, and Sati ends her life in the river. The story is set against the superstition, caste prejudice, poverty and child marriage of rural Odisha.

Work began in 1962 through the efforts of Akshaya Mohanty and Akshaya Mohanty (Kashyap), supported by friends including Sarat Dev, Sriprasad Kanungo and Arabinda Misra. Money ran out after only a few days of shooting; in 1963 Ban Bihari Dev, the former king of Aali, funded the project again, but it halted for another year once about 60 percent had been shot. Producer-director Dhira Biswal then stepped in and saw it through to release. Palit wrote the screenplay, with Bhim Singh and Gobinda Senapati also credited as writers; Alok Das and Sona Mukherjee shot the film and Ramesh Joshi edited it. It was Jharana Das's first film.

The score was Akshaya Mohanty's first as a film composer. Lyrics came from Kabisurya Baladev Rath, Banamali Das, Binodini Devi and others, and the singers were Akshaya Mohanty, Pranab Patnaik, Nandita Ghosh, Kalyani Bhattacharya and Nirmala Mishra. Among the songs are "Rakata Tala Mala", "Mora Antara Mandire", "Mu Ta Kularu Gali" and "Tuchhaku Mahu".

The film opened on 10 December 1965 at Prabhat Cinema in Cuttack, distributed by Sakha Distributors. The novel it is based on is part of the optional Odia syllabus for Class XI under the Odisha Council of Higher Secondary Education.
It received the certificate of merit for best Odia film at the 1965 National Film Awards.

facts: Malajahna, novel by Upendra Kishore Das
Rakata Tala Mala; Mora Antara Mandire; Tuchhaku Mahu

Q28790010.lead: Smile Please is a 2014 Odia-language family drama directed by S. K. Muralidharan and produced by Rabin Kumar Nanda and Rajesh Padhi, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Archita Sahu.

p: Rudra Pratap Samantaray, a proud and wealthy widower who believes money can buy anything, throws his younger daughter out when she marries her music teacher, and drives away his other children when they take her side. Fourteen years later, lonely and drinking heavily, he is jolted by the bluntness of Mahesh, a cheerful photographer from Balangir working in Bhubaneswar, and asks him to reunite the family for a group photograph. Mahesh tracks down each of the children and wins them back, discovering along the way that Sneha, the young woman he loves, is Rudra Pratap's granddaughter; the old man gives the couple his blessing.
Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue and Dhrubananda Panda was the cinematographer. Mihir Das played Rudra Pratap, with Pushpa Panda, Salil Mitra, Hadu and Madhusmita among the supporting cast.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the five songs, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak and Nizam. The singers included Udit Narayan, Pamela Jain, Vinod Rathod, Pankaj Jal, Kumar Bapi, Sangram Mohanty and Majumdar himself.
The film was released on 14 March 2014.

At the 5th Odia Filmfare awards, held at Utkal Mandap, Nizam won best lyricist for the song "Re Sajani" and Sangram Mohanty won best singer for the same song. Archita Sahu was named best actress at the Tarang Cine Awards.

Q19263536.lead: Bhaunri (also titled Bhaunri – The Sinking Reality) is a 2015 Odia-language art-house film directed by Sudhanshu Mohan Sahoo, with Arindam Roy, Bidita Bag and Mihir Das in the main roles.

p: The title means "whirlpool", a force that pulls under anything that comes near it, and the film uses it to show how marginalised people in Odisha are exploited. Nandu, the son of a bonded tribal labourer, is helped into school by the social worker Dibakar but leaves after a teacher's misconduct, and grows up working as a bonded cowherd. After he marries Janha, the local moneylender Jitu, who controls the area's officials, has their house burnt and Nandu falsely arrested. The couple escape, join a Maoist group led by Dibakar, and Janha is later killed during a raid on a jail; Nandu finally turns away from the gun towards the non-violence of Mahatma Gandhi.

Atish Kumar Rout produced the film under the Ritupriya banner. Ratnakar Rout wrote the story and Dilip Choudhury wrote the screenplay and dialogue; Sanjeev Mohapatra was the cinematographer. The budget was ₹3 crore and the running time is 150 minutes. Bidita Bag, who had earlier acted alongside Arindam Roy in Bengali cinema, made her Odia film debut here.

Abhijeet Majumdar composed the music and Nimai Mohanty wrote the lyrics. The songs include "Raghupati Raghava", "Pahada Parbata Jamure", "Dunguri Pahada Tale", "Alasi Janha Mo Priyare" and "A Siali Bane".
The film opened in Bhubaneswar and Cuttack at the start of January 2015 and ran in theatres across Odisha. It was chosen for the Kala Ghoda Arts Festival in Mumbai, where it had three screenings.

Q20965768.lead: Pilata Bigidigala is a 2015 Odia-language romantic comedy film directed by Basant Sahoo and produced by Pooja Bharalawala, starring Sabyasachi Mishra, Archita Sahu and Papu Pom Pom.

p: Buggi, a carefree young man living with his lawyer father and his brother's family, falls for Nisha at a friend's wedding and wins her by pretending to be an orphan. After they marry, he cannot bring her home and rents a house, only for Nisha to pick his own family home as their rental. To hide the truth, Buggi passes off his friend Twiter as Nisha's husband, and the deception grows when Twiter's own bride Mithi is taken by Buggi's family to be Buggi's wife, until the truth finally comes out and Nisha is asked for forgiveness.

Basant Sahoo directed the film and wrote its screenplay. Biraja Prasanna Kar handled the cinematography and Rajesh Dash the editing, and the film was made by Saurav Entertainments on a budget of about ₹60 lakh.

Prem Anand composed the five-song soundtrack, with lyrics by Nizam and Basantaraj Samal. The singers included Sabyasachi, Bibhu Kishor, Humane Sagar, Sricharan Mohanty, Sohini Mishra, Sasmita Mishra and Sanju; Sabyasachi sang the title song. The songs were released on 6 August 2015.
The film was released on 14 August 2015.
It is a remake of the Punjabi film Carry On Jatta, which itself drew on the Malayalam film Chakkikotha Chankaran.

Q48734586.lead: Khyanikaa: The Lost Idea is a 2017 Odia-language independent feature film written, directed, shot and edited by Amartya Bhattacharyya and produced by Swastik Choudhury.

p: Swastik Choudhury produced the film under his Swastik Arthouse banner and also acted in it. Bhattacharyya handled the writing, direction, cinematography and editing himself, and Kisaloy Roy composed the music. The cast includes Amrita Chowdhury as the Idea, Susant Misra as the Lazy Man, Choudhury Bikash Das as the Mad Man, Hrushikesh Bhoi as Fate and Anu Choudhury as a commercial actress. The film runs 89 minutes.

The film takes a satirical approach, mixing humour about serious realities with elements of magic realism and surrealism. It premiered at the Hidden Gems Film Festival in Canada and went on to festivals including the Dhaka International Film Festival and the Ethiopian International Film Festival. It was the only Odia film selected for the Indian Panorama section of the 48th International Film Festival of India in 2017, and was the only Indian film shown at the Zsigmond Vilmos International Film Festival in Szeged, Hungary.

The Navhind Times named it among the must-watch films of IFFI 2017, and reviewers in UK Film Review and The New Indian Express commented on its colourful visual world and its satirical, stream-of-consciousness storytelling. In June 2020 the film appeared on Amazon Prime Video but was withdrawn from the Indian territory within a few days.
Amartya Bhattacharyya received the Best Editing award at the 29th Odisha State Film Awards for the film, and it won an Honorable Jury Mention at the 5th Noida International Film Festival in 2018.

facts: Best Editing, 29th Odisha State Film Awards

Q7638737.lead: Suna Chadhei Mo Rupa Chadhei is a 2009 Odia-language romantic film directed by Himanshu Parija and starring Anubhav Mohanty and Barsha Priyadarshini, remade from the 2005 Telugu film Nuvvostanante Nenoddantana.

p: Raj, the London-raised son of a wealthy family, falls in love with Rani, a village girl from Odisha brought up by her elder brother Bijay after their father abandoned them. Raj's mother Rajashree rejects the match and insults the siblings, so Bijay sets Raj a test: tend the cattle and harvest more grain than Bijay by the end of the season. Despite schemes by the local landlord's family and by the woman Raj was meant to marry, he wins; when the landlord's son attacks Rani, Raj kills him, Bijay takes the blame and serves five years, and the couple marry on his release with Rajashree's blessing.

Soumya Ranjan Patnaik and Ajit Misra produced the film. Himanshu Parija wrote the screenplay and shared story credit with Prasant Jena and Soumya Ranjan Patnaik, while Chinmay Das Pattnaik wrote the dialogue. S. Ranjan was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor. It was the second film to pair Anubhav Mohanty and Barsha Priyadarshini, after Nei Ja Re Megha Mate.
Malay Mishra composed the music, with lyrics by writers including Nirmal Nayak and Arun Mantri. The singers included Mohammed Aziz, Sricharan, Ira Mohanty, Udit Narayan and Suresh Wadkar.
The film was released on 15 February 2009, distributed by Balunkeshwar Films, and was a commercial success.
It is a remake of the Telugu film Nuvvostanante Nenoddantana (2005).

Q15725179.lead: Luchakali ("Hide and Seek") is a 2012 Odia-language drama thriller written and directed by Susant Mani, starring Babushaan, Shriya Jha and Samaresh Routray. It is a remake of the 1996 Bengali film Bhoy.

p: Tanmay, an orphaned sculptor, loves Monalisa, who looks after him. When her father is blinded in an accident, her stepmother marries her off for money to Kalidas Patnaik, an obsessive poet who mistreats her. Monalisa escapes by jumping from a boat, and Tanmay rescues and hides her; Kalidas tracks them down with the help of Inspector Mohan, and in the final confrontation Tanmay kills Kalidas to save Monalisa.

Nilakantha Das produced the film for Chakadola Production. Susant Mani wrote the story and screenplay, Bapu Goswami wrote the dialogue, and Abhiram Mishra was the cinematographer. Shooting took place in and around Bhubaneswar, Cuttack and Dhenkanal. The supporting cast includes Bijay Mohanty, Ajit Das, Choudhury Bikash Das, Shweta Acharya, Ankita Bhowmick and Megha Ghosh, who appears in an item number.
Anbu Selvam composed the music and Bapu Goswami wrote the lyrics.

The film was released on 30 March 2012 and runs 142 minutes. Critics were generally positive, singling out Samaresh Routray's performance and the film's technical work and special effects, though The New Indian Express found the music slow compared with Mani's earlier film Chocolate. It performed poorly at the box office.

At the 4th Tarang Cine Awards in 2013 it won Best Actor in a Negative Role for Samaresh Routray, Best Actress in a Negative Role for Shweta Acharya and Best Cinematographer for Abhiram Mishra. At the ETV Oriya Film Awards 2013 it was nominated for Best Oriya Film, Best Director and Best Actor in a Negative Role.

facts: Luchakali – Catch Me If You Can

Q37946873.lead: Raghupati Raghav Rajaram is a 2015 Odia-language drama film directed by Sudhanshu Mohan Sahoo and produced by Sitaram Agarwal under the Sarthak banner, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra and Riya Dey.

p: Raghupati, a young man with a slight stammer who once spent time in a mental health facility after severe exam anxiety, runs a wedding-card business set up with his mother's help. His honesty about his past leads to repeated rejections from prospective brides, and one, Vidya, runs away on their wedding day. A chance meeting with Raghav Anand, a blind radio jockey who tells him how he won his wife, changes Raghupati's outlook, and after a series of encounters he and Ranjita, the first woman who turned him down, admit their feelings and marry.

It was the fourteenth film from Sarthak. Sahoo wrote the screenplay and Srikant Gautam the dialogue, and Rajesh Dash edited the film. Three newcomers, Debasmita Panda, Tapaswini Mishra and Monisha Samantaray, made their debuts after being chosen through the Sarthak Music talent show Mu Bi Heroine Hebi. Mihir Das, Pupinder Singh, Debashish Patra, Anita Das and Trupti Sinha also appear.
Bikash Das composed the music and Srikant Gautam wrote the lyrics; Namita Agrawal and Sourin Bhatt were among the singers.
The film was released on 28 August 2015.

Q6123392.lead: Jai Jagannatha is a 2007 multilingual socio-mythological film directed by Sabyasachi Mohapatra, made in Odia and Hindi and released in dubbed versions in thirteen further languages.

p: Drawn from the Laxmi Purana, the story is set in an age when untouchables were barred from worship. Sriya, a woman of low caste, worships Goddess Lakshmi and wins her favour, and because Lakshmi encourages such worship, Lord Jagannath sends her away at the urging of his elder brother Balabhadra. Without her the brothers go hungry and suffer for twelve years, and Lakshmi agrees to return only if caste discrimination ends on earth; at the close, Narada reveals that Jagannath had arranged these events to carry that message.

Sabyasachi Mohapatra wrote the screenplay, and the film was shot in Puri and at Umargaon. Sritam Das played Jagannath, Jyoti Mishra played Lakshmi, Pintu Nanda played Balabhadra and Mohini Shilalipi played Sriya, with Sadhu Meher, Sarat Pujari and Ratan Meher in supporting roles. The budget was ₹28 crore.

Akshaya Mohanty composed the six songs and wrote lyrics alongside Binodini Devi and Abhilash. The playback singers included Lopita Mishra, Bibhu Kishor, Sailabhama, Pritinanda, Vinod Rathod and Anuradha Paudwal.

The film was released on 13 July 2007, at the time of Rath Yatra, and was distributed by Adlabs. Besides the Odia and Hindi originals, dubbed versions appeared in English, Bengali, Assamese, Chhattisgarhi, Bhojpuri, Rajasthani, Punjabi, Gujarati, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam and Nepali.
It received Odisha State Film Awards for special jury and best editing.

Q115551490.lead: Pratikshya is a 2022 Odia-language drama film produced and directed by Anupam Patnaik, based on Gourahari Das's short story "Bapa". It won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia.

p: In a middle-class household in Bhubaneswar, the unemployed graduate Sanjay will settle for nothing less than a government job, even as his father Bipin, close to retirement, urges him to take any work. The family is still repaying loans from his elder sister Supriya's wedding when Bipin is found to have a terminal illness, leaving Sanjay torn between his ambition and the need to save his father.

Roshan Bisoi wrote the screenplay and dialogue and also appears as Bijit. Dipanwit Dashmohapatra plays Sanjay, Choudhury Jayaprakash Das his father, Barsha Patnaik plays Kalyani and Sreela Tripathy Sanjay's mother, with Siddhanta Mahapatra in a guest role as a doctor. Deepak Kumar was the cinematographer and Deven Mishra the editor; the film runs 137 minutes.

The music was composed by Ankesh Anand, Ashish Pradhan and Bivash Rath, with lyrics by writers including Durga Madhab Panda and Priyaranjan Sahu. Ashish Pradhan, Bivash Rath and Biswajit Mahapatra were among the singers.

The film was screened in the Indian Panorama section of the International Film Festival of India in Goa in 2022 and opened in cinemas on 2 December 2022. Reviewers for Kalinga TV and Orissa Post praised it, the latter noting an uneven pace between its two halves but commending its subtlety. At an IFFI press conference, Anupam Kher announced that he would produce and act in a Hindi remake.
It won the 69th National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia and the Best Story Feature Film award at the Washington DC South Asia Film Festival in 2022.

facts: National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia

Q6124327.lead: Jajabara is a 1975 Odia-language film directed jointly by Bijay Mishra, Akshaya Mohanty and Hemanta Das under the shared name Trimurty, starring Sriram Panda, Banaja Mohanty and Tripura Mishra. A colourised version was later released as Rangin Jajabara.

p: The landlord Rashbihari Samantrai has promised to give Sundari Tota, land he owns where villagers have lived for generations, to his religious guru for an ashram, while his elder son Anu wants it for a factory. The villagers, led by Jhili's father, resist being evicted. Rashbihari's younger son Arup, who loves Jhili, eventually persuades his father to keep the land, and the two marry.

Bijay Pattnaik produced the film for Trimurty Films. The three directors kept their own names off the direction credit: Bijay Mishra also wrote the story and screenplay, Akshaya Mohanty composed the music, and Hemanta Das played the role of Nilakantha. Srinivas Mohapatra was the cinematographer and Madan Gupte the editor. Actress Anita Das began her Odia film career with this film.
Akshaya Mohanty scored the film. Its songs include "Jajabara Mana Mora Niti Gadhe" and "Hai Se Harini Akhi", and Geeta Patnaik sang "Phura Kina Udigala Bani".

The black-and-white film was later digitally colourised by Bapu Lenka with digital painting director Tilak Ray and a team of 18 roto artists. Twenty-one technicians worked for 736 days to colour about 219,000 frames, making it the first black-and-white regional film in India to be colourised and the first Odia film to be re-released in colour.
Banaja Mohanty won the Best Actress award at the 1975 Orissa State Film Awards.

facts: Trimurty (Bijay Mishra, Akshaya Mohanty, Hemanta Das)
"Jajabara Mana Mora Niti Gadhe", "Hai Se Harini Akhi"

Q111942188.lead: Adieu Godard is an independent Odia-language drama film written and directed by Amartya Bhattacharyya. After a 2021 festival premiere in Moscow, it reached Indian cinemas on 2 September 2022.

p: The film is set in a village in rural India. An old man who usually watches pornographic films with his friends ends up, by accident, with a Jean-Luc Godard film; captivated by the French director, he decides to stage a Godard festival in the village.

Swastik Choudhury produced the film under his Odisha banner Swastik Arthouse, partnering with FilmStop Entertainment of Kolkata and the French company Les Films de la Haute-Vallée. Besides writing and directing, Bhattacharyya handled the camera and the edit; Kisaloy Roy wrote the score. The cast is led by Choudhury Bikash Das as Ananda, with Sudhasri Madhusmita, Dipanwit Dashmohapatra, Swastik Choudhury and Choudhury Jayaprakash Das in other main roles.

Its world premiere came at the 43rd Moscow International Film Festival, where it was named among ten films to watch, and Indian festival selections followed in Kerala, Kolkata, Bengaluru and Pune. Anu Choudhury presented the theatrical release, handled by Platoon Distribution; the film played for four weeks in Odisha and was also shown in Kolkata, New Delhi and Bangalore, with special screenings in Jaipur and Mumbai. In the United States and Canada, Film Movement released it digitally.
Anurag Kashyap and Taran Adarsh praised it. Writing for The New York Times, Devika Girish was critical, finding that it wasted a strong premise on regressive stereotypes.

In 2022 it took the Best Film award in the Indian Languages competition of the 27th Kolkata International Film Festival, and the Third Best Indian Cinema award at the 13th Bengaluru International Film Festival.

facts: Swastik Arthouse, FilmStop Entertainment, Les Films de la Haute-Vallée

Q15725050.lead: Mo Duniya Tu Hi Tu is a 2013 Odia-language drama film directed by Sudhakar Basant and produced by Soumya Ranjan Patnaik, starring Anubhav Mohanty and Barsha Priyadarshini. It is a remake of the Tamil film Unnidathil Ennai Koduthen.

p: Heera, a small-time thief, hides from the police in a house where Payal, who works there as a maid, locks him in the kitchen for a week, and the time with her changes him. Through her diary he learns she is the unacknowledged daughter of the household's lawyer and hopes to marry a relative, Akash, so he hides his own feelings. When Payal is thrown out, Heera supports her and builds her career as a singer; later accused of theft and sent away, he leaves behind his own diary, which reveals his love, and Payal chooses to marry him.

The film was made by Manjari Movies. The story came from the Tamil original by Vikraman, and Basantaraj Samal wrote the dialogue. Siddhanta Mahapatra, Salil Mitra and Pratibha Panda appear in supporting roles.

Malay Mishra composed the music, with lyrics by Basantaraj Samal and Arun Mantri. Bappi Lahiri, Javed Ali, Ira Mohanty, Roop Kumar Rathod and Debashish sang the songs, which include "Tu Daki Delu", "Sathi Tora Sundara", "Mo Duniya Tu Hi Tu", "Kanhei Re" and "To Sathe Jebethu".

The film was released on 11 January 2013. Reviews were generally positive: IncredibleOdisha rated it 4 out of 5, praising Salil Mitra's comedy and the leads' performances, and FullOrissa gave it 4.3 out of 5. It did well at the box office and became one of the highest-grossing Odia films.
At the Filmfare Awards East it received nominations for Best Oriya Film, Best Director, Best Actor for Anubhav Mohanty and Best Actress for Barsha Priyadarshini.
It is a remake of the Tamil film Unnidathil Ennai Koduthen.

facts: "Mo Duniya Tu Hi Tu", "Tu Daki Delu", "Kanhei Re"

Q6026858.lead: Indradhanura Chhai (Shadows of the Rainbow) is a 1993 Odia-language film written and directed by Susant Misra about three women of different generations in a changing Bhubaneswar. It won the Grand Prix at the Sochi International Film Festival.

p: Set in Bhubaneswar as urban growth reshapes family and social life, the film follows three women. Vijaya, widowed days after her wedding, struggles with her feelings for a kind local teacher; her friend Sonia is torn between modern life and traditional ideas of female virtue; and their Aunt Nila finds it hard to accept growing old. Their lonely moments are set against questions of tradition, religion, culture and relations between men and women.

Jugala Debata produced the film with the Orissa Film Development Corporation and was also its cinematographer. Misra wrote the story and screenplay and Devdas Chhotray the dialogue; Chakradhar Sahu edited, Asim Basu was art director and Himanshu Shekhar Khatur handled sound. The cast includes Robin Das, Bijayini Mishra, Sonia Mohapatra, Surya Mohanty, Deba Das and Muktabala Rautray. The film runs 110 minutes.
The music was arranged by Vikash Das.

The film received the Grand Prix for Best Feature Film at the Sochi International Film Festival in Russia and a Special Jury Award at the 1994 National Film Awards. In 1995 it was an official selection in the Un Certain Regard section at Cannes. At the 1994 Orissa State Film Awards it won Best Direction, Best Dialogues and Screenplay, Best Supporting Actress and a Special Jury Award. It was also shown at festivals in Cairo, Rotterdam, Moscow and Montreal, at the Institut Lumière in Paris, and as the closing film of the Indomania "100 Years of Indian Cinema" celebration in Paris.

facts: Grand Prix, Sochi International Film Festival; Special Jury Award, National Film Awards (1994)

Q64768042.lead: Prem Kumar: Salesman of the Year is a 2018 Odia-language action film directed by Tapas Sargharia for Tarang Cine Productions, starring Anubhav Mohanty, Tamanna Vyas and Sivani Sangita.

p: Prem Kumar appears to be a star insurance agent but is in fact an undercover RAW officer. Learning that someone named Saroj plans to assassinate the defence minister in Bhubaneswar, he investigates three people of that name while lodging at the house of Simran, with whom he falls in love. The suspects prove innocent, the minister's secretary turns out to be the mastermind, and Prem rescues Simran and stops the attack before setting off after the conspirator behind the secretary.

Sanjay Mahakul and Sakti Baral wrote the story, and Tapas Sargharia and Debidutta Mohanty wrote the screenplay; Rajesh Dash edited the film. Shooting was delayed after Anubhav Mohanty was injured on set, and the songs were filmed in Kashmir. The story was initially thought to draw on Rocket Singh; at the audio launch Mohanty said the film was neither a remake nor inspired by another film, though its plot resembles the 2016 Punjabi film Ambarsariya.
Prem Anand composed the music, with lyrics by Basantraj Samal, Subrat Swain and Debidutta Mohanty.
Planned for release at the Raja festival, the film instead opened in theatres across Odisha on 16 October 2018, during Durga Puja.

Q35993155.lead: Hello: In Love is a 2015 Odia-language romantic film written and directed by Susant Mani, introducing newcomers Sudhanshu Narayan Dash and Sushree Rath in the lead roles.

p: Subrata Chatterjee, a flautist from Kolkata with an Odia mother and a Bengali father, comes to Puri to play at a hotel. Swapna, a college student whose brother Sitanshu has arranged her marriage to a man living in America, loves the flute music without knowing who plays it. Subrata befriends the family and falls for Swapna, but her brother takes away her phone and brings the wedding forward when he learns of their relationship; in the end, by which time Subrata has become a celebrated musician, the marriage arranged is with him, and his parents attend the wedding.

Niranjan Nayak and Purnachandra Nayak produced the film under the Nayak Film Entertainment banner. Susant Mani wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue; Sitanshu Mahapatra was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor. Hara Rath, Priyanka Mahapatra, Aparajita Mohanty, Prithviraj and Samaresh Routray appear in supporting roles, with Sudarshan Pattnaik and Ileana Citaristi in guest appearances.
Biswaswarup Mahapatra composed the music and Debidutta Mohanty wrote the lyrics. The singers included Ira Mohanty, Jasaswini Nayak, Sarthak Kumar, Asima Panda, Sashank and Biswaswarup.
The film was released on 25 December 2015.

Q16250269.lead: Kaunri Kanya ("Possessed Girl") is a 2013 Odia-language horror film directed by first-time director Soumya Ranjan Sahu. It was the first Odia film made in 3D.

p: Akash, a doctor, is posted to a village, where after a string of strange events his wife Riya becomes possessed by a spirit. With the help of the psychiatrist Dr. Rajiv, he uncovers the story of Ravi and Anusuya, two villagers who loved each other until the villagers killed Anusuya on suspicion of witchcraft. The film deals with superstition and the killing of innocent people branded as practitioners of black magic.

Ramya Ranjan Sahu produced the film for Angel Bee Medias and wrote the story with Jayendra Kumar Sahu; Soumya Ranjan Sahu wrote the screenplay and dialogue, edited the film and played a lead role alongside Ardhendu Sahu, with Kavya Keeran and Pupul Bhuyan as the heroines. Many of the actors were newcomers, and Prakruti Mishra made a guest appearance. Most of the filming took place in Surangi in Ganjam district, and an underwater sequence shot in Vizag was the first in an Odia film. Tusharkanta Sahu was the cinematographer. Work on Mita Basichi Mun Bhuta Sathire had begun earlier as a 3D film, but Kaunri Kanya reached cinemas first.
The South Indian composers Satya Kashyap and Mithun provided the songs and background score. The soundtrack includes "Soniya Soniya", "Rangabati", "Priya Re" and "Dara Lage".
The film was released in 2013 and was also dubbed into Tamil, the first Odia film to be dubbed into that language.

Q4854478.lead: Bande Utkala Janani ("Salute to Mother Utkala") is a 2008 Odia-language film written and directed by Suvendu Swain about three police officers and a journalist fighting political corruption.

p: A woman journalist drives the plot: her courage and willingness to take risks bring a hidden secret to light. Working from a police station that functions like a family, she and three honest officers join forces to root out political corruption and hooliganism, with themes of patriotism and integrity at work.

Debasish Dogra and Pragati Mohanty produced the film. Suvendu Swain wrote the story and screenplay and Hara Barik the dialogue; Abhiram Mishra was the cinematographer and Susanta Mani the editor. The cast is led by Siddhanta Mahapatra, Sabyasachi Mishra, Hara Rath and Arpita Mukherjee, with Minaketan Das as the main villain. The budget was about ₹1.5 crore.

Sarat Nayak composed the songs, with lyrics by Bapu Goswami, Panchanan Nayak and Bijay Malla and arrangements by Nityashri Ranjan; all the songs were produced with keyboard sequencing to appeal to younger audiences. Singers included Arabinda, Kumar Bapi, Mita Mahakud, Tapu Mishra and Pami. Composer Abhijit Majumdar also sang a song, becoming the first composer since Akshaya Mohanty to sing in a film for another music director.

Lotus Films released the film on 2 October 2008; it was the first Odia film distributed by satellite using the UFO digital system, and it grossed about ₹2.5 crore. Reviews were negative, criticising its revealing scenes and weak songs, though Minaketan's performance as a coarse-spoken corrupt politician was singled out for praise.

Q134966565.lead: Bou Buttu Bhuta is a 2025 Odia-language horror comedy thriller directed by Jagdish Mishra and produced by Trupti Satapathy under Babushaan Films, starring Babushaan Mohanty, Archita Sahu and Aparajita Mohanty.

p: Buttu, a struggling fish farmer, lives in a village with his mother Ratnamala, a sorceress, and wants to leave in search of work but cannot afford to. Rinki, the daughter of the village doctor, is in love with him. Walking home one night, Buttu is possessed by the ghost of Amari, a villager killed by the community, setting off a series of eerie events involving Rinki and Ratnamala; the ending is left open, suggesting a sequel.

Mohammad Imran wrote the story and screenplay and Pranab Prasanna Rath the dialogue. Rudrakanta Singh was the cinematographer and Rashmi Ranjan Dash the editor. The supporting cast includes Jagannath Seth as Amari, Choudhury Jayaprakash Das as Rinki's father, Mangu Kumar Sahoo, Krishna Kar, Rabi Mishra, Angulia Bunty, Udit Guru and Robin Das. The film runs 176 minutes.
Gaurav Anand composed the songs and Abhishek Panigrahi the background score. Cookies Swain appears in the item song "Dungu Thili".

Prakash Films released the film at midnight on 12 June 2025, during Raja Parba, in 61 theatres across Odisha. It collected about ₹40 lakh on its first day and around ₹6–7 crore in its first week, and is reported to have reached ₹20 crore in 50 days, becoming the highest-grossing Odia film.

Q15725198.lead: Sala Budha is a 2012 black-and-white feature film in the Kosli language directed by Sabyasachi Mohapatra. It won seven Odisha State Film Awards, including Best Film and Best Director.

p: In the mid-1930s, when Indian villages were governed by local kings who paid tax to the British, Bhagatram Gauntia heads a poor village in Odisha. Kind and honest, and nicknamed Sala Budha ("the stupid old man") by the villagers, he cannot bring himself to collect taxes during five years of drought, leaving his own land and position at risk. Rivals in the village turn the king against him, but when the king comes to strip him of his land and office, he learns the truth and praises him instead.

The film was largely a family project: the story was written by the director's father, Kapileswar Prasad Mohapatra, and the director's brothers Aum Prakash Mohapatra and Rajendra Mohapatra handled the cinematography and editing, while his son Chodaganga Mohapatra was co-director. The lead role went to the 83-year-old theatre artist Atal Bihari Panda, and many newcomers were cast alongside Ratan Meher and Prithviraj Nayak. The film runs 90 minutes.
The music was composed by Pankaj Jaal and Ghasiram Mishra.
Sala Budha was selected for the Indian Panorama section of the 44th International Film Festival of India in 2013 and was also shown at the Kolkata International Film Festival.
Besides its seven Odisha State Film Awards, the film received an honour at the 2013 Jakarta International Film Festival for Spirituality, Religion and Visionary.

Q15724784.lead: Babu I Love You is a 2005 Odia-language romantic drama film directed by Sanjay Nayak, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra, Anu Choudhury, Chandan Kar and Archita Sahu. It is a remake of the 1985 Hindi film Teri Meherbaniyan.

p: The village strongman Raghupati kills the local zamindar, takes over his mansion and keeps his daughter Arati in fear, along with Jagu, who was handed over as a bonded servant to settle his father's debt; Arati and Jagu fall in love. Forest officer Akash arrives, falls for Bijuli and becomes the voice of the villagers against Raghupati and his associates Raghab and Rajaram. While Akash is away, Bijuli shuts up the dog he left to protect her and dies resisting an assault by the trio; they later murder Akash and frame Jagu, but Akash's loyal dog uncovers the evidence that brings them to justice, and Jagu and Arati marry.

Soumya Ranjan Patnaik wrote the story, and Malay Mishra and Sanjay Nayak wrote the screenplay and dialogue. The cinematography was by S. Ranjan and Samba Shiva Rao, and the film was made and distributed by Balunkeswar Films. Bijay Mohanty, Raimohan Parida, Jairam Samal and Biju Badajena appear in supporting roles. The film runs 172 minutes.
Manmath Mishra composed the music and wrote the lyrics with Sanjay Nayak. Mohammed Aziz, Kumar Bapi, Bibhu Kishor and Ira Mohanty were among the singers.
The film was released in May 2005.
At the 2006 Orissa State Film Awards, Archita Sahu won Best Supporting Actress and Amiya Maharana won Best Art Director.
It is a remake of the Hindi film Teri Meherbaniyan (1985).

Q136496952.lead: Charidham – A Journey Within is a 2025 Odia-language family drama film directed by Tapas Sargharia and produced by Himadri Tanaya Das under Camera Queen Production, starring Anubhav Mohanty and Anuradha Panigrahi.

p: Abhi, a devoted son, sets out to fulfil his parents' lifelong wish to visit the four Char Dham shrines of Puri, Rameswaram, Dwarka and Badrinath. Along the way he takes on hardships, responsibilities and physical challenges to honour their faith.

Akhil Mohan Rautray wrote the story, Suresh Pattnaik the screenplay and Kumarshree Sahu the dialogue; Smruti Ranjan Mishra edited the film. It was shot at the four shrines: the Jagannath Temple in Puri, the Ramanathaswamy Temple in Rameswaram, the Dwarkadhish Temple and the Badrinath Temple. Sukanta Rath, Ashok Das and Mamata Tripathy play Abhi's brother, father and mother, with Pradyumna Lenka, Ashish Kumar Das, Sujit Paikaray and Shakti Baral in other roles. The film runs 150 minutes.

Somesh Satpathy and Baidyanath Dash composed the songs and Abhishek Panigrahi the background score. Lyrics were by Arun Mantri, Ranjan Nayak, J. P. Wordsmith and Biraj Rath, and the singers included Krishna Beura, Humane Sagar, Pamela Jain, Satyajit Jena, Ananya Sritam Nanda and Gaurav Anand. Sivani Sangita appears in the special song "KerKera".
The film was released in cinemas on 25 September 2025, during Dussehra, with Rajshri Productions as distributor.

Q17069453.lead: Nirbachana ("Election") is a 1994 Odia-language drama film written, directed and edited by Biplab Ray Chaudhuri about vote-buying and greed in a poor Odisha village.

p: In a poor village in Orissa, people can either farm for the wealthy zamindar or work in his quarries, where the pay is better but the rock dust ruins the land and their health. When the zamindar pays villagers for their votes in the election of a new village chief, a chief who needs a dowry for his daughter adopts the village beggar, who is dying of tuberculosis, and promises to have him cured in exchange for his vote money. The chief and his son take the beggar on a long journey for treatment, struggling to keep him alive until polling day, and the story ends in tragedy.

The film was made with financial support from the National Film Development Corporation and Doordarshan. Ray Chaudhuri wrote the story with Prafulla Roy, and Raju Mishra was the cinematographer. Nikhil Baran Sengupta, who also acted in the film, was the art director, and Nagen Barik handled sound. The cast includes Bhima Singh, Durlav Singh, Choudhury Bikash Das, Chandra Singh, Bidyut Prava Patnaik and Sangita Dutta. The film runs 100 minutes.
The music was arranged by Shantanu Mahapatra.

Nirbachana was selected for the Indian Panorama of the 1996 International Film Festival of India in Delhi. Reviewing it there, S. R. Ashok Kumar of The Hindu said the film told its story of destructive greed neatly.

Q50825299.lead: Romeo: The Lover Boy is a 2009 Odia-language film written and directed by Hara Pattanaik and produced by Sanjay Nayak. It marked the screen debuts of Babushaan and Lovely.

p: Hara Pattanaik wrote the story and screenplay and Ranjit Pattnaik the dialogue. Niranjan Das was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor. Babushaan and Lovely played the lead roles, supported by Uttam Mohanty, Aparajita Mohanty, Arindam Roy, Pritiraj Satpathy, Bijay Mohanty, Mala Bose and Bibhuti Sahu, with Pattanaik himself also in the cast.
Swarup Nayak composed the music and wrote the songs. Babushaan sang in the film alongside Sujit Bhoi, Tapu Mishra and Debashish Mahapatra.
The film was released on 12 June 2009.

Q23044938.lead: Krantidhara is a 2016 Odia-language film directed by Himanshu Khatua, based on a story by Iti Samanta, who also produced it. It stars Gargi Mohanty, Samaresh Routray and Debasis Patra.

p: The film centres on a village woman and her struggle. Its themes are women's empowerment, the place of women in politics and society, and a husband's domination over his wife, following the hardships a woman endures after sacrificing everything for her husband while trying to stand on the side of what is right.

The story is taken from Iti Samanta's work Jhada Pare Surya. Gargi Mohanty, who had acted in serials on Tarang TV, was given the lead role of Pratigyan. Samaresh Routray, often cast as a villain, played a positive character, Abhay, while Debasis Patra took the antagonist's role as Babu Swain. The dialogue was recorded live on set with sync sound rather than dubbed afterwards. Bikash Das composed the music.
Krantidhara opened on 19 February 2016 in around 14 cinemas across Odisha. It was selected for the 12th Chennai International Film Festival and the 7th Bangalore International Film Festival.

At the Odisha State Film Awards (the 26th edition, for the year 2014) the film was named Best Film. Gargi Mohanty won Best Actress, and Iti Samanta received the Best Story prize, the Mohan Sundar Dev Goswami award.

facts: Jhada Pare Surya by Iti Samanta

Q4918638.lead: Biswaprakash, also known as The Young Rebel, is a 1999 Odia-language film written and directed by Susant Misra, starring Sanjeev Samal and Nandita Das. It won the National Film Award for Best Oriya Film.

p: Biswaprakash, a man in his early twenties, rebels against his family's rigid, tradition-bound way of life and feels out of place in a fast-changing consumer society. Anjali, an independent young woman who looks after her paralysed mother and plans to turn her large house into a holiday home, becomes his friend until a policeman breaks up the relationship. Despairing, Biswa turns to religious rituals; he later befriends June, a traveller from abroad, but she too leaves, and he is left alone with no way out.

The film was produced and distributed by the National Film Development Corporation of India. Misra also edited it, with Jugal Debata as cinematographer; the Odia credits name Debdas Chhotray for the screenplay. It was shot in Puri, where the crew used an old palatial building in the centre of the town owned by Kaviraj Purna Chandra Rath.
The music is credited to Bikash (Vikash) Das, although one account names Jugal Debata as having arranged it.

The film was shown at the Shanghai and Cairo international film festivals in 1999, at Singapore, and in the Indian Panorama section of the International Film Festival of India in 2000. At the Rotterdam Film Festival in 2001 it won a Critics Choice award.
Biswaprakash received the Silver Lotus for Best Oriya Film at the National Film Awards in 2000.

Q15725087.lead: Raja Jhia Sange Heigala Bhaba is a 2012 Odia-language romantic drama film directed by Sudhanshu Sahu and produced by Sitaram Agrawal, starring Arindam Roy, Archita Sahu and Mihir Das.

p: Balia, raised by his widowed mother Janaki in a slum, is enormously strong but naive, and to please her he forces his way into college. There he meets Kandhei, daughter of the powerful Pratap Choudhury, who falls for him and helps him change from a street tough into a gentleman. Her family has Balia jailed and arranges her marriage; he escapes, only to find that Kandhei has taken her own life, and he spends the rest of his days with her memory.
The film was made by Sarthak Films on a budget of ₹30 lakh from a story by Sidharth Agrawal. Mahasweta Roy played the hero's mother and Mihir Das the heroine's father.
Prem Anand composed the score and Srikanta Gautam wrote the lyrics. The soundtrack was launched at Red FM 93.5 in Bhubaneswar on 28 May 2012.

It opened on 10 June 2012 during the Raja festival, alongside Rangeela Toka and Love Master, and grossed ₹2 crore. Critics gave it a mixed response; Incredible Orissa praised its colourful picturisation but found the storyline familiar.
At the 4th ETV Oriya Film Awards in 2013 Arindam Roy won Best Actor and Sudhanshu Sahu Best Director. At the 4th Tarang Cine Awards, Mahasweta Roy and Kirti Mohanty received nominations.

Q15725220.lead: Shesha Shrabana is a 1976 Odia-language drama film directed by Prashant Nanda, adapted from Basant Mahapatra's novel of the same name. Nanda also stars alongside Mahasweta Roy, Banaja Mohanty and Hemant Das.

p: Sania, a village fisherman who lives with his sick mother and his friend Makara, rescues a girl named Manika from the river. When they take her home, her family refuses her because she has stayed among lower-caste people, so Sania shelters her. Manika falls in love with him, but he holds back because of her higher caste and arranges a match with a doctor who has come to treat plague in the village; the doctor leaves to seek his family's consent and never returns. Unable to bear the villagers' gossip, Manika disappears, and Sania loses his mind.

The film was made under the Shri Jagannath Films banner and produced by Nagen Roy, with a screenplay by Shibabrata Das and cinematography by Rajan Kinegi. It marked Prashant Nanda's start as a director. Mahasweta Roy, who had earlier played a small part in Sindura Bindu, made her debut as a lead actress in it.
Prafulla Kar composed the music.

Shesha Shrabana was released on 14 September 1976. It set a box-office record, ran for several weeks and was well received by reviewers. It was included in the Indian Panorama of the 9th International Film Festival of India in New Delhi in 1977.

The film won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia at the 24th National Film Awards. At the Orissa State Film Awards for 1976 it was named best feature film, with further prizes for Prashant Nanda as director, Basant Mahapatra for the story and Prafulla Kar for music.
Prashant Nanda directed a Hindi remake, Naiyya, produced by Rajshri in 1979.

Q137570236.lead: Bindusagar is an Odia-language musical romantic drama film directed by Abhishek Swain and starring Prakruti Mishra and Dipanwit Dashmohapatra. It premiered in 2025 and reached cinemas in April 2026.

p: Sreeja, 22, travels from London to Bhubaneswar carrying a puzzling letter left by her late mother and sets out to trace her roots. Her search crosses paths with a grieving father's journey towards faith in the old city, with the sacred Bindusagar lake at the centre of a story about love, loss, healing, belonging and tradition.

Abhishek Das wrote the story, with Pranab Prasanna Rath contributing to the screenplay and dialogue. The film was produced by Shiladitya Bora of Platoon One Films together with Vinay Reddy and Shubho Shekhar Bhattacharjee of Boundless Blackbuck Films. Shooting took place in Odisha and London, with Deepak Kumar as cinematographer.

Kisaloy Roy, Mahadev Rout and Ashish Pradhan composed the eight original songs, which draw on Odia culture. Singers included Kuldeep Pattanaik, Aseema Panda, Smrutika Padhi, Nihar Bagudai and Human Sagar. Among the songs is "Bhola Shankar", composed by Mahadev Rout with lyrics by Ranjan Nayak. Tarang Music released the soundtrack.

The film premiered as a Gala Presentation at the 56th International Film Festival of India in Goa in November 2025. Its theatrical release, distributed by Prakash Films, came on 17 April 2026, after an earlier plan to open on 10 April around the Odia New Year.

Q51885955.lead: Hello Arsi is an Odia-language romantic drama film written and directed by Sambit Mohanty and produced by Ajaya Routray, starring Prakruti Mishra and Partha Sarathi Ray. It won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia.

p: The film follows Arsi, a young woman from Rourkela who turns to sex work to survive. Told entirely inside a car, where it opens and closes, it pairs her with an unnamed taxi driver and deals with displacement, the grief over compensation that follows it, social alienation and industrialisation, giving more weight to ideas than to character.

Originally titled Pakhilagna, the 90-minute film was shot in Rourkela around November 2016. Sambit Mohanty died during the making of the film, and technicians from the Film and Television Institute of India helped finish it, as Partha Sarathi Ray later recounted in an interview. Mitrabhanu Mohanty composed the songs and sound designer Subash Sahu the background score.

Critics praised the story, the screenplay and Prakruti Mishra's performance. Chief Minister Naveen Patnaik, filmmaker Shekhar Kapur and actor Bijay Mohanty spoke well of it; after the award, Kapur remarked that he would fail if he attempted a film like it. The film is regarded as a significant one in the careers of both lead actors.

At the 65th National Film Awards in 2018, the film was named Best Feature Film in Odia, Sambit Mohanty received a posthumous Rajat Kamal for its dialogue, and Prakruti Mishra received a Special Mention. It was the first Odia film to receive a national award for dialogue.

Q116689371.lead: Phalguna Chaitra is an Odia-language family drama from 2023, co-directed by Sisir Kumar Sahu and Peenakee Singh. Partha Sarathi Ray, BM Baisali and Ananya Mishra head the cast.

p: The producers were Sakti Jagdev and Babushaan Mohanty, working through their companies Aadya Jagdev Films and Babushaan Films. The story is by Sulagna Mohanty; Pranab Prasanna Rath turned it into a screenplay, wrote the dialogue and took a role on screen. Supporting parts went to Choudhury Jayaprakash Das, Sukanta Rath and Bhaswati Basu. Rudrakant Singh was the cinematographer and Rashmi Ranjan Dash the editor.

Music came from the trio Abhishek, Eshan and Kaushik, and the lyricists were J.P. Wordsmith, Sthita Pattnaik and Sumit Panda. The playback singers were Gaurav Anand, Ananya Sritam Nanda, Kuldeep Pattanaik, Suril Bispute and Aishwarya Kumar.
Theatrical release came on 12 May 2023.

The 35th Odisha State Film Awards, covering 2023 and presented in 2026, gave the film three prizes: Choudhury Jayaprakash Das was named Best Supporting Actor, Pranab Prasanna Rath won for Best Screenplay, and Wasidia Tabassum was Best Costume Designer.

Q5614495.lead: Gud Boy is a 2012 Odia-language film directed by Jyotee Dass and starring Arindam Roy, Priya Choudhury, Ipsita Mohanty and Mihir Das. It is a remake of the 2008 Tamil film Pazhani.

p: Raja, who killed a man at the age of ten, is released at 25 after fifteen years in prison and sets his heart on working in a particular mansion. He wins over its owner, the wealthy Mihir Samantray, and his wife Tulasi, and becomes their driver; he comes to see Tulasi as a mother figure, and a photograph reveals that she looks exactly like his dead mother. The film sets Raja's crime against Samantray's respectable standing, which turns out to rest on criminal methods, while questions about Raja's own past unfold.

Hrudananda Samal and Tuna Babu produced the film. In the Odia credits, Rina Samal is named for the story, Rajani Ranjan for the dialogue and Jyotee Dass for the screenplay; the original Tamil story is by Perarasu.
Baidyanath Dash composed the music, with lyrics by Mohit Chakraborty, Arun Mantri and Nirmal Nayak. The playback singers included Javed Ali, Pamela Jain, Vinod Rathod, Shaan, Suman and Suresh Wadkar.
The film was released on 10 May 2012 through Surya Shankar Films.
Gud Boy is the Odia version of the Tamil film Pazhani (2008).

Q122203754.lead: Pushkara is a 2023 Odia-language film directed by Subhransu Das, his first as director, based on Shankar Tripathy's novel Nadabindu. Sabyasachi Mishra and Supriya Nayak play the leads.

p: Tarang Cine Productions made the film, with Ramesh Barik as producer. The screenplay was written by Debidutta Mohanty, Chitra Pattanaik and Janmejay Singh. Subhransu Das had previously worked as a cinematographer; on this film the camera was handled by Falgu Satapathy. Shot at locations around Puri, it depicts local traditions such as the jagaghara, Sahi Jata and the boat-floating ritual, along with other rites of Lord Jagannath. The budget was ₹50 lakh.

Bibhuti Bhusan Gadanayak composed all the songs, and Debidutta Mohanty wrote the lyrics. The soundtrack also uses "Nua ghara khandi dine purana heba", a composition by the saint-poet Bauli Das. The songs were released on 9 September 2023.
Distributed by Rajshri Productions, the film reached cinemas on 19 September 2023, during Ganesh Puja.

facts: Nadabindu, a novel by Shankar Tripathy

Q7654081.lead: Swayamsiddha is a 2010 Odia-language film directed by Sudhanshu Sahu, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra and Yukta Inderlal Mookhey. It deals with young people drawn into the Maoist insurgency in Odisha.

p: The film looks at young people who join the Maoist movement and become cut off from mainstream society. It follows the problem from social trauma through an unjust state system that feeds the Naxal insurgency, and suggests that love and affection can change the minds of those who have taken up violence. Siddhanta Mahapatra plays Digvijay, and Yukta Inderlal Mookhey plays Shreya, the Swayamsiddha of the title.

Prabhat Ranjan Mallick produced the film for N K Media Ventures from a story by Namita Malik. Dilip Choudhury wrote the dialogue and the screenplay, the latter together with Sahu. The muhurat was held at Taupadar near Deomali, and much of the film was shot in insurgency-affected parts of Koraput district under difficult conditions. Sanjeev Mohapatra was the cinematographer and Chandra Sekhar Mishra the editor.
Swarup Nayak composed the music and wrote the lyrics; the playback singers were Kumar Bapi, Tapu Mishra and T. Souri.

The film was released on 13 August 2010. Because Siddhanta Mahapatra, a Biju Janata Dal member of parliament, played a Maoist leader in it, opposition parties in the state protested and called for the film to be banned.

At the Odisha State Film Awards the film was named Best Film and also won for cinematography, screenplay and sound design; it also received the Mohan Sundar Deb Goswami Award. At the 2nd ETV Oriya Film Awards in 2011 it won Best Odia Film, Best Director and Best Cinematographer, and Siddhanta Mahapatra was named Best Actor. The 2nd Tarang Cine Awards in 2011 gave it a Special Jury Award along with prizes for direction, cinematography, editing, screenplay and sound design.

Q26787389.lead: Chini is a 2016 drama film in Odia and Sambalpuri directed by Pradeep Bhol, starring Amlan Das and Patrali, with Mihir Das and Mahasweta Ray in supporting roles. It deals with the stigma faced by a family whose child has HIV/AIDS.

p: Khira Nayak and his wife Pani live in Vikhampur village with their three children, Chaha, Pati and Chini. When young Chini, a schoolgirl, is found to have HIV/AIDS, the villagers shun the whole family, barring them from the school, the shops, the village street and the pond. Manav, a young doctor who has come to the village and fallen for Jagi, works against many setbacks to help the girl. The film's message is to hate the disease rather than the patient.

The film was made under the Navajiban Films banner. Pradeep Bhol wrote the story and screenplay as well as directing. The Bengali actress Patrali played the female lead, and Dillip Ray was the cinematographer.

Shankar Pradhan and Hemant Pandey composed the music. The lyricists included Haladhar Nag, Lal Ratnakar Singh, Binod Pasayat and Durga Madhab Panda. Asha Bhosle sang a Sambalpuri song, written by Durga Madhab Panda, with a western Odisha flavour; it was her first song in Sambalpuri. Tapu Mishra also sang for the film.
Chini was released on 9 September 2016.
The film won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Film for 2016.

Q7240259.lead: Premi No.1 (Lover No. 1) is an Odia-language film from 2005 directed by Sudhanshu Mohan Sahu, with Anubhav Mohanty, Koel Mallick, Chandni and Bijay Mohanty in the cast. It remakes the 2003 Telugu film Dil.

p: Sanjay joins a college where Pooja, whose father Mahabahu is the town's best-known gangster, is also enrolled, and he saves her from ragging. Their growing romance enrages Mahabahu, whose men threaten Sanjay's parents; Sanjay strikes back and declares he will become Mahabahu's son-in-law. Badly injured in a trap, he still elopes with Pooja to marry her as her father tries to part them.

Sahu directed with Bhabani Prasad as co-director and shared the screenplay with Ranjit Pattnaik, who also wrote the dialogue. Sanjay Nayak (Tutu) is credited with the story. The film was made under the Brajaraj Movies banner, with Ramesh as cinematographer and Chandra Sekhar Mishra as editor. Anubhav Mohanty plays Sanjay and Bijay Mohanty plays Mahabahu Chhotray; Uttam Mohanty, Aparajita Mohanty, Rahul Dev and Harihara Mohapatra are also in the cast.

Swarup Nayak composed the songs and also wrote them. Anubhav, Kumar Bapi, Tapu Mishra, T. Souri, Udit Narayan, Ira Mohanty and Nayak himself sang; Anubhav's number "Mu Khanti Odia Toka Premi No. 1" and the Udit Narayan–Ira Mohanty duet "Tu Nahin Kichi Mate Bhala Lagu Nahin O My Love" are among the tracks.
Released on 12 June 2005 in Odia and Bengali, the film returned to cinemas in February 2018, 13 years later.
Its source is Dil (2003), a Telugu film starring Nithiin.

facts: Mu Khanti Odia Toka Premi No. 1

Q3277122.lead: Sri Lokanath is a 1960 Odia-language socio-fantasy film directed by Prafulla Sengupta from a story by Aswini Kumar Ghosh. It was the first Odia film to win a National Film Award.

p: Dr Ajay Patanayak, an atheist, and his devout, childless wife Basanti have a son after Ajay's brother Bijay prays at the Sri Lokanath Temple in Puri, and they name the boy Lokanath. Years of misfortune follow: Bijay leaves home and later loses his reason after an accident, the child is taken for dead after a snakebite, and Basanti loses her memory. Eventually a young man named Ashok, in love with Uma, the daughter of Bijay's former sweetheart Laxmi, is revealed to be the lost Lokanath; the family reunites at the temple, and Ajay accepts that a higher power shapes human fate.

Ruprang Pvt. Ltd. produced the film. Premendra Mitra wrote the screenplay, Ramananda Sengupta was the cinematographer and Sukumar Sengupta the editor. The cast was led by Akshaya Mohanty, Manimala, Urbashi, Dukhiram Swain and Samuel Sahu.

Balakrushna Das composed the music. The songs include "Phoola Rasiyare", sung by Sandhya Mukherjee, "Chanhena Chanhena Michha E Bandhana", "Tuki Paradeshi Nija Deshe" and "Aji Akashe Ki Ranga Lagila Chora Pabane".
At the National Film Awards the film received the President's silver medal for Best Feature Film in Oriya, the first national award for an Odia film.

Q6936776.lead: Munna – A Love Story is a 2008 Odia-language romantic action drama film directed by N. Padhi and starring Anubhav Mohanty, Naina Das, Dushmant Panda, Romi and Mihir Das. It is an unofficial remake of the Hindi film Jeet.

p: Munna is a gangster working for a mafia don, his life split between crime and his mother. Nisha, a bar dancer, loves him silently. When Munna is hired to kill a police officer, he learns that the officer has married Pooja, the woman he once loved but could not marry; a flashback reveals what kept them apart.
