In the end Munna kills the don and dies.
K.M. Rai produced the film. Raman Ranjan wrote the story and Rajani Ranjan the dialogue, while N. Padhi wrote the screenplay as well as directing. S. Ranjan handled the cinematography.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music. The lyricists were Soumendra Mahapatra, Arun Mantri, Nirmal Nayak, Panchanan Nayak and Rajani Ranjan, and the singers included Majumdar, Shakti Mishra, Ira Mohanty, Pami and Babul Supriyo.

The film was released on 15 August 2008. Made on a medium budget, it opened strongly, but takings fell from the second week, with its storyline and music judged weak and rain, strikes and an Orissa bandh also hurting business. It ended as an average performer at the box office.
The film is an unofficial remake of the Bollywood film Jeet.

Q55465674.lead: 4 Idiots is a 2018 Odia-language comedy film written and directed by Basanta Sahoo, starring Sabyasachi Mishra, Akash Dasnayak, Kuna Tripathy, Chittaranjan Tripathy, Elina Samantray, Lipsa Mishra and Poonam Mishra.

p: Four carefree friends, the "4 idiots" of the title, are accidentally pulled into trouble. Three of them are married; the fourth, played by Sabyasachi Mishra, is engaged to and in love with a woman played by Elina Samantray.

Akshay Kumar Parija, Prashant Behera and K Sunil Kumar Yadav produced the film through Akshay Parija Productions and Prakash Films Productions; it was also the first production for Zee Sarthak, which distributed it. Rajani Ranjan wrote the screenplay and dialogue. The film was launched at a hotel in Bhubaneswar, and principal photography began on 20 April 2018. Biraja Kar was the cinematographer and Rajesh Dash the editor.

Prem Anand composed the songs, except "Mad Romeo", which was composed by G. Durga Prasad, Nabs and Saroj. Basantaraj Samal and Subrat Swain wrote the lyrics, and the singers included Human Sagar, Biswajit Mahapatra, Diptirekha Padhi, Asutosh and Sabisesh. The music was launched at Forum Mart, Bhubaneswar, on 25 May 2018.
The film was released in mid-June 2018, around the Raja festival.

Q15723848.lead: Kaa is an Odia-language drama film released in 1966, credited to the director "Siddharth" and based on Kanhu Charan Mohanty's novel of the same name. It won the President's Silver Medal for Best Odia Film.

p: Nandika and Sunanda live contentedly in his ancestral village home with his mother Abhaya and sister Kuni, but after seven years they still have no child, and Nandika is blamed for it. She persuades Sunanda to take a second wife, Lalita, who soon has him move with her to the city. Nandika then becomes pregnant, stirring Lalita's jealousy, but dies after giving birth; Lalita repents and raises the child as her own.

The film was produced by Parbati Ghose under the Sarathi Films banner on a budget of ₹1,12,500. The director's credit, "Siddharth", was a pseudonym. One account gives it as the collective name of Gour Prasad Ghose, Parbati Ghose and the Bombay director Ram Chandra Thakur, while the Odia credits name Sarada Prasanna Naik. The music director and the leading lady were also credited under pseudonyms. Deoji Bhai and Bijoy De handled the cinematography.
Bhubaneswar Mishra composed the music.
Kaa was released on 5 August 1966. It drew a strong response and was a box-office hit.
At the National Film Awards for 1966 it received the President's Silver Medal for Best Odia Film.

facts: Kaa, novel by Kanhu Charan Mohanty

Q130728829.lead: Karma is a 2024 Odia-language action thriller film directed by Anupam Patnaik, starring Anubhav Mohanty as a Special Investigation Officer. It was the highest-grossing Odia film of 2024.

p: Special Investigation Officer Amar Patnaik is stranded in an isolated graveyard, where he uncovers disturbing secrets and finds himself caught up in a story of karma and fate.

The film was made under Amiya Patnaik Productions, with Barsha Patnaik as producer and Anupam Patnaik also credited as co-producer. Manas Padhiary wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue, with Nishant Majithia contributing to the dialogue. Suryamayee Mohapatra, Divya Disha Mohanty, Sanoj Kumar, Manmay Dey, Udit Guru and Choudhury Jayaprakash Das play supporting parts. Deepak Kumar Gharai was the cinematographer and Rashmi Ranjan Dash the editor.

Ashish Pradhan composed the music. The lyrics were written by Durga Madhab Panda, Sumit Panda and Manoj Kumar Panda, and the singers included Human Sagar, Ashish Pradhan, Mantu Chhuria, Ananya Sritam Nanda, Gaurav Anand and Soumya Prakash.
The film opened across Odisha on 9 October 2024, during Durga Puja. It received positive early reports and finished as the year's top-grossing Odia film.
At the Odisha State Film Awards for 2024, Karma was named best entertainment film, and Durga Madhab Panda won Best Lyrics for the song "Mo Hrudayata Nuhen".

Q17068594.lead: Manika is a 1986 Odia-language socio-mythological film directed by R. Asrar, telling the legend of Manika, the milkmaid devotee of Lord Jagannath. Tandra Ray plays the title role, with Bijay Mohanty.

p: Manika, an orphaned milkmaid, is devoted to Lord Jagannath and longs to see him and attain moksha. After the Gajapati king of Kalinga is defeated in the Kanchi campaign, he prays to Jagannath, who rides out with his brother Balabhadra. On the bank of the Mahanadi the two gods drink curd from Manika and give her a jewelled gold ring, telling her the king will pay when he passes. When she stops the king and shows the ring, he recognises it as Jagannath's and marches on with renewed confidence, while Manika, having glimpsed the god, gives the rest of her life to his worship.

The film was made by Rupa International and produced by Yogendra Mahapatra and Purna Mahapatra. Nagraj was the cinematographer and Madhavan the editor. Gurudatta Samantsinhar played Lord Jagannath and Bijay Mohanty played Chandra Behera.
Upendra Kumar composed the music, with lyrics by Narayana Prasad Singh. The songs were sung by Chitta Jena, Pranab Pattnaik and S. Janaki, among others.
Manika was released on 19 July 1986.

facts: Legend of Manika the milkmaid and the Kanchi expedition

Q15724802.lead: Balunga Toka is a 2011 Odia-language romantic drama film directed by Sudhakar Basant, starring Anubhav Mohanty and Barsha Priyadarshini. It is a remake of the 2004 Tamil-Telugu film 7G Rainbow Colony.

p: Chiku, who lives with his parents and younger sister, brawls in the streets, ignores his studies and is constantly scolded by his father. Falling for Preeti changes him, and with her help he finds a job. Her mother arranges a marriage for her elsewhere; Preeti runs away to Chiku, but a misunderstanding parts them and both are hurt in an accident that costs Chiku his memory. Once he recovers, he fights off the thugs attacking his father, and Preeti's father finally accepts the couple.

Prabhas Chandra Rout produced the film. Muni Patra wrote the story and Sudhakar Basant the screenplay. R. Bhagat Singh was the cinematographer and Chandra Sekhar Mishra the editor. Papu Pom Pom and Minaketan Das appear in supporting roles.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the songs, released by Amara Muzik. The title song "Balunga Toka" is based on "Hey Vetri Velaa" from the Tamil film Padikkadavan.
The film opened on 2 October 2011 and was a commercial success, running for more than 100 days in several cinemas in Odisha.

At the 3rd Tarang Cine Awards in 2012 it won Best Film, Best Actor for Anubhav Mohanty, Best Supporting Actor for Minaketan Das and Best Comedian for Papu Pom Pom. The 3rd ETV Oriya Film Awards gave it Best Film, Best Director, Best Actor, Best Comedian, Best Music Director for Abhijit Majumdar and Best Lyricist for Nirmal Nayak. Mohanty was also named Best Actor at the Lalchand Entertainment Awards 2012.
The film is a remake of 7G Rainbow Colony (2004).

Q15725414.lead: Haata Dhari Chaalutha is a 2013 Odia-language drama film directed by Himansu Parija and produced by Anubhav Mohanty and Anuprash Mohanty, starring Anubhav Mohanty and Barsha Priyadarshini. It is a remake of the Telugu film Solo.

p: Sai, an orphan, wants to marry into a joint family so that he can have the blessings of elders. He falls for Samparna, who is close to everyone in her large family, and wins her over. Her father Abinash Choudhury objects to an orphan and wants her to marry into an influential family, but in the end he gives his consent.

The film was first planned under the English title "Made for each other", but Parija persuaded the producers to give it an Odia name. Bijay Mohanty and Tandra Ray play the heroine's parents. R. Bhagat Singh was the cinematographer and Chandra Sekhar Mishra the editor.

Prem Anand composed the music, with lyrics by Basantaraj Samal and Arun Mantri; Udit Narayan and Ira Mohanty were among the singers. The songs include "Mo Haata Dhari Chaalutha" and "Sathire Sathi". The audio was launched in Cuttack on 20 April 2013.
The film was released on 14 June 2013. It was well reviewed and did good business.

At the Tarang Cine Awards 2014 it won Best Film, Best Actor for Anubhav Mohanty and Best Dialogue for Bijaya Malla. At the Filmfare Awards East it was nominated for Best Odia Film, with nominations also for Parija, Mohanty and Priyadarshini.
The film is a remake of the Telugu film Solo.

Q30646503.lead: Sister Sridevi is a 2017 Odia-language romantic comedy film directed by Ashok Pati and produced by Tarang Cine Productions, starring Babushaan and Sivani Sangita. It is a remake of the 2016 Tamil film Remo.

p: A young man, Sanju, goes as far as disguising himself as a woman in order to win the love of Sunayana, the woman he adores.

Ashok Pati wrote the screenplay and Ranjit Pattnaik the dialogue. Sivani Sangita had earlier worked in Odia films as a child artist. Mihir Das, Aparajita Mohanty and Salil Mitra play supporting roles. Kuni Mahapatra was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music and Nirmal Nayak wrote all the lyrics. The singers included Rituraj Mohanty, Tarique Aziz, Pamela Jain, Kuldeep, Sanju Mohanty and Pragyan. Rituraj Mohanty, who had sung many Hindi songs, recorded his first Odia song for the film, "Darli Tu Mo Tharu Kain Nelu Alabida".

The film was released across Odisha on 9 June 2017, during the Raja festival, to positive reviews. It took ₹18 lakh on its opening day and ₹70 lakh in its first week, followed by ₹1.03 crore in the second week and ₹30 lakh in the third.
At the Pratibha Samman awards of the film magazine Chalachitra Jagat, Babushaan was named best actor and Ranjit Pattnaik best dialogue writer.
The film is based on the Tamil film Remo (2016).

Q117324857.lead: T is a 2023 biographical film in Odia and Hindi written and directed by Jitesh Kumar Parida. It tells the life of Meghna Sahoo, India's first transgender taxi driver, and stars Debasish Sahoo, Prasanjeet Mohapatra, Usasi Misra, Ranbeeir Kalsi and Hara Rath.

p: Born Vishnu, Meghna is mistreated for her feminine behaviour and later enters sex work in a Kinnar community while coming to terms with her identity. She loses a corporate job when her transgender identity becomes known, transitions, and begins driving a taxi. Despite hostility and violence, she becomes an advocate and leader for the Kinnar community, working to improve their lives.

Jitesh Kumar Parida produced the film with Jitendra Rai under the Jitesh Kumar Films banner, and wrote it with Jitendra Rai and Kuwar Shakti Singh. Sarbeswar Dash was the cinematographer and Amarjit Ojha the editor. The trailer and poster were presented at the India pavilion of the 75th Cannes Film Festival.
Tuhin K Biswas composed the music. Ranjan Kumar Das wrote the Odia lyrics, while Arjun Meher, Subhra Bhattacharya and Sanjay Gaikwad wrote the Hindi songs.

The film was shown at the Jaipur International Film Festival in 2022. The censor board at first objected to it, and it was cleared with a U/A certificate after some cuts. It opened in cinemas in Odia on 25 May 2023.
It won Best LGBT Film at the Golden Jury Film Festival in Mumbai.

Q15724883.lead: Bou (Mother) is a 1998 Odia-language drama film written, produced and directed by Sabyasachi Mohapatra, starring Mahasweta Roy and Bijay Mohanty. Usasi Misra, Jyoti Misra and Akshaya Bastia made their debuts in it.

p: Umakant and Durga live contentedly with their sons Deepak and Amar and Deepak's wife Seema, until an accident leaves Umakant disabled and the sons abandon their parents. Durga, who is skilled at dress design, finds work as a designer with the help of Atal Bihari and prospers. When the sons later fall on hard times and go bankrupt, Durga refuses to help, but Umakant persuades her to forgive them and the family reunites.

The film was made by Kumar Pictures on a budget of about ₹98.25 lakh. Mohapatra wrote the screenplay, and Bijay Mishra the dialogue. Aum Prakash Mohapatra was the cinematographer and A. Sreekar Prasad the editor. Siddhanta Mahapatra played the elder son and Mihir Das played Atal Bihari.

Ramesh Mahananda composed the music. The lyricists were Srikanta Gautam, Nizam and Rajani Ranjan, and the singers included Mohammed Sikandar Alam, Gita Dash, Ramahari Das, Subash Das, Bibhu Kishore, Bishnu Nayak and Pritinanda Routray.

Q7418588.lead: Sanju Aau Sanjana is a 2010 Odia-language romantic film written and directed by Ashok Pati, starring Babushaan, Parijaat and Mihir Das. It is a remake of the 2008 Telugu film Parugu.

p: Parsuram Paikray, a powerful man in the city, insists on choosing husbands for his daughters Anjana and Sanjana. When Anjana runs off and marries Amar, Parsuram has his men kidnap Amar's friends to find her. Sanju, one of the captives, falls in love with Sanjana and the two escape together; Parsuram sends his men to kill Sanju, but he survives and marries Sanjana.

Lutu Mohanty produced the film for Jay Hanuman Films. Ashok Pati wrote the story and screenplay and Rajani Ranjan the dialogue. Sudarshana Sengupta, credited as Parijaat, played Sanjana, and Usasi Misra played her sister Anjana. Sitanshu Mahapatra was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor.
Prasant Padhi composed the music, with lyrics by Basantaraj Samal and Lutu Mohanty. The playback singers were Tapu Mishra, Bibhu Kishore, Krishna Beura and Kumar Bapi.
The film was released on 12 June 2010.
At the 2nd Tarang Cine Awards in 2011 it won Best Film, Best Actor, Best Cinematographer and Best Dance Director for 2010.
The film is based on Parugu (2008), a Telugu film starring Allu Arjun, Sheela and Prakash Raj.

Q54933364.lead: Sundergarh Ra Salman Khan is a 2018 Odia-language film directed by Ashok Pati and made by Tarang Cine Productions, starring Babushaan and the newcomer Divya Mohanty.

p: Sachikanta Jena produced the film with Tarang Cine Productions, and Ranjit Pattnaik wrote the dialogue. Divya Mohanty, making her film debut in the lead, had earlier played the goddess Lakshmi in the Tarang TV serial Jay Maa Laxmi before acting in South Indian films and serials. Babi Mishra played Nayak Mardaraj and Krishna Kar played Pralay Mardaraj, with Papu Pam Pam, Mihir Das, Usasi Misra, Satyaki Misra and Pushpa Panda in other roles. Sitanshu Mahapatra was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics. The singers included Human Sagar, Biswajit, Satyajit Pradhan, Amrita, Rashmita, Saroj Pradhan, Jagruti Mishra, Tarique Aziz, Pamela Jain, Soyam Padhi and Sohini Mishra.
The censor board gave the film a U certificate, and it opened on 13 June 2018, during the Raja festival.

Q139819431.lead: Mantra Muugdha is a 2026 Odia-language adventure fantasy musical thriller directed by Anupam Patnaik, with an ensemble cast led by Sanoj Kumar and Manmay Dey.

p: The film follows a mysterious, magical journey in which music unlocks hidden forces and draws its characters into a dangerous adventure full of secrets, supernatural events and surprising revelations.

Barsha Patnaik and Anupam Patnaik produced the film. Roshan Bishoyi wrote the story and Pranab Rath the dialogue, while the screenplay was written by Rohit Gehlot and Anupam Patnaik with contributions from Nishant Majithia. Working under the initial title MM, the crew completed shooting in 50 days. Deepak Kumar Gharai was the cinematographer and Rashmi Ranjan Dash the editor.

The songs were composed by Anurag Panda, Anurag Patnaik, Sangita Pattnaik, Ashish Pradhan and Roumyaj Pradhan, with lyrics by Manoj Kumar Panda, Ranjan Nayak, Debajyoti Nayak and Papu Pam Pam. The singers included Ashish Pradhan, Subhashree Jena, Human Sagar, Antara Chakraborty and Papu Pam Pam. Promotional tracks were issued through Tarang Music.

A teaser came out in March 2026 and a trailer on YouTube ahead of release. The film opened on 1 May 2026 in 52 cinemas in Odisha and 70 across India, including Hyderabad, Bengaluru, Chennai, Mumbai and Pune. It earned more than ₹15 crore in its first 15 days.

Q7425833.lead: Sasura Ghara Zindabad is a 2010 Odia-language film written and directed by Sanjay Nayak, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Megha Ghosh. It follows three sons-in-law of a wealthy industrialist.

p: Three men marry the daughters of a rich industrialist who has two wives. The two elder sons-in-law, Arvind and Hadu, live idly off their father-in-law's wealth. The arrival of the youngest, Raja, a small-time thief, quickly changes things in the household.

Uttam Chand Jain produced the film for Top Films. Sanjay Nayak wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue and also edited it, with S. Ranjan as cinematographer. Bijay Mohanty, Tandra Roy, Pushpa Panda, Snigdha Mohanty, Jairam Samal and Hadu Patnaik are among the supporting cast. The film entered the Limca Book of Records because it and Dil Tate Deichi, two films sharing the same producer, director, cinematographer and hero, were cleared by the censor board on the same day.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak, Arun Mantri, Basantaraj Samal and Sujit Parija. Bibhu Kishore, Kumar Sanu, Abhijit Majumdar, Manas Pritam and Ira Mohanty were among the singers.
The film was released on 13 August 2010.
At the 2nd ETV Oriya Film Awards in 2011 the film earned nominations for Sabyasachi Mishra (Best Actor), Hadu Patnaik and Arabinda (Best Comedian) and Bibhu Kishore (Best Playback Singer).

Q40543638.lead: Kabula Barabula is a 2017 Odia-language comedy film directed by Ramesh Rout, starring Anubhav Mohanty and Elina Samantray. It is a remake of the 2013 Punjabi film Singh vs Kaur.

p: Kabula, a man from an Odisha village, travels to Malaysia in search of his beloved, the daughter of a wealthy father, and finds that winning her is no easy task.

Vijay Kandoi and Aviram Sahu produced the film under the Vidisha Kraft and AB Films banners. Ashok Pati wrote the screenplay and Basantaraj Samal the dialogue. Pratap Rout was the cinematographer and Rajesh Dash the editor. The song sequences were filmed in Malaysia.

Prem Anand composed the music and Basantaraj Samal wrote the lyrics. The singers included Biswajit Mahapatra, Ananya Sritam Nanda, Diptirekha Padhi, Abhijit Majumdar and Human Sagar. The soundtrack also has an Odia version of "Sonu", a song then popular on social media, with words by Subrat Swain, sung by Abhijit Majumdar.
The film and its soundtrack were released on 27 September 2017, during Durga Puja. It was a box-office hit.
The film is based on the Punjabi film Singh vs Kaur (2013).

Q7399494.lead: Sahara Jaluchi is a 1998 Odia-language action film written and directed by Sudhanshu Mohan Sahu, with Uttam Mohanty, Siddhanta Mahapatra, Jyoti Misra, Mihir Das and Aparajita Mohanty in the cast.

p: Biraj Das, a schoolteacher known for his honesty, sees the gang of Pappu Raula commit a murder in the street and goes to the police despite his family's pleas. The gang threatens him and later kills him. His son Priya, together with a journalist girlfriend and Raja, a man seeking revenge for his own brother's death, eventually kills Raula.

Laxminarayan Agarwal and Snehalata Sahu produced the film. Sahu also wrote its story and screenplay, while Bijay Mishra wrote the dialogue. B. Satish handled the cinematography and Rabi Shankar Patnaik the editing. Mithun Chakraborty made a special appearance, his first in an Odia film, and his presence led the makers to dub the film into Bengali under the title Sahar Jolche.

The music is credited to Swarup Nayak in one account and to Radhakrishna Bhanja in another. Nimai Mohanty and Nizam wrote the lyrics, and the playback singers included Abhijeet, Mohammed Aziz, Subash Das, Kavita Krishnamurthy, Udit Narayan, Anuradha Paudwal and Babul Supriyo. The soundtrack was released by Amara Muzik.

Q15725411.lead: Hakim Babu is a 1985 Odia-language drama film directed by Pranab Das, starring Ajit Das, Jaya Swami and Bijaya Jena. It is adapted from Bibhuti Patnaik's novel of the same name.

p: Set among the Juang tribe, the film deals with industrialisation and the displacement it causes in an Odisha village. It follows Kanhu Majhi, who rises to become a collector and uses the position to help his people.

Amiya Ranjan Patnaik produced the film, and Pranab Das adapted the novel and wrote the screenplay, with dialogue by Bijay Mishra. It was the second film Pranab Das and Ajit Das made together, after Sesha Pratikhya (1979). Because the story is set in the Keonjhar area, about three-quarters of the shooting took place there and the remainder at Kalinga Studio. Rajan Kinagi shot the film, Mukhtar Ahmed edited it and Nikhil Baran Sengupta was art director.

Bijaya Jena joined the cast after Ajit Das, who was also executive producer, approached her in Mumbai. She played a wealthy, educated young woman who is rude to her elders; her character is introduced ahead of the song "Mun Tuma Aina".
Saroj Patnaik composed the music.
The film was released on 6 June 1985, ran 163 minutes and did well at the box office. Its success made Ajit Das a familiar name with audiences.

Hakim Babu won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia, given to Pranab Das and Amiya Patnaik. At the Odisha State Film Awards, Ajit Das was named Best Actor, Jaya Swami Best Actress and Rajan Kinagi took the award for photography, while Nikhil Baran Sengupta was honoured for art direction.

facts: Hakim Babu, novel by Bibhuti Patnaik
National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia

Q7259057.lead: Pooja Pain Phulatie (A Rose for Pooja) is a 2007 Odia-language film written, directed and edited by Gadadhar Puty, starring Adyasha Mahapatra and Akankshya Kabi. It won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia.

p: Pooja, an orphan raised by her grandfather at a brickyard, is taken to the city by the yard's owner, but his wife puts her to work as a maid instead of sending her to school. She forms a close friendship with the family's spoilt daughter Mickey and turns her into an all-round achiever, until Pooja is thrown out of the house. Years later, Mickey suffers an eye injury; Pooja, now ill with cancer, cares for her while hiding her identity, and after her death her donated eyes restore Mickey's sight.
Padmini Puty produced the film, with cinematography by Jugal Debata and music by Vikash Das. The budget was ₹65.25 lakh. The story centres on a 13-year-old girl and is set in and around Bhubaneswar.
The film was released on 29 September 2007 with a running time of 96 minutes. It was screened at the 5th International Film Festival of Thrissur.

At the 54th National Film Awards it was named Best Feature Film in Odia. It also won several Odisha State Film Awards, including Best Film, Best Direction, Best Story, Best Cinematography, Best Child Artist and Best Female Playback Singer.

facts: National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia (54th)

Q109643422.lead: Cuttack Weds Sambalpur is a 2021 Odia-language romantic film directed by Bapi David, with Sambit Acharya and Susmita Pradhan in the lead roles.

p: Samir, a stage performer who lives with his grandfather in Sambalpur, falls in love with Kanika, a Cuttack office worker visiting the town for a workshop. After she leaves, their contact breaks down, his grandfather dies, and Samir vows not to reach out until she apologises, throwing himself instead into building an events company, R.R. Events. His brother and sister-in-law learn from Kanika that she had been trying to reach him, and together with her father they arrange for Samir to organise her supposed wedding. At the ceremony a rival suitor, Kunal, admits he had tampered with their phone numbers and abducts Kanika at gunpoint, and Samir rescues her.

Ramesh Barik and K. Tamanna produced the film. Jitendra Pradhan and Jitendra Dash wrote the story and dialogue, while Bapi David wrote the screenplay. Amaresh Jena was the cinematographer and Amarjit Ojha the editor. Kuna Tripathy, Pintu Nanda, Guddu, Pradeep Debata and Mahaprasad Kar appear in supporting roles.
The music was composed by Baidyanath Dash and Kamalesh Chakraborty.

Q41562383.lead: Tu Mo Hero is a 2017 Odia-language romantic drama film written and directed by Dilip Panda, starring Jyoti Ranjan Nayak, Jhilik Bhattacharya and Mihir Das.

p: Sambhu and his wife Lata of Salia Sahi in Bhubaneswar bring up his sister's son, Prem. Khushi, the daughter of a State Bank manager, falls for the stylish Prem, but her father opposes the match and wants her to marry a rich builder's son. Prem survives a suicide attempt after the setback, and the rest of the film follows the couple's struggle to stay together.

Chamarti Srinibas Rao produced the film under Uday Movies. Dilip Panda wrote the story and screenplay, and Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue. S. H. Prasad was cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra editor.

Baidyanath Dash composed the score. The lyricists were Nirmal Nayak, Jayanta Das, Arun Mantri, Bapu Goswami and Bijay Malla, and the songs were sung by Human Sagar, Tariq Aziz, Satyajit, Asima Panda, Pragyan Hota, Ananya Sritam Nanda and Sobha. The full album came out on the film's release day. The song "Aashiqana" is based on "Awaara Dil" from the 2016 film Ki Kore Toke Bolbo.
The film was released on 20 October 2017.
Rajani Ranjan received the award for best dialogue, screenplay and story at the 12th Film and Television Award Show Time 2018.

Q6382527.lead: Kedar Gouri is a 1954 Odia-language tragic romance film directed by Nitai Palit, adapted from Radhanath Rai's poem of the same name, with Gour Ghose and Gloria Mohanty as the title lovers.

p: Kedar and Gouri, children of two rival village heads, grow from childhood friends into lovers, but their families keep them apart; when Kedar slips into Gouri's birthday celebration in disguise he is caught and thrown out. The pair run away into the jungle. While Kedar fetches water, Gouri hides from a tiger; finding her bloodied clothes, Kedar believes she has been killed and takes his own life, and Gouri, returning to find him dead, does the same.

Manaranjan Das wrote the film, which was made under the Radha Pictures banner and distributed by Pancha Sakha Films. One account credits Balaram Das as producer, while another names Dhira Biswal and Manoranjan Das and describes the film as jointly directed by Nitai Palit and Manoranjan Das. Govinda Tej made his acting debut in the film.
Balakrushna Das composed the music and Kalicharan Patnaik wrote the songs, which include "Kehi Ki Dekhichha Palli Ma Ra Hasa Ra" and "Rama Je Laikhana Ho Gale Mruga Mari".

The film opened on 25 September 1954 and ran 176 minutes. Though its acting and cinematography were noted as good, it failed commercially, as audiences did not take to a tragic love story of this kind.

facts: Kedar Gouri, poem by Radhanath Rai
Kehi Ki Dekhichha Palli Ma Ra Hasa Ra; Rama Je Laikhana Ho Gale Mruga Mari

Q6786343.lead: Mate Ta Love Helare is a 2008 Odia-language action film directed by Ashok Pati, starring Anubhav Mohanty, Subhashree Ganguly and Siddhanta Mahapatra. It is a loose remake of the Telugu film Student No. 1.

p: Akash is a serious, ambitious student who wants to secure a good future for his mother and sister, and at college he falls for Megha. His plans unravel when he is caught in a trap set by the mafia don Bhalu Bhai and his brother King. The film follows how he escapes, punishes the don and wins Megha.

Bijaya Pattnaik produced the film and wrote its story; Ranajit Patnaik wrote the dialogue and Ashok Pati the screenplay. The cinematography is credited to K. R. Ramesh, and Susanta Mani edited the film. Siddhanta Mahapatra played the villain Bhalu Bhai, Anubhav Mohanty played Akash and Subhashree Ganguly played Megha; it was Subhashree's first film.

Bachu Mukherjee composed the music, with lyrics by Arun Mantri, Purnendu Das Mohapatra, Swarup Nayak and Nizam. The singers included Kumar Bapi, Subhasish Mahakud, Tapu Mishra, Pami, Sailabhama Mahapatra and T. Souri.

The film was released in March 2008. Although it was made on a large budget, with considerable graphics work aimed at young viewers, its release fell during the examination season and its box-office performance was only slightly above average.

Q50825290.lead: Jogi is a 2018 Odia-language political drama film directed by Niranjan Behera and produced by Sridhar Martha, with Aryan Dash and Nikita Mishra in the lead roles.

p: Jagabandhu Mishra, a freedom fighter, hopes for an ideal, just state, but his elder son Sangram turns corrupt soon after becoming chief minister and is voted out. His successor, a woman social worker, proves just as corrupt. When fresh elections come, people look to Jagabandhu's younger son Biplab, who has renounced worldly life and is known as Jogi; he decides to enter politics to clean up the state and fulfil his father's dream.

Chhabita Martha wrote the story, Rajani Ranjan the dialogue and Niranjan Behera the screenplay. It was Behera's first released film as director; he had earlier started work on Aunty Namaskar, which did not reach release first. The Colombian dancer Maria Ola and the Hindi film actress Rumpa Sarkar appear in item numbers. Producer Sridhar Martha has announced a sequel, Jogi 2.

Deepak Kumar composed the music. The lyrics were written by Subha Kumar Das, Rajanikanta Nayak, Sujata Jena and Shirshananda Das Kanungo, and the singers included Tariq Aziz, Satyajit Pradhan, Asima Panda, Pami and Sanju.
The film was released on 20 April 2018.

Q4900733.lead: Bhai Bhai is a 1956 Odia-language social drama film directed by Nitai Palit and produced by Gour Prasad Ghose. Based on Santanu Kumar Das's book of the same name, it deals with untouchability and caste in rural Odisha.

p: In a village split between the landowning Pradhans and the Bauris, who labour on their fields and are treated as untouchable, the upper-caste headman Suduria rejects untouchability and is close to Nidhi, a Bauri who calls him brother. Bana, a Pradhan, has the village punish Nidhi by barring him from work and from drawing water at the pond, and Suduria stays silent. The Bauris respond by refusing to work the Pradhans' land, which falls barren until the Pradhans admit their wrong and accept the bond between the two men.

The film was made under the Dalit Jatisangha Chitram banner with financial support from the Government of Orissa. Denen Gupta was the cinematographer and Biswanath Nayak the editor, and Manoj Das is credited with the dialogue. The cast included Parbati Ghose, credited as Chapala Nayak, who is described as the first woman filmmaker from Odisha.
The music was composed by Balakrishna Das and Bhubaneswar Misra.
Bhai Bhai was released on 21 June 1956, with a running time of 151 minutes.

facts: Bhai Bhai, book by Santanu Kumar Das

Q29440795.lead: Tu Mo Love Story is a 2017 Odia-language teen romance film directed by Tapas Sargharia and produced by Deepak Kumar Mishra, starring Swaraj Barik and Bhoomika Dash.

p: The film was made under the Tarang Cine Productions and DK Movies banners, with a screenplay by Tapas Sargharia. Its story is a love affair between two teenagers. Swaraj Barik, who had worked as a child actor in several films, played his first lead role here, and Bhoomika Dash, a child artist in Rumku Jhumana, played the heroine. Mihir Das, Debasish Patra, Manoj Mishra and Choudhury Bikash Das were among the supporting cast.

Prem Anand composed the film's five songs, which were written by Subrat Swain and Arun Mantri. The singers were Human Sagar, Diptirekha Padhi, Ananya Sritam Nanda, Asutosh Mohanty and Biswajit Mohapatra.
The film was released on 7 April 2017.

At the Pratibha Samman of the film magazine Chalachitra Jagat, Swaraj Barik and Bhoomika Dash were named best debut actor and best debut actress. The film was named Best Film at the 12th Film and Television Award Show Time 2018, and it also received honours for lyrics, direction and music direction.

Q15724962.lead: Mana Akasha is a 1974 Odia-language drama film directed by Nitai Palit, based on Basant Kumar Mahapatra's Jhara Baula. It deals with social and economic conflict in rural Odisha.

p: Sashank Patnaik and Rudra Choudhury are close friends, and Rudra's son Bhanu falls in love with Sashank's daughter Mala. After Rudra dies, Sashank schemes to take over his property and, though he knows Mala is pregnant by Bhanu, tries to poison the young man. He later recognises his wrong and helps bring Bhanu and Mala together.

Rahas Bihari Mishra of Sambalpur produced the film, and his son Shanti Swaroop Misra played one of the leads, Bhanu Pratap. Nitai Palit wrote the screenplay. Outdoor scenes were filmed at Cuttack, Daitari and other locations, and interiors at Indrapuri Studio in Kolkata. Krishna Chakraborty shot the film and Ramesh Joshi edited it; Batu Sen and Gopi Sen handled art direction, and Dhira Biswal, who also played Sashank, was chief production manager.

Upendra Kumar, then based in Madras, made his entry into Odia cinema as the film's composer, and the songs were recorded at Gemini Studio in Madras. The lyricists were Narayan Prasad Singh, Gurukrushna Goswami, Shibabrata Das and Rahas Bihari Mishra, and the singers included Bhikari Bal, Md. Sikandar Alam, Chittaranjan Jena, Mohini Mohan Rath, Punyaprabha Bahidar, S. Janaki and S. G. Gita. Songs include "Chora Chora Priti Asa Sathi", "Mora Kaniaan Sunapaniaan", "E Bana Jharana Nachi Nachi Jaa Na" and "Mane Mane Bhabu Tu Bhari Sundara".
The film was released in 1974 and runs 167 minutes.

facts: Jhara Baula by Basant Kumar Mahapatra
Chora Chora Priti Asa Sathi; Mora Kaniaan Sunapaniaan

Q6405153.lead: Kie Kahara is a 1968 Odia-language drama film directed by Nitai Palit and produced by Dhira Biswal, starring Sarat Pujari and Saudamini Misra. It depicts the strains on declining zamindar families trying to hold on to their social standing.

p: Prakash is raised by his aunt Mamata after his widowed father leaves, and grows up to become an engineer. Working in town, he lodges with Rajendra Samantrai, a descendant of zamindars who struggles to meet his wife Subhadra's expectations of status, and falls in love with Rajendra's daughter Malati. Subhadra favours Nagen, son of the rich contractor Nabin Mahapatra, and when Rajendra turns down Nagen's proposal, Nagen sets out to damage the family and to divide the couple. Prakash's father finally appears and clears up the misunderstandings, and Prakash and Malati marry.

The film was written by Nitai Palit, Gopal Chhotray and Bhim Singh and made under the Pancha Sakha Films banner. Dinen Gupta was the cinematographer. Producer Dhira Biswal also played the antagonist Nagen, while Samuel Sahu and Lila Dulali played Rajendra and Subhadra.
Akshaya Mohanty composed the music.

Released in 1968 with a running time of 178 minutes, Kie Kahara was a box-office hit. It played to full houses for around five months in Cuttack alone and became the first Odia film to complete more than 100 days in several theatres.

facts: First Odia film to run over 100 days in several theatres

Q28855721.lead: Suna Pila Tike Screw Dhila is a 2017 Odia-language film directed by Sudhakar Basant and produced by its lead actor Babushaan, about a group of four friends.

p: One of four close friends is married off suddenly against his wishes. After an accident he loses part of his memory: he still recalls his college years and his friends, but not his romance or his marriage, and the confusion that follows drives the plot. Babushaan plays the absent-minded Kunja.

It was the first film produced by Babushaan, made by his company together with Prakash Dhiraj Entertainment; Prasanta Behera and K. Sunil Kumar Yadav are also credited as producers. Sudhakar Basant wrote the screenplay, and the dialogue was the first screen work of Sarika, from Pattamundai in Kendrapara. Papu Pam Pam, Pintu Nanda and Pragyan Khatua played the hero's friends and Sheetal Patra the heroine; she had earlier been paired with Babushaan in films including Bhala Pae Tate 100 Ru 100 and Tu Je Sei.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the five songs, all written by Nirmal Nayak and Bapu Goswami. The singers included Majumdar, Babushaan, Pragyan Hota, Tariq Aziz and Pinky Pradhan. The music was launched at an event in Bhubaneswar on 26 July 2017.
The trailer went up on YouTube on 7 July 2017 and drew roughly 250,000 views in its first five days. The film, which runs 2 hours 17 minutes, was released on 4 August 2017.

Q27150386.lead: Gapa Hele Bi Sata is a 2015 Odia-language drama film directed by Murali Krishna, starring Anubhav Mohanty and Barsha Priyadarshini. It is a remake of the 2013 Kannada film Charminar.

p: Akash, now running a software company in Bangalore, returns to his village for a school reunion hoping to see Barsha, the childhood friend and sweetheart who had pushed him to take his studies seriously before she moved away. When she does not turn up, he tracks her down at her home and learns that an accident had cost her a leg and her mother. The two then begin a new life together.

Jagi Mangat Panda produced the film, the second from Tarang Cine Productions. The story is credited to R. Chandru and the writing to Nirmal Nayak, with cinematography by Abhiram Mishra. The title had earlier been used for a 1976 film, the first Odia film in colour.

Prem Anand composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak, Arun Mantri, Basantaraj Samal and Jayanta Das. Udit Narayan sang the title song with Ira Mohanty; the other singers were T. Souri, Kumar Bapi, Sasmita and Human Sagar.
The film opened on 12 June 2015, during the Raja festival, alongside Super Michhua and Love You Hamesha. It did not succeed at the box office.

Q57384687.lead: Prem Kumar is a 2018 Odia-language film directed by Tapas Sargharia for Tarang Cine Productions, starring Anubhav Mohanty, Sivani Sangita and Tamanna Vyas.

p: Ranjan Satapathy wrote the story, Tapas Sargharia and Debidutta Mohanty the screenplay, and Sanjay Mahakud, Debidutta Mohanty and Shakti Baral the dialogue. Rabindra Behera was cinematographer and Rajesh Dash editor.

Shooting stopped a few days after it began when Anubhav Mohanty was injured in an accident, so the film missed its planned release at the Raja festival of 2018; work resumed on 9 July. According to the director, the unit was also affected by the deaths of producer Pradyumna Lenka's father and choreographer Girish Mohanty's mother. Part of the film was shot at Doodhpathri in Jammu and Kashmir. Returning from the location on 13 September 2018, the car carrying Mohanty lost its brakes on a hill road, but the driver brought it under control; another group from the unit came upon a militant attack near Baramulla and took a village road towards Delhi to avoid it.
Prem Anand composed the music, with lyrics by Basantaraj Samal, Subrat Swain and Debidutta Mohanty. Rituraj Mohanty, Human Sagar, Lopamudra, Asutosh and Diptirekha Padhi were among the singers.
The film was released on 16 October 2018.

Q57315013.lead: Sriman Surdas is a 2018 Odia-language action comedy film directed by Ashok Pati and produced by Tarang Cine Productions, starring Babushaan and Bhoomika Dash. It is a remake of the 2017 Telugu film Andhhagadu.

p: Ashok Pati wrote the story and screenplay, and Ranjit Pattnaik the dialogue. Babushaan played the title role, Bhoomika Dash was cast opposite him, and Mihir Das took a negative role; Buddhaditya Mohanty also had a lead part. Sitanshu Mahapatra handled the camera and Sukumar Mani the editing. The film's composer, Abhijit Majumdar, also appears on screen.

Abhijit Majumdar's soundtrack, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak, came out on 24 September 2018. The singers included Kaushik Satapathy, Tariq Aziz, Pamela Jain, Swayam Padhi, Rajnandini Panda, Satyajit Pradhan, Majumdar himself, Antara Chakraborty and Human Sagar.
The film reached cinemas on 16 October 2018, during Durga Puja. It runs 157 minutes.

Q60580576.lead: Chal Tike Dusta Heba is a 2019 Odia-language teenage love story directed by Tapas Sargharia, which introduced its three leads, Rishan, Mahima and Sayal, to Odia cinema.

p: The film follows two teenagers, Rishan and Annie, who fall in love.

Manoranjan Sarangi produced the film under the Tarang Cine Productions banner. Dasaratha Singh is credited with the story, Debidutta Mohanty and Sanjay Mohakul with the dialogue, and Sargharia, Mohanty and Mohakul with the screenplay. Mihir Das and Priyanka Mahapatra played Rishan's parents, with Pradyumna Lenka, Tribhuban Panda and Saroj Das in supporting roles and Bhoomika Dash in a cameo as herself. Rabindra Behera was cinematographer and Rajesh Dash editor.
Bibhuti Bhusan Garnaik composed the music to lyrics by Debidutta Mohanty, with Shyam Padhi, Ananya Sritam Nanda and Nabhya Jyoti among the singers. Tarang Music released the soundtrack.
The film opened across Odisha on 11 January 2019, the 18th release from Tarang Cine Productions. It runs 122 minutes.

Q15723924.lead: Kebe Tame Naahan Kebe Mun Naahin is a 2012 Odia-language romantic film produced and directed by Chakradhar Sahu, starring Sabyasachi Mishra, Archita Sahu and Manoj Mishra.

p: Milly Choudhury of Sambalpur runs away to Bhubaneswar to escape a marriage her frightened father has accepted with the local strongman Ruturaj Panda. Swagat Das, a struggling singer, mistakes her for a friend's sister at the railway station, and she stays with him under the name Rekha until the two fall in love. An accident wipes out her memory and her parents take her home; when Ruturaj again tries to force the marriage, Swagat arrives, Milly's memory returns, and together they defeat Ruturaj.

Chakradhar Sahu wrote the story and also edited the film, with a screenplay by Ranjan Das and cinematography by Prasantanu Mohapatra. Besides Odisha, the film was shot in Kerala and Hyderabad to give it a fresh look.
Bikash Das composed the music.
The film was released on 17 February 2012 and was also shown in Bengaluru. It did not connect with the young audience it was aimed at and did average business.
Mohit Chakraborty won Best Lyricist at the 4th ETV Oriya Film Awards in 2013. At the 23rd Orissa State Film Awards, Arun Mantri was named Best Lyricist and Chakradhar Sahu Best Editor.

Q28174140.lead: God Father (also titled God Father – True Story of a Man) is an Odia-language film directed by Ramesh Rout and produced by Jugansu Sekhar Panda, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra and Anu Choudhury.

p: The film centres on a man who wins the affection of his village through good deeds while gangsters around him try to undo his work.

It was the second release from Chaturbhuja Films. Jugansu Sekhar Panda wrote the story and Nirmal Nayak the dialogue; Abhiram Mishra was cinematographer and Rajesh Das editor. The budget was reported as ₹2 crore. Hindi film and television actress Rakhi Sawant made her first Odia film appearance in the item number "Chuti Kholile".

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak and Nizam. Majumdar, Nabhya, Vinod Rathod, Pamela Jain, Mohammed Irfan, Tapu Mishra and Javed Ali sang the songs, and Amara Muzik released the soundtrack in December 2016.

One account dates the release to 27 December 2016; another places it on New Year's Day 2017. The film was reported as the highest-grossing Odia film of 2016, a record it is said to have held until Daman (2022). It was also dubbed into Bengali.

facts: God Father – True Story of a Man

Q7647411.lead: Suryamukhi is a 1963 Odia-language drama film directed by Prafulla Sengupta and produced by Saumendra Misra, who also played the lead. It won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Oriya.

p: Raju, a gifted village student promised to Gita, goes to Cuttack to study and falls in love with his classmate Usha, but her wealthy father Rai Bahadur humiliates him and drives him away. While Raju is missing, a family friend arranges Usha's marriage to Raju's brother Mohan. Raju is blinded in a factory accident, his mother dies of the shock, and after his sight is restored he returns home to find Usha married to his brother. Usha persuades him to accept the situation, and he marries Gita.

The film was made under the Uday Pictures banner on a budget of ₹86,000. Gurukrushna Goswami and Saumendra Misra wrote it, Goswami supplying the dialogue. Kanai Dey was cinematographer and Sukumar Sengupta editor. Minati Mishra played Usha, Sukhalata Mohanty Gita and Dhira Biswal the family friend Lokanath, while Laxmipriya Mahapatra appeared as an Odissi dancer.
Shantanu Mahapatra composed the music, and Lata Mangeshkar and Manna Dey sang in the film.
Suryamukhi was released on 2 October 1963. It was well received by audiences and was a commercial success.
At the 10th National Film Awards it received the award for Best Feature Film in Oriya.

facts: National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Oriya (10th)

Q7124149.lead: Pagala Premi is a 2007 Odia-language romantic drama film directed by Hara Patnaik, a remake of the 2004 Telugu film Arya. It marked the screen debuts of its leads, Sabyasachi Mishra and Arpita Mukherjee.

p: College student Surya falls for Gitanjali at first sight. Ajay, the spoilt son of the local MLA Abinash, has already pressured the timid Gitanjali into dating him by threatening to jump from the college roof, so she turns Surya down in front of him. Convinced that she does not truly love Ajay, Surya keeps trying to win her over through his attitude and goodwill, without trying to break the couple apart.

A. Ramesh Prasad produced the film. Hara Patnaik cast Sabyasachi Mishra in the lead after seeing him at a stage show. Pradyumna Lenka played the MLA, and Abhinayashree appeared in the item number "Aa Mane Anandapur". Niranjan Dash was cinematographer and Chandra Sekhar Mishra editor. A Bengali version, Pagal Premi, was shot at the same time with Ritwick Chakraborty, Yash Dasgupta and Arpita.

Manmatha Misra scored the film, reusing all the songs of the Telugu original. The lyrics were by Arun Mantri and Basantaraj Samal, and the playback singers were Kumar Bapi, T. Souri, Tapu Mishra and T. Srinu.
The film was released on 14 June 2007.
Sabyasachi Mishra received the Best Actor award at the Orissa State Film Awards in 2007.

Q50825295.lead: Happy Lucky is a 2018 Odia-language romantic action comedy film directed by Sudhanshu Sahu for Tarang Cine Productions, starring Sambit Acharya, Jyoti Ranjan Nayak, Elina Samantray and Sasmita. It is an official remake of the Tamil film Vettai.

p: The film is about two brothers, Happy and Lucky, who fall in love with two sisters.

Sanjay Mahakul and Debidutta Mohanty wrote the screenplay and dialogue, and R. Bhagat Singh was the cinematographer. Sasmita, who plays opposite Sambit Acharya, had won the third season of Tarang TV's Kie Heba Mo Heroine. Mihir Das, Bobby Mishra, Pradyumna Lenka and Choudhury Bikash Das were in the supporting cast.

Prem Anand composed the music to lyrics by Basantraj Samal. The singers included Diptirekha Padhi, Lopamudra, Human Sagar, Biswajit Mohapatra, Sasank Sekhar, Asutosh Mohanty, Asima Panda and Satyajit. The audio was launched at the Municipality Kalyan Mandap in Chandrasekharpur during Odisha Television Limited's Rasagola Mahotsav.

Released on 21 January 2018 as the year's second Odia film, it runs 159 minutes. Accounts of its box-office performance differ: one reports that it did well with a total collection of ₹4.50 crore, while another says it fell short of expectations.

Q37833797.lead: Bhala Pae Tate 100 Ru 100 is a 2015 Odia-language action comedy film directed by Sudhanshu Sahu and produced by Sitaram Agrawal, starring Babushaan and Sheetal Patra. It remakes the 2007 Kannada film Krishna.

p: Rahul, an orphan who hosts one of the most popular shows on Sarthak TV, lodges with Hari. His life runs smoothly until he turns down the advances of his landlord's daughter, and the reasons for his refusal are revealed as the story unfolds.

The Kannada original's second half was itself drawn from the 2002 Tamil film Unnai Ninaithu. Ranjit Patnaik wrote the dialogue and Rajesh Dash edited the film. Alongside Sheetal Patra, Suryamayee Mohapatra played a heroine; she was cast after winning Sarthak TV's talent show Mu Bi Heroine Hebi. Harihara Mahapatra, Pruthiviraj Nayak, Amit Pani and Debasish Patra had supporting roles.
Bikash Das composed the music and Srikanta Gautam wrote the lyrics. The songs were sung by Namita Agrawal, Sourin Bhatt and Babushaan, among others.
The film was released during Durga Puja on 18 October 2015 and runs 160 minutes. It was declared a hit after doing good business across Odisha and was reported to have drawn positive reviews.

Q42158752.lead: Superstar is a 2013 Odia-language drama film directed by Barada Prasanna Tripathy and produced by Debananda Panda and Sampurnananda Panda, with Anshuman and Rali Nanda in the lead roles.

p: A talented newcomer is given the hero's role by a director, but a jealous established star has him sent to prison on a false charge. On his release he finds that his son has grown up and is facing struggles much like his own. The son is competing in a reality dance show against the child of the man who framed him, and the father helps his son win.

Debananda Panda and Barada Prasanna Tripathy wrote the story, Tripathy the screenplay and Saranarabinda Ojha the dialogue. Dhrubananda Panda was cinematographer and Rajesh Dash editor. The large supporting cast included Ashwini Brahma, Mihir Das, Ratan Meher, Mahasweta Ray and Jayiram Samal. Hindi film actor Nana Patekar had been due to make a guest appearance, but this did not happen.

Mihir Mohanty composed the music, with lyrics by Bapu Goswami, Ajay Jena and Saranarabinda Ojha. The singers included Boni Chakraborty, Shibani Das, Goutam Ganguly, Ira Mohanty, Manas Pritam and Rati Satapathy.
The film was released on 13 May 2013.

Q116482549.lead: Niyati is an Odia-language crime thriller from 2023, the first film written and directed by Pinaki Srichandan. Sudhanshu Narayan Dash and Divya Mohanty play the leads.

p: Premalata Routray and Samaresh Routray were the producers. Srichandan supplied the story and screenplay as well as directing. Dash is cast as Mohan Pattnaik and Mohanty as Radhika Pattnaik; the supporting players include Samaresh Routray (ACP Tiger), Pupul Bhuyan (Sadhana) and Krishna Kar (Kalia Bhai). Akshaya Kumar Nayak handled cinematography and KD Sipun the editing.
Anurag Pattnaik composed every song in the film.
Niyati reached cinemas on 21 July 2023, and viewers and members of the Odia film industry praised its story and direction.
Srichandan received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Story for 2023 for this film.

facts: Odisha State Film Award for Best Story (2023)

Q15725032.lead: Mu Eka Tumara is a 2013 Odia-language romantic drama film directed by Susant Mani and produced by Sitaram Agrawal, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Archita Sahu. It is a remake of the 2003 Kannada film Chandra Chakori.

p: Two families gather at Virendra's farmhouse for four days of celebrations ahead of the wedding of his son Mahesh to Chitralekha, daughter of Pratap. Raju, a servant in the house who understands everything but never speaks, saves Chitra from danger. She learns that he is not actually mute but has chosen silence, and after discovering his past she falls in love with him and resolves to marry him instead of Mahesh; the reason for his silence and its consequences drive the rest of the story.

It was the seventh film to pair Sabyasachi Mishra and Archita Sahu. Sitaram Agrawal and Namita Agrawal produced it, the writing is credited to Sidharth with screenplay by Ranjit Patnaik, Abhiram Mishra was cinematographer and Sukumar Mani editor. Mihir Das played Virendra, Debasish Patra played Mahesh and Pruthiviraj Nayak played Pratap.

Bikash Das composed the music, with Biju Swain also credited. Sourin Bhatt, Namita Agrawal and Udit Narayan sang the songs, which include "Mun Eka Tumara", "Dine Ei Ranga", "Suna Jhia Mo Sathe", "Mo Luhara Ranga Aji" and "Maa Lo Mali".
Released in June 2013 with a running time of 140 minutes, the film grossed ₹4.16 crore.
At the Filmfare Awards East 2013 it won Best Odia Film, and also took the Odia awards for direction, best actor and best actress.

facts: Mun Eka Tumara; Dine Ei Ranga; Suna Jhia Mo Sathe

Q24905234.lead: Lubeidak (The Necklace) is a 1994 drama film in Odia and Desiya about the Bonda people, written by Ashok Mishra and produced by Sushanta Kumar Adhikari for Lopamudra Productions of Jeypore.

p: The film tells the story of Sania, a Bonda boy who won a national archery award; his achievement inspired the film's producer and writer. Its title is the Bonda word for a necklace. The film depicts the social and cultural life of the Bonda, who call themselves remo, meaning human being, and questions the outside view of them as wild and hostile to strangers, presenting them instead as people with abilities that need direction.

The direction is credited to Ashok Mishra and Padmalochan Das. It was described as the first film of its kind about the Bonda. Satya Narayan Adhikari composed the music and Niranjan Das was the cinematographer. The film runs 95 minutes.

Lubeidak won five state film awards in 1994: Padmalochan Das and Ashok Mishra shared the award for best director, Sushanta Kumar Adhikari received the Mohan Das Goswami Award for best producer of a feature film, Niranjan Das won for cinematography, and the film also won for sound recording and art direction.

Q5306368.lead: Dream Girl is a 2009 Odia-language film directed by Ashok Pati and produced by A. Ramesh Prasad of Prasad Productions, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Priya Choudhury. It is a remake of the Telugu film Bommarillu.

p: The film looks at a young man, his family and the gap between generations. His father, who once taught him to walk, has never let go of his hand, and even at 24 every choice in the son's life is made for him. Wanting to live on his own terms, he becomes determined to marry the girl he has chosen, and the film follows how far he succeeds.

Ashok Pati is credited as writer and Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue. Sitanshu Mahapatra was the cinematographer. Priya Choudhury began her acting career with this film. Mihir Das, Aparajita Mohanty, Bijay Mohanty and Jayiram Samal were among the supporting cast.

Prashant Padhi composed the music to lyrics by Arun Mantri and Nizam, with Tapu Mishra, Udit Narayan, Kumar Bapi and Krishna Beura singing. The songs include "Akhi Mora Khola Thai Kehi Jane", "Janha Shoichi Shoi Padile Tara", "Priyare Priyare Najare Najare" and "Sathire Sathire Pahili Pritire".
The film was released on 5 February 2009.

facts: Priyare Priyare Najare Najare; Sathire Sathire Pahili Pritire

Q4902124.lead: Bhukha is a 1989 Sambalpuri-language film produced and directed by Sabyasachi Mohapatra, based on Mangalu Charan Biswal's play of the same name and starring Sarat Pujari and Sadhu Meher.

p: The film depicts the hardships of the Bajnia Dombo community of western Odisha, traditionally drummers, and the damage done to them by the cultural dominance of a more powerful class. It shows how they hold on to their livelihood, culture and traditions in the face of oppression by the wealthy and the pressures of modern life.

Mohapatra made the film under the Kumar Productions banner. It is described as the first feature film made in the Sambalpuri language. The cast included Sarat Pujari, Sadhu Meher, Bijaya Pujari, Swati Roy, Chitta Pattnaik and Mantu Mahapatra.

Ramesh Kumar Mahananda composed the music, with Khiti Pathi Sahu also credited. The folk songs are performed on the dhol and mahuri used by the Bajnia drummers and reflect the festival traditions of western Odisha. They include "Phatai Khaili Bella Kukila Re", "Malli Phuti Mahakila" and "Subha Lagane Bara Kale Gamana Ho".

Bhukha won the International Jury Award at the Gijón International Film Festival in Spain in 1990, the first film from Odisha to receive it. It was also selected for the World Rural Film Festival at Aurillac, France.

facts: Bhukha, play by Mangalu Charan Biswal
International Jury Award, Gijón International Film Festival (1990)
Phatai Khaili Bella Kukila Re; Subha Lagane Bara Kale Gamana Ho

Q15723755.lead: Emiti Bi Prema Hue is a 2012 Odia-language romantic drama film directed by Nishikant Dalabehera, starring Sabyasachi Mishra, Riya Dey and Mihir Das.

p: Surya, a mafia don, lives with his wife Suchitra and his assistant Kiran. When his daughter Shibani is born, he makes Kiran's son Amar her companion, and the two eventually fall in love. On learning of it, Surya tries to have Amar killed and Shibani attempts to take her own life, after which Surya recognises his mistake and the couple are united.

Raman Kumar Sahu and Rajendra Narayan Rout produced the film under the Shiny Creations banner. Dalabehera wrote the screenplay from a story by Asit Das Mahapatra, and Amarjit Mohanty was the cinematographer. Mihir Das played Surya, Aparajita Mohanty played Suchitra, Asrumochan Mohanty played Kiran, and Lovely appeared in an item song.
Prasant Padhi composed the music, with lyrics by Mohit Chakraborty, Jatindra Pradhan, Panchanan Nayak, Arun Mohanty and Jiten Mohanty. The audio was launched at Hotel Presidency in Bhubaneswar.
The film was released on 10 February 2012 with a running time of 143 minutes and did average business at the box office.

At the 24th Orissa State Film Awards, Sabyasachi Mishra won Best Actor and Asrumochan Mohanty Best Supporting Actor. Aryan Misra was named Best Child Actor, and Mihir Das received the Special Jury Award.

Q4700343.lead: Akashe Ki Ranga Lagila is an Odia drama from 2009, directed by S. K. Muralidharan, with Anubhav Mohanty, Archita Sahu and Rali Nanda in the main roles. It remakes the 2008 Tamil film Mahesh, Saranya Matrum Palar.

p: Sitaram Agrawal made the film for Sarthak Music, sharing producer credit with Namita Agrawal and Raj Thorani. The story and screenplay are by Bijay Malla, with dialogue by Sudipta Nanda; R. Bhagat Singh was director of photography and Chandra Sekhar Mishra the editor. Mohanty is cast as Akash, Sahu as Barsha and Nanda as Chutki. The title is borrowed from "Aji Akashe Ki Ranga", a song in Sri Lokanath (1960).

Bikas Das composed the soundtrack. Mohit Chakraborty, Arun Mantri and Bijay Malla were among the lyricists, and Sricharan Mohanty, Karunakar, Udit Narayan, Nibedita, Padma, Pami and Suresh Wadkar among the singers.
The 164-minute film opened on 12 June 2009, became one of the year's biggest Odia hits and played in theatres for 100 days.
At the 2009 Odisha State Film Awards, Anubhav Mohanty was named Best Actor, and the film took the prizes for screenplay, editing and art direction.

facts: Song "Aji Akashe Ki Ranga", Sri Lokanath (1960)

Q6690531.lead: Love Dot Com is a 2009 Odia-language romantic film produced and directed by Rahat Quddusi, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Megha Ghosh. It is a remake of the 1991 Malayalam film Godfather.

p: Two rival families are headed by the characters played by Bijay Mohanty and Snigdha Mohanty. Raj, the only son of one, and Debajani, the daughter of the other, attend the same college and each pretends to fall in love to take revenge for their family. Over time the pretence becomes real, and they decide to marry.

Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue; the story and screenplay are credited to Quddusi in one account, while another credits the writing to Ramashankar and the screenplay to Rajani Ranjan. Tapas Jena is also named as co-director. Digvijay Singh was cinematographer and Chandra Sekhar Mishra editor. Sambhavana Seth appeared in an item number.
Prem Anand composed the music and Rajani Ranjan wrote the lyrics. The singers included Kumar Bapi, Sricharan Mohanty, Diptirekha Padhi, Bapi Lahiri, Tapu Mishra, Raj Nagendra, Pami and Manas Pritam.
The film was released on 21 September 2009.

Q23697739.lead: Pahada Ra Luha (Tears of the Mountain) is a 2015 Sambalpuri-language feature film written and directed by Sabyasachi Mohapatra, which won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia.

p: The film looks at the industrialisation of Koraput district and the displacement it caused among the Paraja tribal people. It also depicts the difficulties that large-scale mining and insurgent activity created for the communities of the Niyamgiri hills.

Shooting began in 1990 but was halted partway through because of financial and other difficulties. Work resumed in June 2015 with the original cast, after a gap of about 25 years. Mohapatra revised the storyline to suit present-day audiences and kept the footage already shot with performers who had died in the meantime. Filming took place in Koraput and Kalahandi districts. The finished film runs 77 minutes, with music by Ramesh Kumar and cinematography by Kumar Chodaganga.

At the 63rd National Film Awards the film was named Best Feature Film in Odia. It also received a jury award for best film at the Odisha State Film Awards and was named best Odia film at the Nashik International Film Festival.

facts: National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia (63rd National Film Awards)

Q7495618.lead: Shesha Drushti is a 1997 Odia-language film directed by Apurba Kishore Bir about a dying freedom fighter who is forced to pay a bribe to a government official to secure a job for his son.

p: Kedar Babu has been part of the freedom struggle since the Civil Disobedience Movement. Widowed early in his marriage, he raises his only son, Sangram, alone. Living in town in the house of the zamindar Surriyakant Singh, Sangram watches the moral decay of the feudal order and is left confused and torn. A final meeting with his dying father gives him a new outlook, as he sets out to fulfil the old man's last wish.

Bir wrote and photographed the film as well as directing it. Ramachandra Behera wrote the story. The National Film Development Corporation backed and distributed the film, and Kailash Kopikar is also credited as producer. Aseem Sinha edited the film, which runs 125 minutes.
The music was composed by Bhavdeep Jaipurwale.

The film received the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia in 1998. It was screened at the Singapore Film Festival, the International Film Festival of India (1998) and the Pyongyang International Film Festival (1998).

facts: National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia (1998)
IFFI 1998; Pyongyang International Film Festival 1998; Singapore Film Festival

Q6958289.lead: Naga Phasa is a 1977 Odia-language film directed and produced by Basant Nayak, with Shriram Panda, Prashanta Nanda, Malvika Roy, Banaja Mohanty, Bijay Mohanty and Mohammad Mohsin in leading roles.

p: The film was the first Odia feature from Brajaraj Movies, which also distributed it. Akshaya Mohanty is also credited as co-director alongside Nayak; Basanta Mahapatra wrote the story and Nayak the screenplay. Bijay Mohanty played the villain, and Jairam Samal, Guman Singh and Nari appeared in supporting parts. The film runs 169 minutes.

Akshaya Mohanty composed the score and wrote the lyrics for several songs; Rajanikanta Nayak and Debadas Chhotaray also contributed lyrics. The songs were sung by Mohanty, Trupti Das and Geeta Patnaik and include "Mo Kola To Jhulana", "Tik Tik Tik Ghanta Chale", "Gaadi Chale Pachhei Debi" and "Nadi Phere Sagaraku".

facts: Mo Kola To Jhulana; Tik Tik Tik Ghanta Chale; Bada Bedaradi Mo Naali Paan Raja

Q115248753.lead: Boura Hatabaksa: The Eternal Bond is an Odia-language family drama released in December 2022. Narayan Pati directed it from a story by Arati Pattajoshi.

p: The drama explores a mother's selfless love for her son, the closeness of a married couple and the emotional link between two generations.

Sanjay Das and Rosalin Das produced it for Chairosana Film Productions. Pati adapted the story into the screenplay and took the part of Raghunath himself; Lopamudra Mishra, Sabita Palei and Rajesh Panda complete the main cast, and Abhishek Sahoo, Binay Kumar Biswal and Ayush Bal appear as child actors. Biraja Prasanna Kar was behind the camera and Chandrasekhar Mishra edited. The budget was ₹80 lakh and the running time is 128 minutes.
Khiti Prakash Mahapatra scored the film, and Devdas Chhotray and Managobinda Barik supplied the lyrics. The soundtrack came out on 20 July 2022.
Its release was postponed more than once before it finally reached theatres on 30 December 2022.

Q27959594.lead: Tu Kahibu Na Mu is a 2016 Odia-language romantic drama film written and directed by Susant Mani and made by Tarang Cine Productions, starring Niharika Dash and Amlan Das.

p: The film was the fourth production of Tarang Cine Productions, and Jagi Mangat Panda, head of Odisha Television Limited, produced it. Mani wrote the story and screenplay, Harihar Mahapatra wrote the dialogue, Sitansu Mohapatra shot the film and Sukumar Mani edited it. Aparajita Mohanty and Mihir Das took supporting roles, with Papu Pom Pom, Akash Dasnayak and Jairam Samal also in the cast.
Niharika Dash, who had won the second season of the Tarang TV show Kie Heba Mo Heroine, made her Odia film debut in the lead role.
Goodly Rath composed the music, and Arun Mantri and Bapu Goswami wrote the lyrics. Amara Muzik acquired the music rights and released the soundtrack.
The film was released on 15 January 2016.

At the 28th Odisha State Film Awards, Goodly Rath was named Best Music Director and Shashank won Best Male Playback Singer. Niharika Dash received a best newcomer award at a ceremony organised by the Odisha Film Producers' Association.

facts: Odisha State Film Awards: Best Music Director, Best Male Playback Singer

Q7852475.lead: Tumaku Paruni Ta Bhuli is a 2007 Odia-language film directed by Chakradhar Sahu, starring Sunil Kumar, Anu Choudhury and Amelie Panda.

p: Sisters Anu and Ameli both love Sunil, who returns only Anu's feelings. Learning of her sister's love, Anu steps aside, pushes Sunil to marry Ameli, and herself marries Manoj, a local thug who goes on to abuse her and her son. When Sunil learns of her suffering he comes to help, and in the final confrontation Anu kills Manoj as he tries to kill Sunil.

Sahu produced the film with Rukmani Das and also edited it. Shankar Tripathy wrote the story, and Sahu and Ranjan Das wrote the dialogue. Dreamland Cine Crafts distributed the film. Manoj Mishra, Uttam Mohanty, Ashok Das and Rukmani were also in the cast.

Malay Mishra composed the music. Mohit Chakraborty, Bijay Malla, Jatindra Pradhan and Nirmal Nayak wrote the songs, which were sung by Kunal Ganjawala, Pankaj Jal, Kailash Kher, Abhijeet Majumdar and Ira Mohanty, among others.
The film won Best Director, Best Supporting Actor, Best Supporting Actress, Best Lyrics and a Special Jury award at the Orissa State Film Awards for 2006.

facts: Orissa State Film Awards: Best Director, Best Supporting Actor, Best Supporting Actress, Best Lyrics, Special Jury award

Q24555142.lead: Agastya is a 2016 Odia-language action thriller film directed by K. Muralikrishna and produced by Akshaya Kumar Parija, a remake of the 2014 Kannada film Ugramm, with Anubhav Mohanty in the title role.

p: The film was made by Akshaya Parija's production house and distributed by AA Films. It adapts the story of Ugramm, credited to Prashanth Neel, with Nirmal Nayak credited as writer of the Odia version. Akash Dasnayak played Suraj and Jhilik Bhattacharya played Neha, with Mihir Das as Rudra Pratap and Minaketan Das, Manoj Mishra, Prithviraj Pattnaik, Salil Mitra and Priyanka Pattnaik among the supporting cast. Chandrasekhar Mishra edited the film, which runs 160 minutes.

Prem Anand composed the five songs, with lyrics by Subrat Swain and Arun Mantri. They were sung by Human Sagar, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Satyajit, Ashutosh, Pragyan and child singer Aryan; Indian Idol Junior winner Ananya Sritam Nanda sang in an Odia film for the first time. Amara Muzik released the music.
The film opened on 12 June 2016, during the Raja festival. Sarthak TV bought its satellite rights for ₹4 crore, reported as a record sum for an Odia film.
Agastya is a remake of the Kannada film Ugramm (2014).

Q15724107.lead: Chha Mana Atha Guntha is a 1986 Odia-language feature film directed by Parbati Ghose, adapted from Fakir Mohan Senapati's novel of the same name (Six Acres and a Third).

p: The landlord Ramachandra Mangaraj covets the fertile plot owned by Bhagia and his wife Saria and schemes to take it from them. Having lost the land and their cow, Bhagia loses his mind and Saria dies after being beaten by the landlord. Haunted by the voice of the woman demanding her land and her cow, Mangaraj suffers and finally dies, paying for his deeds.

Ghose had announced the adaptation with her husband after completing Sansaar in 1971, but the project was delayed for more than a decade. When it was finally made, it was her first film as director, and she also produced it and played Saria. Bijay Mohanty played Bhagia and Sarat Pujari the landlord Mangaraj; Gloria Mohanty, Asim Basu, Sidhant Mohapatra, Niharika Sahu and Dukhiram Swain also appeared. Tapas Mukhopadhyay edited the film and Prafulla Kar composed the music.
The film was released on 30 November 1986, and both it and Ghose's work on it drew praise from critics.

facts: Chha Mana Atha Guntha, novel by Fakir Mohan Senapati

Q26225381.lead: Bye Bye Dubai is a 2016 Odia-language comedy drama film directed by Basanta Sahoo and produced by NRI businessman Akshaya Kumar Parija, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Archita Sahu.

p: The hero and heroine travel to Dubai, run into a series of predicaments there, and manage by their wits to return to their homeland.

Sahoo also wrote the screenplay, and Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue. Sabyasachi Mishra played Prem, Archita Sahu took the double role of Saina and Nisha, Buddhaditya Mohanty played Raj and Bijay Mohanty was cast as Prem's father. Filming took place in Hyderabad at Ramoji, in Odisha and in Dubai, where some song sequences were shot. Biraja Prasanna Kar was the cinematographer and Rajesh Dash the editor.
Bikash Das composed the songs, with Rajani Ranjan also credited for music direction. Pami, Tapu Mishra, Bibhu Kishore and Manas Pritam were among the singers, and Amara Muzik released the music.
The film opened on 2 September 2016, around Ganesh Puja. It fell short of box-office expectations, and a reviewer for Update Odisha dismissed it as a plotless and crass comedy.

Q15724331.lead: Dharitri is a 1973 Odia-language social satire drama directed by Nitai Palit and produced by Dhira Biswal, based on Amulya Kumari Patnaik's novel of the same name.

p: Girish Choudhury, a politician who poses as a social worker, arranges for his son Subhendu to marry Mamata, a girl from a poor family, to boost his public image. Subhendu rejects his wife and lives in town running a contracting business with his father's backing, while Girish's wife torments Mamata and demands dowry. Girish's other son, the rebellious Sudhir, stands up to his parents and brother and finally brings Subhendu and Mamata together.

The film was made and distributed by Progressive Films Productions. Dhira Biswal played Girish Choudhury, Sarat Pujari played Subhendu, Sriram Panda played Sudhir and Sandhya Acharya played Mamata, with Bhanumati Devi, Prashant Nanda, Dinabandhu Das and Anima Pedini in other roles. It was Sriram Panda's debut film. S. Swant was the cinematographer, Ramesh Joshi edited the film, and Upendra Kumar composed the music.
Dharitri was released on 30 March 1973.
At the 2nd Orissa State Film Awards in 1974 it won Best Film, and Nitai Palit was named Best Director.

facts: Dharitri, novel by Amulya Kumari Patnaik
Orissa State Film Awards: Best Film, Best Director (1974)

Q4829598.lead: Aw Aaakare Aa is a 2003 Odia-language film written, produced and directed by Subash Das that takes a critical look at the rigid, monotonous character of the modern education system.

p: Mini, a schoolteacher, tries to break away from conventional teaching methods, and her refusal to compromise damages her career and leads to repeated transfers between schools. Drawing comfort from memories of her own childhood, she finally quits and opens a school of her own with no walls and no regimentation.

Adyasha Mohapatra played Mini as a child and Dipti Panda played her as an adult; Debu Bose, Debi Das and Choudhury Jayaprakash Das were also in the cast. Jugal Debata shot the film and Gadadhar Puty edited it. Bidyadhar Sahu composed the music. The film, distributed by Om Films, runs 90 minutes.

It was released on 27 September 2003 and was shown at several national and international festivals, including the 13th Golden Elephant International Children's Film Festival and the children's section of an international film festival in Jamshedpur.
The film received the National Film Award for Best Odia Film in 2004. At the 2003 Orissa State Film Awards it won Best Film, Best Direction, Best Child Actress and Best Editing.

facts: National Film Award for Best Odia Film (2004); Orissa State Film Awards: Best Film, Best Direction, Best Child Actress, Best Editing

Q5098955.lead: Chilika Teerey is a 1977 Odia-language film directed by Biplab Roy Choudhury about exploited fisherfolk on the shores of Chilika Lake who rise up against the companies that cheat them.

p: Fishing villages near Chilika Lake are exploited by large fishing companies. Raghu, a young villager, leads the community against one such company, whose manager Sricharan tries to break their unity; as he attempts to flee, the villagers throw him into the lake. Barred from marrying Padma, the girl he loves, because she belongs to another caste, Raghu hands leadership of the struggle to Jadu and rows away across the lake with Padma in search of a new life.

Shyamghana Roy Choudhury produced the film and wrote its story, while Biplab Roy Choudhury wrote the screenplay and edited it as well as directing. Bijay Mohanty played Raghu and Tandra Roy played Padma; it was the first Odia film for both. Netrananda Misra played Sricharan and Hemanta Das played Jadu. Pintu Dasgupta was the cinematographer. The film was made under the Haragouri Films banner and runs 164 minutes.
Shantanu Mahapatra composed the music.
At the National Film Awards in 1978 the film received a certificate of merit as best Odia film.

facts: National Film Award certificate of merit for best Odia film (1978)
First Odia film of Bijay Mohanty and Tandra Roy

Q62514176.lead: Biju Babu is a 2019 Odia-language political action film written and directed by Debi Prasad Lenka and Vishal Mourya, with Anubhav Mohanty in the lead. It was the first Odia film produced by Nila Madhab Panda.

p: Mohanty's character, Babu, takes on the spread of fake news, drawing inspiration from the former Odisha chief minister Biju Patnaik. Despite rumours to the contrary, the film draws on Patnaik's ideals and is not a biopic of him.

Panda produced the film with Manav Rath, Barnali Rath and Anuj Tyagi under the Prakash Films and Eleeanora Images banners. Supriya Nayak played Ragini, and Chittaranjan Tripathy, Ashrumochan Mohanty and Prangyan Khuntia were also in the cast. Sandeep Sethi edited the film, which runs 162 minutes. Mourya described it as the costliest Odia film made up to that point. Its first motion poster came out on International Mother Language Day.

Prem Anand composed the soundtrack, released by Siddharth Music, with Human Sagar, Ananya Sritam Nanda and Diptirekha among the singers. For the song "Oye Ramji" he used the singa, a horn instrument from Dhenkanal.

The film opened on 29 March 2019. Because its release coincided with Mohanty's candidacy for the Biju Janata Dal in Kendrapara in the 2019 Lok Sabha election, it drew criticism over its possible political influence.

Q19891600.lead: Golapi Golapi is a 2014 Odia-language film directed by Susant Mani and produced by Sitaram Agrawal, starring Amlan Das and Riya Dey, with Siddhanta Mahapatra and Aparajita Mohanty in supporting roles.

p: Sidharth Agarwal wrote the story, Mani wrote the screenplay and edited the film, and Srikant Gautam wrote the dialogue. Amlan Das played Aditya and Riya Dey played Shweta, while Siddhanta Mahapatra appeared as the love guru Prem, Mihir Das as Aditya's father, Aparajita Mohanty as Shweta's mother and Jiban Panda as a lecturer. Sitansu Mohapatra was the cinematographer, and the film was made under the Sarthak Entertainment banner. It runs 162 minutes.

Bikash Das composed the music, with Srikant Gautam writing the lyrics. The male vocals were by Udit Narayan, Babul Supriyo, Krishna Beura and Vinod Rathod, and Nivedita sang the female parts. The seven tracks include the title song, "Sima Deingale", "Rangila Rangila" and "Jharaphula".
The film was released on 13 June 2014.

facts: Golapi Golapi; Sima Deingale; Rangila Rangila

Q20787997.lead: Manasi is a 1981 Odia-language romantic comedy film directed by Malay Mitra and produced by Jayant Kumar, starring Sriram Panda, Saudamini Misra, Tripura Misra and Swarup Naik.

p: Akash, who runs the business of his industrialist father Surendra Das, attends a function at the home of Seema with his engineer friend Prashant. Seema takes Akash for a driver and Prashant for Akash; her friend Surekha falls for Prashant, believing him to be Akash, while Seema falls for the supposed driver. Tension builds when Akash's family seek his marriage to Seema, until the mix-up is cleared and the true identities come out.

Bimal Sadhu wrote the story and Kumar Anand the dialogue, while Mitra wrote the screenplay. The film was made by Abhiyatrik Productions, with Ashu Dutt as cinematographer. Samuel Sahu played Surendra Das, Geeta Rao played Akash's mother, and Radha Panda and Shyamalendu Bhattacharjee were also in the cast. It runs 148 minutes.
Prafulla Kar composed the music. Gokulananda Parida and Kar wrote the lyrics, and Debashis Mahapatra and Kar were among the singers.
The film was released on 27 November 1981.

Q26857832.lead: Baby is a 2016 Odia-language drama film directed by K. Muralikrishna and produced by Pooja Bharlawala under Saurav Entertainment, a remake of the Tamil film Pichaikkaran starring Anubhav Mohanty and Jhilik Bhattacharya.

p: The plot revolves around a small child, and Mohanty plays a millionaire.

The film's mahurat was held at the Gadagadia temple in Cuttack on 31 July 2016. Muralikrishna wrote the screenplay with Aditya Raj Panigrahi, and Chinmay Das Pattnaik is credited as writer. Bengali actress Poulomi Das made her Odia film debut, and child actor Preeti Priyadarshini played the title role; Suresh Bal and Prithviraj were also in the cast. Pratap Chandra Rout was the cinematographer and D. Mani the editor. Some scenes were planned to be shot in Dubai as well as Odisha.

Prem Anand composed the songs to lyrics by Arun Mantri and Subrat Swain, with Krishna Beura, Ananya Sritam Nanda and Human Sagar among the singers.
