The title song and "Sun Zara" came out on 24 and 26 September 2016, promotional videos for "Askaa 40" and the title song followed, and Amara Muzik launched the full album on 1 October 2016.
The film was scheduled for release at Dussehra 2016 and opened on 7 October 2016.
Baby is a remake of the Tamil film Pichaikkaran.

Q25212073.lead: Dhauli Express is a 2007 Odia-language film written, directed and produced by Chittaranjan Tripathy, starring Samaresh Routray, Mihir Das, Siddhanta Mahapatra, Anu Choudhury and Aparajita Mohanty. It won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Film.

p: Dhauli, the ambitious son of the postman Dibakar Das, dreams of becoming a singer. Circumstances lead him to the criminal Jaga Bhai, and for the sake of money he is drawn into the world of crime.

The title comes from the train of the same name. Tripathy produced the film with Srinivash Routray and also composed its music, while Bharadwaj Panda wrote the dialogue. Samaresh Routray played Dhauli, Mihir Das his father, Aparajita Mohanty his mother, Siddhanta Mahapatra played Jaga Bhai and Anu Choudhury played Tila. Abhiram Mishra was the cinematographer and Sushant Mani the editor. The budget was about ₹1.24 crore.
The film was released on 16 May 2007.
It received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Film for 2007.

facts: Odisha State Film Award for Best Film (2007)

Q7067765.lead: Nua Bou is a 1962 Odia-language film directed by Prabhat Mukherjee that depicts the social and cultural life of a village in rural India.

p: Sura Babu lives with his wife Parbati, his younger brother Raju and his son Debi; Parbati dotes on Raju more than on her own child. When Parbati falls ill, Raju fetches Lord Jagannath's prasad from Puri, and she recovers under the care of the village doctor Das. Her mother and sister Champa then come to stay, and the mother's efforts to turn Parbati against Raju fail because Champa sides with him. A string of misunderstandings over who is to marry Champa ends with her wedding to Rabi, the young doctor she loves.

Dhira Biswal and Ramakrishna Tripathy produced the film, which was distributed by Panchasakha Films. Sarat Pujari, Prashant Nanda, Manimala, Dhira Biswal and Leela Dulali headed the cast, with Padma Biswas also appearing.

Balakrishna Das composed the music and Narasingha Mahapatra wrote the lyrics. Sikandar Alam, Shipra Bose and Swarnaprava Sadangi are named as singers, and "Jaare Mana Doli Udi Jaa" is one of its songs.
The film was released on 9 March 1962.
It received a National Film Award certificate of merit for best feature film in Oriya, listed under 1961.

facts: National Film Award certificate of merit, best feature film in Oriya

Q20926172.lead: Deewana Deewani is a 2013 Odia-language romantic film directed by Ashok Pati, starring Babushaan Mohanty and Madhumita Chakraborty. It is a remake of the 2012 Bengali film Khokababu.

p: Pramod Kumar Swain wrote the story and produced the film with Siba Prasad Das under the Mahadev Films banner. Pati wrote the screenplay and Rajani Ranjan the dialogue. Bengali actress Madhumita Chakraborty made her screen debut in the film. Mihir Das, Minaketan Das, Debashis Patra, Pintu Nanda, Runu Parija and Jiban Panda were also in the cast. Sitansu Mohapatra shot the film and Sushant Mani edited it.
Prasant Padhi composed the music. Bapu Goswami, Arun Mantri and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics, and the songs were sung by Sangram Mohanty, Human Sagar, Nivedita, Tariq Aziz and Jagruti, among others.
The film was released on 24 March 2013.
It is a remake of Khokababu (2012), a Bengali film starring Dev.

Q21334837.lead: Ishq Tu Hi Tu is a 2015 Odia-language drama film directed by Tapas Sargharia and made by Tarang Cine Productions, starring Arindam Roy and Elina Samantray, with Aparajita Mohanty and Mihir Das in supporting roles.

p: The film tells a love story across communities, set against the communal riots of 1991 in the Dhamnagar area of Bhadrak district.

Sargharia wrote the story, and Bharadwaj Panda is credited with the screenplay and dialogue. Elina Samantray was chosen for the heroine's role through the Tarang TV programme Kie Heba Mo Heroine and made her Odia film debut. Arindam Roy played Swadhin Mohapatra and Samantray played Simran, with Mihir Das, Aparajita Mohanty, Minaketan Das, Pragyan Khatua and Samaresh Routray in other roles. Rabindra Behera shot the film and Sukumar Mani edited it.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music.
The film was released on 14 January 2015.

Q15724742.lead: Bandhu Mohanty is a 1977 Odia-language mythological film written and directed by Nitai Palit, with Gobind Tej in the title role of a poor devotee of Lord Jagannath.

p: Bandhu Mohanty, a devotee of Jagannath, supports his wife and children by begging. When famine strikes his village he takes the family to Puri, where they still find nothing to eat. At his wife's urging he prays for help, and Jagannath answers by asking the goddess Lakshmi to provide for them.

Dhiren Patnaik produced the film under the Priya Darshini Films banner, and Gopal Chhotray wrote the dialogue. Shanti Swarup Misra played Jagannath, Dhira Biswal played King Gajapati and Anita Das played Lakshmi, with Banaja Mohanty, Lila Dulali, Bhim Singh and Biren Routray also in the cast. Madhu Banerjee edited the film, which runs 172 minutes.
Prafulla Kar composed the music and wrote lyrics along with Brundaban Jena. Vani Jairam, S. Janaki and Chitta Jena sang the songs, which include "Hata Chhada Chhada Mora Nagara" and "Na Ja Sajani".
Released on 6 June 1977, the film was a commercial success.
At the 1977 Odisha State Film Awards it won Best Film, Best Director for Palit, Best Actor for Gobind Tej and Best Music Director for Kar.

facts: Hata Chhada Chhada Mora Nagara; Na Ja Sajani
Odisha State Film Awards: Best Film, Best Director, Best Actor, Best Music Director

Q26444418.lead: Bhaina Kana Kala Se is a 2016 Odia-language film written, produced and directed by Sanjay Nayak that deals with the question of the casting couch in the Odia film industry.

p: The film follows an actor's struggle to reach the top of his profession and the controversies he becomes entangled in on the way.

The film was first titled Excuse Me Kana Kala Se before being renamed. Comedian Balakrushna Nayak played the lead role of Dipu Ding Dong opposite Tamanna Vyas, and Uttam Mohanty appeared as himself. Kuna Tripathy, Chandan Kar, Jina Samal, Premanjan Parida, Biju Badajena, Biren Mishra and Pradyumna Lenka were also in the cast. Pradeep was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor.

Prem Anand composed the music. The lyricists included Arun Mantri, Madhusudan Das, Subrat Sahu and Debidutta Mohanty, and Human Sagar, Sohini Mishra, Sanju, Diptirekha Padhi and Satyajit Pradhan were among the singers.
Distributed by Tarang Cine Productions, the film was released on 16 September 2016.

Q6963330.lead: Nandini I Love U is a 2008 Odia-language film written and directed by Ashok Pati, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra, Buddhaditya Mohanty and Krisha. It was the first production of Anama Charana Sahoo.

p: Sahoo produced the film under the Laxmi Puja banner, which also distributed it. Pati wrote the story and screenplay, and Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue. Siddhanta Mahapatra played Sri Ram and Buddhaditya Mohanty played Jeet, while Krisha, an actress known from Hindi films, took the female lead as Nandini. Ajit Das, Snigdha Mohanty, Anita Das, Bobby Mishra, Pintu Nanda, Mamuni Mishra and Roja were also in the cast. Sitansu Mohapatra shot the film and Chandra Sekhar Mishra edited it.

Prasant Padhi composed the music. Basantaraj Samal, Debadas Chhotray, Nirmal Nayak and Padhi wrote the lyrics, and the singers included Kumar Bapi, Bibhu Kishore, Tapu Mishra, Arabinda Sadangi and Sailabhama Mahapatra.

facts: First film produced by Anama Charana Sahoo

Q61126370.lead: Nimki is a 2019 Odia-language political film directed by Susant Mani, with Varsha Priyadarshini in the title role. Its full Odia title is Nimki – Nimpur ru Naveen Niwas.

p: The film traces a girl's journey from the village of Nimpur to Naveen Niwas in Bhubaneswar. She meets a fresh obstacle at every step but keeps going and finds a way past each one.

Priyadarshini wrote the story and produced the film with Kuna Mangaraj. Mani wrote the screenplay and Dilip Choudhury the dialogue, while Subhranshu Das was the cinematographer. Ashrumochan Mohanty, Chittaranjan Tripathy, Trupti Sinha and Pragyan Khatua were in the supporting cast, and Anubhav Mohanty made a cameo appearance as himself.

Prem Anand composed the music, released by Zee Music, with lyrics by Basantaraj Samal and Subrat Swain. Human Sagar, Ananya Sritam Nanda, Sabisesh, Ashutosh, Antara Chakraborty and Sohini Mishra were among the singers. The songs were launched at the Bali Jatra ground in Cuttack.
The film was released in January 2019. Hindi film actress Jaya Bachchan attended its premiere.

Q21283042.lead: Nai Separi Kanaka Gori is a 2013 Odia-language film directed by Pankaj Padhi and produced by Ajay Mohanty, with Partha Sarathi Ray and Rali Nanda in the lead roles.

p: The film was made under the Ananya production banner. Ajay Mohanty, who produced it, also wrote the story, co-composed the music and played a small role as a postman, while Deba Prasad Das wrote the dialogue. Partha Sarathi Ray played Abinash and Rali Nanda played Kanak, with Roji as Nilima and Mihir Das, Aparajita Mohanty, Debu Bose, Jairam Samal, Minaketan, Samaresh Routray and Pritiraj Satpathy among the large supporting cast. Gagarin Mishra was the cinematographer and Manas Ranjan Patra the editor.

Mahendra Acharya and Ajay Mohanty composed the music. Sachi Mohanty, Bijay Malla, Mahendra Acharya, Raja Ardhendu Sekhar Mohanty and Gita Khuntia wrote the songs, and the singers included Trupti Das, Srikanta Das, Tapu Mishra, Pami, Arabinda, Chitrabandhu Mohanty, Ajay Mohanty and Mahendra Acharya.
The film was released on 1 March 2013.

At the 24th Odisha State Film Awards, given by the state culture department, Gagarin Mishra received the award for best cinematography (the Pramod Pati award) and Bijay Malla was named best lyricist. The film also won the award for best sound recording.

facts: Odisha State Film Awards: Best Cinematography, Best Lyricist, Best Sound Recording

Q18170451.lead: Something Something 2 is a 2014 Odia-language comedy drama film directed by Sudhakar Vasanth and produced by Anuprash Mohanty, starring Anubhav Mohanty and Barsha Priyadarshini. It is a sequel to Something Something (2012).

p: The film was made under the Vishnupriya Arts and Graphics banner. It was the first sequel produced in the Odia film industry, and its story is a remake of the 2007 Kannada film Milana. Nirmal Nayak wrote the dialogue and lyrics. Anubhav Mohanty played Shree Ram and Barsha Priyadarshini took the double role of Shayira Banu and Bhumi; Anjana, Ashwini Tripathy, Guddu, Salil Mitra and Dhirendra Nath were also in the cast. R. Bhagat Singh shot the film and Chandrasekhar Mishra edited it. It runs 140 minutes.

Prem Anand composed the music. The singers were Udit Narayan, Human Sagar, Krishna Beura, Abhijeet Bhattacharya, DJ Papu and Ira Mohanty; Bhattacharya sang the title track and Human Sagar sang "Prema Hei Jae Re".
The film opened on 14 June 2014 and had an average run at the box office.
It is a remake of the Kannada film Milana (2007).

facts: Prema Hei Jae Re; title track

Q7810866.lead: To Bina Bhala Lagena is a 2008 Odia-language romantic film directed by Jyoti Das and produced by Prasant Jena, starring Sabyasachi Mishra, Rupali and Pupinder Singh.

p: Deepak meets Jyoti, and their romance grows through violin lessons and the times Deepak steps in to protect her. When he discovers that his friend Suraj also loves Jyoti, Deepak tries to give her up for the sake of his friend's happiness.

Jena wrote the story, Das wrote the screenplay and Prakash Baral the dialogue. Sabyasachi Mishra played Deepak, Rupali played Jyoti and Pupinder Singh played Suraj, with Prabhas Acharya, Anita Das, Mihir Das, Minaketan, Pintu Nanda, Saheb Singh and George Tiadi in other roles. Magi Nagesh was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor. Richa Cine Lab distributed the film.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music.

Q15724603.lead: Pua Mora Bhola Sankara is a 1996 Odia-language film directed by Hara Patnaik, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra, Rachana Banerjee and Mihir Das. It succeeded at the box office and brought Mihir Das wide popularity.

p: Patnaik wrote the story and also played Ajay Patnaik, while Subodh Pattanaik wrote the screenplay and dialogue. Pradyumna Lenka produced the film, though Sailabala Lenka is also listed as producer. Siddhanta Mahapatra played Kumar Rai and Rachana Banerjee played Geetha, with her lines dubbed by Rakhee Dash. Mihir Das was cast as Sankar, a naive servant, opposite Priyanka Mohapatra, who made her film debut as Shanti. Debu Bose, Jairam Samal, Uttam Mohanty and Aparajita Mohanty were also in the cast.

Rama Murthy choreographed the fight scenes and Chandi Parija was associate director. Dilip Ray handled the cinematography and Deben Misra the editing. Das later said in an interview that he considered this his best work.

Swarup Nayak and Subash Ram composed the music. Songs include "Daiba Hatare Manisa Jibana" sung by Subhash Ram, "Tutamu Tutamu Tanana" by Bibhu Das and Gita Das, "E Mani E Sanga Bayata" by Debasish Mohapatra, "Jay Jay Bhola Sankara" by Subas Das and "Sukha Dukha Duniara" by Trupti Das.
The film was released on 12 June 1996 and was a box-office success.

facts: Jay Jay Bhola Sankara; Daiba Hatare Manisa Jibana; Sukha Dukha Duniara

Q6732539.lead: Magunira Shagada (Maguni's Bullock Cart) is an Odia-language film directed by Prafulla Mohanty and produced by the National Film Development Corporation, based on a story by Godabarisha Mohapatra. It won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia.

p: Maguni makes his living carrying people and goods in his bullock cart, but the new minibuses outdo him and he struggles to cope with the changing times. After his wife falls ill and dies, Maguni loses his mind and eventually dies.

Mohanty wrote the screenplay himself. Ashru Mochan Mohanty played Maguni, with Jaya Seal, Dhirendra Basa, Nilamani Behera and Manorama Mohanty also in the cast. Bharat Nerkar and Brundaban Swain were the cinematographers and Madan Mohan Prasad edited the film, which runs 95 minutes.

Amarendra Mohanty composed the music, with Shirsananda Das Kanungo credited as lyricist; he is also credited with the dialogue. The playback singers were Suresh Wadkar, Amayendra Mohanty, Sweta Pandit, Rudra Mohanty and Arati Goswami.
The film was shown in the Indian Panorama section of the International Film Festival of India in 2002. At the National Film Awards announced in 2002 it was named Best Feature Film in Oriya for 2001.

facts: National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Oriya

Q26444232.lead: Tora Dine Ku Mora Dine is an Odia action comedy-drama from 2016, directed by Sudhanshu Mohan Sahu. A remake of the Tamil film Drohi, it stars Arindam Roy, Amlan Das, Riya Dey and Sheetal Patra.

p: Sitaram Agrawal and Pradyumna Lenka produced the film. Its story is credited to Siddharth Agarwal, with screenplay and dialogue by Ranjit Pattnaik. Built around two male and two female leads, it was the first film to pair Arindam Roy with Amlan Das. The supporting cast included Mihir Das, Pradyumna Lenka, Ratan Meher, Asit Pati, Satyaki Mishra, Kirti Mohanty and Pragyan Khatua. S. Ramesh shot the film and Rajesh Dash edited it.
Malaya Mishra was the composer, and the songs were written by Mohit Chakraborty, Bapu Goswami and Arun Mantri. The soundtrack was released on 1 October 2016.
It reached cinemas in October 2016, drew negative reviews and was declared a flop.
The film is based on the Tamil film Drohi.

Q4784163.lead: Aranya Rodan (Cry in the Wilderness) is an Odia-language film directed by Biplab Ray Chaudhuri, based on the novel Ashanta Aranya by Satakadi Hota. It was selected for the Indian Panorama at the International Film Festival of India.

p: Kalyani, a journalist, investigates the rape and killing of a tribal woman by a policeman in rural Orissa. She adopts the dead woman's child and becomes drawn into the lives of the tribal community, while her own marriage runs into difficulties.

Prasan Prusti produced the film, which was made with financial support from the film development corporation. Ray Chaudhuri wrote the screenplay and edited the film, and Bijay Mishra wrote the dialogue. Priyambada Ray played Kalyani, with Sarat Pujari, Lalatendu Rath, Raicharan Das and M. Ramdas in other roles. Raju Mishra was the cinematographer. Gouri Pictures distributed the 90-minute film.
Shantanu Mahapatra composed the music, Laxman Marandi wrote the lyrics and Sarojini Hembrum was the playback singer.
The film was chosen for the Indian Panorama section of the International Film Festival of India.

facts: Ashanta Aranya, novel by Satakadi Hota

Q16246762.lead: Aranyaka (A Trip into the Jungle) is a 1994 drama film directed by Apurba Kishore Bir, based on Manoj Das's short story of the same name, starring Sarat Pujari, Navni Parihar, Sanjana Kapoor and Mohan Gokhale.

p: Set in rural Odisha, the film follows a former local ruler who arranges a hunt for his invited guests, an outing that goes badly wrong. It brings out the conflict between the ruling class and the indigenous people of the area.

The film was produced by the NFDC and Doordarshan. Bir wrote the film and was also its cinematographer, while Supabitra Babul wrote the dialogue and Dilip Panda edited it. Manoj Das's story was first published in 1960. Sarat Pujari played Raja Saheb, Mohan Gokhale and Navni Parihar played Mr and Mrs Mitty, and Sanjana Kapoor played Elina; Lalatendu Rath, Sunil Singh, Subrata Mahapatra, Jagyaseni Jena, Ajay Nath, Pritikrushna Mohanty and Ashim Basu completed the cast. Accounts differ on its language, which is given both as Hindi and as Odia.
The music was composed by Bhavdeep Jaipurwale.
Released in 1994, the film was praised at the national level.

facts: Aranyaka, short story by Manoj Das

Q15725076.lead: Rakta Golapa is a 1977 Odia-language romantic tragedy directed by Bhimeswar Rao, starring Suresh Misra, Banaja Mohanty, Sriram Panda, Radha Panda and Ramesh Panigrahi.

p: College sweethearts Sharat and Mira are separated when Sharat's family forces him to marry Sneha, who herself loves Ajay. A heartbroken Mira disappears, and Sharat, unable to bear her fate, loses his balance and turns against his wife. When Sneha becomes pregnant, suspicion falls on her until Ajay steps in to clear up the matter, and Sharat and Mira are finally reunited.

Bibhuti Mishra and Sashanka Sekhar Mishra produced the film under the Banani Films banner. Bijay Kumar Nanda wrote the story and Rao the screenplay. Suresh Misra played Sharat, Banaja Mohanty played Mira, Sriram Panda played Ajay and Vatchla played Sneha. Benjamin was the cinematographer and J. Narasimha Rao the editor; the film runs 166 minutes.
The music marked the debut of Dhananjay Satpathy as both composer and singer.
Distributed by Udaya Shashi Pictures, the film failed at the box office, as it was released mainly in smaller towns rather than in the major cinemas.

facts: Debut of Dhananjay Satpathy as composer and singer

Q39390003.lead: Mun Khanti Odia Jhia is a 2017 Odia-language film written and directed by Avtar Singh, with Elina Samantray in the lead role alongside newcomer Ranbir and Siddhanta Mahapatra.

p: The film tells the story of the struggles of a village schoolteacher's daughter.

Rajendra Singh Bhurji and Avtar Singh Bhurji produced the film. Singh wrote the story and screenplay, and Satyanarayan Sahu wrote the dialogue. Elina Samantray played the lead, with debutant Ranbir and Siddhanta Mahapatra as the heroes; Papu Pom Pom, Manoj Pattnaik, Manisha Mishra, Mamuni Mishra, Jiban Panda, Salil Mitra and Narayan Pati were among the supporting cast. Ranjan was the cinematographer.

Baidyanath Dash, Gopal Biswal and Manas Kumar composed the music, recorded by Amara Muzik. The singers included Asima Panda, Human Sagar, Tapu Mishra, Sricharan, Sailabhama, Tariq, Papu Pom Pom and Sanju Mohanty. The songs were launched at Bhanja Kala Mandap, at an event attended by guests including Pratibha Ray, Iti Samanta and Akshaya Parija.
The film opened on 8 September 2017, the same day as the Odia film Bhairav, and both did good business.
Ranbir was named best debut actor at the 12th Film and Television Award Show Time in 2018.

facts: Best debut actor (Ranbir), Film and Television Award Show Time 2018

Q28833707.lead: Katha Deli Matha Chhuin is a 2017 Odia-language film directed by Sailendra Parida and produced by Sridhar Martha, with Riya Dey as the heroine and Abhishek Rath and Aman as two parallel heroes.

p: At its heart is a grandfather who raises an orphaned child in the hope of securing a good future for him. Lekha falls for Jeet, and when their families ignore their feelings the pair run away to the city, where the wealthy Pratap Babu gives them shelter. Jeet struggles to earn a living until Pratap Babu's grandson Krish offers him money to start a business, on condition that Lekha becomes his forever; the film follows where that bargain of love for money leads.

Sabita Martha wrote the story and Bapu Goswami is credited as writer. The mahurat took place on 10 November 2016 at a Durga Puja pandal in Jharpada. Aman, who had earlier worked on stage and television, made his Odia film debut as Jeet. Abhishek Rath played Krish, Riya Dey played Lekha and Bijay Mohanty played Pratap Babu, with Papu Pom Pom, Mihir Das, Pintu Nanda, Salil Mitra and Chandini Jena also in the cast. Dhrubananda Panda was the cinematographer.
Prem Anand composed the music, and Arun Mantri, Saranarabinda Ojha and Subrat Swain wrote the lyrics.
The film was released on 24 February 2017.

Q6480383.lead: Lalita is a 1949 Odia-language folklore film directed by Kalyan Gupta. It was the second film made in Odia, coming thirteen years after the first, Sita Bibaha.

p: King Indradyumna has completed a temple at Puri but cannot find the living deity Nila Madhaba, and sends messengers out to look for him. The Brahmin Bidyapati reaches a Savara village deep in the forest, where he learns that the Savara chief Biswabasu secretly worships the deity in a hidden cave. Feigning love, Bidyapati marries Biswabasu's daughter Lalita, who persuades her father to take her husband to the cave; but when Bidyapati plans to carry the deity to Puri, it vanishes.

The film was made by Great Eastern Movieton, with Gourendra Pratap Singhdeo as producer. Kali Charan Pattanayak wrote the story, dialogue and songs and composed the music. Lokanatha Mishra played Bidyapati and Uma Banerjee played Lalita, with Sumati Devi as Maya, Pankaj Nanda as Biswabasu and Damodar Das as Indradyumna. Uma Banerjee was the wife of Makhanlal Banerjee, the lead actor of Sita Bibaha. Prakash Digpal was the cinematographer and B. Chatterjee the editor. The budget was a little under one lakh rupees.

facts: Second Odia-language film, after Sita Bibaha (1936)

Q45036360.lead: Mu Premi Mu Pagala is a 2011 Odia-language film directed by Sudhanshu Mohan Sahu, which introduced Harihar Das and Anubha Sourya in the lead roles.

p: Lutu Mohanty, Pratap Sahu and Baishali Pratap Sahu produced the film. Pratibharani Mohanty wrote the story, Sahu wrote the screenplay and Rajani Ranjan the dialogue. Both leads, Harihar Das and Anubha Sourya, made their Odia film debuts here. Bijay Mohanty, Pushpa Panda, Mihir Das, Usasi Misra, Minaketan, Lawrence Behera, Munna Khan, Harihar Mahapatra and Biju Badajena were among the large supporting cast, with Om Prabhat, Sai Siddharth Mohanty and Chandan Mohanty as child actors. Dhrubananda Panda was the cinematographer and Biswaranjan Pradhan the editor.

Prasant Padhi composed the music. The lyricists included Nimai Mohanty, Nirmal Nayak, Arun Mantri, Basantaraj Samal, Jiten and Lutu Mohanty, and Tapu Mishra, Kumar Bapi, Krishna and Manas Pritam were among the singers.
The film was released on 12 August 2011.

facts: Debut film of Harihar Das and Anubha Sourya

Q7490669.lead: Shatru Sanghar is a 2009 Odia-language film written and directed by Sudhanshu Sahu and produced by Harsha Wardhan Lal, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra, Akash Dasnayak and Rahul Dev.

p: Ajay Patnaik wants to become a boxing champion and goes to Visakhapatnam to train. On his return he learns that his elder brother Bijay has been missing for a month, and neither his own search nor a police complaint turns him up. When Bijay is found dead, Ajay is accused of the killing; he breaks out of jail with his friends and takes revenge on Nagabhushan and Nilambar, the men responsible.

The film was the second from Pine Cask, which also distributed it, following the failure of Anubhav Mohanty's Mahanayak. Mohanty was first signed as the hero but withdrew because of scheduling problems. Akash Dasnayak played Ajay and Siddhanta Mahapatra played Bijay, with Shriya Jha as Deepa, Samapika Debnath as Jyoti, Rahul Dev as Rahul, Ashru Mochan Mohanty as Nagabhushan, Bijay Mohanty as Nilambar Das and Mihir Das as a police DCP. Shankar Tripathy is also credited as a writer.
Sarat Nayak composed the music.
Released in February 2009, the film made a profit and was the second-highest-grossing Odia film of the year.

Q18129091.lead: Pagala Karichu Tu is a 2014 Odia-language film directed by Susant Mani and produced by Sitaram Agrawal under the Sarthak banner, with Amlan Das, Riya Dey and Siddhanta Mahapatra in leading roles.

p: S. Narasingha wrote the story, while Susant Mani handled the screenplay and editing in addition to directing. Srikant Gautam contributed the dialogue and the song lyrics, and Sitanshu Mahapatra was the cinematographer. Amlan Das played Shiba, Riya Dey played Shardha and Siddhanta Mahapatra appeared as Bagha, with Mihir Das, Priyanka Mahapatra, Bijay Mohanty, Satyaki Mishra and Harihara Mahapatra in the supporting cast.

Bikash Das composed the soundtrack to lyrics by Srikant Gautam. The playback singers included Udit Narayan, Kumar Sanu, Babul Supriyo, Vinod Rathore, Namita Agarwal and Dibya Das. Ankita Bhowmick featured in an item number and Papu Sahoo in a DJ song.
The film was released on 1 October 2014.

Q6353131.lead: Kalishankar is a 2007 Odia-language film written, directed, scored and edited by Prashanta Nanda and produced by Suchitra Sahu.

p: Prashanta Nanda was responsible for the story, screenplay and dialogue as well as direction, music and editing. The cinematography was handled by Niranjan Das and V. Prabhakar. The lead cast comprised Siddhanta Mahapatra, Anu Choudhury, Anubhav Mohanty, Meghna Mishra, Arindam Roy and Swastika Mukherjee, supported by Bijay Mohanty, Mihir Das, Ashish Vidyarthi, Snigdha Mohanty and others.
Nanda composed the songs and wrote their lyrics himself. Subas Das, Pankaj Jal and T. Souri were among the playback singers.
The film was released on 23 January 2007.

Q5978210.lead: I Love You is a 2004 Odia-language romantic action film directed by Hara Patnaik and produced by Sanjay Nayak, starring Anubhav Mohanty and Namrata Thapa in their debut roles.

p: The film is a remake of the 1999 Tamil film Thullatha Manamum Thullum. Anubhav Mohanty plays Sanjay and Namrata Thapa plays Gita.

Sanjay Nayak produced the film and also provided the story. Hara Patnaik wrote the screenplay and directed, while Subodh Patnaik wrote the dialogue. Niranjan Das was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra edited the film. Both leads, Anubhav Mohanty and the Mumbai-based model Namrata Thapa, made their Odia film debuts here. The supporting cast included Bijay Mohanty, Anita Das, Pintu Nanda, Hara Patnaik and Tandra Ray. The budget was 28 lakh rupees.
Swaroop Nayak composed the music and wrote the songs. The playback singers included Kumar Bapi, Tapu Mishra, Ira Mohanty and T. Souri.
Sanjay Nayak began making a second part, I Love You 2, with Jyoti Ranjan Nayak and Jhilik Bhattacharya in the lead roles.

Q50825281.lead: Emiti Bi Heipare is a 2017 Odia-language film directed by Rajib Mohanty and produced by Rabi Narayan Das, featuring Sasikant Barik and Rupali Dibedi in the lead roles.

p: Chinmayee Mohanty wrote the story, Subhajit Ananda the dialogue, and Rajib Mohanty the screenplay. Pradeep Sahu was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei edited the film. The principal actors Sasikant, Rupali, Deepak and Suman all made their Odia film debuts with this project. Director Sangram Biswal also took an acting role, alongside Padmalochan, Sulochana Bhuyan, Harihar Swain, Prahlad Patra, Dilip Panda, Sandhya Satapathy and others.

Baidyanath Dash composed the score. The lyrics came from Bapu Goswami, Panchanan Nayak and Arun Mantri, and the songs were sung by Human Sagar, Tariq Aziz, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Satyajit, Anjali Das, Asima Panda, Arpita Choudhury, Jagruti Mishra and Suchismita.
The film opened across Odisha on 17 September 2017, the day of Vishwakarma Puja.

Q134699793.lead: Ananta is a 2025 Odia-language film directed by Sabyasachi Mohapatra, adapted from Fakir Mohan Senapati's short story Randipua Ananta, with Sabyasachi Mishra and Suryamayee Mohapatra in the lead roles.

p: The film draws on Fakir Mohan Senapati's short story Randipua Ananta. Sabyasachi Mishra plays the title character Ananta, Suryamayee Mohapatra plays Gehli, and Jyotirmayee Panda appears as Ananta's mother.

Nabin Bhandari, Suraj Mohanta and actress Archita Sahu produced the film as a joint venture of Amar Studio, Shivansh Production and Sabyasachi Films. Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue, Huentsang Mohapatra was the cinematographer, and Kumar Mohapatra and Lambodar Takri edited it. Kuna Tripathy, Prithviraj Nayak, Tapas Sargharia and Sushila Nayak were among the supporting cast. The project was originally titled Randipua Ananta before being renamed Ananta during production.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak. Sricharan Mohanty, Karunakar Sethi, Sanju Mohanty, Antara Chakraborty, Subasish Mahakud, James and Anusaya Nath were among the singers.
The Censor Board passed the film with a U certificate and no cuts. Distributed by Rajshree Films, it reached theatres on 12 June 2025, during the Raja festival.

facts: Randipua Ananta, short story by Fakir Mohan Senapati

Q4802248.lead: Arundhati is a 1967 Odia-language film directed by Prafulla Sengupta and produced by Dhiren Patnaik, starring Minati Mishra, Braja and Sarat Pujari. It won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia.

p: Arundhati and her lover Manoj perform with an Odissi dance troupe. During a crowded show, a man named Biswajeet insists that Arundhati is his wife Madhumati, who had in fact been killed in a train accident; Manoj, suspicious, abandons Arundhati. Biswajeet eventually learns that the two women were twin sisters, tracks Manoj down at a small railway station and convinces him to return to Arundhati.

The film was made under the Kanakprabha Productions banner. Gurukrushna Goswami and Prafulla Sengupta are credited as writers, Bishu Chakravarty was the cinematographer and Sukumar Sengupta the editor. Minati Mishra played the double role of Arundhati and Madhumati, Sarat Pujari played Manoj and Braja played Biswajeet. The running time is 145 minutes.
Shantanu Mahapatra composed the music.
The film received the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia for 1967, the President's silver medal.

facts: National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia (1967)

Q15725345.lead: Sindura Bindu is a 1976 Odia-language romantic film written and directed by Sisir Misra, his first film as a director. It stars Sriram Panda, Tripura Misra, Prashant Nanda and Sujata Anand.

p: The film follows a pair of childhood sweethearts who are separated and finally brought back together. Its story was drawn from Sarapancha Pua, a novel by Chintamani Jena.

Mahalaxmi Films produced the picture, with Kedar Guru, Lokanath Guru, B. K. Agrawal, S. K. Agrawal and L. G. Patra credited as producers. Dilip Dutta shot the film and Madan Gupte edited it. Sriram Panda played Akash, Tripura Misra played Sandhya, Prashant Nanda played Ajay, Sujata Anand played Anita and Ajit Das played Pratap, while producer Kedar Guru appeared as Sadhu Baba. The film runs 153 minutes.

Prafulla Kar composed the soundtrack. The film includes the bhajan Keun Nama Dhari Dakibu Tumaku, written by Kalicharan Pattnaik and originally composed for All India Radio, sung by Pranab Patnaik under Kar's direction.
The film succeeded at the box office and ran to silver jubilee weeks in several theatres.
At the 1976 Orissa State Film Awards, Pranab Patnaik won Best Playback Singer (Male).

facts: Sarapancha Pua, novel by Chintamani Jena

Q35482409.lead: Sapanara Pathe Pathe is a 2017 Odia-language film directed by Sushant Mani and produced by Sitaram Agrawal under the Sarthak Music banner, starring Amlan Das and newcomer Sanmira Nagesh.

p: According to director Sushant Mani, the story was based on a real incident. Siddhanta Mahapatra plays a police officer.

It was the 21st film from Sarthak. Siddharth Agrawal wrote the story and Dr. Nirmal Nayak the dialogue, while Sushant Mani handled screenplay and editing alongside direction. Amlan Das returned to the Sarthak banner after Tora Dine Ku Mora Dine; his co-star Sanmira Nagesh, who had earlier worked as a child artist, made her debut as a heroine. Manoj Pattnaik, Prithiraj, Chitta Tripathy and Tiki Tripathy were among the supporting cast.
The music was directed by Asad Nizam, son of the late lyricist Nizam. Arun Mantri, Nirmal Nayak and Tapu Nayak wrote the songs, which were sung by Nibedita, Saurin Bhatt, Sangram and Satyajit.
Initially planned for a Raja festival release, the film instead came out on 25 August 2017, the day of Ganesh Puja.

Q39075077.lead: Daha Balunga is a 2013 Odia-language drama film directed by Sudhakar Vasanth and produced by Pupinder Singh, starring Babushaan Mohanty, with Jackie Shroff in his first Odia film.

p: Made as an Odia–Bengali bilingual, the film was shot in Mumbai and Thailand. Bapu Goswami wrote the dialogue, Ramesh Krishna and K. V. Ramana handled the cinematography, and Ashok Sharma edited it. Babushaan played Omkar Mohanty, Sonia Sarkar Dey played Shalini and Sanjana Mitra played Ruby. Hindi actor Jackie Shroff, cast as Arun Singh Deo, made his Odia debut, with Bijay Mohanty, Tandra Ray, Aparajita Mohanty, Pintu Nanda, Pragyan Khatua, Saroj Das and Trupti Sinha in supporting roles. The running time is 169 minutes.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music. The songs include Aakhi Kholile Tu, Anta 26, Daha Balunga, Jaithili Badi Pataku and Maula Maula.
The film was released on 12 July 2013.

facts: Aakhi Kholile Tu; Daha Balunga; Maula Maula

Q4900735.lead: Bhai Bhauja is a 1967 Odia-language film directed by Sarathi, based on a story by Rama Chandra Misra about a farmer and a cruel landlord.

p: The farmer Manu Pradhani, his wife Dukhi and his brother Bhaiga struggle to win back land Manu has mortgaged to the landlord, or Sahukar. When the Sahukar's son has his own father killed and pins the crime on Manu, Manu is jailed for ten years while Dukhi and Bhaiga raise her son Prakash. On release, Manu believes a rumour about Dukhi and Bhaiga and stays in the city as a servant in a judge's household, where Prakash has fallen for the judge's daughter Sabitri; Manu's eventual return home clears his doubts and the family accepts the marriage.

Sarat Pujari played Prakash, Rama Chandra Pratihari played Manu, Samuel Sahu (Babi) played Bhaiga, Manimala played Dukhi and Minati Mishra played Sabitri. Priyanath Mishra (Pira) and Sagar Kumar Das also appeared. The budget was ₹7.1 lakh.
The film was released in 1967 and distributed by Rupanjali.

Q117218738.lead: Delivery Boy is a 2023 Odia-language film directed by Ashwini Tripathy and produced by Jyoti Ranjan Mohanty, based on the life of a delivery boy named Durga Prasad Nayak.

p: Jyoti Ranjan Mohanty wrote the story as well as producing, Deepak Jena wrote the dialogue and Ashwini Tripathy wrote the screenplay. Deepak Kumar was the cinematographer and Manas Kumar Sahu the editor. The leads were Sailendra Samantray, Priyambada Swain, Buddhaditya Mohanty and Suryamayee Mohapatra, with Choudhury Bikash Das, Jiban Panda, Shakti Baral, Saroj Das, Pupul Bhuyan and Guddu among the supporting cast.

Baidyanath Dash, together with Nabs and Saroj, composed the music. Nirmal Nayak, Arun Mantri, Surya Mohapatra and Ustad wrote the lyrics, and Satyajit Pradhan, Human Sagar, Asima Panda and Ruturaj Mohanty were among the singers. The songs were released on 10 January 2023.

Before release, the Government of Odisha announced that the film would be exempt from entertainment tax. It premiered at Maharaja Hall in Cuttack in the presence of Governor Ganeshi Lal and opened in theatres on 7 April 2023.

facts: Life of delivery boy Durga Prasad Nayak

Q15526724.lead: Badhu Nuhen Mu Bandhu is a 2013 Odia-language film directed by Sailendra Parida and produced by Kirti Ranjan Choudhury, starring Prabhas and newcomer Bidusmita.

p: Sailendra Parida wrote the screenplay as well as directing, and Chinmay Das Pattnaik wrote the dialogue. Rajkumar and Bijay Pati shot the film. Alongside the two leads, the cast included Munna Khan, Uttam Mohanty, Pintu Nanda, Hara Patnaik and Snigdha Mohanty.

Manmath Mishra composed the music, with lyrics by Arun Mantri, Jitendra Pradhan and Nizam. The soundtrack includes Megha Malhara, the title song, Aee Ghara Sri Mandira, Sathire Sathire Khojuchi and Muna To Chora Prema.
The film was released on 1 January 2013 and distributed by RCL Entertainment.

facts: Megha Malhara; Aee Ghara Sri Mandira; Sathire Sathire Khojuchi

Q26787383.lead: Love Pain Kuch Bhi Karega is a 2016 Odia-language romantic drama film directed by Ashok Pati for Tarang Cine Productions, starring Babushaan Mohanty and newcomer Supriya Nayak.

p: Sanju and Parinita are in love, but her father opposes the match and has arranged her marriage to the captain of a cricket team. To win her, Sanju must take on the captain in a cricket match.

Pooja Bharalawala produced the film under the Tarang Cine Productions banner. It was the first time Babushaan and Supriya Nayak worked together. The cricket sequence was filmed in front of about 500 onlookers at the Gopinathpur ground in Parichhak village near Begunia in Khordha district. The title song features Babushaan dancing with ten foreign dancers. Mihir Das and Ushasi Mishra appeared in supporting roles, along with Trupti Sinha, Jiban Panda and Salil Mitra.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics.
The film was released on 7 October 2016, during the Durga Puja season.

Q109519709.lead: Charitra is a 2020 Odia-language film directed by Sisir Kumar Sahu and Peenakee Singh, produced by Manjari TV and P.S. Motion Pictures.

p: Government officer Abhishek Pattnaik is posted to Koraput along with his newly married wife Madhu. While settling into their quarters, Madhu comes across a diary kept by Kalpana, wife of the previous occupant, officer Sudhir Panigrahi, recording her loneliness, hopes and relationships. The entries stop partway through, and Madhu becomes determined to learn how Kalpana's story ended.

Amit Kumar Das and Peenakee Singh wrote the screenplay, and Sisir Kumar Sahu wrote the dialogue. Deepak Kumar was the cinematographer and Rashmi Ranjan Dash the editor. Gargi Mohanty played Kalpana Panigrahi, Ananya Mishra played Madhusmita Pattnaik and Partha Sarathi Ray played Abhishek Pattnaik, with Hara Rath and Dipanwit Dash Mohapatra also in the cast.

Kasturi Kaushik and Ishan Sharma composed the music. Lyrics were written by Sumit Panda, Kasturi Kaushik, Gyan Ranjan Kar and Tapu Nayak, and the singers included Lavita Lobo, Pooja Venkat, Gaurav Anand and Kuldeep Pattnaik.
The film opened in theatres on 25 December 2020 and premiered on Manjari TV on 25 April 2021.

Q4682886.lead: Adina Megha (The Unwanted Cloud) is a 1970 Odia-language film directed by Amit Maitra for Chhayabani Pratisthan, starring Prashanta Nanda, Jharana Das and Dukhiram Swain.

p: Babulal Doshi produced the film. Its story came from Kuntala Kumari Acharya and the screenplay from Gopal Chhotray, with Sailaja Chatterjee as cinematographer. Prashanta Nanda played Suresh Mahapatra and Jharana Das played Champak Das, while Dukhiram Swain, Bhanumati Devi, Samuel Sahu, Sandhya, Geeta Rao, Niranjan Satapathy and Sagar Das filled other roles. The film runs 154 minutes.

Balakrushna Das composed the songs to lyrics by Kalicharan Pattnaik, Narayan Prasad Singh, Baikunthanath Mohanty and Gouranga Samantray. The playback singers were Sikandar Alam, Shipra Bose, Geeta Pattnaik, Trupti Das, Nirmala Mishra and Akshaya Mohanty. Songs include Boulo Ki Kahibi Nua Bhaujanka Katha, Ei Bhara Janharati, Ei Amari Gaan and Jibane Sapana Jete Sabu Sata.
The film received the State Film Award for Best Story.

facts: Boulo Ki Kahibi Nua Bhaujanka Katha; Ei Bhara Janharati

Q55467299.lead: Aama Ghara Aama Sansara is a 1991 Odia-language film written and directed by Ravi Kinagi, starring Uttam Mohanty and Prajakta Kulkarni.

p: Ashok Kumar Lenka, Sailabala Lenka and Gyan Pattnaik produced the film. Kinagi wrote both the story and the screenplay, while Sirshananda Das Kanungo wrote the dialogue. Ranjan Kinagi was the cinematographer and Deben Mishra the editor. The large cast included Bijay Mohanty, Ajit Das, Sujata Anand, Debu Bose, Hara Patnaik, Dukhiram Swain, Suresh Bal, Raimohan Parida and Binayak Mishra.
Akshaya Mohanty composed the music and also wrote lyrics, alongside Sirshananda Das Kanungo. Kavita Krishnamurthy, Udit Narayan and Anuradha Paudwal were among the singers.
The film was released on 6 June 1991.

Q55502217.lead: Bastra Harana is a 1991 Odia-language film written and directed by Sisir Mishra and produced by Rabindra Sahu, with an ensemble cast led by Bijay Mohanty, Mahasweta Ray and Uttam Mohanty.

p: Sisir Mishra wrote the story and screenplay, and Sirshananda Das Kanungo wrote the dialogue. Dilip Ray handled the cinematography and Dilip Satam the editing. Besides the leads, the cast included Sriram Panda, Aparajita Mohanty, Mihir Das, Hara Patnaik, Asit Pati, Sujata Anand, Dhira Biswal and many others; producer Rabindra Sahu also appeared. The film runs 172 minutes.

The music was by Prafulla Kar, Jugal Kishore and Tilak Raj, with lyrics by Sirshananda Das Kanungo and Nizam. Mohammed Aziz, Anjana Das, Kavita Krishnamurthy, Debashish Mahapatra, Tilak Raj, Vinod Sehgal, Jayashree Shivaram and Mehul Kumar sang the songs.
The film was released on 16 May 1991.

Q112625240.lead: Mr. Kanheiya is a 2022 Odia-language film directed by Ramesh Rout and produced by Sitaram Agrawal under the Sarthak Movies banner, starring Papu Pam Pam and Jhilik Bhattacharya.

p: Ramesh Rout wrote the screenplay and Deepak Jena the dialogue. Pratap Rout was the cinematographer and Rajesh Dash the editor. Pradyumna Lenka, Tukuna, Rajib, Pratibha Panda and Anjana Dash appeared in supporting roles.
Baidyanath Dash composed the music and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics. The singers included Papu Pam Pam himself, Human Sagar, Asima Panda, Debesh Pati and Diptirekha Padhi.
The film was released on 4 February 2022.

Q141129804.lead: Yogini is a 2024 Odia-language film written and directed by Biyot Projna Tripathy, who also co-produced it with Susmita Das and appears in the cast.

p: Tripathy wrote both the story and the screenplay. Haraprasad Das served as narrator, Dhrubananda Panda as cinematographer and Rajesh Dash as editor. The large cast included Tripathy along with Anubha Sourya, Shahrukh Nag, Pradeep Nag, Sudha Rani Dash, Rashmipriya Lenka and Monalisa Beuria. The film runs 87 minutes.
Omprakash Mohanty composed the music, Haraprasad Das wrote the songs, and Susmita Das sang them.
The film had a special release in Delhi on 20 January 2024.

Q7810868.lead: To Bina Mo Kahani Adha is an Odia-language film from 2007, directed by Sanjay Nayak. Anubhav Mohanty and Archita Sahu play the leads, with Jairam Samal in support.

p: A wealthy young man goes to a village to meet the bride his parents have picked, but the girl falsely accuses him and he is sent to prison. After his release he woos and finally marries her, then admits on their fourth night that he had been manipulating her to take revenge. The film ends on a happy note.

The producers were Purna Chandra Das and Bijay Kumar Patra, and Omm Movies made and distributed the film. Samba photographed it and Siba Prasad Mohanty edited it. Anubhav Mohanty plays Amar and Archita Sahu plays Gauri; Ajit Das, Anita Das, Arabinda, Biju Badajena, Debjani, Jeena Samal, Raimohan Parida, Jairam Samal and Chakradhar Jena make up the supporting cast.

Santiraj Khosla was the composer. The lyricists were Bijay Malla, Dr. Nirmal Nayak, Arun Mantri and Basantaraj Samal, and the songs were sung by Nibedita, Abhijit, Babul Supriyo, Pankaj Jal, Sanju and Swayam.

Q43379014.lead: Family No.1 is a 2011 Odia-language film directed by Nishikant Dalabehera and produced by Rabindra Panda and Ashok Sahu, starring Deepak Barik and Madhusmita.

p: Akash, an orphan raised only by his maternal uncle, falls in love with his office colleague Meghna, also an orphan, who hopes to marry into a complete family. To win her, Akash assembles a make-believe family, casting a drunken former jatra actor as his father, a thief as his mother and a young woman as his sister. Meghna eventually discovers the deception and decides to leave, but the stand-in relatives apologise and the group of orphans comes together as a real family.

Bijayalaxmi Panda wrote the story, Rajani Ranjan the dialogue and Dalabehera the screenplay. Amarjit Mohanty was the cinematographer and Ajit Mandhual the editor. Choudhury Jayaprakash Das played the uncle, with Choudhury Bikash Das, Biju Badajena, Niranjan Pati and Bijaya Patnaik among the supporting cast.
Goodly Rath composed the music, and Bapu Goswami and Deepak Jena wrote the songs.
The film was released on 27 May 2011.

Q42044841.lead: Rumku Jhumana is a 2013 Odia-language film directed by Tapas Sargharia and produced by Ramachandra Pradhan, with Harihara Mahapatra in the lead role.

p: Harihara Mahapatra wrote the story and dialogue in addition to starring, while Tapas Sargharia wrote the screenplay. Rabindra Behera was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor. Bhumika Dash made her screen debut in the film as a child artist, one of several children in the cast. The adult cast included Mihir Das, Priya Choudhury, Hara Patnaik, Akash Dasnayak, Choudhury Bikash Das, Runu Parija, Hadu, Rabi Mishra, Pintu Nanda and Snigdha Mohanty.

Baidyanath Dash composed the music to lyrics by Nirmal Nayak, Arun Mantri and Surya Mohapatra. The singers included Jolly Mukherjee, Pamela Jain, Sohini, Arati Mishra, Ratikant Satapathy, Sanju, Mohammed Irfan and Bishnu Mohan Kabi.
The film was released on 19 April 2013.

Q15725357.lead: Suna Panjuri is a 1995 Odia-language romantic drama film directed by Ravi Kinagi, a remake of the Bengali film Amar Sangee, starring Bijay Mohanty, Siddhanta Mahapatra, Indira Krishnan and Debu Bose.

p: Subas Rout and Somya Ranjan Raut produced the film under Shree Ganesh Productions, and Maruti Films International distributed it. Shankar Kinagi wrote the story, Ravi Kinagi the screenplay and Sirshananda Das Kanungo the dialogue and lyrics. Ranjan Kinagi and Samba Shiva Rao were the cinematographers and Vishwanath Rao the editor. The cast also included Namrata Das, Hara Patnaik, Jayiram Samal and Sasmita Pradhan as Rupa. The film runs 165 minutes.

Amarendra Mohanty composed the songs, which became hits in 1995, Puchuki Gali in particular. The soundtrack features Sonu Nigam, Kavita Krishnamurthy, Prasenjit Mohanty and Suresh Wadkar, with tracks including Moro Mana Udijayere, Sunara Chadei, Puchuki Gali, Tumaku Pai Mu and Soija Mama.

facts: Puchuki Gali; Sunara Chadei; Moro Mana Udijayere

Q28946403.lead: Dil Ka Raja is a 2017 Odia-language romantic film directed by Dillip Panda and produced by Rabindra Panda, built around a love triangle with Jyoti Ranjan Nayak in the lead.

p: The film centres on a love triangle and deals with love, sacrifice, keeping others happy and hiding one's own pain. Jyoti Ranjan Nayak plays the hero, with Pinky Priyadarshini and Deepika as the two heroines.

Suragini Pathak wrote the story and Rajani Ranjan the dialogue. It was Jyoti Ranjan Nayak's third film, after Dele Dhara Katha Sare and Nijhum Ratira Sathi. Debasmita Panda was originally cast in Deepika's role and attended the launch ceremony, but was later replaced. Mihir Das, Uttam Mohanty, Pradyumna Lenka and Papu Pam Pam had supporting roles; actor Babu Pradhan and his son Papu, making his debut, also appeared. Sudhakar Vasanth choreographed the dances.
Baidyanath Dash directed the music. Pulak and Anjali Dutta got their first break as playback singers in this film.
The film was released for Valentine's Day 2017.

Q41273746.lead: One Way Traffic is a 2014 Odia-language film directed by Suresh Pattnaik and produced by Srikant Gautam, starring Sambhav Mansingh and Tapasya Tripathy.

p: Srikant Gautam wrote the story, screenplay, dialogue and songs besides producing, and also appeared on screen. Suresh Pattnaik edited the film as well as directing it, and Prafulla Sahu was the cinematographer. The supporting cast included Sritam Das, Meghna Mishra, Sasanka Basu Mallick, Ilu Banerjee, Pushpa Panda, Hara Rath and Ankita Bhowmick.
Brahma Kumbhar composed the music. Kumar Bapi, Krishna Beura, Debananda, Pankaj Jal, Ira Mohanty, Abhay Mulia, Asima Panda, Ritu Pathak, Vinod Rathod and Sanju sang the songs.
The film was released on 12 December 2014.

Q29317968.lead: Jabardast Premika is a 2016 Odia-language film directed by Raju Sarabaiah and produced by Arun Pandian and Kavitha Pandian, starring Babushaan and Jhilik Bhattacharya.

p: Raju Sarabaiah, a director from South India, wrote the screenplay and directed, while Dr. Nirmal Nayak wrote the dialogue. P. Selvakumar was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor. Tamil actor Siddharth made his Odia film debut here. Mihir Das, Aparajita Mohanty, Pushpa Panda, Saroj Das, Priyanka Mahapatra, Debu Pattnaik, Harihara Mahapatra and Ankita Rout were also in the cast.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak and Nizam. Saurin Bhatt, Satyajit Pradhan, Anjali Mishra, Suman, Abhijit Majumdar, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Babushaan and Human Sagar sang the songs, which were released on 26 March 2016.
The film was released on 13 April 2016.

Q33554059.lead: Gunda is a 2016 Odia-language film written and directed by Subhashish Pati and produced by N. K. Nayak, with Siddhanta Mahapatra in the lead role.

p: Raju and Minu are caught up in an MMS scandal, and Minu lies in court to protect Raju before taking poison. Raju, who loves her deeply, sets out to uncover the truth behind her lie, leaves home and becomes a gangster in the process, and finally tracks down the real culprit.

Subhashish Pati wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue. Dhrubananda Panda was the cinematographer. Nikita and Himika played the heroines opposite Siddhanta Mahapatra, with Mihir Das, Pragyan Khatua, Jhansi Rani, Mamuni Mishra, Rock Patra, Bapi Ray and Subhransu Nayak in other roles.

Deepak Kumar Behera composed the music and also wrote lyrics, alongside Bapu Goswami, Mohit Chakraborty and Nizam. Manas Pritam, Liza Patra, Snehalata Behera, T. Souri, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Ratikant Satapathy and Tapu Mishra were among the singers.
The film was released on 18 November 2016.

Q6786328.lead: Mate Bohu Kari Nei Jaa is a 2011 Odia-language film directed by Bikash Das about Odia families who hold on to their culture despite living abroad for decades.

p: The film follows two expatriate Odia families settled in Bangkok and the ways they keep their traditions and culture alive.

Gyana Ranjan Priyadarshan produced the film for Darshan Music and Films. Jyotsna Misra Priyadarshan wrote the story, Bikash Das the screenplay and Rajani Ranjan the dialogue. Rabindra Behera was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor. The cast included Siddhanta Mahapatra, Dipen, Aishwarya Pathi, Malabika, Mihir Das, Raza Murad, Aparajita Mohanty, Hadu, Pushpa Panda and Asrumochan Mohanty.

Bikash Sukla composed the music to lyrics by Nizam, Bijay Malla and Panchanan Nayak. Ira Mohanty, Abhijit, Suresh Wadkar and Kavita Krishnamurthy sang the songs, which include Agana Tora Dakuchi Mate, Ame Kana Tama Pain Fit Nuhan Ki, Ete Bhala Paa Nahin, Gotie Chithi Dui Thikana, Thiri Thiri Chori Chori and Hasibara Michha Abhinaya.
The film was released on 3 April 2011.

Q34963459.lead: Tiger is a 2016 Odia-language film directed by Dillip Panda and produced by Mukesh Kapoor and Ramesh Barik, starring Amlan Das and Deepika.

p: The story was written by Saroj Kapoor, Mukesh Kapoor and Dipti Barik, with dialogue by Dr. Rajani Ranjan and screenplay by the director. Prasad was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor. The supporting cast included Smruti Sinha, Bijay Mohanty, Saroj Das, Bhupati Tripathy, Pradyumna Lenka, Salil Mitra, Anita Das, Babu Pradhan, Pratibha Panda and Minaketan.

Goodly Rath composed the music to lyrics by Nirmal Nayak, Bapu Goswami, Rajani Ranjan and Debidatta Mohanty. The singers included Tapu Mishra, Goodly Rath, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Nabhya, Asima Panda, R. S. Kumar and Sohini Mishra.
The film was released on 20 May 2016.

Q20782280.lead: Dharini, also known as Whispers of Change, is a 2002 Odia-language drama film directed by Susant Misra about four women in a traditional middle-class household.

p: Four women in one conservative family each seek dignity in their own way. Sarala, who cannot have children because of an illness passed on by her unfaithful husband, feels trapped; Kamala refuses her husband's demand for yet another abortion and walks out; the widowed Shweta, treated as a burden, is urged to build a respectable life of her own; and the socially active Nandini longs for independence away from home.

Susant Misra wrote the film with Ashima Chiber, who also wrote the dialogue and co-wrote the screenplay; R. N. Trivedi is also credited as a writer. Jugal Debata was the cinematographer and Ravi Patnaik the editor. The cast included Kirti Kulhari, Rachna Shah, Avni Vasa, Jyoti Dogra, Richa Nayyar, Subrat Dutta, Ashok Chakraborty, Robin Das and Sudhanshu Pandey.
Sujeet Chaubey and Akshaya Mohanty composed the music.

Q109430907.lead: Sahid Raghu Sardar is a 2021 Odia-language historical film directed by Rajeev Mohanty and produced by Biswanath Pattnaik, based on the life of Odia freedom fighter Raghunath Pattnaik.

p: The film centres on Raghunath Pattnaik, who was a young man in Kolkata when British rulers began oppressing Indians. He spoke out against the British there, and in time both Odia migrants and local Bengali residents joined his movement, after which he became known as Raghu Sardar.

Biswanath Pattnaik wrote the story as well as producing, Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue and Rajeev Mohanty the screenplay. Niranjan Dash was the cinematographer and Soumya Sobhan Nayak the editor. Debasish Patra played Raghu Sardar opposite Kavya Kiran, with Rudra Panigrahi, Jina Samal, Lipsa Mishra, Akshay Bastia, Pintu Nanda, Pushpa Panda, Debu Pattnaik and Sudhakar Vasanth in supporting parts; the director also appeared. Filming took place in Odisha and West Bengal.
Bikash Sukla composed the music, with lyrics by Bijay Malla and Ranjan Dash. Bishnu Mohan Kabi sang the title song.
The film was released on 16 August 2021.

Q114804727.lead: Premare Risk Hela Mote Ishq is a 2022 Odia-language film directed by K. Muralikrishna and produced by Sanjay Kumar Patra and Umesh Sahu, starring Sailendra Samantray and Divya Mohanty.

p: Rajani Ranjan wrote the story and dialogue, and K. Muralikrishna the screenplay. Narendra Gaud was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor. Ratan Meher, Rabi Mishra, Anjana Mishra, Tulu Choudhury, Chintamani Biswal and Suryan Rath were in the supporting cast, and Pritiraj Satapathy made a guest appearance.

Sanjay Patra and Situ Rath composed the music, with lyrics by Satyananda Nayak, Sanjay Kumar Patra and MBJ Bunty. The singers included Krishna Beura, Lipsa Mahapatra, Asima Panda, Kuldeep Pattnaik, Arpita Choudhury, Human Sagar, Satyajit Pradhan, Nabhya Jyoti and Sushant Mishra. The songs came out on 11 March 2022.

Unable to secure cinema halls in Odisha, the makers released the film on 9 October 2022 in a government community hall at Odagaon in Nayagarh district, which seated 300 and ran three shows a day. It reached theatres later.

Q41803398.lead: A.C.P. Sagarika is a 2013 Odia-language film written and directed by Biranchi Narayan Panda and produced by Dillip Das, with Archita Sahu in the lead role.

p: Biranchi Narayan Panda wrote the story and screenplay, and Ananta Ojha the dialogue. Abhiram Mishra was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor. Papu Pam Pam, Prakruti Mishra, Mihir Das, Priyanka Mahapatra, Jayiram Samal, Biju Badajena, Pritiraj Satapathy, Choudhury Bikash Das and Ashok Das were in the cast, and Abhishek Rath made his Odia film debut. Singer Tapu Mishra appeared on screen in one song.

Manmath Mishra composed the music and wrote lyrics along with Basantaraj Samal and Bapu Goswami. Abhijit Mishra, Tapu Mishra, Krishna Mishra, Sailabhama, Udit Narayan and Vinod Rathod were among the singers.
The film was released on 8 March 2013.

Q33097325.lead: Mitha Mitha is a 2017 Odia-language film written and directed by lyricist Srikant Gautam and produced by Sanjay Kumar Rout and Trilochan Das, starring Jyoti Ranjan Nayak and a group of newcomers.

p: Srikant Gautam wrote the story, screenplay, dialogue and songs, and also acted in the film. To find his leads, he ran a programme called Mitha Mitha Jodi on ETV Odia in 2015; Jyoti and Ankita won the contest, and Rajesh, Shraddha and Sambhav from the same show were also cast. Prakruti Mishra joined the five newcomers as a heroine, and Smita Mohanty, Harihara Mahapatra, Asrumochan Mohanty and Hara Rath took other roles. Chandan Majumdar was the cinematographer. Although it was Jyoti Ranjan Nayak's first film, delays meant three of his other films had already come out before it was released.
Malay Mishra composed the music to Srikant Gautam's lyrics. Ira Mohanty, Sangram, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Human Sagar, Satyajit and Asima Panda sang the songs.
The film was released on 26 May 2017.
Smita Mohanty won Best Supporting Actress at the 12th Film and Television Award Show Time 2018.

facts: Through the ETV Odia show Mitha Mitha Jodi (2015)

Q6930622.lead: Mu Sapanara Soudagar is a 2008 Odia-language film directed by Sanjay Nayak and produced by Sarada Prasanna Panda, starring Arindam Roy, Archita Sahu and Sabyasachi Mishra.

p: The film takes its inspiration from the Hindi film Agni Sakshi, itself based on the English-language film Sleeping with the Enemy. Sabyasachi Mishra plays Omm, the title character and the film's antagonist, while Archita Sahu plays Shriya, who is loved by both Omm and Chandan (Arindam Roy).

Sarada Prasanna Panda wrote the story, Sanjay Nayak the screenplay and Nirmal Nayak the dialogue. Ramani Ranjan Das was the cinematographer and Sanjay Nayak also edited the film. It was the first film to pair Sabyasachi Mishra and Archita Sahu. Ajit Das played Omm's father, Bina Moharana his mother and Akhila Patnaik played Raja, with Mihir Das in a guest appearance. The film runs about 2 hours 38 minutes.
Santiraj Khosla composed the music.
Following Dhana Re Rakhibu Sapatha Mora, it was the second release from Subham Films and came out at the time of the Raja festival. It ran for over 100 days in Odisha theatres.

facts: Agni Sakshi (Hindi); Sleeping with the Enemy

Q41840397.lead: Jagannatha Dhama Puri is a 2017 Odia-language film produced, written and directed by Narayan Ghadei, starring Debadutta Sahu and Ritika Rath.

p: Narayan Ghadei wrote the story and screenplay, and Satya Prakash wrote the dialogue. Pradeep Sahu was the cinematographer and Jyoti Prakash the editor. Bijay Mohanty, Devi Barik, Choudhury Bikash Das, Debu Brahma, Kumud Tripathy and Priya Sundar Mishra were among the supporting cast.
Bidyut Ray and Himanshu Sekhar Mohanty composed the music to lyrics by Sachi Mohanty and Samit. The singers included Kumar Bapi, Gautam Giri, Anu Singh, Abhipsa, Saurav and S. K. Pattnaik.
The censor board awarded the film a U certificate. It was scheduled for release on 8 December 2017.

Q7653804.lead: Swapna Sagara is an Odia-language film from 1983 that Prashanta Nanda wrote, produced and directed, with music by Akshaya Mohanty. It holds the distinction of being the first Odia film made in 70 mm.

p: As a nine-year-old, Nanda had read Baliraja, a novel by Kahnucharan Mohanty; it later served as the inspiration for his screenplay. The film was shot by Bhanu Kumar and Rajan Kinagi. Nanda also took a role, sharing the screen with Sriram Panda, Mahasweta Ray, Dukhiram Swain, Anita Das, Bijay Mohanty, Hemant Das, Dhira Biswal, Jayiram Samal, Pira Mishra and Shyamalendu.
Akshaya Mohanty's songs for the film include "Chithi Mora Tiki Chadhei", "Sei Dipa Achi Sei Phoola", "Ae Panire Panire", "Batoi Bhai", "Sikari Sikari" and "Sagara Sagara Sagara Buku Re".

facts: Chithi Mora Tiki Chadhei; Sei Dipa Achi Sei Phoola

Q140315309.lead: Delivery Boy 2 is a 2025 Odia-language film directed by Ashwini Tripathy and produced by Jyoti Ranjan Mohanty, starring Archita Sahu, Sailendra Samantray and Buddhaditya Mohanty.

p: Jyoti Ranjan Mohanty wrote the story, Deepak Jena the dialogue and Ashwini Tripathy the screenplay. Ishwar Barik was the cinematographer and Manas Kumar Sahu the editor. The cast also included Priyambada Swain, Pupinder Singh, Sritam Das, Santu Nijee, Alisha Samantray, Shakti Baral, Sushant Das Mohapatra and Bhumika Dash.

Baidyanath Dash composed the music, with lyrics by Arun Mantri and Nirmal Nayak. The singers included Human Sagar, Mantu Chhuria, Ananya Sritam Nanda, Antara Chakraborty, Asima Panda and Chiragdeep Panda.
The film opened in theatres on 27 August 2025.

Q140667863.lead: Ghamaghot is a 2025 Odia-language film written and directed by Raja D and produced by Kaushik Das, starring Sailendra Samantray, Krishna Kar and Deepak Parida.

p: Raja D wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue. Biswajit Kuldi was the cinematographer, and Smruti Ranjan Mishra and Biswa Ranjan Subudhi edited the film. The large cast also included Saroj Kumar, Vibhash Rout, Abhishek Panda, Tapi Mishra, Akash Hota, Jhalak Soni, Jayashree Sadangi, Balakrushna Nayak and Prakruti Mishra.

Anurag Pattnaik, Gaurav Anand and Surya Jit composed the music, with lyrics by J.P. Wordsmith, Ranjan Nayak and Debajyoti Nayak. Nakash Aziz, Asima Panda, Gaurav Anand, Ashutosh Sadangi and Gobinda Chandra were among the singers.
The film opened in theatres on 13 March 2025.

Q41729784.lead: Tu Mo Suna Tu Mo Hira is a 2013 Odia-language film directed by Rajeev Mohanty and produced by Jayadev Mandal, starring Babi Mishra and Priyanka Haldar. It won several Odisha State Film Awards.

p: Chinmayee Mohanty wrote the story, Rajani Ranjan the dialogue and Rajeev Mohanty the screenplay. Kuna Raul edited the film. Kuna Tripathy, Snigdha Mohanty, Munna Khan, Romi, Pushpa Panda, Debu Brahma, Bhagaban and Sonali Monalisa were also in the cast.
Prasant Padhi composed the music. Basantaraj Samal, Arun Mantri, Nizam, Pabitra Pradhan and Rajani Ranjan wrote the lyrics, and Kumar Bapi, Tapu Mishra and Arabinda Muduli were among the singers.
The film was released on 1 January 2013.

At the 24th Odisha State Film Awards, Chinmayee Mohanty won Best Story, Tapu Mishra won Best Playback Singer (Female), Pushpa Panda won Best Supporting Actress and Hrushi won Best Comedian. Snigdha Mohanty received a Special Jury Award.

facts: 24th Odisha State Film Awards: Best Story, Best Playback Singer (Female), Best Supporting Actress, Best Comedian, Special Jury

Q41159566.lead: Ganja Ladhei is a 2014 Odia-language film directed by Sudhakar Vasanth and produced by Sanjeev Rout, Shyamasundar Rout and Nishikant Pradhan, starring Sambit Acharya and Siddhanta Mahapatra.

p: Prasanna Kumar Pattasani wrote the story and Nirmal Nayak the dialogue, while Sudhakar Vasanth wrote the screenplay and also acted. B. Satish was the cinematographer and Shailesh Lal the editor. Sophia Alam, Braja, Anjana Das, Saroj Das, Guddu, Salil Mitra, Pintu Nanda and Trupti Sinha were among the cast, and Anu Choudhury appeared in an item dance.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music, with lyrics by Basantaraj Samal, Nirmal Nayak and Nizam. Gautam Giri, Abhijit Majumdar, Tapu Mishra, Asima Panda, Vinod Rathod, Sujata and Babul Supriyo sang the songs.
The film was released on 21 November 2014.

Q81936497.lead: Babu Bhaijan is a 2020 Odia-language biographical film directed by Tapas Sargharia and produced by Santosh Narayan Das under the Tarang Cine Productions banner, based on the life of Odia Muslim entrepreneur Abdul Amin Khan.

p: The film traces the struggles of businessman Abdul Amin Khan on his journey from Balasore to Delhi.

Santosh Narayan Das wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue, with Debidatta Mohanty contributing additional dialogue, and also acted in the film. Rabindra Behera was the cinematographer and Rajesh Das the editor. Arindam Roy and Sivani Sangita played the leads, supported by Mihir Das, Babi Mishra, Samaresh Routray, Sritam Das, Pushpa Panda, Bidusmita, Pradyumna Lenka and Choudhury Bikash Das.
Malay Mishra composed the music to lyrics by Arun Mantri, Panchanan Nayak and Nirmal Nayak. Sangram, Prafulla Behera, Shaan, Ira Mohanty and Abhijeet Bhattacharya were among the singers.
The film was released on 12 January 2020.

facts: Life of entrepreneur Abdul Amin Khan

Q136339481.lead: Indradhanu is a 2025 Odia-language anthology film directed by Arjun Samantaray, made up of seven stories that correspond to the seven colours of the rainbow.

p: The seven segments, named violet, indigo, blue, green, yellow, orange and red, were written by Nikhilesh Mishra, Suryasnata Tripathy, Saroj Bal and Badal Mohanty, and Suryasnata Tripathy and Nikhilesh Mishra wrote the screenplay. Suryasnata Tripathy, Surabhi Pattnaik and Rajendra Mohanta produced the film. Arjun Samantaray served as cinematographer and editor as well as director. The ensemble included Bhaswati Basu, Choudhury Bikash Das, Dipanwit Dash Mohapatra, Abhishek Giri, Dharitri Khandual, Sudhashree Madhusmita, Ratikant Mishra and Smita Mohanty. The film runs 134 minutes.
Omprakash Mohanty and Anurag Pattnaik composed the music, Debadas Chhotray wrote the lyrics, and Ratikant Satapathy and Susmita Das were among the singers.
The film opened in theatres on 18 July 2025.

Q51080363.lead: Manara Manasi is a 2018 Odia-language action film written and directed by Sachidananda Samal and produced by Jogendra Kumar Sahoo, starring newcomers Vivash and Sonali.

p: Sachidananda Samal wrote the story and screenplay, and Tusharkanta Pattnaik wrote the dialogue. Chandan Maharana was the cinematographer and Saumya Sobhan Nayak the editor. Both lead actors made their Odia film debuts, with K. K., Pragyan Khatua, Ajit Das and Kuni Mishra in supporting roles. The film runs 140 minutes.

The music was composed by Sushil Dalai, with lyrics by Arun Mantri and Bapu Goswami. Human Sagar, Diptirekha Padhi, Antara Chakraborty, Tariq Aziz, Khyati Prakash and Sasank Sekhar sang the songs, and the soundtrack was released by Cine 24.

Q29033639.lead: Pheria Mo Suna Bhauni is a 2007 Odia-language film directed by Ranjit Mohanty and produced by Hari Biswal, with Jina Samal in the lead role in her debut film.

p: Hari Biswal wrote the story, and Ranjit Mohanty wrote the screenplay and dialogue. Satya Pattnaik was the cinematographer and J. Ranganathan the editor. Jina Samal made her Odia film debut, heading a cast that included Mihir Das, Ushasi Mishra, Babi Mishra, Debu Bose, Asrumochan Mohanty, Runu Parija, Harihara Mahapatra, Shweta Acharya, Minaketan Das, Aparajita Mohanty and Jayiram Samal.
Debabrata Mishra composed the music and Nizam wrote the songs. The singers included Bibhu Kishore, Shakti Mishra, Pami, Sailabhama and Srinivas.
Jina Samal won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress for her performance.

facts: Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress (Jina Samal)

Q33027061.lead: Romeo Juliet is a 2017 Odia-language romantic comedy film directed by Sudhakar Vasanth and produced by Ramesh Barik, with Arindam Roy and Barsha Priyadarshini in the lead roles.

p: Ramesh Barik produced the film under the M. R. Movies banner. Bhaskar V. Reddy was the cinematographer and Chandra Mishra the editor. Mihir Das, Dipika Tripathy and Prativa Panda appeared in supporting roles. It was the third film to pair Arindam and Barsha, following E Mana Manena and Parshuram.

Prem Anand composed the music, with lyrics by Basantaraj Samal and Subrat Nayak. The songs were sung by Ananya Sritam Nanda, Diptirekha Padhi, Humane Sagar and Sabisesh. The soundtrack also included the earlier popular song "Nahin Mo Pade Aji Ghungura".
A release during the Raja festival had been widely expected, but the film reached theatres a month later, on 14 July 2017.
The film won the Best Actor (hero) award at the 12th Film and Television Award Show Time in 2018.

Q109498108.lead: Mane Mane Mana Khojuthila is a 2021 Odia-language romantic film directed by Narasingha Padhi, starring Omkar Acharya and Namrata Singh Deo.

p: Om, son of Abhimanyu, and Gauri, daughter of Duryodhana, belong to two families locked in a long feud. Aware of the hostility between their households, the two still fall in love and pursue their goal together.

Prabhati Acharya produced the film. Durga Acharya wrote the story, and Deepak Jena wrote the screenplay and dialogue. Jitu Mishra was the cinematographer. The film marked Omkar Acharya's debut as an actor in Odia cinema. The supporting cast included Mihir Das, Priyanka Sahoo, Asrumochan Mohanty, Pratibha Panda, T. Apparao, Anjana Das, Akshay Sahoo, Suchismita, Tapan and Raj Purohit.

Ashok Kumar composed the music. The lyrics were written by Nirmal Nayak, Arun Mantri, Omkar Lenka and Deepak Jena, and the playback singers included Humane Sagar, Tariq Aziz, Ananya Acharya, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Satyajit Pradhan, Ira Mohanty and Basanta Patra.
The film was released on 8 October 2021.

Q114804719.lead: Chumki Seta Panire Budiba Nahinki is a 2022 Odia-language film directed by Girish Mohanty and produced by Upahar Bhadra, with Shreyan Nayak and Upasana Mohanty in the lead roles.

p: Bharadwaj Panda wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue. Rabindra Behera handled the cinematography and Rajesh Dash the editing. Pradyumna Lenka and Pushpa Panda played the parents of Sagar, the hero, while Jyoti Mishra, Choudhury Bikash Das, Shakti Baral, Pragyan Khatua and Tapi Mishra had other roles. Swaraj Barik, Bhoomika Dash and Anubha Sourya made guest appearances.

Bibhuti Bhushan Gadanayak composed the score. Songs were written by Bharadwaj Panda, Santosh Panda and Gadanayak himself, and sung by Udit Narayan, Humane Sagar, Kumar Sanu, Swayam Padhi, Mantu Chhuria, Papu Pom Pom, Asima Panda, Antara Chakraborty, Diptirekha Padhi and Arpita Choudhury.
The film opened in 37 theatres across Odisha on 16 September 2022.

Q41183822.lead: Hero No.1 is a 2017 Odia-language film directed by Tapas Sargharia, starring Babushaan Mohanty and Bhoomika Dash. It was released during the Durga Puja season of 2017.

p: Sanju, a fan of the Odia actor Babushaan Mohanty, dreams of becoming a film hero, while his father, a lawyer, wants him to follow the same profession. Sanju deliberately fails his college exams to pursue acting, but circumstances in society draw him back to law, which he comes to love, and he sets out to win justice for ordinary people.

The film was made under the Tarang Cine Productions banner. Ranjit Patnaik wrote the story and Tapas Sargharia the screenplay. Rabindra Behera was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor. It was Bhoomika Dash's second film as a heroine, after Tu Mo Love Story, also with Tarang Cine Productions; she played a news reporter. Mihir Das, Kuna Tripathy, Pintu Nanda, Deepak Mishra, Asit Pati, Tribhuban Panda, Jayaprakash, Pushpa Panda, Shakti Baral and Pradyumna Lenka also appeared.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics.

Q119889702.lead: To Let – Ghara Saha Mausa Free is a 2023 Odia-language film written and directed by Anupam Patnaik, starring Dipanwit Dashmohapatra and Aroshikta Mishra. It premiered on television rather than in theatres.

p: Anupam Patnaik produced the film with Barsha Patnaik and also wrote its story. Nandalal Mahapatra and Manas Parihari wrote the screenplay and dialogue. Deepak Kumar was the cinematographer and Sabyasachi Mishra the editor. The supporting cast included Choudhury Jayprakash Das, Shakti Baral, Rabi Mishra, Swagatika Mohanty, Master Sai, Sunanda Parida, Uditguru Mahapatra, Rakhee Dash, Rakesh Parida, Debananda Soni, Debadutta Nanda and Niranjan Acharya.

Anurag Patnaik composed the music. Lyricists included Jagabandhu Sahu, Sumit Panda and Rishabh Prateek, and the songs were sung by Satyajit Pradhan, Antara Chakraborty, Abhijit Majumdar, Swayam Padhi and Rishabh Prateek, among others.
The film premiered on Tarang TV and Tarang Plus on 4 June 2023. It runs for 150 minutes.

facts: To Let – Ghara Saha Mausa Free

Q56825828.lead: Paglu is an Odia-language film directed by Ram Prasad Samal and Abhishek Behura, starring Prakruti Mishra and Abhishek Behura. It premiered on television in 2023.

p: Jagannath Patajoshi Mahapatra produced the film. Behura both co-directed and played the male lead opposite Prakruti Mishra, with Mihir Das, Aparajita Mohanty, Daitari Panda and Papu Pam Pam in supporting roles.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music.
The film premiered on Colors Odia on 2 July 2023.

Q50825292.lead: Krishna – Story of a Dancer is a 2019 Odia-language film written, produced and directed by Krishna Reddy, based on the story of the Odisha dance troupe Prince Dance Group.

p: The film draws on the struggles of Prince Dance Group, the Odisha troupe that won the first season of India's Got Talent. It follows Krishna, the group's leader, on his path from daily-wage labourer to acclaimed dancer.

Krishna Reddy, the dance teacher of Prince Dance Group, wrote the story and screenplay, directed and produced the film, and co-wrote the dialogue with Chandan Kumar. He also played the lead role, with Suryamayee Mohapatra as the heroine; she had first been a member of the dance group before moving into acting. All the members of the group appeared in the film along with some outside actors, including Someswar Reddy. Dhrubananda Panda handled the cinematography and Ranjan Khatei the editing.

Krishna Reddy and Sai Lakhan composed the music, and Kumar Shree Sahu wrote the lyrics. The film has six songs, and it also uses "Bande Utkala Janani" and "Vande Mataram". Singers included Krishna Beura, Ananya Sritam Nanda and Arpita.
The film was released on 26 April 2019.

facts: The story of Prince Dance Group

Q42895829.lead: Tu Mo Dehara Chhai is a 2013 Odia-language film directed by Himanshu Parija, starring Amlan Das in a double role alongside Riya Dey and Shilpa Dey.

p: Sunil Kumar Raut and Shibaprasad Das produced the film. Sujata Raut and Sipra Das wrote the story, Debidutta Mohanty the dialogue, and Himanshu Parija the screenplay. Abhiram Mishra was the cinematographer and Sushant Mani the editor.

Amlan Das played the twin roles of Dev and Jeet, his first double role. Riya Dey played Neha and Shilpa Dey played Piya. Mihir Das, Smita Mohanty, Runu Parija, Jiban Panda, Saroj Das, Salil Mitra, Suresh Bal, Namrata Das, Minaketan, Dhir Mallick, Rabi Mishra, Rabi Nanda, Niranjan Pati and Braja Singh completed the cast.

Prem Anand composed the music. Lyrics were by Basantaraj Samal, Bijay Malla and Arun Mantri, among others, and the singers included Javed Ali, Kumar Bapi, Ramhari Das, Ira Mohanty, Sanju Mohanty, Udit Narayan and Vinod Rathod.
The film was released on 15 October 2013.

Q55814361.lead: Mindgame is a 2023 multilingual Indian film directed by Rajesh Touchriver, released in Odia (including Sambalpuri), Telugu and Hindi. Its story is based on the 2018 bomb blast in Patnagarh, Odisha.

p: Sridhar Martha produced the film, and Chhabita Martha is credited with the story. Rajesh Touchriver wrote the screenplay and directed, and Ravi Punam is credited as writer. The film was made in both Odia and Telugu. J. D. Rama Tulasi handled the cinematography and K. Sasi Kumar the editing.

The cast included Manoj Mishra as Kunjilal, Pushpa Panda as a school principal, Atul Kulkarni as IPS officer Arun Agnihotri, Anu Choudhury as Meera Agnihotri, Chinmay Mishra as Sushil Panda, Yashpal Sharma as IPS officer Ranjan Prasad Sharma, Shiju as an IPS officer named Mohanty and Tanikella Bharani as Appa Rao, along with Chittaranjan Tripathy, Ishika Singh, Sanju Sivram, Apsara Rani and Binny Mobstaz.
George Joseph composed the music.

The film was first titled Patnagarh in 2018. After a dispute arose during its screening at the 2019 Kolkata International Film Festival, it was renamed Mindgame. It was released in Odia, Hindi and Telugu on 6 October 2023, with a runtime of 128 minutes.

Q141088560.lead: Dear Purusha is a 2024 Odia-language film written and directed by Jiit Chakraborty and produced by Jhillik Bhattacharya, with an ensemble cast led by Siddhanta Mahapatra and Mahasweta Ray.

p: Jhillik Bhattacharya produced the film under Jhillik Motion Pictures and also acted in it. Jiit Chakraborty wrote the screenplay and dialogue and shared the story credit with Tarka Bagish and Sayandip Das. Ishwar Chandra Barik was the cinematographer and Manas Kumar Sahu the editor. The large cast included Samaresh Routray, Babi Mishra, Debasish Patra, Choudhury Jayprakash Das, Partha Sarathi Ray, Ananya Mishra, Dipanwit Dashmohapatra, Kuna Tripathy, Pradyumna Lenka and Amlan Das, among many others.

Gaurav Anand composed the music. The lyricists included JP Wordsmith, Sthita Patnaik, Sumit Panda and Ranjan Nayak, and the singers included Swayam Padhi, Saranya Mishra, Anurag Das, Kuldeep Pattanaik and Gaurav Anand.
The film was released in theatres on 11 January 2024.

Q28855779.lead: Chhai Pari Rahithibi is an Odia-language romantic film about reincarnation, directed by Prashant Pal and featuring newcomers Rupesh, Rojalin, Satya and Lipika in the lead roles. It was described as awaiting release.

p: Two lovers run away from home after their families refuse to accept their relationship. An accident follows in which the hero, played by Rupesh, dies, and the film deals with the couple's reunion after his rebirth.

Prashant Pal directed the film. Ranjit Patnaik wrote the story and Manas Patra wrote the screenplay and also edited it. The four lead actors made their screen debuts in the film, and Minaketan, Asrumochan Mohanty, Gyanaranjan, Rabi Mishra and Nilu played supporting roles.

P. Kumar composed the music, with lyrics by Sasmal Masan and Panchanan Nayak. The singers included Udit Narayan, Kumar Sanu, Mohammed Aziz, Kumar Bapi, Madhab and Sanju. The songs were launched on 17 February 2017 at Hotel Excellence.
