Q25991189.lead: Jhiata Bigidigala is a 2016 Odia-language film directed by Bini Patnaik and produced by Sachikant Jena, starring Babushaan Mohanty and Elina Samantray. It centres on a lively, mischievous young woman.

p: The film was made under the Moon TV banner. Sachikant Jena wrote the story, and Rajani Ranjan wrote the screenplay and dialogue. Shooting began in Bhubaneswar on 4 February 2016.

Alongside the leads, Jina Samal played an ACP, her first role fighting politicians and dishonest people on screen, with Rudra Panigrahi as the hero opposite her. Ipsita, Lina, Dev, Minaketan, Asit Pati, Salil Mitra, Bijaya Patnaik, Ashok Mallick and Smaranika Priyadarshini also appeared.

Prem Anand composed the four songs, with lyrics by Basantaraj Samal and Subrat Swain. The singers were Humane Sagar, Pragyan, Sricharan, Dipti, Satyajit and Aryan. The soundtrack was released on 29 June 2016.
The film was released on 14 July 2016, during the Bahuda Yatra.

Q21283093.lead: Prema Sabuthu Balaban is a 2013 Odia-language film directed by Arun Mohanty, starring Dusmanta Panda and Barsha Priyadarshini. Barsha received the Best Actress award at the State Film Awards for her role.

p: Meena Mohanty produced the film. Chittaranjan Prusty and Ramesh Rout wrote the story, while Arun Mohanty, besides directing and composing the music, wrote the dialogue together with Shirshananda Das Kanungo. Rabi and Amresh Swain shot the film and Ashok Sharma edited it.

Arindam Roy was originally cast as the hero, and at that stage the film was titled Swargadwara Sakhi. After he left the project, Dusmanta Panda took over the lead and the title was changed to Prema Sabuthu Balaban.

Dusmanta played Rahul Mishra and Barsha played a character of the same name. Siddhanta Mahapatra appeared as Major Karan Panda (Kalia), Uttam Mohanty as Nilakantha Mishra, Aparajita Mohanty as his wife, Hara Patnaik as Inspector Bhujang and Pradyumna Lenka as the chief minister. Mihir Das, Illu Banerjee, Akshay Bastia, Ashok Das, Jiban Panda and others completed the cast.
Arun Mohanty composed the music and also wrote the lyrics.
The film was released on 17 May 2013 and runs for 164 minutes.
Barsha Priyadarshini won the Best Actress award at the State Film Awards for this film.

Q34203019.lead: Jouthi Tu Seithi Mu is a 2016 Odia-language film directed by Sushant Kumar Rout and produced by Anupama Rout, introducing Yash Mishra in the lead. It was also released in Bhojpuri.

p: The film was made under the Sabitri Pictures banner. Anupama Rout wrote the story, Bijay Malla the dialogue, and Sushant Kumar Rout the screenplay. B. Satish was the cinematographer.

Newcomer Yash Mishra played the lead opposite Anjali Mishra, with newcomer Anjana Singh, Sritam Das, Anara Gupta, Seema Singh, Gopal Rai, Ayaz Khan, Harihara Mohapatra, Pintu Nanda and Saroj Das in other roles.
Baidyanath Das composed the music. The songs were written by Bijay Malla, Panchanan Nayak and Nizam and sung by Udit Narayan, Suresh Wadkar, Vinod Rathod and Pamela Jain, among others.
The film opened in 45 theatres in Odisha on 1 January 2016, coinciding with the New Year. Its Bhojpuri version was titled Humka Ishq Hua Hai Yaaron.

Q56785789.lead: Satyameba Jayate is a 2008 Odia-language film directed by Basant Sahu, starring Akash Dasnayak and Sonali Chakraborty.

p: Biranchi Narayan Panda produced the film and wrote its story. Ranjit Patnaik wrote the dialogue and Basant Sahu the screenplay. Abhiram Mishra was the cinematographer and Ashok Sharma the editor. The large supporting cast included Bijay Mohanty, Kuna Tripathy, George Tiadi, Suresh Bal, Anita Das, Gyana Hota, Harihara Mohapatra, Akshay Bastia, Rabi Mishra, Debu Bose and Salil Mitra.
Swarup Nayak composed the music and wrote the songs. The singers included Kumar Bapi, Gyana Hota, Tapu Mishra, Mira Mishra, Ashirbad Muduli, Swarup Nayak and T. Souri.
The film was released in 2008 and runs for 158 minutes.

Q60220250.lead: Rahasya is a 2018 Odia-language mystery film directed by Bighneswar Panda, written by Somya Ranjan Sahu, about five film-institute students who encounter strange events in an old bungalow.

p: Dev, Sruti, Alli, Ridhima and Lala, five students at a film institute, decide to make a film together. Dev wants to base it on a story he keeps seeing in his dreams, and the group travels to an old bungalow that also appears in those dreams. Once they arrive, a series of strange and mysterious incidents begins.

Narayan Chandra Sahu and Santosh Kumar Sai produced the film. Somya Ranjan Sahu wrote the story and screenplay and B. Chandan Kumar the dialogue. The cast included Tushar Sinha, who made his Odia film debut, director Bighneswar Panda, Kavya Keeran, Abakash Mishra, Ankita Mohanty and Abhishek. Filming took place at Narasinghpur Kothi, Gopalpur beach, Chilika, and various locations in Cuttack and Bhubaneswar.
Nihar and Shantanu composed the music, and the singers included Antara Chakraborty, Shantanu Kumar Sai, Subhechha Mohanty, G. Tabu and Sai Suchitra.
The film was released on 14 December 2018 in Odisha, and also in Bangalore and Surat.

facts: Narasinghpur Kothi, Gopalpur, Chilika, Cuttack, Bhubaneswar

Q29645675.lead: Rakhile Siba Mariba Kie is a 1994 Odia-language film directed by Sangram Biswal, starring Uttam Mohanty and Aparajita Mohanty. It was Biswal's first film as a director.

p: Ranjit Biswal and Manasi Biswal produced the film. T. Rajendar wrote the story and Ratikanta Mishra the dialogue, while Sangram Biswal wrote the screenplay in addition to directing. Samba Siva Rao handled the cinematography and A. Sreekar Prasad the editing.

Besides the two leads, the cast included Bina Maharana, Raimohan Parida, Siddhanta Mahapatra, Priyanka Mahapatra, Debu Bose, Dukhiram Swain, Jayiram Samal, Mamina, Gita Dutta, Satya, Braja Singh, Dhira Biswal, Narendra Behera, Asit Pati, Nabanita, Munu Pati and Kulamani Sahu.

Akshaya Mohanty composed the music. The lyricists included Shirshananda Das Kanungo, Purnendu Das Mahapatra and Akshaya Mohanty, and the singers included Gita Dash, Bibhu Kishore, Lopita Mishra, Akshaya Mohanty, Debasish Mahapatra and Pritinanda Routray.

Q6916796.lead: Most Wanted is a 2011 Odia-language crime film directed by Sushant Mani, starring Anubhav Mohanty, Megha Ghosh and Mihir Das.

p: Abhaya Mohanty, an innocent young man, arrives in the city hoping for a decent job and a good life. Forced by circumstances to fight local thugs, he is drawn into the criminal underworld, rises to become the feared don known as Baba, and ends up as the police's most wanted man.
Prabhas Rout produced the film. Muna Patra wrote the story, Bapu Goswami the dialogue, and Sushant Mani the screenplay; Mani also edited the film. Sitansu Mohapatra was the cinematographer.

Anubhav Mohanty played Abhaya Mohanty/Baba, Megha Ghosh played Monika James and Mihir Das played Albert James. Minaketan, Pushpa Panda, Samaresh Routray, Baisakhi Mohanty, Papu Pam Pam, Jiban Panda, Hara Rath and Satwaki Mishra had supporting roles.
Goodly Rath composed the music, with lyrics by Mohit Chakraborty and Bapu Goswami. Pabitra Entertainment acquired the music rights.
The film was released on 14 January 2011.

Q50825291.lead: Blackmail is a 2018 Odia-language film directed by Amit Nayak and produced by Adikanda Sahu, starring Ardhendu Sahu with Ahana Baral and Tamanna Vyas as the heroines.

p: Adikanda Sahu produced the film through his company Maa Singhabahini Movies and also wrote the story. Bapu Goswami wrote the dialogue. Director Amit Nayak had earlier worked as a dance choreographer.

Ardhendu Sahu, who had debuted in Tapori, played Anurag/Dev. Ahana had entered Odia films with Bhairab, and Tamanna with Bhaina, Kana Kala Se. Siddhanta Mahapatra, Manoj Mishra, George Tiadi, Ratan Meher, Saroj Das, Rajeswari Ray, Pratibha Panda, Pragyan Khatua and Pupul Bhuyan were also in the cast.

Prem Anand composed the music, and Basantaraj Samal and Subrat Swain wrote the lyrics. Udit Narayan and Diptirekha Padhi sang a Holi song in the film; other singers included Ashutosh, Humane Sagar, Kaushik Shibashish and Ananya Sritam Nanda.
The film was released on 31 August 2018.

Q7137121.lead: Parinam is an Odia-language film directed by Biswanath Nayak and produced by Krushna Chandra Tripathy, starring Pramod Panigrahi, Geetisudha, Kartik Ghosh and Sarat Pujari. It marked the screen debut of actress Sudharani Jena (Geetisudha).

p: The film was made on a budget of 95,000 rupees. Its cast also included Dhira Biswal, Mania, Dukhiram Swain and Tushar.

The music is credited to Bhubaneswar Mishra in one account and to Akshaya Mohanty in another. Sipra Bose, Nirmala Mishra, Akshaya Mohanty and Sandhya Mukherjee sang in the film. Its songs include "Chhaya Pachhe Pachhe Ghuri Bule".

The film opened on 3 November 1960 at the Capital in Cuttack, the Srikrishna in Puri and Utkal Talkies in Aska; it is also dated to 1961. All of its prints were destroyed in 1969. A copy was later recovered from Aska by the Film Journalist Forum, digitised, and screened again in Bhubaneswar on 6 November 2023.

facts: Digitised copy screened in Bhubaneswar, 6 November 2023

Q28919007.lead: Dil Diwana Heigala is a 2017 Odia-language film directed by Sudhanshu Mohan Sahu, starring Babushaan Mohanty and Sheetal Patra. It was the 20th film from Sarthak Movies.

p: Sitaram Agarwal produced the film and Ranjit Patnaik wrote the story. It was the fourth film pairing Babushaan and Sheetal, after Jiye Jaha Kahu Mora Dho, Bhala Pae Tote 100 Ru 100 and Tu Je Sei; Sheetal played Shikha. Veteran actor Pradyumna Lenka also appeared, Pragyan Khatua played a comic role, and television actor Chintu was cast as the villain in his first Odia film.

S. Kumar composed the music, and Arun Mantri and Bapu Goswami wrote all the songs. The singers included Babushaan, Sangram Mohanty, Tariq, Humane Sagar, Jagruti, Nibedita, Saurin Bhatt, Adesh Kumar and Namita Agrawal.
The film was released on 13 January 2017, during the New Year season.

Q42824558.lead: Mita Basichi Mu Bhuta Sathire is a 2013 Odia-language 3D film written and directed by Sanjay Nayak, starring Akash Dasnayak, Dusmanta Panda, Priya Choudhury and Nikita.

p: Production began with the film planned as the first Odia 3D film, but its release was delayed and Kauri Kanya came out first as the first 3D film. Bhabani Charan Rath and Anam Charan Sahu produced it. Laxmipriya Sahu wrote the story, and Sanjay Nayak wrote the screenplay and dialogue, directed and edited the film. S. Ranjan was the cinematographer.

The supporting cast included Bijay Mohanty, Snigdha Mohanty, Biju Badajena, Premanjan Parida, Kuna Tripathy, Akhil Patnaik, Manisha Mishra and Chandan, with Sachin, Ankit, Ayush, Papun and Sivani Sangita (Niki) as child artists.
Prem Anand composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak and Arun Mantri. Tapu Mishra, Kumar Bapi, Sricharan, Diptirekha Padhi, Mamuni and Aryan were among the singers.
The film was released on 20 September 2013.

Q33305466.lead: He Prabhu Dekha De is a 2016 Odia-language film written and directed by Gopi Anand, starring Harihar Das with Anu Choudhury.

p: Uma Maheswar Rao and Prasanna Kumar Teki produced the film, with Dusmanta Sahoo as executive producer. Gopi Anand wrote the story and screenplay. Ramu Pinisetty was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor. Harihar Das took the lead after appearing in Mu Premi Mu Pagala. Anu Choudhury, Pragyan Khatua, Papu Pam Pam, Mihir Das, Amandeep, Salil Mitra, Dusmanta Sahoo, Bagala and Mousumi were also in the cast.

The film had two music directors, V. Yadagiri and Prakalpini Patnaik. Panchanan Nayak and Nirmal Nayak wrote the songs, which were sung by Hema Chandra, Revanth, Sri Dhruti, Satyajit Pradhan, Prakalpini Patnaik, Ramya Behera, Geetha Madhuri and Lipsika, among others.
The film was released on 11 November 2016.

Q141104385.lead: Dasama is a 2024 Odia-language film directed by Raja Dash and produced by Deepak Kumar Jena, featuring Sailendra Samantray, Nilakhi Patra, Suman Pattnaik and Akash Hota.

p: Kumarshree Sahu and B. Uttam Kumar wrote the screenplay and dialogue. Biswajit Kuldi was the cinematographer and Kalpataru Dash the editor. The cast also included Armaan Mohanty, Xonty, Phani Prateek, Jyoti Ranjan Rout, Rabi Mishra, Udit Guru and others.

Several composers worked on the soundtrack: Gaurav Anand, Anurag Patnaik, Preet Priyo, Subrat Behera, Sandeep Panda, Subhrajit Mohanty and Binay Rath. The lyricists included Ranjan Nayak, Preet Priyo, Rakesh Dash, Kumarshree Sahu, JP Wordsmith, Sandeep Panda, Tapu Nayak and Soumya Ranjan Panda. Humane Sagar, Asima Panda, Kuldeep Pattanaik, Sandeep Panda, Gaurav Anand, Sailendra Samantray and Babushaan Mohanty were among the singers.
The film was released in theatres on 18 January 2024.

Q99457122.lead: Suna Sansar is an Odia-language film written and directed by Hara Patnaik and produced by Keshab Rout, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra and Smita Mohanty.

p: Hara Patnaik wrote the story and screenplay, and Subodh Patnaik wrote the dialogue. Dilip Ray was the cinematographer and Rabi Patnaik the editor.

An earlier film with the same title was made by Sisir Mishra in 1997, in which Hara Patnaik had a small part. About twenty years after that release, Patnaik made this film under the same name and played the villain himself. Uttam Mohanty, Aparajita Mohanty, Debu Bose, Raimohan Parida, Suresh Bal, Asrumochan Mohanty, Mihir Das, Liza Das, Anisha Das, Upendra Nayak, Himanshu Parija, producer Keshab Rout, Jayiram Samal and Braja Singh were also in the cast.
Biju Swain composed the music and Shirshananda Das Kanungo wrote the songs. The singers included Srikanta Das, Subash Das, Tapas Das, Deepak, Ira Mohanty, Bishnu Nayak and Mohammed Sajid.

Q50824826.lead: Rangila Baba is a 2015 Odia-language film directed by Sanjay Nayak, with Kuna Tripathy in the title role of Baba Bharati. Its story draws on the life of Sarathi Baba.

p: Biranchi Narayan Panda and Dillip Dash produced the film, and Panda also wrote the story. Basantaraj Samal wrote the screenplay. Pradeep was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor. Sanjay Nayak completed the shooting in just two weeks.

Kuna Tripathy played Baba Bharati and Guddu played his son. Chandan Kar appeared as Akash and newcomer Sonika Roy as Rashmi; Nayak cast her as the heroine after she reached the top 12 of the Femina Miss India 2015 contest, and the film was her acting debut. Jiban Panda, Biju Badajena, Premanjan Parida, Chakradhar Jena, Biren Mishra and Bidusmita had supporting roles.
Manmath Mishra composed the music, with lyrics by Basantaraj Samal and Panchanan Nayak.
The film was released on 2 October 2015.

Q28946523.lead: Maya is a 2015 Odia-language film directed by Aswini Gadanayak and produced by Kamalakanta Das, starring Sunil Kumar with Anu Choudhury and Lipsa Mishra.

p: Kamalakanta Das wrote the story and Bapu Goswami the dialogue. Ranjan Khatei edited the film. The supporting cast included Sritam Das, Pradyumna Lenka, Mihir Das, Aparajita Mohanty, Chandrasekhar Jena, Biju Badajena, Jiban Panda, Salil Mitra, Akshay Bastia and Pintu Nanda, among others.
Bibhuti Bhushan Gadanayak composed the music and Bapu Goswami wrote the songs. Udit Narayan, Nikita Das, Bibhu Kishore, Pami, Nabhya, Kuldeep, Binay Mohanty and Rudra Mohanty were among the singers.
The film was released on 7 August 2015.

Q141579873.lead: Chandrabanshi is a 2024 Odia-language film directed by Yash Varman Panda and Sunil Sahoo and produced by Kumar Pritam Sahoo, with an ensemble cast including Siddhanta Mahapatra, Akash Dasnayak and Sritam Das.

p: Kumar Pritam Sahoo produced the film, wrote its story and also acted in it. Raj Rajesh wrote the screenplay and dialogue and appeared in the cast. Pratap Rout was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor. Other cast members included Daitari Panda, Poonam Mishra, Lipsa Mishra, Jasmine Rath, Ashwini Tripathy, Usasi Misra, Pratibha Panda, Smita Mohanty, Tapas Sargharia, Debu Brahma and Shakti Baral.

Asad Nizam composed the music. Ranjan Nayak, Pushpak Parida and Tapu Nayak were among the lyricists, and the singers included Kuldeep Pattanaik, Swayam Padhi, Asima Panda, Antara Chakraborty, Arpita Choudhury and Kalki Rapper.
The film was released in theatres on 14 June 2024.

Q14475136.lead: Rolls – 28 is an early Odia-language film directed by Kalyan Gupta and produced by Ratikanta Padhi. It is described as the first Odia social film and the fourth Odia feature film.

p: The film was produced under the Great Eastern Movietone banner. Kalicharan Pattanayak wrote the story, and Kalyan Gupta wrote the screenplay; Brundaban Mohapatra is also credited as a writer. The cast included Bimala Devi, Kishori Devi, Giridhari, Ratikanta Padhi, Pankaj, Anima Pedini and Rajendra.
The music was composed by Gour Goswami together with a second composer, named as Nrupendra Pal in one account and Suren Pal in another. Its songs included "Marua Phutila Bane".

Histories of Odia cinema by Kartik Ghosh, Bhim Singh and Randhir Das record the release year as 1951 without a date. Research published by Surya Deo on 13 October 2022 places the release on Friday, 28 April 1950, at the Capital theatre in Cuttack. That was the same date on which Sita Bibaha, the first Odia film, had been released in Odisha fourteen years earlier.

Q7395731.lead: Saathire is a 2004 Odia-language film directed by Hara Patnaik, starring Anubhav Mohanty, Madhumita Basu, Pintu Nanda and Anita Das. The title translates as "Oh my dear friend".

p: The film is based on Leena Gangopadhyay's story Janmadin, which was itself based on the 1982 Bengali film Troyee; it is also stated that Hara Patnaik wrote the story and screenplay. Sailabala Lenka and Hara Patnaik produced it, and Niranjan Das was the cinematographer.

Madhumita Basu, from Kolkata, made her debut in the film after local girls declined to act in a romantic film. Shooting took place in Agra and Kullu-Manali. Sritam Das, Hara Patnaik, Deepak Parida, Soma Bhowmik, Debu Bose, Runu Parija, Pradyumna Lenka and Kanta Singh were also in the cast.
Manmath Mishra composed the music and wrote the songs.
The film was released on 26 August 2004 and was a box office success.

Q59330892.lead: Pyar Alaga Prakara is a 2018 Odia-language romantic film written and directed by Hira Choudhury, starring Jyoti Ranjan Nayak and Jhillik Bhattacharya.

p: Nisha is beautiful but very stubborn, and refuses to marry the grooms her grandfather Rajeswar Ray keeps looking for. She then meets Jeet, who deceives her while pretending to be in love, setting off a chain of events.

Bibesita Ghadei and Akshay Pradhan produced the film. Hira Choudhury wrote the story and screenplay, and Bijay Malla the dialogue. Ranjit Rath was the cinematographer and Deben Mishra the editor. Bijay Mohanty, Mihir Das, Jayiram Samal and Pragyan Khatua had supporting roles.

Amarendra Mohanty composed the music, with lyrics by Shirshananda Das Kanungo and Arun Mantri. Humane Sagar, Asima Panda, Diptirekha Padhi, Satyajit Pradhan and Ananya Sritam Nanda were among the singers.
The film was released on 23 November 2018, on Panchaka Purnima. Another Jyoti Ranjan Nayak film, Sathi Tu Feria, opened on the same day.

Q60454728.lead: Mal Mahu Jibana Mati is a 2019 Odia-language film directed by Ramesh Rout and produced by Nabin Bhandari, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Elina Samantray.

p: Lyricist Nirmal Nayak wrote the story and dialogue as well as the songs. Somio R. was the cinematographer and Manas Kumar Sahu the editor. Sabyasachi Mishra played Michael. Singer Asima Panda made her acting debut in the film, and Odissi dancer Saswat Joshi and Harihar Das appeared as guest artists. Salil Mitra, Jiban Panda, Pradyumna Lenka, Bidusmita, Krishna Kar, Biju Badajena, Swapna Pati, Rabi Mishra and Rushi Pattnaik were also in the cast.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music to Nirmal Nayak's lyrics. The singers included Tilak Chakraborty, Tariq Aziz, Diptirekha Padhi, Humane Sagar, Sonali Nanda, Swayam Padhi, Sohini Mishra and Abhijit Majumdar.
The film was released on 8 November 2019.

Q60368280.lead: Sangam is a 2014 Odia-language film produced, written and directed by Jatin Kumar Agarwal, starring Akash Dasnayak, Buddhaditya Mohanty and Siddhanta Mahapatra.

p: Jatin Kumar Agarwal wrote the story, while Abhijit Ghatwari and Bijay Mishra wrote the screenplay and dialogue. Nitin Ghag was the cinematographer and Nakul Prasad the editor. The supporting cast included Jyoti Pani, Payal Srivastava, Bijay Mohanty, Snigdha Mohanty, Mihir Das, Jayiram Samal, Abhishek, Rakesh Biduwa, Abhijit Ghatwari, Abani Kumar, Manini Mishra and Nandini.
Harpreet Singh composed the music and Asit Patra wrote the songs. Manoj Manu, Antara Mitra, Monali, Rex, Som and Abhijeet Sawant were among the singers.
The film was released on 14 June 2014.

Q109519715.lead: Chumki My Darling is a 2021 Odia-language film directed by Sudhanshu Mohan Sahu, starring Sambit Acharya and Mahasweta Ray. It premiered on television.

p: Pradyumna Lenka, Pradeep Kumar Swain and Prakash Kumar Swain produced the film. Debidutta Mohanty wrote the story and screenplay, and Monalisa Mohanty and B. Chandan Kumar the dialogue. Dhrubananda Panda handled the cinematography and Rajesh Dash the editing.

Sambit Acharya played Bhabani Shankar Mahapatra and Mahasweta Ray played Chumki. Pradyumna Lenka appeared as A. K. Mishra and Tribhuban Panda as Balia, with Piyali, Pushpa Panda, Mahaprasad Kar, Alaka Satapathy, Subhranshu, Rabi Mishra, Saroj Das, Banku and Sushil in other roles.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics. The singers included Humane Sagar, Antara Chakraborty, Gautam Giri, Kuldeep Pattanaik, Jyotirmayee Nayak, Jagruti Mishra and Abhijit Majumdar.
The film premiered on Tarang TV and Tarang Plus on 14 March 2021.

Q45037037.lead: To Premare Padila Pare is a 2017 Odia-language romantic film directed by Saroj Kant and produced by Chinmayee Priyadarshini, who also starred opposite Debraj; both leads made their Odia film debuts in it.

p: Prasanna Kumar Pattasani wrote the story, Dr. Rajani Ranjan the dialogue, and Saroj Kant the screenplay. Laxman Yadav was the cinematographer. The supporting cast included Pralipta, Munna Khan, Puja, Sasmita Panda, Jiban Panda, Pragyan Khatua, Pushpa Panda, Asit Pati, Dhiren Mitra, Kuni Panda, Manisha Mishra, Ashish Sendre and Anjana Dash. Bidusmita danced in an item number.

Baidyanath Dash composed the music. Prasanna Kumar Pattasani, Nirmal Nayak, Arun Mantri, Ashutosh and Jayanta Das were among the lyricists, and Humane Sagar, Tapu Mishra, Satyajit, Asima Panda, Sanju and Baidyanath sang.
The film was released on 24 November 2017.

Q52154522.lead: Sabata Maa is a 2003 Odia-language film written and directed by Sisir Mishra, with Mahasweta Ray, Bijay Mohanty, Barsha Priyadarshini and Anu Choudhury in leading roles.

p: Ashok Kumar Lenka and Gyana Patnaik produced the film. Sisir Mishra wrote the story and screenplay, and Subodh Patnaik the dialogue. Kader R. Khan was the cinematographer and Guddu Jafri the editor.

The cast also included Hara Patnaik, Sritam Das, Deepak Parida, Saroj Das, Pradyumna Lenka, Namrata Das, Soudamini, Binayak Mishra, Sadhana Parija, Nimananda Patra, Bijay Mishra, Gitanjali Kar, Niranjan Pandey, Julia and Shweta Mallick. Prakruti Mishra began her career in Odia films as a child artist in this film.

Amarendra Mohanty composed the music. The lyricists included Shirshananda Das Kanungo, Arun Mantri, Manmath Mishra and Subodh Patnaik, and the singers included Pankaj Jal, Manmath Mishra, Shakti Mishra, Ira Mohanty, Arabinda Muduli and Sailabhama Mahapatra.

Q4687010.lead: Ae Jugara Krushna Sudama is an Odia-language film from 2003, directed by Hara Patnaik and starring Mithun Chakraborty and Uttam Mohanty. It remakes the Hindi film Khudgarz.

p: The plot follows the bond of love and friendship between a rich man, played by Uttam Mohanty, and a poor one, played by Mithun Chakraborty.
Basanta Nayak was the producer. The story is credited to Binay Nayak, and Hara Patnaik wrote the screenplay besides directing. Niranjan Das shot the film and Chandrasekhar Mishra edited it.

Mithun Chakraborty had previously made a special appearance in the Odia film Sahara Jaluchi (1998); this was his second Odia film. Hara Patnaik, Suraj Kumar, Barsha Priyadarshini, Rachna Banerjee, Jayiram Samal, Jyoti Mishra, Debu Bose, Usasi Mishra and Anita Das rounded out the cast.
The music was by Swarup Nayak.
Running 125 minutes, it came out in 2003 and did well at the box office.
Its source, the Hindi film Khudgarz, was in turn drawn from Jeffrey Archer's 1979 novel Kane and Abel.

Q51080351.lead: Arjun is a 2005 Odia-language film directed by Hara Patnaik and produced by Pradyumna Lenka, starring Anubhav Mohanty and Gargi Mohanty.

p: Hara Patnaik wrote the story, and Subodh Patnaik wrote the screenplay and dialogue. Niranjan Das was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor. Producer Pradyumna Lenka also acted, alongside Rameswari, Hara Patnaik, Amrita Shukla, Kirti Mohanty, Suresh Bal, Raimohan Parida, Chakradhar Jena, Saroj Das, Premanjan Parida, Debu Bose, Jiban Panda, Salil Mitra and a large supporting cast.
Swarup Nayak composed the music and wrote the songs, which were sung by Kumar Bapi, Tapu Mishra and T. Souri, among others.

Q133830606.lead: Aparahnara Surjya is a 2024 Odia-language film produced, written and directed by Ajay Kumar Mohanty. Its story centres on the Mundapota Kela, a tribal community of southern Odisha.

p: Ajay Kumar Mohanty wrote the story and screenplay and produced the film through Ananya Production. Satwik Raja wrote the dialogue. Ajit Kishore Das was the cinematographer and Gadadhar Purti the editor. The cast included Pramod Rout, Jaya Swami, Kalinga Dash, Munmun Khuntia, Susandhya Narayani Mohanty, Ajay Mohanty, Somnath Das, Manabi Bhadra, Shubham, Lalit Behera, Pulin Sahu, Rahul Bindhani and Rina Mishra.
Mahendra Acharya composed the music and wrote the songs.
The film was released in theatres on 6 September 2024, during Ganesh Puja. It was later screened again at Madhab Hall in Bhadrak.
Ajay Kumar Mohanty received the Best Story Writer award for the film at the 49th annual festival of the film magazine Chalachitra Jagat.

facts: Mundapota Kela community of southern Odisha

Q5226773.lead: Dashyu Ratnakar is an Odia-language mythological film directed by Prabhat Mukherjee and produced by Krushna Chandra Tripathy. It was the first partly coloured film in the history of Odia cinema.

p: The bandit Ratnakar kills travellers to support his family. At the urging of the sage Narada, he asks his father, mother, wife and children whether they will share in the sins he commits on their behalf. They all reply that providing for them is his duty and that they bear no responsibility for how he earns. Shaken by their answer, Ratnakar renounces his crimes and becomes a sage through intense penance.

Krushna Chandra Tripathy produced the film with Utkal Chalachitra Pratisthan, on a budget of 98,000 rupees. Sarat Pujari played the hero, and Prashanta Nanda appeared as a child artist. Krishna, Master Mania, Dhirendra, Ramesh and Shanti were also in the cast.
Balakrushna Dash composed the music.

Q116136310.lead: Tora Mora Kati is a 2023 Odia-language film written and directed by Ramesh Rout and produced by actress Jhillik Bhattacharya, starring Sailendra Samantray and Sheetal Patra.

p: Ramesh Rout wrote the story and screenplay, and Deepak Jena the dialogue. Ishwar Chandra Barik was the cinematographer and Rajesh Dash the editor. Siddhanta Mahapatra, Pradyumna Lenka, Sudhanshu Mohan Sahu, Sanjay Nayak, Babi Mishra, Sudipta, Tukuna, Kalia Shandha, Aishwarya, Rupsa and Debika appeared in supporting roles.

Prem Anand composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak and Arun Mantri, among others. Humane Sagar, Diptirekha Padhi, Ashutosh Mohanty, Sabisesh, Ananya Sritam Nanda and Debakrupa were among the singers. The songs were released on 11 December 2022.
Released on 6 January 2023 in 30 theatres across Odisha, it was the first Odia film to reach theatres that year.

Q29385995.lead: Sitaramanka Bahaghara Kali Jugare is a 2017 film directed by Telugu filmmaker G. N. S. Prasad, made with actors from Odia and Telugu cinema. It was the first film released in both Odia and Telugu.

p: Edupuganti Seshagiri and Maredi Pichi Reddy produced the film. Dr. Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue for the Odia version. Prasad Edara was the cinematographer and V. S. Nagireddy the editor.
The Odia actors included Sabyasachi Mishra, Bijay Mohanty, Anita Das, Papu Pam Pam, Jiban Panda and Manisha Chatterjee, while Manesha, Suman Talwar and Neha came from Telugu cinema.
Kishan Kavadiya composed the music, and Arun Mantri and Nirmal Nayak wrote the Odia songs. Bibhu Kishore, Satyajit Charan, Humane Sagar, Sanju Mohanty, Sabyasachi Mishra and Asima Panda sang them.
The film was released on 31 March 2017.
Jiban Panda won the Best Comedian award for his role at the Pratibha Samman ceremony of the film magazine Chalachitra Jagat.

Q116838665.lead: Break Up Wala Love Story is a 2023 Odia-language film directed by Rashesh Mohanty, starring Pradeep Kumar Sahoo and Debasmita. It premiered on television.

p: Debi Prasad Patra produced the film, and B. Chandan Kumar wrote its story, screenplay and dialogue. SK Arif was the cinematographer and Pintu Nayak the editor. Illu Banerjee, Kedar Mishra, Shakti Baral, Tribhuban Panda, Dipti Panda, Devi Barik, Swagatika, Bibhu Mishra and Lopamudra Mishra were among the supporting cast.

Diptiman Sarangi composed the music. Debidutta Mohanty and Debajyoti Nayak were among the lyricists, and the singers included Swayam Padhi, Neha Niharika Kar, Antara Chakraborty, Amrita Nayak, Kuldeep Pattanaik and Diptiman Sarangi.
The film premiered on Tarang TV and Tarang Plus on 19 February 2023.

Q21283203.lead: Tu Au Mun is a 2014 Odia-language romantic film directed by Nishikant Dalabehera, introducing Bijendra Kumar Mishra and Bandana Paramanik in the lead roles.

p: Soumya Ranjan Patnaik produced the film. Trilochan Tarai wrote the story, Deepak Jena the dialogue, and Nishikant Dalabehera the screenplay. Sushil Behera was the cinematographer. Both leads made their Odia film debuts; Bandana Paramanik played Preeti. Mihir Das, Aparajita Mohanty, Kuna Tripathy, Salil Mitra and Lina were in supporting roles.

Debitosh Acharya composed the music, his first film as a music director. Chinmay Acharya, Manas Samal, Arun Mantri and Basantaraj Samal were among the lyricists, and the singers included Debitosh Acharya, Kumar Bapi, Sailabhama Mahapatra, Madhab, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Mama Das and Manas Pritam. The songs were launched on 12 December 2013 at Hotel Suryansh.
The film was released on 10 January 2014.

facts: Bijendra Kumar Mishra and Bandana Paramanik (leads); Debitosh Acharya (music director)

Q60617127.lead: Panjuri Bhitare Sari is a 1992 Odia-language film directed by Avtar Singh and produced by Rabi Swain, starring Bijay Mohanty, Tandra Ray, Mihir Das and Aparajita Mohanty.

p: Rabi Swain wrote the story, Gopal Dey the dialogue, and Avtar Singh the screenplay. Samba Siva Rao handled the cinematography and Deben Mishra the editing. Hara Patnaik, Debu Bose, Jayiram Samal, Kuni Mishra, Kanta Singh, Gita Dutta, Byomkesh Tripathy, Braja Singh, Sanjay Nayak, Lipsa, Namrata Das, Krishna Das and Bairagi Mohanty were also in the cast.

Swarup Nayak composed the music. Alekh Biswal, Satya Mohanty, Swarup Nayak and Srikanta Parida were among the lyricists, and the singers included Trupti Das, Srikanta Das, Gita Dash, Dipti Mohanty, Debasish Mahapatra and Mohammed Sajid.
The film was released on 4 June 1992 and runs for 157 minutes.

Q52764266.lead: Maa Pari Kie Heba is a 1999 Odia-language feature film directed by Sisir Mohan Pati, with Siddhanta Mahapatra, Usasi Misra, Mihir Das, Mamuni Mishra, Uttam Mohanty and Aparajita Mohanty in leading roles.

p: Birakishore Mahapatra and Lulu Mahapatra produced the film. Its story came from Ramachandra Behera, while Subodh Pattnaik wrote both the screenplay and the dialogue. Niranjan Das was the cinematographer and A. Sekhar Prasad edited the film. The supporting cast included Raimohan Parida, Biraj Dash, Rakesh Jain, Jayiram Samal, Saroj Das and Rabi Mishra.

Biju Swain composed the music. The songs were written by Sirsananda Das Kanungo, Subodh Pattnaik and Nizam, and sung by playback artists including Mohammed Aziz, Prakash Dubey, Ira Mohanty, Sonu Nigam, Udit Narayan, Roop Kumar Rathod and Sadhana Sargam.

Q50825304.lead: Aaa Re Saathi Aa is a 2009 Odia-language film directed by N. Padhi, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra, Sonali Mahapatra, Dushmanta Panda and Payal Banerjee.

p: Rajesh Mallick and Amar Mohanty produced the film. Raman Ranjan wrote the story and Chinmay Das Pattnaik the dialogue, while N. Padhi prepared the screenplay in addition to directing. Ramesh Babu shot the film and Chandrasekhar Mishra edited it. Mihir Das, Snigdha Mohanty, Minaketan, Devi Barik, Biju Badajena, Namrata Das and Jiban Panda were among the supporting cast.
Goodly Rath was the music director. Bapu Goswami, Rajani Ranjan and Nizam wrote the songs, which were sung by Kumar Bapi, Sujit Bhoi, Tapu Mishra and Arabinda Sadangi, among others.

Q21283051.lead: Target is a 2013 Odia-language film directed by S. K. Muralidharan. It marked the screen debut of Amlan Das, son of actor Mihir Das, as a lead actor, opposite Bengali actress Jhilik Bhattacharya.

p: Niranjan Rana produced the film. Gitanjali Rana wrote the story, Muralidharan prepared the screenplay and Debidutta Mohanty is credited as writer. Rabindra Behera handled the cinematography and Manas Ranjan Patra the editing.

Amlan played Bibek and Jhilik played Sneha; both began their careers in Odia cinema with this film. Target was also the first film in which the Odia actresses Aparajita Mohanty and Mahasweta Ray appeared together, with Aparajita cast as Bibek's mother. Minaketan played Nuru Bhai and Pinky Pradhan appeared as a police superintendent.
The score was shared by Abhijit Majumdar and Rabi Narayan Nanda. The soundtrack contained six songs, among them "Eiki Se Prema", "Kie Chhuinla", "Target" and "Tume Mo Nayana Tara".
The film was released on 12 April 2013.

facts: Eiki Se Prema; Kie Chhuinla; Tume Mo Nayana Tara

Q43379258.lead: Aashiq is a 2015 Odia-language film written and directed by Sudhakar Vasant, with Sambit Acharya and Koel Banerjee in the lead roles.

p: Pramod Kumar Swain and Sudhakar Vasant produced the film. Vasant wrote the story and screenplay, and Dr. Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue. R. Bhagat Singh was the cinematographer. Jhilik Bhattacharya was initially chosen as the heroine but was later replaced by Koel Banerjee. Papu Pam Pam, Harihara Mahapatra, Sofia Alam and Saroj Das were in the supporting cast, and both producers also acted in the film.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music to lyrics by Dr. Nirmal Nayak and Nizam. The singers included Goutam Giri, Antara Chakraborty, Humane Sagar, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Satyajit Pradhan, Asima Panda, Tariq Aziz and Asha Panda.
Aashiq opened in 45 cinemas across Odisha on 17 September 2015.

Q110441087.lead: Lucky Ra Lock Down Love Story is a 2020 Odia-language film directed by Ashok Pati and premiered on television, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Tamanna Vyas.

p: The film was shot during the first COVID-19 lockdown. Debidutta Mohanty and Santosh Narayan Dash wrote the story and screenplay, while Monalisa Mohanty and B. Chandan Kumar wrote the dialogue. Sudarshan Senapati was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor. Babi Mishra, Trupti Sinha, Papu Pam Pam, Pradyumna Lenka, Jiban Panda and Choudhury Jayprakash Das appeared in supporting roles.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics. Satyajit Pradhan and Lipsa Mahapatra were among the singers.
The film premiered on Tarang TV and Tarang Plus on 18 October 2020.

Q44817159.lead: Ae Milana Juga Jugara is a 2010 Odia-language film written and directed by Ashok Kumar, with Rajdeep and Elli Padhi in the lead roles.

p: Jharana Mallick and Bijay Barik produced the film. Ashok Kumar wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue and also appeared on screen. Rabindra Behera was the cinematographer and Ashok Sharma the editor. The supporting cast included Chandan Kar, Minaketan, Biju Badajena, Nupur Ghosh, Pushpa Panda and Asit Pati.

Subash Ram composed the music and also sang. Manas, Manoranjan, Arun Mantri and Nizam wrote the songs, with Kumar Bapi, Tapu Mishra, Sakti Mishra, Pami and Sailabhama Mahapatra among the other singers.
The film was released on 13 September 2010.

Q139545798.lead: Kabita Banita Lata 3 is a 2026 Odia-language film directed by Mrutyunjay Sahu that premiered on television. It is the third film released under the Kabita Banita Lata title.

p: Ajay Kumar Rout produced the film. Priyabrata Panda wrote its story, screenplay and dialogue, with Manas Mallick contributing additional dialogue. Sarbeswar Dash was the cinematographer and Pintu Nayak the editor. Jagjit Pal, Sasmita and Ragini Sutradhar played the main roles, supported by Hiranmayee, Biswarupa, Tribhuban Panda, Mihir Swain and Pruthwiraj Nayak, among others.

The film has four songs, with music by Baidyanath Dash, Baibhab Prusty, Sanjay Sahu and Sanjay Dash. Nihar Priyasish, Baibhab Prusty and Panchanan Nayak wrote the lyrics, and the singers included Kuldeep Pattanaik, Antara Chakraborty, Baibhab Prusty, Rajashree Das, Asima Panda and Siddharth Shankar.
The film premiered on Tarang TV and Tarang Plus on 12 April 2026.

Q119889689.lead: Shayari Shayari is a 2023 Odia-language film directed by Ranjit Mohanty, starring Durgamadhab Patra and Priyanka Sahoo.

p: Rajendra Prasad Patra produced the film from a story by Pramod Kumari Patra. Ranjit Mohanty wrote the screenplay and dialogue besides directing. Sudarshan Senapati shot the film and Pintu Nayak edited it. The supporting cast included Pradyumna Lenka, Pintu Nanda, Akshay Bastia, Asit Pati, Braja Singh, Jiban Panda and Alaka Satapathy.

Baidyanath Dash composed the music. Nirmal Nayak, Arun Mantri and Bapu Goswami wrote the lyrics, and the songs were sung by Humane Sagar, Kumar Bapi, Asima Panda, Diptirekha Padhi, Sanju and Amrita Nayak, among others.
The film was released on 14 April 2023, coinciding with Pana Sankranti.

Q141501620.lead: Nirnaya is a 2024 Odia-language film directed by Rajendra Mahanta, with Suryamayee Mohapatra, Naina Das, Sradha Panigrahi and Bijayini Mishra in the cast.

p: Laxmikanta Pattnaik produced the film and also appeared in it. Subhashree Subhasmita Mishra wrote the story and Sumit Panda the dialogue. Deepak Kumar was the cinematographer and Rashmiranjan Dash the editor. Bhaswati Basu, Sukanta Rath and Choudhury Jayprakash Das were also in the cast.

Somesh Satapathy and Gaurav Anand composed the music. The lyrics were by Sumit Panda and Sthita Pattnaik, among others, and the singers included Gaurav Anand, Anuradha Panigrahi, Sanchita Subhadarshini and Ashish Pradhan.
The film opened in cinemas on 26 April 2024.

Q55698207.lead: Hasa Luha Bhara Dunia is a 1990 Odia-language drama film written and directed by Pranab Das, starring Uttam Mohanty, Aparajita Mohanty, Mihir Das, Hara Patnaik and Raimohan Parida.

p: Five young men who grew up together in an orphanage are trying to make their own way in the world when a young woman named Asha turns to them for help. A villain is plotting to murder her and take over her wealth. The five take up her cause and in the end sacrifice their lives to protect the property.

Kalindi Tripathy produced the film and also acted in it. Pranab Das wrote the story and screenplay, and Sirsananda Das Kanungo wrote the dialogue. Asit Padhi was the cinematographer and Bibekananda Satapathy the editor.
Akshaya Mohanty composed the music, with lyrics by Debdas Chhotray and Sirsananda Das Kanungo, among others.
The film was released on 16 March 1990.

Q55465761.lead: Mani Nageswari is a 1995 Odia-language film directed by Bijay Bhaskar, with Siddhanta Mahapatra, Liza, Mihir Das, Debu Bose and Raimohan Parida in the cast.

p: Sanjeev Sahu produced the film. Chanchala Sahu wrote the story and Subodh Pattnaik the dialogue, while Bijay Bhaskar prepared the screenplay as well as directing. B. Satish was the cinematographer and N. Maheswar the editor. Pradyumna Lenka, Runu Parija, Braja Singh, Bina Moharana, Mamina and Saroj Das were among the large supporting cast.

Akshaya Mohanty composed the music. The songs were written by Samanta Nanda Kishore, Nizam, Rabindra Sahu and producer Sanjeev Sahu, and sung by K. S. Chithra, Badri Narayan, Kailash Sahu and T. Souri, among others.

Q21283027.lead: Love Master is a 2012 Odia-language romantic film directed by Himanshu Parija and produced by actress Aparajita Mohanty, starring Babushaan Mohanty, Riya Dey and Poonam Mishra.

p: Actor Uttam Mohanty wrote the story, and Bapu Goswami wrote the dialogue. Dhrubananda Panda was the cinematographer and Sushant Mani the editor. Babushaan played Jeet, with Riya Dey as Ananya and Poonam Mishra as Lagna. Uttam Mohanty appeared as Jeet's father, Mihir Das as Surya Pratap and Aparajita Mohanty as Aparna; Samaresh Routray, Pintu Nanda, Minaketan, Jiban Panda, Saroj Das and Salil Mitra filled other roles.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the soundtrack of six songs, including the title track "Tu Love Master", "Hai Mote Chhapan Chhori", "Mo Mane Prema Sajei" and "Nijaku Pachare".
The film, which runs 154 minutes, was released on 19 October 2012.

facts: Tu Love Master; Hai Mote Chhapan Chhori; Mo Mane Prema Sajei

Q44016098.lead: To Akhire Mun is a 2010 Odia-language film directed by S. K. Muralidharan, with Babushaan Mohanty and Sweety in the lead roles.

p: Prabhas Rout produced the film from a story by Bijayalaxmi Rout. Muralidharan wrote the screenplay and Debidutta Mohanty the dialogue. R. Bhagat Singh was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor. Uttam Mohanty, Aparajita Mohanty, Papu Pam Pam, Salil Mitra, Hara Patnaik and Namrata Das were among the supporting cast.

Bikash Das composed the music. Basantaraj Samal, Mohit Chakraborty and Debidutta Mohanty wrote the lyrics, and the playback singers included Bibhu Kishore, Tapu Mishra, Jolly Mukherjee, Udit Narayan and Suresh Wadkar.
The film was released on 25 March 2010.

Q7585843.lead: Sri Jagannath (also titled Shri Jagannatha) is a 1950 Odia-language mythological film directed by Chitta Ranjan Mitra. By order of release, it was the third feature film made in Odia.

p: The film draws on the culture and traditions surrounding Jagannath. Its narrative concerns the deity's presence on Nila Parvata, where he was worshipped as Nilamadhav.

Ashwini Kumar Ghosh wrote the story and Gopal Chhotray the screenplay. The film was made on a budget of about ₹4,00,000. Gopal Chandra Ghosh played Bidyapati, Gloria Mohanty played Lalita, Chapala Nayak played Nila and Rama Chandra Mania played Bishwabasu; Khagendra Nath Mitra, Samuel Sahu and Bhima Singh were also in the cast. Chapala Nayak, later known as Parbati Ghose, made her first screen appearance here as a child artist.

Ranajit Rai and Balakrishna Dash composed the music, and the lyrics were written by Surendra Kumar Das, Krushna Prasad Basu and Nikunja Kishor Das. The songs included "Nila Sindhu Tire Nila Achala", "Ho, Aja Bane Mausuma", "Piyasi-re Nira Khoje Khira Debi Muhin" and "Katha-tie Kahun".
The film was released on 2 February 1950.

facts: Nila Sindhu Tire Nila Achala; Ho, Aja Bane Mausuma

Q28362920.lead: Pathara Khasuchi Bada Deulu is a 1993 Odia-language film produced, written and directed by Raju Misra, starring Bijay Mohanty, Tandra Ray, Siddhanta Mahapatra, Debu Bose and Sujata Anand.

p: Raju Misra wrote the story and screenplay and shared the cinematography with Samba Siva Rao, while Ramesh Panigrahi wrote the dialogue. Deben Mishra edited the film. Priyanka Mahapatra, Chakradhar Jena, Raimohan Parida, Asrumochan Mohanty and Jayiram Samal were among the supporting cast.

Shantanu Mahapatra composed the music, and Nizam, Sirsananda Das Kanungo and Gurukrushna Goswami wrote the songs. The singers included Debashis Mahapatra, Abhijeet, Kavita Krishnamurthy, Lopita Mishra, Murali Nayak and Mohammed Abid, with Raju Misra and Shantanu Mahapatra also singing.

Q55461527.lead: Tokata Fasigala is a 2018 Odia-language romantic comedy directed by Ramesh Rout, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Elina Samantray, with Papu Pam Pam in a key supporting role.

p: Radhe, played by Papu Pam Pam, is the brother-in-law of the heroine played by Elina Samantray. Wanting to stop her wedding, he asks his friend Bunty (Sabyasachi Mishra) to help him break it off, but Bunty slowly falls in love with her himself.

Sitaram Agrawal and Namita Agrawal produced the film, and Nirmal Nayak wrote the dialogue. Pratap Rout was the cinematographer and Rajesh Das the editor. It was the first feature in which Sabyasachi Mishra and Elina Samantray were paired, although the two had earlier appeared together in an advertisement for Bangur Cement. The film was made in both Odia and Bengali. Lipsa Mishra, Priyanka Panigrahi, Mihir Das, Pradyumna Lenka and Salil Mitra were also in the cast.

Baidyanath Dash composed the music to lyrics by Nirmal Nayak and Arun Mantri. Nibedita, Humane Sagar, Sourin Bhatt, R. S. Kumar, Asima Panda, Arpita and Kaushik sang, and Sabyasachi Mishra and Papu Pam Pam also lent their voices.
The film was released on 12 July 2018, during the Rath Yatra festival.

Q55466014.lead: Nila Mastarani (also spelled Nila Masterani) is a 1996 Odia-language comedy film directed by Chakradhar Sahu, with Minaketan Das and Priyanka Mahapatra in the cast.

p: Rabi Rath produced the film. Its story was written by Godabarish Mohapatra together with the director, Chakradhar Sahu. Chandrasekhar Sahu edited the film, and Malay Mishra composed the music.
In 1997 the film won five Odisha State Film Awards, including the Special Jury Award and the awards for Best Story, Best Recording and Best Actor.

Q122677910.lead: Sankar is a 2023 Odia-language film written and directed by N. Padhi, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra, Supriya Nayak, Debananda and Divya Mohanty.

p: Arabinda Sahu produced the film. N. Padhi wrote the story and screenplay, and Manoranjan Das wrote the dialogue. Ajit Das was the cinematographer. Kuna Tripathy, Krishna Kar, Biju Badajena, Diptirekha Panda, Mita Chakraborty and Nupur Ghosh were among the supporting cast.

Baidyanath Dash composed the music. Arun Mantri, Nirmal Nayak, Surya Mahapatra and Subha Das wrote the lyrics, and the singers included Kuldeep Pattanaik, Udit Narayan, Asima Panda, Diptirekha Padhi, Humane Sagar, Rituraj Mohanty and Priyanka Sahoo.
A theatrical release had been planned for 22 September 2023, but it was postponed, and the film reached cinemas on 29 September 2023.

Q73663470.lead: From Me To You is a 2019 Odia-language film written and directed by Hemant Sahu, with Amlan Das, Jyoti Ranjan Nayak and Sradha Panigrahi in the lead roles.

p: Rajesh Mohanty produced the film. Hemant Sahu wrote the story and screenplay, and Sanjukta Nayak wrote the dialogue. Sitanshu Mahapatra was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor. Pragya Khatua, Bijay Mohanty, Smita Mohanty, Jiban Panda and Pintu Nanda were among the supporting cast.
Prem Anand composed the music and Basantaraj Samal wrote the lyrics. The singers included Humane Sagar, Diptirekha Padhi, Ananya Sritam Nanda, Asima Panda and Ashutosh.
The film was released on 1 November 2019.

Q64912204.lead: Tu Mo Love Story 2 is a 2019 Odia-language film written and directed by Tapas Sargharia. A sequel to the 2017 film Tu Mo Love Story, it stars Swaraj Barik, Bhoomika Dash, Siddhanta Mahapatra and Anu Choudhury.

p: Subhendu Sahu produced the film. Tapas Sargharia wrote the story and shared screenplay credit with Debidutta Mohanty and Ranjan Satapathy, while Dilip Choudhury and Antarjami Sargharia wrote the dialogue. Rabindra Behera was the cinematographer and Rajesh Dash the editor. Namrata Das, Subhasis Sharma and Partha Sarathi Ray also appeared.
Prem Anand composed the music to lyrics by Basantaraj Samal. Humane Sagar, Ananya Sritam Nanda, Lopamudra Dash, Diptirekha Padhi and Sabisesh Mishra were among the singers.
The film was released on 14 June 2019, during the Raja festival.

Q114804696.lead: Bidyarana is a 2022 Odia-language film directed by Jyoti Das, starring Babushaan Mohanty and Sivani Sangita.

p: Niranjan Nayak produced the film. Jyoti Das wrote the screenplay and Bapu Goswami the dialogue. Subrat K. Khatoi and N. Mahendran handled the cinematography, and Chandrasekhar Mishra edited the film. Uttam Mohanty, Soma Bhowmick, Abhishek Giri, Pupul Bhuyan, Piyush Tripathy and Sudhanshu Mohan Sahu were in the supporting cast.

Baidyanath Dash composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak and Bapu Goswami, among others. Gaurav Anand, Asima Panda, Swayam Padhi, Ananya Sritam Nanda, Humane Sagar and Lipsa Mahapatra sang, and Babushaan also sang in the film.
The film was released in cinemas on 1 July 2022, during Rath Yatra. It had its television premiere on Star Kiran on 11 September 2022 and was also made available on Disney+ Hotstar.

Q47090801.lead: Tu Tha Mun Jauchi Rushi is a 2010 Odia-language film written and directed by Sritam Das, his first film as director, starring Arindam Roy and Koel Banerjee.

p: Tribeni Kumar Mohanty produced the film. Sritam Das wrote the story and screenplay and also acted in it, while Chinmay Das Pattnaik wrote the dialogue. Ramesh Babu was the cinematographer. The supporting cast included Mihir Das, Usasi Misra, Jina Samal, Debasish Patra, Suresh Bal, Pradyumna Lenka, Hara Patnaik and Saroj Das.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music and Nizam wrote the lyrics. Majumdar sang alongside Tapu Mishra, Udit Narayan, Pami, Manas Pritam and Babul Supriyo.
The film opened in cinemas on 16 December 2010.
Abhijit Majumdar received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Music Director for the film, his first win in that category.

Q43452720.lead: Kemiti a Bandhan is a 2011 Odia-language film directed by Saroj Satapathy, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Arpita Mukherjee. It marked the Odia film debut of Hindi actor Chandrachur Singh.

p: Pradeep Kumar Sahu produced the film and wrote its story. Saroj Satapathy wrote the screenplay and Dr. Rajani Ranjan the dialogue. Rabi and B. Satish handled the cinematography, and Samir Ranjan Das and Rabi Shankar Patnaik edited the film. Anu Choudhury, Bijay Mohanty, Mahasweta Ray, Mihir Das, Harihara Mahapatra and Asrumochan Mohanty were also in the cast.

Prem Anand composed the music. Arun Mantri, Basantaraj Samal, Nizam and Prabodh Rout wrote the songs, which were sung by Alka Yagnik, Tapu Mishra, Kumar Bapi, Mohammed Aziz, Sakti Mishra, Pami and Sricharan Mohanty, among others.

Q33125764.lead: Tamaku Dekhila Pare is a 2017 Odia-language film directed by Chandan Mahapatra, with Sambit Acharya, Siddhanta Mahapatra, Jhilik Bhattacharya and Naina Das in the lead roles.

p: Subham Padhi produced the film. Bharati Padhi wrote the story, Chandan Mahapatra the screenplay and Alok Ray the dialogue. Dhrubananda Panda was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor. Harihara Mahapatra, Minaketan, Mihir Das, Priyanka Pattnaik, Pradyumna Lenka and Jiban Panda were in the supporting cast.

Malay Mishra composed the music and Arun Mantri wrote the lyrics. The songs were sung by Ira Mohanty, Humane Sagar, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Sailabhama Mishra, Abhijit Mishra, Nabhya, Prafulla Behera and Bibhu Kishore.
The film was released on 13 January 2017.

Q109519692.lead: Arundhati is a 2021 Odia-language film directed by Ramesh Rout, starring Rajveer Deo, in his first Odia film, and Elina Samantray in the title role.

p: Ramesh Barik and Amitabh Mallick produced the film. Khageswar Sejpada wrote the story, and Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue and co-wrote the screenplay with Ramesh Rout. Pratap Rout was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor. Rajveer Deo played Shiba, and the supporting cast included Sanjay Bhol, Babi Mishra, Pradyumna Lenka, Jaya Swami, Pratibha Panda and Jiban Panda.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics. Sohini Mishra, Amrita Nayak and Satyajit Pradhan were among the singers.
The film was released on 13 October 2021 and was later made available on Disney+ Hotstar.

Q109519686.lead: Bapa ICU Re Achhanti is a 2021 Odia-language film directed by Tapas Sargharia that premiered on television, with Jagjit Pal and Mitali Sargharia in the lead roles.

p: Arun Sahu produced the film. Debidutta Mohanty wrote its story, screenplay and dialogue. Rabindra Behera and Bhagat Singh were the cinematographers, and Rajesh Dash edited the film. Pradyumna Lenka, Satyaki Mishra, Ratan Meher, Usasi Misra, Madhumita Mohanty, Saroj Das and Ilu Banerjee were among the supporting cast.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music, and the lyrics were by Nirmal Nayak and Debidutta Mohanty, among others. Swayam Padhi, Abhijit Majumdar, Amrita Nayak and Karunakar sang.
The film premiered on Tarang TV and Tarang Plus on 31 October 2021.

Q114804732.lead: Rudrani is a 2022 Odia-language film written and directed by K. Muralikrishna, produced by and starring actress Jhilik Bhattacharya.

p: K. Muralikrishna wrote the story and screenplay, and Rajani Ranjan wrote the dialogue. Iswar Chandra Barik was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor. Alongside Jhilik Bhattacharya, the cast included Subhasis Sharma, Tutu Nayak, Babi Mishra, Pintu Nanda, Lohitakshya Pattnaik, Ilu Banerjee, Jiban Panda, Choudhury Jayprakash Das and Dharitri Khandual.
Prem Anand composed the music and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics. The singers included Satyajit Pradhan, Ananya Sritam Nanda, Humane Sagar, Diptirekha Padhi and Sasanka Sekhar.
The film was released on 21 October 2022.

Q56025365.lead: Thakura Achanti Chaubahaku is a 1990 Odia-language film directed by Bijay Bhaskar, featuring Uttam Mohanty, Suresh Bal, Debu Bose, Anita Das, Bijay Mohanty and Gloria Mohanty.

p: Dillip Mishra and Biswanath Mishra produced the film, and Biswanath Mishra also wrote the story. Ramesh Panigrahi wrote the dialogue and Bijay Bhaskar the screenplay. Samba Siva Rao was the cinematographer and Anil Malnad the editor. Jayiram Samal, Ananga Dwivedi, Tushar Panigrahi, Runu Parija, Premanjan Parida and Braja Singh were among the supporting cast.

Akshaya Mohanty composed the music and also wrote lyrics, together with Sirsananda Das Kanungo, Dillip Mishra and Tutu Mishra. Mohammed Abid, Gita Dash, Subash Das and Bibhu Kishore were among the singers.

Q46067987.lead: Mu Raja Tu Rani is a 2013 Odia-language film directed by Sudhanshu Mohan Sahu, starring Arindam Roy and newcomer Sambhabana Mohanty.

p: Atisa Kumar Rout produced the film from a story by Amiyabala Rout. Pradipta Nanda wrote the dialogue and co-wrote the screenplay with the director. Niranjan Das was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor.

Arindam Roy played Bijay and Sambhabana Mohanty played Chandrika; the film was Sambhabana's acting debut. She is the daughter of actress Snigdha Mohanty. Siddhanta Mahapatra appeared as ACP Arya Kumar, Harihara Mahapatra as Mama, Akshay Bastia as Kirtan and Anita Das as Bijay's mother.
Malay Mishra composed the music. Nimai Mohanty, Arun Mantri and Amiyabala Rout wrote the songs, which were sung by Ira Mohanty, Udit Narayan and Suresh Wadkar, among others.
The film was released on 14 October 2013.

Q55439516.lead: Maa is a 1992 Odia-language film produced and directed by Prashanta Nanda, starring Uttam Mohanty, Aparajita Mohanty, Hara Patnaik, Prosenjit Chatterjee, Namrata Das and Raimohan Parida.

p: Besides producing and directing, Prashanta Nanda wrote the screenplay and edited the film. Basanta Nayak wrote the story and Bijay Mishra the dialogue. V. Prabhakar was the cinematographer. The cast also included Rakhee Gulzar, Abhishek Chatterjee, Biplab Chatterjee, Ritu Das, Satabdi Roy, Suresh Bal and Debu Brahma.

Rahul Dev Burman composed the music and Swarup Nayak wrote the lyrics. The playback singers included Asha Bhosle, Kavita Krishnamurthy, Amit Kumar, Babla Mehta, Lopita Mishra, Debashis Mahapatra, Jolly Mukherjee and Swagatika Sen, and actor Uttam Mohanty also sang.

Q122802835.lead: Kasturi is a 2023 Odia-language film written and directed by Sangram Mohanty, with Dushmanta Panda, Cookies Swain and Sanjay Patra in the main roles.

p: Sanjay Kumar Patra produced the film and also played one of the leads. Sangram Mohanty wrote the story and screenplay, and Bhaba Binod Mahapatra wrote the dialogue. Gopal Krishna Sahu was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor. Asrumochan Mohanty, Pradyumna Lenka, Bijayini Mishra, Pratibha Panda and Pruthwiraj Nayak were among the supporting cast.

Sibu Jena composed the music to lyrics by Bijay Malla, Arun Mantri and Panchanan Nayak. Humane Sagar, Asima Panda, Sourav Nayak, Sohini Mishra, Arabinda Dutta, Nazia Alam and Saroj Pradhan were among the singers.
The film was released on 17 September 2023.

Q44706712.lead: Tora More Jodi Sundara is a 2010 Odia-language film directed by Debu Pattnaik, starring Sabyasachi Mishra, Archita Sahu and Arpita Mukherjee.

p: Adhiraj Panigrahi produced the film. Debu Pattnaik wrote the story and shared screenplay credit with Subodh Pattnaik, who also wrote the dialogue. Dhrubananda Panda was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor. Debu Bose, Mihir Das, Pradyumna Lenka, Harihara Mahapatra, Bijay Mohanty, Pintu Nanda and Hara Patnaik were among the supporting cast.

Shantiraj Khosla composed the music. Basantaraj Samal, Arun Mantri and Bijay Malla wrote the songs, and the playback singers included Mohammed Aziz, Sunidhi Chauhan, Ira Mohanty, Udit Narayan, Sanghamitra, Sadhana Sargam and Shaan.
The film was released on 3 September 2010.

Q114804721.lead: Bali - The Saviour is a 2022 Odia-language film written and directed by K. Muralikrishna, starring its producer Suryakant Samal alongside Mama Samal.

p: K. Muralikrishna wrote the story and screenplay. Narendra Goud and Pratap Rout handled the cinematography, and Ranjan Khatei edited the film. Manoj Mishra, Asrumochan Mohanty, Smita Mohanty, Choudhury Jayprakash Das, Harihara Mahapatra and Chintamani Biswal were in the supporting cast.

Sanjay Situ composed the music, and Satyananda Nayak, Deepak and Bunty wrote the lyrics. Humane Sagar, Asima Panda, Tariq Aziz, Arpita Choudhury, Sasanka Sekhar and Diptirekha Padhi sang, as did Mama Samal. The songs were launched at Lohia Academy on 20 November 2022, the day of Kartika Purnima.
The film was released on 23 September 2022.

Q112155187.lead: Kukuda Chor is a 2022 film in the Koraputia variety of Odia, directed by Ananda Kumar and produced by Subhendu Padhi.

p: Jiban Mishra wrote the story, Ananda Kumar wrote the screenplay, and Rajendra Padhi is credited as writer. Ranjan was the cinematographer, and Rajib and Rahul edited the film. The cast included Pragya, Suman, Archi, Gutu, Raja, K. Mohan Rao and Lal Bahadur Mallick, with producer Subhendu Padhi also appearing on screen.
Mitu Suna composed the music, and Jiban Mishra wrote all four songs. Mitu Suna sang along with Dushmanta Suna, Kalicharan Bag, Amrita Nayak, Sanju Mohanty and Antara Chakraborty.
The film opened on 27 May 2022 at the S.R. Mall cinema in Jeypore.

Q139964660.lead: Motorcycle is a 2025 Odia-language film directed by Ashwini Tripathy, starring Jyoti Ranjan Nayak and Preeti Biswal.

p: Jhuni Lata Biswal produced the film. Amit Kumar Dash and Pranab Prasanna Rath wrote the screenplay and dialogue. Akshaya Kumar Nayak was the cinematographer and Manas Kumar Sahu the editor. Jyoti Ranjan Nayak played Kelu and Preeti Biswal played Kaberi; Abhishek Panda (Raja), Kuna Tripathy (Harischandra), Alisha Samantaray (Madhuri), Sushant Dashmahapatra (Kunja Bihari), Pruthwiraj Nayak (Madhu Babu) and Bhaswati Basu (Basanti) filled other roles.
Somesh Satapathy composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak and J. P. Wordsmith. Gobinda Chandra, Humane Sagar and Ananya Sritam Nanda were among the singers.
The film opened in cinemas on 19 December 2025.

Q55455011.lead: Vasudha is a 1996 Odia-language film directed by Avatar Singh, with Bijay Mohanty, Tandra Ray, Mihir Das, Bina Moharana and Jayiram Samal in the cast.

p: Basudev Tripathy produced the film, wrote its story together with Avatar Singh, and also acted in it. Singh wrote the screenplay and Nizam the dialogue. Samba Siva Rao was the cinematographer and Madan Mohan Prasad the editor. Liza, Trupti Sinha, Braja Singh, Debu Brahma, Arabinda Sadangi and Saroj Das were among the supporting cast.

Amarendra Mohanty composed the music to lyrics by Nizam and Sirsananda Das Kanungo. The singers included Bhikari Bal, Nandita Bhanja, Trupti Das, Gita Das, Sakti Mishra, Prasanjit Mohanty and Debashis Mahapatra.
The film was released on 14 July 1996.

Q47335484.lead: Mate Ani Dela Lakhye Faguna is a 2008 Odia-language film directed by Sanjay Nayak, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Archita Sahu.

p: Sarada Prasanna Panda, Ranjan Kumar Palai and Prashant Kumar Martha produced the film, with Panda also writing the story. Sanjay Nayak wrote the screenplay and edited the film in addition to directing it. Ranjan Mishra and Satya Pattnaik were the cinematographers. Siddhanta Mahapatra, Anita Das, Pradyumna Lenka, Namrata Das, Trupti Sinha, Saroj Das and Mihir Das were among the supporting cast.

Shantiraj Khosla composed the music. Basantaraj Samal, Arun Mantri and Nirmal Nayak wrote the songs, and the singers included Kumar Bapi, Sasmita Mishra, Tapu Mishra, Sakti Mishra, Sahadev Nayak, Pami and Sailabhama Mahapatra.

Q109519706.lead: Ea Bi Gote Love Story is a 2021 Odia-language film directed by Mrutyunjay Sahu that premiered on television, starring Raj Rajesh Panda, Divya Mohanty, Rakesh Deo and Deepika Tripathy.

p: Ramesh Barik and K. Tamanna produced the film. Debidutta Mohanty wrote the story and screenplay, and B. Chandan Kumar wrote the dialogue. S. Ranjan was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor. Divya Mohanty played Sweety; Amelie Panda, Pintu Nanda, Bhupati Tripathy and Guddu were in the supporting cast, and Sivani Sangita made a guest appearance.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak, Tapu Nayak and Debidutta Mohanty. The singers included Humane Sagar, Swayam Padhi, Satyajit Pradhan, Tariq Aziz, Jagruti Mishra, Amrita Nayak and Sweta Mishra.
The film premiered on television on 20 June 2021.

Q50825301.lead: Tu Mori Pain is a 2009 Odia-language film directed by Jayaprakash Mohanty, starring Sabyasachi Mishra and Lipi Parida.

p: Dibya Jyoti, Chittaranjan Prusty and Ashok Sahu produced the film. Diptimayee Mohanty wrote the story and screenplay, and Pradeep Nanda the dialogue. Ashok Darshan was the cinematographer and Ajay Mishra the editor. Mihir Das, Runu Parija, George Tiadi, Anita Das, Harihara Mahapatra, Uttam Mohanty and Salil Mitra were among the supporting cast.

The director, Jayaprakash Mohanty, shared music credit with Prem Anand, and also wrote lyrics and sang. The other lyricists included Bijay Malla and Arun Mantri, and the other singers included Tapu Mishra, Sakti Mishra, Sanju Mohanty, Sourav and Sricharan Mohanty.

Q119889707.lead: Love In London is a 2023 Odia-language film directed by Tapas Sargharia, starring Anubhav Mohanty, Swapna Priyadarshini and Somya Sachdeva.

p: Naveen Bhandari and J. Barkha produced the film. Tapas Sargharia wrote the story, Suresh Pattnaik the screenplay and Antarjami Sargharia the dialogue. Subrat Kumar Khatoi was the cinematographer and Rajesh Dash the editor. Anubhav Mohanty played Prem, Swapna Priyadarshini played Sophie and Somya Sachdeva played Sweta, while Saroj Parida appeared as Professor Mohit Sharma.

The music was composed by Baidyanath Dash, Somesh Satapathy, Asad Nizam and Binay Rath. Nirmal Nayak, Biraj Rath and J. P. Wordsmith wrote the lyrics, and the singers included Humane Sagar, Asima Panda, Biraj Rath, Gaurav Anand, Smrutika Padhi and Kuldeep Pattanaik.
The film opened in cinemas on 13 June 2023, at the time of the Raja festival.

Q112510488.lead: Biswanath is a 2022 Odia-language film directed by Bobbili Kiran, starring Sambit Acharya, Sambhabana Mohanty and Sangita.

p: Dindu Shankar Goud produced the film. Bobbili Kiran wrote the story, K. Murali Krishna the screenplay and Rajani Ranjan the dialogue. Chandra Kiran was the cinematographer and Kishore the editor. Mihir Das, Pruthwiraj Nayak, Raimohan Parida, Pratibha Panda, Salil Mitra and Pintu Nanda were among the supporting cast, and Ananya Mishra featured in an item song.

Abhijit Majumdar composed the music, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak and Basantaraj Samal, among others. Rituraj Mohanty, Swayam Padhi, Rajnandini Panda, Humane Sagar, Sohini Mishra, Rozalin Sahu and Jagruti Mishra were among the singers.
The film had been due for release in 2018, but was delayed, partly by the COVID-19 pandemic, and finally opened on 12 June 2022.

Q114804706.lead: Sesha Rati is a 2022 Odia-language film directed by Amaresh Pati, with Debasish Patra and Riya Dey in the lead roles.

p: Kumar Pritam Sahu produced the film. Shashank Nayak wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue. Swarnaprasad was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor. The supporting cast included Subhangi Jena, Debu Brahma, Usasi Misra, Choudhury Jayprakash Das, Biren Mishra, Abhipsa Bhanja and Pintu Nanda.
Asad Nizam composed the music and Pushpak Parida wrote the lyrics. Humane Sagar, Kuldeep Pattanaik, Asima Panda and Ashutosh Sadangi were among the singers.
The film was released on 5 August 2022.

Q114804717.lead: Mahabahu is a 2022 Odia-language film written and directed by actor Sritam Das, starring Akash Dasnayak, Poonam Mishra and Tanushree Dash.

p: Ramesh Barik and K. Tamanna produced the film, and Tamanna also appeared in it. Sritam Das wrote the story and screenplay and acted in a supporting role, while Saranarabinda Ojha wrote the dialogue. Rabindra Behera was the cinematographer and Rajesh Dash the editor. Usasi Misra, Harihara Mahapatra, Tapi Mishra, Debendra Pati and Saroj Das were also in the cast.

Prem Anand composed the music to lyrics by Saranarabinda Ojha and Premananda. Diptirekha Padhi, Humane Sagar, Alaka Abhilekha, Sasanka Sekhar, Sourav Bharadwaj, Antara Chakraborty and Charan Mohanty were among the singers.
The film opened in cinemas on 2 September 2022.

Q73532073.lead: Baala - The Rhythm of Life is a 2019 Odia-language film written and directed by Amaresh Pati. It marked the screen debut of Sameer Satpathy, who played the lead opposite Divya Mohanty and Ananya Mishra.

p: Jagi Mangat Panda produced the film. Amaresh Pati wrote the story and Sanjay Mahakul the dialogue. Dipankar Jahna was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor. Aparajita Mohanty, Salil Mitra, Jay Prakash Das, Ananta Mishra and Aishwarya were among the supporting cast.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the music and also sang, and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics. The other singers included Humane Sagar, James Bharat and Sanju Mohanty.
The film was released on 1 November 2019. Its first screening took place at the Jayashree cinema hall in Cuttack, where bald viewers were admitted free of charge.

Q119889708.lead: Guddu Gangster is a 2023 Odia-language film directed by Ashok Pati, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra, Sailendra Samantray, Sivani Sangita and Namrata Thapa.

p: Pritam Sahu produced the film, and Bharadwaj Panda wrote its story, screenplay and dialogue. Swarna Prasad was the cinematographer and Manas Kumar Sahu the editor. Sailendra Samantray played the title character Guddu and Siddhanta Mahapatra played Gangadhar. Babi Mishra, Elli Padhi, Krishna Kar, Choudhury Jayprakash Das, Rakhee Dash, Jiban Panda and Suryamayee Mohapatra were also in the cast.

Asad Nizam composed the music. Pushpak Parida, Ranjan Nayak and Tapu Nayak wrote the lyrics, and the singers included Nabhya Jyoti, Kuldeep Pattanaik, Asima Panda, Humane Sagar, Antara Chakraborty and Swayam Padhi.
The film opened in more than 40 cinemas across Odisha on 13 June 2023, coinciding with the Raja festival.

Q56418449.lead: Suna Sankhali is a 2003 Odia-language film written and directed by Ravi Kinagi, with Jeet, Swastika Mukherjee and Barsha Priyadarshini in the leading roles.

p: Ravi Kinagi was responsible for the story, the screenplay and the direction, and is also credited with the editing. Pradeep Bhol produced the film, Subodh Patnaik wrote the dialogue and Dilip Ray was the cinematographer. The Bengali actor Jeet played one of the leads, and the supporting cast included Mihir Das, Harihara Mohapatra, Debu Bose, Hara Patnaik and Suresh Bal.

Manmath Mishra directed the music and also wrote lyrics, alongside Shirshananda Das Kanungo. The playback singers included Mohammed Aziz, Lopita Mishra, Sweta Mishra, Arabinda Muduli, Rudra, Sadhana Sargam and Suresh Wadkar.

Q109474580.lead: Chal Tike Prema Kariba is an Odia-language film directed by Saroj Kant and produced by Chinmayee Priyadarshini, who also stars in it alongside Devraj and Lipsa Mishra. It was released on 22 October 2021.

p: Debaki Sahu wrote the story and Ashutosh Barik the dialogue, while Saroj Kant prepared the screenplay in addition to directing. Dhiren Sahu was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor. Salil Mitra, Pupinder Singh, Biren Mishra, Pragyan Khatua, Guddu, Jiban Panda and Saroj Das were among the supporting cast.
Bibhuti Bhusan Gadanayak composed the music to lyrics by Panchanan Nayak. Humane Sagar, Tapu Mishra, Pragyan Hota, Satyajit Pradhan, Abhijit Majumdar and Abhijit Mishra sang the songs.

Q56423987.lead: Maa Gojabayani is a 1999 Odia-language film directed by Basant Sahu, with Manoj Panda and Anu Choudhury in the main roles.

p: Sanak Debata produced the film and wrote its story. Basant Sahu wrote the screenplay as well as directing, and Shirshananda Das Kanungo supplied the dialogue. Samba Siva Rao handled the camera and Ashok Sharma the editing. The film marked the Odia screen debut of the actresses Anu Choudhury and Kuna Tripathy. Namrata Das, Pradyumna Lenka, Pintu Nanda, Binayak Mishra, Priyambada Roy and Trupti Sinha also appeared.
Swarup Nayak was the music director. The lyrics came from Shirshananda Das Kanungo and Suresh Parida, and Srikanta Das, Trupti Das and Ghanashyam Panda were among the singers.

Q15725112.lead: Raju Awara is a 2012 Odia-language film written and directed by Debanand Nayak, starring Akash Dasnayak and Arpita Mukherjee.

p: Elora Priyadarshini and Santosh Tripathy produced the film. Debanand Nayak wrote the story and screenplay, directed, and is also credited as editor, while S. Ranjan was the cinematographer. Bijay Mohanty, Namrata Das, Choudhury Jayaprakash Das, Pragyan Khatua and Jayiram Samal were in the supporting cast.

Bidyadhar Sahu directed the music. Mohit Chakraborty, Chintamani Das, Banaja Mahapatra, Debanand Nayak and Panchanan Nayak wrote the songs, which were sung by Antara Mitra, Sanju Mohanty, Arabinda Muduli, Pradeep and Sourav, among others.
The film was released on 2 March 2012.

Q56061898.lead: Dharma Nikiti is a 1999 Odia-language film directed by Sangram Biswal, featuring Siddhanta Mahapatra, Mihir Das, Debu Brahma and Suresh Bal.

p: Phelu Mohanty and Kanwaljit Singh produced the film, and Shirshananda Das Kanungo wrote the dialogue. Samba Siva Rao was the cinematographer and A. Sreekar Prasad the editor. The large cast also included Minaketan, Namrata Das, Saroj Das, Pradyumna Lenka, Shweta Malik, Rabi Mishra, Aparajita Mohanty, Uttam Mohanty and Jayiram Samal.

Deepak Kumar composed the score. Lyrics were written by Shirshananda Das Kanungo, Phelu Mohanty and Nizam, and the singers included Mohammed Aziz, Sonu Nigam, Purnima, Mohammed Sajid, Kumar Sanu and Sadhana Sargam.

Q28946521.lead: Samaya Bada Balaban is a 2016 Odia-language film directed by S. K. Muralidharan and produced by Pupinder Singh, who plays the lead opposite Anubha Sourya and Lipsa Mishra.

p: The film borrowed its title from an earlier Odia film of 1985. Pupinder Singh produced it with Suren Mahapatra and Atmaprakash Panda as co-producers. Rajani Ranjan wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue. Senior actors Asrumochan Mohanty, Pushpa Panda, Pratibha Panda, Suresh Bal and Jiban Panda appeared in supporting parts.
Abhijit Majumdar set Nirmal Nayak's lyrics to music, and the vocals were by Nabhya, Sanju and Majumdar himself.
It was released on 4 March 2016.

Q36976021.lead: Just Mohabbat is a 2017 Odia-language film directed by S. K. Muralidharan, starring Akash Dasnayak and Archita Sahu.

p: Kalyan Sundar Chhotaray and Samaresh Routray produced the film, and Bapu Goswami wrote the dialogue. R. Bhagat shot it and Biren Jyoti Mohanty edited it. Akash Dasnayak played an assistant director. Samaresh Routray, Papu Pam Pam, Dhir Mallik and Ankita were also in the cast; the Bengali actress Ankita made her first Odia film appearance here.

Abhijit Majumdar was the music director and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics. The songs were launched on 13 August 2017 at the Odisha Press Club, at an event attended by Archita Sahu, Akash Dasnayak, Papu Pam Pam, Samaresh Routray and Tapu Mishra.
The film opened on 25 August 2017, the day of Ganesh Puja.
Archita Sahu received the best actress award at the Pratibha Samman ceremony held by the film magazine Chalachitra Jagat.

Q42126478.lead: Bhairaba is a 2017 Odia-language film directed by Mrutyunjay Sahu, with Asit, Ahana Baral and Elsa Ghosh in the leading roles.

p: Sisir Chandra Das and Prabhat Kumar Pradhan produced the film, and Debidatta Mohanty wrote the dialogue. S. Ranjan was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor. Papu Pam Pam, Pintu Nanda, Samaresh Routray, Shakti Baral, Debu Brahma, Hadu, Biju Badajena and Devi Barik were among the supporting players.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the songs, with lyrics by Nirmal Nayak. Majumdar and Papu Pam Pam were among the singers.
The film came out on 8 September 2017, the same day as another Odia release, Mu Khanti Odia Jhia, and both films did good business.
Ahana won the award for best female newcomer at the 12th film and television awards, Show Time 2018.

Q43706284.lead: Don is a 2010 Odia-language film directed by Sudhanshu Mohan Sahu, starring Anubhav Mohanty and Lovely.

p: Sanjay Nayak and Binay Nayak produced the film. Ranjit Patnaik wrote both the screenplay and the dialogue. Ramesh Babu was behind the camera and Chandrasekhar Mishra edited. Babi Mishra, Debjani, Siddhanta Mahapatra, Aurosmita, Bijay Mohanty and Uttam Mohanty were also cast, and the director appeared on screen as well.
The music was composed jointly by Shantiraj Khosla and Swarup Nayak, and the lyrics were by Nizam and Swarup Nayak. Anubhav Mohanty sang one of the songs himself.
Released on 15 January 2010, the film did not do well and incurred a commercial loss.

Q98821826.lead: Kie Kahara is a 1997 Odia-language film written and directed by Avtar Singh, featuring Bijay Mohanty, Tandra Ray, Uttam Mohanty, Mihir Das and Kuna Tripathy.

p: H. Anraj and Laxminarayan Agarwal produced the film. Avtar Singh wrote the story and screenplay in addition to directing, while Sanjay Nayak wrote the dialogue. Narayan Kumar was the cinematographer and Deben Mishra the editor. The cast also included Munna Khan, Namrata Das, Asrumochan Mohanty, Suresh Bal, Debu Bose, Jayiram Samal and Mamina. Kuna Tripathy began an Odia film career with this film.

Saroj Nanda composed the music, and Nizam and Alekh Biswal wrote the lyrics. Debasish Mahapatra, Geeta Das, Bishnu, T. Souri, Mohammed Sajid, Pritinanda Routray and Anita Goswami were among the singers.
The film was released on 3 July 1997.

Q35138705.lead: Tu Mora Sapana Rani is a 2016 Odia-language film produced and directed by Prashant Pal, with Santosh Mohanty in the lead role.

p: Prashant Pal wrote the story, directed and produced the film, with Janakinath Parida and Soubhagya Kumar Parida as co-producers. Santosh Mohanty, the lead actor, also wrote the screenplay and dialogue. The cinematography was credited to Ajit, Chandan and Keshu, and the editing to Manas. Biswa, Rozalin, Janaki, Sharmistha, Asrumochan Mohanty and Krushna Tripathy were in the supporting cast.
P. Kumar was the music director, and the lyrics were by Manas Samal and Gagan Rout. Udit Narayan, Mohammed Aziz, Kumar Bapi, Pankaj Jal, Sanju, Asima Panda and Rashmi were among the singers.
It was released on 3 June 2016.

Q117221490.lead: Bajiba Lo Sahanai is a 2023 Odia-language film written and directed by the actor and playwright Ashutosh Mahapatra, starring Amlan Das, Jhillik Bhattacharya and Sambit Acharya.

p: Janmejay Dogra produced the film. Ashutosh Mahapatra wrote the story and screenplay, co-wrote the dialogue with Biswa, directed, and also acted in it. The title comes from his first jatra play, which had been staged by Gouri Gananatya. Bibhu Prasad Mishra was the cinematographer. Raimohan Parida, Pratibha Panda, Dharitri Khandual, Jayiram Samal, Asrumochan Mohanty and Manisha Mishra played supporting roles.
Tapas Das and Amrutanshu Pattnaik composed the music, and Humane Sagar and Bibhu Kishore were among the singers.
The film opened in cinemas on 3 March 2023.

facts: Title of Ashutosh Mahapatra's jatra play Bajiba Lo Sahanai

Q140198779.lead: Chhaki Suna is a 2026 Odia-language film written and directed by Manas Padhiary, with Anubhav Mohanty and Sambhabana Mohanty in the lead roles.

p: Nabin Bhandari, Jagruti A. Mohanty, Subham Mohanty and Suraj Mahant produced the film. Manas Padhiary wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue as well as directing. Deepak Kumar handled the cinematography and Rashmi Ranjan Dash the editing. The supporting cast included Abhishek Panda, Divya Mohanty, Choudhury Jayprakash Das, Sukumar Tudu, Sukanta Rath, Neetu Singh, Udit Guru, Tapas Sargharia and Jitu Mangaraj.

Baidyanath Dash directed the music, with lyrics by Pramod Parida and Nihar Priyadarshi. Anubhav Mohanty, Papu Pam Pam, Swayam Padhi and Antara Chakraborty sang. The songs were remakes of numbers originally composed by Abhijit Majumdar.
The film, which runs 146 minutes, was released on 12 June 2026.

Q42377734.lead: Om Sai Tujhe Salam is a 2013 Odia-language film directed by Biswajit Mohanty, in which Anshuman, Dipak Das, Bhagyalaxmi and Puja Chakraborty played the main roles.

p: Kali Prasanna Satpathy and Sudha Patnaik produced the film. Bharati Das wrote the story and dialogue, and Biswajit Mohanty prepared the screenplay besides directing. All four lead actors made their Odia film debuts here. Uttam Mohanty, Kuna Tripathy, Gyanaranjan Nayak, Snigdha Mohanty, Jayiram Samal, Debu Brahma, Braja Singh and Prasanna Patsani were among the other performers.
Bidyut Ray was the music director and Panchanan Nayak wrote the lyrics. Goutam Giri, Arabinda, Sourav Nayak, Tapu Mishra, Pami and Sweta Mishra sang the songs.
It was released on 30 August 2013.

facts: Anshuman, Dipak Das, Bhagyalaxmi, Puja Chakraborty

Q140428675.lead: Shri Jagannath Nka Nabakalebara is a 2025 Odia-language film directed by Soubhagyalaxmi Jena, featuring Siddhanta Mahapatra, Sritam Das, Pinky Pradhan and Jyoti Ranjan Nayak.

p: Dilip Kumar Jena and Soubhagyalaxmi Jena produced the film, and Shankar Prasad Tripathy wrote its story, screenplay and dialogue. Dhrubananda Panda was the cinematographer and Sukumar Mani the editor. Sibani Sangita, Anshuman, Suryamayee Mohapatra, Nabhpreet Arora, Kuna Tripathy, Asrumochan Mohanty, Kedar Mishra, Pratibha Panda, Saheb Singh and Ratan Meher were also in the cast.
