Q40435663.lead: Ameta Toka Sandha Marka is a 2014 Odia-language film directed by R. Bhagat Singh and produced by Sangita Satpathy, with Papu Pam Pam and Koel Banerjee in the lead roles.

p: R. Bhagat Singh also served as cinematographer, and Deepak Jena wrote the dialogue. The supporting cast included Mihir Das, Priyanka Mahapatra, Hara Rath, Arabinda Sadangi, Minaketan, Rajiv and Asim Basu.
Abhijit Majumdar composed the songs, which were written by Nizam and Nirmal Nayak.
The film opened on 29 August 2014.

Q56860601.lead: Mana Khali Tate Chahen is a 2018 Odia-language film directed by Nimai Ojha, starring Sambit Acharya and Ankita in the lead roles.

p: Kanhei Meher and Deepak Sahu produced the film. Kailash Sahu wrote the story, and Nimai Ojha prepared the screenplay as well as directing. Chitta Biswal was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor.
Bijay Mohanty, Anita Das, Harihara Mohapatra, Choudhury Jayaprakash Das, Anshuman and Debi appeared in supporting roles.
The music was directed by Abhijit Majumdar.
The film was released on 28 September 2018.

Q140798373.lead: Angel is a 2025 Odia-language film written and directed by Jitendriya Pradhan and produced by Sanghamitra Behera. It was released in cinemas on 31 January 2025.

p: Jitendriya Pradhan wrote the story and also acted in the film. Judhisthira Behera was the cinematographer. The cast included Partha Sarathi Ray, Kavya Keeran, Prasanjeet Mohapatra, Sai Trishna, Abhishek Mohanty, Sarbeswar Sutar, Tukun, Amitabh Patra, Sushil Mishra and Pratima.
The film had a theatrical release on 31 January 2025.

Q15724261.lead: Thukul is a 2012 Odia-language film written, directed and scored by Prashanta Nanda and produced by Akshaya Kumar Parija. Babushaan Mohanty, Archita Sahu and Prakruti Mishra played the main roles.

p: Prashanta Nanda handled the story, screenplay and editing as well as direction, while Abhiram Mishra was the cinematographer. Prakruti Mishra, who had earlier worked as a child artist, took on her first role as a heroine in this film.
The cast also included Samaresh Routray, Kuna Tripathy, Sritam Das, Pupinder Singh, Illu Banerjee, Aparajita Mohanty and Minaketan.

Prashanta Nanda composed the songs and wrote their lyrics. The playback singers included Udit Narayan, Babul Supriyo, Krishna, Sadhana Sargam, Prashant Muduli, Subhashish Mahakud, Sangram, Pami, Ira Mohanty, Sohini and Sangita Gosain.
The film was released on 12 January 2012.

Q139807357.lead: Swapna Sundari is a 2026 Odia-language film directed by Pinu Nayak and produced by Sitaram Agrawal and Namita Agrawal. It premiered on television.

p: Bijay Raul wrote the story. Shubham was the cinematographer and Deepak Sahu edited the film. Bikram Mohanty and Mithi headed the cast, which also included Tanmay, Dan, Mahaprasad Kar and Chintamani Biswal. The film was made under the Siddharth Movies banner.
Sarthak Agrawal composed the music to lyrics by Arun Mantri. The songs were sung by Arpita Choudhury, Sheikh Taufiq Alli, Swarup Gautam and Shraddha Shree.
The film was released on television on 26 April 2026, with Sidharth TV as distributor.

Q29110267.lead: Jay Maa Mangala is a 1980 Odia-language film directed by Akshaya Mohanty (Kashyap) and produced by Jatadhari Mishra.

p: Akshaya Mohanty (Kashyap) and Rabindra Das shared the writing. B. D. Mathur was the cinematographer and Ajay Kumar the editor. The cast included Samuel Sahu, Mahasweta Ray, Deepa Sahu, Chakrapani, Babu Singh and Roja Ramani.
Basudeba Rath directed the music. Narayan Prasad Singh and Sarod Nayak were among the lyricists, and the songs were sung by singers including Bhubaneswari Mishra, Vani Jairam and Chakrapani.
The film was released on 10 July 1980.

Q64867054.lead: Bobal Toka is a 2019 Odia-language film directed by Sudhakar Vasant, who also co-produced it with Prakash Srichandan. Pradeep Dutta and Tapasya played the lead roles.

p: The story was written by Dilip Srichandan and the dialogue by Sarika Swain, with Sudhakar Vasant preparing the screenplay. Pradeep Sahu was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor. Pintu Nanda, Pratibha Panda, Madhu and Sudhakar Vasant also appeared in the film.
Gouri Shankar Singh directed the music, with lyrics by Manoj Mohanty. Gautam Giri, Swetami, Tariq Aziz, Satyajit, Ashutosh, Antara Chakraborty and Sashank Sekhar were among the singers.
The film was released on 15 February 2019.

Q51080193.lead: Hatya is a 2018 Odia-language film directed by T. Ganesh and produced by Sarat Chandra Pattnaik and Ajay Kar. It marked the Odia film debut of its lead pair, Arpan and Anwesha.

p: Bijayalaxmi Pattnaik wrote the story and Ajay Samal the dialogue, while T. Ganesh wrote the screenplay. Kali, Jyoti, Illu Banerjee, Suresh Bal, Chakradhar Jena, Biswabhushan Panda and Babu Pradhan appeared in other roles.
S. Chandrakant was the music director.
The film was released on 8 March 2018.

Q110441088.lead: Mo Mummy Papanka Bahaghara is a 2020 Odia-language film directed by Rajesh Mohanty and produced by Jagi Mangat Panda. It was released on television and on a streaming platform rather than in cinemas.

p: The film was made under the Tarang Cine Productions banner. Santosh Narayan Das wrote the story and Debidutta Mohanty the screenplay, while Ranjan Khatei edited it. Sai Yashobanta, Cookies Swain, Ananta Mishra and Aishwarya Behera were in the cast.
Biswaswarup was the music director.
The film premiered simultaneously on Tarang TV and the Tarang Plus streaming service on 6 September 2020.

Q53551695.lead: Udandi Seeta is a 1992 Odia-language film directed by Avatar Singh and produced by Rabi Swain.

p: Avatar Singh wrote the screenplay and Gopal De the dialogue. Samba Siva Rao was the cinematographer and Deben Mishra the editor. The cast included Uttam Mohanty, Aparajita Mohanty, Raimohan Parida, Jayiram Samal, Bijay Mohanty, Durlav Singh, Asrumochan Mohanty and Netrananda.
Akshaya Mohanty directed the music. The film marked the start of T. Souri's playback singing career in Odia cinema.

Q15526705.lead: Mo Dil To Deewana is a 2013 Odia-language romantic film written and directed by Alka Nanda and produced by Arup Nanda.

p: Alka Nanda was responsible for the story, screenplay and dialogue in addition to directing. The cast comprised Subhendu, Kajal, Raj, Asrumochan Mohanty and Bansuri.
The music was composed by Mina Nanda.
The film was released in Odisha on 1 January 2013, distributed by Alka Infomedia.

Q41461204.lead: Omm is a 2014 Odia-language film directed by Sudhakar Vasant, with Sambit Acharya and Prakruti Mishra in the lead roles.

p: Sudhakar Vasant produced the film together with Samaresh Routray under the S3 Movies banner, and also wrote the screenplay. Sukumar Mani was the editor. Supporting roles went to Sudhakar Vasant, Samaresh Routray, Saroj Das, Guddu, Illu Banerjee, Salil Mitra, Pintu Nanda, Tripti Panda and Pratibha Sahu.
The songs were composed by Vignaz Rock Band.
The film was released on 23 May 2014.

Q141257413.lead: Jayveer is a 2024 Odia-language film directed by Vivek Kumar from a story and screenplay by Rajani Ranjan. It was first shown on television.

p: Rajani Ranjan wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue. Dhiren was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor. The cast included Divya Mohanty, RK, Babi Mishra, Pushpa Panda, Choudhury Jayprakash Das, Tilu, Monalisa and Neer.
Japani Bhai composed the music, and Tapu Nayak wrote the lyrics. Humane Sagar, Kuldeep Pattanaik, Ruturaj Mohanty, Jyotirmayee and Rupali were among the singers.
The film was broadcast on Alankar TV on 8 March 2024.

Q141432072.lead: B Gang is a 2024 Odia-language film written and directed by Sanjay Nayak and produced by Sitaram Agrawal and Namita Agrawal. It premiered on television.

p: Sanjay Nayak wrote both the story and the screenplay. S. Ranjan handled the cinematography and Rajesh Das the editing. Lipsa Mishra and Rajdeep were in the cast.

Bikash Das and Baidyanath Dash composed the music, with lyrics by writers including Srikant Gautam and Arun Mantri. Satyajit Pradhan, Sourav Nayak, Kumar Bapi, Sashank Sekhar, Sangram Mohanty and producer Namita Agrawal sang on the soundtrack.
The film was released on Sidharth TV on 26 March 2024.

Q140061720.lead: Darpana is a 2025 Odia-language film directed by Bharat Pushparag and Ananda Kumar and produced by Dilip Kumar Sahu.

p: Ankit Kumar, Tripti Mirambika, Bharat Pushparag and Hiranmayee Das played the main roles. The supporting cast included Pradyumna Lenka, Ranu Padhi, Kalicharan, Janu, Soni, Pragyan, Roja and the producer, Dilip Kumar Sahu.
Tunu Pattnaik directed the music and also wrote the songs, which were sung by Humane Sagar and Ananya Sritam Nanda, among others.
The film was released on 21 November 2025.

Q56046986.lead: Nari Bi Pindhipare Rakta Sindura is a 1997 Odia-language film written and directed by Hara Patnaik and produced by Durga Nanda.

p: Hara Patnaik wrote the story and screenplay, directed the film and also acted in it. Rachna Banerjee, Mihir Das and Siddhanta Mahapatra headed the cast.

Other roles were played by Suresh Bal, Monalisa Kar, Debu Bose, Namrata Das, Braja Singh, Saroj Das, Debu Patnaik, Chandan Mishra, Abhipsa Das, Binayak Mishra, Panchanan Panigrahi, Manisha Rath, Pradyumna Lenka and Naba Acharya.

Q112282028.lead: Panigrahana is a 2022 Odia-language film directed by Himanshu Parija and produced by Bini Samal. It was released on television.

p: Abhishek Rath and Suryamayee Mohapatra played the lead roles, supported by Mahasweta Ray, Pruthviraj Nayak and Bhupati Tripathy.
Prasant Padhi composed the music to lyrics by Bijay Malla. The singers included Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Antara Chakraborty, Asima Panda and Swayam Padhi.
The film premiered on Zee Sarthak on 20 March 2022.

Q117324709.lead: Saragapuraru Asichi Priya is a 2023 Odia-language film directed by Sanjay Nayak and produced by Kabir Das. It was released on television.

p: The story was written by Pratik Sil. Nilakshi Patra, who played Menaka, appeared alongside Abhijit Das and Suman Maharana.

Baidyanath Dash composed the music, with lyrics by writers including Nirmal Nayak and Nihar Priyasish. Humane Sagar, Neha Niharika Kar, Satyajit Pradhan, Antara Chakraborty and Subhashish Sahu were among the singers.
The film premiered on Zee Sarthak on 26 March 2023.

Q141135258.lead: Love Tuition is a 2024 Odia-language film directed by Ashok Pati and produced by Sitaram Agrawal and Namita Agrawal. It premiered on television.

p: Bhoomika Dash and Raj Rajesh Panda played the leads, with Babi Mishra, Rabi Mishra, Udit Guru and Jiban Panda in supporting roles. Shubham was the cinematographer and Rajesh Das the editor.
Abhijit Majumdar was the music director.
The film was released on Sidharth TV on 26 January 2024.

Q140356384.lead: Parikaribe Bholashankar 4 is a 2025 Odia-language television film directed by Mrutyunjaya Sahoo and made by Zee Sarthak Telefilms.

p: Priyabrata Panda wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue. Sujit Paikaray, Ananya Das and Badal Mohanty starred.
Baidyanath Dash composed the music and Arun Mantri wrote the lyrics. The singers included Sashank Sekhar, Kunmun, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Arpita Choudhury and Sangram.
The film premiered on Zee Sarthak on 10 August 2025.

Q140363462.lead: Omm Namah Shivaya Bhaktire Sakti is a 2025 Odia-language film directed by Alok Behera and produced by Tarang Films. It was released on television and streaming.

p: The story and screenplay were developed by the Tarang team, and Sunil wrote the dialogue. Deepak Sahu edited the film. Jasmine Rath, Swadhin Kumar and Krishna Kar were in the cast.
Lalit Kumar composed the music to lyrics by Bapu Goswami, with Ashutosh Mohanty and Diptirekha Padhi among the singers.
The film was released on Tarang TV and Tarang Plus on 3 August 2025.

Q140033476.lead: Bohu 420 is a 2025 Odia-language television film directed by Rajesh Mohanty and produced by Ardhendu Sekhar Sahu, starring Nikita Mishra and Jyoti Prakash Panda.

p: The film was made under the Adilaxmi Entertainment banner from a story by Priyabrata Panda.

Santanu Nayak composed the music. The lyrics were written by Pushpak Parida, Umakanta Nayak and Satya Ranjan Bal, and the singers included Chiragdeep Panda, Abhijit Padhi, Gitisri Padhi, Santosh Kumar Nayak and Priyambada Sahu.
Bohu 420 premiered on Zee Sarthak on 30 November 2025.

Q55814826.lead: Asha is a 1993 Odia-language film directed by Santanu Mishra and produced by Alaya Mohanty. It received five state film awards, including Best Film.

p: Alaya Mohanty, the producer, also wrote the story. The cast included Aparajita Mohanty, Asrumochan Mohanty, Choudhury Jayaprakash Das, Snigdha Mohanty, Pushpa Panda, Binayak Mishra and Debajani.
Prafulla Kar directed the music, and Pranab Patnaik provided the playback vocals.

The film won five state film awards: Best Film, Best Actress for Aparajita Mohanty, Best Supporting Actor for Choudhury Jayaprakash Das, Best Playback Singer for Pranab Patnaik, and Best Sound Recording for Nagen Barik.

Q20890814.lead: Ram Rahim is a 1983 Odia-language film directed by Sushil Mukherjee and produced by Chitta Ranjan Mohanty.

p: Z. A. Khan was the cinematographer and Amiya Mukherjee the editor. The cast included Uttam Mohanty, Aparajita Mohanty, Bijay Mohanty, Shyamalendu Bhattacharya, Jaya Swami, Debu Brahma, Anita Das, Asit Pati, Hemant Das and Lila Dulali.
Prafulla Kar composed the music and wrote the songs. The singers included Geeta Das, S. Janaki, Chitta Jena and Pranab Patnaik.

Q15725426.lead: He Sakha is a 2012 Odia-language film directed by Asish Bhattacharya and produced by Sangram Gajendra, with Samir as Sri Krishna and Santu as Sudama.

p: Asish Bhattacharya wrote the screenplay and was also the cinematographer, while Nirmal Panda and Saranabinda wrote the dialogue. Gargi Mohanty shared the lead with Samir and Santu, and the cast also featured Kabula Mohanty, Prabhati Sahu, Ashok Bal, Nirmal Panda, Sangram and Ram Singh.

Amarendra Mohanty composed the music to lyrics by Dr. Prasanna Samal, Mohit Chakraborty and Satyaban. Antara Chakraborty, Amarendra Mohanty, Pami, Karunakar and Gobindachandra sang the songs, which included "He Sakha", "Hari Hari", "Phula Phutichi", "Runu Jhunu" and "Srikrushna".
The film was released on 1 January 2012.

facts: He Sakha, Hari Hari, Phula Phutichi, Runu Jhunu, Srikrushna

Q27125394.lead: Chhati Tale Ding Dong is a 2016 Odia-language film directed by Mrutyunjaya Sahoo and produced by Soumya Ranjan Patnaik. It is an adaptation of Size Zero, a 2015 Telugu and Tamil film.

p: Basantaraj Samal wrote the film. S. Ranjan Rao was the cinematographer and Chandrasekhar Mishra the editor. Sabyasachi Mishra, Archita Sahu, Barsha Priyadarshini and Shakti Kapoor headed the cast, with Sambit Acharya and Kirti Mohanty also appearing. It was the first film in which Archita Sahu and Barsha Priyadarshini acted together.
Malay Mishra was the music director, and the lyrics were written by Basantaraj Samal and Bapu Goswami.
The film was released in October 2016 during the Dussehra festival.
The film was based on Size Zero, which was released in Telugu and Tamil on 27 November 2015.

Q56449728.lead: Sapana Banika is a 1985 Odia-language film produced and directed by P. D. Shenay.

p: Surendra Sahu was the cinematographer and Rabi Shankar Patnaik the editor. The cast included Sriram Panda, Uttam Mohanty, Mahasweta Ray, Dukhiram Swain, Swarup Nayak, Dipti Nath, Hemant Das, Pira Mishra, Jayiram Samal, Isha Bebarta, Prabhanshu Samantaray and Asim Basu.
Bhubaneswar Mishra directed the music and Debdas Chhotray wrote the lyrics. Anuradha Paudwal and Suresh Wadkar were among the singers.

Q139987983.lead: Saha Hebe Mote Maa Mangala is a 2025 Odia-language film directed by Ajay Kumar Singh and produced by Khirod Pattnaik, with Tushar and Simran in the lead roles. It premiered on television.

p: Priyabrata Panda wrote the dialogue. Pradyumna Lenka, Namrata Das and Dibyansha appeared in supporting roles.
Prasant Padhi composed the music to lyrics by Nirmal Nayak, and the singers included Antara Chakraborty and Satyajit Pradhan.
The film was released on Zee Sarthak on 14 December 2025.

Q119889703.lead: Twins is a 2023 Odia-language television film directed by Rasesh Mohanty and produced by Khirod Pattnaik, in which Riya Dey plays a double role as Arati and Abha.

p: Satyaki Kundu wrote the story. Alongside Riya Dey, the cast included Harihar Das, Santosh Narayan Das, Kirti Mohanty and Latasa.

Goodly Rath directed the music, and Surya Mohapatra wrote the songs, which were sung by Swayam Padhi, Lipsa Mohapatra, Arpita Choudhury and Santanu Siddhisna, among others. The songs came out on 1 June 2023.
The film premiered on Zee Sarthak on 4 June 2023.

Q110409186.lead: Love You Priya is a 2020 Odia-language film directed by Vivek Kumar and produced by Jay Sen, starring Soham Singh and Mahima Das. It was released on television.

p: Ashutosh Barik wrote the story and dialogue, and Vivek Kumar the screenplay. Dhiren Sahu was the cinematographer and Ranjan Khatei the editor. The supporting cast included Pushpa Panda, Pritiraj Satpathy, Guddu, Raja, Niki, Jiban Panda and Mita Chakraborty.
Ashesh Das directed the music, with lyrics by writers including Ashutosh and Tapu Nayak.
The film was released on television on 27 December 2020.

Q119889690.lead: Happy Ending is a 2023 Odia-language film directed by actor Tushar and produced by Atisa Kumar Rout. It was released on a streaming platform.

p: Saswat Bhuyan wrote the story and screenplay, and Prasanna Pattasani the dialogue. Lipu was the cinematographer. Tushar and Priyanka played the leads, with Manas and Lipika in other roles. The film runs for 1 hour 45 minutes.
Biswajit Mohapatra was the music director.
The film was released on the Kanchalanka OTT platform on 21 April 2023.

Q140676781.lead: Sasu Nuhe Se Sunami Jhada is a 2025 Odia-language television film directed by Manoj Sinha and produced by Khirod Pattnaik.

p: Priyabrata Panda and Manas Mallick wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue together. Mitali Sargharia, Priyambada Ray and Ankit Kumar were in the cast.
Prasant Padhi composed the music, with Swayam Padhi, Antara Chakraborty and Arpita Choudhury among the singers.
The film premiered on Zee Sarthak on 9 March 2025.

Q109519688.lead: Hello Ravana is a 2021 Odia-language film directed by Ramesh Rout and produced by Sangita Satpathy, with Papu Pam Pam in the lead role. It was released on a streaming platform.

p: The film was made under the Papu Pam Pam Creations banner, and Ramesh Rout wrote the screenplay. Arabinda Sadangi, Pratibha Panda, Kalicharan Acharya, Rajiv, Deepak Tripathy and Sudipta appeared in supporting roles.
Papu Pam Pam also composed the music and sang, alongside Debesh Pati and Antara Chakraborty. The lyricists included Deepak Jena, Rup Sagar and Tukuna.
The film was released on an OTT platform on 15 October 2021.

Q56442777.lead: Prema Pain Mahabharata is an Odia-language film directed by Niranjan Behera and produced by Pradeep Kishore Acharya, with Sambit Acharya and Riya Dey in the lead roles.

p: Chhabita Martha wrote the story. The supporting cast included Sritam Das, Mihir Das, Babi Mishra, Pintu Nanda, Samaresh Routray, Pupinder Singh, Biju Badajena, Priyanka, Pratibha, Babuli and Debu.
Abhijit Majumdar was the music director.
The film was released on 8 February 2019.

Q110441090.lead: Mu Tume Lockdown is a 2020 Odia-language television film directed by Dwipayan Majumdar, with Deepika Tripathy and Biswabhushan Panda in the lead roles. It was shot entirely on mobile phones during the 2020 lockdown.

p: Alok Ray wrote the screenplay, and Dwipayan Majumdar also served as cinematographer. Deepika Tripathy played Priya and Biswabhushan Panda played Abhi. The whole shoot was carried out on mobile phones while the 2020 lockdown was in force.
Goodly Rath composed the music and Surya Mohapatra wrote the lyrics. Swayam Padhi, Lipsa Mohapatra and Sashank Sekhar were among the singers.
The film premiered on Zee Sarthak on 14 June 2020.

facts: Shot on mobile phones during the 2020 lockdown

Q50824825.lead: Lekhichi Naa Tora is a 2015 Odia-language feature film directed by Dilip Panda and produced by Rabindra Panda, with Sambit Acharya and Pinki Priyadarsini in the lead roles.

p: The film was the fifth production of the Excel Movies banner. Bijayalakshmi Panda wrote the story, and Dilip Panda prepared the screenplay in addition to directing. Chinmay Das Pattnaik is credited as writer.
Baidyanath Dash was the music director.
The film was released on 8 May 2015. Alongside the two leads, the cast included Krishna Kar, Harihara Mohapatra and Pradyumna Lenka in supporting parts.

Q15725300.lead: Sakhi Rahila Ae Singha Duara is a 2004 Odia-language feature film directed by Sanjay Nayak, featuring an ensemble cast led by Siddhanta Mahapatra.

p: Sanjay Nayak made the film, with Ranjan as cinematographer and Bijay Mishra as editor. Its budget is recorded as ₹85 lakh 52 thousand.
Other cast members included Mama Mishra, Bijay Mohanty, Uttam Mohanty, Aparajita Mohanty, Mihir Das, Tandra Ray, Kuna Tripathy and Biju Badajena, among others.

Malay Mishra directed the music. Songs were written by lyricists including Srikanta Gautam and Arun Mantri, and the playback singers included Kumar Bapi, Bibhu Kishore, Ira Mohanty and Sailabhama Mahapatra.

Q60558726.lead: Bapa Tame Bhari Dusta is a 2019 Odia-language feature film directed by T. Ganesh and produced by Sitaram Agrawal, starring Jayjit Das and Smita Mandal.

p: Nirmal Nayak wrote the dialogue. Pratap Rout handled the cinematography and Rajesh Dash edited the film. Pradyumna Lenka appeared in a supporting comic role opposite the two leads.

The score was shared by three music directors: Baidyanath Dash, Anup Mohanty and Asad Nizam. Arun Mantri wrote the songs, which were sung by Human Sagar, Nibedita, Asima Panda, Arpita, Jagruti and Satyajit Pradhan, among others.
The film was released on 11 January 2019.

Q110713568.lead: Jhiata Alaga Prakara is a 2019 Odia-language feature film produced, directed and scored by actor Sritam Das, with Tushar and Koel Banerjee in the lead roles.

p: Rajani Ranjan wrote the screenplay and Niranjan Das was the cinematographer. The supporting cast included Pushpa Panda, Kuna Tripathy, Ushasi Mishra and Guddu.
Sritam Das composed the music, and Nirmal Nayak wrote the lyrics. Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Antara Chakraborty, Subhasish Mahakud, Pragya Hota and Abinash were among the playback singers.
The film was released on 30 June 2019.

Q15725172.lead: Labnya Priti is a 1993 Odia-language film written for the screen, shot and directed by Apurba Kishore Bir, adapted from Mahapatra Nilamani Sahu's short story "Prathama Pranaya".

p: Bir handled the screenplay and cinematography himself, while Dilip Panda edited the film. The principal cast comprised Tarasankar Mishra, Soumyashree Mishra, Aditi Bir, Bibhuti Bhusan Mishra and Lalatendu Rath.
Bhabadeep Jaipurwala composed the music.
After its 1993 release the film was screened at a number of national and international film festivals, where it won recognition.

At the 8th International Children's Film Festival in 1993 it was named Best Film and also took the Best Child Actor prize. At the 41st National Film Awards it received Best Children's Film and Best Child Actor. It was also named Best Asian Film at an international film festival in Osaka.

facts: "Prathama Pranaya", short story by Mahapatra Nilamani Sahu
Best Children's Film; Best Child Actor (41st)

Q140406059.lead: Wife Nuhan Se Wifi is a 2025 Odia-language television film directed by Sanjib Dwivedi and produced by Minakshi Pattnaik, starring Swapna Priyadarshini and Girija Shankar Jena.

p: Sushant Mani wrote the story. Mili and Sumanta also appeared in the cast.
Santanu Nayak composed the music and Bapu Goswami wrote the songs. Abhijit Padhi, Smaranika Nayak and Neha Niharika Kar were among the singers.
Rather than opening in cinemas, the film premiered on the Zee Sarthak channel on 13 July 2025.

Q53016185.lead: Akuha Katha is a 1994 Odia–Bengali bilingual film written and directed by Tarun Majumdar and produced by Purnachandra Rao; its Bengali version was titled Katha Chhilo.

p: Tarun Majumdar wrote the story as well as directing. The cast included Debu Bose, Uttam Mohanty, Aparajita Mohanty, Mahasweta Ray, Jayiram Samal, Dukhiram Swain and Hemanta Das.
Bappi Lahiri was the music director, and Mohammed Aziz sang in the film.

Q51080202.lead: Nayak Nuhen Mun Khalanayaka is a 2005 film directed by Ratan Adhikari and produced by Bijay Kandoi, released in both Odia and Bengali, with Anubhav Mohanty and Rachna Banerjee in the lead roles.

p: Locket Chatterjee, Rajatava Dutta and Tapas Paul were among the supporting cast. Atish De Sarkar edited the film.
Anupam Dutta directed the music. The lyricists included Arun Mantri and Jatindra Pradhan, and the songs were sung by Deepmala, Mohammed Nasir, Pami and T. Souri, among others.

Q139919183.lead: Mistira Dustami is a 2026 Odia-language television film written and directed by Mahesh Hazra and produced by Sitaram Agrawal and Namita Agrawal.

p: Hazra wrote the story as well as directing. The cast included Ananya Das, Rushik Mishra and Tanmay Kumar. Shubham was the cinematographer and Deepak Sahu the editor.
Sarthak Agrawal composed the music, with lyrics by Arun Mantri. Swayam Padhi, Arpita Choudhury and Swarup Gautam were among the singers.
The film premiered on Sidharth TV on 24 May 2026.

Q140634519.lead: Ajab Ae Prema Kahani is a 2025 Odia-language television film directed by Rajesh Mohanty and produced by Khirod Pattnaik, starring Srijit Mahapatra and Bhakti Patnaik.

p: Priyabrata Panda wrote the dialogue.
Goodly Rath composed the score, and Surya Mahapatra wrote the songs. Lipsa Mahapatra, Bishnu Mohan Kabi, Lopamudra Das and Rupesh Patra were among the singers.
The film premiered on Zee Sarthak on 30 March 2025.

Q60738444.lead: Love Express is an Odia romantic film from 2018, directed by Ramesh Rout. Swaraj Barik and Sunmeera Nagesh play the leads, and Sitaram Agrawal and Namita Agrawal produced it.

p: The script was written by Nirmal Nayak and the editing done by Rajesh Dash. Bobby Mishra, Pintu Nanda and Salil Mitra appear in supporting roles.
Baidyanath Dash wrote the music, and the song lyrics came from Nirmal Nayak and Arun Mantri.
It was released across Odisha on 28 December 2018.
The film remakes Jaanu, the 2012 Kannada film starring Yash.

Q140458229.lead: Jwain Puara Jibana Bima is a 2025 Odia-language television film directed by Rajesh Mohanty and produced by Bijay Kandoi.

p: The cast included Sandip, Mitali Sargharia, Rabi Mishra and Krishna Kar.
Goodly Rath composed the music, and the songs were written by Nirmal Nayak and Surya Mahapatra. Tariq Aziz, Asima Panda, Lipsa Mahapatra and Human Sagar were among the singers.
The film premiered on Zee Sarthak on 8 June 2025.

Q99353609.lead: Sandhya Tara is an Odia-language feature film from 1977, directed by Gopal Ghosh from a story by the playwright Chintamani Jena.

p: Gopal Ghosh directed the film, working from a story written by Chintamani Jena. The cast included Samuel Sahu (credited as Babi), Sujata Anand, Niharika Sahu, Ajit Das, Hemant Das and Jaya B. The production budget is given as ₹10,25,000.
Basudeba Rath composed and directed the music, and the lyrics were written by Shibabrata Das. Asha Bhosle, Mahendra Kapoor, Amit Kumar and Anuradha Paudwal were among the playback singers.
Although dated to 1977, the film never reached a theatrical release.

Q30004120.lead: Baata Abaata is a 1980 Odia-language film directed by Brundaban Jena, with Ajit Das and Mahasweta Ray in the lead roles.

p: Brundaban Jena directed the film. Ajit Das and Mahasweta Ray played the principal parts, and Bijaya Jena and Narayan Pati appeared in supporting roles.

The score was composed jointly by Bhubaneswar Mishra and Hariprasad Chaurasia, while the director, Brundaban Jena, also wrote the song lyrics. The playback singers included Arati Mukherjee, Minakshi Nanda, Pranab Patnaik, Anuradha Paudwal and K. J. Yesudas.

Q110441092.lead: Anu Didi Not Out is a 2020 Odia-language television film directed by Tapas Sargharia, with Anu Choudhury in the title role.

p: Jagi Mangat Panda produced the film under the Tarang Cine Productions banner, and Tapas Sargharia directed it. Anu Choudhury headed the cast, which also included Aman, Tanushree, Samaj Pati, Soma Hota, Anada, Manisha, Megha, Twinkle, Khushi, Anita and Mamata. Anil Kumar directed the music.
Rather than opening in cinemas, the film premiered on Tarang TV on 8 March 2020, timed to coincide with International Women's Day.

Q4907192.lead: Bijay Mohanty (1950–2020) was an Odia film actor, director and playwright whose screen career began with Chilika Teerey in 1977 and spanned more than 190 Odia films in roles ranging from villain and comedian to hero and character parts.

p: Mohanty was born at Pandiri village in Kendrapara district, the eldest of five children of Adikanda Mohanty and Santilata Mohanty, and grew up in Baripada, Mayurbhanj, where his father worked as a government bus conductor. He first acted on stage at the annual function of Maharaja Krushna Chandra school while in class ten. After matriculation he took a job in the state transport department while studying at Maharaja Purna Chandra College, where a college play earned him a best actor prize.

With friends he formed the Jugechha theatre group in Baripada. He then trained at the National School of Drama in Delhi (1973 batch) on a national merit scholarship and worked in Delhi theatre until 1975 before returning to Odisha to direct plays.

In January 1977 Mohanty joined the drama department of Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya, later retiring from it as a professor. The same year he acted in Biplab Roychoudhury's Chilika Teerey, his first film, which received a National Film Award; Naga Phasa, however, reached cinemas first, and his villain's role in it brought him many offers.

Negative roles dominated his early years, in films such as Naga Phasa, Samaya Bada Balaban, Dandabalunga, Dora, Sahari Bagha and Chaka Bhaunri. Kaberi (1983) showed him in a positive role, and he went on to lead parts, comedy and character work in films such as Arati, Jaga Hatare Pagha, Mamata Mage Mula, Bhai Hela Bhagari, Suna Panjuri and Laxman Rekha. He directed one film, Bhuli Huena (1987), which did not succeed commercially, and appeared in Doordarshan serials including Sri Jagannath and Sara Akasa.

Outside cinema, he joined the Indian National Congress in February 2014 and contested the Bhubaneswar Lok Sabha seat in that year's general election, losing; he left the party in 2018. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2020.

Mohanty won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor for Arati (1981), Ei Aama Sansar (1986), Bhisma Pratigyan (1993), Bhai Hela Bhagari (1994) and Bou (1998); Best Supporting Actor for Mamata Mage Mula (1985), Pratisodha Aparadh Nuhen (1989) and Satyameva Jayate (2008); and Best Comedian for Aama Ghara Aama Sansara (1991). He received the Jayadev Award in 2014, the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award in 2009 for his play Ajati, and the Orissa Cine Critics award for Best Actor of the Decade in 1987. Chilika Teerey won a National Film Award certificate of merit as best Odia film.
He was married to the Odia film actress Tandra Ray, with whom he played opposite in a number of films; the couple had one daughter.

facts: National School of Drama, New Delhi (1973)

Q5881427.lead: Sanjukta Panigrahi (1944–1997) was an Odissi dancer and choreographer from Berhampur who trained under Kelucharan Mohapatra and played a central part in reviving Odissi and presenting it in India and abroad.

p: She was born in Berhampur, Ganjam district, to Abhiram Mishra and Shakuntala Mishra in a Brahmin family. As a small child she would dance to everyday rhythmic sounds. Her mother, from a Baripada family long associated with patronage of Chhau, encouraged her, while her father at first objected, since dance in Odisha was then largely confined to the temple Maharis.

She began learning from Kelucharan Mohapatra at the age of four and was judged best child artist at the Bisuba Milan for three years running between 1950 and 1953; in 1952 she won first prize at the International Children's Film Festival. Her parents then sent her to Kalakshetra in Chennai, where she studied for six years under Rukmini Devi Arundale, earning a Nrityapraveen diploma in Bharatanatyam with Kathakali as a second subject, and toured with the Kalakshetra Ballet Troupe. Back in Odisha at 14, she was given a state scholarship to study Kathak in Mumbai but left the course to focus on Odissi.

Her early professional years with her husband were financially hard. A turning point came in 1966, when she performed Odissi in New Delhi at the ceremony at which Kelucharan Mohapatra received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award. Her husband Raghunath Panigrahi, a vocalist, went on to provide the music for her recitals, and the pair performed together for decades. She also toured with her guru across India.

She represented India in government cultural delegations to the United States and the Philippines (1969), the United Kingdom (1983), Israel and Greece (1989), and performed in France for eleven weeks. In 1986, 1990 and 1992 she taught short Odissi courses at the International School of Theatre Anthropology in Bologna, Italy. Her repertoire with her husband drew on Jayadeva's Gita Govinda, Surdas, Tulasidas, Vidyapati and Rabindranath Tagore, and she closed her recitals with Moksha Mangalam. She died in Bhubaneswar in 1997.

She received the Padma Shri in 1975 and, jointly with her husband, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1976. In 1999 Raghunath Panigrahi set up the Sanjukta Panigrahi Memorial Trust, which since 2001 has given scholarships and awards in Odissi dance on her birth anniversary. A documentary, Encounter With the Gods: Odissi Dance With Sanjukta Panigrahi, was made in 1999.

She married Raghunath Panigrahi, a Gita Govinda singer ten years her senior whom she met at Kalakshetra and who gave up a career in film music in Chennai to accompany her. They married when she was 16 and had two sons.

facts: Padma Shri (1975); Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1976)

Q4701823.lead: Akshaya Mohanty (1936/1937–2002), known as Khoka Bhai, was an Odia singer, composer, lyricist and writer who sang in 129 Odia films, scored 75, and wrote modern light songs, bhajans and legend-based ballads.

p: Born Akshaya Kumar Mohanty at Bankimundai village to Bichitrananda Mohanty and Subarna Manjari Devi, he studied at Stewart Science College, took a BA from Ravenshaw College and also studied law at Madhusudan Law College. He had no formal training in music; influenced by his elder sister Sulakshana Patnaik, he first appeared as a child artist on the foundation day of All India Radio, Cuttack, in 1948.

He entered government service at 22 and left after seven years, in 1963, to concentrate on music. He was approved by All India Radio, Cuttack, as a lyricist in 1956 and as a composer by 1959, and a group song he led took first place at a youth festival in Delhi in 1957. His first recorded song, Gadiala Bhai Dharichhi Sura Re, dates from the 1950s, and his first film playback was Gori Gori Gori in Maa (1959).

He began composing for films with Nitai Palit's Malajahna (1965), whose song Rakata Talamala became a hit. Over his career he scored 75 Odia films, wrote lyrics for 92 and sang in 129; his scores include Jajabara, Naga Phasa, Sri Jagannath, Dandabalunga, Jaaiphula, Mamata Mage Mula, Chakabhaunri, Kurukshetra, Aama Ghara Aama Sansara and Laxmana Rekha. He also acted in three films and co-directed Jajabara.

He experimented with recording and sound effects and created ballads drawn from Odia legend, among them Kanchi Abhijana, Randipua Ananta and Konarak Gatha. His radio drama based on Fakir Mohan Senapati's Patent Medicine won All India Radio's best radio drama award. His well-known songs include the bhajan Kene Gheni Jauchha Jagannathanku, Sata Daria Pare, He Phaguna Tume, Raja Jhia Sange and Chakori Jharana Luha. He wrote more than 18 books, including short-story collections, the travelogue Ba Ba Re America, semi-autobiographical works and novels such as Bamapanthi, Aphera Nadi and Gayaka.

He received the Jayadev Award, seven Odisha State Film Awards for best playback singer, the state award for best music director, and several Orissa Cine Critics awards. He was posthumously given the Utkal Gaurav honour at the Kalinga Cine Awards in January 2016.
He married Prabina Mohanty in 1967. Their son Chitrabhanu Mohanty is a stage singer, and the actor Hemant Das was his cousin.

facts: Stewart Science College; Ravenshaw College; Madhusudan Law College
Rakata Talamala; Kene Gheni Jauchha Jagannathanku; Sata Daria Pare

Q212512.lead: Hariprasad Chaurasia (born 1938) is an Indian bansuri player and composer in the Hindustani classical tradition who began his career at All India Radio, Cuttack, and composed music for Odia films in partnership with Bhubaneswar Mishra.

p: Chaurasia was born in Allahabad (now Prayagraj). His mother died when he was six, and he was raised by his father, the wrestler Chhedilal Pehelwan, who wanted his son to follow him into wrestling. He trained at the akhada for a time but studied music without his father's knowledge, taking Hindustani vocal lessons from his neighbour Pandit Rajaram from the age of 15 and then learning the flute from Bholanath Prasanna of Varanasi for eight years.

After working as a stenographer in Allahabad, he joined All India Radio in Cuttack in 1957 as a composer and performer, moving to Bombay on transfer around 1962. There he later studied with the surbahar player Annapurna Devi of the Maihar gharana; he has played left-handed ever since that period. In 1967 he recorded the album Call of the Valley with santoor player Shivkumar Sharma and guitarist Brij Bhushan Kabra.

In Odia cinema he worked with Bhubaneswar Mishra as the composing pair Bhuban-Hari, scoring films including Samaya (1975) and Gapa Hele Bi Sata (1976), whose song Mun Je Janena Kaha Bata was sung by Suman Kalyanpur, as well as Maa O Mamata. In Hindi films he and Shivkumar Sharma composed as Shiv-Hari, with scores including Silsila, Chandni, Lamhe and Darr.

He has performed as a soloist and in jugalbandi at venues such as Carnegie Hall and the Royal Albert Hall, played on the Beatles' The Inner Light and George Harrison's Wonderwall Music, recorded Making Music (1987) with Zakir Hussain, John McLaughlin and Jan Garbarek, and toured with Remember Shakti in 1997. He became artistic director of Indian music at the Rotterdam Conservatory in 1991 and founded the Vrindaban Gurukul in Mumbai in 2002, opening a second in Bhubaneswar in 2010.

His honours include the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1984), the Konark Samman and Padma Bhushan (1992), the Padma Vibhushan (2000), a Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (2011), appointment as Officer of the Order of Orange-Nassau by the Netherlands (2008) and Knight of the Order of Arts and Letters by France (2009), and an honorary doctorate from North Orissa University (2009).

He married Kamala Devi around 1957 and later the classical vocalist Anuradha Roy, whom he met at All India Radio, Cuttack. He has two sons, Vinay and Ajay, from his first marriage and a son, Rajeev, from his second.

Q4777685.lead: Anu Choudhury (born Anusuya Dash Choudhury) is an Odia film actress and politician from Bhubaneswar who has also worked in Bengali, Telugu and Hindi cinema, and who first played a lead role in Maa Gojabayani (1999).

p: She was born in Bhubaneswar. She studied science at Biju Patnaik College of Science and Education, graduated from Rama Devi Women's University, and later completed a postgraduate qualification in information technology from Manipal University.

Choudhury appeared as a child artist in small roles in Mamata Mage Mula and Badhu Nirupama before taking the lead in Maa Gojabayani in 1999, a film that was well received. She followed it with Biswaprakash, which featured Nandita Das and was selected for the Indian Panorama, and with Mana Rahigala Tumari Thare, Maa O Mamata, Gare Sindura Dhare Luha, Rakhi Bandhili Mo Rakhiba Mana and Sashu Ghara Chalijibi, a Rajshri Productions film co-starring Siddhanta Mahapatra. In 2007 she had seven releases as the lead actress. After a two-year break from Odia films she returned, and later played a police officer in Pahili Raja.

Outside Odisha, she starred in the Telugu film Subhavela (2000) and in Muthyam and Manasu Telusuko. In Bengali cinema she began with Surya (2004) opposite Prosenjit Chatterjee, followed by Ram Lakshman, Dadar Adesh, Rajmohol, Jamai Raja and Rajkumar among others. Her Hindi films include Nirvana 13, directed by Jitin Rawat, and Babloo Happy Hai (2013), directed by Nila Madhab Panda. In 2022 she began appearing on Odia television in Sarbajita Anu on Zee Sarthak.

She has worked as a brand ambassador for UNICEF, safe-motherhood and electricity-awareness campaigns, and the HIV-education initiative TeachAids. She joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in January 2018 and served as vice-president of the party's Mahila Morcha in Odisha from 2021 to 2023.

Choudhury has won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress four times: for Gare Sindura Dhare Luha (2001), Rakhi Bandhili Mo Rakhiba Mana (2002), Om Shanti OM (2004) and Sashu Ghara Chalijibi (2005). She was named best actress at the 4th Cine India International Film Festival in Noida for her role as a second-generation refugee from East Bengal in Kathantara, received the Chalachitra Jagat Pratibha Samman for Lal Tuku Tuku Sadhaba Bahu in 2007, and won a best actress award in Los Angeles in 2011 for Nirvana 13.

facts: Rama Devi Women's University; Manipal University

Q4843231.lead: Baijayant "Jay" Panda (born 1964) is an industrialist and Bharatiya Janata Party politician from Cuttack who has represented Kendrapara in the Lok Sabha and served as the party's national vice-president.

p: Panda was born in Cuttack to the industrialist Bansidhar Panda and Ila Panda. He studied engineering and management in communications at Michigan Technological University.

He entered Parliament in 2000 as a Rajya Sabha member from Odisha for the Biju Janata Dal and served two terms there until 2009. He then won the Kendrapara Lok Sabha seat, holding it through the 15th and 16th Lok Sabha. He left the Biju Janata Dal in 2018, joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in New Delhi in March 2019 and was named its national vice-president and spokesperson that month. He lost Kendrapara to Anubhav Mohanty in 2019 and won it back in 2024.

As a parliamentarian he took part in the Citizens' Alliance against Malnutrition and introduced private members' bills, including one proposing plain packaging for tobacco products. A collection of his newspaper columns, Lutyen's Maverick, was published in 2019.

facts: Bharatiya Janata Party (from 2019); earlier Biju Janata Dal

Q717997.lead: Nandita Das (born 1969) is an Indian actress, director and writer who has worked in films in ten languages, Odia among them; her Odia work includes Biswaprakash (1999).

p: Das was born in Bombay (now Mumbai) to the painter Jatin Das and the writer Varsha Das, and was raised largely in Delhi in an Odia household. She went to Sardar Patel Vidyalaya, then took a geography degree at Miranda House and a Master of Social Work from the Delhi School of Social Work, both under the University of Delhi. In 2014 she was a Yale World Fellow.

Her acting began in street theatre with Jana Natya Manch. She went on to appear in more than 40 feature films, working with directors including Mrinal Sen, Adoor Gopalakrishnan, Shyam Benegal, Deepa Mehta and Mani Ratnam. Her roles include Deepa Mehta's Fire (1996) and Earth (1998), Bawandar (2000), Kannathil Muthamittal (2002) and Before the Rains (2007). Her Odia films include Parinati (1989) and Biswaprakash (1999).

Das moved into direction with Firaaq (2008), an ensemble drama set in the weeks after the 2002 Gujarat riots, which was shown at the Toronto Film Festival. Her second feature, Manto (2018), about the Urdu writer Saadat Hasan Manto, screened in the Un Certain Regard section at Cannes. Zwigato, about a food delivery rider and his family, followed and reached Indian cinemas in March 2023. She founded the production company Nandita Das Initiatives in 2016 and has also written the book Manto and I (2019).

Earth brought her the Filmfare award for best female debut. France named her a Chevalier de l'Ordre des Arts et des Lettres in 2011, and she was the first Indian inducted into the International Women's Forum's International Hall of Fame. She sat on the Cannes Film Festival jury in 2005 and on its Cinéfondation and short films jury in 2013, and in 2009 became chairperson of the Children's Film Society of India.
Das is the daughter of the artist Jatin Das. She was married to Saumya Sen and later to Subodh Maskara, with whom she has a son; both marriages ended in divorce.

facts: Miranda House; Delhi School of Social Work
Chevalier de l'Ordre des Arts et des Lettres (2011)

Q6986875.lead: Neena Gupta (born 1959) is an Indian film and television actress and television director, mainly in Hindi; her Odia work on this site is Aadi Mimansa (1991).

p: Gupta grew up in Karol Bagh, New Delhi. She studied at Delhi University, earning a BA, an MA in Sanskrit and an MPhil on stagecraft in Sanskrit drama. She was active in university theatre and, encouraged by Satish Kaushik, joined the National School of Drama in 1977, graduating in 1980.

Her early screen work included international productions such as Gandhi (1982) and several Merchant Ivory films, along with Indian parallel cinema such as Mandi (1983) and Drishti (1990). In Hindi cinema she was noted for Jaane Bhi Do Yaaro and appeared in Khalnayak (1993). Her role as a young widow in Woh Chokri (1994) was her breakthrough.

After a public appeal for work in 2017, she took the lead in the comedy-drama Badhaai Ho (2018), playing a middle-aged woman who becomes pregnant; the role revived her film career. Later films include Panga, Shubh Mangal Zyada Saavdhan and Sandeep Aur Pinky Faraar.

On television she acted in serials such as Khandan, Mirza Ghalib and Bharat Ek Khoj, hosted the quiz show Kamzor Kadii Kaun, and directed series including Saans and Siski. Her autobiography, Sach Kahun Toh, was published in 2021.

Gupta has won three National Film Awards: Best Supporting Actress for Woh Chokri and for Uunchai (2022), and an award for Bazar Sitaram (1993) as best first non-feature film of a director. Badhaai Ho earned her the Filmfare Award for Best Actress (Critics).
Her daughter, Masaba Gupta, is a fashion designer. Gupta married Vivek Mehra in 2008.

facts: University of Delhi; National School of Drama

Q7285813.lead: Rajasmita Kar (born 1991), also called Niki, is a dancer from Rourkela, Odisha, who won the third season of the Zee TV dance reality series Dance India Dance in 2012.

p: Kar was born in Rourkela to Ramesh Kumar Kar, who ran an electrical goods shop in the town's Basanti Colony, and Ranjita Kar. She took an interest in dance as a child and trained in several styles.

Before her national appearance she reached the final rounds of the Tarang TV dance shows Jhum Odisha Jhum and Dhoom Machale Dhoom. She was selected at the Dance India Dance auditions held in Bhubaneswar in October 2011 and competed in Geeta Kapoor's team, Geeta Ki Gang. Grand Master Mithun Chakraborty called her a 'dark horse' during the season. She was the only contestant from Odisha in the finale, aired on 21 April 2012, and won the title ahead of runner-up Pradeep Gurung with more than 48 lakh votes.

Q5223859.lead: Uttam Mohanty (died 2025) was an Odia film and television actor from Baripada who appeared in more than 130 Odia films, about 30 Bengali films and the Hindi film Naya Zaher.

p: Mohanty grew up in Baripada, where he studied at M.K.C. High School and then took his intermediate and science degree at Maharaja Purna Chandra College. He was drawn to stage acting in college and also played badminton and table tennis. After graduating he began chartered accountancy studies, first in Ludhiana and then in Kolkata, where he lived with his elder brother.

Hearing that the film Abhimaan was being shot in Baripada, he came home to try for a part, and director Sadhu Meher cast him in the lead opposite the newcomer Rita Chand. The 1977 film did well at the box office. Pati Patni followed, opposite Mahasweta Ray, and then films such as Nijhum Ratira Sathi, Chinha Achinha, Ramayan and Ram Balaram, which established him as a romantic lead.

The 1980s were the high point of his career, when he appeared in a large share of Odia releases in romantic, rural and character parts. He made around 20 films with Mahasweta Ray in the early 1980s and more than fifty with Aparajita Mohanty, starting with Astaraga (1982). From the mid-1990s he moved into character roles in films such as Kala Manikora. He also acted in television serials including Sara Akash, Je Pakhi Ude Jete Dura, Panatakani and Uttaradayi, the Hindi serial Palash and the Bengali serial Bideshini Bohu.
His performances in Abhimaan, Danda Balunga and Bhakta Salabega are among his best remembered.

He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor for Phula Chandana, Jheeati Sita Pari, Danda Balunga and Suna Chadhei, and for Best Supporting Actor for To Binu Anya Gati Nahin. His other honours include the Jayadeb Puraskar (1999), the Odisha Living Legend Award (2012) and a FITFAT Biscope Award (2008).
He married the actress Aparajita Mohanty in 1987; their son Babushan Mohanty is also an Odia film actor. Mohanty died in New Delhi in 2025.

Q29955816.lead: Rajat Kumar Kar (1933–2022) was an Odia playwright, educationist, researcher of Jagannath culture and radio and television commentator; his only film role was in the Odia film Ulka (1981).

p: Kar was born at Mahanga in Cuttack district to Kulamani Kar and Indumati Devi. He studied at Ravenshaw Collegiate School and took a master's degree in economics from Utkal University.

Kar spent his working life in the Odisha government's education department. He served as an inspector of schools from 1968 to 1979, later directed elementary and adult education, and retired in 1992 as Director of Teacher Education and SCERT. He also held posts with the NCC, the Board of Secondary Education and the Bharat Scouts and Guides, and taught Odia literature at Utkal University as a visiting professor.

Alongside this he wrote more than 600 radio plays and several books on Lord Jagannath and on the poet Upendra Bhanja. For 62 years he gave the running commentary on the Ratha Jatra of Lord Jagannath on radio and television, and he presented programmes such as Baidehisha Bilasa and judged Badi Pala on Prarthana TV.
Ulka (1981) was the first and last film he acted in. Some scenes of his were added to the film without his knowledge, and after objecting to this he kept away from screen acting.

The Government of India awarded him the Padma Shri in 2021 for his work in literature. His other honours include the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi's best playwright award (1994), the Ramchandra Mishra Natak Award (2009), the Pandit Godabarish Mishra Award (2011), an Odisha Sahitya Akademi lifetime achievement honour (2017) and an honorary D.Litt from Utkal University of Culture (2017).
Kar died in Bhubaneswar in 2022.

Q4901702.lead: Bhikari Charan Bal (1929–2010), known in Odisha as Bhajan Samrat, was an Odissi music guru and singer of devotional bhajans to Lord Jagannath who also sang in Odia films.

p: Bal was born at Sobala in Kendrapara district to Ramachandra Bal and Gellharani Devi. His mother's earlier children had not survived, and the name Bhikari reflected that. Both parents died when he was small, and he was brought up by his elder half-brother Dhaneswar and his wife. He studied up to class nine, then joined his village jatra troupe, where he learned singing, acting and the harmonium. He later taught music at a local school, married at 20, and moved to Cuttack for work.

In Cuttack he became an Odissi vocalist at Kala Bikash Kendra, where he trained further. He was made an A-grade singer at All India Radio, Cuttack, in 1963, and his early broadcast Prana Mitani Bare Chahan Re drew attention. Songs such as Kotha Bhoga Khia and Sathie Pauthi made him widely popular in the 1970s.

His repertoire drew on older poets such as Gopalakrushna, Dinakrushna, Baladev, Banamali and Salabega, as well as lyricists including Prasanna Samal, Arabinda Muduli and Khirod Chandra Pothal. Besides bhajans and Gita Govinda recitals he recorded champu, chhanda, chautisha and folk songs. In films he sang playback for titles including Bhakta Salabega, Agni Pariksha, Mathura Bijaya, Abhilasha, Amar Prem, Kie Kahara and Srikrushna Rasa Leela. His last bhajan album, Chagala Mana, came out in 2005.

The Gajapati of Puri, Dibyasingha Deb, gave him the title Bhajan Samrat, and he was allowed to perform the chamara seba for Lord Jagannath at the temple. After his death the Bhikari Bal Foundation was set up in his memory and holds annual music and cultural programmes.
He married Usharani Devi, and they had two sons and a daughter. Bal died in Cuttack in 2010 and was cremated at Swargadwara in Puri.

facts: Kotha Bhoga Khia; Prana Mitani Bare Chahan Re; Jagannatha Kichi Maagu Nahin Tote

Q31319995.lead: Kalicharan Pattnaik (1897–1978), known by the title Kabichandra, was an Odia playwright, poet, lyricist and Odissi musician who also worked in early Odia cinema, directing and writing songs for Lalita (1949).

p: Pattnaik was the second child of Durga Charan Pattnaik, dewan of Badamba, and Radhamali Devi. He went to the Charchika school at Banki and Khurda High School, then to Ravenshaw College in Cuttack, but his father's death in 1919 ended his studies. As a boy he learned classical music from Basudeb Mahapatra and Khanu Mian, among others.

After a spell as a sub-inspector of schools at Khandapara, he worked in Cuttack on the newspaper Utkala Dipika and as assistant editor of Mukura. In 1922 he moved to Mayurbhanj, where he led a drama group and brought elements of Odissi into the local Chhau dance. He then became court musician and adviser to Gajapati Ramachandra Deba at Puri, edited the weekly Puribasi and started the music monthly Sangita Prabha.

From 1925 his Rasa Lila productions became popular across the state. He then moved to social and historical plays, beginning with Pratisodha, and founded the Odisha Theatres company in 1939; his play Girl School (1939) gave women the chance to act on the Odia stage. He wrote some forty full-length plays along with dance dramas, one-act plays, stories, poems, children's books and works on Odissi music, and his autobiography is titled Kumbhara Chaka.
In cinema, he directed Lalita (1949) and wrote songs for it and for Matira Manisha (1967).

The Gajapati of Puri gave him the title Kabichandra in 1926, and the Utkal Sahitya Samaj named him Natyacharya in 1944. He became a fellow of the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1968, received a D.Litt from Sambalpur University in 1975, and won the Kendra Sahitya Akademi Award in 1977 for Kumbhara Chaka. He turned down the Padma Shri in 1974.
The singer Shyamamani Devi was his niece.

Q402203.lead: Koel Mallick (born Rukmini Mallick, 1982) is an Indian actress who works mainly in Bengali cinema and has also appeared in Odia films, beginning with Premi No.1 (2005); she is also a Rajya Sabha member from West Bengal.

p: Mallick was born in Kolkata to the Bengali actor Ranjit Mallick and Deepa Mallick, of the Mallick Bari family of Bhowanipore. She studied at Modern High School for Girls and earned a BSc (Honours) in psychology from Gokhale Memorial Girls' College, under the University of Calcutta.

Her first film, Nater Guru (2003), opposite Jeet, did well at the box office and brought her a best actress prize at the Tele Cine Awards; she and Jeet went on to make eleven films together. Bandhan (2004) was the highest-earning Bengali film of its year. Her other commercially successful titles include Shubhodrishti (2005), Mon Mane Na (2008), Paglu (2011) and Besh Korechi Prem Korechi (2015), while MLA Fatakeshto (2006), Hemlock Society (2012) and Mitin Mashi (2019) drew critical praise.

In 2005 she made her Odia debut in Premi No.1, opposite Anubhav Mohanty. On television she played the goddess in Zee Bangla's Mahalaya in 2007, hosted the talk show Katha O Kahini and judged dance reality programmes. In 2026 she entered the Rajya Sabha from West Bengal, resigned in July that year and was nominated again in October after joining the Bharatiya Janata Party.
Her awards include a Filmfare Award Bangla, two BFJA Awards and an Anandalok Puraskar. The Government of West Bengal gave her the Mahanayak Samman in 2023.
She is the daughter of the actor Ranjit Mallick. In 2013 she married the producer Nispal Singh; they have a son and a daughter.

Q15724850.lead: Biswajit Das (1936–2004) was an Odia playwright, short story writer, film director and screenwriter, a leading figure in the New Theatre Movement who directed the films Priyatama (1978) and Nijhum Ratira Saathi (1979).

p: Das was born at Jajpur, the eldest of four children of Subodh Das, a homeopathic doctor who was also a freedom fighter, dramatist and actor, and Krushna Kamini Devi, also a freedom fighter. Village jatra performances shaped his interest in theatre. He attended Peary Mohan Academy in Cuttack from 1946 and then graduated from Ravenshaw College, where his contemporaries included Ananta Mahapatra, who later directed and acted in many of his plays.
From 1958 to 1994 Das worked in the Odisha government's Information and Public Relations Department, serving as public relations officer to four chief ministers and a governor.

He began writing one-act plays in 1952, starting with Gotte Drushya, and produced more than sixty of them. His full-length play Banhi won a state competition in 1957, and later works included Nishipadma, Nalipana Rani Kalapana Tika, Nija Pratinidhinka Tharu, Mrugaya (1970) and Samrat (1972), the last adapted from Camus's Caligula. He founded the Rupakar theatre group in Bhubaneswar and later headed its offshoot Sanket. He is also credited with improving stage lighting in Odia theatre.

In cinema he directed Priyatama, Nijhum Ratira Saathi and Maana Abhimaan, and wrote scripts or dialogue for films including Ahalya, Kaberi, Naga Phasa and Gouri. He also wrote the Doordarshan serials Satya and Sadhu Sabdhan and a weekly column, Bhinna Swar, for the Sambad daily.

His honours include the Orissa Sangeet Natak Akademi award for playwriting and direction (1982), Cine Critics Association awards in 1987 and 1991, a state government award for his contribution to Odia cinema (1989) and the Ramachandra Mishra Memorial Award (1998).
Das married the educationist Gayatri in 1962; they had a son and four daughters.

Q560178.lead: Jackie Shroff (born Jaikishan Kakubhai Saraf, 1957) is an Indian actor and former model who has worked mainly in Hindi cinema, appearing in about 250 films across several languages, including Odia.

p: Shroff was born in Bombay (now Mumbai). His father, Kakubhai Haribhai Shroff, was Gujarati and worked as an astrologer. The name "Jackie" came from a school classmate, and director Subhash Ghai kept it when he launched him as a lead actor. Lacking money, the family could not support his studies, and he left school after the 11th standard.

After failing to secure jobs as an apprentice chef and a flight attendant, Shroff worked for a travel firm before an advertising agency employee approached him about modelling. A shirt photo shoot started his modelling work, and he later joined an acting class run by Aasha K Chandra, where Suneil Anand introduced him to his father, Dev Anand. Dev Anand gave him an uncredited part as a henchman in Swami Dada (1982).

His first lead role came in Subhash Ghai's Hero (1983), opposite Meenakshi Seshadri, which became one of the biggest earners of that year. Through the 1980s and 1990s he starred in commercially successful films such as Karma (1986), Ram Lakhan, Tridev and Parinda (all 1989), Saudagar (1991), Khalnayak (1993), 1942: A Love Story (1994), Rangeela (1995) and Border (1997).

From 2000 he increasingly took supporting and negative roles, in films including Mission Kashmir (2000), Devdas (2002), Bhagam Bhag (2006) and Housefull 3 (2016). He has also acted in Marathi, Punjabi, Konkani, Tamil and Telugu films; his Odia work includes Daha Balunga (2013). On television he hosted programmes such as Lehrein and Missing, and in 2019 he moved into web series with Criminal Justice.

Shroff has received four Filmfare Awards: Best Actor for Parinda, and Best Supporting Actor in consecutive years for 1942: A Love Story and Rangeela. His first Konkani film, Soul Curry (2017), brought him the Goa State Award for Best Actor.
He married model and later producer Ayesha Dutt on 5 June 1987. Their son Tiger Shroff is an actor, and their daughter Krishna Shroff is an entrepreneur and filmmaker.

Q3349404.lead: Salil Chowdhury (1925–1995) was an Indian music director, songwriter, lyricist, writer and poet who scored films in 13 languages, chiefly Bengali, Hindi and Malayalam, and also composed for the Odia film Batasi Jhada.

p: Chowdhury was born in Ghazipur, a village in the 24 Parganas district of Bengal, and grew up in the tea-garden region of Assam, where his father, Dr Gyanendra Chowdhury, served as medical officer at the Hathikuli Tea Estate. He heard western orchestral music on a gramophone owned by the estate's chief medical officer, learnt the piano from his elder brother at six, and also played the flute, harmonium and esraj. He attended Harinavi D.V.A.S High School and graduated from Bangabasi College under the University of Calcutta.

In the 1940s he joined the Indian People's Theatre Association (IPTA), the cultural wing of the Communist Party of India, writing songs for the peasant movement that the troupe carried to villages and towns. Pieces such as "Bicharpati", "Runner" and "Gnaayer bodhu" became widely popular, and many leading Bengali singers recorded his songs.

His first film score was for the Bengali film Paribortan (1949); his last Bengali work was Mahabharati (1994). He entered Hindi cinema in 1953 as music director of Bimal Roy's Do Bigha Zamin, for which he also wrote the story. He moved into Malayalam films with Chemmeen and eventually scored more than 75 Hindi, 41 Bengali and about 27 Malayalam films, along with a few in Marathi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Gujarati, Odia and Assamese. His Odia work was the music for Batasi Jhada.

He usually composed a tune to fit a film situation first, with the lyricist writing words afterwards. In 1966 he directed Pinjre Ke Panchhi from his own story and screenplay, and in 1958 he founded the Bombay Youth Choir as its composer and conductor. He mentored composers including R. D. Burman and Hridaynath Mangeshkar.

Do Bigha Zamin, which carried his story and music, won the first Filmfare Best Movie Award and a prize at the Cannes Film Festival. For his contribution to the 1971 Bangladesh Liberation War through the Swadhin Bangla Betar Kendra, he was posthumously given the Muktijoddha Maitreye Samman in 2012.

He married the painter Jyoti Chowdhury in 1952 and they had three daughters; after their separation he married the singer Sabita Chowdhury. Of their children, Sanjoy Chowdhury became a film music composer and Antara Chowdhury a musician and singer. He died in Calcutta in 1995.

facts: Sanjoy Chowdhury, Antara Chowdhury and others

Q982809.lead: Mrinal Sen (1923–2018) was an Indian film director and screenwriter who worked mainly in Bengali, with some Hindi and Telugu films, and made the Odia film Matira Manisha (1966). He was a key figure in India's parallel cinema movement.

p: Sen was born in Faridpur, in present-day Bangladesh, to Dineshchandra Sen, a lawyer who backed the freedom movement, and Saraju Sen. In the early 1940s he went to Kolkata to study physics at Scottish Church College, and he also studied at the University of Calcutta. His family moved to Kolkata for good after Partition in 1947. While working as a private tutor, he read books on film theory, including Rudolf Arnheim's Film as Art, that drew him towards filmmaking. He was also associated with the Indian People's Theatre Association and left-wing politics from his student days.

His first feature, the Bengali film Raat Bhore, came out in 1955. In 1966 he directed the Odia film Matira Manisha, adapted from Kalindi Charan Panigrahi's novel of the same name; he later described the experience of making it in his autobiography, Always Being Born. Bhuvan Shome (1969) is credited with starting India's New Wave cinema movement.

His films of the following years were strongly political, and Kolkata appears as a recurring presence in his work from Punascha (1961) to Mahaprithivi (1992). In 1976 he made the Hindi film Mrigayaa, based on Bhagabati Charan Panigrahi's story "Shikar". His other works include Calcutta 71, Padatik, Ek Din Pratidin, Akaler Sandhane, Kharij, Khandhar, Antareen and his final film, Amar Bhuvan (2002). He headed the Film and Television Institute of India from 1984 to 1986 and served on juries at the Berlin and Moscow film festivals.

Sen won eighteen National Film Awards, among them Best Feature Film for Bhuvan Shome, Chorus, Mrigayaa and Akaler Sandhane, and Best Direction for Bhuvan Shome, Ek Din Pratidin, Akaler Sandhane and Khandhar. He won awards at the Cannes, Venice and Berlin festivals. The Government of India conferred the Padma Bhushan on him and later the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2003; France made him a Commandeur of the Ordre des Arts et des Lettres in 1985, and Russia gave him the Order of Friendship in 2000. He was a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha from 1998 to 2003.
He married Geeta Shome in 1953. He died at his home in Bhawanipore, Kolkata, in 2018.

facts: Scottish Church College; University of Calcutta

Q15723875.lead: Kanhu Charan Mohanty (1906–1994) was an Odia novelist who published fifty-six novels between 1930 and 1985, several of which were adapted into Odia films. He received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1958 for his novel Kaa.

p: Mohanty was born in Nagabali village in Cuttack district to Suryamani and Durgadevi. The novelist Gopinath Mohanty was his younger brother. He studied at Peary Mohan Academy in Cuttack, where some of his early poems appeared in the school magazine. Financial hardship forced him to abandon an engineering course, and he graduated from Ravenshaw College in 1929. He then worked as a government clerk, retiring as a Senior Administrative Officer in 1964.

He drew early inspiration from the writings of Fakir Mohan Senapati and turned from poetry to fiction. His first novel, Utshabe Byasane, was written in 1923–24; his first published novels appeared in 1930, and Jaksha (1985) was his last. Among his better-known works are Ha Anna (1935), set during the Orissa famine of 1866, Shasti (1946), which followed the famine's aftermath, Tunda Baida (1944), Bhala Paibara Sesha Katha (1944), Jhanja, Sarbari and Kaa (1956).
His fiction, mostly set in coastal and rural Odisha, dealt with the position of women, caste and economic exploitation, written in plain language.

Several of his novels reached the screen. Abhinetri (1965), based on his 1947 novel of the same name, featured Jharna Das in a double role, the first in Odia cinema. Kaa was filmed in 1965 and received the Certificate of Merit for Best Feature Film in Odia at the 14th National Film Awards, and Tunda Baida was filmed under the same title in 1987.

Besides the 1958 Sahitya Akademi Award for Kaa, he received the Jeevan Rang Prize in 1970 and the Neela Saila Award in 1992. The Sahitya Akademi elected him a fellow in February 1994, but he died that April before it was formally presented. In 2007 the Akademi and Sarala Sahitya Sansad held a national seminar marking his birth centenary.
His younger brother Gopinath Mohanty was a Jnanpith Award-winning novelist, and the poet Guruprasad Mohanty was his nephew. He died in 1994.

facts: Kaa, Ha Anna, Shasti, Tunda Baida, Abhinetri

Q29109094.lead: Laxmikant Shantaram Kudalkar (1937–1998) was an Indian film composer, one half of the duo Laxmikant–Pyarelal with Pyarelal Ramprasad Sharma, which scored about 750 films between 1963 and 1998.

p: Kudalkar was born on Diwali, the day of Laxmi Puja, and his name refers to Vishnu, Laxmi's consort. His father died when he was young, and the family's poverty kept him from finishing school. On the advice of a musician friend of his father, he took up the mandolin, spending two years with the mandolin player Hussain Ali, and later studied mandolin with Bal Mukund Indorker and violin with Husnalal. He performed in classical instrumental concerts to earn money and appeared as a child actor in Bhakt Pundalik (1949), Aankhen (1950) and some Gujarati films.

With Pyarelal, he began composing for films with Babubhai Mistri's Parasmani (1963), whose songs became hits. The Rajshri Productions film Dosti (1964), featuring Mohammed Rafi solos, made their name. Through the late 1960s the pair scored a string of successful films, among them Shagird, Patthar Ke Sanam, Farz and Milan (all 1967), Intaqam, Jeene Ki Raah and Do Raaste (all 1969).

In the early 1970s they faced competition from R. D. Burman but continued with hit scores for films such as Aan Milo Sajna, Jeevan Mrityu, Haathi Mere Saathi and Mera Gaon Mera Desh. Their music for Raj Kapoor's Bobby (1973) was among their most successful, and other notable work of the decade included Daag, Loafer, Shor, Roti Kapada Aur Makaan, Dost and Amar Akbar Anthony.

The duo won the Filmfare Award for Best Music Director for Dosti, Milan and Jeene Ki Raah, and received further nominations for films including Do Raaste, Shor, Bobby, Daag, Roti Kapada Aur Makaan and Dulhan.

Q1968297.lead: Soumitra Chatterjee (1935–2020) was an Indian actor, director and writer who worked in Bengali cinema and theatre, best known for fourteen films with Satyajit Ray. He acted in more than 210 films, including the Odia films Dhare Alua and Sesha Pratikshya.

p: Chatterjee was born in Calcutta and spent his first ten years in Krishnanagar, a town with an active amateur theatre scene; his grandfather led a theatre group and his father, a lawyer, also acted. He later studied at Howrah Zilla School, earned an honours degree in Bengali literature from City College under the University of Calcutta, and began an MA in Bengali there. As a student he trained in acting under Ahindra Choudhury and came to regard the stage director Sisir Bhaduri as his mentor until Bhaduri's death in 1959.

He worked as an announcer at All India Radio before entering films. Ray first considered him for Aparajito but judged him too old for the teenage Apu, and two years later cast him as the adult Apu in Apur Sansar (1959), his debut. Their collaboration continued in films such as Abhijan, Charulata, Kapurush, Aranyer Din Ratri, Ashani Sanket, Hirak Rajar Deshe, Ghare Baire, Ganashatru and Shakha Proshakha. He was the first actor to play the detective Feluda, in Sonar Kella and Joi Baba Felunath.

Outside Ray's films he worked with Mrinal Sen in Akash Kusum (1965), Tapan Sinha in Kshudhita Pashan and Jhinder Bandi, and directors such as Asit Sen, Ajoy Kar and Tarun Mazumdar; later he acted for Goutam Ghose, Aparna Sen and Rituparno Ghosh, and played a swimming coach in Kony (1986). He directed Stree Ki Patra (1986), based on a Tagore story. He also acted on the Kolkata stage, published more than twelve books of poetry, and co-founded the magazine Ekkhon in 1961.

Chatterjee won three National Film Awards as an actor, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for theatre, the Padma Bhushan (2004) and the Dadasaheb Phalke Award (2012). France made him a Commandeur of the Ordre des Arts et des Lettres in 1999 and conferred the Légion d'honneur on him in 2017.
He died in Kolkata in 2020.

Q7250587.lead: Prosenjit Chatterjee (born 1962) is an Indian actor, director, producer and television personality working mainly in Bengali cinema, with more than 250 films in Bengali, Hindi and Odia over a career of over four decades.

p: Prosenjit was born in Calcutta to actor Biswajit Chatterjee and Ratna Chatterjee; the actress Pallavi Chatterjee is his sister. He paused acting after childhood to continue his studies, and after graduating in 1979 he joined the Nandikar theatre group, where Rudraprasad Sengupta mentored him.

He first appeared on screen at about five in Hrishikesh Mukherjee's Chotto Jigyasa (1968), which brought him a BFJA award, and later played child roles in his father's films Rahgir and Rakta Tilak. As a young adult he played the younger version of Uttam Kumar's character in Dui Prithibi (1980) and took supporting and villain roles before his first lead in Duti Pata (1983). Pathbhola (1986) gained him notice, and Amar Sangee (1987) made him a top box-office star.

Through the late 1980s and 1990s he headlined many commercially successful romances and action films, including Chhoto Bou, Amar Prem, Apan Amar Apan, Badnam and Bhai Amar Bhai. He directed Purushottam (1992). In the 2000s his roles in Pratibad, Devdas, Chokher Bali, Dosar and Khela drew critical attention, and from 2010 he moved towards parallel cinema with Autograph, Moner Manush, Baishe Srabon, Jaatishwar, Praktan, Mayurakshi, Jyeshthoputro and Gumnaami. He also played Kakababu in a series of adventure films beginning with Mishawr Rawhoshyo (2013). Alongside his Bengali work he acted in Hindi films such as Shanghai and in Odia films.

His awards include two National Film Awards, among them a Special Mention for Dosar, five Filmfare Awards and six BFJA Awards. He received the Mahanayak Samman in 2013, the Banga Bibhushan in 2018 and the Padma Shri in 2026.
He is married to actress Arpita Pal, with whom he has a son. His earlier marriages were to actress Debashree Roy and to Aparna Guha Thakurta, with whom he has a daughter.

Q3899724.lead: Ashok Kumar (born Kumudlal Ganguly; 1911–2001) was an Indian actor who worked in Hindi cinema from the 1930s to the 1990s, first as a romantic lead and later as a character actor. He received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1988.

p: He was born Kumudlal Ganguly in Bhagalpur, in present-day Bihar, the eldest of four children of lawyer Kunjlal Ganguly and Gouri Devi. He studied law at Presidency College, Calcutta, but was more drawn to cinema and initially hoped to work as a film technician.

Kumar made a reluctant debut opposite Devika Rani in Franz Osten's Jeevan Naiya (1936), and his breakthrough followed that year in Osten's Achhut Kannya. Kangan (1939), Bandhan (1940) and Jhoola (1941), all with Leela Chitnis, were each silver jubilee hits.

His lead role in Gyan Mukherjee's Kismet (1943), in which he played an anti-hero, became a record box-office success, running 184 weeks at Kolkata's Roxy Cinema. He produced and acted in Kamal Amrohi's Mahal (1949), remembered as Hindi cinema's first horror film, and in Bimal Roy's Parineeta (1953). Other successes of the period included Samadhi (1950), Sangram (1950), Afsana (1951), in which he played a double role, Deedar (1951) and Ek Hi Raasta (1956). He later moved into character roles, and his career lasted until 1997.
The Government of India awarded him the Padma Shri in 1962, the Dadasaheb Phalke Award in 1988 and the Padma Bhushan in 1999.

His siblings included Sati Devi, wife of producer Sashadhar Mukherjee, and the actors Anoop Kumar and Kishore Kumar, the latter also a playback singer. He married Shobha in 1938; their children were Aroop Ganguly, who acted in Bezubaan (1962), Bharati Patel, Rupa Verma and the actress Preeti Ganguly. Actress Anuradha Patel is his granddaughter. He died in Mumbai in 2001.

Q2992971.lead: Rituparna Sengupta (born 1970) is an Indian actress and producer who has worked in Bengali, Odia and Hindi cinema. Her first lead role in a feature film came in the Odia film Kotie Manisha Gotie Jaga (1991).

p: As a child Sengupta trained in painting, dance, singing and handicrafts at the Chitrangshu art school. She attended Carmel High School, took a history degree from Lady Brabourne College, and started an MA in Modern History at the University of Calcutta, which she left to pursue acting.

She first appeared on screen in the Bengali television series Rong Berong (1989) and made her film debut in the NFDC production Bahattar Din Par (1990). After seeing her stage performance in Jaisa Ka Taisa, director Shishir Majumdar cast her in Shesh Chithi, where co-star Bijay Mohanty encouraged her to audition for Vijay Bhaskar's Odia film Kotie Manisha Gotie Jaga (1991). In that film, a remake of Velai Kidaichuduchu, she played Radha opposite Mohanty and was credited as Chumki; it was a major commercial success.

The film led to further offers in Odia and Bengali cinema. She reunited with Mohanty in Bhagya Hate Dori (1993) and took the role of Titli in the Bengali film Shwet Pathorer Thala (1992). Her Hindi debut came in Teesra Kaun (1994). In the later 1990s she starred opposite Prosenjit Chatterjee in many commercially successful Bengali films, among them Mayar Badhon, Moner Manush, Tomake Chai and Sasurbari Zindabad, and also had hits in Bangladeshi cinema. In 2004 she appeared in the Odia film Katha Deithili Maa Ku with Sidhant Mohapatra.

Her other notable work includes Dahan (1997), Paromitar Ek Din (2000), Mondo Meyer Upakhyan (2002), Anuranan (2006), the Hindi film Main, Meri Patni Aur Woh (2005) and Chaturanga (2008), an adaptation of the Tagore novel.
She has received a National Film Award, two Filmfare Awards, four BFJA Awards and four Anandalok Awards.

facts: Lady Brabourne College; University of Calcutta

Q3630894.lead: Roopa Ganguly (born 1966) is an Indian actress, playback singer and politician, known for playing Draupadi in B. R. Chopra's television series Mahabharat. She has acted in Bengali and Hindi film and television, and in the Odia film Ranabhumi (1995).

p: Ganguly was born to Samarendra Lal Ganguly and Juthika Ganguly and grew up in a joint family. She attended Beltala Girls' High School and Jodhpur Park Girls' High School, then graduated from Jogamaya Devi College, affiliated to the University of Calcutta. She is trained in Rabindra Sangeet and classical dance.

She had not planned an acting career; after she was spotted at a wedding, Bijoy Chatterjee cast her in the title role of his Hindi telefilm Nirupama (1986), adapted from a Tagore story. Soumitra Chatterjee then cast her as Mrinal in his telefilm Stree Ki Patra (1986). The Bengali series Muktabandha (1986) gave her a breakthrough, the Hindi series Ganadevta (1987–88) brought national attention, and her Draupadi in Mahabharat (1988–90) made her widely known. Later television work included Chandrakanta, Kanoon and Agle Janam Mohe Bitiya Hi Kijo.

Her first feature film was Prabhat Roy's Bengali film Prateek (1988), opposite Chiranjeet. She was praised for her roles in Goutam Ghose's Padma Nadir Majhi (1992), Janani (1993) and Aparna Sen's Yugant (1995), and later in Antarmahal, Tarpor Bhalobasa and Krantikaal (all 2005). She has worked with directors including Mrinal Sen, Aparna Sen, Goutam Ghose and Rituparno Ghosh.

She won the National Film Award for Best Female Playback Singer for the Bengali film Abosheshey and the BFJA Award for Best Supporting Actress for Ujan (1995) and Antarmahal (2005).
