Antarmahal also earned her a special jury mention at the Osian's Cinefan Festival, and she was named Best Actress for Krantikaal at the 9th Dhaka International Film Festival.

She joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in 2015 and led its women's wing in West Bengal from 2015 to 2017. She was a nominated member of the Rajya Sabha from 2016 to 2022 and was elected to the West Bengal Legislative Assembly from Sonarpur Dakshin in 2026.

facts: Jogamaya Devi College, University of Calcutta

Q379604.lead: Mithun Chakraborty (born Gouranga Chakraborty, 1950) is an Indian actor, producer, entrepreneur and politician who has appeared in about 350 films, mainly in Hindi and Bengali, with a few in Odia and other languages.

p: Chakraborty was born in Calcutta to Basanta Kumar Chakraborty and Shanti Rani Chakraborty. He studied at Oriental Seminary and read chemistry at Scottish Church College, leaving after the second year of his BSc, and later graduated from the Film and Television Institute of India in Pune.

His debut came in Mrinal Sen's Mrigayaa (1976), which won him the National Film Award for Best Actor. He entered Bengali films with Nadi Theke Sagare (1978) and followed it with Hindi successes such as Surakksha (1979). B. Subhash's dance film Disco Dancer (1982) made him a star in India and abroad, particularly in the Soviet Union, and the same year Troyee established him in Bengali cinema.

Through the mid-1980s he headlined commercially successful films including Pyar Jhukta Nahin, Ghulami, Swarag Se Sunder and Pyar Ka Mandir, and was noted for Basu Chatterjee's Sheesha (1986). His role in Agneepath (1990) received strong reviews, and he won a second National Film Award for Best Actor for Buddhadeb Dasgupta's Bengali film Tahader Katha (1992). From the mid-1990s he worked mostly in lower-budget productions. Over his career he has also acted in Bhojpuri, Telugu, Odia, Tamil, Kannada and Punjabi films.

Outside acting, he owns the Monarch Group, started Paparatzy Productions, helped set up the Cine & T.V. Artistes Association in 1992, and was Grand Master on the television dance show Dance India Dance.

He has received three National Film Awards and four Filmfare Awards, including Best Supporting Actor for Agneepath. He was given the Banga Bibhushan in 2013, the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2022 and the Padma Bhushan in 2024.
He served as a Rajya Sabha member from West Bengal from 2014 to 2016 for the All India Trinamool Congress, and joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in March 2021.

facts: Scottish Church College; Film and Television Institute of India

Q5299396.lead: Jeet (born Jeetendra Madnani, 1978) is an Indian actor and film producer known mainly for his work in Bengali cinema, where he has appeared in more than fifty films since his 2001 debut.

p: Jeet was born in Kalighat, Kolkata, into a Sindhi family. He studied at Bhawanipur Education Society College.

He started out with modelling work and advertisements. A 1994 Doordarshan Bangla commercial led to his casting as Taracharan in the television series Bish Briksha, adapted from Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay's novel, and he went on to roles in serials such as Janani. He also assisted Tapan Sinha on the anthology film Daughters of This Century and appeared in two of its segments.

In late 1996 he moved to Mumbai, where he appeared in music videos, a segment of the series Aahat and a cameo in Jai Hanuman, but a film in which he was cast as the lead, Suraj Dhalne Ke Baad, was never released. Returning to Kolkata in 1998, he again assisted Tapan Sinha and acted in stage plays at the Proscenium Art Centre.

His feature debut was the Telugu film Chandu (2001), in which he was credited as Pavan Kumar; it failed commercially. His first Bengali film, Sathi (2002), an adaptation of Charlie Chaplin's City Lights, became the highest-grossing Bengali film of that year and made him a leading star. Hits such as Sangee (2003), Nater Guru (2003), Premi (2004) and Bandhan (2004) followed, the last pairing him again with Koel Mallick.

In 2004 he starred opposite Swastika Mukherjee in Mastan, a bilingual film made in Bengali and Odia, directed by Ravi Kinnagi, with whom he worked repeatedly afterwards. His later commercial successes include Josh (2010), Boss: Born to Rule (2013), Badsha – The Don (2016), Raavan (2022) and Chengiz (2023), the last being the first Bengali film released in Hindi at the same time.

He turned producer in 2012 with 100% Love and runs the production companies Grassroot Entertainment and Jeetz Filmworks. Since 2022 he has served as executive president of the West Bengal Motion Picture Artists' Forum.

For Sathi he received the Most Promising Actor award of the BFJA and the Anandalok Puraskar for Best Actor, and Bandhan brought him the BFJA Best Actor award. His role in Shakti (2004) won him Best Actor at the Bangla Sangeet Chalacchitra Samman in 2005. Other honours include Filmfare Awards East (2014) and Bengali Film & Television Awards (2023, 2024).
He married Mohna Ratlani, a school teacher from Lucknow, in 2011; the couple have a daughter and a son.

Q7635908.lead: Bandreddi Sukumar (born 1971) is a Telugu film director, screenwriter and producer. Arya, Rangasthalam and the two Pushpa films are among his works.

p: The youngest of six children of Tirupathi Rao Naidu, a rice trader, and Veera Veni, he was born in Mattaparru near Malikipuram in what was then East Godavari district. After schooling at Zilla Parishad High School, Razole, he completed a master's in mathematics and spent about seven years teaching mathematics and physics at Aditya Junior College, Kakinada.
He and a fellow lecturer, Prakash Toleti, gave up teaching to write for Telugu films. He then worked as an assistant director, including with Editor Mohan and on V. V. Vinayak's Dil (2003).

Arya (2004), starring Allu Arjun, was his first film as director and a big hit with audiences and critics. Jagadam (2007) did poorly at the box office but later found a cult audience; Arya 2 (2009) and 100% Love (2011) were commercial successes. The psychological thriller 1: Nenokkadine (2014) got mixed reviews and lost money before it too gained a cult following. That year he also made I Am That Change, a short film with Allu Arjun.

His later films are Nannaku Prematho (2016), Rangasthalam (2018), Pushpa: The Rise (2021), which was the top-grossing Indian film of its year, and Pushpa 2: The Rule (2024). As a producer, through Sukumar Writings, he has made Kumari 21F (2015), Uppena (2021) and Virupaksha (2023).

For Arya he received the Filmfare Award for Best Director – Telugu and the Nandi Award for Best Screenplay Writer. He is also a National Award-winning screenwriter and received the K. V. Reddy Memorial Award in 2014. 100% Love was named Best Home-viewing Feature Film at the Nandi Awards.

Q5584168.lead: Gopal Chhotray (1916–2003) was an Odia playwright and screenwriter who wrote for the professional stage, radio, television and Odia films, including the dialogue for Sri Jagannath (1950) and Amada Bata.

p: He was born in Puranagarh village in Jagatsinghpur district and lived in Cuttack for his whole life.

Chhotray began as an amateur actor with Bharati Theatres in Cuttack. From Pheria in 1946 he wrote more than fifteen original plays and eight stage adaptations of Odia novels, and for over three decades his work dominated Odia professional theatre. He moved Odia drama away from opera and melodrama and reduced the influence of Bengali theatre on its themes and form.

He was linked to All India Radio, Cuttack, from 1948 and was its staff script writer from 1956 to 1975, writing more than five hundred radio plays, musicals and features. He revived rural opera for broadcast from 1960 and produced the musical Srimati Samarjani with Akshaya Mohanty. He later helped shape the drama output of Odisha Doordarshan, scripting around a hundred plays and features.

In cinema, his reputation as a script writer began with the mythological Sri Jagannath (1950). Over the next thirty-five years he wrote screenplays and dialogue for Odia films; his writing for Amada Bata, Kie Kahara, Matira Manisha and Badhu Nirupama was critically praised. In later life he published two collections of short stories.

His film credits include Shree Jagannatha (1950), Maa (1958), Nua Bou (1962), Amada Bata (1964), Abhinetri (1965), Matira Manisha (1967), Kie Kahara (1968), Bandhan (1969), Adina Megha (1970), Dharitri (1973), Ramayana (1980), School Master (1985) and Badhu Nirupama (1985).

He received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1982 for Hasyarasara Nataka, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1987, the Padma Shri in 2002, the Sarala Award in 2000 and an Odisha Sahitya Akademi award, along with the Bisuba Samman and the Governor's Plaque of Honour (1991).
His children are Devdas Chhotray and Kasturi. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2003.

Q5886033.lead: Raghunath Panigrahi (1932–2013) was an Odissi vocalist, composer and music director, best known for singing Jayadeva's Gita Govinda and for accompanying his wife, the Odissi dancer Sanjukta Panigrahi. He also sang in Odia and South Indian films.

p: He was born in Gunupur, in present-day Rayagada district, into a family that had been linked with Odissi music for generations. He first learned from his father, Pandit Nilamani Panigrahi, who had gathered traditional Gita Govinda melodies from the Jagannath Temple in Puri, and went on to study under Pandit Narasingha Nandasarma and Pandit Biswanath Das. He later trained in Carnatic music with Madu Pappa Rao and in Hindustani vocal music with D. V. Paluskar in Madras.

In 1948 he became a regular artist at All India Radio, Cuttack. He sang bhajans, jananas, Odissi chhandas, champus and ghazals, and worked as a playback singer and music director in Odia, Kannada, Tamil and Telugu cinema before giving up film work in Chennai to sing for his wife's dance performances.

The couple performed together from the 1960s to the 1990s, touring Asia and Europe, and he composed music for many Odissi pallavis, abhinaya pieces and dance dramas. After Sanjukta's death in 1997 he composed for productions of the dance village Nrityagram, and in 1999 set up the Sanjukta Panigrahi Memorial Trust, which has given scholarships to young dancers since 2001.
His first Odia playback work was in Shri Shri Patitapaban (1963). He also sang in Sindura Bindu (1976), Mukti (1977) and Ahalya (1998), and was music director of Abhinetri (1965).

He won Odisha State Film Awards for playback singing in Mukti (1977) and for music in Ahalya (1998). A Mumbai cultural body gave him the title Surmani in 1968. Other honours include the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1976), the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1993), the Jayadeva Samman (2008), the Padma Shri (2010) and honorary doctorates from Berhampur, Utkal and Ravenshaw universities.
He met Sanjukta Panigrahi at the Kalakshetra dance school and married her in 1960; they had two sons, the elder of whom, Parthasarathi Panigrahi, is a singer. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2013.

facts: Ahe Nila Saila, Lalita Labanga Lata, Na Ja Radhika Eka Eka

Q7425857.lead: Satabdi Roy (born 1969) is an Indian actress, film director and politician, known mainly for Bengali films of the late 1980s and 1990s and a Lok Sabha member for Birbhum since 2009.

p: She was born in Agarpara to Shailen and Nilima Roy, passed her Madhyamik from Sorojini High School in 1986 and studied at Jogamaya Devi College in Kolkata.

Her first released film was Tapan Sinha's Atanka (1986), opposite Prosenjit Chatterjee, which brought her a BFJA award for best supporting actress. Pairings with Tapas Paul in Amar Bandhan (1986), Guru Dakshina (1987), Antaranga (1988) and Angar (1989) made her a star.

Through the 1990s she had commercial successes including Apan Amar Apan and Abishkar (both 1990), Shraddhanjali (1993), Lathi (1996), Sakhi Tumi Kar (1996), Chandragrahan (1997) and Trishul (2000). She also appeared in Prashanta Nanda's Ghar Sansar (1993) and made her Hindi debut in Jyoti Sarup's Naya Zaher (1991).

Her later work included Debipaksha (2004), the stage production Teesta (2016) and the film Bizli (2018), in which she played the antagonist. As a director she made Abhinetri (2006), Om Shanti (2012) and Paribartan (released 2017); the first two failed with critics and at the box office.
She received the BFJA award for best supporting actress twice, for Atanka in 1987 and for Debipaksha in 2005.
She is married to Mrigank Banerjee and has a son and a daughter. Outside films she has taught acting at the Satabdi Foundation.

Q16233840.lead: Hariprriya (born Shruthi Chandrasena, 1991) is an Indian actress and model who works mostly in Kannada cinema and has also acted in Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam and Tulu films.

p: She was born in Chikkaballapur, trained in Bharatanatyam after school, and completed her pre-university studies in Bangalore after her family moved there.

While she was in class 12, director Richard Castelino cast her as the lead in the Tulu film Badi. Her Kannada debut was Manasugula Mathu Madhura (2008), and Kallara Santhe (2009), opposite Yash, earned her a Filmfare nomination. In 2010 she began working in Tamil with Kanagavel Kaaka and in Telugu with Thakita Thakita, later appearing in Pilla Zamindar and in the Malayalam film Thiruvambadi Thamban.

She returned to Kannada films with the gangster drama Ugramm (2014), a commercial success that revived her career there. Ranna (2015), Bullet Basya (2015), Ricky (2016), in which she played a Naxalite, and Neer Dose (2016), in which she played a bar dancer, followed.

Later work includes Bharjari (2017), the Telugu film Jai Simha (2018), Samhaara (2018), where she played a negative role, Bell Bottom (2019), Soojidara, D/O Parvathamma, Kurukshetra (her 25th Kannada film), Bicchugatti: Chapter 1 (2020), Petromax (2022), the Tamil film Naan Mirugamai Maara (2022) and Yadha Yadha Hi (2023). In 2025 two of her films, Thaayi Kasthur Gandhi and Amruthamathi, were released directly on Amazon Prime Video.
She married the Kannada actor Vasishta N. Simha in Mysuru in January 2023.

Q3595279.lead: B. V. Karanth (Babukodi Venkataramana Karanth, 1929–2002) was an Indian theatre director, playwright, actor, screenwriter and composer who worked in Kannada and Hindi theatre and cinema and headed the National School of Drama.

p: Karanth was born at Manchi, near Babukodi in Bantwal taluk of Dakshina Kannada. He acted in a school play in standard III and later ran away to join the Gubbi Veeranna drama company. Veeranna sent him to Banaras for a master's degree, where he also studied Hindustani music under Omkarnath Thakur. He graduated from the National School of Drama (NSD), New Delhi, in 1962, receiving its best all-round student award.

After teaching drama at Sardar Patel Vidyalaya in Delhi from 1969 to 1972, he returned to Bangalore and, with his wife Prema Karanth, founded the theatre group Benaka in 1974. His Kannada productions of the early 1970s, such as Jokumara Swamy, Sankranti, Huchu Kudure and Oedipus, broke with the formal proscenium style and were noted for their use of classical, traditional and folk music.

He directed the NSD from 1977 to 1981, was founding director of the Rangamandal repertory at Bharat Bhavan, Bhopal, and from 1989 to 1995 led Rangayana, the repertory he set up in Mysore for the Karnataka government. He directed more than a hundred plays in Kannada, Hindi and several other languages, and translated plays including Girish Karnad's Tughlaq into Hindi.

In cinema he directed four feature films and four documentaries, co-directed Vamsha Vriksha and Tabbaliyu Neenade Magane with Girish Karnad, and composed music for 26 films. He died in Bangalore in 2002.

He won six National Film Awards, including Best Direction for Vamsha Vriksha, Best Feature Film for Chomana Dudi and Best Music Direction for Rishya Shrunga and Ghatashraddha. He also received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1976), the Kalidas Samman (1976) and the Padma Shri (1981), along with Karnataka State Film Awards and Filmfare Awards South for direction. A Films Division documentary about him, BV Karanth: Baba, was made in 2012.
His wife, Prema Karanth, was a theatre figure who looked after Benaka.

facts: Padma Shri (1981), Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1976)

Q3503124.lead: Kelucharan Mohapatra (1926–2004) was an Odissi dancer, guru and choreographer who played a leading part in reviving Odissi dance and gaining it recognition as a classical form in the 20th century.

p: He was born into a family of artisans in the crafts village of Raghurajpur, Puri. His father, Chintamani Mohapatra, was a painter and mardala player. Drawn to Gotipua dance as a boy, he was instead placed by his father in Mohan Sundar Dev Goswami's Kunja Bihari Rasa Lila troupe in Puri, where he spent ten years learning dance, music, acting, make-up and stagecraft, along with mridanga from Agadhu Maharana and tabla from Kshetramohan Kar. He was also skilled in Pattachitra painting.

After his father's death he worked for a time as a labourer in a betel garden before moving to Cuttack, where he joined Kabichandra Kalicharan Pattnaik's Odisha Theatres as a stage hand and mardala player. He then joined the Annapurna B troupe, where, under Guru Pankaj Charan Das, he came to notice as Nataraja in the dance drama Devi Bhasmasura, opposite Laxmipriya as Mohini.

Moving to Puri with Laxmipriya after their marriage, the two researched Mahari and Gotipua dance, which he used to reshape Odissi. In 1953 he joined Kala Vikash Kendra in Cuttack, introducing Odissi to its curriculum and teaching there for fifteen years; works from this period include Pancha Pushpa, Krishna Gatha, Gita Govinda, Urvashi and Konark. He also studied dance poses carved on Odisha's temples.

From the 1980s he taught across India and performed in Japan, Germany, Russia, France, the United Kingdom and the United States. He was associated with the Odissi Research Centre in Bhubaneswar for about ten years; it was later named after him. In 1993 he founded Srjan with Laxmipriya and their son Ratikant. He is credited with around 200 solo compositions and 50 dance dramas. His disciples included Sanjukta Panigrahi, Kumkum Mohanty, Sonal Mansingh, Madhavi Mudgal, Protima Bedi and Sujata Mohapatra. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2004.

He received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1966), the Padma Shri, the Padma Bhushan, the Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship (1991) and the Padma Vibhushan (2000), the first person from Odisha to receive the last. Other honours include the Kalidas Samman, the Srimanta Sankardeva Award, the Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja Samman (2000) and a doctorate from the Akhil Bharatiya Gandharva Mahavidyalaya Mandal (1981). In 2023 India issued a postage stamp bearing his image.
He was married to the dancer Laxmipriya Mohapatra; their son Ratikant Mohapatra is also a dancer.

Q3345399.lead: Bappi Lahiri (born Alokesh Aparesh Lahiri, 1952–2022) was an Indian singer, composer and record producer who popularised synthesised disco music in Indian film songs, working mainly in Hindi, Telugu and Bengali cinema and also scoring an Odia film.

p: He was born in Siliguri, West Bengal, the only child of the singers Aparesh and Bansuri Lahiri; the singer Kishore Kumar was his maternal uncle. He began playing tabla at three, learning first from his parents and later from Samta Prasad. He attended Chetla Boys' High School.

Lahiri moved to Mumbai at 19. His first film was the Bengali Daadu (1972), and his first Hindi score was for Nanha Shikari (1973). Zakhmee (1975), for which he composed and also sang, was his breakthrough, and the songs of Chalte Chalte (1976) brought him national recognition.

In the 1980s he scored many hits, including Disco Dancer, Namak Halaal, Himmatwala, Tohfa, Sharaabi and Adhikar, and composed for twelve silver-jubilee films starring Jeetendra between 1983 and 1985. In 1986 Guinness World Records recognised him for recording more than 180 songs for 33 films in a single year. He was also known for his look of gold chains and sunglasses.

Beyond Hindi, he composed for Kannada and Tamil films and for the Odia film Michha Maya Sansara. Later he voiced Tamatoa in the Hindi version of Moana (2016) and appeared as a guest judge on television music shows. In 2014 he contested the Lok Sabha election from Sreerampur as a Bharatiya Janata Party candidate and lost. He died in Mumbai in 2022.
He received the Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award at the 63rd Filmfare Awards and the Banga Bhushan from the Government of West Bengal in 2017.

Q2107874.lead: Prashanta Nanda (born 1947) is an Odia film actor, director, writer, lyricist and playback singer, and a politician who has served as an Odisha state minister and a Rajya Sabha member. He worked mainly in Odia cinema, with Bengali and Hindi films as well.

p: Nanda was born in Cuttack to Jagannath and Kanchan Nanda. He attended Ravenshaw Collegiate School, took a B.Sc. at Ravenshaw College, an M.A. and Ph.D. at Utkal University and an LL.B. at Madhusudan Law College. As a child he acted in school plays and played the character Bulu in the children's programme Sishu Sansar on All India Radio, Cuttack.

While he was performing in a play at Kala Vikash Kendra in Cuttack, Kaviraj Krushna Chandra Tripathy and Dhira Biswal cast him in Dasyu Ratnakar (1962). He played the lead in Nua Bou the same year. Nua Bou, Matira Manisha (1966) and Adina Megha (1970) each won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia. He also worked with directors including Prabhat Mukherjee and Mrinal Sen.

He first directed Mamata (1975), though Byomkesh Tripathy was credited because of Nanda's age; Shesha Shrabana (1976), which introduced Mahasweta Ray, was his acknowledged debut. After it was shown at IFFI, Rajshri Productions asked him to remake it in Hindi as Naiyya (1979), which he directed and starred in; he made Paheli for the same company and directed Grahasthi (1984). Maa O Mamata (1980), drawn from a story he wrote as a ninth-grade student, was a major success. His other Odia films as director include Balidan, Hisab Nikas, Swapna Sagara, Dora, Jaga Balia, Hira Nila, Lal Pan Bibi, Ghara Sansara, Om Shanti Om, Jianta Bhoota and Thukul, and he also directed the Bengali film Maa (1992). He is credited with acting in about 40 films and directing 24, and he composed the music for Ghara Sansara (1993). He frequently worked with the actor Sidhant Mohapatra.

Nanda has also written four novels and three short-story collections and writes newspaper columns. In politics, he was a BJP state vice president before moving to the Nationalist Congress Party and then the Biju Janata Dal; he represented Begunia in the Odisha Legislative Assembly (2000–2004 and 2009–2014), served as an Odisha minister, and entered the Rajya Sabha in 2018.

Jianta Bhoota won the National Film Award for Best Film on Environment Conservation/Preservation at the 56th National Film Awards. He received Odisha State Film Awards as best actor for Mamata, Mana Akash and Gauri, and as best director for Maa O Mamata, Om Shanti Om and Thukul. Other honours include the Jayadev Award, a lifetime achievement award at the Odisha Filmfare Awards and the Utkala Viswa Gaurab Samman (2025).
He is married to Anupama Nanda; their son is Rhishav Nanda.

facts: Ravenshaw College, Utkal University, Madhusudan Law College

Q4907191.lead: Bijaya Jena, also known as Dolly Jena, is an Indian actress, film director and producer from Cuttack who acted in Hindi and Odia films and directed the Odia film Tara (1992).

p: Jena was born in Cuttack, the youngest of three children of B. C. Jena, a civil engineer. As a teenager she joined the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII), where she earned a diploma in film acting.

In Hindi cinema she appeared in The Naxalites (1981), Razia Sultan (1983), in which she played Laila, Holi (1984) and Uparaant (1987), and she acted in Nicholas Meyer's British film The Deceivers (1988). Her Odia films include Ashara Akash (1983), Jaga Balia (1984), Heera Neela (1984) and Hakim Babu (1985). On television she appeared in Ek Kahani, Vikram Aur Betaal and Param Veer Chakra.

She made her directing debut with Tara (1992), based on a short story by Bimal Dutt; she co-wrote, produced and played the title role, financing the film with loans from family and government agencies. Tara was shown at festivals in Marseille and Cairo. Her second film, the Hindi Abhaas (1997), which she wrote, directed, produced and acted in, was screened at La Rochelle, Penang and Cairo and later broadcast in Britain and Mauritius. She later wrote a screenplay of Gopinath Mohanty's novel Danapani and in 2022 began the English short film Winter Interlude.

She served on the FTII Governing Council from 1992 to 1995 and has sat on many film juries, including the 40th and 67th National Film Awards, the International Film Festival of India and festivals in Iran, Armenia, Estonia and Egypt.

She won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress for Jaga Balia. Tara received the National Film Award for Best Odia Film in 1992. She also received a Lifetime Dedication Award at the 3rd Real Vision Odisha Film Fair Awards in 2012.

facts: Film and Television Institute of India

Q15725391.lead: Soumya Ranjan Patnaik (born 1952) is an Odisha journalist, media owner, film producer and politician who founded the Odia daily Sambad and has produced several Odia films.

p: His father, Brajabandhu Patnaik, was a forest ranger, so he completed his schooling in several places across Odisha. He graduated in political science from Ravenshaw College and studied further at Banaras Hindu University and Utkal University, and later at the London School of Economics and Oxford University.

He began teaching at Banaras Hindu University in 1972. In 1984 he founded the Odia daily Sambad, introducing features such as a separate editorial page, a sports page and offset printing. Through Eastern Media Limited he went on to run the news channel Kanak News, the entertainment channel Manjari, the FM station Radio Chocolate and the Eastern Opera jatra troupe, and he founded an engineering college and a media school. He writes the column Ama Gharara Halchal and stepped down as editor of Sambad in October 2023.
In Odia cinema he produced Lal Odhani, Tu Bhari Beautiful, Tu Au Mu and Mimansa, co-produced To Pain Nebi Mu Sahe Janama, and wrote the story of Babu I Love You.

In politics he won the Bhubaneswar Lok Sabha seat for the Congress in 1996, later formed the Aama Odisha Party, merged it into the Biju Janata Dal in 2018 and was nominated to the Rajya Sabha that year. He represented Khandapada in the Odisha Legislative Assembly from 2019 to 2024.

He is married to Sudatta Patnaik, daughter of former Chief Minister Janaki Ballabh Patnaik and Jayanti Patnaik; they have two daughters, Tallina and Tanaya. His elder brother is the politician Niranjan Patnaik.

facts: Ravenshaw College, Banaras Hindu University, Utkal University

Q13560184.lead: Prafulla Kar (1939–2022) was an Odia music director, singer, lyricist, writer and columnist from Puri who composed music for more than 70 Odia films and was awarded the Padma Shri in 2015.

p: Kar was born in Puri into a family of musicians; his parents were Baidyanath Kar and Sushila Kar, and his uncle Khetra Mohan Kar played the tabla. Visits by musicians to the family home exposed him to music as a child. After his father died when Kar was young, he grew up in his maternal grandparents' household, raised by Bhagaban Mishra and Aparna Devi.

He studied at Gadadhar High School and Samanta Chandrasekhar College in Puri, then took graduate degrees in arts and law from Utkal University. He later earned the Sangeet Visharad qualification through the Akhil Bharatiya Gandharva Mahavidyalaya, studying under teachers including Guru Markandeya Mahapatra.

Kar began his professional music career in 1960 and became an A-grade composer, singer and lyricist for All India Radio and for television. He directed music, and often sang, in about 70 Odia films, released and unreleased, as well as four Bengali films. His film scores drew heavily on Odissi classical music and Odia folk tunes, and singers such as Anuradha Paudwal, Usha Mangeshkar, Kavita Krishnamurthy, Suresh Wadkar, Vani Jairam, S. Janaki, Yesudas and S. P. Balasubrahmanyam recorded Odia film songs under his direction.

Outside cinema he composed music for Odissi dance dramas with choreographers including Kelucharan Mohapatra, Sharmila Biswas and Kumkum Mohanty, and recorded albums such as an Odia Bhagabata series. He wrote a regular column for the daily Dharitri, later collected in the book Saunta Kahani, and published two books of bhajans, Ajnamala and Krupajala. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2022.

Kar received the Odisha State Film Award for best music direction eight times. Other honours included the Jayadev Puraskar for lifetime contribution (2004), the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award (2006), the Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja Samman from the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi (2009), a D.Litt. from Utkal University of Culture, and the Padma Shri in 2015. A foundation set up in his name in 2007 has presented the annual Prafulla Kar Samman since 2008.

He was married to Manorama Kar. Their elder son Mahadeep plays guitar and harmonium, their daughter Sandhyadipa Kar is an Odissi dancer, and their younger son Mahaprasad is a Hindustani classical vocalist.

facts: Music director, singer, lyricist, writer, columnist
Utkal University (arts and law); Sangeet Visharad
Padma Shri (2015); Odisha State Film Award for music direction (8 times)

Q2787402.lead: Haldhar Nag (born 1950) is a poet and writer in the Sambalpuri (Kosli) language from Ghens in Bargarh district, Odisha, known as Lok Kabi Ratna and awarded the Padma Shri in 2016.

p: Nag was born in Ghens, Bargarh district, the youngest of six children of Bhaja Nag and Gurubari, in a poor family. Financial hardship ended his schooling in the third grade. He later worked as a dishwasher in a sweet shop and then spent 16 years as a cook at a high school, near which he opened a small stationery shop with borrowed money.

Nag first composed traditional Sambalpuri songs such as bhajans, Rasarkeli, Dalkhai and Sajani, which were performed in local Danda Nata. His early poem Dhodo Bargachh (The Old Banyan Tree) appeared in a local magazine and was followed by further published poems. His poetry deals with everyday life, social issues, nature, religion and resistance to oppression. Among his works are Mahasati Urmila, Achhia, Tara Mandodari, Bachhar, Siri Somalai, Veer Surendra Sai, Karamsani and Rasia Kavi; Sambalpur University published a collection of his work, Haldhar Granthabali-2, and included it in its syllabus. His writing has been translated into Odia, Hindi and English.

He acted in two Sambalpuri films, Sahamate Maa Samalei and Maa Budhi Kamgei Kathani, and made a brief appearance in the 2015 Hindi film Kaun Kitne Paani Mein. A short film about him narrated by Gulzar formed part of Bharatbala's Virtual Bharat series.

Nag received the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award in 2014, the Padma Shri in 2016 for his contribution to the Sambalpuri language, and the Sahitya Akademi Bhasha Samman in 2017, shared with Prafulla Tripathy. Sambalpur University awarded him an honorary doctorate in literature. A Kosli language and literature research centre named after him was set up in Ghens.
He is married to Malati Nag and has a daughter, Nandini.

facts: Padma Shri (2016); Sahitya Akademi Bhasha Samman (2017)

Q26981431.lead: Akshay Kumar Parija (born 1954) is an Odia film producer and former banker from Jagatsinghpur whose films, including the National Award-winning Jianta Bhoota (2008), focus on Odia culture and Odissi dance.

p: Parija was born in Jagatsinghpur to Alekha Bihari Parija and Khetramani. He attended Jagannathpur High School in Tiran in the former Cuttack district, graduated from BJB College, took a master's degree at Utkal University, and later studied at Harvard Business School.

He began his banking career at Indian Overseas Bank in Bissam Cuttack in 1976 and spent more than 30 years in banking, including senior posts at Burgan Bank in Kuwait, National Bank of Oman and Bank Muscat. In 2010 he founded Blue Lines Shipping Group, and he lives in Dubai.

His exposure to tribal life around Bissam Cuttack led him to produce Jianta Bhoota (The Living Ghost), directed by Prashant Nanda, about the displacement of the Dongria Kondh of the Niyamgiri Hills by mining. His second Odia production, Thukul, told the story of an Odissi dancer, starred Archita Sahu, Babushaan and Pakruti Mishra, and was made for about Rs 3 crore with locations in the Middle East. He followed it with Kehi Nuhen Kahara and was associated with God's Own People, a documentary on the Nabakalebara of Lord Jagannath directed by Nila Madhab Panda.

Parija also produced the Hindi film Kadvi Hawa with Nila Madhab Panda, as well as television reality shows and serials such as Sahanai for Tarang TV and Dancing Stars and Aaina for Colors Odia. For more than 15 years he presented Odissi dance on stages in the Far East, the Middle East, Europe and the United States. His international co-production Papa Buka was selected as Papua New Guinea's entry for the 98th Academy Awards.

Jianta Bhoota won the National Film Award for Best Film on Environment Conservation/Preservation at the 56th National Film Awards, seven Odisha State Film Awards including Best Film, and awards at the Independent South Asian Film Festival in the United States. Thukul received five State Film Awards. Kadvi Hawa brought him recognition at the 64th National Film Awards, and Kehi Nuhen Kahara earned him the Odia Film Fair Award for Best Producer in 2015.
His daughter is Payal Parija.

facts: BJB College; Utkal University; Harvard Business School

Q15724579.lead: Parbati Ghose (born Chapala Nayak; 1933–2018) was an Odia film actress, director and producer, recognised as the first woman filmmaker from Odisha.

p: She was born Chapala Nayak in Manasinghpatana, Cuttack district, one of eight siblings. Her father, Basudev Naik, managed the Manmohan Press, a book publisher. She studied at Sanat Nalini Girls High School in Cuttack and trained in dance under Kelucharan Mohapatra, Dayal Sharma and Suresh Routray. She began performing at the age of five, in the Odia play Mamata and the Hindi play Do Aansoo, and also worked as a child voice artist for All India Radio.

Her screen debut came as a child artist playing Nila Madhab in Sri Jagannath. Her first leading role, opposite Gour Prasad Ghose, was in Amari Gaan Jhua (1953), a film about child marriage that earned her good reviews. She next played the female lead in the successful Bhai Bhai (1956), produced by Gour Prasad Ghose, which raised her profile and sparked her interest in directing and producing; Maa (1959) followed.

With her husband she produced, co-directed and acted in Lakshmi (1962), Kaa and Stree (1968), all three of which won National Film Awards. She also appeared in Sansar, which the couple produced and directed together, and acted in the Hindi telefilms Prashna and Sopan. In 1986 she produced and directed Chamana Atha Guntha, based on the novel by Fakir Mohan Senapati, in which she also played Saria, wrote the dialogue and sang as a playback singer. Her last film as producer and director was Salabega. She died in Bhubaneswar in 2018 and was given a state funeral.

Her honours included the Lions Award (1970), the Jayadev Puraskar (1988), a Bengal Film Journalists' Association award and the Odisha Cine Critics Award (1998). In 2023 she was featured on an Indian postage stamp.

In 1959 she married the actor, producer and director Gour Prasad Ghose and took the name Parbati Ghose. Their daughter Ratri is an actress. Her elder brother Sarada Prasanna Nayak was a director and lyricist, and her younger brother Swarup Nayak a music director and lyricist.

facts: Sanat Nalini Girls High School, Cuttack

Q29841194.lead: Iti Rani Samanta (born 1970) is an Odia writer, journalist, magazine editor and film producer who edits the monthly Kadambini and the children's magazine Kunikatha and produced the Odia films Kathantara and Krantidhara.

p: Samanta was born in Kalarabanka village in Cuttack district, the youngest of seven children of Anadi Charan Samanta and Nilimarani Samanta. Her father died when she was about two, and her mother raised the family in financial hardship. After school in Kalarabanka and Cuttack and higher secondary science at Ramadevi Women's College, she studied electronics and telecommunication. She went on to master's degrees in Odia literature and in mass communication and journalism at Utkal University, and a PhD in literature from Visva-Bharati University, Santiniketan.

Her writing includes short stories, novels and feature articles, many on women's empowerment and gender issues; her books include the story collections Tathapi and Iti Tora Lipsa and the novel Nirab Alap. In 2000 she set up Kadambini Media Pvt Ltd, together with her brother Achyuta Samanta, which publishes The Kadambini and The Kunikatha and has produced television series, telefilms and music albums.

The company's first feature film, Kathantara, directed by Himansu Sekhar Khatua, dealt with refugees affected by the super cyclone in Odisha. Its next feature, Krantidhara, was based on her short story Jhada Parara Surya and follows a woman's struggle in politics. She also produced the films Chithi and Kanyaratna and a short film, Kahani Nuhen, based on her own life. In November 2023 she served on the Indian Panorama feature film jury at the 54th International Film Festival of India.

Kathantara won the National Film Award for Best Odia Feature Film (2006) and the Odisha State Film Award for Best Film. Krantidhara received the Odisha State Film Award for best feature film in 2014, along with the award for best story writer for Samanta, and later won at the Asian Excellence Film Awards in South Korea in 2019. As an editor she received the Rajiv Gandhi Sadbhabana Award in 2007 and 2008.
Her elder brother is Achyuta Samanta.

Q6665461.lead: Locket Chatterjee (born 1974) is an Indian actress, classical dancer and politician, known chiefly for Bengali films, who represented the Hooghly constituency of West Bengal in the Lok Sabha from 2019 to 2024.

p: Chatterjee was born in Dakshineswar, West Bengal, and grew up beside the Hooghly on the northern edge of Kolkata. Her father, Anil Chatterjee, and her grandfather were priests at the Dakshineswar Kali Temple. Her mother enrolled her in dance school, and while in class VIII she toured abroad with Mamata Shankar's ballet troupe. She trained in Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, Manipuri and creative dance, and later studied at Jogamaya Devi College under the University of Calcutta.

Chatterjee began acting in Bengali cinema in the early 2000s with films such as Ektu Chhoa (2002) and Mayer Anchal (2003). Her later Bengali films include Minister Fatakeshto, Bye Bye Bangkok, Khokababu, Kayekta Meyer Galpo, Kiriti Roy and Sannyasi Deshonayok (2020). On television she appeared in Maa Manasha, Bhalobasha Theke Jaye, Behula and Tarun Majumdar's adaptation of Durgeshnandini, in which she played Munnibai.

She entered politics with the Trinamool Congress and moved to the Bharatiya Janata Party in 2015. She led the party's women's wing in West Bengal from 2017 and became a state general secretary in 2020. She won the Hooghly Lok Sabha seat in 2019 and lost it in 2024 to Rachna Banerjee.
She received a Kalakar Award and was nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress (Bengali) for Nayika Sangbad.

facts: Jogamaya Devi College, University of Calcutta

Q2723357.lead: Moushumi Chatterjee (born Indira Chattopadhyay) is an Indian actress and politician who worked mainly in Hindi and Bengali cinema, where she was a leading actress of the 1970s.

p: Chatterjee was born in Calcutta into a family with roots in Bikrampur, in present-day Bangladesh. Her father, Prantosh Chattopadhyaya, served in the Indian Army. Indira was her given name; Moushumi became her screen name. She married young, while still a school student.

As a preteen she played the child bride in Tarun Majumdar's Bengali film Balika Badhu (1967), followed by Bengali films such as Parineeta and Anindita. Encouraged by her father-in-law and husband, she accepted Shakti Samanta's offer to play a blind girl in Anuraag (1972), her first Hindi lead, which brought her a Filmfare Best Actress nomination.

Through the 1970s she acted opposite Shashi Kapoor, Vinod Khanna, Rajesh Khanna, Amitabh Bachchan and Sanjeev Kumar, and was paired with Vinod Mehra in ten films. Her role as a rape survivor in Manoj Kumar's Roti Kapada Aur Makaan (1974) earned a Filmfare Best Supporting Actress nomination. Other films included Benaam, Swayamvar, Manzil, Angoor and the Bengali Ogu Bodhu Sundari (1981) with Uttam Kumar.

From the mid-1980s she moved mostly into character parts, such as Sunny Deol's sister-in-law in Ghayal, while still taking occasional leads in the 1990s. Later work included Bollywood/Hollywood (2003), Zindaggi Rocks (2006), The Japanese Wife (2010) and Goynar Baksho (2013). In politics she stood unsuccessfully for the Congress from Calcutta North East in 2004 and joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in 2019.
She won two Bengal Film Journalists' Association Awards, the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress (Bengali) for Goynar Baksho in 2014, and the Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award in 2015.
She married Jayanta Mukherjee, a Rabindra Sangeet singer and son of the composer and singer Hemanta Mukhopadhyay (Hemant Kumar). The couple had two daughters.

Q5320261.lead: Kalindi Charan Panigrahi (1901–1991) was an Odia poet, novelist, short-story writer, dramatist and essayist, best known for the novel Matira Manisha, which Mrinal Sen adapted into the 1966 Odia film of the same name.

p: Panigrahi was born in Biswanathpur in Puri district to Swapneswar Panigrahi, a lawyer and freedom fighter, and Saraswati Panigrahi. He went to Puri Zilla School and then Ravenshaw College in Cuttack, where his writing career began.

At Ravenshaw he founded the Nonsense Club, whose members produced a handwritten magazine, Abakash, later renamed Shakti Sadhana. In 1920 he was part of the Sabuja Samiti with Annada Shankar Ray and Baikuntha Patnaik, a group influenced by Rabindranath Tagore that gave rise to the Sabuja Juga movement in Odia literature; he contributed seven poems to the anthology Sabuja Kabita. He later edited the English journals Bhanja Pradipa and Mayurbhanja Chronicle.

His writing often depicted rural Odisha and its customs and spoke against injustice. Influenced by Gandhian thought, he wrote Matira Manisha, a novel about quarrels and the division of property within a village family. His other works include the poetry collections Jadu Ghara, Puri Mandira, Mahadipa and Mo Kabita; the novels Mukta Gadara Kshudha, Amarachita, Luhara Manisha and Aajira Manisha; short stories such as Rashi Phala and Sagarika; the plays Padmini and Priyadarshi; and the autobiography Jaha Ange Nibhaichi. He died in Cuttack in 1991.
In 1971 he was made a fellow of the Sahitya Akademi and received the Padma Bhushan. He also received the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award, and Sambalpur University gave him an honorary D.Litt. in 1976.

facts: Matira Manisha (1966), directed by Mrinal Sen

Q5276809.lead: Dilip Kumar Ray (born 1954) is an Odia politician and hotelier from Rourkela who served as a Union minister of state and founded the Mayfair group of hotels.

p: Ray was born in Rourkela; his father was Hrushikesh Ray. He holds MBA and LLB degrees.

Ray became chairman of the Rourkela Notified Area Council in 1985 and in the same year won the Rourkela Assembly seat, which he held again from 1990. From 1990 to 1995 he was industries minister in Biju Patnaik's Janata Dal government in Odisha. He entered the Rajya Sabha in 1996 and served two terms up to 2008, during which he held independent charge as Union minister of state for animal husbandry and dairying, food processing industries, coal and steel, and was also minister of state for parliamentary affairs.

After Biju Patnaik's death, Ray was among the Janata Dal leaders who founded the Biju Janata Dal. He represented Rourkela in the Assembly again from 2014 to 2019 and was elected to the Rajya Sabha in 2026 with the support of the Bharatiya Janata Party. Outside politics he is the founder and chairman of the Mayfair Group of Hotels, which operates mainly in eastern India.

Q13627042.lead: Pradeep Rawat (1952–2026) was an Indian actor from Jabalpur who worked mainly in Hindi, Telugu and Tamil films, chiefly in villain roles, and appeared in the 2012 Odia film ACP Ranveer.

p: Rawat was born in Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh. He took an early interest in sport and acting and performed regularly in cultural programmes at school and college, and worked in theatre and some Doordarshan serials before films.

His first screen appearance was as Ashwatthama in B. R. Chopra's television series Mahabharat, a role that made him widely recognised. Through the 1990s and 2000s he worked steadily in Hindi and South Indian cinema, often cast as gangsters, corrupt politicians, police officers and feudal lords. He entered Telugu cinema with Sye, played a double negative role in the Tamil Ghajini (2005) and reprised it in the Hindi remake. He also made debuts in Kannada with Parodi, Malayalam with China Town, Bengali with Hero 420 and Bhojpuri with Crack Fighter.

Other films in his career included Sarfarosh, Lagaan, Chatrapathi, Stalin and Pokiri. In Odia cinema he acted in ACP Ranveer, released in 2012. His last film, the Nepali Aa Bata Aama 2, was released after his death. He died in Mumbai in 2026.

For Sye he won the Filmfare Award for Best Villain (Telugu), the Nandi Award for Best Villain and the Santosham Best Villain Award in 2004. He was later nominated for the SIIMA Award for Best Actor in a Negative Role (Telugu) for Mangala and Naayak.
He was married to Kalyani Rawat.

facts: Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali, Odia

Q15724699.lead: Prem Anand (born Prem Anand Samal, 1975) is an Odia music director and composer who has scored more than 60 Odia films since his debut with Tu Eka Aama Saha Bharasa (2006).

p: Prem Anand was born in Saanagaan in Kendrapara district, the middle of three children of Nrusingha Charan Samal and Malati Devi. Despite his family's opposition to a music career, he learned harmonium in his village. After Gopinathpur Sanskrit Vidyalaya he joined Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya, where he trained in Odissi music under gurus including Bhikari Bal, Gopal Chandra Panda and Ramahari Das; he also accompanied Bhikari Bal on harmonium. He graduated in history from Marshaghai College in 1997 and later studied Hindustani classical music.

After a short spell as a music teacher in Rayagada, he composed for plays and travelling jatra troupes. In 1993 he wrote a song for Janani Gananatya's play Naalu Bhai Ra Mo Naali Gaamuchhaa, and later worked for troupes such as Parbati Gananatya, Kalinga Gananatya and Tarapur Opera. His first album, the devotional Maa Gojabayani, came out in 1996, and Anamika Nayika made his name; he has composed more than 200 Odia albums.

His first film as music director was Tu Eka Aama Saha Bharasa, starring Siddhanta Mahapatra, Jyoti Mishra and Mihir Das, released in 2006. Later Odia films include Rasika Nagara, Love Dot Com, Abhimanyu, Chandini I Miss You, Haata Dhari Chaaluthaa, Agastya, Kabula Barabula, Prem Kumar, Nimki and Biju Babu. Outside Odia cinema he scored the Hindi film Dekh Bhai Dekh (2009), a song for Luv U Turn (2019), and the Marathi film Short Cut, as well as Bengali work.

On television he composed for serials including Nua Bohu, Sankha Sindura and Abhinetri, and for the series Srimandira, whose a cappella title track was a first for the Odia music industry. He judged the reality shows Amari Swara and Sa Re Ga Ma Pa on Odia channels. He composed the patriotic song Ae Maati Odisha, Ae Jaati Odia for Utkal Dibasa in 2021 and the anthem Jai Ho Hindustan Ki for the 2023 Men's FIH Hockey World Cup.

He received the Odisha State Film Award for Chandini I Miss You in 2011, Odia Filmfare Awards for Gapa Hele bi Sata, Baby and Tu Mo Love Story 2, Tarang Cine Awards, and the Odisha Excellence Award in 2018.
He is married to Saswati Acharya; they have two sons.

Q15725027.lead: Minati Mishra (née Das; died 2020) was an Odissi dancer, teacher and Odia film actress from Cuttack who acted in five Odia films in the 1960s and received the Padma Shri in 2012.

p: Mishra was born in Cuttack, the youngest of three children of Basanta Kumar Das, a school headmaster. She studied Odissi with Kabichandra Kalicharan Pattnaik and Deba Prasad Das, and from 1950 with Kelucharan Mohapatra, and also learned from Pankaj Charan Das. In 1954 a Government of Odisha scholarship took her to Rukmini Devi Arundale's Kalakshetra to study Bharatanatyam, followed by further training under Pandanallur Chokkalingam Pillai and Meenakshisundaram Pillai. In 1962 she received a doctorate in Indology from Philipps University of Marburg, Germany, for a thesis on the Natyashastra.

She began performing in 1956 and toured Indian cities over the following years. In 1959 she was invited to Switzerland, where she danced in Zurich, Lucerne, Geneva and Winterthur, and in 1963 she performed at the Berlin Film Festival. She was noted for her skill in bhava and abhinaya.

Her film career began with Suryamukhi in 1963, followed by Jeevan Sathi, Sadhana and Arundhati; all four won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia, and she acted in five Odia films in all. She also danced an Odissi number choreographed by Kelucharan Mohapatra in the Bengali film Nirjana Saikate (1963). She was an A-grade artist with All India Radio and held the Sangeet Prabhakar title in Hindustani vocal music.

As principal of Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya in Bhubaneswar, she helped regularise its curriculum, formalise Odissi dance and music training and set examination standards, working alongside gurus such as Pankaj Charan Das and Deba Prasad Das. After her husband's death in 1980 she stopped performing, retired formally in 1990 and settled in Switzerland, where she gave lectures and workshops. She died in Switzerland in 2020.

She received the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1975), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (2000), the Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja Samman and the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Samman (both 2006), and the Padma Shri (2012).
She was married to Nityananda Mishra, an engineer; they had one son.

facts: Padma Shri (2012); Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (2000)

Q3346924.lead: Tarun Majumdar (1931–2022) was a Bengali film director who also made documentaries, wrote screenplays and books, and worked as an illustrator. The Government of India gave him the Padma Shri in 1990.

p: He was born in Bogra, in what was then the Bengal Presidency and is now Bangladesh. His father, Birendranath Majumdar, had been a freedom fighter. He did his intermediate studies at St. Paul's Cathedral Mission College and his degree at Scottish Church College, both part of the University of Calcutta.

Illustrating posters and technical film work came first. With Sachin Mukherji and Dilip Mukherji he then directed under the joint name Yatrik, starting with Chaowa Paowa (1959), which starred Uttam Kumar and Suchitra Sen, and continuing with Kancher Swarga (1962); after 1963 each was credited individually.

His solo films began in 1965 with Ektuku Basa and Alor Pipasa. Balika Badhu (1967), based on a Bimal Kar story, gave Moushumi Chatterjee her first role, and he later made a Hindi version. Nimantran (1971), Shriman Prithviraj (1973), Fuleswari (1974), which he later named as his favourite, Sansar Simante (1975) and Ganadevata, from Tarasankar Bandyopadhyay's novel, followed. Tapas Paul made his debut in Dadar Kirti (1980) and returned in Bhalobasa Bhalobasa (1985) and Apan Amar Apan (1990).

He favoured story-led adaptations of literature over experimental forms, and Rabindra Sangeet featured in his soundtracks. His later films were Alo (2003), Bhalobasar Onek Naam (2006), Chander Bari (2007) and, finally, Bhalobashar Bari (2018). His books include Cinemapara Diye. He died in Kolkata on 4 July 2022.

His tally of awards came to five National Film Awards, seven BFJA Awards, five Filmfare Awards and one Anandalok Award. Nimantran won him a National Award, a BFJA Award and a Filmfare Award, and Ganadevata was the first Bengali winner of the National Film Award for Best Popular Film Providing Wholesome Entertainment. Besides the Padma Shri, he received a lifetime achievement honour from the West Bengal Film Journalists' Association in 2017.
In 1967 he married the actress Sandhya Roy, who played the female lead in a number of his films.

facts: Scottish Church College, University of Calcutta
Padma Shri (1990); five National Film Awards

Q11141293.lead: Nirad Narayan Mohapatra (1947–2015) was an Odia film director, documentary maker and film teacher from Bhadrak, best known for his feature film Maya Miriga (1984).

p: Mohapatra was born in Bhadrak, the eldest of seven children of Shailen Mohapatra, a freedom fighter who later took up journalism and politics, and Surama Mohapatra, a schoolteacher. A cinema hall near his childhood home drew him to films. He completed a BA with distinction in 1967 and began postgraduate studies in political science at Utkal University, but left in 1968 to study film direction at the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII) in Pune, finishing the diploma in 1971.

From 1972 he taught direction at FTII. In 1974 he founded Cinexstasy, a film society in Bhubaneswar that screened and discussed world cinema, and ran it until 1983. In those years he edited the film section of the arts journal Mana Phasal, wrote for national journals, made documentaries and taught a film appreciation course at Utkal University.

His only feature, Maya Miriga (1984), was made on a small budget and filmed in Puri; it deals with a family's aspirations and its gradual break-up. The film was shown in the Critics' Week at Cannes and at the London, Locarno and Los Angeles film festivals. In 1985 he lectured on film at four universities in the United States.

He went on to concentrate on documentaries, among them Dhauligiri (1974), Chhau Dance of Mayurbhanj (1985), Patta Painting (1986), Maestros of Odissi (1995) and Chilika: A Fragile Ecosystem (2002), and also made television serials. He served on the national film jury and the Indian Panorama selection panel, on the governing council of FTII, and as chairman of the academic council of the Biju Patnaik Film and Television Institute in Cuttack, and taught as a guest lecturer at the KIIT film school. He died in Mumbai in 2015.

Maya Miriga came second for Best National Film in that year's Indian Panorama, was named Best Third World Film at the Mannheim-Heidelberg International Film Festival in Germany, and received a special jury award at the Hawaii International Film Festival. A restored version was re-released in 2024.
He married Sabita Mohanty in 1978; she had attended his film appreciation course and Cinexstasy screenings. They had two sons and a daughter.

facts: Utkal University; Film and Television Institute of India

Q19896075.lead: Elina Samantray (born 1996), also credited as Ray Elina Samantray, is an Odia film actress and model who won the first season of Tarang TV's talent show Kie Heba Mo Heroine and debuted in Ishq Tu Hi Tu (2015).

p: Samantray is the daughter of Jyotiranjan Samantray and Anuradha Samantray. She graduated in English (Honours) from Ravenshaw University and went on to postgraduate study in English at Utkal University; she had originally hoped to become a teacher.

Winning the first season of Kie Heba Mo Heroine on Tarang TV earned her the female lead opposite Arindam Roy in Ishq Tu Hi Tu, Tarang's first film production, directed by Tapas Sargharia and set against the 1991 communal riots in Dhamnagar, Bhadrak. Kehi Nuhen Kahara, directed by Susant Mani with Abhishek Rath, followed, and during Durga Puja 2015 she appeared with Anubhav Mohanty and Buddhaditya Mohanty in Jaga Hatare Pagha.

In 2016 she starred opposite Babushan in Love Station, directed by Ashok Pati, and Jhiata Bigidigala, directed by Bini Pattnaik. In 2017 she was paired again with Anubhav Mohanty in Abhaya and Kabula Barabula, the latter shot largely outside India, and played a village girl in Mu Khanti Odia Jhia. Her 2018 releases included Happy Lucky with Jyoti Ranjan Nayak, a comic role in Kie Heba Mo Stri, and two films opposite Sabyasachi Mishra: 4 Idiots, produced by Akshay Parija and directed by Basanta Sahu, and the comedy Tokata Fasigala, directed by Ramesh Rout. She has also worked in Bengali films.
She married Anurag Panda in 2024.

Q1749634.lead: Ayesha Jhulka (born 1972) is an Indian actress and entrepreneur who has worked mainly in Hindi cinema, with further roles in Telugu, Bengali, Kannada and Odia films.

p: Jhulka was born in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir. Her father, Inder Kumar Jhulka, was a wing commander in the Indian Air Force, and her mother, Sneh Jhulka, worked as a costume designer on films including Dalaal and Vishwavidhata. She first appeared on screen as a child artist in the 1983 Hindi film Kaise Kaise Log.

Her first lead role came in the 1990 Telugu film Neti Siddhartha, opposite Akkineni Nagarjuna. A year later she entered Hindi films opposite Salman Khan in Kurbaan, and also appeared that year in Meet Mere Man Ke, Hai Meri Jaan and the Bengali film Katha Dilam.

In 1992 she played a college prankster in Khiladi with Akshay Kumar and a college student in Jo Jeeta Wohi Sikandar with Aamir Khan; both performances brought her a nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Female Debut. She worked in ten films in 1993, among them Sangram, Waqt Hamara Hai, Dil Ki Baazi, Dalaal, Rang, Balmaa and Meherbaan. Later work included Jai Kishen (1994), Aashique Mastaane (1995), Masoom (1996), Chachi 420 (1997) and the Kannada film Kanasalu Neene Manasalu Neene (1998).

In 2006 she acted in the Odia film Rakate Lekhichi Naa, playing a police officer who was the sister-in-law of Siddhanta Mahapatra's character. She then moved to supporting parts, appearing in Socha Na Tha, Umrao Jaan and Ada... A Way of Life (2010), before stepping away from films to run her spa business, Ananta Salon. She returned with Anil Sharma's Genius in 2018 and later appeared in the web series Hush Hush (2022) and Happy Family: Conditions Apply (2023).
Jhulka married construction businessman Sameer Vashi in 2003.

Q29053580.lead: Susmita Das is an Odia singer from Cuttack who has performed for All India Radio, Cuttack and Doordarshan, and on stage in Odisha and abroad. She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Sugam Sangeet in 2021.

p: Born Susmita Parija in Cuttack, she was the eldest daughter of Shyamsundar Parija and Sanghamitra Parija. Her mother, a former music college student who had trained under Balakrishna Das, was her first teacher. After her marriage in 1985 she studied classical music with Sunakar Sahu, and she later took lessons from other teachers, including one in Dehradun.

Das passed the entrance test at All India Radio and began singing there in 1987, mainly performing old Odia songs, devotional music and Odissi sangeet. Once her daughters had grown up and the family moved to Bhubaneswar, she took up singing as a profession from 2003. Her stage repertoire covers old Odia and Hindi film songs, bhajans, ghazals, Odissi and classical music, and modern songs.
In 2007 she toured the United States and Canada and sang at OSA Conventions held in the United States, London and Canada. She served on the jury of the 63rd National Film Awards.

Her albums include Madhura E Chanda Rati, her first, with Omprakash Mohanty; Maya Darpan (2006), based on the poem by Mayadhar Mansingh; Hati Saja Kara, sixteen modern poems by Debdas Chhotray set to music by Omprakash Mohanty; Deha Bideha (2015), on the Vajrayana Buddhist tradition of Odisha; Hrudaya Ballabha (2015), a Jagannath bhajan album released during Nabakalebara; and Swabhiman (2016), recorded with visually impaired children and singer Abhijit Mishra.
Das received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Sugam Sangeet in 2021.

Q5225662.lead: Dukhiram Swain (1925–1995) was an Odia film and television actor, best known for playing villains in Odia cinema across a screen career that ran from 1960 to 1994.

p: Swain was born in Daraba in Jagatsinghpur district, Odisha. He began acting while still at school and later left home for Cuttack, where he joined Kalicharan Pattnaik's Odisha Theatres and, with Pattnaik's encouragement, continued his studies alongside acting. He was a linguist who spoke several languages fluently.

For a time Swain held a government job in the supply department, but he eventually gave it up to act full time, working with Sadananda Natya Niketan and Annapurna Theatre in Cuttack. He entered Odia films in 1960 with Sri Lokanath and went on to appear in 46 Odia films.

Although he was cast mostly in negative roles, and became strongly identified with them, he also played heroes, comic parts and character roles, and acted in television serials. Among his best-known films were Matira Manisha (1966), Jajabara (1975), Shesha Shrabana (1976), Phula Chandana (1986), Paradeshi Chadhei (1990) and Ranabhumi (1995). Off screen he was known as sociable and generous and was a member of several organisations. He died in Cuttack in 1995.

Swain won a National Film Award for Shesha Shrabana (1976). He received the Orissa Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for acting for 1984–85 and the Orissa State Film Award for Best Supporting Actor for Bhulihuena in 1987, along with several Best Villain awards. In 1994 he was given the Jayadev Award for his contribution to Odia cinema.

facts: Jayadev Award (1994); Orissa Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1984–85)

Q4777709.lead: Anubhav Mohanty is an Indian actor, producer and politician from Cuttack who works mainly in Odia cinema and has also appeared in Bengali films. He represented Kendrapara in the Lok Sabha from 2019 to 2024.

p: Mohanty was born in Nandi Sahi, Cuttack, to Abhay Kumar Mohanty, a lecturer and recognised All India Radio artist, and Madhusmita Mohanty. His brother Anuprash Mohanty works in film production. He studied at DAV Public School, Cuttack, and was a student at Christ College, Cuttack, when he was offered his first film role. Before that he had already built a following through Odia music videos and albums.

His film debut was I Love You (2004), opposite Namrata Thapa, followed the same year by Saathire and Barsa My Darling. Films described as commercial successes include Neijaare Megha Mate (2008), Suna Chadhei Mo Rupa Chadhei (2009), Akashe Ki Ranga Lagila (2009), Abhimanyu (2009), Diwana (2010), Balunga Toka (2011), Something Something (2012), Matric Fail (2012), ACP Ranveer (2012), Mo Duniya Tu Hi Tu (2013), Something Something 2 (2014), Agastya (2016), Abhaya (2017), Kabula Barabula (2017), Prem Kumar (2018), Love In London (2023), Kuhudi (2024) and Karma (2024).

After Balunga Toka he set up his own production company, Vishnupriyaa Arts & Graphics, in 2012; Something Something became the biggest Odia hit of that year. He entered Bengali cinema with a special appearance in Saathi Amaar opposite Rachna Banerjee. In 2019 he starred in Biju Babu, produced by Nila Madhab Panda, his most expensive Odia film, which fell short of box-office expectations amid a political controversy.

Mohanty joined the Biju Janata Dal on 27 April 2013 and was elected unopposed to the Rajya Sabha in June 2014. In the 2019 general election he won the Kendrapara Lok Sabha seat, defeating Baijayant Panda. He left the BJD on 30 March 2024 and joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in New Delhi on 1 April 2024.
He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor in 2009 and received the Rajiv Gandhi Pratibha Samman for 2004–05.

facts: Bharatiya Janata Party (earlier Biju Janata Dal)

Q19663402.lead: Asim Basu (1935–2017) was an Odia painter, theatre actor and director, playwright and art director, known for stage and set design, Odia book covers and film posters, and art direction for Odia films.

p: Basu was born in Kakhada village, Bhogarai, in Balasore district, to Motilal Basu, a veterinary doctor, and Bijanbala Basu; several of his uncles were artists. After matriculation he studied at Fakir Mohan College, but left for Kolkata against his family's wishes to learn painting, supporting himself with odd jobs. With the help of a scholarship he completed his studies at the Calcutta art school in 1959. During this period he worked with actor Utpal Dutt's theatre as an assistant art director, gaining experience in acting, direction and stage design.

Back in Odisha, Basu took a government job but soon left it and became known as a cover artist before moving into stage design, art direction and acting. His first stage role in Odia was in Rupantara, and he first designed sets for Bibhuti Pattnaik's play Tapaswini. With Biswajit Das he founded the Bhubaneswar theatre group Rupakar, and after it broke up he joined the group Uttar Purusha. He directed Bijay Mishra's Duiti Surya Dagdha Phula Ku Nei, designed sets for hundreds of plays, and served as president of the Odisha Natya Sangha. He also designed Odisha's tableau for the Republic Day parade in Delhi on several occasions and sat on the selection committee for the state film and television awards.

In films he was art director for Chha Mana Atha Guntha, Indradhanura Chhai and the Hindi film Shodh. While working as art director on Prashanta Nanda's Jaga Balia, he was given an acting part, which began his screen acting career; his film work also included Nirab Jhada, Sautuni, Dadagiri, Tara, Mukti Tirtha and Agni Bina, along with many telefilms. He wrote stories, plays and newspaper columns, an autobiography titled Kathare Kathare, the story collection Cactusra Phula and the essay collection Chhota Bada Katha Kahu. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2017.

Basu received the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1998), the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award, the Dharmapada Award of the Odisha Lalit Kala Akademi (2010), the Bhasha Bharati Samman (2003–04), the Parampara Samman (2012) and the Shilpi Divas Samman of the Odisha Modern Art Gallery (2015). A Koraput theatre group, Nandanik, later instituted the Asim Basu Memorial Award for young theatre artists.
He was married to Gita Basu. Their children include actress Bhaswati Basu.

facts: Painter, art director, theatre director, actor, writer
Fakir Mohan College; art school, Kolkata

Q1372499.lead: Jharana Das (1945–2022) was an Odia film actress, broadcaster and Doordarshan official who played the female lead in around 40 films, among them Amada Bata, Malajahna, Abhinetri, Adina Megha and Sri Jagannath.

p: Das was born into a Christian joint family at Chandini Chowk, Cuttack, the second of five children of schoolteacher Edwin Sukumar Das and Charuprava Das, a block development officer; she was known at home as Jhumu. As children she and her cousins staged plays written by her mother. While still at school she took part in the children's programme Shishu Sansar on All India Radio, Cuttack.

She passed her matriculation from Mission Girls' School (now Buckley Girls' School) and graduated from Sailabala Women's College, where she began acting in radio plays. She learned Odissi dance from Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and also trained in voice culture in Kolkata. Her conservative family at first objected to a film career, and her brother, an Indian Air Force officer, persuaded them to allow it.

Das worked as an announcer and programme maker at All India Radio, Cuttack, and later served as assistant station director at Doordarshan, Cuttack, and as station director at Doordarshan, Kolkata. Her first stage lead was in a play by Narasingha Mohapatra.

She entered Odia films with Amada Bata (1964). Malajahna, in which she played the heroine, was shot in 1962 but released only in 1965. Her other films included Naba Janma and Abhinetri (1965), Adina Megha (1970), Sri Jagannath (1979), Tike Hasa Tike Luha (1981), Hisab Nikas (1982), Mahasati Savitri (1983), Hira Nila (1984), Pooja Phula (1985), Kasturi (1987) and Lal Paan Bibi (1988). She also directed a biographical documentary on freedom fighter and former chief minister Harekrushna Mahatab, and acted in television programmes such as Ghara Bhada Dia Jiba and Manisha. She died at her home in Cuttack in 2022 and was given a state funeral.

Her honours included the Jayadev Puraskar, the Odisha Living Legend Award (2011), an honour from the Odisha Society of the Americas (2011) and the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Award for lifetime achievement (2016).
She was married to cinematographer Deepak Das, who shot her film Malajahna.

Q6575090.lead: Sarat Pujari (1934–2014) was an Odia film actor, director and producer, and an educationist, who worked in Odia cinema from 1959 until 2012 and directed films including Tapoi, Ashanta Graha and Astaraga.

p: Pujari was born in Nayagarh, where his father, Sachidananda Pujari, whose family came from Jhaduapada in Sambalpur, served as dewan of Nayagarh state. He attended schools in several parts of Odisha and studied at Allahabad University, earning a postgraduate degree in economics and, in 1956, a diploma in painting. He developed an interest in drama and the performing arts as a student.

Pujari first worked as a block designer and publicity agent. From 1959 to 1966 he taught economics at Panchayat College, Bargarh, and then briefly managed works at Tapang Light Foundry, Nayagarh. Between 1966 and 1968 he worked as a freelance film actor to learn filmmaking, and at 34 he became principal of Larambha College, a post he held until 1992. He later headed Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya, Bhubaneswar (1992–1994), and served as president of the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi from 2011. He was also a member of the board of the Odisha Film Development Corporation.

His film career began with Shree Shree Mahalaxmi Puja (1959), followed by Jeevan Sathi, Sadhana, Matira Manisha and Arundhati, and he received a best actor award from the President of India. Kie Kahara ran for 100 consecutive days in Cuttack cinemas. He directed Tapoi (1978), Ashanta Graha (1982) and Astaraga (1982) and more than 75 plays. Later films included Kaa, Andha Diganta, Bhukha (1989), in which he played a negative role, Aranya Rodan, Aranyaka, Shesha Drushti and Sata Michha. His last film was Gadadhar Puty's Puja Pain Phulatie (2007), which won national and international awards. He also acted in television serials. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2014.

The Government of Odisha gave him the Jayadev Award in 1985 for his contribution to Odia cinema. His other honours included the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Award (2007), the Kadambini Samman (2010), the first Hemanta Das Kala Samman (2011) and the Orissa Cine Artist Association Award (2012).
He was survived by his wife, Santwana, and four children; his son Soumen Pujari is also an actor.

facts: Principal, Larambha College; President, Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi

Q6575740.lead: Mahasweta Ray (born 1962) is an Odia film actress, dancer, television performer and politician from Puri who has acted in more than 50 Odia, Bengali and Telugu films since the mid-1970s.

p: Ray was born in Puri, the youngest daughter of writer and actor Rajkishore Ray and Manorama Ray, and was called Rashmi as a child. Influenced by her father, she was drawn early to dance and acting, with a particular interest in Kuchipudi and Bharatanatyam. She studied at Sri Aurobindo School, Puri, and Samanta Chandra Sekhar College.

Ray entered films in her teens. A former student of her father, Kedar, was making Sindura Bindu and asked for her to appear as a dancer; while she worked on it, Rajan Kinagi and Prashanta Nanda offered her a role in Shesha Shrabana (1976). Early films included Hira Moti Manika, Janmadata, Priyatama, Sankha Mahuri, Sati Anusuya and Gauri. In 1978 she acted opposite Chiranjeevi in the Telugu film Pranam Khareedu, becoming the first Odia actress to work in Telugu cinema.

She appeared in most of Sisir Mishra's films, and her screen pairings with Prashanta Nanda, Uttam Mohanty and Sriram Panda were popular. Her Odia work of the 1980s and 1990s included Pooja, Hisab Nikas, Kaberi, Jaga Balia, Hira Nila, Gruhalakshmi, Golamgiri, Panchu Pandav, Kandhei and Suna Bhauja. From 1991 she also worked in Bengali films such as Sajani Go Sajani, Nyayachakra, Katha Chhilo, Sujan Sakhi and Aranyer Adhikar, and she acted opposite Farooq Shaikh in the Hindi serial Chamatkar on Sony TV. In later years she has taken character roles in films such as Mu Eka Tumara, Superstar, Target and Jaga Hatare Pagha, along with television serials.
Ray joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in February 2018.
Ray has won eight Odisha State Film Awards, including acting awards for Gauri (1979), Pooja (1981) and Kaberi (1983). She also received the Jayadev Puraskar (2009) and the Fitfat Bioscope Award.

Her elder sisters Malavika Ray and Manaswini Ray are also Odia film actresses, and actress Aparajita Mohanty is her cousin. She married Mumbai businessman Sirish Routray in 1982; they have a son, Rishiraj.

facts: Malavika Ray, Manaswini Ray (sisters); Aparajita Mohanty (cousin)

Q7898244.lead: Upendra Kumar (1941–2002) was an Indian film composer with roots in Digapahandi, Odisha, who scored about 210 films, chiefly in Kannada, along with more than 25 Odia films and work in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam and Tulu.

p: Kumar's family came from Digapahandi in present-day Ganjam district, Odisha; one source gives Madras as his birthplace and another Digapahandi. His father, Lakshman Swamy, was an astrologer. After schooling up to the seventh grade he turned to music with help from his uncle Apparao, training in Hindustani classical music, Western instruments and Indian string instruments. He took a bachelor's degree in Indian classical music, Odissi music and sitar from the Utkal College of Music and Dance, then moved to Madras to look for work.

In Madras he taught vocal music and sitar, and director Y. R. Swamy hired him to score Katari Veera (1966), starring Rajkumar. He went on to a long partnership with Rajkumar and his family, with Rajkumar singing many of his songs, usually to lyrics by Chi. Udayashankar. His popular Kannada soundtracks included Premada Kanike, Shankar Guru, Ravichandra, Kaamana Billu, Nanjundi Kalyana, Hrudaya Haadithu and Jeevana Chaitra; the song "Naadamaya" from Jeevana Chaitra earned Rajkumar the National Film Award for Best Male Playback Singer. His orchestrations made prominent use of mandolin and sitar, and he favoured melodies in raga Kafi.

In Odia cinema he composed for films including Dharitri, Mana Akasha, Punarmilan, Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja, Pipasa, Kulachandrama, Samarpan, Pati Patni, Paribar, Ae Nuhen Kahani, Alibha Daag and Manika. Odia songs he composed include "Jaha Mun Khojichhi Taha Mun Paichhi", "Indradhanura Sapta Ranga" and "Sapanara Pathe Pathe". A book, Sajala Smruti, was published in 2009 in memory of his Odia film work. He stopped composing for films in the 1990s; his last film was the Kannada Vishwamithra (2001). He died in Bangalore in 2002.
Kumar won the Karnataka State Film Award for Best Music Director for Nanjundi Kalyana (1990), Hrudaya Haadithu (1992) and Jeevana Chaitra (1993). He also held the title Sangeet Saraswati.
He was married to singer H. P. Geetha, the sister of Kannada actress H. P. Saroja.

facts: Utkal College of Music and Dance

Q55409221.lead: Bhaswati Basu (born 1973) is an Odia film, television and stage actress, playwright, theatre director and poet. She won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for Kathantara.

p: Basu was born in Bapuji Nagar, Bhubaneswar, to Gita Basu and the painter, actor, director and art director Asim Basu; her siblings are Atasi and Gautam. She studied drama at Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya and later taught there as guest faculty.

Her first film was Raju Mishra's Jibana Mrutyu (2005). Her second, Himanshu Khatua's Kathantara (2006), won eight Odisha State Film Awards, one of them for her supporting performance. She later appeared in Amartya Bhattacharyya's Khyanikaa: The Lost Idea (2017), which was selected for the Indian Panorama at the International Film Festival of India; the short film Rasagola, directed by Swaraj Mishra and based on the story collection Babuna; and Kokoli: Fish Out of Water (2021), a film about the effect of rising sea levels on Odia fishing communities, in which she played the title character's mother. She also had a prominent part in Phalguna Chaitra (2023), the first Odia film released simultaneously in nine countries, and acted in Indradhanu (2025) and several Odia television serials.

On stage, Basu began with the group Satabdira Kalakar. She has acted in more than 25 plays, scripted 19 and directed 13, including Aparna (2009), her adaptation of a Bengali play by Balai Chand Mukhopadhyay, and Kandhei Ghara, her own translation of Henrik Ibsen's A Doll's House. She also adapted Habib Tanvir's Charandas Chor for Satabdira Kalakar.

After her father's death in 2017 she returned to poetry, publishing the collections Bata Abata (2021) and Raga Malkosh (2023). In 2018 she helped organise the Asim Utsav in his memory, and she conceptualised the Odisha Pavilion at the India International Trade Fair in New Delhi.
She received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for Kathantara.
Her father was stage and film art director Asim Basu. She is married to Vijay Mandal, and they have a daughter, Dishani.

Q5223491.lead: Rachna Banerjee, born Jhumjhum Banerjee and also credited as Rachana, is an Indian actress, television presenter and politician from Kolkata, known mainly for Bengali and Odia films. She has been Member of Parliament for Hooghly since 2024.

p: Banerjee was born in Calcutta (now Kolkata), the only child of Rabindranath Banerjee. She finished higher secondary schooling at National Girls' High School and was in her second year at South City College when she won the Miss Kolkata title in 1991. She took part in several other pageants, often winning Miss Beautiful Smile, including at the Miss India contest.

Director Sukhen Das cast her as the female lead in the Bengali film Daan Pratidaan (1993) and gave her the screen name Rachana, taken from the title Rabindra Rachanabali. Her Odia career began with Sagara Ganga (1994), and she went on to act in around 45 Odia films, including Subhadra, Jashoda, Laxmana Rekha, Santana, Suna Harini, Kandhei Akhire Luha, Sarapancha Babu and Nari Nuhen Tu Narayani. She also worked in Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and Hindi films, appearing opposite Amitabh Bachchan in Sooryavansham.
On television she hosted the Zee Bangla programme Didi No. 1 until June 2026, when Swastika Mukherjee took over as host.

Banerjee joined the Trinamool Congress in 2024 and won the Hooghly Lok Sabha seat in that year's general election, defeating the sitting BJP member Locket Chatterjee by 76,853 votes. In June 2026 she was among 20 MPs who left the Trinamool Congress to join the Nationalist Citizens Party of India.
