Her awards include the Kalakar Award for Best Actress for Sabuj Saathi (2004), an Odisha State Film Award, a special film award from the West Bengal government, the Bharat Nirman Award and the Mahanayak Samman, along with several awards as a television host, including Best Anchor for Didi No. 1 at the West Bengal Tele Academy Awards 2025.
She was married to her Odia co-star Sidhant Mohapatra until their divorce in 2004. She married Probal Basu in 2007; they separated in 2016 and have a son.

Q56043744.lead: Shiladitya Bora is an Indian film producer, director, marketer and distributor from Assam, and the founder of the Mumbai production company Platoon One Films.

p: Bora grew up and went to school in Assam. He took a bachelor's degree in engineering from Lalbhai Dalpatbhai College of Engineering, Ahmedabad, in 2005, and then joined the Mudra Institute of Communications, Ahmedabad (MICA), for a postgraduate programme in communication management and entrepreneurship. As a student he launched the FulMarxx Shorts Fest in 2008, which became the Ahmedabad International Film Festival the following year, and he received MICA's award for creative and entrepreneurial excellence for it.

Bora's first film venture was a film club, Sunset Boulevard, which held screenings at PVR Cinemas. Building on that model, PVR made him head of its independent release banner, PVR Directors' Rare, in 2010; around 85 fiction, documentary and experimental films were released under it. In 2015 he was chosen for the Berlinale Talents programme.

Also in 2015 he became the first chief executive of Drishyam Films, serving as associate producer on Masaan, Waiting, Rukh and Newton, and as executive producer on Nagesh Kukunoor's Dhanak. He helped develop Newton from a one-line idea, and the film was later chosen as India's entry for the 90th Academy Awards.

In 2017 he founded Platoon One Films with his wife, costume designer Shilpi Agarwal. The company has marketed and distributed more than 60 films, among them Rohena Gera's Is Love Enough? Sir (2020). Its productions include the Hindi film Yours Truly, which premiered at the Busan International Film Festival in 2018; the Marathi film Picasso, which received a special mention at the National Film Awards in 2021; the Marathi thriller Ghaath (2023), selected for the 73rd Berlin International Film Festival; and Bayaan, starring Huma Qureshi, which premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival in 2025. Bora directed the short film Aapke Aa Jane Se (2019) and his first Hindi feature, Bhagwan Bharose, which closed the 25th UK Asian Film Festival and won its Flame Award for Best Film.
He is married to costume designer Shilpi Agarwal, his partner in Platoon One Films.

Q6575816.lead: Sadhu Meher (1940–2024) was an Indian actor, director and producer from Boudh, Odisha, who worked in Hindi parallel cinema and Odia films. He won a National Film Award for his role in Ankur and received the Padma Shri in 2017.

p: Meher was born in Gudabhelipadar village in the Kantamal block of Boudh district, to weaver Radhamohan Meher and Dipti Meher. After early schooling in his village, at his maternal uncle's home in Tarbha and at Maharaja High School, Sonepur, he passed his matriculation from P. R. High School, Balangir, and studied for a BA at Gangadhar Meher College, Sambalpur. Drawn to acting from childhood, he went to Rabindra Bharati in Kolkata to study theatre and cinema, the first Odia student to do so there, and then earned a diploma in acting from the Film and Television Institute of India, Pune.

Meher moved to Bombay in 1966 and struggled for several years to find good roles. He turned to theatre, acting in many plays directed by Satyadev Dubey and working in the Hindi Theatre Unit alongside actors such as Amrish Puri, Naseeruddin Shah, Shabana Azmi, Smita Patil and Amol Palekar. His screen career began in 1969 with Bhuvan Shome, in which he played a mute bird-catcher. Shyam Benegal saw him on stage and cast him in Ankur (1974). His other Hindi films included Ichhapuran, 27 Down, Nishant, Manthan, Mrigaya, Debshishu, Safed Haathi, Charachar and Uttaran, and he appeared in two stories of the television series Byomkesh Bakshi.

He later moved towards Odia cinema, making his debut as a director with Abhimanyu (1977), which gave first breaks to actors Uttam Mohanty, Ajit Das and Aparajita and to music director Radhakrishna Bhanja. He directed five films in all, including Aparichita, Abhilasha and Gopare Badhuchi Kalakanhei, and acted in more than 38 Odia, Bengali and Hindi films; his Odia and Sambalpuri work included Sita Rati, Bhukha and Jai Jagannatha (2007), his last Odia film. He served several times on juries for the Indian Panorama and the National Film Awards. He died at his home in Mumbai in 2024.

Meher won the National Film Award for Best Actor (Silver Lotus) for Ankur in 1974. He received Odisha's Jayadev Award for 2008 for his contribution to Odia cinema, and the Government of India awarded him the Padma Shri in 2017.

facts: FTII, Pune (acting); Gangadhar Meher College, Sambalpur
National Film Award for Best Actor (1974); Padma Shri (2017); Jayadev Award (2008)

Q4779123.lead: Aparajita Mohanty, born Aparajita Khan and known mononymously as Aparajita, is an Odia film and television actress and politician who has appeared in more than 70 films since her debut in Sita Labakusha (1980).

p: She was born to Abdul Aziz Khan, a magistrate, and Harapriya Ray, a zoology professor, and grew up in Sambalpur with two elder sisters. Her paternal grandfather, Maulavi Abdus Sobhan Khan of Bhadrak, served as law minister of Orissa Province from 1941 to 1944 in Krushna Chandra Gajapati's ministry. Her mother was the younger sister of writer Rajkishore Ray, which makes actress Mahasweta Ray her cousin. She studied at Sambalpur University.

Aparajita made her screen debut in 1980 opposite Uttam Mohanty in Sita Labakusha. Over more than three decades she acted in over 70 Odia and Hindi films, among them Phula Chandana (1982), Jheeati Sita Pari, Janani, Jaaiphula, Mamata Mage Mula, Badhu Nirupama, Jahaku Rakhibe Ananta, Mamatara Dori, Kapala Likhana, Asha, Lakhe Siba Puji Paichhi Pua and Sunya Swarupa. In later years she has played supporting roles in films such as Abhimanyu (2009), Loafer, Daddy and Golapi Golapi, and she has also worked in Odia television serials.

Mohanty joined the Indian National Congress in February 2014 and contested the Cuttack Lok Sabha seat, losing to Bhartruhari Mahtab. She moved to the Bharatiya Janata Party in February 2018 and stood for Bhubaneswar North in the 2019 Odisha Assembly election, losing to Susant Kumar Rout.
She won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress for Phula Chandana (1982), Tunda Baaida (1987), Jahaku Rakhibe Ananta (1988), Sasti (1989) and Asha (1993), and received ETV's Priya Odia honour.
She married Odia actor Uttam Mohanty in 1987; their son, Babushaan Mohanty, is an actor and singer in Odia cinema.

Q7521197.lead: Simran Kaur Mundi is an Indian actress, model, television presenter and beauty pageant titleholder from Mumbai who won Femina Miss India Universe 2008 and has acted mainly in Hindi films, as well as in Punjabi and Telugu cinema.

p: Mundi was born in Mumbai to a family from Mundian Jattan in Hoshiarpur, Punjab. She studied at Delhi Public School, Vijaipur, and Scindia Kanya Vidyalaya, Gwalior, and earned a biotechnology degree from Holkar Science College, Indore, in 2007. She then worked as a guest relations executive at Fame Cinemas in Andheri, Mumbai.

Encouraged by make-up artists she met at the cinema, Mundi entered Femina Miss India 2008 with no modelling background and won the Miss India Universe title. At Miss Universe 2008 in Nha Trang, Vietnam, she did not reach the final placements but featured in several preliminary rounds. She went on to model at Lakme India Fashion Week, Wills India Fashion Week and India Couture Week, appeared in commercials and in Sukshinder Shinda's music video "La La La La", and later judged regional Miss India contests.
On television she competed in Zor Ka Jhatka: Total Wipeout in 2011, hosted the first Hockey India League in 2013, and in 2019 co-hosted NBA coverage on Sony and anchored the first NBA India Games.

Her Hindi film debut came in December 2011 opposite Sunny Gill. In 2013 she starred in the Punjabi film Best of Luck with Gippy Grewal and Jazzy Bains, and in the Telugu film Potugadu with Manoj Manchu. Later films included Kuku Mathur Ki Jhand Ho Gayi and the Punjabi Mundeyan Ton Bachke Rahin (both 2014), and Kis Kisko Pyaar Karoon, opposite Kapil Sharma.
In 2020 she married Gurickk Maan, son of Punjabi singer and actor Gurdas Maan; the couple have a son.

knownFor: Kuku Mathur Ki Jhand Ho Gayi

Q7260123.lead: Puneet Issar is an Indian actor, director, writer, producer and dialect coach, working mostly in Hindi cinema and television. His Duryodhana in B. R. Chopra's Mahabharat (1988–1990) made him widely known.

p: His screen career opened with a villain's role in Manmohan Desai's Coolie (1983). The same year he was second lead in the horror film Purana Mandir, and more horror titles such as Tehkhana followed in the 1980s.

Over 150 films have cast him as a villain, among them Zakhmi Aurat, Kal Ki Aawaz, Palay Khan, Teja, Prem Shakti and Ram Jaane. His other credits include Chandra Mukhi, Border, Refugee, Krrish, Partner, Bachna Ae Haseeno, Ready, Son of Sardaar and The Kashmir Files (2022), in which he was DGP Hari Narain, as well as Punjabi and Telugu films.

Garv: Pride and Honour (2004), a police film with Salman Khan and Shilpa Shetty, was his first film as director; I Am Singh (2011), which he also wrote the story for, dealt with Sikh immigrants in the US after the September 11 attacks. On television he has acted in more than 12 serials, including Param Vir Chakra, Bharat Ek Khoj, Junoon, Noorjahan, the 2013 Mahabharat, where he played Parashurama, and Choti Sarrdaarni, and he directed the serials Hindustani and Jai Mata Ki. He reached the final seven of Bigg Boss 8. In 2018 he wrote and directed the stage show Mahabharat: The Epic Tale and played Duryodhana in it. He has also taught speech, diction and gesture as a dialect coach.

His father is the film director Sudesh Issar. His wife, Deepali, is the daughter of actor Daljeet Puri and sister of actor Satyajeet Puri; she wrote Garv and I Am Singh. Their son Siddhant Issar is an actor.

facts: Actor, writer, director, producer, dialect coach

Q16734929.lead: Akkineni Ramesh Prasad (born 1936) is an Indian film producer and businessman who heads Prasad Studios and Prasads Multiplex. He is the son of the filmmaker L. V. Prasad.

p: Born in Andhra Pradesh, he had a short spell as a child actor, appearing as the son of N. T. Rama Rao's character in Samsaram (1950); cricket appealed to him more, and after his father scolded him on set he gave up acting. He went to the United States to study engineering and began his working life in fabrication.

He set up Prasad Film Laboratories in Madras in 1974, at a time when the city had no high-quality processing lab. It opened branches in Hyderabad, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Thiruvananthapuram, Bhubaneswar and elsewhere, as well as offices in Singapore, Dubai and the United States, and won the National Award for laboratory processing eight times. In 2002 the company set up Asia's first integrated digital film lab, in Mumbai. Under him the Prasad Group introduced digital intermediate and HD post-production in India, took on special effects and the restoration of old Hollywood films, and eventually returned to producing films.

A visit to the Smithsonian in Washington, D.C., in the early 1990s, where he saw the IMAX film To Fly, led him to open Prasads, an IMAX theatre in Hyderabad, in 2003; about 300,000 people watched Avatar (2009) there. He is a founder trustee of the L. V. Prasad Eye Institute, which was set up with a donation from his father.

His industry posts have included the presidency of the South India Film Chamber of Commerce (1986–87 and 1991–92), the Film Federation of India (1988–89) and the Andhra Pradesh Film Chamber of Commerce (2000–01). He has also served on the governing council of the Film and Television Institute of India and the advisory committee of the Children's Film Society of India.
L. V. Prasad was his father, and the film editor A. Sreekar Prasad is his cousin.

Q60736468.lead: Atal Bihari Panda (died 2021) was a Sambalpuri playwright, lyricist and actor from Binika who acted on stage from 1944 and made his film debut in his eighties in Salabudha, winning two consecutive Odisha State Film Awards for Best Actor.

p: Panda was born in Binika, in present-day Subarnapur district, the eldest son of Kabiraj Basudev Panda and Lakshmi Priya Panda. Drawn to drama from childhood, he began acting in plays in 1944. After retiring from government service he settled in Burla.

Panda acted in more than 100 plays and wrote over 65 stage and radio plays, mostly in Sambalpuri; his Phata Kapala was the first Sambalpuri play to appear in print. Other Sambalpuri plays of his include Bhainsa Age Nagadhuni, Phata Mandal, Kuan Bhitare Dendu and Lenjatara, and he wrote two Odia plays, Mani Sangraha and Klanta Aparahna, as well as the popular opera Bagha Matichhi. From 1985 he was an approved lyricist for All India Radio, Sambalpur and Cuttack, and many of his Sambalpuri songs were sung by Fakir Pattnaik.

Director Sabyasachi Mohapatra first approached him to write dialogue for Salabudha. Unable to find a suitable lead, Mohapatra then cast Panda himself, and the film became his screen debut in 2013. He played the lead again in the sequel Adima Bichara (2014) and in the third film of the series, Sala Budhar Badla, released on 17 January 2020. He died in 2021 at Veer Surendra Sai Institute of Medical Sciences and Research, Burla.

Panda won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor for Salabudha (2013) and for Adima Bichara (2014), along with the award for Best Dialogue for Adima Bichara. He was felicitated by the Odisha Sahitya Akademi in 2013, and Sambalpur University awarded him an honorary D.Litt. in 2019.

Q15724091.lead: Chittaranjan Tripathy (born 1971) is an Indian actor, director, writer and music director whose work spans Hindi and Odia cinema, theatre and television.

p: Tripathy was born in Chandabali in Odisha. After graduating from Ravenshaw College in Cuttack, he took a master's degree in sociology at the University of Hyderabad in 1992. He then trained in acting at the National School of Drama (NSD) in Delhi, earning a diploma in 1996; Nawazuddin Siddiqui was in the same batch. With a Charles Wallace India Trust Scholarship he later studied musical theatre direction at the Guildford School of Acting in London. He is also trained in Hindustani classical music.

Tripathy entered Odia cinema in 2007 with Dhauli Express, taking on the roles of producer, director, scriptwriter, music director, lyricist and playback singer. The film won three Odisha State Film Awards. He followed it with Mukhyamantri in 2009, and in 2020 appeared in the Odia film Adrushyam alongside Samaresh Routray.

Away from Odia films, he has staged more than 50 plays, among them Taj Mahal Ka Tender for the NSD Repertory, for which he also wrote the lyrics and music, and he has composed over 500 songs for the stage. He directed episodes of television series including Mano Ya Na Mano and Savdhan India, and acted in Hindi films such as Delhi 6, Talvar and Tera Mera Tedha Medha. On streaming platforms he played Trivedi in Sacred Games and a negative role in M.O.M – Mission Over Mars (2019).
In October 2023 he was appointed Director of the National School of Drama, his alma mater.

For Dhauli Express (2007) he received the Mohan Sundar Dev Goswami Award and Odisha State Film Awards for Best Music Director and Best Singer. He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Comedian in 2016 for Love You Jessica.

facts: Ravenshaw College; University of Hyderabad; National School of Drama; Guildford School of Acting
Actor, director, writer, music director, lyricist
Director, National School of Drama (from 6 October 2023)

Q47065861.lead: Jyoti Ranjan Nayak, known as Jyoti, is an Indian actor who works mainly in Odia films, active since 2016.

p: Nayak was born in Cuttack to Ramesh Kumar Nayak, an officer in the Indian Air Force, and Jayashree Nayak, a homemaker. He studied engineering in Chennai, completing a B.Tech. While a student there he was selected for a Tamil film but withdrew because he did not know the language.

After returning to Odisha he took part in Mitha Mitha Jodi, a reality show on Colors Odia held to pick the lead pair for Shrikant Gautam's film Mitha Mitha. He won the contest and the role, but the film's release was delayed, so his first film to reach cinemas was Shailendra Mishra's Dele Dhara Katha Sare (2016), opposite Malabika Banerjee.

In 2017 he appeared in Sanjay Nayak's Nijhum Ratira Sathi, released around New Year, and Dilip Panda's Dil Ka Raja in February; Mitha Mitha finally came out in May. His fifth film, Tu Mo Hero, directed by Dilip Panda with Jhilik Bhattacharjee, was a Diwali release that year. In 2018 he starred in Sudhanshu Mohan Sahoo's Happy Lucky and Kailash Mohapatra's Ole Ole Dil Bole, and on 23 November two of his films, Sathi Tu Pheria and Pyar Alaga Prakara, opened on the same day.
He was named Best Entertainer of the Year at the Tarang Cine Utsav 2022 for Super Boy.
His brother is Ankit Kumar Nayak. He married Simran Maharana in 2025.

Q7683304.lead: Tanikella Bharani (born 1954) is an Indian actor, screenwriter, poet and playwright who works mainly in Telugu cinema, with more than 750 acting credits and screenplays for 52 films.

p: Bharani was born in Jagannathapuram in present-day Andhra Pradesh. His family included figures from Telugu literature: Diwakarla Venkatavadhani and Viswanatha Satyanarayana were his grand-uncles, and Divakarla Tirupati Sastry of the poet pair Tirupati Venkata Kavulu was his great-grand-uncle.

He acted in stage plays in the mid-1970s, when he met the Telugu actor Rallapalli, who encouraged him to write short dialogues and scenes. After a diploma in theatre arts he moved to Chennai on Rallapalli's advice. His first assignment as dialogue writer was Kanchu Kavacham (1984), followed by films such as Ladies Tailor (1985), Siva (1989) and Seenu Vasanthi Lakshmi (2004).

His acting work began with Ladies Tailor and Sri Kanaka Mahalakshmi Recording Dance Troupe (1987). The role of Nanaji in Ram Gopal Varma's Siva (1989) brought him wide attention, and his villain in Samudram won a Nandi Award. From the 2000s he took on older character parts in films including Manmadhudu, Samba, Godavari and Happy. He has also appeared in some Tamil, Kannada and Hindi films.

In 2012 he directed the drama Mithunam, starring S. P. Balasubrahmanyam and Lakshmi. He has written and sung devotional songs on Shiva, and his published works include books, plays and playlets in Telugu.

He has received three Nandi Awards: Best Villain for Samudram, Best Character Actor for Nuvvu Nenu and Best Dialogue Writer for Mithunam. Mithunam also earned him the CineMAA Special Jury Award for Best Director. His short film Sira – The Ink won awards at the Hyderabad International Film Festival and the Idaho Panhandle International Film Festival, and he has received several literary awards.
He married Durga Bhavani in 1988; they have two children. Their son Teja made his acting debut in Mr Lavangam (2012).

Q15725056.lead: Mohan Sundar Deb Goswami (1892–1948) was an Odissi musician, poet, composer and Rahasa guru who produced, directed and acted in Sita Bibaha (1936), the first Odia film.

p: Born Shyama Sundar Deb Goswami in Puri, he was the youngest son of Harishchandra Deb Goswami and Sulakshana Devi. The family lived on Marichikot Lane in Puri.

Before turning to film he promoted Odia language, literature and culture through Rahasa (Rasa), a theatrical form that enacts the love of Radha and Krishna. Following the earlier example of Gobinda Chandra Surdeo of the Tarala royal family, he formed a touring Rasa troupe that became known across Odisha. Its performances combined chaupadi, chhanda and janana by older poets with new compositions in the traditional style, including short songs of his own, and opened with his discussion of Rasa philosophy and a kirtana by the child performers. Babaji Benudhar Das was among his disciples. He wrote several Rasa texts, of which Manabhanjana became the most popular; others include Sri Sri Brajamadhuri and Sri Sri Govinda Lilamruta.

He sang classical Odissi songs, chhanda, champu, kirtana, bhajana and janana, many by poets such as Gopalakrushna, Gourcharan and Banamali, on His Master's Voice gramophone records and on All India Radio, including broadcasts from Calcutta. These recordings made him a familiar name in Odisha, where he was popularly called Mohan Gosain. He also played several instruments and acted in plays.
His efforts were central to the making of Sita Bibaha (1936). He produced and directed the film, played Vishwamitra, and wrote 12 of its 14 songs. He has been described as the father of Odia cinema.
The Mohan Sundar Dev Goswami Award, an annual film award in Odisha, is named after him.

Q5006843.lead: C. S. Rao (Chittajallu Srinivasa Rao, 1924–2004) was a director, actor and writer who made about 65 films in Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam and Odia. Satya Harishchandra and Gruhalakshmi were among his Odia films.

p: The son of the director Chittajallu Pullayya, he was born in Kakinada, East Godavari district. He first faced the camera as a child in Anasuya and Dhruva, both directed by his father and released in 1936. Later he trained under cinematographer K. Ramnoth, art director V. A. K. Sekhar and Uday Shankar, and on his father's Pakkinti Ammayi (1953) he both acted and adapted the screenplay.

Ponni (1953) marked his debut as a director in Tamil, and Sri Krishna Tulabharam (1955) his first in Telugu. Among his well-known Telugu films are Manchi Manasuku Manchi Rojulu (1958), Lava Kusa (1963), Kanchu Kota (1967), Ekaveera (1969), Yashoda Krishna (1975) and Mahakavi Kshetrayya (1976). For Odia cinema he directed Satya Harishchandra (1984) and Gruhalakshmi (1985).

His acting credits include Pelli Sandadi (1959), Intlo Ramayya Veedhilo Krishnayya (1982), Jebu Donga (1987) and Kokila. Muktha V. Srinivasan and K. S. Sethu Madhavan both worked as his assistants before becoming directors.
Lava Kusa (1963) and Desamante Manushuloyi (1970) each won him a National Film Award for direction.

He was first married to a daughter of Kannamba and Kadaru Nagabhushanam. After her death he married the dancer and actress Rajasulochana, and they had twin daughters. He died in Chennai on 8 December 2004.

Q10935114.lead: Sanjay Nayak (born 1975) is an Odia film director, producer and writer who has also written scripts, lyrics and screenplays and runs the production house Sanjay Nayak Films.

p: Nayak began directing with Rakhi Bandhili Mo Rakhiba Mana (2002) and had made 32 films over about 15 years. In 2003, 2005 and 2008 three of his films were released in each year. He worked with actor and MP Siddhanta Mahapatra in 12 films, eight of them in a row. Under his own banner he produced and directed Keun Duniaru Asila Bandhu (2009), the first Odia science-fiction film, which featured an alien.

Many of his films were built around an unusual device: a hand in his debut, 100 scorpions in Rahichi Rahibi Tori Pain, a blind hero in Dharmara Heba Jaya and the hero's returning soul in Tate Mo Rana, both played by Siddhanta Mahapatra. Animals appeared in Babu I Love You and To Bina Mo Kahani Adha, a skeleton in De Maa Shakti De and magic in To Pain Nebi Mu Sahe Janama, while child actors Chandan and Piyali had central roles in Rahichi Rahibi Tori Pain and To Pain Nebi Mu Sahe Janama.

Dil Tate Deichi and Sasura Ghara Zindabad, both produced by Uttam Chand Jain's Top Films with Sabyasachi as hero and S. Ranjan as cameraman, were certified by the censor board on the same day, for which he was nominated to the Limca Book of Records. On television he wrote 150 episodes of the ETV Oriya serial Mausi and directed 52 episodes of Tike Khara Tike Chhai for Doordarshan Odia.

He received the Odisha State Film Award for Pagala Karichi Paunji Tora, and was named Best Director by Chalachitra Jagat and Banichitra on five occasions. Best Director honours went to films including Rahichi Rahibi Tori Pain, Babu I Love You, To Pain Nebi Mu Sahe Janama, Mu Sapanara Soudagar and Keun Dunia Ru Asila Bandhu. He has received more than 100 awards in all, and an honorary doctorate in 2018 for his contribution to Odia cinema.

Q15724317.lead: Debu Bose (born Rabindranath Bose; 1942–2018) was an Odia film actor and trained dancer who appeared in more than 120 films over four decades, beginning with Tapasya in 1980.

p: Bose was born in Odisha in 1942. While at college in Berhampur he belonged to the Ganjam Kala Parishad and performed in several dance dramas. Drawn to dance, he trained in Odissi under Kelucharan Mohapatra.

His film work began in 1974, when he was a dancer and assistant choreographer on Nitai Palit's Mana Akasha; he later also choreographed dances for Odia films. His first film as an actor was Tapasya (1980). Over the following decades he appeared in films such as Kaberi, Sahari Bagha, Suna Chadhei, Ki Heba Sua Posile, Pua Moro Kala Thakura and Samay Kheluchhi Chaka Bhaunri. His later films included Raasta (2014) and Apna Hath Jagannath (2015).

On television he began with the Odia serial Satya and ended with Durga on Tarang TV, and he also acted in the Hindi film Ashram and the Hindi serial Bahu. He was associated with the theatre group Diganta, acting in and directing plays. Alongside his artistic work he joined government service as a labour officer and retired as general manager of the Industrial Development Corporation.
He was married to Madhumita Bose. He died in Hyderabad in 2018.

Q622342.lead: Apurba Kishore Bir (born 1948), known as A. K. Bir, is an Indian cinematographer, screenwriter and director whose Odia films include Aadi Mimansa, Lavanya Preeti, Aranyaka, Shesha Drushti and Nandan.

p: Bir was born in Balikuti village in Odisha, the youngest child of Ajoy and Hemalata Bir; his father was a physics professor and a former principal of Fakir Mohan College in Balasore. Keen on painting as a youth, he enrolled at his father's urging at the Film and Television Institute of India, Pune, in 1969, the first Odia to train there in cinematography.

After the institute he shot short films, advertisements and documentaries; he has photographed more than 300 short films and about 50 documentaries. His first feature as cinematographer was 27 Down (1973), around 70 percent of which was filmed with a handheld camera. He was one of the first-unit camera operators on Richard Attenborough's Gandhi, and his camera work also includes Daasi.

Aadi Mimansa (1991) marked his debut as a director. He went on to direct Lavanya Preeti, Aranyaka, Shesha Drushti, Nandan, Baaja and Hamari Beti, which he also wrote and photographed and which was shown in competition at the Chicago International Film Festival in 2006. Several of his films centred on children.

In 2012 he was appointed a director of the National Film Development Corporation of India, and in 2014 he chaired the feature film jury at the 45th International Film Festival of India. He has also taught as a visiting professor at FTII, Pune and SRFTI, Kolkata.

By 2014 he had won nine National Film Awards. These include Best Cinematography for 27 Down, Daasi and Aadi Mimansa; the Nargis Dutt Award for Best Feature Film on National Integration for Aadi Mimansa; Best Children's Film for Lavanya Preeti and Baaja; and Best Odia Film for Shesha Drushti and Nandan. Lavanya Preeti also won Best Asian Film at the Osaka International Film Festival and was screened at the Berlin International Film Festival. He received the Jayadeva Award in 2010 and the Padma Shri in 2013.
His wife's name is Pratibha.

facts: Film and Television Institute of India, Pune

Q3177812.lead: A. Sreekar Prasad (Akkineni Sreekar Prasad) is an Indian film editor who has edited more than 600 films in 17 languages, Odia among them, since 1983.

p: Prasad was born in Madras into a Telugu family whose roots lie in Somavarappadu near Eluru, Andhra Pradesh. His father, Akkineni Sanjeevi, was a film editor and director and a younger brother of L. V. Prasad. He took a degree in literature from the University of Madras and learned editing from his father.

He began in Telugu cinema and later gained national recognition through Tamil, Malayalam and Hindi films. His editing credits include Yodha, Vanaprastham, Alaipayuthey, Dil Chahta Hai, Kannathil Muthamittal, Okkadu, Yuva, Guru, Firaaq, Kaminey, Pazhassi Raja, Talvar, RRR, Ponniyin Selvan: I and The Goat Life.

In Odia cinema he edited films including Kaberi (1983), Sahari Bagha (1985), School Master (1985), Bhuli Huena (1987), Tunda Baida (1987), Maa Mate Shakti De (1990), Sakala Tirtha To Charane (1995), Krushna Kaveri (1999), Bou (2000) and Bidhata (2003).

He has won nine National Film Awards, seven of them for Best Editing, the highest number in that category; the films include Raakh, Rag Birag, The Terrorist, Vanaprastham, Kannathil Muthamittal, Firaaq and Sivaranjiniyum Innum Sila Pengalum. He has also received five Kerala State Film Awards, two Nandi Awards and Filmfare Awards for Dil Chahta Hai, Firaaq, Talvar and Shershaah. The Limca Book of Records named him among its People of the Year for 2013 and lists him for editing films in the most languages.
His cousins include producer A. Ramesh Prasad and filmmaker K. B. Tilak. His son, Akshay Akkineni, directed Pizza and is married to P. S. Keerthana, daughter of actors R. Parthiban and Seetha.

Q15724801.lead: Balakrushna Dash (1923–1993), titled Sangita Sudhakara, was an Odissi music guru, singer, composer and music director who scored around 20 Odia films between 1950 and 1984.

p: Dash was born at Basantapedi in Balakati, the son of Dinabandhu Das and Kamala Devi. Gotipua dance, songs and theatre drew him to music as a child. While studying in Bhubaneswar he met Satyapriya Mohanty of Cuttack, who introduced him to Guru Gokul Chandra Srichandan, under whom he learned traditional Odissi music. He studied Hindustani classical music with the khayal singer Kshitish Chandra Maitra at the Lakshmikanta Choudhury Sangeet Samaj in Cuttack. In Calcutta, at the home of Raichand Boral, he met Bade Ghulam Ali Khan, whose style influenced his later compositions, and learned music direction and orchestral composition from Boral.

From 1944 he sang Odissi, chhanda, champu and other forms on All India Radio, Calcutta, and he joined AIR Cuttack as a staff artist when it opened in 1948 before leaving to concentrate on promoting Odissi music. He composed pallavis based on raga Basanta for Odissi dance, and set Kabichandra Kalicharan Patnaik's song "Bitila ta jamini" in the manner of a Bade Ghulam Ali Khan thumri.

His film work, as music director and playback singer, included Sri Jagannath (1950), Kedar Gouri (1954), Bhai Bhai, Sri Lokanath, Nua Bou, Dashyu Ratnakar, Jeevan Sathi, Amada Bata, Naba Janma, Adina Megha, Kanakalata, Sankha Mahuri, Mathura Vijay and Basanta Rasa (1984). He also produced many non-film recordings and programmes for AIR Cuttack.
He taught at the Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya and the GKCM Odissi Research Centre; his disciples include Shyamamani Devi and Ramhari Das.

He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Music Director for Mathura Vijay (1979) and Basanta Rasa (1984). His other honours include the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for Odissi vocal (1975–76), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1984), the Jayadeva Award (1987), the Mohan Sundar Dev Goswami Award (1989) and the Tulsi Samman of the Madhya Pradesh government (1991).

facts: Odissi music guru, singer, composer, music director

Q7359907.lead: Roja Ramani (born 1959), also known as Chemparathy Shobana, is an Indian actress and dubbing artist who worked mainly in Telugu, Malayalam and Tamil films and also appeared in Odia cinema.

p: She was the daughter of a journalist who wrote for Picture Post, and grew up in Madras.

As a child she played the title role in the Telugu film Bhakta Prahlada, produced by AVM Productions, which won her the National Film Award for Best Child Artist. She went on to appear in dozens of films as a child artist. At 13 she took her first lead role in the Malayalam film Chemparathy, a major success that was remade in Telugu as Kanne Vayasu and in Tamil as Paruva Kaalam, both with her in the lead.

She worked through the 1970s and early 1980s in Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam, Kannada, Hindi and Odia films. Her Odia films include Punarmilan (1977), Sati Anusuya (1978), Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja (1978) and Seeta Labkush (1980). As a dubbing artist she voiced leading actresses such as Suhasini, Meena, Soundarya, Ramya Krishna and Vijayashanti in more than 400 Telugu and Tamil films.

Besides the National Film Award for Bhakta Prahlada, she won the Filmfare Award for Best Actress (Malayalam) for Chemparathy in 1972, along with Nandi and Kerala state awards and others for acting and dubbing. She was honoured at the celebrations of 75 and 100 years of Indian cinema, received the Santosham Lifetime Achievement Award at the 15th Santosham Film Awards, and the Santosham Excellence Award in 2019.

In 1981 she married Chakrapani, whom she met while filming the Odia film Punarmilan; he was an actor in Odia and Telugu films who later became a producer, director and head of ETV Oriya. Their son Tarun is a Telugu film actor.

Q64356066.lead: Salil Mitra (Salil Kumar Mitra, 1967–2019) was an Odia comic actor who worked in films, television serials and theatre from 1999 until his death.

p: Mitra entered Odia cinema in 1999 with Pua Bhangi Dela Suna Sansara. Over the next two decades he appeared in a long list of Odia films, among them Rahichi Rahibi Tori Paain, Saathire, Arjun, Rakate Lekhichi Naa, Kalishankar, Nari Nuhen Tu Narayani, Subha Vivaha, Hero, Balunga Toka, Matric Fail, Idiot, Love Master, Something Something 2, Love Station, Agastya and Sister Sridevi.

On television he played negative characters in serials such as Bada Ghara Bada Gumara Katha on ETV Odia. He also performed in stage plays, modern Odia music albums and devotional videos. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2019, aged 52.
His father was Bankim Mitra.

facts: Bada Ghara Bada Gumara Katha (ETV Odia)

Q24525216.lead: Amartya Bhattacharyya (born 1987) is an Indian independent filmmaker, writer and poet from Kolkata who makes films in Odia and Bengali, including the Odia features Capital I, Khyanikaa and Adieu Godard.

p: Bhattacharyya was born in Kolkata and studied for ten years at The Modern Academy, where his art teacher Siddhartha Mukherjee introduced him to painting and experimentation. He first acted on stage at six and continued in school theatre. In 2009 he graduated with a B.Tech in information technology from Techno India College of Technology.

After several short films he made his first feature, Capital I (2015), described as the first independent feature film from Odisha. It was shown at festivals including the International Film Festival of Kerala and the South Asian Alternative Film Festival in Paris, and was picked up by the Italian distributor The Open Reel.

His second feature, Khyanikaa – The Lost Idea (2017), was the only Odia film in the Indian Panorama of the 48th International Film Festival of India and played at around 30 festivals in 14 countries. He then made the Bengali film Runanubandha – The HE without HIM in Kolkata. Adieu Godard, an Odia-language Indo-French co-production, premiered at the 43rd Moscow International Film Festival in 2021 and opened in Indian cinemas in September 2022. His later films, alternating between Odia and Bengali, include Whispers of a Storm, Ketu, Son of Adam and Lahari.

Besides directing, he works as a writer, editor, cinematographer, lyricist and actor, and calls his films psychodramas. He has published two poetry collections, Ekush (21) and Shatarupa, launched at the Kolkata Book Fair in 2011 and 2012.

At the 63rd National Film Awards he received the Silver Lotus for Best Cinematography (non-feature) for the documentary Benaras – The Unexplored Attachments. He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Editing for Khyanikaa at the 29th Odisha State Film Awards.

Q15725279.lead: Samaresh Routray is an Odia film and television actor and producer, trained at the National School of Drama, who is known mainly for playing villains.

p: Routray was born in Bhubaneswar to Alekha Prasad Routray and Laxmipriya Routray, the youngest of seven children. He studied at the National School of Drama in New Delhi and also holds an MBA in HR and marketing. After NSD he worked in modelling and acting in Mumbai before returning to Odisha.

His first film was the Hindi 23rd March 1931: Shaheed (2002), in which he played Yashpal. In Odisha he started on television, in serials such as Uttaradayee, Sanskaar, Basundhara and Debi, before entering Odia cinema with Mo Suna Pua. He then played the lead in Dhauli Express, which won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Film.

His role as an ambitious politician in Mukhyamantri (2009) began a run of negative characters in films such as Loafer (2011), Most Wanted and Luchakali (2012). Other films include Sanju Aau Sanjana, Criminal, 1 4 3 I Love You, Thukul, Krantidhara and Niyati. He has also performed in some 500 theatre shows.

He founded the music company Odiaone Entertainment and the production house S3 Movies, and turned producer with Luchakali in 2012. In 2023 he assisted the K-pop group Blackswan with their music video Karma, filmed in Bhubaneswar.

He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor for Namard at the 28th Odisha State Film Awards (2017), and a state award for Best Supporting Actor for Ishq Tu Hi Tu. He received Tarang Cine Awards for Best Actor in a Negative Role for Loafer and Ishq Tu Hi Tu, along with several television awards for his negative role in Sanskaar.

facts: National School of Drama, New Delhi

Q7286096.lead: Rajesh Touchriver (born M. S. Rajesh) is a director, screenwriter and producer whose films are in English, Malayalam, Telugu and Hindi. His best-known works are In the Name of Buddha and Naa Bangaaru Talli.

p: The youngest son of Siva Sankaran Nair and Rukmini Amma, he was born at Arakulam in Idukki district, Kerala, and had some training in Kalaripayattu. He completed a bachelor's degree in design and direction at the School of Drama and Fine Arts, Thrissur, in 1992. With a Charles Wallace Trust Award in 2001 he went on to a master's in scenography and direction at Wimbledon College of Art, London.

In 1995 he was a designer with the National School of Drama, and by 1998 he had directed over 30 plays in Malayalam, English and Telugu. He also worked in the art department of Bavagaru Bagunnara! (1998).

In the Name of Buddha (2002), his debut feature, was set against Sri Lanka's ethnic conflict. After premiering at the Oslo International Film Festival, it played in the Spotlight on India section at Cannes in 2003 and won best foreign film awards at the Beverly Hills, Newport Beach and Wine Country festivals. Two Telugu films, 10 the Strangers and Alex, the Blue Fox, came next, and in 2013 he wrote and directed the social drama Naa Bangaaru Talli.

For the United Nations and NGOs he has made short films and documentaries on human trafficking, HIV/AIDS and communal riots, including One Life, No Price, Anamika, the Nameless and The Sacred Face. He also directed M.I.A.'s music video "Sunshowers" (2004).

Naa Bangaaru Talli won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Telugu and the Nandi Award for Second Best Feature Film, as well as international prizes. Anamika, the Nameless was named Best Documentary at the 2008 Hyderabad International Film Festival, and the Rajasthan International Film Festival gave him its Best Director (Regional cinema) award in 2018.

facts: School of Drama and Fine Arts, Thrissur; Wimbledon College of Art

Q7544821.lead: Smita (born Smita Vallurupalli, 1980) is an Indian pop and playback singer who also acts and hosts television. Her pop albums and Telugu film songs are her best-known work.

p: Her mother secretly sent a tape of her singing to Padutha Theeyaga, the ETV Telugu talent show hosted by S. P. Balasubrahmanyam, and she was spotted there in 1997. She sang a few film songs early on, but her parents felt her style suited pop, and her first album, Hai Rabba, came out in 2000. Masaka Masaka was among her best-selling albums; Smita, composed by Sajid–Wajid and released by Sony BMG in Hindi and Tamil, followed later. Ishana (2012) was a devotional album made for the Isha Foundation, which received all its proceeds.

In Telugu cinema she has recorded over 75 playback songs. Her acting credits include Malliswari (2004), Aata (2007) and the 2015 short film Dying To Be Me, and she has hosted Nijam With Smita, a talk show on SonyLIV.
"Evaraina Chusuntara", composed by M. M. Keeravani for Anukokunda Oka Roju, brought her the 2005 Filmfare Award for Best Female Playback Singer – Telugu.

Q312789.lead: Shakti Kapoor (born Sunil Kapoor, 1952) is an Indian actor and comedian of Hindi cinema, known for villainous and comic roles in more than 700 films, who has also appeared in Odia films.

p: Kapoor was born in Delhi, where his father ran a clothes shop in Connaught Place. He studied at Kirori Mal College and later at the Film and Television Institute of India.

After years of minor parts, beginning with Khel Khilari Ka (1977), he was noticed by Sunil Dutt, who cast him as the villain in Rocky, the launch film of Sanjay Dutt; Dutt also suggested the screen name Shakti Kapoor. Rocky and Qurbani (1980–81) established him, and in 1983 he played villains in Himmatwala and Subhash Ghai's Hero. Through the 1980s and 1990s he formed a regular comic or villainous trio with Asrani and Kader Khan in over 100 films.

In the 1990s he moved increasingly into comedy, with roles such as Crime Master Gogo in Andaz Apna Apna, Batuknath in ChaalBaaz, Goonga in Bol Radha Bol and Nandu in Raja Babu. From 2000 he appeared often in Priyadarshan's films, including Hungama, Hulchul, Chup Chup Ke and Malamaal Weekly. He has also acted in Bengali, Assamese and Odia films; his Odia work includes Bahudibe Mo Jaga Balia (2003) and Chhati Tale Ding Dong (2016). In 2011 he took part in the reality show Bigg Boss 5.
He received several Filmfare nominations for Best Comedian and won once, for playing Nandu in David Dhawan's Raja Babu.
He is married to Shivangi Kapoor, elder sister of actresses Padmini Kolhapure and Tejaswini Kolhapure. Their children are Siddhanth Kapoor and Shraddha Kapoor.

facts: Kirori Mal College; Film and Television Institute of India

Q18618641.lead: Saswat Joshi (born 1984) is an Odissi dancer, choreographer, dance teacher and model from Titlagarh, Odisha, and founder of the Lasyakala Institute of Performing Arts.

p: Joshi was born in Titlagarh in Bolangir district and began learning dance at five under Prasanta Patnaik and Shantanu Behera. He took up professional Odissi training under Kumkum Mohanty in 2000, follows the style of Kelucharan Mohapatra and also trained with Ileana Citaristi. With a national scholarship from the Ministry of Culture he completed a Visharad at Chandigarh University, and he received the Sangeet Ratna from Rabindra Bharati University.

He has performed Odissi in many countries, among them Italy, France, Hungary, Finland, Japan, South Korea and Thailand, including a 2012 performance at the Musée Guimet in Paris, and has given lecture demonstrations at universities. In 2008 he appeared in the production I Have a Dream in Palermo alongside Carla Fracci and Luciana Savignano.

His choreography includes Odissi dance dramas such as Matru Rupa, Mallhar, Devi, Shiva Tandava and a work based on Rama Devi Choudhury, as well as fusion pieces and an Odisha dance presented by NCC cadets at the Republic Day parade in Delhi. Through Lasyakala he teaches Odissi and organises the annual Aekalavya Dance Festival. In films he worked on Nila Madhab Panda's Kaun Kitney Paani Mein and Himanshu Khatua's Kranti Dhara, and has consulted on choreography for Bollywood films. He has also modelled for brands including Manyavar and Boyanika.

Q15625462.lead: Sabyasachi Mishra is an Indian actor, model and playback singer who works mainly in Odia cinema; he made his film debut with Pagala Premi in 2007.

p: Mishra was born in Burla, Sambalpur district, to Surendra Prasad Mishra, an IAS officer, and Sushama Mishra, a writer. He studied at Government Boys' School, Unit-1 in Bhubaneswar and earned a B.Tech in electronics and communications from the Silicon Institute of Technology. He was placed with Infosys but left to work in films.

He started in music videos after Saroj Satapathy introduced him on the Doordarshan Odia programme Rangarang, and went on to appear in more than 200 music videos, including some in Bhojpuri, Bengali, Chhattisgarhi and Punjabi. Director Hara Patnaik saw him at a stage show and cast him in Pagala Premi, released on 14 June 2007.

His later Odia films include Mu Sapanara Soudagar, in which he played an anti-hero; Keun Dunia Ru Asila Bandhu, as a physically challenged character; Mu Eka Tumara (2013), as a mute young man; Pilata Bigidigala (2015), a major box-office success; Hela Mate Prema Jara (2016); Tokata Fasigala (2018); and Mal Mahu Jibana Mati (2019). He sang the title songs of Pilata Bigidigala and Hela Mate Prema Jara. He entered Telugu cinema with Neerajanam and has also acted in Bengali films.

He has served as brand ambassador for the IPL team Deccan Chargers and the Odisha Tennis Premier League, and co-hosted the opening ceremony of the 2018 Men's Hockey World Cup in Bhubaneswar with Archita Sahu.

He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor for Pagala Premi and a second state award for Emiti Bi Prema Hue. Mu Eka Tumara earned him the Filmfare Award East for Best Actor in 2013. He was also named an Outlook Person of the Year in 2020.
He married Odia actress Archita Sahu in March 2021.

Q29947416.lead: Rakhee Dash is an Odia actress, dubbing artist and radio jockey who has worked in films, television serials, advertisements and animation, and is also a trained Odissi and Chhau dancer.

p: She is the daughter of Radhakrushna Dash and Manorama Dash, the fourth of five siblings. She learned Odissi and Chhau dance but gave up dancing after breaking her leg.

She began acting as a child, in Prafulla Mohanty's film Bhanga Silata, the Doordarshan Odia serial Aahuti and short films such as Maguni Ra Sagada and Barsha Bindu. As an adult she found roles hard to get at first because of her short height. Her first adult role was in the ETV serial Duhita, followed by serials such as Sanskar and Parichaya. She has acted in several films directed by Ashok Pati, including Deewana Deewani, Prem Rogi, Dream Girl and Sanju Aau Sanjana, and also in Ishq Tu Hi Tu.

She took up voice dubbing after her marriage, first for supporting actresses and later for heroines. Her first film as a dubbing artist was Pua Mora Bholashankara, voicing Bengali actress Rachana Banerjee, whom she later dubbed for in Laxmana Rekha, Ganga Jamuna, Kandhei Akhire Luha, Santana and other films. Aged about 19 or 20, she voiced a 60-year-old woman in Sabyasachi Mohapatra's serial Jangalara Sathi.
As a radio jockey she started at 93.5 S FM, later worked with Big FM 92.7 and SOA Community Radio, and has freelanced for Radio Chocolate 104 FM. She has also hosted television and stage programmes.
She was named Best Dubbing Artist at the Odia Film Fare awards in 2013.
She is married to singer and music director Bibhu Kishore and lives in Bhubaneswar. She is managing trustee of the Bibhu Kishore Charitable Trust.

Q15650149.lead: Namrata Thapa (born 1986) is an Indian film and television actress who has played leading roles in Odia films and appeared in Hindi television serials such as Yahaaan Main Ghar Ghar Kheli.

p: Thapa was born in Delhi and graduated from Delhi University. She was modelling in Delhi at 16, and moved to Mumbai at about 18.

Her screen career began in 2001 with an episode of Ssshhhh...Koi Hai, cast during auditions held in Delhi. In Mumbai her first serial was Vaidehi, followed by Stree Teri Kahaani, Naaginn, Kuch Apne Kuch Paraye, Kahiin To Hoga and Yahaaan Main Ghar Ghar Kheli, in which she played Swarnlata Raj Singhania.

In Odia cinema she played heroines in films including I Love You, To Pain, Priya Mo Priya, Prema Rutu Asilare, I Love My India, Rasika Nagara, Mu Tate Love Karuchi, Mitare Mita and 1 4 3 I Love You, several of them directed by Hara Patnaik. She also danced in an item number in Abhimanyu and appeared later in Sindura, Guddu Gangster and Racket. She has worked in Bengali and Bhojpuri films and had small roles in the Hindi films Knock Out and Prem Ratan Dhan Payo (2015). In 2025 she judged the Odia reality shows Odisa Ra Best Cinestars Ra Khoj on Zee Sarthak and Raja Sundari on Sidharth TV.

Q3514905.lead: Archita Sahu (born 1990), often credited simply as Archita, is an actress, model and television personality who works mostly in Odia cinema. She has won Best Actress at the Odisha State Film Awards more than once.

p: Born in Rourkela, she grew up in Bhubaneswar and did her +2 at the Demonstration Multipurpose School there. At KIIT she studied engineering, graduating in 2011 with a B.Tech in Information Technology, and also completed an MBA. A trained Odissi dancer, she won a national scholarship for dance. She was crowned Miss Kalinga in 2004 and finished first runner-up in the Kolkata regional contest of Femina Miss India in 2013.

Although beauty titles often lead to Bollywood offers, she chose to act in Odia films. O My Love (2005) was her first film, and by 2021 she had appeared in about 25 Odia films. She played Moina Bai in The Light: Swami Vivekananda, her first Bengali and Hindi film.

She has been a state ambassador for the UNICEF and Government of Odisha campaign to end child labour and an ambassador of the Junior Red Cross, and she promoted the Deccan Chargers as brand ambassador in the fifth IPL season.

The Odisha State Film Awards named her Best Actress for Pagala Karichi Paunji Tora (2009), Chocolate (2011) and A.C.P. Sagarika (2013), and Best Supporting Actress for Babu I Love You (2006). Mu Eka Tumara won her the Filmfare Awards East prize for Best Odia Actor (female). At the Tarang Cine Awards she was Best Actress for Smile Please, Pilata Bigidigala and Bye Bye Dubai, and Star Entertainer of the Year for Shiva Not Out. She was also named Best Newcomer for O My Love in 2005.
She and the actor Sabyasachi Mishra were married in Jaipur on 1 March 2021. Their son was born in January 2026.

Q15724412.lead: Nimai Charan Harichandan (1901–1983), honoured with the title Banikantha, was an Indian singer of Odissi music, described as Odisha's first professional vocalist.

p: He was born on 9 July 1901 into the family of Radhashyam Narendra, a zamindar of Kendrapara; his parents were Brundaban Chandra Harichandan and Indramani Devi. Money troubles at home and his father's poor health ended his schooling early, and a passenger transport business he started to support the family ran at a loss.

Drawn to music as a teenager, he began training in 1916 under his uncle Gokul Chandra Srichandan, a musician and researcher, who taught him mridanga, harmonium and Odissi forms such as chaupadi, chhanda, champu, bhajan and janana. He later studied with Ustad Madho Rao, father of the singer Biswanath Rao, and then with Babaji Ramdas in Calcutta.

On returning from Calcutta he became court musician of the Athagarh durbar. His repertoire covered the traditional Odissi forms, Ramalila and Krishnalila songs and folk songs, and he recorded verses from classical works including Baidehisha Bilasa, Bidagdha Chintamani, Bichitra Ramayana and Mathura Mangala. Many of his bhajans were devoted to Jagannath, and he set to music the poetry of Upendra Bhanja, Kabisurya Baladeba Rath, Salabega, Gopalakrushna Pattanaik, Banamali Das and others. He also sang songs on moral themes and public awareness songs for government campaigns.

HMV began recording him in 1933, and his gramophone records, made until 1976, carried his singing across Odisha. He was a known artist at the Calcutta radio station by 1934, and All India Radio Cuttack first broadcast him on 28 December 1947. In 1954 he performed at the Red Fort at the invitation of the Sangeet Natak Akademi. The Odissi music teacher Gopal Chandra Panda learned from him, collected traditional ragas through him and published notations of his songs. From 1970 he lived in Puri, where he performed the chamara seva at the Jagannath Temple, an honour granted by the Gajapati of Puri, and sang jananas there.

HMV gave him the title Banikantha, and he received the Padma Shri in 1976. His other honours included a gold medal from the Utkal Sangeet Samaj in 1938, a gold medal from the Athagarh court, the Central Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1954, the Bishuba Milan award in 1966 and the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1978.
He married Lakshmipriya, a princess of the Athagarh royal family. He died in Puri in 1983, on the day of the Bahuda Yatra.

facts: Chakadola Kimpa Daka; Patitajananku Uddhariba Pain

Q5320715.lead: Manmohan Mahapatra (1951–2020) was an Odia filmmaker who directed, produced and wrote. Eight of his Odia features in a row won National Film Awards.

p: He was born in Khordha; his parents were Radhakrushna and Pramila Mahapatra. Once he had graduated from BJB College he met the director Nirad Mahapatra, who pointed him towards books on cinema and urged him to join the Film and Television Institute of India in Pune. He completed its three-year film-making course there with a gold medal.

Anti-Memoirs, a short film from 1975, was his first work. A year later he directed Seeta Raati, his first Odia feature, which won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia; its 1982 festival screening abroad made it the first Odia film shown at an international festival. Some short films followed, and then Neeraba Jhada, which earned him another national award.

Klanta Aparahna, Trisandhya, Majhi Pahacha, Nisiddha Swapna, Kichi Smruti Kichi Anubhuti, Andha Diganta, Bhinna Samaya, Agni Veena and Muhurta were among his later features. He had writing credits on several of his own films and produced Neeraba Jhada and Forbidden Dream. His documentaries include Voices of Silence and Konark: The Sun Temple, and in Hindi he directed films including Bits and Pieces, starring Nandita Das, Rahul Bose and Dia Mirza.

His Odia films won the National Film Award for best regional film eight times in succession; Seeta Raati, Neeraba Jhada, Klanta Aparahna, Majhi Pahacha, Nisiddha Swapna and Bhinna Samaya were among the winners. He also won Odisha State Film Awards, the Jayadev Award (2001) and an honorary DLitt from Utkal University of Culture (2017). The Padma Shri for art was conferred on him posthumously in 2020.
His wife was Bidya Mahapatra, and they had three sons, Ashutosh, Manatosh and Bhabatosh. He died in Bhubaneswar on 13 January 2020.

facts: Film and Television Institute of India, Pune; BJB College

Q6392028.lead: Papu Pom Pom (born Tattwa Prakash Satapathy) is an Odia comic actor in film, television and on stage, and also a stand-up comedian, director and music director.

p: He comes from Nuasahi in Kaptipada, Mayurbhanj district, and grew up in a family of performers: his father, a high school headmaster, received a presidential award for magic. From childhood he performed jatra, songs and dances, winning prizes at district and state level. He studied chemistry for his BSc at Udala College, then part of North Odisha University, and was secretary of the college drama society.

Trained as a Hindustani vocalist, he came to Bhubaneswar after his degree hoping to work as a singer and actor. Work was hard to find at first; he sang on about 60 Odia album songs that did not take off, and then spent some time presenting on the private radio station Radio Chocolate 104 FM under the name Papu Pom Pom. A 2009 contract with Tarang TV for comedy serials changed his fortunes, and he has since played comic parts in many Tarang TV and Tarang Music productions. He headed the cast of the comedy serial Excuse Me: Jaha Kahibi Sata Kahibi, also appeared in Faltu Katha and Eita Bayata, and has played over 500 characters on television.

His film roles include To Akhire Mu, Sanju Aau Sanjana, Diwana and Balunga Toka. In 2018 he announced Chirkut, produced by Akshay Kumar Parija, on which he served as director and music director instead of acting in a comic role. He also runs Papu Pom Pom Creations, a production house for YouTube.
Standing for the Biju Janata Dal in Champua in the 2014 Odisha Assembly election, he was defeated by Sanatan Mahakud and then withdrew from politics.
Tarang TV's Tarang Cine Awards named him Best Comedian.

facts: Excuse Me: Jaha Kahibi Sata Kahibi

Q7684462.lead: Tapas Paul (1958–2020) was an Indian actor and politician, known chiefly for Bengali films, who also served as a Trinamool Congress legislator and Member of Parliament.

p: Paul was born in Chandannagar, West Bengal. He studied at Hooghly Mohsin College and earned a BSc in bio-science from the University of Burdwan.

He was noticed in a train compartment by Shrinibas Chakraborty, an assistant director, who brought him to Tarun Majumdar, then searching for a new actor to play Kedar in Dadar Kirti (1980). The film was a box-office success and launched his career, which continued with Saheb (1981), Parabat Priya (1984), Bhalobasa Bhalobasa (1985), Amar Bandhan (1986) and Guru Dakshina (1987). His first Hindi film was Hiren Nag's Abodh (1984), with Madhuri Dixit.

Bhalobasa Bhalobasa, his second film with Majumdar, paired him with Debashree Roy, and the two went on to appear together in Arpan, Surer Sathi, Surer Akashe, Nayanmani, Chokher Aloy, Shubha Kamana, Mayabini and Tobu Mone Rekho. He was also known for films with Mahua Roy Choudhury, and he worked with Buddhadeb Dasgupta on Uttara (2000) and Mondo Meyer Upakhyan (2002). His acting career ran from 1980 to 2013.
As a Trinamool Congress politician he represented Alipore in the West Bengal Legislative Assembly for two terms between 2001 and 2009, and was Member of Parliament for Krishnanagar from 2009 to 2018.

Saheb brought him a Filmfare Award (listed as Filmfare Awards East Best Actor, 1981). He received Kalakar Awards for Best Actor for Rupban (1993), Mejo Bou (1996), Mama Bhagne (2001) and Pratishodh (2005), and for the television series Nayak (2003), as well as a Bharat Nirman Award in 2012.
He was married to Nandini Paul; their daughter Sohini Paul is a Bengali film actress. He died in Mumbai in 2020.

facts: Hooghly Mohsin College, University of Burdwan (BSc)

Q5225034.lead: Mihir Das (1959–2022), full name Mihir Kumar Das, was an Odia film actor whose career lasted more than 30 years. He played heroes, character parts, villains and comic roles.

p: Born in Mayurbhanj, he started in films with the art film School Master; his first commercial release was Mathura Bijay (1979). His performance in Pua Mora Bhola Sankara won him wide recognition, and over the next decades he moved between leading, character, negative and comedy roles in a long list of Odia films.

Odisha's state government gave him a series of film awards. He was named Best Actor for Pua Mora Bhola Sankara (1996), Bidhata (1999) and Pheria Mo Suna Bhauni (2005), and Best Supporting Actor for Soubhagyabati (1997), Rakhi Bandhili Mo Rakhiba Mana (2002) and Prema Adhei Akshara. Laxmi Pratima also brought him a state award. Mu Tate Love Karuchhi earned him the Best Comedian award in 2007.

His wife, the singer and film artist Sangita Das, was the daughter of the popular singer Chitta Jena; she died in 2010. Their son Amlan Das is also an actor. Mihir Das died in Cuttack on 11 January 2022.

Q15725421.lead: Himansu Sekhar Khatua (born 1965) is an Odia film director, sound specialist and film educator. Kathantara, which he directed, won him state awards for best director and best story.

p: His parents, Rabindra and Kunjalata Khatua, lived in Khatuapatana village in Bhadrak district, where he was born and had his first schooling. He finished school and college at other places in Odisha, then completed a postgraduate diploma in cinema at the Film and Television Institute of India, Pune, in 1992, with sound recording and engineering as his specialisation.

Following a brief period of work in Mumbai, he came back to Odisha and did the sound recording and sound design for Indradhanura Chhai, a film by his close friend Susant Misra produced by Jugal Debata. He also recorded sound for Asha.

It was Alaya Mohanty who urged him to direct. Sunya Swarupa, his first film, was started in 1996 and took renunciation as its subject; it was screened in India and abroad, was honoured at the 44th National Film Awards, and collected five Odisha State Film Awards, best film and best direction among them. Kathantara, the first film produced by Kadambini Media, followed under his direction in 2005.

Besides his own stories he has filmed other writers' work: Jayanta Mahapatra's Trunk of Ganesh became Matira Bandhana, and Iti Samanta's Jhada Parara Surjya became Krantidhara. Kahe Ballabha, on the Odia folk theatre form Mughal Tamasha, was screened at the International Dadasaheb Phalke Film Festival, the Mumbai International Short Film Festival and the South Asian Short Film Festival, while Kahani Nuhen won the first Odia State Telefilm Award for best short film. He has also made a Doordarshan telefilm from Fakir Mohan Senapati's Prayaschita, the serials Abhishapta Jarayu and Bhagnansha, a 16 mm documentary about Akhandalamani, educational films, Odishare Gandhiji (2021) and The Sea and Seven Villages (2023). He organised the Kalinga Global Film Festival in Odisha to bring Indian cinema closer to the public.

He has led the sound department at the Biju Pattnaik Film and Television Institute, Cuttack. In 2009 KIIT University made him head and director general of its schools of film, fashion and mass communication, and in 2015 he took charge of Kalinga TV as managing director. The Government of India then appointed him director of the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute. Since leaving that institute he has resumed his posts at KIIT and Kalinga TV.

For Kathantara he received the Rajat Kamal, with the film named best Odia film at the National Film Awards and honoured at the Odisha State Film Awards for best director, best film and best story. Sunya Swarupa also won a National Film Award. Krantidhara earned an Odisha State Film Award, an Asian Excellence Award and a best film prize in South Korea.

facts: Film and Television Institute of India, Pune

Q21029277.lead: Amlan Das is an Odia film actor, active since 2013, who has also worked in advertisements; he is the elder son of the actor Mihir Das.

p: Das was born in Cuttack to the actor Mihir Das and the singer and film artist Sangita Das. He went to school in the CDA area of Cuttack, passing his Class 10 examination in 2008 and Class 12 in 2012, and acted in several plays at school and college. He then studied film technology at the Sivaji Ganesan Film Institute of SRM Institute of Science and Technology in Chennai, graduating in 2013 before returning to Odisha.

His first film was Target (2013), directed by S. K. Muralidharan and produced by Niranjan Rana, in which newcomer Jhilik Bhattacharya played opposite him and his father Mihir Das was also in the cast. Later in 2013 he played a double role in Chandi Parija's Tu Mo Dehara Chhai, which brought him wider attention, though several of his subsequent releases did not do well commercially.

In 2014 he worked with director Susant Mani on Golapi Golapi, released during Raja, and Pagala Karichu Tu, released at Durga Puja, both opposite Riya Dey. In 2015 he appeared in Sudhanshu Mohan Sahu's College Time, again with Riya Dey, and in S. K. Muralidharan's Nua Nua Premare opposite Patrali Chattopadhyay. His other films include Tu Kahibu Na Mu, Tiger, Tora Dine Ku Mora Dine, Chini, Bajrangi and Sapanara Pathe Pathe.

On television he served as a judge and host for the second season of the Tarang TV programme Kie Heba Mo Heroine, and he later acted in Tu Kahibu Na Mu with Niharika Dash, the heroine chosen through that show.
His father, Mihir Das, was a long-serving Odia film actor, and his mother, Sangita Das, worked as a singer and film artist.

facts: Sivaji Ganesan Film Institute, SRM Institute of Science and Technology

Q5224380.lead: Hara Patnaik (1958–2015), also credited as Hara Pattanaik and Hari Patnaik, was an Odia film actor, director, producer and screenwriter from Cuttack. He acted in more than 60 films.

p: His film work started in 1977, assisting director Sisir Mishra on Suna Sansar. Jivan Sangram (1984) was his first film as an actor, and his many later roles included parts in Sahari Bagha, Jor Jar Mulak Tar, Suna Chadhei, Chaka Akhi Sabu Dekhuchi, Jahaku Rakhibe Ananta, Kapala Likhana, Ram Laxman, Ganga Jamuna, Kalki Abatar, Dharma Debata, Barsa My Darling, Arjun and Om Sai Ram.

As a director he made films including Daiba Daudi (1990), Kapala Likhana (1991), Bhagya Hate Dori, Yashoda, Suhaga Sindura, Pua Mora Bhola Sankara, Nari Bi Pindhipare Rakta Sindura, Kalki Abatar, Ae Jugara Krushna Sudama, Barsa My Darling, I Love You, Arjun, Thank You Bhagban, Pagala Premi, which he also made in Bengali, Romeo – The Lover Boy and Om Sai Ram. Anubhav Mohanty, Sabyasachi Mishra and Babushaan were among the actors he introduced. He remained active until 2013.
He won a number of state-level awards during his career.
His wife was Jharana Pattanaik. He died in Bhubaneswar on 13 January 2015.

Q15723616.lead: Anita Das (1953–2018) was an Indian film and television actress in Odia cinema, best remembered for mother roles, who received three Odisha State Film Awards.

p: Das was born in Nayagarh district to Banamali Das and Satyabhama Das. After attending her village school she moved to Cuttack in 1973 to study at Sailabala Women's College, living in the hostel of Kala Bikash Kendra while training in dance. During this period she learned Odissi from Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dash.

She made her screen debut in a lead role in Jajabara (1975), while in the final year of her degree; her first line was spoken opposite the veteran Hemanta Das. Her second film, Nagaphasa (1976), made her popular, helped by the song "Natha Natha He Natha, Mo Prana Natha", which was picturised on her.

Her first mother role came in Bhakta Salabega (1983), and after Pua Mora Kala Thakura she became firmly associated with such parts. From the 1980s onward she played mostly supporting roles, often as a mother, across more than a hundred films, including Odia, Bengali and Hindi productions such as Bhigi Palkein and Ashray. Her career spanned about 43 years, ending with Excuse Me in 2018.

During Rajiv Gandhi's time as prime minister she declined an offer to contest the Dharmasala seat. In 1992 she stood as a Congress candidate from Jajpur Road and lost narrowly, after which she withdrew from politics.

She won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress for Tapasya (1980) and for Bhakta Salabega (1983), and the award for Best Supporting Actress for Eai Ta Dunia (1987). She also received a Banichitra Lifetime Achievement Award and honours from Chitrapuri, Cinema Sansar, Chalachitra Jagat and Cine Critic.
She died at her home on Mission Road in Cuttack in 2018.

facts: Odissi, under Kelucharan Mohapatra and Raghunath Dash

Q56380352.lead: Pupul Bhuyan (born 1992), also known as Payal Bhuyan, is an Indian actress, television presenter and model who works mainly in Odia films and television.

p: Bhuyan was born in Sainkul village in Keonjhar district to BataKrishna Bhuyan and Baijayantimala Bhuyan. She graduated from Buxi Jagabandhu Bidyadhar College in Bhubaneswar.

She began as a stage presenter before hosting television programmes, among them E-News, A-Gossip and Tele Travel on O TV, The Review Show on MBC TV, Aama Rosei Ghara and Jita Odisha Jita on Tarang TV, Apananka Pasand on ETV Oriya, and Swara Odishara, Mun Bi Heroine Hebi and Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Little Champs on Sarthak TV.

Her film debut came in 2013 as the female lead of Kaunri Kanya, directed by Somya Ranjan Sahu and described as the first Odia 3D film. She later took character roles in films such as Blackmail and Bidyarana, and appeared in Niyati (2023) from S3 Movies. She was also cast as Barsha in Anubhab – A Lover Boy, directed by Saroj Barik, opposite Suraj Kumar.

As a model, she won the Opera Mrs India Global title in 2018, reportedly from about 700 contestants, and received the best ramp walk prize in the semifinal. She has appeared on the covers of the Odia magazines Kadambini (2016) and Shubhapallaba (2022).

Kaunri Kanya brought her Best Female Debut awards at the Rupanagara Mayanagara Awards and the Show Time Awards. The song "Bou Mariba" from Blackmail won Most Popular Song of the Year at the Star Ollywood Awards.
She married Deep Thadani in 2016.

Q15724222.lead: Babushaan Mohanty (born Tanmay Mohanty, 1989) is an Odia film actor, playback singer and producer. Super Michhua, Sister Sridevi, DAMaN and Bou Buttu Bhuta are among his best-known films.

p: The son of actors Uttam Mohanty and Aparajita Mohanty, he was born in Bhubaneswar. His parents wanted him to make his name as a playback singer, and he was given vocal training with that aim. He studied at KIIT University.
Hara Patnaik cast him as the hero of Romeo – The Lover Boy (2009), his first film, with Lovely as his co-star and his real parents playing his parents on screen; it was not a big success.

Three of his 2015 releases, Jie Jaha Kahu Mora Dho, Super Michhua and Bhala Pae Tate 100 Ru 100, did well, and Super Michhua brought him his highest fee for an Odia film. Bidyarana, a Ratha Jatra release of 2022, paired him with Sivani Sangita, Soma Bhoumick and Pupul Bhuyan; later the same year his role as a doctor in DAMaN was well received by audiences.

He has also sung in films such as Romeo, Loafer, Daha Balunga, Love Station, Hero No.1, Ajab Sanjura Gajab Love, Premam, Bidyarana, DAMaN, Malyagiri, Dasam, Pabar and Bou Buttu Bhuta, and he is credited as a lyricist on Chocolate (2011).

His company Babushaan Films was founded in 2017. Its first project, made jointly with Prakash & Dhiraj Entertainment, was Sunapila Tike Screw Dhila, in which he also starred. He shared production credit on two 2023 films, Phalguna Chaitra (with Aadya Jagdev Films) and Malyagiri (with Rain Drop Pictures), and Babushaan Films made Pabar in 2024.
Both his parents, Uttam Mohanty and Aparajita Mohanty, are actors. His wife is Trupti Satapathy.

Q115096687.lead: Dipanwit Dashmohapatra (born 1995) is an Odia actor who works in theatre, feature films and web series.

p: Born in Soro in Balasore district to Jeetendra and Jyotsna Dashmohapatra, he went to school at Ramakrishna Sikhshya Niketana and S.N. High School in Soro and did his higher secondary studies at Upendranath College. He then took an electrical engineering degree from ITER, Siksha 'O' Anusandhan, Bhubaneswar, finishing in 2017.
Acting began for him on the college stage, with the Siksha 'O' Anusandhan drama group Toneelstuk; he went on to Uttar Purush and is a member of Bhubaneswar's Jeevan Rekha Theatre Group.

In Amartya Bhattacharyya's Khyanikaa – The Lost Idea (2017), a selection for the Indian Panorama at the 48th International Film Festival of India, he played the postman and travelled to Goa as one of the film's delegates. Samaresh Routray's company OdiaOne cast him in music videos and web series, and the success of the web series Rabana Podi brought him wide recognition.

He was Joe in Bhattacharyya's Adieu Godard, a winner of several international prizes including Best Feature Film (Indian section) at the 27th Kolkata International Film Festival, which opened in theatres in September 2022. He gained wider attention with a supporting role as a compounder in DAMaN, starring Babushaan. In Pratikshya (2022) he took the lead; the film was chosen for the Indian Panorama at IFFI 2022 and won Best Story Feature Film at the Washington DC South Asia Film Festival, and Anupam Kher committed to remaking it in Hindi with himself in the cast.

Q26232782.lead: Kuna Tripathy (born Satyabrata Tripathy) is an Odia actor, radio artist and television presenter from Cuttack. In 2018 he became chairman of the Odisha Film Development Corporation.

p: He took a master's degree in arts at Ravenshaw University. His first stage performance came when he was six, and as a child he also took part in Shishu Sansar on All India Radio.
Between 1988 and 1999 he was a radio artist with All India Radio, Cuttack, and Vividh Bharati. Satarka Sanghamitra, an AIR play he acted in in 1995, won the award for Best Play in India.

On screen he appeared in the Hindi film Sopan (1987). In Odia cinema he was first cast as a villain and later played supporting and comic parts, in films such as Kie Kahara (1997), Maa Gojabayani, Lat Saheb, Rakata Chinhichi Nijara Kie, Samaya Chakra Re Sansara Ratha, Nari Akhi Re Nia, Tate Mo Rana, Tu Mo Akhira Tara, Dharma Ra Haba Jaya, Satyameba Jayate, Pila Ta Bigidi Gala, Tu Eka Mo Saha Bharasa, Love Dot Com and Prem Kumar. He has also acted in two Bengali films, Bichu Chelly and Bandhu.

Television acting began for him in 1995 with the Odia serial Kahuthile Saribani, and he later appeared in Samparka, Duhita, Sara Akasha, Je Pakhi Ude Jete Dura, Dasi, Rajaniti and Tulasi. He became widely known as presenter of the satirical news show News Fuse on O TV, which he hosted until 2018, and afterwards fronted the satire programme Bampha on Nandighosa TV. His other work includes songwriting, scripts, direction of docudramas and telefilms, and humorous verse, poems and stories.
He became a member of the Biju Janata Dal in 2016. When the Government of Odisha named him chairman of the Odisha Film Development Corporation in May 2018, he gave up News Fuse.
He considers the late actress Parbati Ghose his guru and a mother to him. His wife is Sangeeta Tripathy, and they have two daughters.

Q4864991.lead: Barsha Priyadarshini (born 1984), also spelled Varsha Priyadarshini, is an actress and politician from Cuttack. Most of her films are in Odia, and she has also acted in Bengali cinema.

p: Born in Cuttack to the Odia film actress Deepa Sahu, she studied at Sailabala Women's College. Fashion modelling came before acting, which she took up at the age of 17.

She had appeared as a child artist in Maa and Golamgiri before playing a leading role opposite stars Uttam Mohanty and Mithun Chakraborty in Ae Jugara Krushna Sudama (2003). Successful Odia films such as Sabata Maa, Baazi, Tu Mo Akhira Tara, Topae Sindura Di Topa Luha, Tate Mo Rana and Thank You Bhagban followed. On television she made her first appearance in the ETV Oriya serial Panatakani.

Jor (2008) was her first Bengali film; Golmaal, Love Story, Balika Badhu, Takkar, Hasi Khusi Club, Tupur Tupur Brishti Pore and Achena Prem came after it. Her Odia and Bengali films together number more than 25.

She entered politics with the Biju Janata Dal in April 2024 and was its candidate for Barchana in the Odisha Assembly election that year. With 65,616 votes she came second, 6,310 votes behind Amar Kumar Nayak of the BJP.
Her mother is the actress Deepa Sahu. She married the Odia actor Anubhav Mohanty in February 2014; they later divorced.

Q4802093.lead: Arun Govil is an Indian actor and Bharatiya Janata Party politician, best known for playing Rama in the 1987 television series Ramayan, who has represented Meerut in the Lok Sabha since June 2024.

p: Govil was born in Meerut, the fourth of six sons and two daughters of Chandraprakash Govil, a government officer. He spent his teens in Shahjahanpur, where he took a BSc at a college affiliated to Agra University and acted in college plays. His father hoped he would join government service.

In 1975 he moved to Mumbai to work in his brother's business but soon left it to pursue acting. His sister-in-law Tabassum introduced him to Tarachand Barjatya after his first film, Prashanta Nanda's Paheli (1977). Barjatya then signed him for three films, Sawan Ko Aane Do, Raadha Aur Seeta and Saanch Ko Aanch Nahin, all released in 1979; the first and third were box-office successes. His other films include Jiyo To Aise Jiyo (1981), Himmatwala (1983), Dilwaala (1986) and Govinda Govinda (1994).

He began working in television with Ramanand Sagar's Vikram Aur Betaal (1985) and was then cast as Rama in Sagar's Ramayan, a role he repeated in Luv Kush and Jai Veer Hanuman and voiced in the Indo-Japanese animated film Ramayana: The Legend of Prince Rama. He also played Harishchandra in Vishwamitra, the title role in Buddha, and Laxman in V. Madhusudhana Rao's Lav Kush (1997).
Govil joined the Bharatiya Janata Party on 18 March 2021. The party nominated him for the Meerut constituency in March 2024, and he won the seat in the general election declared on 4 June 2024.
His portrayal of Rama in Ramayan earned him the Uptron Award for Best Actor in a Leading Role in 1988.

He is married to the actress Shrilekha, and they have two children. His elder brother Vijay Govil was married to Tabassum, a former child actress who hosted the Doordarshan celebrity talk show Phool Khile Hain Gulshan Gulshan.

Q15725100.lead: Raimohan Parida (1963–2022), also known as Siddhu, was an Odia film and jatra actor, mainly known for villain roles, who also directed many jatra plays.

p: Parida was born in Udayapur, Keonjhar district, the only son among the five children of Trailokyanath Parida and Tilottama Parida. While at high school he played Mukunda Deva in the play Kala Pahada, and he acted in several stage plays at Karanjia College. After seeing him perform at the village club, his father enrolled him at Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya, where he earned a degree in acting. There he played Bhima in Radha Panda's production of Krushna, and he later worked with theatre groups including Satabdira Kalakar, Anwesan, Natya Chetana and Sabuja Natya Sanstha.

He hoped to become a leading man but did not get such roles. His first film was Gangashiuli (1984), in which he played a character part, followed by a small role in Paka Kambala Pota Chhata (1986). He was cast as the villain in Sagar (1989) and went on to play villains in many films, along with some positive roles. Among his early films only Kotie Manisha Gotie Jaga (1991) did well, but his performances in Bhisma Pratigya, Pathara Khasuchi Bada Deulu, Udandi Sita and Naga Panchami in 1992–93 drew praise and made him a popular screen villain. His last Odia film released in his lifetime was Biswanath, on 12 June 2022.

From 2002 he also worked in Bengali cinema, appearing in 15 Bengali films. In jatra, he co-directed Chinmay Das's play Bhanga Aina with the actor Ashrumochan Mohanty for Tarini Gananatya in 1991–92, and later directed and acted in productions for troupes such as Kalinga Gananatya, Trinath Gananatya, Rudrani Gananatya, Jagannath Gananatya, Odisha Opera and Dharitri Opera. He also acted in television serials, the last being Singhadwara on Manjari TV.
