He received a special jury mention at the 1998 Odisha State Film Awards for Sata Michha, and the Abhinandika award in 2010.
He married Ranjita, a junior student at Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya, in 1992; they had two daughters, Shefali and Udita. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2022.

Q7508087.lead: Siddhanta Mahapatra (born 1966), also written Sidhant Mohapatra and nicknamed Munna Bhai, is an Odia film actor, producer and politician. He has represented Berhampur in the Lok Sabha and Digpahandi in the Odisha Assembly.

p: Born Gyana Ranjan Mohapatra in Brahmapur, Ganjam district, to Kanak and Manmohan Mohapatra, he attended St. Vincent's Convent School there. He then studied commerce at Dharanidhar College, Keonjhar, up to graduation, and later earned a postgraduate management qualification in New Delhi.

Sradhanjali was the film that launched his acting career, although Pathara Khasuchi Bada Deulu was the first of his films to reach cinemas. He has since played the lead in a very large number of Odia films. Omm Divya Vision Home Motion Picture, the production company he set up in 1992, has produced and distributed around 120 films. Forbes India has included him in its income-based Celebrity 100 list.

His political career began with the Biju Janata Dal in 2009, when he won the Berhampur seat in the Lok Sabha; he held it in 2014 with a margin of close to 100,000 votes and did not seek a third term. Having joined the Bharatiya Janata Party, he won the Digpahandi seat in the Odisha Legislative Assembly in 2024.

He won Odisha State Film Awards seven years in succession, from 2000 to 2006, a record for an actor, and was named Best Actor at the state awards in 2011. His other honours include five Filmfare Awards East and two National Film Awards, for Kotiye Re Gotiye (2000) and Swayamsiddha (2010).
His wife is the Odia film actress Mama Mishra.

facts: Omm Divya Vision Home Motion Picture (1992)

Q15724825.lead: Bijay Mishra (1936–2020) was an Odia dramatist who also wrote screenplays, dialogue and lyrics and directed. His output spanned theatre, cinema and television.

p: He was born Bijay Kumar Mishra in Santaragadia near Nilgiri, Balasore district; his parents were Harihar Mishra and Annapurna Devi. A village drama troupe used his family's house for rehearsals, and watching it gave him his interest in theatre. After matriculating from Nilgiri High School he took the I.Sc. course at Fakir Mohan College, Balasore, and in 1957 completed a civil engineering diploma at Bhubanananda Odisha School of Engineering in Cuttack. His first writing appeared in his school's handwritten magazine and in Panchajanya, the engineering school's magazine.

While starting an engineering job at Hirakud he began writing plays, completing Janani at 21. Samuel Sahu, director of Cuttack's Annapurna B company, was not keen on it at first, yet the troupe went on to perform it six days a week for four months in a row, and it was later filmed. Mishra was among the pioneers of the modern theatre movement in Odisha.

Jajabara, based on his play, was released in 1975 and was his first film; he directed it jointly with Akshaya Mohanty and Hemanta Das under the shared name Trimurti. In all he wrote about 60 plays, 55 films and 7 television serials. Tata Niranjana, which won a national award from All India Radio, was translated into Hindi, Nepali, Kannada and other Indian languages.

His play Banaprastha brought him the Kendra Sahitya Akademi Award in 2013. He also received the Kendra Sangeet Natak Akademi Award, the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award, the Konark Samman (1994), the Utkal Sahitya Samaj's Ramachandra Mishra Natak Samman (1995), the Bioscope Award (2016), the Fakir Mohan Sahityashree Award (2016) and the Think Foundation CSR Lifetime Achievement Award.
He died on 26 April 2020, aged 83.

facts: Bhubanananda Odisha School of Engineering (Diploma, Civil Engineering)

Q6437374.lead: Krushna Abhishek (born 1983), born Abhishek Sharma, is an Indian actor, comedian and television host known for comedy programmes such as Comedy Circus and The Kapil Sharma Show.

p: He was born in Bombay to Atma Prakash Sharma and Padma Sharma; the family's roots lie in Dhami village in Shimla district, Himachal Pradesh. He belongs to the film family of the actor Govinda, his maternal uncle, whose dancing he has cited as an influence.

His first Hindi film was Yeh Kaisi Mohabbat (2002), followed by Hum Tum Aur Mother (2005), Jahan Jaaeyega Hamen Paaeyega (2007) and Aur Pappu Paas Ho Gaya (2007), after which he moved into Bhojpuri cinema. In 2007 he played the lead in the Doordarshan serial Sautela.

He became known as a comedian through several seasons of Sony TV's Comedy Circus, entering Comedy Circus 3 (2009) as a wild card alongside Sudesh Lehri. He took part in dance reality shows including Nach Baliye 3 (2007), Kabhi Kabhii Pyaar Kabhi Kabhii Yaar (2008), which he won with Kashmera Shah, and Jhalak Dikhhla Jaa 4 (2010), and judged Krazzy Kiya Re on DD National with Sudha Chandran.

As a host he has fronted Entertainment Ke Liye Kuch Bhi Karega, OMG! Yeh Mera India on History TV18, and Comedy Nights Live and Comedy Nights Bachao on Colors TV. He later joined The Drama Company (2017) and the second season of The Kapil Sharma Show (2018), appeared in Funhit Mein Jaari (2020), and with Kashmera Shah took part in Laughter Chefs on Colors TV in 2024.
He married the actress Kashmera Shah in 2013; the two met on the set of Aur Pappu Paas Ho Gaya. His sister Arti Singh is an actress, and Govinda is his maternal uncle.

facts: Comedy Circus; The Kapil Sharma Show

Q2684290.lead: Bhaskar Chandavarkar (1936–2009) was a sitarist, teacher and composer for cinema and the stage. Among roughly 40 film scores in several Indian languages, he wrote the music for the Odia film Maya Miriga (1984).

p: Raised in Pune, he graduated from Wadia College and also studied at Fergusson College. His sitar teachers in the late 1950s were Ravi Shankar and Umashankar Misra; he learned Indian classical singing as well, and studied jazz and contemporary Western music.

At the Film and Television Institute of India in Pune he served from 1965 to 1980 as resident composer and teacher of applied music. During those years he scored Ghashiram Kotwal, Vijay Tendulkar's Marathi play directed by Jabbar Patel in 1972, which was praised for setting Marathi devotional songs against ironic situations; he went on to score the film version too. His music for P. L. Deshpande's play Teen Paishacha Tamasha was also acclaimed.

His style mixed Indian classical and Western music, and he collaborated with Mrinal Sen, Girish Karnad, Aparna Sen, K. G. George and Amol Palekar, among others, on films in Marathi, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali and Odia. Vamsha Vriksha (1971), Maya Darpan (1972), Samna (1974), Swapnadanam, Ondanondu Kaladalli (1978), Albert Pinto Ko Gussa Kyon Ata Hai (1980), Akriet (1981), Paroma, Maya Miriga and Khandhar (all 1984), Rao Saheb (1985), Thodasa Roomani Ho Jaayen (1990), Kairee (2000), Shwaas (2004) and Maati Maay (2006) are among his scores. The Yard Went on Forever, his autobiography in several volumes, came out in 2008.

His honours included the Kerala State Film Award for Best Music Director for Swapnadanam (1975), the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (1988) and, in 2002, the National Film Award for Best Non-Feature Film Music Direction for Chaitra, a Marathi short by Kranti Kanade.
He died in Pune on 26 July 2009, leaving his wife Meena and son Rohit.

Q7653993.lead: Swastika Mukherjee (born 1980) is an Indian actress who works mainly in Bengali and Hindi films and television; she is the daughter of the actor Santu Mukhopadhyay.

p: Mukherjee was born in Calcutta and grew up with her father Santu Mukhopadhyay, her mother Gopa and her younger sister Ajopa. She attended Carmel School, St. Teresa's Secondary School and Gokhale Memorial School in Kolkata, and completed a postgraduate degree in history at Jadavpur University. In 2001 she joined the Ananda Shankar Centre for Culture to study dance with Tanusree Shankar.

She first appeared on screen in the Bengali television series Devdasi, and her first film was Hemanter Pakhi (2001). Her first leading role came in Mastan (2004), opposite Jeet, with whom she went on to star in Kranti, Sathihara, Priyotoma, Krishnakanter Will, Pitribhumi and Partner. She also worked with Parambrata Chatterjee in Brake Fail. Her first Hindi film was Mumbai Cutting (2008).
She has won four Filmfare Awards East, three of them for Best Actress from five nominations in that category, along with a WBFJA award, an Anandalok Award and a Kalakar Award.
She is the daughter of the Bengali actor Santu Mukhopadhyay.

Q4785559.lead: Archana Joglekar is an Indian actress and Kathak dancer and choreographer who acted in Marathi, Hindi and Odia films and in Hindi television serials between 1987 and 2012.

p: Joglekar was born in Bombay. She learned Kathak from her mother, Asha Joglekar, a dancer and teacher who founded the Archana Nrityalaya dance school in Mumbai in 1963. In 1999 Archana Joglekar opened a branch of the school in New Jersey, United States.

Her first film was the Marathi Khichdi, and she became known through the Marathi hit Ardhangi, in which she was paired with Ajinkya Deo. Her role as Rajni in the Hindi film Sansar, with Rekha, Raj Babbar and Anupam Kher, brought her wider notice, and she also appeared in the Hindi films Mardangi, Aatank Hi Aatank and Aag Se Khelenge. In Marathi cinema her work in Nivdung (1989), Eka Peksha Ek (1990) and Anapekshit, opposite Nitish Bharadwaj, was well received. She acted with Arun Govil in Phoolwanti.

In Odia cinema she appeared in Suna Chadhei, released in 1988. Her television work included the serials Chunauti, Karmabhoomi, Chahat Aur Nafrat and Kissa Shanti Ka, after which she stepped away from the screen.
She won the Maharashtra State Film Award for Best Actress for Anapekshit.

Q15724036.lead: Gloria Mohanty (1932–2014) was an Odia theatre, television and film actress who was also a trained singer and a state-level volleyball player; her film career began with Sri Jagannath (1950).

p: Born Gloria Rout to Robin and Anila Rout at Matha Sahi, Tulasipur, in Cuttack, she was introduced to dance and music as a child by her aunt, the actress Anima Pedini. She learned Odissi from Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and trained in music at the National Music Association in Cuttack under the guidance of the singers Balakrushna Dash and Bhubaneswar Mishra. She also played volleyball, representing Odisha's women's team at the national championships in the late 1950s.

She sang on All India Radio for more than 20 years. Her stage career began in 1944 with the lead role in the play Bhata, and she went on to perform in over 100 plays in Odia, Hindi, Bengali, Urdu and English, staged in cities across India.

She was offered her first film role in 1949, in Sri Jagannath, released in 1950; playing Lalita opposite Gopal Ghosh made her a leading actress. Her 22 Odia films included Kedar Gouri (1954), Sita Rati and Ulka (1981), Mu Tume O Se (1982), Udaya Bhanu (1983), Sesha Pratikshya and Jaga Hatare Pagha (1985), Bastra Harana (1991), Prathama Prema and Oh My Love (2005), Mahanayak and Chaka Chaka Bhaunri (2007), and Aakhi Palakare Tu (2010). On television she appeared in the Odia serials Jibaku Debi Nahin, Thakura Ghara, Sara Akasha and Panata Kani.

She received the Prajatantra Prachar Samiti's best stage actress award in 1952, the Odisha State Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for Ulka (1981), the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1992, and the Jayadev Award, Odisha's highest honour for contribution to Odia cinema. The cultural organisation Srjan gave her the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Award for 2011, and Ghungur presented her with a lifetime achievement award in 2012.
She was married to Kamala Prasad Mohanty and had four children. Her aunt Anima Pedini was also an actress. She died in Cuttack in 2014.

Q6416209.lead: Kirti Kulhari (born 1985) is an Indian actress who works mainly in Hindi-language films and streaming series.

p: She was born and raised in Bombay (now Mumbai), Maharashtra, in a family with roots in Rajasthan's Jhunjhunu district. Her father, Khyali Ram Kulhari, served as a Commander in the Indian Navy.

Kulhari began in theatre and television advertising. After a month-long workshop with the Hindi theatre group Yatri Theatre under Om Katare, she performed in plays including Chinta Chhod Chintamani and a Hindi version of Sakharam Binder, and appeared in advertisements for a long list of brands.

Her first film was Khichdi: The Movie, released in October 2010, and she drew notice with her second, Shaitan (2011). Her role in Pink (2016) earned her a Filmfare nomination for Best Supporting Actress. She went on to play the title role in Madhur Bhandarkar's Indu Sarkar (2017), an Indian Air Force officer in Uri: The Surgical Strike (2019) and a part in Mission Mangal (2019). After joining the cast of Ribhu Dasgupta's The Girl on the Train in 2020, she received a second Filmfare nomination for Best Supporting Actress.
On streaming platforms she has appeared in Four More Shots Please!, Bard of Blood, Criminal Justice and Human. In 2022 she set up the production company Kintsukuroi Films.
She married actor Saahil Sehgal in 2016 and announced their separation in April 2021.

Q29210726.lead: Bhoomika Dash (born 2003) is an Odia film actress and Odissi dancer who started as a child artist in Rumku Jhumana before moving to lead roles.

p: Dash was born in Bhubaneswar to Trupti and Prasanna Kumar Dash. She attended DAV Public School, Unit-8, in Bhubaneswar and later took up a B.D.S. course at the Institute of Dental Sciences there. She has trained in Odissi dance, and after her first two films as a heroine she paused her film work to sit her Class 10 board examinations.

Her first screen appearance was as a child artist in Rumku Jhumana, directed by Tapas Sarghariya, with Harihar Mahapatra, Mihir Das, Hara Pattnaik and Priya Choudhury in the cast. She then played a child role in Tarang Cine Productions' Gapa Hele Bi Sata.

In 2017, while still in Class 9, she played her first lead in Tu Mo Love Story, Tarang Cine Productions' seventh film, opposite Swaraj Barik; the film was a success. Later that year she was paired with Babushan in Hero No.1, again directed by Tapas Sarghariya and released during Durga Puja, in which she played a woman reporter. In 2019 she played Paro in Nayakara Na Debadas, a modern retelling of the Devdas story.

She won the best child artist award at the 5th Tarang Cine Awards in 2014, and the magazine Chalachitra Jagat's Pratibha Samman named her best debut actress for Tu Mo Love Story. She has also been described as receiving an Odisha State Film Award for best child artist for Rumku Jhumana.

facts: DAV Public School, Unit-8, Bhubaneswar; Institute of Dental Sciences, Bhubaneswar

Q6745457.lead: Mamata Shankar (born 1955) is an Indian actress, dancer and choreographer known chiefly for Bengali cinema, who also appeared in the Odia films Balidan (1978) and Nilamadhaba (1979).

p: She was born in Calcutta to the dancers Uday Shankar and Amala Shankar, and learned dance and choreography under her mother at the Uday Shankar India Culture Centre in Calcutta.

Her screen debut came in Mrinal Sen's Mrigayaa (1976), which won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film. Over the following decades she worked with directors such as Satyajit Ray, Mrinal Sen, Rituparno Ghosh, Buddhadeb Dasgupta and Gautam Ghosh, in films including Ek Din Pratidin, Kharij, Shakha Proshakha, Agantuk, Dahan, Utsab, Maacher Jhol and Projapoti.

Alongside acting she leads a dance company. The Mamata Shankar Ballet Troupe was formed in 1978 and staged Chandalika, based on a Tagore work, in 1979; the Udayan - Mamata Shankar Dance Company followed in 1986 and has toured widely abroad.

She received the National Film Award – Special Jury Award for Agantuk (1992), BFJA Best Supporting Actress awards for Shakha Proshakha and Utsab, and Filmfare Awards Bangla for Maacher Jhol, Projapoti and Bijoyar Pore. The Government of India conferred the Padma Shri on her in 2025.
She is married to Chandrodoy Ghosh. Her brother was the fusion musician Ananda Shankar, and the sitarist Ravi Shankar was her uncle.

Q21468105.lead: Saroj Patnaik (1940–2022) was an Odia music director and lyricist whose film work began with Abhimaan in 1977 and who composed for Odia cinema, radio and television for about four decades.

p: Patnaik was born in Mayurbhanj district. Drawn to music as a child, he taught himself to sing at the harmonium and was shaped by the folk songs and landscape of Mayurbhanj, an influence later heard in his melodies. He afterwards took lessons from his elder sister, Kabita Patnaik.

His songs were being broadcast on All India Radio from 1958–59, and he became an approved lyricist and music director for All India Radio and Doordarshan. Producer Ganesh Chandra Jiu gave him his first film assignment, Abhimaan (1977), which he scored jointly with Radhakrishna Bhanja.

He went on to score Phula Chandana, Jheeati Sita Pari, Abhilasha, Hakim Babu, Mo Mana Khali Tori Pain, Ei Sangharsha and Tume Hi Sathi Mora, writing the lyrics as well for Abhilasha, Mo Mana Khali Tori Pain and Tume Hi Sathi Mora. For Abhilasha he set "Jhuma Jhuma Golapi Belare", sung by Harihar and Gayatri Mukherjee. He also composed popular songs for Akshaya Mohanty such as "Ei Je Banalata Pahada" and "To Bina Lagena Bhala Kichhi", devotional and jhumar cassettes, and music for plays, television serials and telefilms. He acted on occasion, including in Bhinna Samaya (1992).
Outside music he worked as a junior engineer in the Odisha government's Works and Housing department, retiring from Balasore.
He received the Odisha State Film Award for best music director for Phula Chandana and Abhilasha; one account counts three such awards, adding Bhinna Samaya.
He had three sons and a daughter. He died at his home in Baripada in 2022.

facts: Jhuma Jhuma Golapi Belare; Ei Je Banalata Pahada; To Bina Lagena Bhala Kichhi
Engineer, Odisha Works and Housing department

Q15725199.lead: Shantanu Mahapatra (1936–2020), also written Mohapatra, was an Odia composer and singer who scored films in Odia, Bengali, Hindi, Assamese and Telugu, beginning with Suryamukhi in 1963.

p: He was born in Baripada, Mayurbhanj district, to Ramesh and Saudamini Mahapatra. He started learning music at five under Guru Banchhanidhi Panda and was performing on stage while still a child. He studied Applied Geology and Geophysics at IIT Kharagpur, where his involvement with the Indian People's Theatre Association introduced him to group singing; he learned music direction from Salil Chowdhury.

Mahapatra spent his working life in government service, joining Odisha's Department of Mines and Geology and retiring as a director; he also worked as a geophysicist with the Odisha Mining Corporation until 1994.

His first film score was for Suryamukhi (1963), followed by work on Arundhati (1967), Chilika Teerey (1977) and Bagh Bahadur (1989), among some fifty films, telefilms and documentaries, many of them art films. He has been credited as the first Odia music director to work in five film languages. With lyricist Gurukrushna Goswami he created Konark Gatha, described as the first modern Odia ballad, sung by Akshaya Mohanty. His output ran to well over a thousand songs, together with music for jatras, radio plays for All India Radio, Cuttack, and dance dramas.

His honours included the Odisha Film Critics Award (1995), the Lalit Kala Akademi Award (2004), the Mother Teresa Millennium Award (2005) and an honorary D.Litt from Utkal University of Culture (2011).
He died in Bhubaneswar in 2020, aged 84.

Q54505341.lead: Pintu Nanda (1977–2023) was an Odia film and television actor who appeared in more than 115 Odia films as hero, villain, character actor and comedian after his debut in Koili (1996).

p: Nanda was born in Jagatsinghpur, Odisha, to Ashok Kumar Nanda and Kantilata Nanda, one of three siblings. After schooling at SK Academy in Jagatsinghpur he went to Delhi for further studies.

He first acted in a daily serial on DD Odia before entering films with Koili in 1996. His long list of Odia films includes Rama Laxmana, Wrong Number, Oh My Love, I Love My India, Prem Rogi, Mitare Mita, Dosti, Gud Boy, Love Master, Hari Om Hari, Haata Dhari Chaaluthaa, Rumku Jhumana and Prema Rutu Asilare.

On television he acted in the serial Sankha Sindura and presented programmes such as Grihalakshmi on Doordarshan. He also featured in Odia music albums, of which E Gaura Kana Khauchu brought him the widest popularity.

He won the Odisha State Film Award for best comedian twice, for Wrong Number (2005) and Prema Rutu Asilare (2006), and the Tarang Cine Award for best actor in a comic role for Deewana Deewani in 2014.
His elder brother Abhiram Nanda is a flautist. He was married to Shilpa Jena. Nanda died in Hyderabad in 2023 at the age of 45.

Q19842252.lead: Bhubaneswar Mishra (1927–1993) was an Odissi musician, composer and violinist who set music for Odissi dance and, in partnership with Hariprasad Chaurasia, scored Odia and Hindi films.

p: Mishra was born in Paralakhemundi, now in Gajapati district, a town whose temples and mathas exposed him to Odissi music from early childhood. Because he spoke very little as a boy, he was nicknamed Muni. He trained in classical music from a young age and studied violin in both the Hindustani and Carnatic styles under Dwaram Venkataswamy Naidu and Dwaram Narasimha Rao Naidu.

At All India Radio, Cuttack, he came under the influence of musicians including Singhari Shyamsundar Kar, Kashinath Pujapanda and Balakrushna Dash. Working closely with Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, he helped carry Odissi dance and music to audiences in India and abroad; he researched the tradition, composed numerous pallavis in the traditional Odissi style and set Jayadeva's Gitagovinda to music for the dance.
With Hariprasad Chaurasia he scored many Odia and Hindi films under the joint name Bhuban-Hari. Because he was employed by All India Radio, he also worked as a music director under the name Srikumar.
He received the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1979 and the Central Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1986. A memorial honour in his name is presented every year.

Q8049765.lead: Yashpal Sharma is an Indian actor from Haryana who works mainly in Hindi films and theatre, known for roles in Lagaan, Gangaajal and Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi.

p: Sharma grew up in a lower-middle-class family in Hisar, Haryana, and as a child took part in local Ramlila performances during Dasara. He graduated from the National School of Drama in New Delhi in 1994 and spent about two years with its Repertory Company before moving to Mumbai in 1997.

His first significant film was Govind Nihalani's Hazaar Chaurasi Ki Maa (1998). After commercial films such as Shool and Arjun Pandit, his part in Lagaan (2001) brought him wider attention, and he played Randhir Singh in Sudhir Mishra's Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi (2003). Later films include Gangaajal, Ab Tak Chhappan, Apaharan, Singh Is Kinng, Aarakshan, Rowdy Rathore and Dev Anand's Chargesheet; he has often worked with Shyam Benegal and Prakash Jha.

On television he debuted in Zee TV's Mera Naam Karegi Roshan in 2010, played Don Rana in Taarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashmah and led Neeli Chhatri Waale from 2014. He remains active on stage in Mumbai, including the plays One on One and Gulzar's Lakeerein. He moved into direction with Dada Lakhmi, a biopic of the Haryanvi poet Pandit Lakhmi Chand that he also wrote.

His performance in Gangaajal earned nominations from the Filmfare, IIFA, Screen and Zee Cine awards. Dada Lakhmi won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Haryanvi at the 68th National Film Awards, and his Haryanvi film Pagdi: The Honour was also honoured at the 62nd National Film Awards.

facts: National School of Drama, New Delhi (1994)

Q15724410.lead: Nizam (1951–2015), born Sheikh Nizam Ul Haq, was an Odia lyricist and writer whose songs featured in about 160 Odia films, beginning with Anutap in 1977.

p: He was born in Sutahat, Cuttack, to Asad Nazim, and studied at Mission School and Christ College. Taught football by his father, he played for Odisha for ten years, and his sporting record earned him a post in Postal Accounts.

His first song, "Saharara Bati Galani Libhi", was broadcast on the Yuvavani programme of All India Radio, Cuttack, in 1968–69. He began writing for films with Anutap (1977), whose song "Nida Bhara Rati Madhujhara Janha" became popular, and went on to further success with Samar Salim Simon, Manini and Phula Chandana.
Across his career he wrote some 500 songs for around 160 films, dialogue or screenplays for more than 50 films and television serials, and scripts for over 70 jatra plays.

He won Odisha State Film Awards for his work on Rajanigandha (1989), Jeebana Sathi (1997) and a third film. Other honours included the Sikandar Award, the Yadumani Das Memorial Talent Award, the National Art Talent Award and the Akshaya Mohanty Foundation Award.
He was married to Gulsar Hara and had two children, Asad and Gazala. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2015 and was laid to rest at Dargah Bazar, Cuttack.

Q15725164.lead: Laxmipriya Mohapatra (1928–2021) was an Odissi dancer and Odia stage and film actress who, with her husband Kelucharan Mohapatra, is credited with reviving Odissi dance in the 1940s and 1950s.

p: She was born in Khurda, Odisha, and first learned dance from her mother, the actress and dancer Tulasi Devi. She also studied acting and dance with gurus including Rama Mania, Kashinath Sahu, Laxmidhar Patra and Lingaraj Nanda.

She began dancing at the Annapurna Theatre in Puri as a child and became its leading attraction in her teens. At the company she met Kelucharan Mohapatra, then accompanying dancers on the tabla. After training with him, she gave a solo Odissi performance on stage in 1946, seen as a landmark in the revival of the form, and she is also described as the first woman to present Gotipua dance on stage. She performed folk dances at the Republic Day parades in New Delhi in the 1950s.

Her stage plays included Manager, Bharasa, Taapoi, Kalapahada, Mulia, Sadhaba Jhia and Dashavatara. She entered films with Maa (1959) and appeared in Odia films such as Manika Jodi, Suryamukhi, Mala Janha and Amada Bata.

In 1985 she gave up professional performance to support her husband's work as a dancer and choreographer. Together they founded and taught at the Srjan dance school in Bhubaneswar, and her pupils included Minati Mishra, Priyambada Mohanty Hejmadi and Kumkum Mohanty.
She received the Adiguru Pankaj Charan Das Award. After her death, a five-day Odissi festival held in September 2021 was dedicated to her, with performances by many of her former students.

She was married to Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra. Their son Ratikant Mohapatra is an Odissi dancer and choreographer, and his wife Sujata Mohapatra is also an Odissi dancer. She died in Bhubaneswar in 2021, and her last rites were held with state honours at Swargadwar, Puri.

Q15724659.lead: Prakruti Mishra (born 1995) is an Odia film actress who also works in Hindi television; she received a National Film Award special mention for Hello Arsi.

p: Mishra was born in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, and is the daughter of music composer Manmatha Mishra. She studied at Rama Devi Women's College in Bhubaneswar and later earned a Bachelor of Arts from Bhavan's College, Mumbai. She trained in Odissi dance under Guru Gangadhar Pradhan.

She started as a child presenter of educational and children's programmes on Doordarshan and ETV, and acted as a child in the ETV serial Tulasi. Her film career began with Sabata Maa (2003), and as a child artist she appeared in Haribhai Harena and Sashu Ghara Chalijibi, the latter bringing her the Odisha State Film Award for best child actor.

In Thukul she shared the screen with Babushan Mohanty and Archita Sahu. Her first lead role came in Hara Pattnaik's Om Sai Ram (2012), followed by A.C.P. Sagarika, Premika and Kaunri Kanya, in which she played a ghost in what is described as Odisha's first 3D film. Later Odia work includes Omm, Bindas Romeo, Mitha Mitha and Hello Arsi (2018), opposite Partha Sarathi Ray.

On Hindi television she was among the top ten on Zee TV's India's Best Cinestars Ki Khoj (2014), played the title role in Bitti Business Wali on &TV and Devanyi in Jai Kanhaiya Lal Ki on Star Bharat, and reached the finale of MTV's Ace of Space 2 in 2019.
She won the Odisha State Film Award for best child actor for Sashu Ghara Chalijibi and a National Film Award (Special Mention) for Hello Arsi.
Her father, Manmatha Mishra, is a music composer.

facts: Bitti Business Wali; Jai Kanhaiya Lal Ki

Q52154705.lead: Nikita (died 2019), born Laxmipriya Behera, was an Odia film and television actress who played lead and supporting roles in Odia films between 2005 and 2016.

p: She was born in Cuttack, Odisha; her father, Sanatan Behera, was a finance officer in the Works department.

Her first film was Sanjay Nayak's Tu Mo Akhira Tara (2005), in which she played the younger sister of the heroine, Barsha Priyadarshini, alongside Siddhanta Mahapatra, Bijay Mohanty, Kuna Tripathy and Papu Pom Pom. In 2011 she took the female lead opposite Debashis Patra in Rajeev Mohanty's Chori Chori Mana Chori.
She went on to appear in Nishikant Dalabehera's Mun (2012) and Sanjay Nayak's Mita Basichi Mun Bhuta Sathire (2013). Her final film was Subhashis Pati's Gunda (2016), with Siddhanta Mahapatra.
On television she played the title role in the ETV Odia serial Tapasya and later the lead in SP Nikita on Tarang TV, leaving the latter partway through its run.
In 2017 she married actor Lipan Sahu, and they had a son. She died in Cuttack in 2019.

Q705446.lead: Subhashree Ganguly (born 1990) is an Indian actress who works mainly in Bengali cinema; her first film was the Odia production Mate Ta Love Helare (2008), directed by Ashok Pati.

p: Ganguly was born in Bardhaman, West Bengal, to Bina and Debaprasad Ganguly, and attended Burdwan Municipal Girls' High School. After finishing Class 10 in 2006 she won the television talent contest Anandalok Nayikar Khonje and began modelling.

She made her screen debut in the Odia film Mate Ta Love Helare and then entered Bengali cinema in a supporting part in Prabhat Roy's Pitribhumi. Her films with Dev, among them Challenge, Paran Jai Jaliya Re, Romeo, Khokababu, Khoka 420 and Dhumketu, and with Jeet, including Boss, Game, Abhimaan and Boss 2: Back to Rule, brought her wide popularity. She also appeared opposite Shakib Khan in Nabab and Chalbaaz.
Her role as Mehul in Parineeta (2019) drew critical appreciation, and she later starred in Boudi Canteen, Babli, Shontaan and Lawho Gouranger Naam Rey.

She won the Filmfare Award Bangla for best actress for Parineeta, the critics' best actress award for Boudi Canteen and a third best actress award for Babli, and was nominated for best supporting actress for Shontaan. Her other honours include Anandalok and West Bengal Film Journalists' Association awards.
She married film director Raj Chakraborty in 2018; they have a son and a daughter.

Q7530831.lead: Sisir Mishra (born 1942) is an Indian film director and screenwriter who made Odia films such as Sindura Bindu and Sabata Maa as well as Hindi films including Bheegi Palkein; he received the Padma Shri in 2018.

p: Mishra was born in Bomkei, near Digapahandi in Ganjam district, Odisha. His father, Purushottam Mishra, was an engineer under the British administration. He took a B.Sc. at Khallikote College, Brahmapur, and an M.Sc. in physics at Ravenshaw College, Cuttack.

After a short spell lecturing in physics, he moved to Mumbai in 1965 to work as an assistant director to Mehboob Khan and later to Jyoti Swaroop. He directed Hindi films there, among them Bheegi Palkein (1982), Samay Ki Dhara, Billoo Baadshaah, TADA and Aseema, before returning to Odisha.

His first Odia film as director, Sindura Bindu, came out in 1976. It was followed by commercially successful films including Suna Sansar, Samaya Bada Balawan, Subarna Sita, Ei Aama Sansar, Bastra Harana, Suna Bhauja and Sabata Maa. He has been called the Dronacharya of Odia cinema and is credited with pioneering modern film-making in the language.

He received the Nitai Palit Award (2004), the Odisha government's Jayadeva Puraskar for lifetime contribution to Odia cinema, the Kalinga Bharati Ratna Samman, Chalachitra Jagat's Pratibha Samman and the Oriya Cinema Gourav at the Show Time awards (2012). The Government of India conferred the Padma Shri on him in 2018.
His wife, Kadambini Mishra, co-wrote the scripts of several of his films. They have two sons, Sagar and Sameer.

Q21468051.lead: Babli, born Abhipsa Panda in 1995, is an Odia film and music-video actress who entered films in 2009 with a supporting part in Keun Dunia Ru Asila Bandhu.

p: Abhipsa Panda was born in Baripada, Mayurbhanj district, the second child of her parents. Her mother first called her Barbie, which her friends later turned into Babli. Drawn to dance from childhood, she passed her matriculation from MKC High School, Baripada, in 2011 and her Class 12 from MPC Junior College, Baripada, in 2013.

While in Class 7 she began acting in Odia music albums, and Sadhaba Bohu became especially popular. Her film debut was a supporting role as Buddhaditya Mohanty's friend in Keun Dunia Ru Asila Bandhu (2009), which starred Sabyasachi Mishra and Archita Sahu.

Director Rabindra Pradhan gave her the female lead opposite Sabyasachi Mishra in Aakhi Palakare Tu (2010), which also featured Mukesh Rishi. She was paired with Tanmay Mishra in Aain Kanoon (2011) and played a supporting heroine in Jayaprakash Mohanty's Bad Girl (2012). In 2015 she shared the lead with Srijala in Aa Aaa Harsaee and played a villain in Galpa Nuhen Alpa Dinara, and in 2017 she was the heroine of Loknath Barik's Tike Anadi Pura Khiladi.
She married film producer Rajesh Mallick in 2015.

facts: MKC High School, Baripada; MPC Junior College, Baripada

Q47063571.lead: Megha Ghosh is a West Bengal-born actress who works in Odia cinema, where she made her debut in Love Dot Com (2009) after an earlier Kannada film.

p: Before moving to Odia films, Ghosh appeared in a 2008 Kannada film directed by Shashank, with Yash as her co-star. Her Odia debut was Rahat Quddusi's Love Dot Com (2009), opposite Sabyasachi Mishra, and she was paired with him again in Sanjay Nayak's Sasura Ghara Zindabad.

She had three releases in 2011: Sushant Mani's Most Wanted with Anubhav Mohanty, Ashok Pati's Dosti, in which she again played Sabyasachi Mishra's heroine and Babushan's sister, and Basanta Sahu's Chandini I Miss You, which also starred Priya Choudhury. In 2012 she danced in an item song in Sushant Mani's Luchakali.
Her 2013 films were S. K. Muralidharan's Mu Aashiq Mu Awara, with Sunil Kumar, and Dillip Panda's Hari Om Hari, with Siddhanta Mahapatra. Herogiri followed in 2021.

Q29317087.lead: Jhillik Bhattacharya (also spelled Jhilik Bhattacharjee) is an actress and film producer working in Odia and Bengali cinema, who entered Odia films with Target in 2013.

p: She was born in Kolkata, West Bengal, to Mrityunjay and Sumana Bhattacharya. After a graduate degree in English she earned a postgraduate degree in Bharatanatyam; she has also trained in Kathak and in modern dance at the Shiamak Davar institute. She worked as an assistant director under Mani Ratnam and choreographed dances for a film titled Rabana.

Her film career began in Bengali with Tomaye Bhalo Bashi, followed by Classmate, Identity, Neel Lohit and Encounter. In 2013 she made her Odia debut in Target, which also introduced Mihir Das's son Amlan Das.

In 2014 she starred opposite Babushan in Sarthak Movies' Akhire Akhire, and the pair went on to make Lekhu Lekhu Lekhi Deli, Super Michhua and Jabardast Premika. She acted with Arindam Roy in Love You Hamesha and with Anubhav Mohanty in Jaga Hatare Pagha, Agastya and Baby. In 2017 she appeared with Sambit Acharya in Tamaku Dekhila Pare and played a mother in the Diwali release Tu Mo Hero, opposite Jyoti Ranjan Nayak, with whom she also starred in Kailash Mohapatra's Ole Ole Dil Bole (2018).
She produced Lahari, directed by Amartya Bhattacharyya.
Lahari, made under her production, won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia at the 72nd National Film Awards.
She married Pritiranjan Ghadai at Chilika in March 2020.

Q17581452.lead: Amiya Ranjan Patnaik (1955–2018) was an Odia film producer, director and playwright whose productions included the National Film Award-winning Hakim Babu and who directed Tulasi Apa.

p: As a student at the Regional Engineering College, Rourkela, he formed a theatre group called Technoarts and staged plays there, including Pruthaka Pruthibi and Byabhichara.

Patnaik began making films in the 1980s. Hakim Babu, directed by Pranab Das under his production, won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia at the 33rd National Film Awards as well as state honours. He made his debut as director with Mamata Mage Mula (1985), which he also produced.

Over about three decades he produced films such as Pua Moro Kala Thakura, Chaka Akhi Sabu Dekhuchhi, Asuchhi Mo Kalia Suna, Chakadola Karuchi Leela, Raja Rani and Pari Mahal, and wrote the stories of Pari Mahal and Paradesi Babu. He also made the Doordarshan serial Gotie Manara Kotie Swapna.

He returned to direction with Tulasi Apa, based on the life of social worker and Padma Shri recipient Tulasi Munda; it was his last film. In theatre, he worked on plays including Ekalabya, Palataka, Barabadhu, Nishipadma, Mruganabhi and Rudhira Kabya, and is credited with first using slow-motion technique on the Odia stage.
Tulasi Apa won Odisha State Film Awards in six categories, among them best film and best director. His staging of Byabhichara earned him a best director award at the Lok Kala Mahotsav.
He was the brother of Niranjan Patnaik and Soumya Ranjan Patnaik. He was married to Seema Patnaik, and their son is Anupam Patnaik. He died in New Delhi in 2018.

Q7409036.lead: Sambhavna Seth (born 1980) is an Indian actress, model, dancer and vlogger, known mainly for dance numbers in Bhojpuri films and for appearances on reality television.

p: Seth was born in Delhi and graduated from Maitreyi College there, after which she started modelling.

She built her career on item songs, especially in Bhojpuri films such as Roop Rang Ki Nagri, Lenga Mein Virus and Kamar Jab Lachkela, and took small parts in Hindi films including Kids No. 1, 36 China Town and Paagalpan. Her dance work earned her the nicknames Bhojpuri Helen and Dancing Queen.

In 2008 she was a contestant on Bigg Boss 2. She later took part in Raaz Pichhle Janam Ka, Dil Jeetegi Desi Girl and Welcome – Baazi Mehmaan Nawazi Ki, won the Colors dance contest Dancing Queen in 2009, finished 13th on Fear Factor: Khatron Ke Khiladi 4 in 2011 and returned for Bigg Boss Halla Bol. She also appeared in the serials Razia Sultan and Gudiya Hamari Sabhi Pe Bhari, and in 2019 entered web series with ALT Balaji's Bhojpuri drama Hero Vardiwala.
Since 2014 she has run a YouTube channel, Sambhavna Seth Entertainment, with her husband.

Q6957155.lead: Nachiketa Ghosh (1925–1976) was an Indian music director who worked mainly in Bengali cinema and also scored Hindi and Odia films, including the 1959 Odia film Shree Shree Mahalaxmi Puja.

p: Ghosh was born at Shyambazar in Calcutta into a musical household. His father, Sanat Kumar Ghosh, was a physician and a lover of classical music. He studied at the University of Calcutta.

His first film as music director was Boudir Bon (1953), and Joydeb (1954) brought him wide recognition. He often worked with the lyricists Gauriprasanna Mazumdar and Pulak Bandyopadhyay, and his music contributed to many films starring Uttam Kumar. His scores include Dhanni Meye, Mouchak, Sannyasi Raja, Nishi Padma, Stree and Bilambita Loy.

For a period he worked in Hindi films in Bombay with singers such as Lata Mangeshkar, Mohammed Rafi, Manna Dey, Kishore Kumar and Hemanta Mukhopadhyay before returning to Calcutta. In Odia cinema he scored Shree Shree Mahalaxmi Puja (1959), whose songs were sung by Hemanta Kumar, Sandhya Mukherjee and Binapani Pati. In all he directed the music for more than sixty films.
Among his well-known film songs are "Mou Bone Aaj", "Nishi Raat Banka Chand" and "Putul Nebe Go", and his non-film songs include "Ek Tajmahal Goro".
He died in Calcutta in 1976. His son is Suparna Kanti Ghosh.

facts: Mou Bone Aaj; Nishi Raat Banka Chand; Putul Nebe Go

Q3595438.lead: Ashish Vidyarthi (born 1965) is an Indian actor known for villain and character roles in over 300 films across 11 languages, including Hindi, Telugu, Tamil and Odia, where he appeared in Kalishankar (2007).

p: He was born in Delhi to Govind Vidyarthi, who catalogued and archived disappearing performing arts for the Sangeet Natak Akademi, and Reba Vidyarthi, a Kathak teacher. He studied at the National School of Drama until 1990 and worked with N. K. Sharma's theatre group Act One.

Vidyarthi moved to Bombay in 1992. His first film role was V. P. Menon in Sardar, though Drohkaal was released first and won him the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor. He also played Ashutosh in 1942: A Love Story and a villain in Is Raat Ki Subah Nahin.

His work has since spanned Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Bengali, Kannada, Malayalam, Marathi, English and Odia cinema. Outside films he co-founded AVID MINER Conversations, a set of interactive sessions for organisations, and runs a YouTube channel centred on food and travel.

Besides the National Film Award for Drohkaal, he won the Star Screen Award for best villain and a BFJA award for Is Raat Ki Subah Nahin, the Filmfare Award for Best Villain – Telugu for Athanokkade (2005) and the Nandi Award for best character actor for Minugurulu (2012). He received further nominations from Filmfare, Zee Cine and SIIMA.

Q18579001.lead: Sarada Prasanna Nayak (1926–2020), also written Naik, was an Odia film director, lyricist and playwright whose films Lakshmi, Kaa and Stree won President's awards and who received the Jayadeva Puraskar in 2013.

p: Nayak was born in Dhuliswar village in the Bayalisha Mauja area of the then Cuttack district, to Basudev and Sebati Nayak; his father managed the Manmohan Press. He attended Victoria School (now Bhaktamadhu Vidyapitha) in Cuttack and then Ravenshaw College, where his interest in drama took shape.

Encouraged towards drama by Suren Mohanty, he played a supporting lead in a radio play directed by Manoranjan Das after All India Radio, Cuttack, opened in 1948. From 1951 he wrote dialogue for, directed and set music to plays, among them Sankhali, Sunamati and Parishodha, and he wrote his first songs for Das's play Abhilasha. In 1973 he was the only Indian on a programme in London, where his screenplay Brotherly Love, centred on Bharata from the Ramayana, was staged.

Prompted by Lokanath Mishra and after studying film studios in Calcutta, he entered cinema by writing the screenplay of Bhakta Kabi Jayadeba and serving as its co-director. At a time when most Odia films were directed by Bengali film-makers, he made Lakshmi (1962) under the pseudonym Siddhartha, on borrowed money of about 95,000 rupees; it ran for 100 days. He followed it with Kaa (1966), Stree (1968), Sansar (1971) and Tamasa Teere (1988), and named V. Shantaram as his inspiration. He also remained active in radio and on Doordarshan.

His films Lakshmi, Kaa and Stree earned President's awards. The Odisha government gave him the Jayadeva Puraskar, its highest honour for Odia cinema, in 2013; his other honours included the Natyashree, Banichitra and Chinta O Chetana awards.
His brother was Swarup Nayak, his sister Parbati Ghosh, and her husband Gour Ghosh. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2020.

facts: Swarup Nayak (brother); Parbati Ghosh (sister); Gour Ghosh (brother-in-law)

Q770376.lead: Nitai Palit (1923–1990), born Nityananda Palit, was an Odia film director, producer, writer and actor whose Malajahna (1965) won the national award for direction.

p: Palit was born in Cuttack to Nagendranath Palit and Sarojini Devi and studied at Ravenshaw Collegiate School. Drawn to drama and music from childhood, he joined the stage and gradually taught himself the craft of film-making.

In 1954 he made Kedar Gouri together with playwright Manoranjan Das, acting in it as well as directing. He then made Bhai Bhai on his own, and its success led him to leave the theatre for cinema full-time, producing through his company Creative Movies Productions.

His films as director include Maa (1959), Malajahna (1965), for which he also wrote the screenplay, Kie Kahara (1968), Bandhan (1969), Dharitri, Mana Akasha (1974), Krushna Sudama (1976), Bandhu Mohanty (1977), Anuraag (1980), Kie Jite Kie Hare (1981) and the telefilm Usha (1987). He was working on Kichhi Asha Kichhi Swapna at the time of his death.

Malajahna brought him the President's award and the Silver Lotus for best direction, the first time an Odia film was so recognised. He won the Odisha State Film Award for best director in 1972, 1975, 1977 and 1982, and received the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi award and the Jayadeva Samman in 1982. The Nitai Palit Award for Odia cinema is named after him.
He had six daughters. Besides films he enjoyed reading, writing poetry, painting and playing the tabla. He died in Cuttack in 1990.

Q15724980.lead: Mohammad Mohsin (1942–2003) was an Odia film director, producer, writer and actor who directed Phula Chandana (1982) and other commercially successful Odia films over a career of more than 30 years.

p: Mohsin was born in Cuttack to Mohammad Ayub and Amina Bibi. He studied at Sayeed Seminary High School and took a BA at Ravenshaw College, where he was elected secretary of the Dramatic Society. He went on to perform with the Annapurna Theatre in Cuttack.

He worked as an assistant director on Hindi films in Mumbai and made his Hindi acting debut as Karim in Rajshri Productions' Naiyya, a remake of the Odia film Shesha Shrabana. Back in Odisha he was associate director to Prashanta Nanda on Shesha Shrabana, Balidan, Maa O Mamata, Puja and Hisab Nikas, and also acted, with roles such as Bagha in Hisab Nikas, Raka in Maa O Mamata and a teacher turned social reformer in Balidan.

Producer Batakrushna Nayak of Baripada gave him his first independent direction with Phula Chandana in 1982. He went on to direct 16 films and act in more than 14, also working on stories, screenplays, dialogue and production. His films ranged from social dramas to crime thrillers and include Danda Balunga, Jaga Hatare Pagha, Sahari Bagha, Laxmana Rekha and Santana.
He won the Odisha State Film Award for best director for Phula Chandana (1982).
He was married to Kausra Khatun, and their son is Abrar. He died in Cuttack in 2003.

facts: Sayeed Seminary High School; Ravenshaw College (BA)

Q55973615.lead: Neetu Singh is an Odia television and film actress, best known for the title role in the ETV Odia serial Gayatri, who has also played supporting parts in Odia films since Rangila Toka (2012).

p: Singh was born in Puri and has an elder sister and a younger brother. She trained in Odissi dance and performed on various stages, and also learned sand art from Sudarsan Pattnaik, tabla and sitar, and pattachitra painting. She worked as an Odissi dancer with the Song and Drama Division.

She appeared in many Odia devotional videos and in saree advertisements. Her first television serial was Jai Santoshi Maa on DD Odia, for which Srikant Gautam cast her after seeing her dance on stage; she has credited Prashanta Nanda with helping her on the show.

She played Gayatri, the heroine of ETV Odia's Gayatri, directed by Mihir Swain, which ran to more than 1,500 episodes. In 2016 she acted in Tulasi on Colors Odia, and in 2017 she took the supporting role of Padmaja, a mother-in-law, in Nuabohu on Tarang TV.

In films, she made her debut in Rangila Toka (2012) as the wife of Siddhanta Mahapatra's character, with Papu Pom Pom and Debjani in the leads, and later acted in Sarthak Movies' Sapanara Pathe Pathe (2017), starring Amlan Das.
She married soon after Gayatri began airing and has a daughter.

facts: Odissi dance; sand art under Sudarsan Pattnaik

Q104909292.lead: Rabi Mishra (died 2021) was an Odia actor in films, television and theatre, known for comic roles and above all for playing Gopala Bhanda in the DD Odia series Gopala Rahasya.

p: Mishra was born in Jajpur. He began acting in college, where as an undergraduate he played a Marwari character in a college play.

His film debut came in 1979 in Ramayan, produced by Dhira Biswal, in which he played Sugriva; he later said that his background in wrestling won him the part. He went on to act in more than 70 Odia films in positive, villainous and character roles, including Bhai Hela Bhagari, Sakala Tirtha To Charane, Saubhagyabati and Dhauli Express.

On television he acted in Kalikati Chenka, the first serial on DD Odia, and in 29 DD Odia serials in all. His portrayal of Jadumani in the 1991 New Year programme Darpana marked a turning point, and his Gopala Bhanda in Gopala Rahasya (1994) made him a household name. He also worked in CD films and stage plays, and at the time of his death was playing a grandfather in the Zee Sarthak serial Hey Prabhu.
He received the Odisha State Film Award for Laxmira Abhisara (1998).
He died in Bhubaneswar in 2021 at the age of 64.

facts: Gopala Bhanda in Gopala Rahasya (DD Odia)

Q15725113.lead: Raju Mishra (1949–2020), born Raj Gopal Mishra, was an Odia film director, cinematographer, actor, screenwriter and music director who directed 12 Odia films, beginning with Jor Jar Mulak Tar (1986).

p: Mishra was born in Gopabandhu Nagar, Jatani, into a musical family: his father, Bimal Mishra, played the tabla and his mother, Sumati Devi, was a singer, both recognised artists of All India Radio, Cuttack. He had no formal musical training but taught himself the harmonium. After studying at Jatani High School and Nirakarpur College, his interest in photography took him to the Film and Television Institute of India, Pune, where he won a gold medal in cinematography.

His first work as a cinematographer was on the Marathi film Sarvasakshi, which won a National Film Award. He entered Odia films in 1978, acting in Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja, and in Ulka (1981) he acted while also serving as cinematographer and composer. He went on to work as cinematographer or director on more than 20 films in Odia, Hindi, Assamese, Marathi and Bengali, including seven Assamese films as director.

As a director in Odia he made 12 films, among them Jor Jar Mulak Tar, Chaka Akhi Sabu Dekhuchi, Pua Moro Kala Thakura, Asuchhi Mo Kalia Suna, Haribhai Harena and Jibana Mrutyu; his last was Kotiere Gotie Mana. He also wrote screenplays, edited and composed music for some films.
He received the Jayadeva Award and the Fitfat Bioscope Award in 2012, and the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Award in 2020.
He was married to Pratima Manjari Mishra, and they had two sons, Mohit and Punit. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2020.

Q7283589.lead: Rahul Dev (born 1968) is an Indian actor and former model who works in Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali and Odia films; his Odia films include Premi No.1, Mahanayak and Shatru Sanghar.

p: Born Rahul Dev Kaushal in New Delhi, he is the son of Hari Dev, an Assistant Commissioner of Police, and studied at St. Columba's School, Delhi. As a youth he played cricket for Delhi at under-19 level, then studied engineering; in his final year in 1993 fashion designer Rohit Khosla encouraged him to model.
Dev modelled from 1994 to 2002, appearing in advertisements for brands such as Tata and Raymond, and in 1994 also set up a leather-garment export company, Rap Overseas.

His film debut as the villain in Champion (2000) brought him a Filmfare nomination for Best Villain. He played the assassin Sheik Imran in the Malayalam film Sagar Alias Jacky Reloaded (2009) and later appeared in the Punjabi film Dharti, Sringaravelan and the Bhojpuri film Dulhan Chahi Pakistan Se 2. In 2013 he made his television debut as the demon Arunasur in Devon Ke Dev...Mahadev, and he was later a contestant on Bigg Boss 10.
His younger brother is actor Mukul Dev. His wife Rina died in 2009; they have a son, Siddhant. As of 2020 his partner was model and actress Mugdha Godse.

Q15723603.lead: Ajit Das (1949–2020) was an Odia film actor, stage director and playwright whose screen career began with the 1976 film Sindura Bindu and spanned more than four decades.

p: Das was born in Karanjia in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha. He was drawn to theatre as a child after watching the plays staged by a family elder, Sudhir Chandra Das, who ran a drama troupe in Mayurbhanj. He completed a bachelor's degree in arts in 1971 and later earned a diploma in acting from the National School of Drama in 1975.

He entered Odia cinema in 1976 as the villain of Sindura Bindu, a period film set in the 16th century and directed by Dhir Biswal. In the years that followed he appeared in a large number of Odia films, both as a leading man and in character parts, including Megha Mukti, Devajani, Baata Abaata, Aashar Akash and Hakim Babu. The title of Hakim Babu (1985) became a nickname that stayed with him.

Away from feature films he acted on Doordarshan and in stage productions. He headed a department at Utkal Sangeet Natak Mahavidyalaya and founded a theatre institute, the Abhinaya Jagruti Institute of Theatre (AJIT), through which he staged plays and trained actors.
He received the Odisha State Film Award in 1985 for Hakim Babu.
He was married to Maya Das. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2020, aged 71.

facts: National School of Drama (diploma in acting, 1975)

Q15725319.lead: Shantiraj Khosla (1966–2021) was an Odia music director and singer who composed songs for Odia films from 2002 onward and won the Odisha State Film Award for his music in Pheria.

p: Khosla was born in Jeypore in Koraput district, Odisha, to Martin and Sabitri Khosla, and studied at Vikram Dev College in Jeypore.

A guitar and mandolin player, he began performing on All India Radio (Akashvani) at Jeypore. He then moved to Cuttack, trained in Hindustani classical music and started composing for Odia albums and devotional bhajans.

His first film as composer was Wrong Number (2002), directed by Bobby Islam. Over the next two decades he scored more than 20 films, among them To Bina Mo Kahani Adha, Mu Sapanara Soudagar, Dhanare Rakhibu Sapatha Mora, Mate Ani Dela Lakhye Faguna, Don, Baisi Pahache Kheliba Mina, ACP Ranveer and Jai Hind, and he is credited with around 2,000 songs for Odia albums. His last album, Jhipi Jhipi Barsha, came out in September 2021, after his death.
In 2019 he received the Odisha State Film Award for best music direction (for the 2018 awards year) for the film Pheria.
He was married to Sagarika Khosla and had a daughter, Shruti Prasarini. He died in Cuttack in 2021.

Q50220690.lead: Tamanna Vyas (born 1996) is an Odia film actress from Berhampur who has also worked in Telugu cinema. Her early Odia films include Bhaina Kana Kala Se, Nijhum Ratira Sathi, Prem Kumar and Blackmail.

p: Vyas was born and grew up in Berhampur (Brahmapur), Odisha, where she completed her schooling and college education; she studied at Khallikote College and holds a degree in business administration. She first became known through reality television on Sarthak TV, finishing as runner-up in the second season of Mu Bi Hebi Heroine and placing in the Raja Queen show in 2015.

Her first film shoot was the comedy Joker, opposite Papu Pom Pom, which was never released. Her screen debut therefore came with Bhaina Kana Kala Se (2016), opposite Balakrushna, followed by Nijhum Ratira Sathi (2017) opposite Jyoti Ranjan Nayak; both were directed by Sanjay Nayak.

In 2018 she appeared with Anubhav Mohanty in Prem Kumar: Salesman of the Year and with Ardhendu in Blackmail, and played the female lead in the Telugu film Shatru. That year she also reached the top 10 of the Miss Diva contest in Mumbai, where she received a popular-choice model award.

Q56666399.lead: Asit Pati (born 1960) is an Odia film actor, producer, writer and director, known mainly for supporting and villain roles. He made his debut in Chinha Achinha (1979) and later entered Odisha politics.

p: Pati began acting in Odia cinema in 1979 with Chinha Achinha. Over the following decades he worked in more than 40 films, usually as a supporting actor or antagonist; his credits include Maanini, Tike Hasa Tike Luha, Ram Rahim, Jaga Hatare Pagha, Sata Kebe Luchi Rahena, Hakim Babu, Ei Aama Sansar, Jor Jar Mulak Tar, Jayadeb and Chaka Akhi Sau Dekhuchhi.

He also turned producer for films such as Maa Kande Aaji Puate Pain, Katha Rahigala Kala Kalaku, Gopare Badhuchi Kalakanhei and Revenge. He directed Maa Kande Aaji Puate Pain and Katha Rahigala Kala Kalaku, and wrote the story of the latter.

During Biju Patnaik's time he was a worker of the Utkal Congress, and Patnaik later arranged a job for him at Paradip Port. In 2017 he joined the Biju Janata Dal at Naveen Niwas in the presence of party founder Naveen Patnaik, together with actor Uttam Mohanty.
He is married to Anjana Pati and has a daughter, Ankita Pati.

facts: Maa Kande Aaji Puate Pain; Katha Rahigala Kala Kalaku

Q28922013.lead: Lipi Mahapatra, known as Lipi, is an Odia actress who has appeared in some 3,000 music albums and in Odia films such as Om Shanti Om, Tu Mori Paeen, Bad Girl, Daddy and Mimansa, and has also worked in television.

p: Born Sushree Sangeeta Mahapatra in Berhampur, Odisha, she is the daughter of Subash Chandra Mahapatra, a police officer who hoped she would join the IPS, and Bandana Mahapatra, a film actress. Drawn to dance and acting from childhood, she trained in Odissi dance. She graduated from Mahamayee Mahila Mahavidyalaya in Berhampur.

Album director Jayaprakash Mohanty gave Lipi her first music-video role, in Mu Bina Ghungurare Nachibi. She went on to appear in more than 3,000 albums, worked with most of the leading album actors of the period and earned the nickname 'Album Queen'; Jai Phula is among her best-known albums.

Her film debut came in 2005 with Prashant Nanda's Om Shanti Om. She then played the lead in two films directed by Jayaprakash Mohanty, Tu Mori Paeen (2008) and Bad Girl (2012), the latter alongside Mihir Das and Babli. Later releases included Daddy, opposite Arindam Roy, Mimansa and Galpa Nuhen Alpa Dinara. She made her Hindi film debut in Adibhumi with Manoj Mishra.

On television she presented Ananya and Apananka Pasanda on ETV Odia and served as a judge on Doordarshan programmes. She played the lead in a serial adaptation of Kanhu Charan Mohanty's novel Ka and in the mega-serial Tara Tarini on Tarang TV, and in Rakta Samparka on Manjari TV. On Zee Sarthak she hosted Didi No. 1 and judged Raja Queen and Dance Odisha Dance.

knownFor: Tu mori paeen-The Last Love Story (2009)
facts: Mu Bina Ghungurare Nachibi, Jai Phula

Q6959697.lead: Naina Das (also spelled Naina Dash) is an Odia actress and television presenter who has worked in Odia films and serials as well as in Telugu, Bengali and Chhattisgarhi cinema.

p: Das was born in Bhubaneswar, Odisha. She graduated from Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya, where she studied Odissi vocal music, and later completed a master's degree in public relations and marketing at the Regional College of Management.

She started out as a presenter, hosting a music programme on O TV at a young age, and in 2002 began acting in the Doordarshan serial Duhita; she also played leading and supporting roles in serials such as Suna Kalasa. For several years she presented Kalyani, a long-running health programme on Odia television.

Her first Odia film was Maa Mangala, after which she appeared in Sashu Ghara Chalijibi, Puja Pain Phulatie, Munna - A Love Story and Bahudibe Mo Jaga Balia. Outside Odia cinema she acted in Telugu films, one Bengali film and two Chhattisgarhi films, and she featured in Odia music albums including Deunchi Mo Baan Aakhi.
After her marriage she stepped back from acting for some years and served as a mentor on Zee Sarthak's Grihalakshmi. In 2022 she returned in the lead role of the serial Shanti on Star Kiran.

Her honours include a best supporting actress award for Duhita (2002), an Odisha state-level Sadbhavana Award (2004), Best Anchor of the Year from AB Visuals (2004) and ETV Odia's Most Wanted Anchor (2005).
She married Siddharth Tiwari in 2011.

facts: Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya; Regional College of Management

Q4700329.lead: Akash Dasnayak, known in films simply as Akash, is an Odia film actor and politician noted for action films. He debuted in Kalinga Putra (2008) and has represented Korei in the Odisha Legislative Assembly.

p: He was born in Jajpur district, Odisha, to Mayadhar and Indira Das, and earned an LLB from Vyasanagar College, Jajpur Road, under Utkal University.

Akash entered Odia cinema in 2008 with Kalinga Putra, which brought him a best actor award. His later films include Satyameba Jayate, Shatru Sanghar, Subha Vivaha, Asibu Kebe Saji Mo Rani, Aalo Mora Kandhei, Raju Awara, Shapath, Dharma, Hari Om Hari, Mita Basichi Mu Bhuta Sathire (made in 3D), Tu Kahibu Na Mu, Agastya, Just Mohabbat and Herogiri. He has also acted in Bengali films.

Standing for the Biju Janata Dal, he won the Korei Assembly seat in the 2014 election and served until 2019. He joined the Bharatiya Janata Party on 1 April 2024 and became the Korei MLA again from 2024.
He received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor for 2008.
His aunt, Anita Das, is a film actress. He is married to Subhrajyoti (Mamuni).

Q56512721.lead: Koel Mishra (born Koel Banerjee) is an actress from West Bengal who works in Odia cinema. She debuted in Tu Tha Mun Jauchi Rushi (2010) and later married actor Bobby Mishra.

p: She was born in West Bengal, went to school in Konnagar and then studied at the University of Calcutta.

Her first Odia film was Tu Tha Mun Jauchi Rushi (2010), directed by Sritam Das with Arindam Roy in the lead. The same year she appeared opposite Debashish Patra in Tate Bhala Pauchi Boli, directed by Prashant Kumar.

In 2011 she acted in Anam Charan Sahu's Mana Mora Prajapati, led by Deepak Barik, and played the heroine opposite Babushan in Ashok Pati's 1 4 3 I Love You. In 2012 she starred with Buddhaditya Mohanty in Om Sai Ram, the last Odia film directed by Hara Patnaik.
She was paired with Papu Pom Pom in R. Bhagat Singh's Ame Ta Toka Shanda Marka (2014) and with Sambit Acharya in Ashiq (2015), directed by Sudhakar Vasant.
After starting her career in Odia films she married actor Bobby Mishra.

Q15724003.lead: Gurukrushna Goswami (1934–2018) was an Odia lyricist, poet and film dialogue writer who wrote around 2,000 songs for radio, television, films and albums over a career of more than five decades.

p: Goswami was born in Nuagaon in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, and grew up in his maternal grandfather's home, where his grandfather, a music lover, gave him his first lessons. He later studied music with Banchhanidhi Panda and Kshitish Chandra Maitra. He originally wanted to be a singer, but while at college in 1952 he began writing songs with encouragement from Santanu Mahapatra.

He became an approved lyricist of All India Radio in 1956, an approved music director there in 1986, and an approved Hindi lyricist from 1993. He wrote his first film songs for the Odia film Maa (1959) and first drew attention with the songs and dialogue of Arundhati. In all he contributed lyrics and dialogue to more than 30 Odia films, and his partnership with composer Santanu Mahapatra produced many popular film songs. He is also credited with script writing and music direction.

Encouraged by Lata Mangeshkar, he learned Hindi and began writing songs in that language. His published song-poem collections include E Mana Chorapathe, Samudunii Mora Juhara Janiba, Abani Gandha, Jagadihudi, Namami Janmabhoomi and Champaka Barani Go, as well as a Hindi collection, He Jagannath Tujhe Pranam.

He received the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award (2004) for Champaka Barani Go, the Bhaktakabi Salabega Award (2000), the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (2000) and a best lyricist award (1996), along with honours from the Utkal Sahitya Kala Parishad, the Odisha Geetikabi Samaj and the Balakrushna Das Foundation (Geeti Saraswati Samman).
He was married to the Odia singer Arati Goswami. He died in Shivaji Nagar, Cuttack, in 2018.

Q14797879.lead: Haraprasad Das is an Odia poet, essayist and columnist and a retired civil servant. He received the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1999 and the Moortidevi Award in 2013.

p: Das was born in Banapur, Odisha, and completed a master's degree at Utkal University.

He joined government service in 1968 and worked in Odisha, West Bengal, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir and Delhi, spending the longest stretch in the Union Ministry of Labour. His posts included Accountant General of Odisha and Principal Accountant General of Bihar, and he has also worked as a consultant and expert for United Nations bodies.

As a writer he has published a dozen or more books of poetry along with prose works, translations and a work of fiction. His titles include Harmoniumre Todi, Garbhagruha, Mantrapatha, Vamsha, Durataara Bhrama and Nastikara Bhaktikabita. He translated Rabindranath Tagore's Gitanjali and Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat into Odia, rendered the Bhagavad Gita in the Odia nabakshari metre, and has written in Hindi as well.

His honours include the Sahitya Akademi Award (1999) for Garbhagruha, the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award (1993) for Mantrapatha, the Moortidevi Award (2013) for Vamsha, the Gangadhar Meher Award (2008), the Sarala Award, the Kalinga Literary Award (2017) and the Bishuba Award (2020).

Q5320710.lead: Sabyasachi Mohapatra (born 1950) is an Odia film director, producer and screenwriter whose films include Bhukha, Bou, Jai Jagannatha, Sala Budha, Adima Bichara and Pahada Ra Luha. He runs the production house Mohapatra Movie Magic.

p: He was born in Lehedi, Odisha, to Kapileswar Prasad Mohapatra, a novelist, and Bishnupriya Mohapatra.

Mohapatra's first film as director was Bhukha (1989), made in the Sambalpuri language, which received the International Jury award at the Gijón film festival in Spain. His other directing credits include Sabu Mayare Baya (1986), Jhili, Bou (1998) and Bahudibe Mo Jaga Balia (2003).

Jai Jagannatha, a mythological film made on a large budget, was released in 15 Indian languages. After a long break he returned with Sala Budha (2012), adapted from a novel by his father; it was shown at the International Film Festival of India in Goa in 2013 and collected seven Odisha State Film Awards, among them best actor.

His Sambalpuri-language Adima Bichara (2014) won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Odia at the 62nd National Film Awards, together with best director and best actor at the 26th Odisha State Film Awards. Pahada Ra Luha (2015) won the same national award the following year, at the 63rd ceremony.

At the Odisha State Film Awards, Bou won best film, best director and best screenplay in 1998, and Bahudibe Mo Jaga Balia won best film and best director in 2003. He was given the Kalinga Ratna title in 2016 and the Ganakabi Samman by the Ganakabi Baishnab Pani Jayanti Committee in 2017, and has also received the Odisha Living Legend Award and a Sambhabana award.
His father, Kapileswar Prasad Mohapatra, wrote the novel on which Sala Budha is based.

facts: Best Odia Feature Film (Adima Bichara; Pahada Ra Luha)

Q31319988.lead: Ananta Patnaik (1912–1987) was an Odia poet, writer and translator. In Odia cinema he wrote the story, screenplay, songs and dialogue of the 1950 film Saptasajya.

p: Patnaik was born in Chanahat, then in undivided Puri and now in Khordha district, and lost both parents in childhood. He began writing poems as a ninth-grade pupil at Ravenshaw Collegiate School, where he persuaded his teachers to let him start and edit a school magazine, Chhatrabandhu. He passed the matriculation examination in 1930.

Because of his revolutionary verse he was at first refused a place at Ravenshaw College; during this period he took part in the Salt Satyagraha, singing patriotic songs to rally the protesters. He was admitted to the college in 1931 and there turned towards leftist ideas.

He played a leading part in setting up the Congress Socialist Party in Odisha and was managing editor of the journal of its literary body, the Nabajuga Sahitya Sansad, which ran for six months; he wrote for it under pen names such as Atanu, Bodhisattva, Kumari Jasodhara and Priyadarshi.

His poetry collections include Raktashikha (1936, with Sachi Routray), Tarpana Kare Aaji, Shanti Shikha, Kinchit, Alodaa Lodaa, Chhaira Chhita and Abantara (1979). He also wrote children's books and plays, and translated Maxim Gorky's The Mother, Mikhail Sholokhov's Fate of a Man and Walt Whitman's Leaves of Grass into Odia. For the screen, he wrote the story, screenplay, songs and dialogue of Saptasajya (1950).
He received the Soviet Land Nehru Award in 1965 and the Sahitya Akademi Award in 1980 for Abantara.
He was married to Niradprabha Patnaik.

Q28946536.lead: Namrata Das, also known as Dolly, is an Odia film and television actress best known for supporting roles as a mother or grandmother. She debuted in Dharitri (1973) and has worked on stage, radio and television as well.

p: Das was born in Alapua in Kendrapara district, Odisha, into a Karan family whose grandfather had been a zamindar. Her mother died when she was a child, and her father, who later remarried, also died some years afterwards; with her elder sister already married, she took up acting as a profession to support the household. She finished school and college in her village before the family moved to Cuttack, where her father worked.

She started acting in school plays at the age of nine or ten, encouraged by her father and her elder sister Manaswini. While she was playing Shakuntala in a production of Dushmanta-Shakuntala at Cuttack's Kala Bikash Kendra, producer Dhir Biswal and Chitrapuri magazine editor Basant Patnaik were in the audience; Biswal then cast her in Dharitri (1973), her first film.

Her later films include Kanakalata, Krushna Sudama, Balidan, Ramayan and Kaberi. Over her career she has appeared in a very large number of Odia films, as well as three Bengali films, many stage plays and serials for radio and television.

She won a state award for best supporting actress for Lakshmi Pratima (1998) and received the Bhumi Kanya award in January 2020 for her contribution to Odia cinema. She has also received the Mohan Sundar Dev Goswami award.

facts: Best supporting actress (Lakshmi Pratima, 1998); Bhumi Kanya (2020)

Q56683041.lead: Pupinder Singh is an Odia film actor and producer, television and stage presenter, and former music-album performer. He began acting in films in 2008 with To Bina Bhala Lagena and first played a lead in Subha Vivaha (2010).

p: Singh started out dancing to Odia and Sambalpuri songs in music albums, including the popular album Jai Phula. His first film was To Bina Bhala Lagena (2008), in which he was second lead to Sabyasachi Mishra, and he had a small part in Love Dot Com (2009).

In 2010 he moved into production with Subha Vivaha, which was also his first film as a lead actor; Barsha Priyadarshini played the heroine and Akash Dasnayak the second lead. He went on to produce and star in Kichhi Khata Kichhi Mitha, Jaggu Autowala and Samaya Bada Balaban. In 2013 he co-produced Daha Balunga with Aparajita Mohanty, starring Babushan Mohanty with Hindi actor Jackie Shroff as the villain.

On television he has acted in Odia serials and hosted Wow and Full Bobal on ETV Odia and Jeenar Jeevan Sathi on Tarang TV. He reached the final of the first season of the dance contest Dance Challenge on ETV Odia, judged Mu Bi Heroine Hebi and served as a mentor on Raja Queen, both on Sarthak TV.
He is married to Rupinder Kaur, who works with his production company.

facts: Subha Vivaha; Kichhi Khata Kichhi Mitha; Jaggu Autowala; Daha Balunga; Samaya Bada Balaban

Q15725231.lead: Srikant Gautam is an Odia lyricist, actor, dialogue writer and director. Active in Odia films since 1979, he wrote songs for many films before directing Mitha Mitha (2017).

p: Gautam's acting credits go back to Mathura Bijaya (1979), in which he played Krishna, and include Dora, Bagula Baguli, Panchu Pandav, Jaa Devi Sarbabhuteshu, Pathara Khasuchi Bada Deulu, Pacheri Uthila Majhi Duaru, Aemiti Bhai Jagate Nahin, Bapa and Ei Akhi Ama Sakhi. Later he played Commissioner Abhinabh Sharma in One Way Traffic (2014) and Rama Hari Dash in Mitha Mitha (2017).

As a lyricist he wrote songs for films including Sakhi Rahila Ae Singha Duara, Rakata Kahiba Kie Kahara, Santana, Bou, Rahichi Rahibi Tori Paain, Rakhi Bandhili Mo Rakhiba Mana, Aakhi Palakare Tu, Raja Jhia Sathe Heigala Bhaba, Paribeni Kehi Alaga Kari, One Way Traffic and Raghupati Raghaba Rajaram. He also wrote dialogue for several films, and both story and dialogue for One Way Traffic and Mitha Mitha. He also works in Odia music albums. Mitha Mitha marked his debut as a director.
Actor and director Prashant Nanda is his elder brother.

Q18912880.lead: Lokanath Misra (1922–2009) was an Indian politician from Odisha who served as Governor of Assam and sat in the Rajya Sabha. Early in life he played the male lead in Lalita (1949), one of the earliest Odia films.

p: Misra was born in Banapur, Khordha, the elder son of the poet and socialist Pandit Godabarish Mishra.
In Odia cinema he is remembered for playing the hero, Vidyapati, in Lalita (1949), the second Odia film.

In politics he began in the Indian National Congress, later moved to the Swatantra Party and then to the Janata Party. He was a member of the Constituent Assembly and represented Odisha in the Rajya Sabha from 1960 to 1978. He was Governor of Assam from March 1991 to September 1997, briefly held the governorship of Arunachal Pradesh in March 1991, and also had additional charge of Nagaland from April 1992.
He was married to Binapani Misra; their son Pinaki Misra became a Lok Sabha member for Puri. His younger brother Ranganath Misra was Chief Justice of India. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2009.

facts: Governor of Assam (1991–1997); Rajya Sabha member (1960–1978)

Q4818791.lead: Atul Kulkarni (born 1965) is an Indian actor, screenwriter and producer whose films span Hindi, Marathi, Kannada, Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu and English. Hey Ram and Chandni Bar each brought him the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor.

p: A native of Belgaum in Karnataka, he started acting on stage in high school and was a regular at the Maharashtra State Drama Competition, collecting acting and direction prizes from 1989 to 1992. He performed in the play Gandhi Viruddh Gandhi and, as a student, worked with Natya Aradhana, an amateur theatre company in Solapur. He enrolled in engineering at the College of Engineering, Pune, but dropped out in the first year, and in 1995 he completed his acting diploma at the National School of Drama, New Delhi.

Hey Ram, Chandni Bar, Rang De Basanti (2006) and Natarang (2010) are among the films he is known for. He wrote the screenplay for Laal Singh Chaddha, the authorised remake of Forrest Gump. The Vienna Independent Film Festival named him Best Actor in 2019 for Murder on the Road to Kathmandu.

He heads the Quest Education Support Trust, which trains teachers and runs workshops in Maharashtra to help children aged 3 to 14 from marginalised communities, and he has taken part in a project to green 24 acres of barren land in Satara district.
He won the National Film Award for Best Supporting Actor twice, for Hey Ram and for Chandni Bar.
His wife, the theatre actress Geetanjali Kulkarni, was a fellow student at the National School of Drama.

facts: National School of Drama, New Delhi
Hindi, Marathi, Kannada, Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, English

Q15724403.lead: Narayan Prasad Singh (1933–2018), honoured with the title Rasaraj, was an Odia poet and lyricist who wrote songs for more than 100 Odia films, beginning with Nua Bou in 1962.

p: Singh was born in Koil, Asureswar, to Bihari Lal Singh and Sarojini Devi. Encouraged by his literature teacher Golak Chandra Pradhan at the Asureswar school, he began writing poetry in the eighth grade.

In 1950 he was invited to read his poems on All India Radio, Cuttack. A few years later he came to know Kalicharan Patnaik, from whom he learned how to shape poems into songs, and in 1960 he became an approved lyricist of All India Radio.

His film career began in 1962 with Nua Bou, whose song 'Ratha Ja Chali Ja' was his first for the screen. Over the following decades he worked on films such as Manika Jodi, Jeevan Sathi, Amada Bata, Bhai Bhauja, Stree, Adina Megha, Dharitri, Ghara Sansar, Kanakalata, Krushna Sudama, Sankha Mahuri, Pipasa, Chinha Achinha, Mathura Bijaya, Aliva Daga, Kasturi and Gare Sindura Dhare Luha. His well-known film songs include 'Jibana Jamunare Juara Uthe Re' (Amada Bata), 'Prabhu Padatale Pranati Dhale' (Ghara Sansar) and 'Chhai Chhabeli Ranga Rameli' (Chinha Achinha).
His published song collections include Priti Prajapati, Thiapuchi Naranga, Dui Akhira Kabita, Bandhu Bhara Basundhara, Nibedana, Megha Phaguna and Chitrageeti, a collection of his Odia film songs.

He received the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award in 2003 and the Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja Samman in 2011, along with honours from the Odisha Film Development Corporation, the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi, the Utkal Sahitya Samaj and the Odisha government's culture department, among others.
He was married to Parbati.

facts: Ratha Ja Chali Ja; Jibana Jamunare Juara Uthe Re; Chhai Chhabeli Ranga Rameli

Q4790714.lead: Arindam Roy (also spelled Arindam Ray) is an Odia film actor and politician who has also appeared in a few Bengali films. He debuted in Prema Rutu Asilare (2006) and has twice won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor.

p: Roy was born in Cuttack to Gopal Chandra Ray, in a Karan family, and studied at Utkal University.

He began his film career in 2006 with Prema Rutu Asilare. His Odia films since then include E Mana Manena, Kalishankar, Lal Tuku Tuku Sadhaba Bahu, Mu Sapanara Soudagar, Mitare Mita, Tu Tha Mun Jauchi Rushi, Hero, Criminal, Gud Boy, Raja Jhia Sathe Heigala Bhaba, Parshuram, Ashok Samrat, Mu Raja Tu Rani, Daddy, Kalki, Bhaunri, Tora Dine Ku Mora Dine and Romeo Juliet.

When he moved into Bengali cinema he briefly used the screen name Rishi before reverting to his own name. Reviewing his Bengali film Target Kolkata, a critic praised his acting but advised him to improve his Bengali diction. His Odia film Babu Bhaijan was his last release before the COVID-19 pandemic; afterwards came RAM, the fourth film from his family banner, Ratna Films.
Formerly associated with the Biju Janata Dal, he contested the Salipur seat in the 2024 Odisha Assembly election as a Bharatiya Janata Party candidate and lost to the BJD candidate by 7,594 votes.

He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor for Prema Rutu Asilare (2006) and for Mu Raja Tu Rani (2013), and the ETV Odia award for best actor for Raja Jhia Sathe Heigala Bhaba (2012). He was nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Actor (Odia) for Ashok Samrat.
He is married to Anupa Das and they have a son.
