Q56395452.lead: Sivani Sangita (born 2000) is an Odia film actress from Cuttack who started as a child artist in television and films and became a leading lady in 2017 with Sister Sridevi.

p: Sangita's first screen role was in the Doordarshan Odia serial Uttaradayee. She then played the young version of the heroine in Debi on Tarang TV, and her final serial as a child was Badhu on Sarthak TV, in which she played the daughter of Sukant Rath's character; she left that show when she was offered a lead film role.
Her film work as a child began with Mitare Mita (2009), followed by Pahili Raja, Gud Boy, Mita Basichi Mu Bhuta Sathire and Lekhu Lekhu Lekhi Deli.

Her first film as a heroine was Ashok Pati's Sister Sridevi, released at Raja in 2017, opposite Babushan Mohanty. In 2018 she starred with Anubhav Mohanty in Tapas Sargharia's Prem Kumar, whose planned Raja release was pushed to Durga Puja after Mohanty was injured. She played opposite Arindam Roy in Babu Bhaijan (2020) and again with Babushan Mohanty in Bidyarana.
For the 2019 Odisha Assembly election, the State Election Commission chose her as one of the faces of its voter-awareness campaign.
She received the Filmfare Award for Best Actress (Odia) in 2019 for Prem Kumar.

Q5010538.lead: Ravi Kinagi (also Rabi Kinagi or Rabi Kinnagi) is an Indian film director and screenwriter who has worked mainly in Bengali and Odia cinema. His Odia films include Maanini, Suna Chadhei, Paradeshi Chadhei and Bhai Hela Bhagari.

p: Kinagi was born into a Kannada-speaking family and learned the basics of filmmaking from his father, the producer and director Shankar Kinagi.

He worked with Rajshri Productions on Paheli, Naiyya and Kanoon Ka Shikar, and assisted directors S. Ramanathan, Anil Ganguly and Prashant Nanda, the last on Hindi films. After directing two Marathi films, Manuski and Halahal, he came to Odisha to make Odia films.

His first Odia film as director was Maanini. He went on to direct Suna Chadhei, Paradeshi Chadhei, Aama Ghara Aama Sansara, Bhisma Pratigyan, Bhai Hela Bhagari and Pabitra Bandhana before moving to West Bengal.

In Bengali cinema his first film as director was Jibon Sangi (1990). His later Bengali work includes Sonar Khancha, Annadata, Champion, Mastan, I Love You, Premer Kahini, Josh, Paran Jai Jaliya Re, 100% Love, Awara and Herogiri, and he wrote the screenplay for Bhalobasa Bhalobasa. He has also worked as a documentary editor.
His father, Shankar Kinagi, was a film producer and director.

Q14476290.lead: Tandra Ray is an Odia film actress who has worked in Odia cinema since 1977, when she made her debut opposite Bijay Mohanty in Chilika Teerey. She later married Mohanty and appeared with him in more than 60 films.

p: Ray's first film, Chilika Teerey (1977), cast her as the heroine opposite Bijay Mohanty. The two went on to form a screen pair in more than 60 films, among them Panjuri Bhitare Sari (1992) and Basudha (1996).

Her other films include Punarmilan, Samarpan, Pipasa, Pati Patni, Sautuni, Alibha Daag, Arati, Nala Damayanti, Palataka, Sata Kebe Luchi Rahena, Para Jhia Ghara Bhangena, Mamata Mage Mula, Ei Aama Sansar, Pua Moro Kala Thakura, Pathara Khasuchi Bada Deulu and Bhai Hela Bhagari. In later years she played supporting parts in films such as Mahanayak, Lal Tuku Tuku Sadhaba Bahu, Subha Vivaha, Katak, Jaggu Autowala, Daha Balunga and Bachelor.
She has also acted in Odia television mega-serials and worked for a time as a television announcer.
She is married to actor Bijay Mohanty; the couple have a daughter, Jasmine Mohanty.

Q59357074.lead: Sudhakar Vasant is a choreographer, film director, producer and actor who has worked mainly in Odia cinema since 1999, directing films such as Mitare Mita and Balunga Toka, and choreographing songs in several Indian film industries.

p: Vasant was born in Tamil Nadu; his mother tongue is Malayalam.

He trained as an assistant to dance director Chinni Prakash, working on Hindi, Tamil and Telugu films, and later choreographed independently for Telugu, Tamil, Hindi, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali and Odia productions.

His first Odia assignment was choreographing Gopal Yogesh's Sola Shukrabaar in 1999. Work on Prema Bandhan and Suna Sankhali followed, and he went on to stage the dances for a large share of Odia films, often making brief cameo appearances in the songs. His choreography for Shakti Baral's Tu Eka Aama Saha Bharasa (2006) brought him wider recognition.

After a decade as a choreographer he turned director in 2009 with Mitare Mita, starring Arindam Roy, Namrata Thapa, Lovely and Tanmay Mishra. The success of Balunga Toka (2011) established him among the leading directors in Odia cinema. He began producing in 2014 with Omm, followed by Aashiq in 2015.

As an actor he played the villain Anna in Ganja Ladhei (2014), which he also directed, and appeared in Kie Deba Takkar and Aashiq in 2015 and in a supporting role in the Tamil film Singam 3 (2017). In 2024 he acted with the Rajarani Rangamancha jatra troupe, leaving the jatra stage about a year later.

Q2107247.lead: Prabhat Mukherjee (1917–1997) was a director, actor and writer from Calcutta who made films in Bengali, Assamese, Odia and Hindi. Nua Bou, Dasyu Ratnakar, Jeevan Sathi and Sadhana were among his Odia films.

p: He started at All India Radio before taking up acting in Bengali cinema in 1950. Maa (1956), a Bengali film, was the first he directed. Bicharak (1959), made with Uttam Kumar, won the National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Bengali. For the Assamese film Puberun (1959) he wrote the script as well as directing, and it went on to screen at the Berlin Film Festival in 1960.
His Odia work as director included Nua Bou (1962), Dasyu Ratnakar, Jeevan Sathi (1963), which featured Geeta Rao, Minati Mishra, Sarat Pujari and Manimala Devi, and Sadhana (1964).

Shayar-e-Kashmir Mahjoor (1972), his first Hindi film, was a biopic of the Kashmiri national poet Ghulam Ahmad, made for the Government of Jammu and Kashmir with Balraj Sahni playing the poet. After two further Hindi films he went back to Bengali cinema. Mallika Sarabhai made her film debut under his direction.

His first wife was the Bengali actress Arundhati Devi, who had co-starred with him in Shorashi (1954) and acted in Maa; they later separated, and a second marriage also ended in divorce. He died in Calcutta in 1997.

Q4907265.lead: Bijoy Ketan Mishra (born 1959) is an Odia director of art films and documentaries and a journalist. His first feature, Ahalya (The Words of Silence), was selected for the Indian Panorama at the 30th International Film Festival of India.

p: Mishra was born in 1959 in Cuttack district, Odisha. He graduated from Ravenshaw College, Cuttack, and took a postgraduate degree in psychology at the University of Delhi.

His debut feature, Ahalya (The Words of Silence), adapts Laxmipriya Acharya's Odia short story of the same name and portrays the silent suffering of a woman widowed as a child. It was chosen for the feature-film section of the Indian Panorama at the 30th International Film Festival of India, where audiences responded well, and was later shown at other festivals, including the SPARROW festival in Mumbai under its 'One River Many Streams' strand.

Over some 15 years he has produced numerous documentaries, the best known being a film on the poet Sachi Routray made for the Sahitya Akademi, and he has worked on a biographical film about Pandit Gopabandhu Das. He works as an independent media producer, is Resident Editor of the Odisha edition of the Political and Business Daily, and edits the Odia features magazine Orissa Now in print and online. Books he has edited include Orissa File: Making Sense of a State in Motion, Editor's Time Capsule (2013) and Turning Tides – An Insightful Miscellany (2024). He has attended workshops and seminars in India, Japan and Sri Lanka.

Q15724380.lead: Namita Agrawal (born 1969) is an Odia singer and producer who sings devotional bhajans under her own name and modern and film songs under the name Nibedita. She co-founded the Sidharth group of music, radio and television channels.

p: Born Namita Das, she was the third child of Laxmidhar Das and Annadamanjari Das; her ancestral village is Nemal. At the age of five she learned traditional Jagannath bhajans from her grandfathers Kashinath Das and Dasarathi Das.

From the age of ten she trained formally in Odissi music, chhanda and champu with Akhil Kumar Lenka, Niroj Nalini Kuanr, Tarani Ranjan Jena and Biswanath Rao. She later studied Hindustani classical music with J. V. S. Rao, Dipak Basu and Nitai Sinha, light music with Sunakar Sahu and Odissi music with Haramohan Khuntia.
She began singing as a child artist at All India Radio, Cuttack, at ten and became an approved AIR artist in 1986, aged 16. From 1989 she also recorded in private studios.

Her first bhajan cassette, Ajhatia Kalia, came out in 1992, and in 1993 she recorded Balaram Das's Lakshmi Purana. Her Hrudayara Gita series covers about a hundred devotional songs by older Odia poets, including Jagannath Das's Odia Bhagabata, and she has also sung Sanskrit hymns such as the Gobinda Damodara Stotra. As Nibedita she released her first modern cassette, Baichadhei, in 1996 and recorded her first film song, 'Akashe Ki Ranga Lagila', in 2009. Her film playback work includes Samaya Hatare Dori, Abhimanyu and Golapi Golapi.

She has appeared on screen in some of her own bhajan videos, produced the films Aama Bhitare Kichhi Achhi (2010) and Mr. Kanheiya, and judged music programmes such as Swara Odishara. She co-founded 91.9 Sidharth FM, Sidharth TV, Sidharth Music, Sidharth Gold, Sidharth Bhakti and Jay Jagannath TV, and earlier co-founded Sarthak Music and Sarthak TV.
In 1992 she married sound engineer Sitaram Agrawal, who with his father had set up the J.E. company to produce Odia songs.

facts: Ajhatia Kalia, Lakshmi Purana, Bhakti Chandan
Sidharth TV, Sidharth FM, Sidharth Music

Q19362995.lead: Gopal Ghosh (1920–2015) was an Odia actor and film director, and is described as Odisha's first documentary filmmaker. He debuted on screen as Vidyapati in Sri Jagannath and directed films including Sri Lokanath, Ghara Sansar and Amar Prem.

p: Born Gopal Chandra Ghosh into a zamindar family at Raghunathpur in Jagatsinghpur district, he first acted at the age of six, playing the title role in the play Bhakta Dhruva. Between 1936 and 1954 he was also an active member of several sports clubs, including the Rovers Club, Cuttack Football Club, Young Utkal Club and Odisha Athletic Club.

Ghosh went on to appear in more than 100 stage plays and worked as a regular artist with Bharati Theatre, Janata Rangamancha and HMV Gramophone. His first film was Sri Jagannath, in which his performance as Vidyapati drew praise. At a time when Odisha had no cinema halls, he started 12 touring theatres.

As a director he made Amari Gaan Jhia, Sri Lokanath, Bhai Bhauja, Ghara Sansar and Amar Prem. He gave Balakrushna Das, Bhubaneswari Mishra, Rakhal Chandra Mohanty and Shyam Sundar Das their first chances as music directors, and introduced Shyamamani Patnaik, Pranab Patnaik, Parbati Ghosh and Jharana Das to films.

His 1949 documentary Black Pagoda, about Konark, was widely praised; the then US ambassador to India, L. Anderson, sent it to America. He made more than 40 documentaries for Doordarshan and the state and central governments, covering the foundation of the Hirakud Dam, the new capital, CRRI, All India Radio and the opening of the High Court, as well as Ei Matira Santana on Subhas Chandra Bose and a film on freedom fighters for the 50th anniversary of independence. In 2004, at 84, he played the lead in the ETV serial Budha Sankhari.

He received the President's silver medal in 1960 for directing Sri Lokanath, and his more than one hundred honours included awards from the Sangeet Natak Akademi, the Kabibar Gourishankar Award and the Utkal Sahitya Samaj award.
He died in Cuttack in 2015, aged 94.

Q135873394.lead: Piyush Tripathy (born Harishankar Tripathy, 1988) is an Odia jatra actor known mainly for villain roles. He has also acted in a few Odia films, including Love You Hamesha and Shambhu, and in television and music videos.

p: Tripathy was born in Khapuria, Cuttack district, to Nagendranath and Usharani Tripathy.

He began in Odia cinema, playing the hero in Ghaila Bagha, produced by Basudev Tripathy, but neither that film nor another of his films, Darling, was released. He played the villain in Love You Hamesha (2015) and the male lead in the ETV Odia serial Rajakanya.

On the jatra stage he started with Biswajanani Gananatya, playing the hero in Saguna Jauchi Shwashura Ghara and Mo Swami Nahanti Ghare. The following year he moved to Konark Gananatya where, influenced by Daitari Panda, he took up villain roles. He later worked with Indrabhuban Gananatya, Jatra Rangamahal and Jatra Surya Mandir; his productions include Mu Kendraparara Baba, Radha Pindhidela Meera Sindura and Kaudikhela (part two).
In 2025 he appeared in the Odia film Shambhu. He was offered a villain's part in Chaaridham, starring Anubhav Mohanty, but withdrew for personal reasons and Sujit Paikray took the role.
He married Rinki on 30 November 2012; they have a son.

facts: Biswajanani, Konark Gananatya, Indrabhuban, Rangamahal, Surya Mandir

Q15724030.lead: Gour Prasad Ghose (1929–1994), known as Gour Ghosh, was an Odia film actor, producer and director. He acted in nine Odia films, and his productions Stree and Sansar won national awards.

p: Ghose was born in Cuttack into a Bengali family whose roots lay in Bardhaman, West Bengal; his birth name was Roy Gour. After passing the matriculation examination from Pyarimohan Academy, Cuttack, in 1947 he joined Indian Railways, and he later studied at Ravenshaw College.

At Ravenshaw he acted in plays staged by the Praja Socialist Party to raise public awareness. While still studying he joined the film company Rupa Bharati and performed with the Annapurna B group; his role as Amar in Manoranjan Das's play August 9 made him popular. He also acted with Jana Sanskruti Sangha, Odisha Theatre and Prithvi Theatre in Mumbai.

His first film was Sri Jagannath (1950), and in Amari Gaan Jhua (1953) he and Parbati Ghosh first appeared as hero and heroine. His first production, Bhai Bhai, gave a start to several newcomers: Manoj Das wrote film dialogue for the first time, Nitai Palit wrote the screenplay, and Bhubaneswar Mishra and Balakrushna Das shared music direction for the first time. Later films such as Lakshmi, Kaa, Stree and Sansar were successes that each ran for 100 days in Cuttack. In all he acted in nine Odia films, produced two and directed one.

He was the first Odia producer to make Hindi telefilms for Doordarshan, among them Sopan, on labour problems, Prashna, on women's issues, and Jasodhara, on drug abuse. He also served on the board of directors of the Odisha Film Development Corporation.
Stree received the President's award for best regional film in 1968, and Sansar won a National Film Award in 1972. He was honoured in 1984 at the golden jubilee of Odia cinema.
His wife, actress Parbati Ghosh, worked with him in all his films, and their daughter Ratri Ghosh is also an actress.

Q3202714.lead: Bhanumati Devi (1934–2013) was an Odia stage and film actress who worked with Cuttack's Annapurna Theatre for over four decades and appeared in Odia films from 1953 to 1987, notably as Harabou in Matira Manisha.

p: She was born in Burma (Sittwe, according to one account) to Sarathi Pattnaik, from Aska in Ganjam district, and Pattadei. After the Second World War the family moved to Puri. She learned classical singing and dance from Manchashree Satyanarayan Panda.

Bhanumati Devi first acted on stage as a young child in 1942. She performed in more than 150 plays with both the A and B groups of the Annapurna Theatre in Cuttack, where she was associated for more than forty years; Lakhye Hira and Napahu Rati Namaru Pati were among her most praised stage roles.

She entered films at 19 with Amari Gaan Jhia and was most active in Odia cinema during the 1950s and 1960s, playing leading roles in more than a dozen films. Her best-known screen role was Harabou in Matira Manisha (1966), which brought her a National Film Award. Her last film was Jayadeba.

She received the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1985, the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Samman in 2001 and the Jayadev Award for lifetime achievement at the Odisha State Film Awards. The Odisha Cine Artists Association honoured her in 2008.
She was married to Harihara Panda and had a daughter, Swarnalata. She died at her home in Puri in 2013, aged 78.

Q15725365.lead: Subas Das is an Odia playback singer and composer who has sung in about 146 Odia films as well as Bengali, Bhojpuri and Kannada films, and has twice won the Odisha State Film Award for best playback singer.

p: Born Subas Chandra Das in Gaudunipokhari village, Mausudha, in the Chandbali area of Bhadrak district, he was the second of nine children of Adikanda Das and Jayamani Das, in a family where everyone sang. He studied at Harekrushna Ray Upper Primary School, Dakha High School, Bhadrak College and Ravenshaw College, and trained in music from childhood under Muralidhar Giri, Dipak Basu and J. V. S. Rao.

While at Ravenshaw College he won first place in a singing competition with 'Suna Chadhei Mo Rupa Chadhei', which All India Radio, Cuttack, recorded and broadcast many times on its Yuba Bani programme. He first sang on All India Radio in 1977 and on Doordarshan in 1981. His song 'Chhota Mora Gaanti', written by Sachi Routray and broadcast on Doordarshan, made him widely known.

His first film song was 'Jhum Jhum Jhum Lo' in Manasi, composed by Prafulla Kar. His film credits include Samar Salim Saiman, Ramayan, Trinath Mela, Jhieenki Jhinka, Akshi Trutiya, Bilwa Mangala, Dora, Jaa Devi Sarbabhuteshu, Daiba Dauri, Mana Rahigala Tumari Thare, Rakhi Bandhili Mo Rakhiba Mana, Kalishankar and Mun Kana Ete Kharap. He has also recorded for more than 500 albums and performed in India and abroad.

He won the Odisha State Film Award for best playback singer for Daiba Dauri (1990) and for Mana Rahigala Tumari Thare (1999). Other honours include the Pranab Parampara Samman (2012), the Akshaya Smruti Samman (2015) and the Bhikari Bal Kanthashilpi Samman (2022) from the Utkal Sahitya Samaj.
His wife, Subhalaxmi Das, is also a singer.

facts: Chhota Mora Gaanti; Suna Chadhei Mo Rupa Chadhei

Q15724955.lead: Manimala Devi (1931–2016) was an Odia stage and film actress who acted in about 30 films and more than a hundred plays, beginning her screen career with Sri Lokanath (1960).

p: Manimala was born in Balibishi village in Cuttack district. She began performing at the age of nine and never attended school.

In 1945 she joined the Annapurna A Theatre in Cuttack, where she acted in Jayadev and learned dance, music and acting from Kalicharan Patnaik, Balakrushna Das and Dhiren Das. Her stage work included Chandaluni, Janaki, Chasha Jhia, Kala Pahada, Mukti Konark and Shree Jayadev.

Her first film, Sri Lokanath, was among 14 of her films that received national awards. She appeared in about 30 films, including Lakshmi, Jeevan Sathi, Suryamukhi, Abhinetri, Malajanha, Kaa, Bhai Bhauja, Kie Kahara, Neeraba Jhada, Maya Miriga, Klanta Aparanha, Nishiddha Swapna and Andha Diganta. Her screen pairing with Samuel Sahoo was popular with audiences.

She received the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for lifetime contribution (1987), the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Award (1999), the Jayadev Award (2000) and the Kabisamrat Upendra Bhanja Award (2008).
Her son is Shankar Ghosh. She died in Bhubaneswar in 2016.

Q60664595.lead: Trupti Sinha is an Odia actress who has worked on stage, in Odia films and in television serials, and is best known in Odia cinema for playing villainous roles.

p: Sinha began as a stage actress, performing in a number of plays with the Annapurna Theatre in Puri. She entered Odia films in 1996 with Vasudha, and in 1999 she appeared in Pabitra Bandhana, as Gouri, and in Maa Gojabayani. In 2003 she acted in Suna Sankhali, a film made in both Odia and Bengali.

From 2008 she took on negative roles in films. In Mate Ani Dela Lakhye Faguna she played Durgadevi, the mother of the villain played by Chandan Kar, and in Sata Sure Bandha E Jibana (2009), featuring Anubhav Mohanty and Sunil Kumar, she was Anita, the sister of Mihir Das's character. In Dosti (2011) she played Parbati, mother of the villain played by Pritiraj Satapathy and wife of Debu Bose's character. She played the hero's grandmother in two 2012 films starring Anubhav Mohanty, Something Something and Matric Fail, and Bijay Mohanty's mother in Daha Balunga (2013). Her later films include Haribol Nuhe Tanka Bol, Ganja Ladhei, Raghupati Raghav Rajaram, Tu Je Sei, Nimki, Jor Ka Jhatka, Bhaijaan, Mu Ashiq Mu Awara, Love Pain Kuchh Bhi Karega and Super Michhua.

On television she appeared in the ETV Odia serials Gayatri and Ahuti, playing a villain in the latter, and later played the mother of the heroine Devika in Jwain Number One on Zee Sarthak. She has also been a mentor on Gruhalaxmi, a programme on Sarthak TV.
She is married to the Odia actor Suresh Bal, and the couple have performed together on stage many times.

Q6933443.lead: Mukesh Rishi (born 1956) is an Indian actor and film producer who has worked mainly in Hindi and Telugu films, usually in villainous supporting roles; he appeared in the Odia film Aakhi Palakare Tu (2010).

p: Rishi's family traces its pre-partition roots to Mirpur. He graduated from Government College, Sector 11, Chandigarh, worked in Mumbai for two years and then moved to Fiji, where he met his future wife. The couple later settled in New Zealand, where he began modelling, though work commitments left him little time for it.

After seven years abroad he returned to Mumbai and trained at Roshan Taneja's acting school. His first break came on television as the villain Mir Sadiq in Sanjay Khan's serial The Sword of Tipu Sultan (1990), and his Hindi film breakthrough followed with Gardish in 1993.

Besides Hindi and Telugu, he has acted in Malayalam, Kannada, Punjabi, Marathi, Tamil and Bhojpuri films. His Tamil work includes Vallarasu (2000), Ramana (2002) and Singam 2 (2013), and his Punjabi films include Jatt James Bond (2014). In Odia cinema he appeared in Aakhi Palakare Tu (2010). He has also worked in web series such as Abhay and Indian Police Force.
He was nominated for the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor for Sarfarosh (2000), and for the Filmfare Award for Best Villain – Telugu for Indra (2003) and Seetayya (2004).

Q55395631.lead: Anubha Sourya (born 1992) is an Odia film actress and Odissi dancer who made her screen debut in 2011 with Mu Premi Mu Pagala.

p: She was born in Khordha. Her father, Lalatendu Narayan Sadangi, is an engineer, and her mother is the Odia film actress Pushpa Panda. Her family's village is Ranapur in Khordha district. She studied at DAV School, Chandrasekharpur, and later took an engineering degree from Silicon Institute of Technology. She trained in Odissi under Guru Gangadhar Pradhan and has danced on many stages.

As a child she appeared in the Odia song videos Mati Ghoda and Akhira Janma, and she also worked as a presenter. While still studying engineering she was cast in Mu Premi Mu Pagala (2011), opposite Harihar Das, an India's Got Talent finalist who was also making his debut as a lead. In 2015 she played a princess in the Hindi film Kaun Kitne Paani Mein.

Three of her films were released in 2016: Samaya Bada Balaban, with Pupinder and Lipsa Mishra; Sweet Heart, with Babushan and Anu Choudhury; and Revenge, produced by Asit Pati, with Abhishek Rath. On television she was one of the mentors, with Jina Samal, Priya Chaudhury and Prakruti Mishra, on the 2016 edition of Sarthak TV's Raja Queen.

For her debut in Mu Premi Mu Pagala she received best newcomer honours in 2011 at the Tarang Cine Awards, as well as from Chitralipi, Cinema Sansar and Banichitra. In 2013 the Biju Patnaik University of Technology students' union gave her its Yuba Prerana Samman.
She is the daughter of actress Pushpa Panda.

Q5224086.lead: Sriram Panda (born 1954) is an Odia film actor, director and screenwriter from Nabarangpur district who worked in Odia cinema from the early 1970s until the early 1990s, when he left acting for a monastic life.

p: Panda was born in Nabarangpur, Odisha, in 1954.

His first film role came in Dharitri, written by Dhir Biswal and directed by Nitai Palit. He was popular with Odia audiences through the 1970s and 1980s. In 1975 he played the lead in Jajabara, directed by Trimurti, which was a major hit and later reissued in a coloured version. In 1976 he appeared in six films, four of them commercially successful. Over his career he acted in more than 52 Odia and Bengali films.

He wrote, directed and produced Kurukshetra, with Tripura Panda also credited as a producer. In 1992 he left the film industry and joined the Bihar School of Yoga, taking the name Swami Nitya Chaitanya, and he has since lived as a monk at an ashram in Munger, Bihar.
He received the Jayadev Samman in 2011.
He is married to Tripura Misra, a former Odia film actress who later became a college lecturer. The couple have two children.

Q7299451.lead: Raza Murad (born 1950) is an Indian actor who has appeared mainly in Hindi films, with more than 600 to his name; in Odia cinema he appeared in Mate Bohu Kari Nei Jaa (2011).

p: Born Raza Murad Khan in Rampur, Uttar Pradesh, he is the son of the Hindi film character actor Hamid Ali Murad. He trained at the Film and Television Institute of India in Pune from 1969 to 1971 and earned a diploma in film acting.

His film career began with Ek Nazar (1972). In the 1970s he often played sympathetic brothers or brother figures, and one of his remembered early parts was the despairing poet in Namak Haraam (1973), alongside Amitabh Bachchan and Rajesh Khanna. From the 1980s onward he worked mostly in supporting roles as fathers, uncles and villains, and he is noted for his baritone voice.

His Hindi films include Prem Rog, Ram Teri Ganga Maili, Henna, Ram Lakhan, Tridev, Mohra, Gupt and Jodhaa Akbar, and he played Jalal-ud-din Khalji in Padmaavat (2018). He has also acted in Telugu films such as Indra (2002), in several Punjabi films and on Hindi television, including Madhubala – Ek Ishq Ek Junoon. His Odia film is Mate Bohu Kari Nei Jaa (2011).
He has received seven Filmfare nominations for playing villains and won once. In 2011 the PTC Punjabi Film Awards gave him a lifetime achievement award for his work in Punjabi cinema.

He is a paternal first cousin of actress Zeenat Aman and a nephew of her father, the screenwriter Amanullah Khan. His son Ali and his nieces Sonam and Sanober Kabir are also performers. He married Samina Murad in 1972.

facts: Film and Television Institute of India, Pune

Q113172371.lead: Rajeswari Ray (also known as Rajeswari Ray Mohapatra) was an Odia actress and television presenter from Baleswar, known mainly for villainous roles in Odia television serials; she also acted in three Odia films.

p: Ray began as a presenter on television and on stage before moving into acting in serials, where she became known for playing villains. Her serials included Basundhara on DD Odia, Sanskar on ETV Odia, Devi on OTV, Swabhiman and Unasi Kanya on Tarang, Kumkum on Colors Odia and To Pain Mun on Zee Sarthak. Her portrayal of the villain Alaka in Unasi Kanya brought her wide popularity, and To Pain Mun was her last serial.
She entered Odia films in 2008 with Satyameba Jayate and went on to appear in Aaa Re Saathi Aa and Blackmail. She also danced in some Odia music albums.
She died in Bhubaneswar in 2022, aged 37.

Q5070937.lead: Chandan Kar (born 1981) is an Odia film actor from Cuttack who also works as a software engineer; he made his film debut opposite Archita Sahu in Babu I Love You.

p: Kar was born in Cuttack to Ramakanta Kar, a retired government engineer, and Archana Mishra. He went to DAV Public School, Unit-4, Bhubaneswar, and in 2003 completed a B.Tech in electronics and telecommunication at Odisha Engineering College.

Alongside acting he works as a software engineer with a multinational IT company. After his debut in Babu I Love You he appeared the same year in De Maa Shakti De. His later films include Mate Ani Dela Lakhye Faguna, Chhati Chiri Dele Tu, Dhire Dhire Prema Hela, Keun Dunia Ru Asila Bandhu, Pagala Karichhi Paunji Tora, Shani Dev, Ae Milana Juga Jugara, Chhatire Lekhichhi Tori Naa and Hero. His short film Papagarbha has won 50 awards and been screened at several film festivals.
On television he has appeared in Ei Ta Jibana on OTV and Phone In on ETV, and in several Tarang programmes including Celebrity Show, Day with a Star, Star Choice and Best in Odisha.

Off screen he has been a member and counsellor of the Save Indian Family Foundation since 2007, has adopted two tigers at Nandankanan Zoological Park, has pledged his eyes for donation, and through the Kar Foundation distributed rations to Odia film technicians during the COVID period.

Q30120332.lead: Sonika Roy (born 1994) is an Odia model and film actress from Cuttack who won the Miss Asia Pacific title in 2017 and made her film debut in Rangila Baba.

p: Roy was born in Cuttack, where her father, Soumitra Roy, worked at the Cuttack board office. She studied at Kendriya Vidyalaya and learned Odissi at Kala Vikash Kendra, training for about three years under Guru Lucky Pragya Pratishthita Mohanty and later at the institution of Padma Shri Kumkum Mohanty.

She began preparing for beauty pageants in 2014. That year she took part in Femina Miss India and in Miss Odisha, where she was first runner-up and won Miss Photogenic. She reached the Femina Miss India finals in 2015 and finished in the top six of Miss Earth India in 2016. Representing Odisha at Femina Miss India in 2017, she was then chosen from seven shortlisted candidates as Miss Asia Pacific 2017, earning the right to represent India at the Asia Pacific International pageant in the Philippines.

Her first film was Rangila Baba, directed by Sanjay Nayak and based on Baba Sarathi, in which she played opposite Chandan Kar; Kuna Tripathy, Guddu, Jeevan Panda and Biju Badajena were also in the cast. She was later set to enter Telugu cinema with Sita Kalyanam, which was being filmed.
Miss Asia Pacific (2017); first runner-up and Miss Photogenic at Miss Odisha (2014).

Q18580084.lead: Raj Kishore Ray (1914–1998) was an Odia writer and college teacher who received the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award, and who also acted in the Odia film Bhai Bhauja.

p: Ray studied at Ravenshaw College, where he played female roles in stage productions.

A lecturer by profession, he had interests ranging across literature, teaching, dance, music, acting and direction. His first published book was the poetry collection Deepali, after which he turned to short stories, many of them drawn from his own experiences and featuring himself as the hero; critics found some of them self-centred. He wrote stories, plays and novels, and his story collections include Bikacha Satadala (1947), Ashoka Chakra (1949), Jayasankha (1950), Adipurusha (1960) and Manwantarara Manaba (1988).

He served as working president of the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi and was the first secretary of the Odisha Sahitya-Sangeet-Natak Akademi founded in 1958. On screen he acted in the Odia film Bhai Bhauja.
He received the Jhankar Award for short stories in 1973, the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award in 1989 for Manwantarara Manaba, and the Sarala Samman in 1993.
He was married to Manorama Ray. Their daughters include the actress and writer Malabika Ray and the actress Mahasweta Ray.

facts: Malabika Ray, Manaswini Ray, Mahasweta Ray

Q18913680.lead: Rakhal Chandra Mohanty (1932–2019) was an Odia music director and teacher who worked for radio, television, albums and Odia films, scoring films such as Akshi Trutiya, Trinath Mela and Srikrushna Raasleela.

p: Mohanty was born at Tatana in Kendrapara district. Drawn to music from childhood, he devoted himself to it fully after passing his matriculation in 1948. He trained under Pandit Bhubaneswar Mishra and Balakrushna Das, and in 1973 completed a postgraduate qualification in vocal music from the Akhil Bharatiya Gandharva Mahavidyalaya Mandal.

Teaching was his main profession: from 1955 to 1973 he taught music at Kala Vikash Kendra in Cuttack. Skilled in both light and classical music, he was an approved music director for All India Radio, Cuttack, and Doordarshan, and worked with leading figures of Odisha's dance and music world, forming a successful partnership with Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra. His radio programmes for All India Radio, Cuttack, included Ganapradhan Samman (1991), Jibanara Swaralipi (1992), Karuna Kendra (1993) and Shantira Pathe (1994). He performed across India and in countries including Germany, the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, France, Russia, Yugoslavia and Bulgaria.
In Odia cinema he was music director for Akshi Trutiya, Trinath Mela, Srikrushna Raasleela, Amar Prem and Ghar Sansar, and music arranger for Manika Jodi.

His honours included the Geeta Govinda Samman from the Nikhila Utkal Sangeet Shilpi Parishad and an award from the Indian School of Dance, Music and Theatre, Canada, both in 1977; the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi award in 2002; the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Samman in 2005; the Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja Samman and the Nitai Palit Samman in 2014; the Talabadya Samman of the Mardala Academy in 2015; and the Sangeet Sudhakar Balakrushna Das Memorial Samman in 2017.

Q15723636.lead: Abhijit Majumdar (1971–2026) was an Odia film music director, composer and singer who began scoring Odia films in 2000 after starting out in Sambalpuri music.

p: Majumdar began working in music in 1991, and his first Sambalpuri album as composer was Daksi Gala. He had been a lecturer, but in 1996 he gave up the job and moved to Cuttack to work in music. After establishing himself in Sambalpuri songs he moved into Odia cinema in 2000. Over his career he composed more than 700 songs for Odia films, modern Odia albums, devotional and Sambalpuri albums and television serials.

His film work includes Love Story, Sister Sridevi, Golmaal Love, Mr. Majnu, Sundergarh Ra Salman Khan and Sriman Surdas. On television he presented and judged an Antakshari programme on MBC TV, and hosted Tarang TV shows including Melody Nights with Abhijit Majumdar, Lockdown Antakshari and Band Baaja Baaraat with Abhijit Majumdar.
He received an Odisha State Film Award in 2011 for Tu Thaa Mu Jauchhi Rushi.
He died in Bhubaneswar in 2026, aged 54.

Q82367873.lead: Barsha Patnaik (née Nayak) is an Odia film actress from Paradip who won the Best Actress award at the 27th Odisha State Film Awards for her debut film, Tulasi Apa.

p: She was born in Paradip, in Jagatsinghpur district, and holds an MBA from Biju Patnaik University of Technology. Before acting she worked for an IT company in Hyderabad.

In 2015, while still in her IT job, she auditioned for Amiya Ranjan Patnaik's Tulasi Apa and was cast as Tulasi Munda, the social activist and Padma Shri recipient whose life the film depicts. The film was shown at festivals including the International Film Festival of India, the Kolkata, Bengaluru, Shimla and Nasik international festivals and the Tehran Jasmine International Film Festival in Iran, before its theatrical release on 19 May 2017. It became the first Odia feature film to be made available worldwide on Amazon Prime.
Her later films include Pratikshya, Karma, Trikanya and Mantra Muugdha.
Best Actress, 27th Odisha State Film Awards, for Tulasi Apa.
She is married to the Odia film director Anupam Patnaik.

facts: MBA, Biju Patnaik University of Technology

Q5583435.lead: Goodly Rath (also spelled Goodli; born 1973) is an Odia film composer, musician and playback singer from Bhubaneswar, known for scoring films such as Loafer, Most Wanted and Chocolate.

p: Rath was born in Bhubaneswar into a musical family. His mother, Pravabati Rath, was a state-level singer and gold medallist, and his maternal grandfather, Khetramohan Kar, was a tabla player. The youngest of five brothers, he also has a sister. He attended Buxi Jagabandhu English Medium School and earned his bachelor's degree at Buxi Jagabandhu College, Bhubaneswar. Interested in music and instruments from childhood, he formed a band called The Brothers with his four elder brothers while still young.

His work spans playback singing, vocal and musical arrangement, background scoring, music programming and production, and he sometimes writes and sings his own songs. He brought Western musical elements into Odia film music. His film credits include Aaa Re Saathi Aa and Chup Kie Asuchi (2009), Anjali (2010), Loafer, 143 – I Love You, Family No.1, Most Wanted and Chocolate (2011), Idiot (2012), and Tiger, Sweet Heart and Tu Kahibu Na Mun (2016).
On television he has been a judge on Tarang's Voice of Odisha and Sarthak TV's Singing Super Star, and Maha Guru on Zee Sarthak's SaReGaMaPa.
He lives in Bhubaneswar and in 2000 married Mili Rath. Their daughter, Priyanka Rath, has begun acting as a child artist. His brother Kabuli Rath is a musician who works with A. R. Rahman.

Q15723664.lead: Ashok Pati is an Odia film director, screenwriter and actor from Bhubaneswar, known for films such as Baazi, Nandini I Love U and Loafer; he has also directed Bengali and Bangladeshi films.

p: Pati began as an assistant director. His Odia assistant credits include Rakhi Bhijigala Akhi Luhare, Suna Palinki, Laxmi Pratima, Kie Pochhi Daba Maa Akhira Luha, Sahara Jaluchhi and Mana Rahigala Tumari Thare, and in Hindi he assisted on Dhai Akshar Prem Ke, Chori Chori, Deewaar: Let's Bring Our Heroes Home and Taxi No. 9211, as well as the DD1 serial Shohrat.

As a director and writer of Odia films he made Baazi, Mu Tate Love Karuchi, To Pain, Mate Ta Love Helare, Nandini I Love U, Prem Rogi, Dream Girl, Sanju Aau Sanjana, Loafer, 143 I Love You, Dosti and Idiot, and he also wrote Diwana, Shapath and Deewana Deewani. He has acted in Prema Adhei Akshyara (2010), Idiot (2012) and Luchakali (2012).
For television he directed Shohrat in Hindi on DD1, Sanskara on ETV Odia and Sihaga Sindura on Star Kiran.

Q15723647.lead: Amarendra Mohanty (1958–2021), known as Bulu Bhai, was an Odia music director and singer who worked mainly in Odia films and television, beginning with Shradhanjali in 1993.

p: Mohanty was born in Kendrapara district to Nagendranath Mohanty and Sarat Kumari Mohanty. He went to school at Pyarimohan Academy in Cuttack and learned music from Balakrushna Das, Sunanda Patnaik and Harekrushna Mohanty.

He started his musical career at All India Radio, Cuttack, and later sang in Odia films. He became a film music director in 1993 with Shradhanjali and went on to score films including Magunira Shagada, Suna Panjuri, Sarapancha Babu, Bhai Hela Bhagari, Stree and Kandhei Akhire Luha. He also sang many of his own compositions. His last film as music director was Ranga Barasiba Tupuru Tupuru, released in 2019.

At a time when Odisha had few recording studios, he set up Asha Studio in his Cuttack home, where singers such as Mohammed Aziz recorded. After his wife's death he moved to Bhubaneswar and founded the Amarendra Mohanty Music Academy to teach music.
He died in Bhubaneswar in 2021.

facts: Balakrushna Das, Sunanda Patnaik, Harekrushna Mohanty

Q60368429.lead: Debasish Patra is an Odia film and music-video actor and a television and stage presenter from Keonjhar, who entered Odia cinema in 2010 with Pahili Raja.

p: Patra was born in Keonjhar district and grew up in Anandapur, where he attended Balabhadra Narayan High School.

He started out acting in Odia music albums. His first film was Pahili Raja (2010), which starred Siddhanta Mahapatra and Anu Choudhury, and the same year he played his first lead role in Bhul Bujhibani Mate. He was again the hero in Tate Bhala Pauchi Boli and Chori Chori Mana Chori.

He has played a range of parts in films including Tu Tha Mun Jauchi Rushi, Chandini I Miss You, Idiot, Love Master, Mo Duniya Tu Hi Tu, Deewana Deewani, Mu Eka Tumara, Krantidhara, Raghupati Raghav Rajaram, Bhala Pae Tate 100 Ru 100, Tu Je Sei and Tu Mo Love Story.

On television he hosted Sunabohu, Sarthak TV's show modelled on Kaun Banega Crorepati, was a mentor on Raja Queen and later a judge on its fifth season, and presented both editions of Tarang Parivar Mahamukabila. He has also anchored award ceremonies and stage events for the Tarang and Sarthak channels, and co-presented a Tarang music show with Jina Samal.

Q56677708.lead: Bidusmita Das, credited as Bidusmita, is an Odia film and television actress from Bhubaneswar who is best known for item dances in Odia films and played the lead in Badhu Nuhen Mu Bandhu (2013).

p: Bidusmita started acting in Odia music albums soon after finishing class ten, and also appeared in Sambalpuri albums. After her marriage she began dancing in item songs in Odia films, the first being in Chocolate, followed by Love Master, Rangila Baba and To Premare Padila Pare. She also choreographed a dance in Rangila Baba.

In films she moved from supporting and negative roles to leading parts. She had a supporting role in Dosti (2011) and was the heroine of Badhu Nuhen Mu Bandhu (2013). Her other films include Kehi Jane Bhala Lagere, Tu Kahibu Na Mu and Jabardast Premika.

Her television work began with a DD Odia serial. In the Sarthak TV serial Pari she played Charu, a character who began as a villain and became the lead heroine as the story changed. She also presented the Sarthak TV programme Maa Rana Michha Kahuni with Harihar Mohapatra.
She married Ananta Das in 2011.

Q15725429.lead: Hemant Das (1933–2010) was an Odia film actor and director who appeared in about 40 Odia, Hindi and Bengali films and co-directed Jajabara under the joint pseudonym Trimurti.

p: Das was born in Khamaranga village in the Banki subdivision of Cuttack district to Radheshyam Das and Baidehi. His father ran a raas troupe, so he grew up around dance, song and music. He passed his matriculation from Barendra Krushna Vidyapitha, Banki, and studied at Christ College, Cuttack.

He began acting on stage and, before entering films, read Odia news for All India Radio in New Delhi. His film career began with Gour Ghosh's Bhai Bhai, and over the following decades he acted in roughly 40 films, including Maa, Shesha Shrabana, Amar Prem, Chilika Teerey, Balidan, Maa O Mamata, Pooja, Ashanta Graha, Ram Rahim, Swapna Sagara, Neeraba Jhada, Dandabalunga, Jaga Hatare Pagha, Kichhi Smruti Kichhi Anubhuti and Akuha Katha, as well as the Hindi film Shodh, which won the Swarna Kamal. His last film was Tume Hi Sathi Mora (2009).

With Akshaya Mohanty and Bijay Mishra he directed Jajabara under the shared name Trimurti. In his last years he hoped to complete Sulochana, a film based on Fakir Mohan Senapati's Patent Medicine, but could not finish it for lack of funds.

He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Supporting Actor for Dandabalunga (1984), a special jury award for Kichhi Smruti Kichhi Anubhuti (1988), and the Jayadev Puraskar in 1991 for his film acting.
He died in Bhubaneswar in 2010.

Q21043196.lead: Priya Chaudhury (born Priyadarshini Chaudhury, 1989) is an Odia film actress and television presenter from Bhubaneswar who made her film debut opposite Sabyasachi in Dream Girl.

p: She was born in Bhubaneswar on 25 November 1989; her father worked in government service. She graduated from Utkal University.

Before acting she worked as an anchor on All India Radio and on television, hosting Sangeet Surabhi, Mitatie Geetatie and Apananka Pasanda on ETV, Hip Hip Hurray and Political Circus on OTV, and Shubha Sakala on DD Odia alongside Pupinder.

She entered films in 2008 with Dream Girl, playing the heroine opposite Sabyasachi. Her later films include Abhimanyu, Megha Sabari Re Asiba Pheri, Dil Tote Deichi, Aalo Mora Kandhei, Baisi Pahache Kheliba Mina, Hero, Chandini I Miss You, Dosti, Gud Boy, Paribeni Kehi Alaga Kari, Rumku Jhumana, Mita Basichi Mu Bhuta Sathire and Lage Prema Najar (2022).

After her marriage in 2013 she stepped away from films for a time but appeared as a judge on Tarang's Kie Heba Mo Heroine (2014) and Sarthak TV's Raja Queen (2016), and hosted Bhagya Badaliba Puni Thare on Sarthak.
She won Best Actress at the ETV Odia Film Awards in 2011 for Megha Sabari Re Asiba Pheri.

Q15725397.lead: Swarup Nayak (1947–2023) was an Odia film music director, lyricist, playback singer and actor from Cuttack who began as a child actor in Jayadeb (1962) and twice won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Music Director.

p: Nayak first appeared on screen as a child artist in Jayadeb in 1962. He turned to film music with HiraNila, his first film as composer, for which he also wrote lyrics. Over his career he composed music for 41 Odia films, wrote songs for 30, sang playback in 6 and acted in 6. His later scores include Premarutu Asilare, Kathantara, for which he also wrote lyrics, and Swayamsiddha (2010).
He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Music Director for Mana Rahigala Tumari Thare and for Kathantara. He also received the Bioscope Award in 2006 and was felicitated by Banichitra.
His sister is the Odia actress Parbati Ghose and his brother is Sarada Prasanna Naik. He was married to Niharika Sahu.
He died in Cuttack in 2023, aged 76.

Q16246971.lead: Ashok Bhadra is an Indian composer and music director working mainly in Bengali and Hindi films since 1995; his Odia credit is Agnee (2004).

p: Bhadra has worked as a music director, background score composer and playback singer. His first credit as music director was Rakhal Raja (1995), and he went on to score a long run of Bengali films including Tomake Chai, Satbhai, Sneher Protidan, Badsha The King, Agni (2004), Dadar Adesh, Takkar, Golmaal, Kakhono Biday Bolo Na, Bhalo Meye Mondo Meye and Phire Eso Tumi. He composed both the songs and background score for the Hindi film Bloody Isshq (2013), and the background score for Love Birds (2011). He sang playback in Kakhono Biday Bolo Na (2010) and has also composed albums such as Shudhu Ektu Bhalobasa and Paroshmani.

Q4795753.lead: Arpita Pal (Arpita Chatterjee) is an Indian actress from Kolkata who has worked mostly in Bengali and Odia films; her Odia work includes Pagala Premi (2007).

p: Pal came to public attention in 1997 by winning Sananda Tilottama, a beauty pageant organised by the ABP Group, and went on to appear in national television advertisements. Her film debut came in 1999 with Prabhat Roy's Tumi Ele Tai, and her other films include Deva, Devdas, Inquilaab, Prem Shakti, Pratarok, Dada Thakur, Pratibad, Utsab and Anupama. She has worked with directors such as Shakti Samanta and Rituparno Ghosh.

After her marriage she paused her career for family life, returning in 2009 with Abhik Mukhopadhyay's Ekti Tarar Khonje. In 2014 she signed her first Hindi film, Onir's Shab. She has also staged a solo musical, My Name Is Jaan, and in 2023 co-hosted the first TV9 Bangla Ghorer Bioscope Awards with Parambrata Chatterjee and Abir Chatterjee.

Through her production house Idea Creations she produced fiction, non-fiction and feature formats for channels such as Zee, Star and Colors in Bengal, and she now runs the Delhi-based production house Studio9, backed by TV9 Network.
She won the Joy Filmfare Award for Best Actor Female (Critics' Choice) in 2022 for Abyakto.
She is married to the actor Prosenjit Chatterjee; they have a son, Trishanjit.

Q15724761.lead: Basant Naik (1937–2011), known as the 'Movie Mogul', was an Odia film director, producer and distributor who made about 20 films, beginning with Naga Phasa (1977), and ran the banner Brajaraj Movies.

p: Naik was born on 16 January 1937 at Haripur in Cuttack district to Gajendra Nayak and Rajkumari Devi. He began his working life as a textile engineer in Mumbai.

He returned to Odisha in 1959 intending to contribute to Odia cinema, and on his return director Bijay Nayak steered him towards films. His first venture was distributing the Odia film Jajabara. He directed his first film, Naga Phasa, in 1977, for which he also wrote the story, and then founded his own company, Brajaraj Movies, under which he distributed around 500 Odia, Hindi and Bengali films.

His directing credits include Ranabhumi (1995), Sashu Ghara Chalijibi (2002), Don (2010) and 143 I Love You (2011), along with the Hindi film Spandan (1984). As producer he backed Dandabalunga (1984), Eai Ta Dunia (1987), Jahaku Rakhibe Ananta (1988), Lakhe Siba Puji Paichhi Pua (1994), for which he also wrote the story, Yashoda (1996), Mana Rahigala Tumari Thare (1999), Mo Kola To Jhulana (2001), Barsa My Darling (2004) and Romeo, the Lover Boy (2011).

He helped launch the careers of Bijay Mohanty, Malabika Ray, Anubhav Mohanty and Babushan, and brought performers from Hindi and Bengali cinema such as Rakhee Gulzar, Mithun Chakraborty, Sujit Kumar, Aruna Irani, Gufi Paintal, Prosenjit, Debashree Roy and Satabdi Roy into Odia films.
He received Odisha State Film Awards for Naga Phasa (1977) and Dandabalunga (1984), and an Indian Panorama award for Jahaku Rakhibe Ananta (1988).
He died in Bhubaneswar in 2011.

Q7285877.lead: Rajatava Dutta (born 1967) is a Calcutta-born actor of stage and screen who works in Bengali, Hindi and English films. He also appeared in the Odia film Nayak Nuhen Mun Khalanayaka (2005).

p: He finished school at Ballygunge Government High School (Madhyamik, 1983), did his Higher Secondary at Goenka College of Commerce and Business Administration (1985) and graduated from Netaji Nagar College in 1987.

Theatre has been part of his work since 1987, when he joined Soumitra Basu's group Antarmukh. He later performed with Ushnik, with Kaushik Sen's Swapnosandhani, and with Gandhar, Natyoanon, Ansambal, Calcutta Performers and Sangsriti, among others.

In cinema he began as a junior artist, and Ajab Gayer Ajab Katha (1998) gave him his first big break. Villain roles in commercial hits such as MLA Fatakeshto, Challenge, Paglu and Boss: Born to Rule made him popular, while Paromitar Ekdin, Open Tee Bioscope, Bogla Mama Jug Jug Jiyo and the web series Byadh drew critical praise. He has also judged the Zee Bangla reality show Mirakkel.
Paromitar Ekdin brought him the Bengal Film Journalists' Association Award for Best Supporting Actor in 2001, and MLA Fatakeshto the Anandalok Award for Best Villain in 2006.

Q28924795.lead: Gargi Mohanty is an Odia film and television actress and trained Odissi dancer who made her film debut as the heroine of Hara Patnaik's Arjun (2005) and won a State Film Award for Krantidhara.

p: Mohanty began learning Odissi at the age of two and a half. Her screen career started in music albums: director Harish Mohanty cast her in a devotional album, and after she recorded all its dances with ease he used her in several more. She also appeared in the Hindi album Aankhon Ne Tujhko Dekha.

Her first television serial was Kahile To Kula Kutumbaku Laja on DD Odia. Soon after, Hara Patnaik chose her as the heroine of Arjun, opposite Anubhav Mohanty. She then returned to television in Gayatri on ETV Odia, and Topae Sindura and Rani on Tarang, playing a mother-in-law in the latter. She also acted in Matira Bandhana, which was not released.

In He Sakha (2012), a film about Krishna and his friend Sudama, she played Sudama's wife Sumati. In 2016 she starred in Krantidhara, a film centred on women's empowerment, with Samaresh Routray and Pushpa Panda, and that year also acted in a documentary film, Spandan.
She won the Best Actress award at the 26th Odisha State Film Awards for Krantidhara.

Q30060523.lead: Sunita Garabadu (born 1990) is an Odia presenter, model and actress from Bhubaneswar who became the first woman from Odisha to commentate on cricket matches, and who made her film debut in Gud Boy (2012).

p: Garabadu was born in Bhubaneswar, the younger of two children of Sripati Garabadu, a businessman, and Lalita Garabadu. She graduated from BJB Autonomous College and also trained as an air hostess.

Without formal training as a presenter, she began anchoring in 2008 and is best known as a video jockey. She has hosted sports events, television, stage, reality and comedy shows, and corporate events. Her sports work includes IPL matches in Visakhapatnam and Cuttack, the Hockey Champions Trophy and the Hockey India League in Bhubaneswar, and she commentated at the 2016 ICC World Twenty20 in Nagpur. On television she has hosted Comedy Darbar and Kichhi Katha Kichhi Geeta on Tarang, Boom Shaka Laka on ETV and E-News on OTV.
She has also acted in the ETV Odia serial Bada Ghara Bada Gumara Katha, and entered Odia films with Gud Boy in 2012.

Q56433237.lead: Pinki Priyadarsini is an Odia film actress and television presenter who entered films in 2012 with Tu Mo Arambha Tu Mo Sesha.

p: Before acting she presented television programmes such as Phone In, Apananka Saha and Rangina Duniya. Her first film, Tu Mo Arambha Tu Mo Sesha (2012), was directed by Nishikanta Dalabehera and also marked Subhashis Sharma's first lead role after years in character parts; Mihir Das, Pushpa Panda, Salil Mitra and Pragyan Khatua were in the supporting cast.

In 2013 she appeared with Deepak Barik in Raj Pradeep's Sapanara Nayika. In Susant Rath's Khaas Tumari Paain (2014) she shared the screen with Dushmant Panda and Debjani. She acted opposite Sambit Acharya in Dillip Panda's Lekhichi Naa Tora (2015), and again with Deepak Barik in Asilu Jebe Tu Jaana Pheri (2016), directed by Babuda and Dipun.

facts: Tu Mo Arambha Tu Mo Sesha (2012)

Q60500309.lead: Sofia Alam is an Odia actress who works mainly in television serials and Odia films; she began on television in 2001 and entered films in 2009.

p: Alam is the elder daughter of the Odia singer Mohammed Sikandar Alam. Her mother, Naima Alam, is a singer and an approved artist of All India Radio, and her younger sister, Nazia Alam, is also a singer. She completed a commerce degree at BJB College and was preparing for a banking career when acting intervened.

In 2001 director Subrat Nayak offered her a role in the DD Odia serial Bidhatara Khela, which launched her career. She went on to lead the DD Odia serials Duhita and Mahayajna, and played character roles in ETV Odia's Bhagya Bidhata, Sanskar and Gayatri. She later played the heroine's mother in Rahichhi Rahibi Tori Pain on Zee Sarthak.

Her film debut was Dream Girl in 2009, and the same year she appeared in Suna Chadhei Mo Rupa Chadhei, alongside Siddhanta Mahapatra, Anubhav Mohanty, Bijay Mohanty, Mihir Das, Barsha Priyadarshini and Snigdha Mohanty, and in Aseem: Beyond Boundaries. She played Sandhya in ACP Ranbir (2012), Baisakhi in Prema Sabuthu Balaban (2013) and Nandini in Ganja Ladhei (2014), and also acted in Aashiq (2015).
Her father, mother and sister are all singers.

Q112625327.lead: Ashutosh Mahapatra is an Odia jatra playwright, lyricist, actor and director who has written more than 80 plays since 2003 and directed the Odia film Bajiba Lo Sahanai (2023).

p: Mahapatra was born in Redhua village in the Raghunathpur block of Jagatsinghpur district. His father, Kishore Mahapatra, was also a playwright, and Ashutosh was drawn to writing plays from childhood. At his father's wish he first completed his studies and worked as an engineer before taking up playwriting.

He began writing jatra plays in 2003. His first, Chari Chhakare Tini Jhia, was staged by Gouri Gananatya, and his second, Sundari Jhianku Duru Juhar, by Tulasi Gananatya. He has since written for troupes including Konark Gananatya, Rangamahal, Swarna Mahal, Shivani, Tarini and Baghajatin, and directs most of his own plays. Other works include Garibara Dukha Dekhichhi Kie, Shrabana Masara Sesha Rati, Station Kuli and Ardhangini.

As an actor he has played negative roles in television serials, gaining wide recognition for Gayatri on ETV Odia; his other serials include Muthae Sapana, Mausi, Bhagya Bidhata and To Aganare Tulasi Mun on Zee Sarthak. He directed the film Bajiba Lo Sahanai, released in 2023.

Q121789530.lead: Sudharani Jena (1942–2023) was an Odia film actress and gynaecologist who made her debut as a lead in Parinam (1961) and, after a long break, acted in Odia films from 1976 to 1994.

p: Jena trained in medicine and practised as a gynaecologist. As a student at medical college she won the Mihir Mukherjee Memorial award for best actress in college drama four years running.

Her first film was Biswanath Nayak's Parinam (1961), in which she played the lead under the screen name Geetisudha. She then stepped away from films and returned in 1976 as a mother in Gapa Hele Bi Sata, the first Odia colour film. Over the next two decades she appeared in films including Sankha Mahuri, Rama Balarama, Kaberi, Jheeati Sita Pari, Topae Sindura Dipata Shankha, Bhagya Hate Dori and Gadhi Janile Ghara Sundara.

Q15725325.lead: Samuel Sahu (1918–2000), better known as Babi, was an Odia stage and film actor and theatre director who acted in more than 20 Odia films, beginning with Sri Jagannath.

p: Sahu was born in Cuttack into a conservative Christian family and was brought up by his aunt, Minika Sahu. His acting began at Mission School, Cuttack, where he played the title role in a play called Mankada (The Monkey). After matriculating there, he earned a diploma from Odisha Engineering School.

He first worked as an engineer at Chakradharpur in Bihar, but left the job around the time of the Second World War and returned to Odisha to act with theatre groups. He joined Kalicharan Pattnaik's Odisha Theatres, founded in 1940, and in 1945 moved to Annapurna B, staying with the company for about three decades. Over his stage career he acted in more than 150 plays and directed more than 200.

His film career began with Sri Jagannath and spanned more than 20 films, among them Bhai Bhai, Sri Lokanath, Jayadeb, Lakshmi, Manik Jodi, Suryamukhi, Jeevan Sathi, Sadhana, Abhinetri, Bhai Bhauja, Kie Kahara, Bandhan, Sansar, Ghara Bahuda, Jajabara, Anutap, Abhimaan, Suna Sansar, Tapoi, Sita Rati and Hakim Babu (1985).

He received the central Sangeet Natak Akademi award in 1961, the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi award in 1970–71, the Jayadev Puraskar in 1984, the Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja Samman in 1990–91, the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Samman in 1998 and the Baishnab Pani Kala Samman from the Utkal Sahitya Samaj in 2000.

facts: Mission School, Cuttack; Odisha Engineering School

Q60617039.lead: Somesh Mohanty is an Odia actor from Brahmapur who works in television serials, films, jatra and theatre, and has also been a radio jockey; he made his film debut in Aila Re Odia Pua (2009).

p: Mohanty started out in Odia music videos; Emiti Ranga De Lo Phulaku, with Naina Das, was well received. His first television serial was Suna Kalasa on DD Odia, and while working on it he began presenting on 92.7 Big FM. He went on to act in the serials Panata Kani, Tulasi, E Gapa Mala Janhara, Unasi Kanya and Chha Mana Atha Guntha, and later in Kuanri Bohu on Tarang TV.

In films he began as a character actor in Aila Re Odia Pua (2009). He played the friend of Anubhav Mohanty's character in Kiese Dakuchi Kouthi Mate (2011), which also starred Barsha Priyadarshini, and appeared in Love Hela Emiti (2013).

He has also performed in jatra, playing the hero for a time with Eastern Opera in productions such as Chupchap Rati Tuptap Katha, Asichhi Mangala Grahara Jhia, Call Girl and Basantira Chithi Mukhyamantrinku.
He won Best Character Actor at the 6th Tele Awards for Rajakanya, and received the Youth Pratibha Samman in 2019.

Q117056383.lead: Partha Sarathi Ray (born 1981) is an Odia actor from Cuttack who works in feature films and short films, and who won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor for Hello Arsi.

p: Ray was born in Cuttack and grew up in Bhubaneswar, where he went to school. He graduated in history.

In 2004 he moved to Delhi and joined Barry John's theatre group, and later went to Mumbai, where he worked in a few Hindi films. He began his acting career in 2010 and entered Odia cinema in 2013 with Nai Separi Kanaka Gori. His performance in Phalguna Chaitra, directed by Sisir Kumar Sahu and Peenakee Singh Rajput, was praised by critics and audiences.
He won Best Actor at the 29th Odisha State Film Awards for Hello Arsi.

Q56617775.lead: Rajani Ranjan (born 1959) is an Odia film dialogue writer, lyricist, story and screenplay writer and occasional actor who has written songs and dialogue for more than 100 films since 1989.

p: He was born at Balakati. His father, Rabi Das, was a lyricist and his mother, Sushilaprabha, a singer, and music directors were regular visitors to the family home. An educationist by profession, he has served as principal of Debaraya College in Bhubaneswar.

Rajani Ranjan began as a lyricist with Ei Sangharsha in 1989, and first wrote both dialogue and story for Mo Bhai Jaga. His lyrics feature in films such as Prema Bandhana, Bou, Bhagya Chakra, Munna – A Love Story, Prem Rogi, Aaa Re Saathi Aa, Love Dot Com and Tiger.

As a dialogue writer his credits include E Mana Manena, Nandini I Love U, Dream Girl, Sanju Aau Sanjana, Pahili Raja, Bhul Bujhibani Mate, Loafer, Mate Bohu Kari Nei Jaa, Family No.1, Mu Premi Mu Pagala, Gud Boy, Tu Mo Arambha Tu Mo Sesha, Deewana Deewani, Sapanara Nayika, Aashiq, Samaya Bada Balaban and Jogi. He also wrote screenplays for films such as Love Dot Com, Pahili Raja, Family No.1 and Sapanara Nayika, and the story of Pilata Bigidigala. He made a guest appearance as an actor in Prema Adhei Akshyara (2010).
He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Lyricist for Bhagya Chakra in 2007 and for Best Dialogue for Mu Premi Mu Pagala in 2011, and received the Daya Nadi Samman in 2024.

Q56786154.lead: Hara Rath is an Odia film and television actor who began as an assistant director in 2005 and has played heroes, villains, supporting and comic roles since his acting break in Bande Utkala Janani (2008).

p: Rath went to school at Dharakote in Ganjam district, where he acted in many plays, and later won best actor awards at Aska, at Khordha College and at Utkal University.

He worked in many jobs in the Odia film industry, including make-up, production management, camera operation and editing, before serving as an assistant director on Jibana Mrutyu (2005) and Mu Tate Love Karuchi (2007). After a small role in Priya Mo Priya, he got a substantial part in Bande Utkala Janani in 2008.

His later films include Satyameba Jayate, Most Wanted, Matira Bandhana, ACP Ranbir, Akhire Akhire, Ame Ta Toka Shanda Marka, Mu Tara Kie, One Way Traffic, Kehi Nuhen Kahara, Hello in Love and Mimansa. For the title role in Jogi (2018) he kept his head shaved for three months.

On television he played the villain Jimmy, son of Jayiram Samal's character, in the ETV Odia serial Apa, and acted with Papu Pom Pom in Tarang TV's Excuse Me – Ethara Michha Kahibi. He has also appeared in the web series Gangs of Puri.
He married Falgu Satapathy on 11 December 2013.

Q7648813.lead: Susant Misra (born 1965) is an Odia film director and writer from Cuttack, trained at FTII Pune, whose films have been screened and honoured at international festivals, beginning with Indradhanura Chhai (1993).

p: Misra was born in Cuttack; his father is Mahindra Mishra. He holds a postgraduate diploma in screenplay writing and direction from the Film and Television Institute of India, Pune, completed in 1989.

His FTII diploma film, Nischal Badal, was shown in competition at the Oberhausen Film Festival in Germany. His first feature, Indradhanura Chhai (1993), won the Grand Prix at the Sochi International Film Festival in Russia and was an official selection in the Un Certain Regard section at Cannes in 1995. His second feature, Biswaprakash, also travelled to international festivals and won the National Film Award for Best Oriya Film (Silver Lotus) in 2000. Dharini, his third feature, was made in both Hindi and Odia, and he later made Joseph – Born in Grace (2019).

He has also made documentaries: Dhenkanal – A Multifaceted Paradise, Samarpanam on the Bharatanatyam dancer Malavika Sarukkai, and Pearls of Wisdom on Odia literature for the Children's Film Society, India. He teaches film at FTII, and through his efforts the Bring Your Own Film Festival (BYOFF) has been held in Puri since 2004.
Grand Prix, Sochi International Film Festival, for Indradhanura Chhai; National Film Award for Best Oriya Film for Biswaprakash (2000).

Q39972688.lead: Amelie Panda (born 1984) is an Odia music-video and film actress who appeared in more than 500 album songs and three Odia films, winning the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress for Tumaku Paruni Ta Bhuli (2007).

p: Panda was born in Jhargram, West Bengal, and has a sister. She studied at Maharshi College before starting her career in Odia music albums.

After acting in more than 500 album songs, she was given her first film role as heroine by director Raju Mishra in Jibana Mrutyu (2005), opposite Sunil Kumar, with Mihir Das, Munna Khan, Aparajita Mohanty and Uttam Mohanty in the cast.

In Chakradhar Sahu's Tumaku Paruni Ta Bhuli (2007) she played the sister of Anu Choudhury's character, again with Sunil Kumar as the hero. Her last film was Kunal Patnaik's Bhul Bujhibani Mate (2010), opposite Debasish Patra, with Samaresh Routray, Mihir Das and Pintu Nanda. She also acted with Debu Brahma in Dhanya Tume Sai Baba, a documentary film directed by Apu Kanungo. After her marriage she withdrew from acting.
She received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress for Tumaku Paruni Ta Bhuli, and a Rajiv Gandhi State Award.

Q15724025.lead: Govinda Tej (1928–2016) was an Odia film actor, writer, producer and director who won Odisha State Film Awards for directing Kaberi, School Master and Tunda Baida, and for acting in Bandhu Mohanty.

p: Tej was born at Amalapada in Angul, where he completed his schooling, and studied engineering at Cuttack Engineering College. He worked as a civil engineer and for a time as a teacher before leaving his job to act in films. He later received doctorates from Utkal University of Culture and from a university in Tirupati.

He began acting in films with Kedar Gouri (1954); his later acting credits include Dharitri, Mana Akasha, Krushna Sudama, Bandhu Mohanty, Naga Phasa, Gauri, Ramayan, Bhakta Salabega, School Master, Tunda Baida, Jayadeb and Raghu Arakhita (1997). Through his company New Life Production he produced Krushna Sudama (1976), his first film as producer.
As a director he made Ramayan (1980), Kaberi (1983), School Master (1985), Tunda Baida (1987), for which he also wrote the story, Jai Shri Ram (1999) and Gare Sindura Dhare Luha.

Outside films he was the founding director of the National Music Association in Cuttack, formed the amateur theatre group Srujani with playwrights Manoranjan Das, Dhiren Das and Ananta Mahapatra, and played a key part in presenting Odisha's Ghumura folk dance at the 1982 Asian Games.

He won four Odisha State Film Awards: Best Actor for Bandhu Mohanty (1977) and Best Director for Kaberi (1984), School Master (1985) and Tunda Baida (1987). He also received the Jayadev Puraskar in 1986, the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Samman in 2006, an ETV Odia lifetime achievement honour in 2012, and the Upendra Bhanja, Bhumiputra, Chinta O Chetana and Banichitra honours.
He died in Bhubaneswar in 2016.

Q21130234.lead: Subodh Pattanaik (1947–2017) was an Odia screenwriter, dialogue writer, playwright, short-story writer, lyricist and stage actor from Cuttack who wrote for more than 60 Odia films, beginning with Dandabalunga (1984).

p: His first screenplay was for Brajaraj Movies' Dandabalunga in 1984, and before that film's release he had also written dialogue and screenplay for Kie Kahara and Baje Bainsi Nache Ghungura. He went on to write films such as Mamata Mage Mula, Chaka Bhaunri, Jaiphula, Pua Mora Kala Thakura, Jaga Hatare Pagha and Sankha Sindura, contributing to more than 60 Odia films in all.
In theatre he wrote and acted in more than 50 Odia plays. His play Mahajatra was staged at the National Theatre Festival in Paradip in 2010.
He received the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award in 1990 in the one-act play category for his book Ho Bhagate.
He died in Cuttack in 2017, aged 70.

Q112131276.lead: Biraj Dash (1959–2022) was an Odia actor who worked across stage plays, radio drama, television serials, telefilms and feature films, and also wrote plays.

p: Dash was born in Kendrapara. He studied management in Mumbai and went on to hold a bank job alongside his acting work.

His first acting role came in 1979 in Bhagabata Tungi, a Doordarshan play produced by Akshaya Mohanty and broadcast from Doordarshan Sambalpur. He continued in productions such as Dekha Barsha Asuchi, Jhara Baula, Kapata Pasa and Bohu Katakiani; he also wrote Bohu Katakiani, which was produced by T-Series. He took villain roles in Sai Baba, Atatayi and Nagaphasa, and worked with Akashvani and Doordarshan as well as in some Hindi serials.

He entered Odia cinema in 1986 with Bagula Baguli, and later appeared in Golamgiri, Maa Pari Kie Heba, Ja Debi Sarba Bhuteshu, Prem Bandhan, Mo Bhai Jaga and Pua Bhangi Dela Suna Sansara. In 1989 he acted in the Bengali film Nyayachakra, directed by Prasanta Nanda.

His job kept him away from acting for 16 years. After retiring in 2019 he returned to the screen and appeared in Mana Mo Neigalu Re (2021). Besides Bohu Katakiani, he wrote the play Jay Bekari Jay Bhikari.
He was married to Binita Tripathy. He died in Cuttack in 2022.

facts: Bohu Katakiani; Jay Bekari Jay Bhikari

Q546833.lead: Anil Chatterjee (1929–1996), also known as Anil Chattopadhyay, was an Indian actor who worked mainly in Bengali cinema from the early 1950s to the mid-1990s, chiefly as a character actor.

p: Chatterjee was born at Balagarh in Hooghly and came from Calcutta. He went to school in Delhi, where he topped North India in the Senior Cambridge Examinations, and later graduated from St. Xavier's College, Kolkata. While at college he worked in theatre with Utpal Dutt.

Over his career he appeared in roughly 150 films, a few of them in Hindi. Although best known for character parts, he also took leading roles and occasionally played antagonists. He worked with the directors Satyajit Ray, Ritwik Ghatak, Tapan Sinha, Tarun Majumdar and Mrinal Sen, collaborating with the first three more than once.

He played the title role in Deshbandhu Chittaranjan, a biographical film on Chittaranjan Das, and his performance drew praise from Das's wife, Basanti Devi. On television he led the Doordarshan serial Naqab. He also served in the West Bengal Legislative Assembly after winning a by-election in the Chowringhee constituency as an independent backed by the Left Front.
He won the BFJA Award for Best Actor in a Supporting Role four times: for Agni Sanskar (1962), Sandhya Deeper Sikha (1965), Sagina Mahato (1971) and Raja (1976).
He died in Calcutta in 1996.

facts: BFJA Award for Best Supporting Actor (four times)

Q26972756.lead: Usasi Misra is an Odia actress who has played both sympathetic and negative roles in films, jatra, television serials and Odia music albums, and has also worked as a television presenter.

p: In 1983 she was a student at the Kendriya Vidyalaya in Farakka, Murshidabad, West Bengal. After a degree in zoology from Rama Devi Women's University she took a fashion design course in 1995, followed the next year by a diploma in export management.

Her Odia film work includes Yashoda (1996) and Bou (1998), and she has acted in more than 30 films, among them Maa Pari Kie Heba, Kashia Kapila, Dharma Debata, Dharmara Heba Jay, Sanju Aau Sanjana, Tu Tha Mun Jauchi Rushi, Dosti, Mu Premi Mu Pagala and Mu Eka Tumara. She has also appeared in two Telugu films, seven Bengali films and Chhattisgarhi cinema.

Television serials made her popular, and she has played lead roles in several of them. From 2001 she presented programmes on Doordarshan, including Kalyani. In jatra she began with Eastern Opera and from 2007 was associated with Bhairab Opera, Bishal Opera and Dibanjani Opera, heading productions such as Baleswar Bohu and Chhatire Rakhichhi Ratira Katha. She also featured in the Odia album Mane Jebe Lage Nian.
She received an Odisha State Film Award in 2011.
On 27 June 2009 she married the Bengali actor Ratan Lakshmani.

Q7288645.lead: Rama Narayanan (1949–2014) was an Indian film director, producer and politician who directed more than 100 films, many of them in Tamil.

p: Narayanan moved to Chennai hoping to write songs but instead found work writing film dialogue. With his friend M. A. Khaja he co-wrote dialogue under the shared pen name Ram-Rahim. He wrote the story, screenplay and dialogue of Aasai Arubadhu Naal in 1976, produced his first film, Meenakshi Kungumam, in 1977, and made his directing debut with Sumai in 1981. He also supplied the story for Punnami Naagu, starring Chiranjeevi.

During the 1980s he became associated with commercial films in which animals had central roles, and in the 1990s a number of his films took up Hindu devotional themes. He was noted for finishing films quickly and within budget. His 50th film, Veeran Veluthambi, had story and dialogue by M. Karunanidhi, and his 100th was Thirupathi Ezhumalai Venkatesa. In the 2010s he completed the comedy Siva Poojaiyil Karadi, starring Shiva and Udhayathara, which was never released in theatres.

Outside filmmaking, he was elected to the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly from Karaikudi in 1989, became chairman of the Tamil Nadu Eyal Isai Nataka Manram in late 1996, and led the Tamil Film Producers Council for three successive terms before resigning in 2011.
The Government of Tamil Nadu gave him the Kalaimamani award.
He was married to Radha and had two children. He died in Singapore in 2014.

Q64786173.lead: Munna Khan, also known as Muzibulla Khan, is an Odia film actor and Biju Janata Dal politician who was elected to the Rajya Sabha from Odisha in 2020.

p: Khan made his Odia film debut in Kasturi (1987). He first worked as a leading man in a few films and later moved into character roles. His films include Gangashiuli, Mamatara Dori, Jibana Dhara, Jibana Mrutyu, Sashu Ghara Chalijibi, Chaati Chiri Dele Tu, Akashe Ki Ranga Lagila, Mu Kana Ete Kharap, Mu Premi Mu Pagala, Tu Mo Suna Tu Mo Hira, Badhu Nuhen Mu Bandhu, Nai Separi Kanaka Gori, Selfish Dil, Kichhi Khata Kichhi Mitha and Premarutu Asilare. He is best known for Mamatara Dori (1989), Kie Kahara (1997), Mu Kana Ete Kharap (2010) and Mu Premi Mu Pagala (2011).
In politics he was first with the Janata Dal and joined the Biju Janata Dal after it was formed, briefly heading its minority cell. He represented Odisha in the Rajya Sabha from April 2020.

facts: Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha (Odisha), from 2020

Q48837852.lead: Swaraj Barik (born 1998) is an Odia film actor who began as a child artist in films and television and made his debut as a leading man in Tu Mo Love Story (2017).

p: Barik was born in Baripada in Mayurbhanj district, Odisha, and was drawn to acting from childhood.

He started acting as a small child in Samparka, a serial broadcast on DD Odia. His first Odia film was Chandi Parija's Rakate Lekhichi Naa (2006), and as a child artist he went on to appear in 19 films, including Pahili Raja, Samaya Hatare Dori, Hero, Akashe Ki Ranga Lagila, Pagala Premi and Suna Chadhei Mo Rupa Chadhei. He also acted as a child in Gayatri, a serial on ETV Odia.

In 2017 he took his first lead role in Tu Mo Love Story, which also introduced Bhoomika Dash as the heroine. After its success, his second release of that year was Laila O Laila, opposite Sanmira Nagesh.
For Tu Mo Love Story he received the best newcomer actor award at the Pratibha Samman ceremony of the film magazine Chalachitra Jagat.

facts: Rakate Lekhichi Naa (2006), as child artist
Chalachitra Jagat Pratibha Samman, best newcomer actor

Q112626109.lead: Pratibha Panda, born Pratibha Sahu, is an Odia actress and Odissi dance teacher who works mainly in Odia films and television serials.

p: She began acting after finishing school. Her first film was Panchu Pandav (1989), in which she played the daughter of Jayiram Samal's character. In the five years that followed she appeared in a small number of films, among them one with Prasanta Nanda, three with Sriram Panda, six with Mihir Das and one with Srikant Gautam. She also acted in some Hindi serials and took part in dance and drama programmes on Doordarshan.

After a road accident and her marriage she left acting. She returned in 2008 with Kalinga Putra, produced by Debananda Panda, and has since acted in television serials including Sunakalasa on DD Odia, Rajaniti on Tarang TV, Manini on Sarthak TV, Kumkum on Colors Odia and Kie Para Kie Apanara on Star Kiran. She runs a dance institution, Nrutya Pratibha, where she teaches dance.
At the time of her accident she was working as the heroine of Dadagiri, produced by Rabindra Panda. The two grew close during that period and later married with the consent of both families.

facts: Odissi dance teaching; institution Nrutya Pratibha

Q31801423.lead: Pinky Pradhan, born Sasmita Pradhan, is an Odia actress who also works as a model, television presenter and playback singer.

p: She was born in Ganjam district, Odisha, and was interested in dance before turning to acting.

Her acting career started with the Hindi serial School Days, and she later appeared in CID on Sony TV. In 2008 she became the first Odia woman to take part in, and win, a national MTV reality show. Her first Odia film was Je Panche Para Manda (2003), in which she played the heroine opposite Siddhanta Mahapatra; her other films include Target (2013) and Akhire Akhire (2014). She also acted in the mega-serial Abujha E Mana on Tarang.

As a presenter she has hosted Boom Shaka Laka on ETV, Big Break, and Grihalakshmi and Rosei Khas Katha Bindas on Sarthak TV. She has judged shows such as Raja Queen and Swara Odisha, and served as chief judge of Raja Queen Ek Saath on Sarthak TV. She has modelled in advertisements for LML Trendy and Bisleri, and has made several Odia modern and devotional albums, singing in some of those she appeared in.
During the 2014 elections she joined the Bharatiya Janata Party.

Q15725394.lead: Snigdha Mohanty is an Odia film actress who has played heroines, supporting parts and negative roles in Odia and Bengali films, and has led several television serials.

p: She was born in Bhubaneswar and took up acting as a profession after completing a postgraduate degree at Utkal University.

Her film career dates from Agni Parikshya (1980); she was also introduced as a newcomer in Lal Paan Bibi, released in January 1988. Her Odia films include Baje Bainshi Nache Ghungura, Sasti, Kalia Bharasa, Asha, Mahua, Mukti Mashal, Santana, Singha Bahini, Pabitra Bandhana, Sashu Hatakadi Bhauja Bedi, Tate Mo Rana, Sashu Ghara Chalijibi, Kalishankar, Chaka Chaka Bhaunri, Nandini I Love U, Love Dot Com, Paribeni Kehi Alaga Kari and Prema ATM. In Mahua she acted alongside Sriram Panda.
On television she starred in Swabhiman and Ambika Khudinka Handisala, both broadcast on Tarang TV. She also works for India Post.
She received the Show Time award for best character actress in 2012.
She is married to Jayprakash Mohanty, a director of albums and films. Their daughter, Sambhabana Mohanty, is an actress and singer.

facts: Show Time award, best character actress (2012)
