Q28005751.lead: Dinabandhu Das (1919–1992), popularly called Tima, was an Odia stage and film actor known for comic and character roles.

p: Das worked on stage and in Odia films, and was especially associated with comedy. He became a familiar voice in Odia homes through radio plays broadcast by Akashvani Cuttack and through its programme Krushi Sansar, in which he played the popular character 'Mausa' alongside Krishnachandra Pande as 'Manguli'. On stage he was among the artists to whom the 1966 play Ambapalli was entrusted, together with Krishnachandra Pande. In film he was part of the large cast of Stree, which also featured Gaura Prasad Ghosh, Parbati Ghosh and Jadunath Routray.

Q60220750.lead: Kavya Keeran is an Indian actress and model who works mainly in Odia films and has twice received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress.

p: Keeran was born in Bhubaneswar. As a child she trained in Indian classical music, and her interest in theatre led her to Odissi dance and drama. She took part in many stage and cultural programmes at school and college.

Her first Odia film was Kaunri Kanya (2013), described as the first Odia 3D film. She then moved to Mumbai and worked in two Hindi films, Rang-e-Ishq and Ram Ratan, and appeared in a music video jointly produced by T-Series and the Times Group. Back in Odia cinema she acted in Rahasya (2018), Khusi (2019) and Sahid Raghu Sardar (2021). In 2022 she featured in Rishi Singh's music video Tu Ki Kitta.

She won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress for Khusi at the 31st awards, and won the same category again for Sahid Raghu Sardar. She also received the Chalachitra Pratibha Samman for best actress in 2021 for Bhoka.

facts: Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress (Khusi; Sahid Raghu Sardar)

Q29033627.lead: Jina Samal, born Swati Samal, is an Odia actress who works in films and television serials and has appeared in Odia music albums and as a judge on television shows.

p: Before films she acted in Odia modern albums such as Batoire Batoi, Sei Barsare and Sanja Nain Gale. She made her film debut as the heroine of Pheria Mo Suna Bhauni (2007). Her other films include Gaddbadd, To Pain Nebi Mu Sahe Janama, Bhaina, Kana Kala Se, Dream Girl, Galpa Nuhen Alpa Dinara, To Bina Mo Kahani Adha, Jhiata Bigidigala and Premara Nisha Niara Niara.

Her television career began with Tulasi on ETV Odia, after which she played the lead in Apa on the same channel. She later left Apa for Kemiti E Bandhan on Tarang TV. She was a mentor on Raja Queen on Sarthak TV, a judge on Mun Khanti Odia Jhia on Tarang TV, and captain of the women's team on Tarang's Ki Versus Ka. From 1 September 2017 she headed Tarang TV's Jinara Jibanasathi, a programme meant to choose her husband.
She received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress for her first film, Pheria Mo Suna Bhauni.
She has been married to Rudra Panigrahi since 2017.

knownFor: To Pain Nebi Mu Sahe Janama (2007)
facts: Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress

Q105671622.lead: Elli Padhi, born Rashmita Padhi, is an Odia actress and television presenter who works in Odia films and serials; her film debut was Ae Milana Juga Jugara (2010).

p: Padhi was born in Bhadrak, Odisha.

She started out in Odia music albums and drew attention with titles such as Taja Khabar and Sohala Puri Satara Hela. Her first film, Ae Milana Juga Jugara (2010), also featured Rajdeep, Chandan Kar, Minaketan, Biju Badajena, Pushpa Panda and Asit Pati. She later acted in 2014 Fear of the Year and Rasta.

On television she appeared in Abujha E Mana on Tarang TV, alongside Jina Samal and Lawrence Barik, and in the serials Tulasi, Sindura and Apa. She has also hosted programmes such as Kie Jite Kie Hare on Tarang Music.
She won the best actress award at the 6th Odisha State Television Awards for Tupur Tapur.
On 25 January 2019 she married Srimay Kumar Panda, a businessman and childhood friend.

facts: Odisha State Television Award for best actress (Tupur Tapur)

Q29046055.lead: Tripura Mishra is an Odia film actress who worked in films between 1975 and 1988 and later became a college lecturer; she is the wife of actor Sriram Panda.

p: Mishra was born at Shyamasundarpur Sasan in the Khallikote area of Ganjam district. Her mother, Pushpalata Mishra, was her first music teacher. She earned a master's degree in history from Berhampur University and later a doctorate for research on festivals in history.

Her first film was Jajabara (1975), followed the same year by Samaya. She appeared in Sindura Bindu and Krushna Sudama in 1976, Tapasya in 1980, Manasi in 1981, Subarna Sita in 1983 and Kurukshetra in 1988. After 1992 she gave up acting and joined a college as a lecturer.
She was honoured as a jury member at the 26th Odisha State Film Awards. On 4 February 2018 she received a lifetime achievement honour at the 12th Show Time film and television awards.
She married actor Sriram Panda in 1978, and they have two children. After Sriram Panda renounced family life in 1992, she brought up their children on her own.

Q15724840.lead: Biplab Roy Chowdhury (1942–2012) was a film director, editor and writer who made films in Odia, Bengali and Hindi, more of them in Odia than in his native Bengali.

p: Roy Chowdhury left his medical studies unfinished to work in films. He began as an assistant director under Ardhendu Chatterjee and worked as an assistant editor on about 20 films before taking on films himself as chief editor, writer and director. His first Bengali film as director, Barna Bibarna, was released in 1975. Over three decades he made about 14 or 15 short and documentary films and roughly 10 feature films.

His first Odia film, Chilika Teerey, dealt with the lives and struggles of the fishing communities of Chilika; it received national acclaim and won the Swarna Kamal at the National Film Awards. Two later Odia films, Aranya Rodan and Nirbachana, also won the Swarna Kamal, in 1994 and 1995.

He headed the direction and editing departments at the Satyajit Ray Film and Television Institute, was nominated a member of the Biju Patnaik Film and Television Institute in 1989, and served as a director of Kalinga Studio. At the invitation of the United States government he visited studios, universities and other film institutions there.
He died in Kolkata in 2012.

facts: National Film Award (Swarna Kamal) for Chilika Teerey, Aranya Rodan and Nirbachana

Q2792151.lead: Jayiram Samal (born 1948), also known as Jayee, is an Odia actor known chiefly for comic roles, with a career in Odia cinema that began in 1975.

p: Samal was born at Kumuda Jaipur, near Mahanga in Cuttack district.

He started acting in the 1970s as a comedian, making his debut in Jajabara (1975), and became recognised for his distinctive laugh. He has also taken negative roles in some films. He is credited in more than 300 works across film, television serials and theatre, including over 217 Odia films.

His films include Krushna Sudama, Ae Nuhen Kahani, Naga Phasa, Balidan, Janmadata, Pati Patni, Sautuni, Arati, Bilwa Mangala, Maan Abhiman, Basanti Apa, Kaberi, Jheeati Sita Pari, Jaga Balia, Janani, Jaaiphula, Hakim Babu, Jaga Hatare Pagha, Jor Jaar Mulak Taar, Thili Jhia Heli Bohu, Anti Churi Tanti Kate, Sabitree, Sindura Nuhein Khela Ghara and Om Sai Tujhe Salaam.

In 2008 he and the singer Raghunath Panigrahi received lifetime achievement awards at the 40th Banichitra Awards, given by Banichitra film magazine. His other honours include the Fit Fat Bioscope award (2007), the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Samman (2009) and the Mohan Sundar Deb Goswami Award (2022).

facts: Banichitra Lifetime Achievement (2008); Mohan Sundar Deb Goswami Award (2022)

Q56121136.lead: Sradha Panigrahi is an Odia actress who works in films, television serials and web series, and who entered acting through the 2015 reality show Mitha Mitha Jodi.

p: In 2015 she competed in Mitha Mitha Jodi, a reality show on ETV Odia. She reached the final without winning, and was given a role in the show's film, Mitha Mitha, which became her first film.

On Tarang TV she played Nandini in the serial Ama Ghara Laxmi, which also featured Snigdha Mohanty and Mamuni Panda. From 2020 she played the lead in Mo Dehe Boli De To Ranga Kala on Manjari TV, alongside Jyoti Prakash Panda, Priyambada Ray, Bhupati Tripathy, Akshaya Bastia, Dushmanta Pati and Kedar Mishra.

Her web series include Adha Lekha Chithi, Saheb Bibi Aur Sala and Saheb Bibi Aur Sasuma. She acted in a short film released on YouTube in 2018 and in Mukha, a short film released on Aao NXT in 2021. In 2021 she was the heroine of Bisarjan, released on Manjari TV for Women's Day, with Subhasis Sharma, Lawrence and Aniket.

facts: Ama Ghara Laxmi; Mo Dehe Boli De To Ranga Kala
Adha Lekha Chithi; Saheb Bibi Aur Sala; Saheb Bibi Aur Sasuma

Q15724688.lead: Prasant Padhi (born 1961) is an Odia music director and singer who has composed and sung for devotional and modern song albums and scored more than 20 Odia films as well as several Bengali films.

p: Padhi was born in Debiti village near Paralakhemundi. His parents loved music, and his father sang Krishna Leela and kirtan. He began learning music and harmonium as a child, studying under teachers including Satyanarayan Panda, Kishore Patnaik, Umamani Patnaik, Bhaktabatsal Patra, Pushpabeni Patnaik and Guru Gostha Chandra Patra. He attended M.R. High School, Sonepur, and studied at Sri Krushna Chandra Gajapati College, Paralakhemundi.

After his studies he joined the Industries Department as an Industry Promotion Officer in Cuttack, where he also learned Hindustani classical music from Guru Gopal Chandra Panda. His growing musical commitments eventually led him to leave the job. He was recognised as an approved artiste of Akashvani in 1990.

He began as a composer and singer of bhajan albums and went on to compose many modern albums. He entered Odia cinema in 2008 with Nandini I Love U, whose songs became popular and brought him wider attention.
He received Banichitra awards in 2008 and 2009 and the Tarang Cine Samman in 2010.

facts: M.R. High School, Sonepur; S.K.C.G. College, Paralakhemundi

Q7653795.lead: Swapan Saha (born 1930) is an Indian film director, producer, story writer and score composer associated mainly with Bengali cinema.

p: Saha directed a long run of Bengali films from the early 1990s onward, starting with Bedenir Prem (1992) and including Maan Samman, Biswas Abiswas, Naginkanya, Bhai Amar Bhai, Jhinukmala, Matir Manush, Nag Nagini, Satyam Shivam Sundaram, Kurukshetra, Sajani, Coolie, Agni, MLA Fatakeshto, Minister Fatakeshto, Golmaal, Achena Prem and Shrestha Bangali (2017). His Ei Ghar Ei Sansar (2000) was a remake of the 1996 film Ei Ghor Ei Songsar. He also produced Manush Kano Beiman (1999).

Q15724868.lead: Buddhaditya Mohanty is an Indian actor and television presenter who works in Odia films and in Hindi television serials, based in both Mumbai and Odisha.

p: Born Gumphul in Sheikh Bazar, Cuttack, he went to Stewart School in Cuttack, then studied at Ravenshaw College and later at Delhi University.

His first Odia film was I Love My India. He went on to appear in Nandini I Love U (2008), Prem Rogi (2009), Pagala Karichi Paunji Tora (2009), Tu Thile Mo Dara Kahaku (2010), Sanju Aau Sanjana (2010) and Loafer (2011).
In Hindi television he has acted in serials including Meher, Stree – Teri Kahani, Kumkum, Waaris, Prratima and Kya Hua Tera Wada. In Odia television he appeared in Srimandira on Tarang TV in 2021.
He is the son of actress Malavika Ray. The actresses Mahasweta Ray and Aparajita Mohanty are his aunts, Uttam Mohanty is his uncle, and the actor Babushan Mohanty is his cousin.

facts: Stewart School, Cuttack; Ravenshaw College; Delhi University
Malavika Ray (mother); Mahasweta Ray, Aparajita Mohanty (aunts); Uttam Mohanty (uncle); Babushan Mohanty (cousin)

Q16202345.lead: Shiju Abdul Rasheed (born 1974), known as Shiju AR, is an Indian actor who works mainly in Malayalam and Telugu films and also in Malayalam television.

p: He was born in Kollam, Kerala, and studied at St Albert's School, Ernakulam, and SSM Polytechnic College, Tirur.

His first film role, and first success, was as the villain in the Tamil film Mahaprabhu (1996), directed by A. Venkatesh. He then played the lead in Kodi Ramakrishna's Telugu film Devi, which earned him the screen name Devi Shiju in Telugu cinema; in Tamil he has been credited as Vishal. Further Telugu films included Manasantha Nuvve, Nuvvu Naaku Nachav, Simharasi and Ammayikosam, and in Malayalam he acted in Ishtamanu Nooru Vattam, King Solomon, Kalachakram, Sidhartha and Vachalam. He also appeared in the international film In the Name of Buddha, directed by Rajesh Touchriver.

In 2004 he stepped back from films to work in television serials, returning to cinema in 2013 with Proprietors: Kammath & Kammath. Later Malayalam films include Sound Thoma, Polytechnic, Dolphin Bar, Cousins and Pullipulikalum Aattinkuttiyum, and later Telugu work includes Kirrak Party, Supreme, Bluff Master, Sathamanam Bhavati, Taxiwaala and Godse. He has acted in over 50 films in Malayalam, Telugu, Tamil, Kannada and English, and returned to Malayalam television with the serial Neeyum Njanum on Zee Keralam.

facts: St Albert's School, Ernakulam; SSM Polytechnic College, Tirur

Q27244492.lead: Sanju Sivram is an Indian actor who works mainly in Malayalam cinema and has also appeared in Telugu films, including the Telugu-Odia bilingual Mindgame.

p: Sivram was born in Kolkata, where his parents were working, and spent his early years in his hometown of Oachira. He studied at St. John's in Kayamkulam up to the third grade, spent a year at St. Pius X Convent in Kuttikkanam, and finished high school at Chinmaya Vidyalaya, Thrissur. He then returned to Kolkata for a B.Com (Honours) at South City College and later completed an MBA in finance at Alliance University, Bengaluru. He worked for Tata AIA Life and Dhanlaxmi Bank, leaving the bank in 2012.

His first film was the Malayalam film Nee Ko Njaa Cha, directed by Gireesh, which was a major hit and is associated with the new-generation wave in Malayalam cinema. His role as Babukuttan in 1983 was well received. Other Malayalam films include Bharya Athra Pora, Monsoon Mangoes and Beware of Dogs, and he played the male lead with Vinay Forrt in Hello Namasthe, a light-hearted film about friendship. He has also acted in short films such as A Friday, Maniyara and The Chef.
He entered Telugu cinema in 2018 with Raktham – The Blood, directed by Rajesh Touchriver, and worked with the same director on the Telugu-Odia bilingual Mindgame.

facts: South City College, Kolkata (B.Com); Alliance University (MBA)

Q1018554.lead: Byomkesh Tripathy (1929–1997) was an Odia playwright, stage actor and director who worked on about 71 plays and acted in around 25 Odia films.

p: Tripathy studied at Ravenshaw College and completed a science degree at Calcutta University in 1958. He then trained in drama at the Asian Theatre Institute, which later became the National School of Drama.

He was associated with Annapurna Theatre and worked as a director or actor on roughly 71 plays. He wrote 13 original plays, among them Ek-Dui-Tin, Raja Mukuta, Kansakabata, Singhadwara, Jagarana, Tola Kania, Akhanda Jyoti, Suna Farua, Matira Swarga, Hema Harini, Gopana Katha, Sati Pariksha and Srikrushna Leela, and translated three: Raja Oedipus, Antigone and Mudra Rakshasa. His younger brother, Biswakesh Tripathy, gathered these plays into a five-volume collection.

In cinema he acted in films including Saptasajya, Jayadeb, Kaa, Ghar Sansar, Mamata, Bati Ghara, Mukti, Ulka, Kachaghara, Devajani, Bhakta Salabega, Abhilasha, Kandhei, Bhai Bhauja, Nirab Jhada, Mansara Bilapa, Sabu Mayare Baya, Udandi Sita and Bhagya Hate Dori.
He was honoured by the Central Sangeet Natak Akademi in 1978 and received the Jayadev Award in 1993.
He died in 1997.

facts: Ravenshaw College; Calcutta University (B.Sc.); Asian Theatre Institute
Jayadev Award (1993); Central Sangeet Natak Akademi honour (1978)

Q28941847.lead: Gungun is an Odia actress and presenter who began as a child artist and has hosted programmes on radio, television and stage.

p: She started acting as a child in the film Om Shanti Om. Her first role as a heroine was in Sakhi Rahila Ae Singha Duara, and she later played the heroine opposite Pupinder Singh in Kichhi Khata Kichhi Mitha.

Inspired by her mother, who worked as a presenter on Akashvani, she also became a presenter, first on Akashvani and then on Doordarshan and at stage events. On ETV Odia she co-hosted Phool Bobal with Pupinder and presented the live Sunday-morning show Phone In. She has compered various award ceremonies, hosted the second and third seasons of Malamal Express on Tarang TV, and presents Gapasapa on O TV.

facts: Phone In; Phool Bobal; Malamal Express; Gapasapa

Q15723794.lead: Omprakash Mohanty (born 1961) is an Odia composer and singer from Cuttack who works as a music director at Akashvani Cuttack and has scored Odia films and poetry albums.

p: Mohanty was guided in music by Guru Nabin Pattnaik and first performed on Shishu Sansar, a children's programme on Akashvani Cuttack. He later performed with the musician Prafulla Kar. As a young man he took up Western music and became an accomplished guitarist, and his playing led Akshaya Mohanty to invite him to work together. He turned down a job with the Indian Air Force to pursue music.
His first work as music director was the bhajan cassette Kalia. He entered Odia cinema with Bhagya Chakra in 2005, whose music brought him considerable success.

He has set the work of several poets to music: two albums titled Hati Saja Kara and another, Nua Luha Purana Luha, based on writing by Debadas Chhotray; Rubai, built on Omar Khayyam's Rubaiyat in Chhotray's Odia translation; Maya Darpana, from poems by Mayadhar Mansingh; and Dipa Jale Dipa Libhe, from unused poems by Akshaya Mohanty. He also works to popularise Odisha's folk and traditional songs.
Bhagya Chakra won him the Odisha State Film Award for Best Music Director for 2005; the film's singer Ratikant Satapathy won Best Singer the same year.

facts: Odisha State Film Award for Best Music Director (2005)
Hati Saja Kara; Rubai; Maya Darpana; Dipa Jale Dipa Libhe

Q26483885.lead: Minaketan Das (1961–2017), known on screen as Minaketan, was an Odia film actor who played villains and comic roles and also worked in television and jatra.

p: He was born in Kendrapara and studied at Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya.

Over a career of more than two decades in Odia cinema he appeared in over 100 films, mostly in supporting parts. Gangashiuli, released in 1984, was a turning point in his acting career, and he has also been credited with a debut in Sindura Nuhein Khela Ghara (2002). His films include Balunga Toka, Idiot: I Do Ishq Only Tumse, Deewana Deewani, My Love Story and Jie Jaha Kahu Mora Dho.
Alongside cinema he acted on television, and in jatra he both directed and performed in productions.
He received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Supporting Actor for Mimansa (2016).
He was married to Kanchanbala Das. He died at his home in Balianta, Bhubaneswar, in 2017.

facts: Odisha State Film Award for Best Supporting Actor (Mimansa)

Q97974808.lead: Dilip Dutta (born 1942) is an Odia cinematographer who has shot Hindi and Odia films, documentaries and Hindi television serials.

p: Dutta was born at his maternal uncle's home in Heragohiri Sahi, Puri; his family's ancestral village is Maheshpur in Baruha Haripur, Jajpur district. He studied up to Class 5 in Bhadrak, passed his matriculation from Jajpur in 1956–57 and completed his I.Sc. at BJB College in 1959. He first worked in the finance department of the state secretariat before leaving to study cinematography in Bangalore.

After finishing his course in 1963 he went to Bombay and on 29 September that year began working at Guru Dutt Studio. His first assignment was as assistant cinematographer on Ghazal, followed by Chhoti Si Mulaqat in 1964; over ten years he assisted on 12 films.

In 1974 he was chief cinematographer on Samaya, the first partly colour Odia film. He later shot Odia films including Sindura Bindu, Sakhi Gopinath, Samaya Bada Balaban and Nijhum Ratira Sathi. He made seven documentaries for the Odisha government's film division, one of which, Folk Paintings of Odisha, gained international recognition. He has been cameraman on more than 6,000 episodes of about 24 Hindi serials, and has also worked on a French film as well as Bengali, Marathi and Bhojpuri films.
He is married to Anjali, from Firingi Bazar in Cuttack.

Q15725133.lead: Ramachandra Pratihari (1936–2019) was an Odia stage and film actor and theatre director who acted in more than 200 plays, directed over 100, and appeared in over 20 Odia films and one Hindi film.

p: Pratihari was born in Harachandi Sahi, Puri. Poverty cut short his schooling, but he was drawn to music from childhood. Between 1952 and 1957 he worked as a cook at the Jagannath Temple.

He first drew attention in 1951 playing Shakuni in the mythological play Karnarjuna, staged by Utkal Natya Sangha. His childhood friend Jagabandhu Mishra introduced him to the Annapurna Theatre, and in 1961 he started work at its camp in Berhampur on a wage of four annas. In 1966 he founded the Mancharupa Natak Academy and in 1986 the Shilpi Natak Academy, through which he staged realistic drama. He worked across theatre as a musician, actor and director, in plays such as Kalapahada, Bakshi Jagabandhu, Bhai Bhauja, Manika Jodi, Ghara Sansara, Kansakabata, Singhadwara, Baisi Pahacha, Debajani, Matira Manisha and Hotel Monalisa, as well as the Hindi plays Payal, Kangan and Bandhan.
He had been an approved artiste of Akashvani since 1957. His film career began with Nua Bou in 1962, and he went on to act in more than 24 Odia films.

He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor in 1979 for Nilamadhaba. He also received the Jayadev Award (2007), the Kanak Manjari Bhumiputra Samman (2011) and the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Samman (2012).

facts: Mancharupa Natak Academy (1966); Shilpi Natak Academy (1986)
Odisha State Film Award for Best Actor (1979); Jayadev Award (2007)

Q18574281.lead: Biren Routray (1939–2014) was an Odia playwright and actor, known on stage, television and film for villain roles.

p: Routray was born in Meria Bazar, Cuttack, the eldest son of a family from Jagatsinghpur. He took a B.Sc. at Ravenshaw College and an engineering degree from REC Burla, then worked as an engineer in several state government departments, retiring as chief engineer of the Housing Department.

He began acting on stage in 1955 and went on to perform in more than 200 plays, over 35 films and on television. He also wrote many plays, including Kasturi Mruga, Trushna, Rana Pratap Singh, Jamukoli Gachha, Anga Raja and Bhanga Behelara Swara, and was connected with the magazine Natyashree. Through cultural organisations such as Chitrotpala and Sanskruti Bihar he worked to promote the arts.
His films include Bandhu Mohanty (1977), Anuraag (1980), Hisab Nikash (1982), Bhakta Salabega (1983), Dora (1984), Jaga Balia (1984), Lal Paan Bibi and Bhishma Pratigya (1992).

He received the Odisha State Film Award in 1983 as best character actor/villain for Bhakta Salabega, a best playwright award for Kasturi Mruga in 1969, an Odisha Film Journalist award and a Rotary award.
He was married to Banashree Routray and had two children, Rajkishore and Itishree. He died in Cuttack in 2014.

facts: Odisha State Film Award (1983, Bhakta Salabega)

Q20202218.lead: Ramananda Sengupta (1916–2017) was an Indian cinematographer who photographed more than 70 films, mostly in Bengali, including the Odia film Sri Lokanath (1960).

p: Sengupta was born in Dhaka and studied at Visva-Bharati University.

He started in 1938 as an apprentice at the Aurora Film Corporation in Calcutta, and was first assistant to G. K. Mehta on Kurukshetra (1941). His first film as an independent cinematographer was Purbaraag, directed by Ardhendu Mukherjee. When the French director Jean Renoir came to Calcutta to shoot The River (1951), Sengupta worked with him.

His other films include Raat Bhore (1955), Mrinal Sen's first film, as well as Shilpi, Headmaster, Megh, Nishithe, Teen Bhubaner Pare, Nagarik, Dakghar, Bindur Chhele and Kankabatir Ghat, and Utpal Dutt's Ghoom Bhangar Gaan. In Odia cinema he shot Sri Lokanath (1960). He also filmed documentaries such as Autobiography of an Elephant and Life in the Backwater of Malabar Cochin.

His life was the subject of Utsav Mukherjee's 2007 documentary Under Exposed, and of a book and a documentary, Alor Frame e Chhayar Saaj, by Siddhartha Maity. He reached the age of 100 in 2016 and died in Kolkata in 2017.

Q61552917.lead: Chakradhar Sahu (1961–2019) was an Odia film producer, director and editor who made both parallel and commercial Odia films and edited Hindi films and television serials.

p: Sahu was born in Titlagarh in Bolangir district. After a law degree from Utkal University, he joined the Film and Television Institute of India in 1988 for a diploma in film editing.

After the institute he worked in Mumbai, where he was associate editor on Shyam Benegal's serial Bharat Ek Khoj. He was co-editor on the Hindi films Patthar Ke Phool and Vishwatma, and editor on Karamati Coat and the serial Zameen Aasmaan. He also worked as an editor for O TV.
Back in Odisha he directed Nila Mastarani (1996). His other Odia work includes Indradhanura Chhai (1993), Tumaku Paruni Ta Bhuli (2007), Kebe Tame Naha Kebe Mu Nahi (2012) and Mimansa (2016).
He received Odisha State Film Awards for Best Editor for Nila Mastarani (1996), Best Director for Tumaku Paruni Ta Bhuli (2007) and Best Editor for Kebe Tame Naha Kebe Mu Nahi (2011).
He died in Bhubaneswar in 2019.

knownFor: Kebe Tame Naha Kebe Mu Nahi (2012)
facts: Odisha State Film Awards: Best Director (2007); Best Editor (1996, 2011)

Q49840836.lead: Nikita Mishra is an Odia film, television and stage actress who began as a child artist and made her debut as a heroine in Jogi (2018).

p: Mishra was born in Cuttack and was drawn to acting from an early age, also training in dance as a child. She studied home science at Indira Gandhi Women's College, Cuttack.

Her first film as a child artist was Samaya Hatare Dori (2007), followed by Neijaare Megha Mate, Tu Thile Mo Dara Kahaku, Prem Weds Priya, Mun Ashiq Mun Awara and Target. As a child she also acted in the television serials Basundhara, Dharmatma, Debi, Kaa and Shri Jagannath, and spent two years performing with the Annapurna Theatre.

She made her debut as a heroine in Jogi (2018), directed by Niranjan Behera, opposite Aryan Dash. Her later television work includes Neijaare Megha Mate on Tarang TV, Singhadwara on Manjari TV and Jhili on Zee Sarthak.

facts: Samaya Hatare Dori (2007), as child artist

Q61911477.lead: Tapas Sargharia is an Indian film director, screenwriter and actor who works mainly in Odia cinema; his directing debut was Pahili Raja (2010).

p: Sargharia began in Odia films as an assistant director in 2003. In 2007 he acted as a character actor in Hara Pattanayak's Pagala Premi, and in 2009 he was assistant director on Suna Chadhei Mo Rupa Chadhei. His first film as director, Pahili Raja, was released in 2010. He has since directed Ishq Tu Hi Tu, Tu Mo Love Story, Hero No.1, Chal Tike Dusta Heba and Babu Bhaijan.
He won the Best Story award for Ishq Tu Hi Tu at the 27th Odisha State Film Awards in 2015, and Best Director at the 8th Ruchi OFA in 2017.

facts: Odisha State Film Award for Best Story (Ishq Tu Hi Tu, 2015); Best Director, 8th Ruchi OFA (2017)

Q15724871.lead: Brundaban Jena (1944–2025) was an Odia lyric poet, film lyricist, playwright, short-story writer, dialogue writer and director who wrote songs for about 30 films and directed Sasti and Baata Abaata.

p: Jena was born in Chandol in the Patkura block of Kendrapara district. As a boy he learned chhanda, chaupadi, bhajan and janana from his grandfather Paramananda Jena, a pala performer. In 1973 he won a gold medal in Odia language and literature from Sambalpur University.

He became an approved lyricist of Akashvani Cuttack in 1965, and began writing film songs in 1972 with Dharitri, crediting producer Dhira Biswal and director Nitai Palit with bringing him into cinema. His popular film songs include 'Pirati Tora Duru Juhara', 'Gelabasara Dina Sarigala', 'Emiti Rati Se Je Abhula Smruti', 'Mo Priya Tharu Kie Adhika Sundara', 'Bana Pakhi Jhure' and 'Chandrika Tume Jhara Phula Pain'.

In all he wrote lyrics for around 30 films and the screenplay and dialogue for eight. He directed Sasti and Baata Abaata, both of which received national recognition. His plays include Rajasakshi, Poshabagha, Batikhunta, Ekabinsha Satabdira Gabesana Kendra, Shahjahan and Aloka.

He received the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award (2005), the Odia Gitikabi Samaj Samman (2006), the Odisha Sahitya Akademi Award (2008) for his lyric collection Priti Smruti Hoi Pheri Ase Jebe, the Fakir Mohan Gitishree Samman (2011) and the Nabarupa Raj Gitikabita Samman (2015).
He died in Cuttack in 2025.

facts: Pirati Tora Duru Juhara; Bana Pakhi Jhure

Q56442849.lead: Sambit Acharya is an Odia film actor who made his debut in Prem Weds Priya (2011) and has also worked as a judge on television talent shows.

p: Acharya was born in Bhubaneswar.

His first film was Prem Weds Priya (2011), and the same year he acted in Bandhan, Katak – The Silver City and Balunga Toka, playing a villain in the last. He followed with Bad Girl (2012), Salaam Cinema and Chowka Chhaka (2013), Omm, 2014 Fear of the Year and Ganja Ladhei (2014), and Lekhichi Naa Tora and Aashiq (2015). He made guest appearances in ACP Ranveer and Chhati Tale Ding Dong.

In 2017 Tamaku Dekhila Pare, with Jhilik Bhattacharjee, was released, and Happy Lucky followed in 2018. That year he was also cast in an Odia film and in his first Telugu film, Lalijo Lalijo, and later worked on Biswanath and Prema Pain Mahabharata.
On television he judged the third season of Kie Heba Mo Heroine on Tarang TV and the fifth season of Raja Queen on Sarthak TV.

facts: Judge, Kie Heba Mo Heroine (S3); Raja Queen (S5)

Q129435226.lead: Syamasundar Mohapatra (1927–1981) was an Odia jatra actor and playwright who founded the troupes Kalinga Natya Parishad and Manchapushpa and played Akrura in the film Mathura Bijaya (1979).

p: Mohapatra was born in 1927 into a zamindar family at Dhamnagar in Bhadrak district. After completing his I.A. he became a teacher.

While he was teaching, his maternal uncle Gangadhar Mohapatra invited him into jatra and handed him charge of a troupe he had formed at Saro, which Mohapatra renamed Kalinga Natya Parishad. His first role was Adhiratha in Raktapuja, written by Krushna Prasad Behera.

After Kalinga Natya Parishad closed he worked with Sarada Kalakunja of Nageshpur, then with Odisha Opera and Janani Gananatya. Returning to Saro he formed another troupe, Manchapushpa, which soon shut for lack of funds. His stage roles included Mir Qasim in Chandrasekhar, and he wrote plays such as Jatiya Pataka, Mahiyasi Mahila, Balya Bidhaba, Labakusha, Buniyad, Chhatrasal, Kharabela, Beiman, Pratidan and Sultan Mamud. In cinema he played Akrura in Mathura Bijaya (1979).
He received a Sangeet Natak Akademi award for jatra in 1980. The Shyam-Shakuntala Trust gives the Jatra Samrat Shyamasundar Mohapatra Smruti Puraskar in his memory.
He died in Bhadrak in 1981.

facts: Jatra Samrat Shyamasundar Mohapatra Smruti Puraskar

Q56061903.lead: Deepak Kumar (born 1957) is an Odia music director who began with a 1979 gramophone album and has scored Odia films since Dharma Nikiti.

p: Kumar was born in Cuttack on 8 December 1957.

His professional career started in 1979 as music director of an album released on gramophone record. Its songs included 'Kede Sundara Dise Kalia Hati', sung by Sikandar Alam, 'Se Ta Sabari Ainthha Khia', sung by Trupti Das, and 'Ahe Chakadola Daki Daki Mora Dina Kala Gala', sung by Pranab Patnaik.

He entered Odia cinema with Dharma Nikiti and went on to compose for To Akhi Mo Aaina (1999), Mahasangram (2000), Bidhata (2003), Hero (2011), Criminal (2011), Dharma (2013), Revenge (2016) and Jogi (2018). Songs from his film work include 'Nali Farak Bali Tora Dekhi Style', 'Suneli Suneli Khara To Muhan Sara', 'Tora Nahaka Nahaka Chali', 'Mun To Hero Gori Tu Heroine', 'Sankata Mochana Kesari Nandana', 'Gun Gun Gaye Bhaunrata', 'Ragicha Ki Katha Kahuna', 'Aji Ama Sanga Bahaghara' and 'Lal Gulabi Lal Gulabi Masta Dishuchhu'.

facts: Kede Sundara Dise Kalia Hati; Nali Farak Bali Tora Dekhi Style

Q55805797.lead: Anisha Sharma, born Anisha Das, is an Odia actress and fashion model known mainly for television serials on Tarang TV, who has also acted in Odia films and music albums.

p: Sharma was born in Sonepur and studied in Bhubaneswar, including a course in hotel management. Before acting she worked at the Taj hotel in Bengaluru.

She moved from Bengaluru to Bhubaneswar for the serial Swabhiman on Tarang TV, which brought her to public attention. With help from the actress Usasi Misra she also entered acting through the serial Uttaradayee, and went on to appear in Aaina. None of her family had been in acting.

In 2015 she made her film debut in Love You Hamesha, opposite Arindam Roy, and in 2017 she had a supporting role in Kabula Barabula. She has also appeared in the album songs Baje Bainshi Nache Ghungura, Niswasa To Bina and Diwana Diwani. Besides acting, she is interested in modelling, painting and costume design.

Her co-star in Swabhiman and Aaina, Subhasis Sharma (also called Mantu), became her husband. They were engaged on 18 March 2016 and married on 13 July 2016 at the Ramanageswar temple in Bidanasi, Cuttack, and live in Cuttack.

Q59404539.lead: Suman Maharana is an Odia film and television actor known mainly for comic roles, who began as a child artist in Kandhei Akhire Luha (2004).

p: Maharana came from a poor family and grew up in a slum area of Bhubaneswar.

He made his film debut as a child in Kandhei Akhire Luha (2004), winning a best child artist award for it, and later received a best comedian award for Laxmi Pratima. His other films include Priya Mo Asiba Pheri, Maya, Tu Mo Akhira Tara, Jagu Autowala, E Mana Manena, Hela Mate Prema Jara, Shubha Bibaha, Kichhi Khata Kichhi Mitha, Pahili Raja, Jabardast Premika, Aain Kanoon, Munna – A Love Story, Prem Rogi, Smile Please, Mu Premi Mu Pagala, Mu Kana Ete Kharap and Dharma.
On television he has acted in Pari on Sarthak TV and played Jadu in Tejaswini on Tarang TV, and has hosted programmes including Mun Bi Tejaswini.
At the 12th Show Time film and television awards in 2018 he was named best comedian for the Tarang TV serial Tejaswini.

Q110734693.lead: Subhasis Sharma, also known as Mantu, is an Odia film and television actor who has played heroes, character parts and villains since his film debut in Prema Adhei Akshara (2010).

p: Sharma began on Odia television as a character actor in Apa, an ETV Odia serial starring Debu Bose and Jina Samal. He then played the hero in Swabhiman on Tarang TV, his first lead role, and later acted in Aaina on Colors Odia and Durga on Tarang.

His first film was Prema Adhei Akshara (2010), in which he played Babushan's friend and the intended husband of Riya Dey's character. In 2012 he took his first lead role in Tu Mo Arambha Tu Mo Sesha, opposite Pinky Priyadarshini. His later films include Krishna Govinda, Nua Nua Premare, Kabula Barabula, Krazzy 4, Dekha Hela Prema Hela, Super Boy, Rudrani and Tu Mo Love Story 2.
On 13 July 2016 he married Anisha Sharma, his co-star in Swabhiman and Aaina.

Q15724385.lead: Narendra Kumar Behera (1943–1995), popularly known as Nari, was an Odia comic actor who appeared in 44 Odia films between 1968 and 1994.

p: Behera was influenced by his music-loving father and could play tabla and mridanga as a child. He had little interest in school and studied at Mission School, Cuttack. Hoping to become an actor, he ran away to Mumbai, but found no work there; he returned home, trained at an ITI and worked for a time as a mechanic.

His acting began on stage with the Kalashree and Annapurna theatres, where he performed comedy and entertained audiences by imitating the voices of other actors. His skill as a musician also brought him work with melody parties.

He entered films with Kie Kahara (1968) and acted in 44 Odia films up to Lakhe Siba Puji Paichhi Pua (1994), often alongside the comedian Shyamalendu. His films include Dharitri, Mana Akasha, Sindura Bindu, Shesha Shrabana, Amar Prem, Mukti, Naga Phasa, Priyatama, Gauri, Megha Mukti, Batasi Jhada, Baje Bainshi Nache Ghungura, Aashar Akash, Jaaiphula, Samay Bada Balaban, Nala Damayanti, Bhuli Huena, Tunda Baida, Papa Punya and Akashara Akhi.
He received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Comedian in 1988 for Kanyadaan.

facts: Odisha State Film Award for Best Comedian (1988, Kanyadaan)

Q6919077.lead: Moumita Gupta is an Indian actress and politician who works mainly in Bengali cinema and television.

p: Gupta has played prominent roles in Bengali television, including Neelima in Bou Kotha Kao and Amba Sarkar in Bhanumotir Khel. Her other serials include Ek Akasher Niche, Ekdin Pratidin, Khela, Rajpath, Erao Shotru, Saat Paake Bandha, Kiranmala, Stree, Mohor, Sarbojoya and Jagaddhatri.

Her Bengali films include Santan (1999), Annadaata (2002), Shubho Mahurat (2003), Nagardola (2005), Bhumiputra (2006), Mone Pore Aajo Seidin (2011) and Ebong Kiriti (2017). She joined the Bharatiya Janata Party in 2019.
She is the mother of actress Rimjhim Gupta and of Ved Chatterjee.

Q17279628.lead: Harihara Mahapatra (born 1975) is an Indian actor, comedian and politician who works mostly in Odia films and is known especially for comic roles.

p: Mahapatra was born on 23 December 1975 at Bhandaripokhari in Bhadrak district. Drawn to drama from childhood, he trained in acting at Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya and took up acting as a profession from 1990.

He entered Odia cinema with Sata Michha, directed by Raju Mishra. His films include Love Dot Com, Dil Tate Deichi (2010), Akhire Akhire, Pagala Karichu Tu, Haata Dhari Chaaluthaa and Katha Deithili Maa Ku. In 2017 he appeared in the children's feature film Sabas Biju, which was screened at the National Children's Film Festival in Rajasthan and the International Children's Film Festival in Hyderabad.
Beyond cinema he acts in and directs for the stage and television. He has been a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party since 2017.
He is married to Monalisa Mahapatra.

facts: Katha Deithili Maa Ku; Akhire Akhire; Pagala Karichu Tu

Q15724672.lead: Pradyumna Lenka (born 1953) is an Odia actor, film producer and college teacher who has acted in more than 100 films and plays and worked as producer or co-producer on about 21 films.

p: Lenka was born in Kapasi village near Niali in Cuttack district. He acted on stage from childhood and continued while at college, and in 1974, with help from Guru Krushna Chandra Singh, joined the Annapurna Theatre as an actor.

His first film as a producer, Puja, was released in 1981; he was co-producer on it and on Pua Mora Bhola Shankara (1996), and producer of Golamgiri (1987) and Arjun (2005). As an actor his films include Suhaga Sindura, Pua Mora Bhola Shankara, Ram Laxman, Sashu Hatakadi Bhauja Bedi, Babu Parshuram, Wrong Number, Bidhata, Arjun, Thank You Bhagaban, Pagala Premi, Nari Nuhen Tu Narayani, Dhauli Express, Agnisikha, Rasika Nagara, Mate Ani Dela Lakhye Faguna, Pagala Karichi Paunji Tora, Tu Tha Mun Jauchi Rushi, Swayamsiddha, Prem Weds Priya, Chocolate and Prema ATM (2022).
Teaching was his profession alongside film, and he retired in 2013 as principal of Alaka Mahavidyalaya.

Q18716606.lead: Niranjan Satapathy (1927–2015) was an Odia stage and film actor and director who founded the Janata Rangamancha theatre in Cuttack.

p: Satapathy was born on 27 August 1927 in Baunsalundi village near Bhanjanagar in Ganjam district. After passing his I.A. he joined the Air Force during the Second World War. He was later offered a post as a sergeant in the Odisha Police but turned it down to become a professional actor.

In 1953, with Biju Patnaik's help, he founded Janata Rangamancha in Cuttack, which ran until 2010. He also joined the Annapurna Theatre 'A' group and later its 'B' group in Cuttack, where his performance as Mr. Verma in the play Ghara Sansara made him a popular actor.
His Odia films include Sri Jagannath, Sahari Bagha, Ghara Bahuda, Alibha Daga, Ghara Sansara, Adina Megha, Jibana Sathi and Nijhum Ratira Sathi.

He received the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi award (1991), the Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja Award (2007–08), the Banichitra Samman (2011) and the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Samman (2014), along with the Sarala Award, the Kalinga Award, an Odisha Cine Critics Association honour, an Artist of the Century honour, the Manana Samman and the Panchamaveda Samman.
He was married to Saudamini. He died in Bhubaneswar in 2015.

facts: Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi (1991); Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Samman (2014)

Q60500400.lead: Ashwini Brahma is an Odia actor who has worked in theatre, television serials and feature films, and has won Odisha State Film Awards for both his film and television work.

p: Brahma was born at Ramachandrapur in Puri district. His father, Paramananda Rajguru, was a stage actor, and Brahma's interest in acting grew from watching plays while his father performed with the Annapurna theatre.
He began on stage, first working with the group Satabdira Kalakar; his first stage role came in a play by Dhira Mallick, and he later appeared in productions staged at Rabindra Mandap.
Brahma moved to television in 1998. His first serial was Mun Bhala Pae, directed by Harish Mohanty, and he has since acted in more than twenty serials.
His first Odia feature film was Gaddbadd (2013), in which he played two roles. He followed it with a villain's part in Superstar.
Brahma received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Newcomer in 2014 for Gaddbadd, and in 2015 the state award for best serial actor for Manini.

Q25644167.lead: Daitari Panda (born 1956), also written Daityari Panda, is an Odia jatra (folk theatre) performer known mainly for playing villains.

p: Panda was born in 1956 in Dukhanda village in the Oupada block of Balasore district. Because his family was poor, his schooling stopped at the seventh class.

To support the household he worked as a priest, as his father had, and as a farmer, and spent a period working in Kolkata. On the advice of Nityananda Padhi of Nilachakra Opera he joined Raghunath Panda's troupe, where his first play was Rohila Nabab, in which he played a commander; he also played Ali Hossain in Ram Rahim.

He then joined Haragouri Kalaniketan of Khaira, appearing in Kanhu, Kalapahad and Taapoi, and later worked with Sri Durga Gananatya of Dungura, Annapurna Gananatya of Chandol, Sri Durga Opera and the troupe of Bijay Ketan Mangaraj. His longest association has been with Konark Gananatya.

His jatra productions include Mudra Rakshasa, Kaha Lo Baula Kie To Bara and Saguna Basichhi Dena Melai. He played the lead in Hari Om Mu Kendrapada Baba, which earned a record ₹16 lakh at the Khandagiri Jatra Mahasamar in 2016. That year he was also praised for playing a transgender character in Maichia Gokhei Sahu.

Q19723498.lead: Sujata Anand was an Odia film actress who appeared in more than 50 Odia films between 1966 and 2000.

p: Her earliest listed film is Matira Manisha (1966), and her career continued until Mo Kanhu Re in 2000. Over these years she acted in films such as Kanakalata, Mamata, Chilika Teerey, Abhimaan, Tapoi, Maanini, Hakim Babu, Kurukshetra and To Binu Anya Gati Nahin.
Kichhi Smruti Kichhi Anubhuti, in which she acted, was honoured at the National Film Festival.
She received the Jayadev Award.
She was married to the film director Kumar Anand.

Q114369458.lead: Subhransu Nayak is an Odia actor who works mainly in Odia television serials and feature films, playing leads, villains and supporting roles.

p: In 1994 Nayak moved from Kamakhyanagar to Bhubaneswar intending either to study medicine or to become an actor. He instead completed an MBA and took up a job before turning to acting.

He started acting in 1999 with the DD Odia serial Sanskar, appearing in ten to twelve episodes. In 2001 he had his first leading role, in the DD Odia serial Duhita. He went on to work in serials on ETV Odia, Tarang TV, Sarthak TV and Zee Sarthak, including Kahara Hebi Mun Kandhei, Mahayagya, Kahile To Kula Kutumbaku Laja, Sanskar Bada Ghara Bada Gumara Katha, Abujha E Mana, Baby and Jeevan Sathi.

His film career began in 2009 with Chup Kie Asuchi. He has since played character, comic and villain roles in films including Mu Kana Ete Kharap, Love Station, Gunda, Sister Sridevi, Sundergarh Ra Salman Khan and Biju Babu.
He received an award at the 2nd Odisha State Television Awards for the serial Pita Prapita Pitamaha.

Q56621285.lead: Aryan Dash is an Odia film actor and Hindi theatre actor who entered Odia cinema with Jogi (2018).

p: Dash's family home is in Puri. His father is an Air Force officer, and Dash is based in Mumbai. He graduated in aircraft engineering and then trained at the Kishore Namit acting institute in Mumbai, after which he acted in a theatre production with Anupam Kher.

He worked as an assistant to Nana Patekar on a Kannada film and as an associate director on some other films. He also appeared in Odia music album videos, among them Sathiya, Premare Tora Deewana Heli and Mora Maa.

His first Odia film was Jogi, directed by Niranjan Behera, after producer Sridhar Martha offered him a part. He played the son of the state's chief minister, opposite Nikita Mishra. His next announced film was Jouthi Thile Bi Tu Mora, directed by Srikant Gautam.

Q20652472.lead: Dhira Biswal (1929–1995), born Dhirendranath Biswal, was an Odia film actor, producer and director who received the Jayadev Award in 1980 for his contribution to Odia cinema.

p: Biswal was born in Cuttack in 1929. His acting first drew attention while he was a student at Ravenshaw College, where his portrayal of Kansa made such an impression that friends began calling him by the character's name. He was elected drama secretary at Ravenshaw and later at Madhusudan Law College.

He first worked as an employee of the Odisha Secretariat, then left the job to study law at Madhusudan Law College. After earning an LLB he practised at the Orissa High Court, though he gave more of his time to acting than to the law.

His first film was Kedar Gouri, in which he played the villain Rahu. His other acting credits include Shree Shree Mahalaxmi Puja, Dasyu Ratnakar, Parinam, Kie Kahara, Dharitri, Naba Janma and Ramayan (1980).

In 1962 he set up his own production company, Panchasakha Pictures, whose first film was Nua Bou. He was involved in the production of around 50 Odia films; those he produced include Nua Bou, Manik Jodi, Naba Janma, Kie Kahara, Agnibeena and Gauri.
Biswal received the Jayadev Award in 1980. He also won Odisha State Film Awards for Dharitri and Agnibeena, and a best director award for Gauri.

facts: LLB, Madhusudan Law College; Ravenshaw College

Q29657132.lead: Kajal Mishra is an Odia film and television actress who made her feature film debut in Dharmara Heba Jay (2005).

p: Mishra started out in a short telefilm for Doordarshan and then appeared in Odia modern song albums, eventually featuring in more than 200 of them. She entered Odia cinema in 2005 with Dharmara Heba Jay.
Her later films include Thank You Bhagaban, Dhauli Express, E Mana Manena, Chaka Chaka Bhaurin, Lal Tuku Tuku Sadhaba Bahu, Neijaare Megha Mate, Aila Re Odia Pua and Sandehi Priyatama.

On television she acted in the ETV Odia serial Bada Ghara Bada Gumara Katha. Her role there as Anjali made her a familiar face in households across Odisha and brought her the widest recognition of her career.
In 2011 she married the Odia film actor Dushmanta Panda.

facts: Anjali in Bada Ghara Bada Gumara Katha

Q140387092.lead: Ramesh Mohanty (1943–2026) was an Odia actor and director of films, jatra and stage plays, who received the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for direction for 2022.

p: Mohanty was born on 14 November 1943 at Nimapada in Puri district.

He directed four films. Three were released: Batasi Jhada (1981), Para Jhia Ghara Bhangena (1985) and Sata Kebe Luchi Rahena (1985); the fourth, Gotie Ashanka Duiti Mana, was not. Para Jhia Ghara Bhangena was the first film to be shot at Kalinga Studio. As an actor he appeared in Sautuni (1979).

He began working in jatra in 1982 and directed 279 jatra productions, among them Phula Baula Beni, Mo Penkali Bajei De, Kancha Dahani and Mo Silata Sukhi Ja. With the theatre group Uttarapurusha he directed stage plays such as Bhanga Ainare Muhan, Moha, Mokoddama and Gandhi Bhumikare, and he later founded his own group, Ananya. In all he directed about 302 plays.

For more than four decades from the 1960s he worked as an engineer, retiring as a senior engineer, and he continued his work in the arts after retirement. He was an approved artist of All India Radio and Doordarshan.
He received the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award for direction for the year 2022.
Mohanty died in Bhubaneswar in 2026, at the age of 82.

Q99286177.lead: Sisir Mohan Pati (1956–2020), known in the Odia film industry as Butu, was an Odia film and television director whose first feature was Panchu Pandav (1989).

p: Pati was born in Cuttack on 24 February 1956.

He entered Odia cinema in 1984 as an associate director on Dora, directed by Prashanta Nanda. He went on to fill the same role on films including Jaga Balia, Hira Nila, Jaga Hatare Pagha, Kandhei, Maa and Ghara Sansar.

His debut as director, Panchu Pandav, was released in 1989 with Prashanta Nanda as producer; Pati also wrote its screenplay and dialogue. He then directed Raja Rani, Maa Pari Kie Heba and Aeithi Swarga Aeithi Narka, and later moved on to directing Odia television serials.
Pati died in 2020 at the age of 64. His last rites were held at Satichoura in Cuttack.

Q96473175.lead: Dipa Sahu (1985–2020) was an Odia actress who worked mainly in Odia music albums, television serials and films, beginning her film career with Nari Akhire Nian (2003).

p: Sahu was born on 25 October 1985 in Dhenkanal district.
Her first Odia film was Nari Akhire Nian in 2003. She followed it with Dharmara Heba Jay in 2005 and College Time.
On television she played the villainous Meera Debroy in the ETV Odia serial Bada Ghara Bada Gumara Katha, and she appeared in several other Odia serials.
Sahu featured in many Odia album songs, including popular numbers such as Hai Hai To Malli Phula Gajara, Tora Lamba Beni, Krushna Chuda Rangara Nali Odhani and Ekada Ekada Ra.
She died in 2020 at the age of 34.

facts: Meera Debroy in Bada Ghara Bada Gumara Katha

Q60629615.lead: Subas Rout (1956–2018) was an Odia film producer and politician who produced nine Odia films between 1988 and 1998.

p: Rout entered Odia cinema in 1988 through Suna Chadhei, a film made as a joint production. His first independent production, Bhagya Hate Dori, was released in 1993. He went on to produce Suna Panjuri, Laxmana Rekha, Jibana Sathi, Singha Bahini and Ram Laxman, and his last film as producer was Santana, released in 1998.
He also produced television serials, among them Tulasi, which aired on ETV Odia, and Bidhatara Khela.
Outside cinema, Rout was active in Odisha politics as a member of the Indian National Congress.
He died at his home in Chhatra Bazar, Cuttack, in 2018, at the age of 62.

Q15725370.lead: Sushant Mani, also spelled Susant Mani, is an Indian film director working in Odia cinema, who also works as an editor, writer and choreographer.

p: Mani began by editing and directing album videos for Sarthak Music. After a number of albums he moved into films as an editor and choreographer, and he has written the story and screenplay for some of the films he directed.

He made his directing debut with Aa Janhare Lekhiba Naa (2009). Later films include Abhimanyu, Aama Bhitare Kichhi Achhi, Most Wanted, Chocolate, Luchakali, Mu Eka Tumara, Akhire Akhire, Golapi Golapi, Lekhu Lekhu Lekhi Deli, Pagala Karichu Tu, Kehi Nuhen Kahara, Hello: In Love, Tu Kahibu Na Mu, Sapanara Pathe Pathe, Laila O Laila, Nimki, This Is Maya Re Baya and 2 Chocolate.

Several of his films are remakes: Abhimanyu of the Tamil film Chithiram Pesuthadi, Chocolate of the Telugu film Oy!, Mu Eka Tumara of the Kannada film Chandra Chakori, Akhire Akhire of the Telugu film Ishq, and Laila O Laila of the Marathi film Sairat. Luchakali was based on Sleeping with the Enemy.
Mani won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Editor in 2005 for Shaashu Ghara Chaalijibi and in 2007 for Mu Tate Love Karuchi, and the award for Best Screenplay in 2015 for Kehi Nuhen Kahara.

Q28946513.lead: Lipsa Mishra (born 1992) is an Odia film and television actress who began on the Tarang TV serial Kichhi Luha Piijaye Othare and made her film debut with Maya (2015).

p: Mishra was born in Puri. She studied for her +2 at Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya and then took an honours degree in Odia at BJB College, graduating in 2012 with the highest marks in the department, before going on to the Odia department of Utkal University. She started learning Odissi dance in the seventh class.
She won Big Break, a programme run by Tarang TV, and was cast as the heroine, Khushi, in the channel's serial Kichhi Luha Piijaye Othare.

After the serial ended she moved to films, debuting in 2015 with Maya alongside Anu Choudhury and Sunil Kumar. The same year saw the release of Pilata Bigidigala, a comedy directed by Basanta Sahu in which she appeared with Sabyasachi Mishra, Archita Sahu and Papu Pom Pom. In 2016 she acted with Pupinder Singh and Anubha Sourya in Samaya Bada Balaban.
Also in 2016 she appeared with Krishna Beura in Chehra Tera, a Hindi song produced by Zee Music that Beura also sang.

Q21565070.lead: Umakanta Mishra (1939–2021) was an Odia politician and actor who represented Bhanjanagar in the Odisha Legislative Assembly from 1985 to 1990 and acted in a few Odia films.

p: Mishra was born on 14 July 1939 at Sanakodanda in the Bhanjanagar block of Ganjam district. His father, Jagannath Mishra, was a social worker. After graduating in law he practised as a lawyer at the Bhanjanagar court.
He acted in a handful of Odia films and one Hindi film. His first Odia film was Amada Bata, and he also appeared in Abhinetri and in the Hindi film Bheegi Palkein, directed by Sisir Mishra.
In politics he worked for the Indian National Congress. He was elected to the 9th Odisha Legislative Assembly from the Bhanjanagar constituency in the 1985 election and served one term, until 1990.
Mishra died in Bhubaneswar in 2021.

Q29178250.lead: Debjani Deghuria is an Odia actress who played supporting roles in several films before her first lead role in Rangila Toka (2012).

p: Deghuria first acted in Tulasi, a serial broadcast on ETV Odia. She moved to films in 2006 with a supporting role in I Love My India, and in 2007 played the heroine's friend in Pagala Premi, directed by Hara Patnaik. Further supporting parts followed in To Bina Mo Kahani Adha, Lal Tuku Tuku Sadhaba Bahu, Rasika Nagar and Brajaraj Movies' Don (2010).

Her first role as heroine came in 2012 in Rangila Toka, opposite Papu Pom Pom, a film that helped her establish her own identity. She then played a parallel lead in Chanda Na Tame Tara and the heroine in Salaam Cinema, Khaas Tumari Paain and Ajatashatru.

Q61893591.lead: Ravi Shankar Patnaik (1948–2021) was a National Film Award-winning film editor from Odisha who edited Odia and Hindi films and received the Jayadev Award for 2017.

p: Patnaik was born in 1948 at Dattapada in Puri district. He completed his higher education at Samanta Chandrasekhar Autonomous College in Puri and then studied film editing at the Film and Television Institute of India in Pune.
He was the first film editor from Odisha. At the age of 23 he won a National Film Award for editing the Hindi film 27 Down. His first Odia film was Abhimaan in 1977.

His Odia editing credits include Arati, Mahasati Sabitri, Sankha Sindura, Dandabalunga, Badhu Nirupama, School Master, Kanyadaan, Majhi Pahacha, Jahaku Rakhibe Ananta, Topae Sindura, Andha Diganta, Ghara Mora Swarga, Hisab Karibo Kalia, Sahara Jaluchi, Pua Mora Jagata Jita and Hello Arsi. In Hindi he edited films such as Chalte Chalte, Swikar Kiya Maine, Kismat, Suchitra, Jeena Isi Ka Naam Hai, Ulta Seedha, Bhula Na Dena, Shayad, Dil Se Mile Dil, Aap Ki Khatir and 27 Down.
Besides the National Film Award for editing 27 Down, Patnaik received the Jayadev Award, Odisha's highest film honour, for 2017 in recognition of his lifetime contribution to film editing.
He died in Bhubaneswar in 2021.

facts: Film and Television Institute of India, Pune; Samanta Chandrasekhar Autonomous College, Puri
National Film Award for editing (27 Down); Jayadev Award (2017)

Q16732972.lead: Arpita Mukherjee is an actress from West Bengal who has worked in Odia, Bengali and Tamil films, entering Odia cinema with Bande Utkala Janani (2008).

p: Mukherjee was born in West Bengal.

Her Odia debut came in 2008 with Bande Utkala Janani, the last Odia film directed by Subhendu Swain, in which she acted alongside Sabyasachi Mishra, Siddhanta Mahapatra, Hara Rath and Minaketan. The same year she appeared in the Bengali film Partner.

In 2009 she played the villain in Prem Rogi, which starred Buddhaditya Mohanty and Barsha Priyadarshini. In 2010 she was the heroine opposite Anubhav Mohanty in Mu Kana Ete Kharap, with Mihir Das, Bijay Mohanty, Smita Mohanty and Harihar Mahapatra in the cast.

She went on to pair with Sabyasachi Mishra in Tora Mora Jodi Sundara and Kemiti E Bandhan, and with Akash Dasnayak in Raju Awara. Her other work includes the Bengali films Jor Jar Muluk Tar and Mama Bhagne and the Tamil film Chinnamma Love.

Q56162529.lead: Sulagna Mohanty is an Indian academic and Odia-language writer of short stories, novels and screenplays, whose story was the basis for the Odia film Phalguna Chaitra (2023).

p: Mohanty was born and grew up in Bhawanipatna, Kalahandi. She graduated from Utkal University and earned a PhD in English from IIT Bhubaneswar.

She began by writing short stories on social media and later wrote editorial columns for the daily newspaper Samaja. Her stories have appeared in various magazines and newspapers, and RJ Sangram recorded them for broadcast on Radio Chocolate under the title Kathatie.
Her books include the collections Nalichuda (2017) and Aanira Rosei Ghara (2019), as well as Paridhi and Bhalugoda, and two English e-books, 90's Nostalgia and Wild Flowers.
In cinema she wrote the story of Phalguna Chaitra (2023) and the screenplay of Baida (2025).
She was felicitated by Prime Minister Narendra Modi under the #SheInspiresUs programme.

facts: PhD in English, IIT Bhubaneswar; Utkal University

Q21281507.lead: Saudamini Mishra is an Odia film actress and Odissi dancer who made her screen debut in Kie Kahara (1968) and has also worked in Hindi film, documentary and television.

p: Mishra was born in Professorpada, Cuttack. The locality took its name from her grandfather, a former head of the chemistry department at Ravenshaw College. Raised in a joint family, she started learning Odissi at the age of four at Kala Vikash Kendra in Cuttack under Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra and Mayadhar Raut, and later took an MA in Odissi dance. She studied at Board School and Ravenshaw College.

Dhira Biswal, impressed by her dancing, offered her a role in Kie Kahara while she was still in the tenth class. Her grandmother objected and she declined, but she accepted when the offer came again after her marriage, and the film was released in 1968.

She went on to act in many Odia films, among them Anutap, Gapa Hele Bi Sata, Manasi, Ramayan, Ei Akhi Ama Sakhi and Kulachandrama, as well as the Hindi film Nishana. She made a documentary titled Kalahandi, which won a national award, acted in the Doordarshan serial Tulasi, and served on the script committee of Kalinga Studio.

facts: Odissi under Kelucharan Mohapatra and Mayadhar Raut
MA in Odissi dance; Ravenshaw College

Q7680192.lead: Talluri Rameswari is an Indian actress known mainly for Hindi and Telugu films. She has also acted in one Odia film and one Malayalam film.

p: She completed her training at the Film and Television Institute of India (FTII) in 1975. Rajshri's Dulhan Wahi Jo Piya Man Bhaye (1977) gave her the big break; it was a huge hit and made her a familiar name. The next year she took the title role in K. Viswanath's Telugu film Seetamalakshmi and won the Filmfare Award for Best Actress – Telugu.

Sunayana, opposite Naseeruddin Shah, Mera Rakshak, with Mithun, and Sharda and Aasha, both with Jeetendra, are among her other well-known films; Aasha earned her a Filmfare nomination for Best Supporting Actress. Her television work includes Padosi (1985), Ganadevta (1987–88), Mitwa Phool Kamal Ke, Babul Ka Aangann Chootey Na, Nanhi Si Kali Meri Laadli, America Ammayi and Jhansi (2022–23). She stepped away from acting for some years to bring up her children, came back in the 2000s, and has lately worked mostly in television series.

Her husband, the Punjabi actor-producer Deepak Seth, was a fellow student at FTII. The couple produced the Hindi film Hum Farishte Nahin (1988) and the Punjabi film Mein Tuun Assin Tussin (2007), an adaptation of Shakespeare's The Comedy of Errors.

knownFor: Dulhan Wahi Jo Piya Man Bhaye
facts: Film and Television Institute of India (1975)
Filmfare Award for Best Actress – Telugu (Seetamalakshmi)

Q27921608.lead: Ashok Swain (1948–2018) was an Odia cinematographer who shot more than 30 Odia films over a 40-year career and received the Jayadev Award in 2015 for lifetime contribution.

p: Swain was born in Cuttack on 10 January 1948. He took a diploma in cinematography from SJ Polytechnic in Bengaluru.

He began working in 1969, and early on found work at film studios in Chennai and at RK Studios in Mumbai. In 1970 he was an assistant cameraman on The Black Mountain, an Indo-Russian children's film, and in 1973 he joined Doordarshan Kendra, Cuttack.

His first Odia film as cameraman was Samar Salim Saiman in 1977. He went on to shoot films including Batasi Jhada, Mu Tume O Se, Para Jhia Ghara Bhangena, Sesha Pratikshya, Puja Phula, Sahari Bagha, Nala Damayanti, Chha Mana Atha Guntha, Bhuli Huena, Jayadev, Bada Bhauja, Shasti, Hisab Karibo Kalia, Dadagiri and Gopare Badhuchhi Kala Kanhei. He also shot many documentaries, television films and serials.
Swain received the Jayadev Award in 2015 for his lifetime contribution.
He died in Cuttack in 2018.

facts: Diploma in cinematography, SJ Polytechnic, Bengaluru

Q56512632.lead: Biju Badajena is an Odia film and television actor who began his film career with Mo Mana Khali Tori Pain and has acted in more than 50 films.

p: Badajena made his debut in Odia cinema with Mo Mana Khali Tori Pain. His later films include Dharmara Heba Jay, Babu I Love You, Tate Mo Rana, De Ma Shakti De, To Bina Mo Kahani Adha, Munna – A Love Story, Aa Re Saathi Aa, Dil Tate Deichi, Ae Milana Juga Jugara, Family No. 1, Baishi Pahache Kheliba Meena, Mu Premi Mu Pagala, A.C.P. Sagarika, Mita Basichi Mu Bhuta Sathire, To Bata Chahinchi Rati Sara, Tame Thile Sathire, Maya, Rangila Baba, Excuse Me Kana Kala Se and Jogi.
Alongside films he has acted in Odia television serials, including Savitri, Mahayagya and Gayatri.

Q27044150.lead: Bishnu Mohan Kabi (born 1987) is an Odia singer who came to attention by winning the first season of Tarang TV's Voice of Odisha in 2011 and now works as a playback singer in Odia films.

p: Kabi was born in Jiritala village under Khantapada police station in Balasore district. He started formal music lessons at the Bharatiya Nrutya Sangeeta Kala Parishad while in the seventh class. He completed his +2 at Baisinga College in Mayurbhanj district and a diploma from NIMS, then took a bachelor's degree in music from the Harekrushna Behera College of Art and Culture and a master's in music from Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya in Bhubaneswar. His teachers have included Gouranga Charan Pradhan, Ramhari Das, Dhiraj Mohapatra, Pradeep Patra and Ravishankar Narayan.

Before entering Voice of Odisha, Kabi spent some years working as a medical representative and at a private nursing home. The competition proved a turning point: he was chosen as its best singer, and the win opened his way into Odia cinema.
As a playback singer he has worked on films including Agastya, Tiger, Jabardast Premika, Aashiq and Kie Daba Takkar.

facts: MA in music, Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya

Q48842456.lead: Babi Mishra is an Odia film, television and music-album actor who has played comic, supporting and villain roles since his debut in Jai Sriram.

p: Mishra entered Odia cinema in 1999 with Jai Sriram, and followed it with films such as To Pain, Nari Akhire Nian and Pheria Mo Suna Bhauni. His villain role in Mu Tate Love Karuchi, released in 2007, changed the direction of his career, and he was increasingly cast as an antagonist, as in Abhimanyu and Prem Rogi. He has also continued to take supporting and comic parts.
He has danced in many songs from Odia modern albums, including popular numbers such as Kau To Bauku Nau, Sahitya Didi and Aaji Tora Bahaghara Priya.
On television he played a villain in the serial Jeevan Sathi on Sarthak TV.

Q99317658.lead: Narayan Pati is an Odia playwright, actor and director, trained at the National School of Drama, who has worked in Odia and Hindi films, theatre and television.

p: As a child Pati was drawn to folk forms such as Pala and Daskathia, and he began acting on stage at school and college. After graduating in Bhadrak he moved to Cuttack. He completed his training at the National School of Drama in 1980.

In Cuttack he started acting in plays by Kartik Chandra Rath and Basanta Rath, and in 1970 he joined Janata Rangamancha. He was one of the founders of the theatre group Satabdira Kalakar and later set up another group, Anweshana. Plays he has written, acted in or directed include Muktipath, Jibana Sauda, Sesha Raktabindu, Abasesha, Sishu Dibasa, Karmayogi, Pratibad and Ganahatya. He also teaches drama through workshops.

His Odia films include Samar Salim Saiman, Bata Abata, Bhagya Chakra, Lakhe Siba Puji Paichhi Pua and Gare Sindura Dhare Luha, and in Hindi he has appeared in Dayavan, Antardaah, Durga, Damini, Jail and Lal Dupatta.

On television he has acted in the Odia serials Pathara Padile Sahi and Tokei and in Hindi series such as Discovery of India, Adhikar, Kahkashan, Byomkesh Bakshi, Dr. Ambedkar, Humrahi and Aur Bhi Hain Rahein. He has served at various times on the selection committee for the Odisha State Film Awards.

Q27736854.lead: Gyana Hota is an Odia satirical poet and the founding editor of the Cuttack monthly satire magazine Byanga Darbar, who has also worked in stage, television and film as a satirist and judge.

p: Hota works as an employee of India Post. He has written a number of short books of satire and performs his satirical verse and short comic pieces on stage.

On television he has appeared as a judge and guest on several Odia programmes. He served as a judge on The Great Odisha Political Circus on O TV from its start, and continued as a guest after the show dropped its judging panel. He was a regular guest presenting satirical poems on a programme on Tarang Music, and a judge on Byangastar on Prameya News7.
In the 2008 film Satyameba Jayate he played Japani Babu, a satirical poet who draws an ordinary auto-rickshaw driver into politics and helps him win an election. He also acted in Shikar (2026).

Q54504417.lead: Sangram Biswal is an Odia film director who made his directing debut with Rakhile Siba Mariba Kie (1994).

p: Biswal started out in 1991 as an assistant director on Bastra Harana, in which he also played a small part. He became a director in 1994 with Rakhile Siba Mariba Kie.

His later films as director include Sakala Tirtha To Charane, Rakhi Bhijigala Aakhi Luhare, Ram Laxman, Mahasangram, Dharma Nikiti, Vidhata, To Akhi Mo Aaena, I Love My India and Lal Tuku Tuku Sadhaba Bahu. As an actor he appeared in Bastra Harana and Prema Adhei Akshyara.
His son, Sajan Biswal, was set to make his acting debut in the Odia film Ram Nama Satya Hai.

Q21119519.lead: Narashingh Mohapatra (1926–1998) was an Odia playwright, lyricist, actor, director and editor who helped popularise Odia radio drama and wrote songs for many Odia films.

p: Mohapatra was born at Koranta in Bhadrak district and began writing as a student.

In 1949 he was recognised as a lyricist by All India Radio, Cuttack, and many of his songs were broadcast on programmes such as Saja Phula, Atasi Kusuma and Raga Manjari. He joined the Cuttack station as a playwright in 1958, and over 27 years there wrote more than a hundred radio plays across social, mythological, historical, comic and mystery themes.
He also acted in and directed plays, edited the magazines Sathi and Nutan Asha, and was a patron of the Janata, Kalashree and Annapurna theatres.

In cinema he wrote lyrics for films including Sri Lokanath, Amada Bata, Stree, Rakta Golapa, Nua Bou, Manik Jodi, E Nuhen Kahani and Bhakta Salabega, and wrote both lyrics and dialogue for Suna Sansar. Phula Rasia Re Mana Mora Chhuin Chhuin Ja Ja from Sri Lokanath is among his popular songs.
He died in Cuttack in 1998.

facts: Phula Rasia Re Mana Mora Chhuin Chhuin Ja Ja (Sri Lokanath)

Q98373186.lead: Divya Mohanty is an Odia actress who works mainly in television serials and Odia and Telugu films, and made her film debut in Sundergarh Ra Salman Khan (2018).

p: Mohanty began acting on television. Her first serial was Jay Maa Laxmi, a devotional series on Tarang TV in which she played the goddess Laxmi.

Her first Odia film, released in 2018, was Sundergarh Ra Salman Khan, in which she was the heroine opposite Babushaan. She went on to act in Baala – The Rhythm of Life, Tu Mora Sathire, Tu Mora Sathire 2, Ea Bi Gote Love Story, Tu Kahide I Love You and Mr Majnu, and she also works in Telugu cinema.
In 2020 she appeared with Tamanna Vyas in Chumbak, the first serial on Tarang Plus.
She has been devoted to Odissi dance since childhood and continues to practise it.

Q112333180.lead: Meera Mohanty (died 2022) was an actress of the Odia stage and screen. Her films included Jajabara (1975), Pratidhwani, Trinath Mela and Subarna Sita.

p: Her stage work started in the 1960s and took her to several companies: Kalashree Theatre and Janata Rangamancha in Cuttack, the Annapurna A Group in Puri, and Ekamra Theatre in Bhubaneswar.

On screen she was cast as Mandara in Jajabara (1975), opposite Jayiram Samal, and later appeared with Nityananda Mishra in Pratidhwani. Ramayan, Samay Bada Balaban and Bhuli Huena were among her other films, along with Trinath Mela and Subarna Sita.
She had one son. She died on 30 June 2022, aged 72.

facts: Kalashree Theatre; Janata Rangamancha; Annapurna A Group; Ekamra Theatre

Q15724804.lead: Basudeba Rath (1956–2019) was an Odia music director who scored more than 150 Odia films, beginning with Saakhi Gopinath (1978), along with musical plays, records, radio and television.

p: Rath was born at Balubazar in Cuttack. He studied at Ravenshaw Collegiate School up to the seventh class and finished his schooling at Birharekrushnapur, his maternal uncle's village. Drawn to music in high school, he bought instruments and taught himself to play them, and learned tabla from Guru Sudhakar. His father, Somnath Rath, opposed his musical training, but he kept at it.

He formed an orchestra, Basudeba Rath and Party, which started performing from Chhatra Bazar in Cuttack and later played across Cuttack and other parts of Odisha. His first chance to direct film music came with Saakhi Gopinath, released in 1978.
Over his career he provided music for more than 150 Odia films and 83 musical plays, and for over 12,000 gramophone records, as well as songs for radio and television.
Rath died in Cuttack in 2019, at the age of 63.

Q18341113.lead: Runu Parija (1965–2014), born Sadhana Das, was an Odia film actress who acted in about 80 Odia films, beginning with Batasi Jhada, as well as in television serials.

p: Parija was born at Karanjia in Mayurbhanj district. Her father, Bholanath, was a director at the Annapurna theatre, and her mother, Krishna, was a film actress.

She began acting with the Annapurna theatre and made her film debut in Batasi Jhada. Films such as Panjuri Bhitare Sari and Nari Nuhen Tu Narayani brought her wide popularity, and she went on to appear in about 80 Odia films.
On television she was well received for her role in Tosha Nohila Mora Chitta on Doordarshan Bhubaneswar, and she was acting in the ETV Odia serial Tapasya.
She won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for Laxmana Rekha. A state film award in 2003 for Dharam Sahile Hela is also recorded.
She married the Odia film director and producer Chandi Parija. Her sister Jharana (Jhunu) is married to the film actor Hara Patnaik.
She died in Cuttack in 2014.

Q42797224.lead: Sagar Das (1940–2017), born Sagar Kumar Das, was an Odia film comedian who acted from Abhinetri in the 1960s to Panchu Pandav in 1989.

p: Das was born in 1940. His father, Prabhat Chandra Das, worked as an artist in the Government of India's song and drama division.
He entered Odia cinema with Abhinetri and went on to appear in Bhai Bhauja (1967), Kie Kahara (1968) and Adina Megha (1970), among other films. His last Odia film was Panchu Pandav in 1989.
His comic acting featured in film songs such as Udi Udi Udi Jaere Mora Gudi, Alapa Hasare Aneka Ashara, Paradeshi Bandhu Tume and Sabi Sabi Tu Ta Mora Nalipana Bibi.
Das was employed as an actor in the central government's song and drama division, from which he retired in 2000.
He received a Cine Critics honour and an artist's honour from the Cuttack Municipality.
He died at Sahid Nagar, Bhubaneswar, in 2017.

Q15725234.lead: Sritam Das is an actor and director in Odia cinema, born in Cuttack. Since starting out in Sabitri (1995) he has appeared in more than 60 Odia films.

p: Sabitri, released in 1995, marked his entry into films, and his acting credits have since passed 60. For Tu Tha Mu Jauchhu Rusi he wrote the story and directed as well as acting. He has also modelled.
Within the Odia film community he has held the post of secretary of the Odisha Cine Artistes Association.
In 2014 he became a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party, which later chose him as its candidate for Mayor of Cuttack Municipal Corporation.
The Five Star Film Awards named him Best Supporting Actor in 2025.

facts: Director and story writer, Tu Tha Mu Jauchhu Rusi

Q109421812.lead: Ghanashyam Mohapatra (born 1933) is an Odia film producer and director, best known for Kanakalata, who received the Jayadev Award, Odisha's highest film honour.

p: Mohapatra was born in Dhenkanal in 1933. While studying at Ravenshaw College in 1951 he became interested in drama under the influence of Bidhubhusan Das. At 22 he enrolled in a three-year diploma course in cinematography at SJ Polytechnic in Bangalore.

After completing the course he joined Filmistan Studio in Bombay, where he worked as an associate director on about 20 films. He returned to Odisha in 1960 and set up a production company, Konark Films Private Limited.

In 1962 he made the documentary Maa O Sishu, which won the Odisha government's award for best documentary. He followed it with Radhu O Shyam in 1969 and another documentary, Krushi Jantrapati; these films won a number of awards. His first full-length feature was Kanakalata, made in 1974.
Mohapatra received the Jayadev Award.

facts: Diploma in cinematography, SJ Polytechnic, Bangalore; Ravenshaw College

Q20890395.lead: Shyamalendu Bhattacharya, known on screen as Shyamalendu, is an Odia film actor, mainly in comic roles, and a dance choreographer, known for films such as Stree, Jhili Mili, Kie Kahara and Abhimaan.

p: His earliest listed film is Abhinetri (1965), in which he played a servant. Over the following decades he appeared in films including Stree and Kie Kahara (1968), Sansar, Dharitri (as Sudhir's friend), Mana Akasha, Jajabara (as Gopi), Sindura Bindu, Suna Sansar, Anutap, Naga Phasa (as Gudia), Tapoi, Jhili Mili (as Sundar) and Sri Jagannath (as Shaktidhar). He made a guest appearance in Abhimaan (1977).

In the 1980s he acted in Maa O Mamata (as Basanta), Manasi, Jwain Pua, Ram Rahim, Kaberi (as Banchhanidhi), Swapna Sagara, Raja Harishchandra, Janani, Nala Damayanti, Sata Kebe Luchi Rahena, Jor Jar Mulak Tar and Samay Bada Balaban (playing police constables in both), Michha Mayara Sansar, Jayadev, Bhuli Huena and Shasti. His last film was Tume Hi Sathi Mora in 2011.
He also choreographed the dances for two Odia films.
He received the Mohan Sundar Deb Goswami Award.

Q29335071.lead: Anubha Gupta (1929–1972) was an Indian Bengali actress and singer known for her work in Bengali cinema, who won the BFJA award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role for Hansuli Banker Upakatha.

p: Born Mridula Gupta in Dinajpur, she was interested in dance and music from childhood. She attended Parry Charan Girls School and Banipith, and later studied at Shantiniketan.

Music director Robin Chatterjee brought her into Bengali films as a playback singer. Her first film as an actress was Samarpan, released in 1949, and she continued to act on stage alongside her screen work.

Her roles in Kabi, Ratna Dip, Champadangar Bou and Hansuli Banker Upakatha established her as a film actress, and within five years she had risen to the front rank of Bengali actresses. She also worked with Satyajit Ray in Abhijan and Kanchanjangha.
She received the award for Best Actress in a Supporting Role at the 26th Annual BFJA Awards for Hansuli Banker Upakatha.
Her second marriage was to the actor Rabi Ghosh.
She died in Kolkata in 1972.

Q80284707.lead: Purna Chandra Khuntia (1947–2019) was an Odia musician who, from 1973, composed and arranged music for more than a hundred Odia films and albums.

p: Khuntia was born on 27 December 1947 in Jachak Lane, Cuttack. His mother, Minarani Khuntia, was a singer who performed on radio, and her influence drew him to music as a child. He began learning piano and accordion at 14. He studied at Mission School and Christ College.

Starting in 1973, Khuntia directed and arranged music for more than a hundred Odia films and albums. He composed over 2,000 songs and arranged music for more than 5,000, and he also directed music for over ten films made outside Odisha. He played the accordion and keyboard.

His Odia films include Tike Hasa Tike Luha, Mahua and Konark, and his album work includes Sei Barsha. Popular songs he composed include Mun Jane Na Tume Jana Na Bhala Paibara Mane, Srabanare Srabana Megha Anibu, Sei Barsha Sei Rati Mane Pade and Nanti Tara Bulbul.
Khuntia died in Cuttack in 2019.

facts: Sei Barsha Sei Rati Mane Pade; Nanti Tara Bulbul

Q61750567.lead: Biswajit Mahapatra (born 1992) is an Indian playback singer from Bhawanipatna, Odisha, who works mainly in Odia films and competed in two seasons of Indian Idol.

p: Mahapatra was born in Bhawanipatna in 1992 and graduated from Utkal University. In 2012 he was runner-up in the singing reality show Voice of Odisha.
