The Voice of Odisha result brought him offers from the Odia film industry, and since 2012 he has sung for Odia films and released a number of solo albums.

He was already an established Odia playback singer when he entered Indian Idol season 9 in 2016, where he sang Phuchuki Gali from the film Suna Panjuri and reached the top 40. In season 10, in 2018, he made the top 14; his rendition of the Marathi song Hi Porgi Konachi in the fourth round was well received by the judges, and he was eliminated in the fifth round.

facts: Indian Idol seasons 9 and 10; runner-up, Voice of Odisha (2012)

Q28919006.lead: Sheetal Patra is an Odia actress and television presenter, trained in Odissi dance, who made her film debut in Jie Jaha Kahu Mora Dho (2015).

p: Patra trained in Odissi from childhood and performed on many stages. Hara Patnaik, director of the Tarang TV devotional serial Shree Jagannath, cast her as Ketaki, a dancer who sends temple offerings to Jayadev after he settles in Puri, and viewers liked her performance.

Minaketan then offered her a role in Jie Jaha Kahu Mora Dho, released at the New Year in 2015, in which she appeared alongside Babushaan and Minaketan. She was paired with Babushaan again in Bhala Pae Tate 100 Ru 100, released during Durga Puja on 18 October 2015, and in Tu Je Sei, a New Year release in 2016 that also featured Riya.
Tora Dine Ku Mora Dine, with Amlan, Riya and Arindam, followed at Durga Puja in 2016, and Dil Diwana Heigala was released at the New Year in 2017.

Q21468156.lead: Biren Mishra, known as Phaku Bhai, is an Odia actor who plays villains in Odia films and television serials and has also worked in jatra.

p: Mishra started acting in stage plays and later worked as a dubbing artist. In jatra he spent a year with Biswa Ranga Mahal before taking a year's break for personal reasons, and he has also worked with Eastern Opera.

On television he appeared in the Doordarshan serial Kahuthile Saribani and played Priyatam Sandhibigraha in Maa on DD Odia. His villain roles in the ETV Odia serials Bhagya Bidhata and Samaya Chakare Sansara Ratha and in Swabhiman on Tarang were popular with audiences, and he also acted in Rajkanya on ETV Odia.

His Odia films include Bhagya Chakra, To Pain Nebi Mu Sahe Janama, Lekhichi Na Tora, Keun Dunia Ru Asila Bandhu, Chhatire Lekhichi Tori Na, Sasura Ghara Zindabad, Matrushakti and Pilata Bigidigala, in which he played a comic villain. He has also appeared in the Hindi film Adibhumi.

Q25644157.lead: Surendra Kumar Das was an Odia producer, documentary maker, playwright, poet and lyricist who set up a public limited company to make the feature film Sri Jagannath (1950).

p: Das was born at Parbatipur, Tudigadia, in Balasore district.

His working life spanned several fields: he was a librarian, an agent and later manager for an insurance company, and a maker of documentary films. He wrote original plays and poetry and also translated into English.

He founded the commercial theatre company Rupashree Theatres, the film production company Rupabharati and the cinema hall Rupashree Cinema. He made about 22 documentaries in English and Odia, and established a public limited company to produce the feature film Sri Jagannath (1950).

In the 1940s gramophone records of his compositions Sakhigopal, Kanchi Kaveri and Nandikeswari were popular. He wrote three songs for Sri Jagannath, among them Shuna Bhamarara Guna Guna, which range across romance, longing and vivid imagery.

Q15725142.lead: Riya Dey (born Swarnali Dey) is an Odia film actress and model, also seen on television. Her first film, Prema Adhei Akshara (2010), earned her an Odisha State Film Award.

p: A native of Balasore, she attended Fakir Mohan College. She learned Odissi dance from childhood and performed as a dancer before acting.

Prema Adhei Akshara came to her while she was still doing her +2 studies, and it was released in 2010. She went on to appear in Criminal, Idiot, Radha Mohan Meera, Emiti Bi Prema Hue, Love Master, Tu Mo Dehara Chhai, Golapi Golapi, Pagala Karichu Tu, College Time, Tu Je Sei, Bandini and Cuttack – Seshru Arambha, among others.
Her work in Prema Adhei Akshara won her an Odisha State Film Award.

Q131283869.lead: Sisir Kumar Sahu (born 1988) is an Indian film director and writer from Keonjhar, known for the Odia films Charitra (2020) and Phalguna Chaitra (2023) and the short film Pharcha (2017).

p: Sahu was born on 11 June 1988 in Keonjhar district. He completed his schooling at Rengali Project High School and later trained at the Biju Patnaik Film and Television Institute.

He started out in 2014 as an associate director on the television series Samvidhaan: The Making of the Constitution of India. In 2016 he worked as an associate director on Mohenjo Daro, the Hindi film by Ashutosh Gowariker.
His short film Pharcha was released in 2017. He has since directed the feature films Charitra (2020), Dalchini (2022), Phalguna Chaitra (2023) and My Sweet Housewife (2023).

facts: Biju Patnaik Film and Television Institute

Q50220273.lead: Akshay Bastia is an Odia film and television actor who entered films with Bou (1998) and became widely known as Gautam, the hero of the DD Odia serial Mahayagya.

p: Bastia's first Odia film was Bou in 1998. He then played the lead role of Gautam in Mahayagya on DD Odia, a part that made him a familiar face in homes across Odisha. He has since played heroes, villains and supporting characters in many serials, including Tasara Ghara, Rajaniti, Badhu and Mo Jejema.

Alongside television he has continued to act in films such as Dharmara Heba Jay, Sashu Ghara Chalijibi, I Love My India, Mo Suna Pua, Dhauli Express, Agnisikha, Satyameba Jayate, Asibu Kebe Saji Mo Rani, Tu Mo Girlfriend, Tora Mora Katha Heba Chup Chap, Prema Sabuthu Balaban, Mu Raja Tu Rani, Jay Hind, Love You Hamesha, Maya and Mo Dil Kahe I Lu I Lu.

Q47482051.lead: Meghna Mishra is an Odia actress who has worked in Odia feature films and on Odia television.

p: Mishra entered Odia cinema with Kula Nandan. She went on to appear in Nari Akhire Nian, Prathama Prema, Priya Mo Asiba Pheri, Kalishankar, Samaya Hathare Dori and One Way Traffic. She was also cast opposite actor Bobby Mishra in Jouthi Thile Bi Tu Mora, which was described as an upcoming release.

On television she played the goddess Mahalakshmi in Shri Jagannath, a devotional serial on Tarang TV. She later appeared on the same channel in Tejaswini, cast as the queen who is mother to Princess Tejaswini.
Her role in Tejaswini earned her the Best Supporting Actress award at the 12th Film and Television Award Show Time in 2018.

Q4667465.lead: Abhishek Chatterjee (1964–2022) was an Indian actor who worked mainly in Bengali cinema from 1986 until his death.

p: Chatterjee was born in Kolkata, the son of Bengali actor Prashanta Chatterjee. He studied at Baranagore Ramakrishna Mission Ashrama High School and then took his degree from Seth Anandram Jaipuria College, part of the University of Calcutta.

His first screen role came in Tarun Majumdar's Bengali film Pathbhola (1986), in which he appeared with established performers including Sandhya Roy, Prosenjit Chatterjee, Tapas Paul and Utpal Dutt. His later Bengali work included Lathi, directed by Prabhat Roy, Swapan Saha's Bakul Priya, Pabitra Papi, Sajoni Aamar Sohag, Chaowa Pawa, Dahan, Bariwali and Alo.
He died at his home in Kolkata in 2022, aged 57.

Q60511399.lead: Mamuni Mishra is an Odia actress who has worked in Odia films since 1999 and in Odia television serials.

p: Her first film was Maa Pari Kie Heba (1999), in which she played Pooja. She then took supporting parts in films such as Kotie Re Gotie, Nari Akhire Nian, Haribhai Harena, Tu Mo Akhira Tara and Kathantara.

Her television roles have ranged from villains to comic characters. On ETV Odia she took over the role of Ratna Debroy in Bada Ghara Bada Gumara Katha, a part previously played by Aparajita Mohanty, and the role brought her wide recognition. Her other serials include Time Pass on ETV Odia, Ama Ghara Laxmi on Tarang TV and Manini on Sarthak TV.
She received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Supporting Actress for Mu Khanti Odia Jhia in 2018.

facts: Bada Ghara Bada Gumara Katha (ETV Odia)

Q55527263.lead: Suresh Bal is an Odia actor who has appeared in more than 80 Odia films since 1977, as well as in television serials, often as a character actor, villain or comedian.

p: Bal began his film career with Suna Sansar (1977) and followed it with Balidan, Gauri, Samar Salim Saiman, Baje Bainshi Nache Ghungura and Ei Aama Sansar. In Jor Jar Mulak Tar (1986) he played Basu, a comic sidekick to the character played by Hara Patnaik. He has become widely known by the name Banku.
On ETV Odia he appeared in the serial Gayatri in a double role, playing Nitia'di and his brother.
He is married to Tripti Sinha.

Q99035887.lead: Gagarin Mishra (died 2020) was an Odia cinematographer who worked in both Odia and Hindi films.

p: Mishra shot Odia films including Phula Chandana and Nai Separi Kanaka Gori. In Hindi cinema he worked on films such as Betaab, Chandni, Tezaab, Chaalbaaz, Pyar Ki Jeet, Jalwa and Ram-Avtar. He was also a cameraman for National Geographic.
Nai Separi Kanaka Gori won him the award for Best Cinematographer at the 24th Odisha State Film Awards in 2013.
He was the brother of Odia film editor Deben Mishra. He died in Mumbai in 2020, aged 67.

Q46930003.lead: Surya Mohanty (born 1952) is an Odia theatre director and actor who trained at the National School of Drama and has worked in Odisha's theatre for over three decades.

p: Born Surya Narayan Mohanty in Badamba to Radharaman Chhamukarana and Shanti Sundari Chhamukarana, he grew up in Bhubaneswar. Plays staged at venues such as Rabindra Mandap and Bhanja Kala Mandap, along with village pala and daskathia performances, shaped his early interest, and contact with Akshaya Mohanty (Kashyap) drew him towards acting. He studied at the National School of Drama from 1978 to 1981 and resolved during that time to return to Odisha and work in theatre.

Back in Odisha he has directed, acted and taught, running a theatre group named Mukti and holding workshops on acting and direction. His stage work includes Abolakara Upakhyana (1982), Rakshaka Hele Bhakshaka (1982), Chandramani Upakhyana, King Oedipus and Kathamancha. His film credits as actor or director include Indradhanura Chhai, Sankha Mahuri, Bhaunri – The Sinking Reality and Dhauli Express.

Q56060895.lead: Sunil Kumar is an Odia film actor who made his debut in 2004 and has also worked in Bengali and Marathi films.

p: Kumar was born in Bhubaneswar. He began school at Kendriya Vidyalaya in Adra, West Bengal, and later graduated from Buxi Jagabandhu Bidyadhar College in Odisha.

His first film was Hari Bhai Harena (2004), with Anu Choudhury as his leading lady. Later Odia films included Jibana Mrutyu, Rakate Lekhichi Naa, in which he was cast as a villain, Agnishikha, Tumaku Paruni Ta Bhuli, Chup Kie Asuchi, Sata Sure Bandha E Jibana, Swayamsiddha, Ae Mana Khoje Mana Tiye, Mu Aashiq Mu Awara and Maya.
Outside Odia cinema he acted in the Bengali films Aparadhi and Window Connection and in the Marathi film Pune via Bihar.

Q84606903.lead: Aseema Panda is an Odia playback singer who sings mainly in Odia and Sambalpuri and has recorded for films, albums and devotional programmes.

p: Panda began singing for Odia films in 2013 with Hari Om Hari. She went on to lend her voice to many films, among them Ganja Ladhei, One Way Traffic, Ashiq, Tu Kahibu Na Mun, Tu Mo Sapana Rani, Premara Nisha Niara Niara, Mu Paradesi Chadhei, Tu Mo Suna Chadhei, From Me To You, Tiger, Love Twist, Mu Khanti Odia Jhia, To Premare Padila Pare, Emiti Bi Heipare, Abhimaan, Mu Diwana Tu Diwani, Tu Mo Hero, Adrushyam, Bapa Tame Bhari Dushta, Dele Dhara Katha Sare, Selfish Dil, Excuse Me, Local Toka Love Chokha, Pyar Alaga Prakar, Love Express, Tike Anadi Pura Khiladi, Nayakara Naa Debdas, Mitha Mitha, Laila O Laila, Happy Lucky, Hello – In Love, Tokata Phasigala, Jogi and Biswaroop.
Beyond films she has recorded album songs and bhajans, and she performs devotional songs on Prarthana TV programmes such as Bhajan Antakshari and Prarthana Mancha.
She has received the Odisha Sangeet Samman.

Q98423218.lead: Deben Mishra (died 2020) was an Odia film editor who cut more than 80 Odia feature films between 1986 and 2018.

p: Mishra started editing in Odia cinema in 1986 with Jor Jar Mulak Tar, and the following year he edited Chaka Akhi Sabu Dekhuchi (1987).

His later credits include Pua Mora Kala Thakura, Rajanigandha, Asuchi Mo Kalia Suna, Daiba Dauri, Paradeshi Chadhei, Maa Mate Shakti De, Chakadola Karuchi Leela, Kasia Kapila, Udandi Sita and Ranabhumi. The last Odia film he edited was Jibanara Chalapathe, released in December 2018.
He died in 2020 at the age of 62.

Q126251736.lead: Bijaya Patnaik (died 2024) was an Odia actor who worked on stage, in television serials and in films, and was honoured by the Sangeet Natak Akademi.

p: Patnaik belonged to the first batch of students at Utkal Sangeet Natak Mahavidyalaya.
He held a job at Utkal University, where his handwriting appeared on the university's older certificates, and acted alongside that work. He also directed plays.

In telefilms and feature films he worked as a character actor. His television serials included Mashal, Juara Bhatta and Suna Bohu. He also appeared in government advertisements and became known for one on heatstroke.
He received an honour from the Sangeet Natak Akademi for his acting.
He died in 2024, aged 78.

Q48076899.lead: Supriya Nayak is an Odia film actress who made her debut in 2016 opposite Babushaan and has since worked in films and television.

p: Nayak was born in Jagatsinghpur district. As a schoolgirl she won many prizes as a runner. In 2014 she finished third in the Miss Odisha contest.

She was cast as Babushaan's heroine in Love Pain Kuch Bhi Karega (2016), produced by Tarang Cine Productions. She then spent time modelling in Mumbai before returning to Odisha to act with Babushaan again in Only Pyar, which came out in January 2018 as the year's first release.
From 25 January 2021 she played the female lead opposite Siddhanta Mahapatra in Kemiti Kahibi Kaha, a serial on Zee Sarthak. Her film Astika Nastika was released in 2022 on Tarang TV and Tarang Plus.

Q123503031.lead: Sakti Jagdev is an Indian film producer working mainly in Odia cinema and the founder and director of the production company Adya Jagdev Films.

p: Born Sakti Prasad Jagdev in Jajpur, he works for an IT company abroad. He moved into film production and set up his own company with the aim of promoting Odia language, literature and culture internationally.

His first production was Phalguna Chaitra (2023), directed by Sisir Kumar Sahu and Pinaki Singh, on which he was chief producer and actor Babushaan was co-producer. The film won awards in three categories at the 35th Odisha State Film Awards. Jagdev announced that a share of the film's profits would go to film artists, technicians and social welfare.

Q50220254.lead: Dipak Barik is an Odia actor who first became known through Odia music albums and entered feature films in 2011 with Mana Mora Prajapati.

p: Barik was born in Cuttack.

He started out as a lead dancer in Odia modern music albums, appearing in many popular album songs and working with album stars such as Lipi and Sweet. His film debut came in 2011 with Mana Mora Prajapati.

He went on to act in Family No.1, Chanda Na Tame Tara, Sapanara Nayika, Akhi Kholile Tu Tu Hi Tu, Tame Thile Sathire and Galpa Nuhen Alpa Dinara. On television he has served as a judge on Sarthak TV, including the 2017 programme Raja Queen.
He married Tanuja in 2018.

Q106602281.lead: Jaya Swami is an Odia film actress who has appeared in more than 50 Odia films and many television serials since 1978.

p: Her family came originally from Visakhapatnam and lived in Choudwar, where her father was employed. She was educated at her maternal uncle's home in Jagdalpur and learned Odissi dance from Dayanidhi Das.

Swami began her film career with Jhili Mili (1978). Her films include Andha Diganta, Jaaiphula, Shankha Sindura, Ram Rahim, Puja Phula, Samar Salim Saiman, Agni Bina and Phula Chandana. After Hakim Babu (1985) she took a break of several years, returning in 2005 with Bhagya Chakra, directed by her husband G. K. Yogesh.
She has also acted in Bengali, Gujarati and Rajasthani films, in many Odia television serials, and in jatra with Natya Mandir in 2026.
She is married to film director G. K. Yogesh.

Q44684126.lead: Saroj Nanda (1959–2000) was an Odia music director who composed for Odia films and albums, as well as for Hindi, Marathi and Chhattisgarhi songs.

p: Nanda was born in Bolangir to Paramananda Nanda and Subarna Nanda, from whom he first learned music. He regarded Shankar Pradhan as his guru. He studied at Nabajiban Vidyapitha in Bolangir and later at Rajendra College, where he began composing.

He composed many modern and devotional albums, among them Prathama Prema, Tama Katha Mane Pade, Chandini, Rajani Gandha, Puni Dekha Heba and Kahile Kahiba Kahuchi, and received awards for this work. Songs he set to music include "Batare Chalu Chalu", "Tu Chali Jibu To Sasughara", "Mun Ta Bada Deulara Para", "Sahe Atha Bela Patara" and "Kerikeri Suna Duba".
His film work includes Laxmi Pratima, Jibana Sathi and Akashara Aakhi. He died in 2000 at the age of 41.
He won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Music Director in 1998 for Laxmi Pratima.

facts: Batare Chalu Chalu; Mun Ta Bada Deulara Para

Q16213575.lead: Arjun Jena (born 1971) is a Chennai-based Indian cinematographer. He learned his craft as a camera assistant to P. C. Sreeram and Jeeva before shooting films on his own.

p: His training began in the 1990s as an assistant cameraman with P. C. Sreeram, whose credits during that time included Thevar Magan (1992), Thiruda Thiruda (1993), May Madham (1994), Subha Sankalpam (1994) and Kurudhipunal (1995). In 1996 he moved to the team of Jeeva, another former Sreeram assistant, as operating cameraman, and worked with him on Indian (1996), Ullasam (1997), Vaalee (1999), Kushi (2000), Run (2002), Zor, Hera Pheri and Yeh Teraa Ghar Yeh Meraa Ghar.

Silent Scream, a short film by Vikram Kumar, gave him his first break; at the 46th National Film Awards (1998) it was named Best Educational/Motivational/Instructional Film. He shot his first feature, Kathir's Tamil film Kadhal Virus, in 2000, and later worked on Oka Oorilo, Aegan, Love Khichdi and Ala Modalaindi.
His work on Kadhal Virus won the Tamil Nadu State Film Award for Best Cinematographer.

Q17598032.lead: Bhima Singh (1934–2010) was an Odia actor of stage, radio, television and film who also worked as an assistant director, screenwriter and writer on Odia cinema.

p: Singh first acted at the age of 13 and went on to perform in more than 300 plays. He worked as a school teacher from 1953 to 1956 and with the Life Insurance Corporation of India from 1958 to 1992.

In cinema he worked with director Nitai Palit on many Odia films as actor and as assistant or associate director, and contributed screenplays and dialogue to numerous productions. His acting credits include Malajahna, Matira Manisha, Kie Kahara, Bandhana, Dharitri, Krushna Sudama, Mana Akasha, Bandhu Mohanty, Raghu Arakhita, Nirbachana, Bhagya Hate Dori, Jibana Sathi and Sata Kahibaku Kian Daribi.

He also wrote scripts for documentaries and essays on Odia drama, music, devotional narrative and folk traditions. In 2008 he compiled Odia Chalachitrara Ajnata Adhyaya, a reference work on Odia cinema with particular attention to older films.
He died in Cuttack in 2010.

Q21005702.lead: Anupam Dutta is an Indian music director and composer, mostly associated with Bengali films directed by Swapan Saha.

p: Dutta's credits as composer run from the mid-1990s to the late 2000s. They include Sujan Sakhi, Shesh Pratiksha, Naginkanya (1995), Bhai Amar Bhai (1996), Pabitra Papi, Matir Manush, Yoddha (1997), Sindurer Adhikar, Putrabadhu (1998), Swamir Ghar (1999), Sajoni Aamar Sohag, Parichay (2000), Ostad (2001), Sukh Dukkher Sansar (2003), Khalnayak, Arjun (2006), Greptar, Sanghat (2007) and Bhagya Chakra (2008).

Q60511430.lead: Hadu, born Bhakta Prahallad Charan Patnaik, is an Odia actor known chiefly for comic roles in films, television serials and stage plays.

p: Hadu entered Odia cinema in 1995. His first film was Mo Mana Khali Tori Pain, directed by Gouri Shankar Das, in which he played Hadu Mamu. He has since worked in many Odia films, serials and stage productions.
His large belly and his style of moustache made him a familiar figure in households across Odisha.
He has twice won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Comedian: in 2008 for Hasiba Puni Mo Suna Sansar and in 2012 for Mate Bohu Kari Nei Ja.

facts: Odisha State Film Award for Best Comedian (2008, 2012)

Q15724842.lead: Bibhu Kishore, born Tapas Kumar Das, is an Odia playback singer and composer from Bhubaneswar who has sung for Odia films since 1997.

p: He was born in Bhubaneswar and studied at Capital High School and BJB College, where he graduated in mathematics and served as the college's dramatic secretary in 1989. He had no formal training in music.

In 1991 music director Manmath Mishra gave him his first chance to sing, for a jatra production. His first album song came from Srikant Gautam's Cuttack Bani, and he began singing for films with Suna Sansar in 1997.
Although he held a government job, he took voluntary retirement to concentrate on music. He names the late Akshaya Mohanty and Kishore Kumar as his role models.
His honours include the Chinta O Chetana Samman, Saradhabali Samman, Sura Taranga Samman, Chalachitra Jagat Samman, Chitralipi Samman and Banichitra Samman.

Q15723914.lead: Kabiraj Krushna Chandra Tripathy (1914–2006) was an Ayurvedic physician, Odia film producer, writer and politician who founded Utkal Chalachitra Pratisthan.

p: Tripathy founded Utkal Chalachitra Pratisthan, the first cooperative set up to produce, distribute and exhibit Odia films. He produced Shree Shree Mahalaxmi Puja (1959), Parinam (1961) and Dasyu Ratnakar (1962).

He represented the Aska constituency in the fifth Odisha Legislative Assembly from 1971 to 1973 and sat on the senate of Berhampur University. He also founded Utkal Ayurvedic Co-operative Pharmacy Ltd. at Aska, Utkal Chemical Company and Kabiraj Bhawan, and wrote several books on Ayurvedic treatment.
He received the Jayadeva Puraskar in 1981.
His wife was Binodini Devi.

Q15724981.lead: Mohammed Mushir is an Odia music director and singer who composed music for Odia films from 1979.

p: Mushir began by composing and singing for the Yuvavani programme on All India Radio, Cuttack. His first Odia film was Samar Salim Saiman (1979).

Between 1979 and 1999 he scored eight Odia films, among them Aparichita, Sahari Bagha, Basanti Apa, Bada Bhauja, Maa Mate Shakti De, Hisab Kariba Kalia and Ei Akhi Ama Sakhi. E Dil Tate Deli, with his music, was released in 2019.
The Odisha Cine Critics Association named him Best Music Director in 1991 for Maa Mate Shakti De.

Q116173663.lead: Pradeep Bhol (died 2022) was an Odia writer, playwright, producer and director whose film Chini received an Odisha State Film Award.

p: For more than 40 years Bhol was involved with theatre groups and cultural organisations in Sundargarh, working to support artists and arts bodies. Plays he wrote were staged in western Odisha, elsewhere in the state and beyond it. His production of the play Mao was entered in the Limca Book of Records in 2009.
In cinema he produced Stree, Suna Sankhali and Pabitra Bandhana. He wrote the story and screenplay for Chini (2016) and directed it; the film won an Odisha State Film Award.
He died in Sundargarh in 2022, aged 59.

Q18066921.lead: Sarat Nayak is a singer and music composer from Pattamundai who works in Odia films and albums. He is especially known for devotional songs.

p: A native of Pattamundai, he took a postgraduate degree in Odia from Utkal University at Vani Vihar, Bhubaneswar.

His non-film work includes modern albums such as Aau Ketedina, Chakori Jharana Luha, Mana Rahena, Sasura Ghara Jindabad, Janha Raati, Smruti, Jibanare Thare Adhe and E Goura. Odia listeners know him chiefly for bhajans; "Sabu Mayare Baya" and "He Narayan" are among his popular devotional songs, and his bhajan albums include Bada Dian, Bhaba Jamuna, Jai Shreeram, Papa Punya and Tuma Pade Sarana.
For the cinema he has been music director of Chakaa Chakaa Bhaunri, Bande Utkala Janani, Shatru Sanghar, Aa Janhare Lekhiba Naa and Bad Girl.

Q112268465.lead: Jagruti Rath is an Odia film and television actress, presenter and dancer, best known for the Tarang TV serial Shree Mandira.

p: Rath was born in Bolangir and is trained in Odissi and Sambalpuri dance.

She worked as a presenter on Ajira Sakala, a programme on DD Odia. In the Tarang TV serial Shree Mandira she played Padmavati, the princess of Kanchi. She later hosted Nupur Junior and the third season of Gyanaguru, both on Prarthana TV.
She played the female lead in Sunayana, an Odia film made by Tarang Cine Productions. She is also active in theatre and played Labanya in the play Debadasi.
She received the Kalinga Birangana Award in 2022 and both the Padmashree Prafulla Kar Samman and the Arya Award in 2024.

Q28105688.lead: Chakradhar Jena (died 2024) was an Odia actor trained at the National School of Drama who worked in Odia films, theatre and television, and also in Hollywood and Hindi productions.

p: Jena entered acting after completing his training at the National School of Drama in 1988. He was known in the film industry as "Chakara Bhai" and placed importance on making original films in Odia.

His first Odia film was Pathara Khasuchi Bada Deulu. Other Odia credits include Ranabhumi, Maya, Arjun, Kathantara, Prem Weds Priya, Rangila Baba, Bhaunri and Om Namah Shivaya, as well as the serial Mahayajna. Outside Odisha he appeared in the Hollywood films City of Joy and Electric Moon and in the Hindi film Sardar Patel.
He died in Bhubaneswar in 2024.

Q135508465.lead: Sudhakar Vasanth (also credited as Sudhakar Basant) is a choreographer, director and actor whose film work is mainly in Odia cinema.

p: He learned choreography as an assistant to his father, Vasanth Kumar, and worked with Prabhu Deva, Chinni Prakash and B. H. Tarun Kumar. His first screen appearance was as one of the leading actors in the Tamil film Innisai Mazhai (1992).

Odia cinema came to him through Gopal Jogesh, who was shooting Sola Shukrabaar (1999) in Chennai and invited him to choreograph a song. On the advice of music director Prasant Padhi he moved into direction, starting with Mitare Mita (2009). His choreography credits run to about 1,200 songs.
The 2nd Tarang Cine Awards (2010) gave him Best Choreography, and the 3rd ETV Odia Film Awards (2012) named him Best Director for Balunga Toka.

Q128302907.lead: Samaj Pati (died 2024) was an Odia actor who worked in theatre, films, television serials and radio plays.

p: Pati started on the stage, with plays such as Pheri Jaa Ramachandra, Chhau Nataka, Sambaluaa, Nishanta, Partha, Cancer and Aurangzeb. His first film was Gopare Badhuchi Kala Kanhei (1994), followed by Bhai Hela Bhagari (1994) and Katha Rahigala Kala Kalaku (1999).
On ETV Odia he played the villain in the serial Tulasi.
He was the nephew of actor Asit Pati, who brought him into acting. He died in Balasore in 2024, aged 61.

Q21620335.lead: Makhanlal Banerjee (1904–1942) played Rama in Sita Bibaha, the first Odia feature film, and is therefore regarded as Odia cinema's first hero.

p: Banerjee was born in 1904 at Balubazar in Cuttack. He worked as a head clerk at the Central Cooperative Bank.

Theatre was a consuming interest. He would travel to Calcutta on Saturdays, watch plays there on Sunday and be back at work in Cuttack on Monday. In Cuttack he organised many music gatherings and was a patron of the Binapani Club. His stage roles included Shahjahan, Konark, Paika Pua, Karnarjuna, Sita and Behula.

Through his efforts the stage and cinema magazine Arati began publication in 1932, edited by Sarat Chandra Mukherjee; it was the first Odia magazine devoted to film. Sita Bibaha, in which he played Rama, opened at Laxmi Theatre in Puri on 28 April 1936. He died during Shyama Puja in 1942.

Q16727188.lead: Bidita Bag is an Indian actress and model whose film work has leaned towards socio-political subjects.

p: Bag was born in Santragachhi, Howrah, West Bengal, and studied economics at Jadavpur University.

She modelled while in college after being noticed by Jeena Mitra Banik and make-up artist Prabeer Kumar Dey, and gained attention in Kolkata working for designers including Sabyasachi Mukherjee. After graduating she moved to Mumbai, where she modelled at Lakme Fashion Week and appeared in campaigns for brands such as Lakmé, Nokia, Motorola, Colgate, Samsung and Bombay Dyeing.
Her first film was the Bengali production Mukti, followed by Icche, released in July 2011.

Q28035707.lead: Akshaya Mohanty (Kashyap) (1937–2004) was an Odia film actor and director who also worked in theatre and jatra.

p: Mohanty was born in 1937 in Kiadingiri village in Cuttack district. Drawn to drama from childhood, he acted in the play Ekalavya while in class five at Ravenshaw Collegiate School.

The play Mamata, staged by the theatre group United Artists, first made his name. He later gave up his job to act full time. He entered Odia cinema in 1959 with Sri Lokanath, and went on to act in Malajahna, Nabajanma, Amada Bata, Sansar, Manik Jodi, Hisab Nikas, Lal Paan Bibi, Chilika Teerey and Batasi Jhada.
As a director his films include Nila Saila, Jay Maa Mangala, Sautuni and Sankha Mahuri. He also acted in and directed jatra productions.

Q29645363.lead: Priyanka Mahapatra, also known as Pinky, is an Odia film and television actress who made her screen debut in 1993 with Pathara Khasuchi Bada Deulu.

p: After her debut in Pathara Khasuchi Bada Deulu (1993), Mahapatra played heroines and supporting characters in films such as Suna Bhauja, Bhai Hela Bhagari, Rakhile Siba Mariba Kie, Jibana Dhara, Suhaga Sindura, Pua Moro Bhola Shankara, Nila Mastarani, Jashoda, Stree, Kalachakra, Babu Parsuram, Kasia Kapila and Samaya Chakare Sansara Ratha.
In later years she has taken comic and character roles in many films.
She is married to Odia director Debu Patnaik. Her husband's elder brother, Hara Patnaik, was a well-known Odia actor and director.

Q56260334.lead: Rudra Panigrahi is an Odia film actor who entered Odia cinema in 2011 with Mane Rahiba E Prema Kahani.

p: Panigrahi's first film was Mane Rahiba E Prema Kahani (2011), directed by Narayan Ghadei, with Rupali as his co-star. He followed it with Galpa Nuhen Alpa Dinara (2014), Apna Hath Jagannath (2015) and Jhiata Bigidigala (2016). Premi Diwana, in which he acted, was released in 2018.
In 2017 he took part in Jeenara Jibanasathi, a programme on Tarang TV, and went on to marry Jeena Samal.

Q48838493.lead: Sanmira Nagesh is an Odia film actress and Odisha State Film Award winner who moved from child roles to leading parts in 2017.

p: Apart from acting, Nagesh enjoys painting, singing, dancing and playing football. Before acting she had hoped to become an educationist.
She first appeared on screen as a child artist in Suna Chadhei Mo Rupa Chadhei. Her first role as a lead heroine came in Sapanara Pathe Pathe (2017), after which she acted in Laila O Laila.
She received an Odisha State Film Award in 2017.

Q105735054.lead: Gayatri Chand is an Odissi dancer, actress and writer who won the Odisha State Film Award for Best Actress for Agni Sanketa.

p: Chand trained under Guru Deba Prasad Das and performs in his style of Odissi. In 2010 she established the Deba Prasad Nrutya Pratisthan in Bhubaneswar to promote that style, and she has written a book on her guru, Guru Deba Prasad Das: Icon of Odissi.
She has acted in four Odia films, including Agni Sanketa, and in one Bengali film, a remake of an Odia original. She has also appeared in two telefilms.

Besides the State Film Award for Best Actress for Agni Sanketa, she has received a Senior Fellowship from the Union Ministry of Culture, the Nrutya Shiromani and Pratibha Samman in 2008, and the Haripriya Debadasi Samman from Rupashree Kalamandir, Puri, in 2012.

facts: Guru Deba Prasad Das: Icon of Odissi

Q25643890.lead: Manoj Patnaik (born 1956) is an Odia stage actor and theatre director, founder of the Bhubaneswar theatre group Manan Natya Sanstha, who has also acted in many Odia films.

p: Patnaik was born in Balakati (Sagua) to Banabihari Patnaik and Kokila Patnaik. He first appeared on stage at the age of six months and began directing plays while in class nine.

He founded Manan Natya Sanstha in Bhubaneswar and has served as programme in-charge with the Song and Drama Division of the Government of India. In 2014 he was appointed to the programme committee of the National School of Drama Repertory Company, the first Odia to be named to it.

Plays he has acted in or directed include Tingabudha, Asha Bharasa Nirasha, Ekadasa Abatara, Jibana Gudi, Astha, Sanskara, Asustha Aparahna, Anartha and Ati Achambita Katha. He has also acted in many Odia films.
He received the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi award in 2013.

Q112229142.lead: Bachu Mukherjee (died 2020) was an Indian music director who scored Odia films and composed for All India Radio and Doordarshan programmes.

p: Mukherjee devoted more than five decades to music. He founded Surasangam, a music school in Baripada, where he taught.

He started in films as an associate of Saroj Patnaik before composing independently. His films as music director include Gopare Badhuchi Kala Kanhei (1994), Katha Rahithiba Kala Kalaku, Mate Ta Love Helare, Pua Bhangidela Suna Sansar (1999) and Simili (2025).
He died in Cuttack in 2020, aged 64.

Q15724164.lead: Jyoti Mishra (born 1978) is an Odia actress who has worked in films, television serials and album songs, making her film debut with Bou in 1998.

p: Mishra was born in Odisha in 1978 and completed a postgraduate degree at Buxi Jagabandhu Bidyadhar College, Bhubaneswar.
While still a student, she began presenting a programme on DD Odia in 1996. Her film career started with Bou (1998), and she has since acted in many Odia films as well as in Odia serials.
She married Buddha Ghosh in 2000.

Q29639636.lead: Mama Mishra is an Odia actress who worked mainly in Odia films between 1995 and 2007.

p: Mishra's first film was Mo Mana Khali Tori Pain (1995), in which she played Smruti. She went on to appear in Suna Sansar, Bapa, Kie Pochhiba Maa Aakhi Ra Luha, To Akhi Mo Aaena, Babu Parsuram, Samaya Chakare Sansara Ratha, Samay Kheluchhi Chaka Bhaunri, Rahichi Rahibi Tori Paain, Aeithi Swarga Aeithi Narka, Sakhi Rahila Ae Singha Duara and Nari Akhire Nian.
In 2003 she married Odia film actor and politician Siddhanta Mahapatra.

Q15724969.lead: Manmath Mishra is an Odia lyricist and music composer who has worked in Odia films and in jatra theatre.

p: Mishra was born in Kumarpur Sasan, Athagarh, to Dinabandhu Mishra and Induprabha. He studied at Athagarh College and Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya.

He composed tunes and directed the music for a film for the first time with Aashar Akash (1983). When the four or five films he worked on after that went unreleased, he turned to jatra, writing lyrics, composing and directing music for productions such as Mo Penkali Bajei De, Jeje Tame Michha Kahila and Adua Suta.
His later film scores include Ganga Jamuna (1997), Suna Harini (1999), Saathire (2004), Thank You Bhagban (2006), Pagala Premi (2007), Jianta Bhoota (2008) and Suhaga Sindura.
He is married to Krishna Mishra; their children are Prakruti Mishra and Manab.

Q106750625.lead: Tilottama Khuntia (died 2022) was an Odia actress known for playing mothers in Odia television serials.

p: Khuntia was regularly cast in mother roles on Odia television. Her serials included Tulasi on ETV Odia, Sindura Bindu on Tarang TV and Kemiti E Bandhana.
She was married to Odia theatre director Himanshu Samal. Their younger daughter, Debika Arundhati Samal, acts in Odia films and serials. Khuntia died in 2022, aged 57.

facts: Tulasi; Sindura Bindu; Kemiti E Bandhana

Q47086666.lead: Nagen Roy (1935–2018) was an Odia film director and stage actor who directed Gapa Hele Bi Sata, the first Odia colour film.

p: Roy was born in 1935 at Bagalasahi, Niali, in Cuttack district. While studying at Christ College, Cuttack, he acted at the Annapurna Theatre.

He began in cinema as associate director on Kanakalata, directed by Ghanashyam Mahapatra. His own first film as director, Gapa Hele Bi Sata, came out in 1976 and was the first Odia film in colour. For Priyatama (1978) he wrote the story and also acted, and for Tapasya (1980) he wrote the story and dialogue as well as directing.
He worked in the Labour Department and took voluntary retirement in 1988.

Q7645720.lead: Suresh Balaje is a film producer from Chennai whose work is mostly in Malayalam and Tamil cinema. His father was the producer and actor K. Balaji.

p: Films he has produced include Billa, Vazhvey Maayam, Gandharvam, Ulladakkam, 13B, Yaavarum Nalam, Malamaal Weekly, Phir Milenge and Billa 2.

Together with his business partner George Pius he now runs Wide Angle Creations, working as executive and line producer. The company partnered with the French director Jacques Audiard on Dheepan, which won the Palme d'Or at the 68th Cannes Film Festival.
The actor Mohanlal is his brother-in-law, married to his sister Suchitra; Pranav Mohanlal and Vismaya Mohanlal are their children.

Q43967122.lead: Kedar Guru (1936–1987) was an Odia stage and film actor from Puri who also founded theatre and children's cultural organisations.

p: Guru was born in 1936 at Gaudabad Sahi in Puri. From childhood he was interested in music, drama and physical exercise, and he acted in school and neighbourhood plays.

His first film was Patita Pabana. He later appeared in Gauri, Sindura Bindu, Bandhu Mohanty, Sakhi Gopinath, Suvarna Sita, Ramayana, Nilamadhaba and Sri Jagannath. His stage work included Hansadhwani, Kalabatira Ghata and Nartaki.
In 1967 he formed the theatre group Shilpi. He also established the children's organisations Nilachala Shishu Srota Samiti and Kishore Chakra, and created Srikshetra Kala Prakashika.
The organisation Rangashala presents an annual Kedar Guru Award in his memory.
He died at Gaudabad Sahi, Puri, in 1987.

Q50220366.lead: Poonam Mishra (born 1993) is an Odia film actress who made her debut in 2011 with Baisi Pahache Kheliba Mina.

p: Mishra's first film, Baisi Pahache Kheliba Mina (2011), was directed by Sanjay Nayak. She then acted opposite Babushaan in Love Master and opposite Bulu in Rockstar. She was also cast with Bulu again in Facebook, directed by Manoranjan Pal, which was slated for release in 2018.
On television she played the title role in the serial Taapoi.

Q5654113.lead: Haranath Chakraborty (born 1959) is an Indian film director and screenplay writer who works mainly in Bengali cinema.

p: Chakraborty began directing with Mangaldeep in 1989. His later work includes Raja Rani Badsha, Sangharsha (1995), Sathi (2002), Sangee, Nater Guru, Sasurbari Zindabad, Pratibad, Tulkalam, Swapno and Cholo Paltai. Several of his films were both critical and commercial successes.

Two of his films, Sathi (2002) and Ganrakal (2004), each won the Bengal Film Journalists' Association award for Best Clean & Entertainment Film. In 2024 the Ministry of Information & Cultural Affairs of West Bengal presented him with the Mahanayak Samman for his contribution to Bengali films as a director.

Q60809313.lead: Shweta Malik is a former Indian actress who appeared mainly in Odia feature films and Odia music albums between 1995 and the early 2000s.

p: Malik started out in Odia music albums before moving to cinema with the 1995 Odia film Suna Panjuri. She went on to act in seven Odia films, two Bengali films and one Telugu film. Her Odia credits include Suhaga Sindura, Suna Harini, Krushna Kaberi, Dharma Nikiti, Mana Rahigala Tumari Thare and Sabata Maa. She stopped acting in 2000.
She married Biswambar Sabat, owner of the Odia album production house Samrat Cassette. After the marriage the couple took up a life of renunciation, and she adopted the name Maheshwari.

Q15724144.lead: Jalal Adeni (1936–2021) was an Indian instrumentalist, music director, lyricist, singer and film director who worked in Odia and Hindi cinema.

p: Adeni was born on 23 June 1936 at Bhanjanagar in Odisha's Ganjam district. He studied at Khallikote College and Jadavpur University.

In the Odia film Anutap (1977) he served as director, music director and singer. He produced and directed Hira Moti Manika, directed Sabu Swapna, and directed Pujarini (1981). He also directed the Hindi films Zamana Kya Kahega (1982), Humne Pyar Kiya (1992) and Prem Upahar (1994).
He died in Cuttack in 2021.

facts: Instrumentalist, music director, lyricist, singer, film director

Q60511414.lead: Kirti Mohanty is an Indian actress who works in Odia films, television serials and theatre, and is known in Odisha for playing villainous roles.

p: Mohanty has appeared in Odia films including Arjun, Dhire Dhire Prema Hela, Hero, Raja Jhia Sange Heigala Bhaba and Superstar. On television she has acted in the Tarang TV serials Rani and Kuari Bohu.

She is married to Subhakanta Mohanty. Their elder daughter, Sheetal Patnaik, is an actress who began with the Tarang TV serial Rani and later also performed in jatra. Their younger daughter also acts; she started as a child artist in Rani and works in serials and theatre.

Q56162626.lead: Choudhury Bikash Das is an Odia actor and director who works in film, theatre and television.

p: Das was born in Kotian Barang village in Jagatsinghpur district, Odisha. His father, a doctor, hoped he would follow the same profession, but Das was drawn to painting and acting. While a student at BJB College he acted in the play Mun, Ambhe, Ambhemane, where he met its director Ajit Das, who encouraged him to study drama further. He then enrolled in the drama department of Utkal Sangeet Mahavidyalaya, training under Bijay Mohanty, Ajit Das and other teachers.
His portrayal of Dhadi Gosain in the television serial Shri Jagannath brought him wide popularity.
His brother is Choudhury Jayaprakash Das.

Q15723863.lead: Kartik Kumar Ghosh (1903–1997) was an Odia actor, playwright, lyricist, singer and dancer who appeared in Odia films between 1950 and 1981.

p: Ghosh was born on 23 October 1903 at Bakharabad in Cuttack. His elder brother was the writer and lyricist Ashwini Kumar Ghosh.

His screen roles included Sri Jagannath (1950), Parinam (1961), Matira Manisha (1966) and Sita Labakusa (1980). He wrote the song 'Aji Akashe Ki Ranga Lagila' for the film Sri Lokanath. His book on the history of Odia cinema, Odia Chalachitrara Itihasa, was published in 1984.
He received the Kabi Samrat Upendra Bhanja Samman for 1993–94 and the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Samman in 1996.
He died on 19 May 1997.

Q55758397.lead: Atish Mazumdar (1933–2012) was an Odia singer and music director who sang for many Odia films and for All India Radio.

p: Mazumdar was born in Cuttack in 1933. He was drawn to music as a child and learned it from his mother.
He provided playback vocals for a large number of Odia films and was a regular voice on All India Radio, where he completed 50 years in 2002. He also composed the music for the 1989 film Sasti.

He received the Odisha Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2002, the same year the Cuttack station of All India Radio honoured him. In 2009 he was felicitated by the Sarala Award committee. He died in May 2012.

Q105671780.lead: Manisha Mishra is an Indian actress active since 1996 in Odia feature films and Odia television serials.

p: Mishra first appeared on screen in the 1996 Odia film Pua Moro Bhola Shankara. Her later films include Superstar, Mu Diwana To Pain, Dharma, God Father, Bindas Romeo and To Premare Padila Pare. She played the hero's mother in the Odia film Tora Mora Prema Kahani, which was never released. She appeared in Gaon Ra Na Galuapur (2021) and in Bajibalo Sahanai (2023), directed by Ashutosh Mahapatra. On television she acted in the Manjari TV serial Rakta Samparka.

Q15725367.lead: Surendra Sahoo is an Odia film cinematographer from Odisha who photographed Gapa Hele Bi Sata, the first Odia feature film made in colour.

p: Sahoo trained at the Film and Television Institute of India in Pune, completing his course in 1971.

He was the cinematographer of Gapa Hele Bi Sata (1976), the first Odia colour film. His other credits behind the camera include Dora (1984), Sankha Sindura (1985), Sapana Banika (1985), Pakakambala Pota Chhata (1986), Bagula Baguli (1986), Sabu Mayare Baya (1987) and Topae Sindura Di Pata Sankha (1989). He has also headed the Biju Patnaik Film and Television Institute.
He won the Odisha State Film Award in 1984 and 1989. He was given the Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra Samman in 2005 and the Jayadev Samman in 2006.

facts: Film and Television Institute of India, Pune (1971)

Q42892444.lead: Binoda Nanda (1955–2017) was an Odia film lyricist who also worked as a story writer, director and producer, and was active in literature and publishing.

p: Nanda wrote the lyrics of popular songs such as 'Jhumuka Tike Tu Ta Halei De', 'Jahaku Mun Ete Bhala Pauchhi' and 'Priya Mora E Ki Kala'. His lyric credits include the films Puja Chandana and Chinha Achinha. He wrote the stories of Chinha Achinha and Pratisodha Aparadha Nuhen, and directed the latter. Beyond songwriting he also produced films and made short films.
Outside cinema he wrote the novel Prema O Upahara and was associated with the magazines Bulbul and Chitrapari. He died in Cuttack in 2017.
He received the Odisha State Film Award for Best Story in 1981 for Chinha Achinha.

facts: Jhumuka Tike Tu Ta Halei De; Jahaku Mun Ete Bhala Pauchhi; Priya Mora E Ki Kala

Q38182954.lead: Arun Mohanty is an Odia filmmaker who has worked as producer, director, story writer, screenwriter, dialogue writer, lyricist and music director since 1988.

p: Mohanty entered Odia cinema in 1988 by directing Kanyadaan. On that first film he also wrote the story, screenplay and songs, composed the music and served as producer. He went on to make Ghara Mora Swarga, Sakhi Rahiba Mo Shankha Sindura, Katha Kahiba Mo Matha Sindura, Pua Bhangidela Suna Sansara and Prema Sabuthu Balaban.

Q60511531.lead: Smita Mohanty is an Odia actress from Puri who has worked in Odia films and television serials since 1996.

p: Mohanty made her screen debut in the 1996 Odia film Yashoda. She then played the female lead in films such as Bapa, Jibana Sathi, Pabitra Bandhana, Kalki Abatar and Krushna Kaberi.

In later years she moved to character roles in films including Bande Utkala Janani, Tume Hi Sathi Mora, Ama Bhitare Kichhi Achhi, Asibu Kebe Saji Mo Rani, Kie Se Dakuchi Kouthi Mate, Love Master, Akhire Akhire and Tu Mo Girlfriend. On television, her ETV Odia serial Mausi was popular during its run.

Q28318864.lead: Malobika Banerjee is a Bengali actress from Kolkata, active since 2008, who has also appeared in Odia films.

p: Banerjee was born in Kolkata and studied at Calcutta University.

Her Bengali film work includes Chorabali, Katmundu and Mister Bhaduri. In Odia cinema she has acted in Mate Bohu Kari Nei Jaa, Dele Dhara Katha Sare and Badmash Toka, in which she played Prem Anand. She was also a participant on Bigg Boss Bangla.

In 2018 she moved into Hindi music videos, appearing in 'Dilbar', sung by Shahid Mallya for Zee Music, and 'Pretty Girl', sung by Kanika Kapoor for T-Series. The same year she appeared on the cover of Filmfare magazine.

Q30004756.lead: Baishali Parida is an Odia film actress who worked in Odia cinema from 1985 to 2002.

p: Parida began her screen career in 1985 with Jaga Hatare Pagha. She went on to appear in Mamata Mage Mula, School Master, Ei Ama Sansar, Jor Jar Mulak Tar, Sabu Mayare Baya, Kurukshetra, Bada Bhauja, Rajanigandha, Loot Taraj, Maa Mate Shakti De, Hisab Kariba Kalia and Bastra Harana. In 1995 she acted in Kula Nandan, and her last film was Samay Kheluchhi Chaka Bhaunri in 2002.

Q21030754.lead: Dipak Das (1933–2015) was a Bengali-born cameraman and cinematographer who worked in both Bengali and Odia cinema.

p: Das was born on 13 March 1933 in Mymensingh, in present-day Bangladesh, where he completed his primary schooling.

At the age of 19 he started working as a cameraman and cinematographer in Bengali films. Over his career he shot around 40 Bengali films along with many Odia productions, among them Bandhan, Malajanha and Krishna Sudama.
In 1967 he married the Odia film actress Jharana Das. He died in 2015.

Q47541949.lead: Rali Nanda is an Odia film actress from Odisha who appeared in Odia films between 2008 and 2014.

p: Nanda entered Odia cinema in 2008 with Kalinga Putra. Her later films include Akashe Ki Ranga Lagila, Tu Thile Mo Dara Kahaku, Om Namah Shivay, Nai Separi Kanaka Gori, Superstar, Tanka Tate Salam, Puni Dekha Heba Ara Janamare, Maa Khoje Mamata and Abhimani Priya Mora. In Om Namah Shivay she played a double role. She withdrew from acting after her marriage.

Q124571933.lead: Indramani Behera (died 2024) was an Odia comic actor and local politician who worked on stage, in television serials and in Odia films.

p: Behera was drawn to acting from childhood and started out in stage plays. He later moved on to Odia television serials and films, including Ei Akhi Ama Sakshi.
In politics he won election as the member for ward 10 of Dhenkanal Municipality and also served as its chairperson.
He died in Dhenkanal in 2024, aged 67.

Q138974039.lead: Rabi Swain (1951–2026) was an Odia film producer and industrialist whose productions included Jor Jar Mulak Tar and Udandi Seeta.

p: Swain produced the Odia films Jor Jar Mulak Tar, Ki Heba Sua Posile, Panjuri Bhitare Sari and Udandi Seeta. Outside cinema he was an industrialist who set up several businesses and educational institutions around Pipili, among them the Kshetramohan Memorial Trust, Om Shanti College of Science and Technology, Kshetramohan ITC and Daitari ITC.
He died in Bhubaneswar in 2026, aged 75.

facts: Om Shanti College of Science and Technology; Kshetramohan Memorial Trust

Q15724967.lead: Manoj Mishra is an Odia film actor from Sambalpur who began his career playing villains and has also appeared in Tamil films.

p: Mishra entered Odia cinema as a villain in Suna Sankhali. Alongside his Odia work he has acted in a few Tamil productions. His later Odia films include Jianta Bhoota, Jaggu Autowala, Ashok Samrat, Shiva Not Out, Paika Bidroha and Tandav.

He joined the Indian National Congress and stood as its candidate for the Bolangir Lok Sabha seat in the 2024 general election. He finished third with 230,874 votes, behind the BJP's Sangeeta Kumari Singh Deo, who won by a margin of 386,870 votes.
He is related to Chinmay Mishra.
